> निर्जघानायुधं शक्रो वृत्रेण क्षिप्तमोजसा । वृत्रस्य गात्रादन्यो यः
> प्रादुर्भूतो महासुरः ॥ वृत्रं पूर्वं निहत्येंद्रो द्वितीयं शुष्णसंज्ञकं ।
> पुनर्जघानेंद्र इति पराभिः कीर्तयत्कृषिरिति ॥ इंद्रो महतः प्रभूतस्य मृगस्य
> मृगवच्छीघ्रगामिनस्त्यस्य चित् तस्य वृत्रस्य संबंधि वधरायुधं तविषीभिः स्वकीयैर्बलैनिर्जघान । निःशेषेणावधीत् । एक इदसहाय एवाप्रतिः प्रतिद्वंद्विरहितो
> मन्यमान आत्मानं योऽत्तीति शेषः । आत्तदानीमस्माद्वृतात्तव्यान्प्रवृद्धतरोऽन्नोऽसुरोऽजनिष्ट । प्रादुरभूत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa quotes verses to explain the Ṛk: Indra (Śakra) struck down the weapon that Vṛtra had hurled with force; another great asura, who had appeared from Vṛtra's body, he also struck down; having first slain Vṛtra, Indra again slew a second, named Śuṣṇa, as the seer proclaims in the following Ṛks. He then explains: Indra, with his own powers (तविषीभिः (*taviṣībhiḥ*)), struck down completely the weapon (वधः (*vadhaḥ*)) of that great (महतः (*mahataḥ*)) Vṛtra, who was swift like a deer (मृगस्य (*mṛgasya*)). Vṛtra, thinking himself alone, without help, and without a rival (अप्रतिः (*apratiḥ*)), is the one who devours, this being understood. Then another asura, stronger (तव्यान् (*tavyān*)) than that Vṛtra, was born, that is, appeared.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Vṛtra
- एक इत् (*eka it*)—as the only one
- अप्रतिः (*apratiḥ*)—as without a rival
- मन्यमानः (*manyamānaḥ*)—had thought (such)
- महतः (*mahataḥ*)—of marvellous nature
- मृगस्य (*mṛgasya*)—of sharp nature like a deer
- तस्यचित् (*tasyacit*)—of that very Vṛtra
- वधः (*vadhaḥ*)—the weapon
- तविषीभिः (*taviṣībhiḥ*)—with his powers
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- निः जघान (*niḥ jaghāna*)—has destroyed
- आत् (*āt*)—then
- आस्मात् (*āsmāt*)—than that Vṛtra
- तव्यान् (*tavyān*)—still stronger
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—another asura named Śuṣṇa
- अजनिष्ट (*ajaniṣṭa*)—was born

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, with his powers, has destroyed the weapon of that very Vṛtra, of marvellous nature and sharp like a deer, who had thought himself the only one and without a rival. Then another asura, named Śuṣṇa, still stronger than that Vṛtra, was born.

##### English translation
Indra, by his prowess, has annihilated the weapon of that mighty beast, from whom another more powerful, conceiving himself one and unmatched, was generated.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अन्य: (*anya:*)—The explanation concerning Śuṣṇa is given on page 201 of this same volume.

### Printed p. 231

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्यं चि॑देषां स्व॒धया॒ मदं॑तं मि॒हो नपा॑तं सु॒वृधं॑  ॒
> तमोगां ।  
> वृष॑प्रभर्मा दान॒वस्य॒ भामं॒ वज्रे॑ण व॒ज्री नि ज॑घान॒  ॑
> शुष्णं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्यं । चित् । एषां । स्वधया । मदंतं । मिहः । नपातं । सुवृधं । तमःऽगां ।  
> वृषप्रभर्मा । दानवस्य । भामं । वज्रेण । वज्री । नि । जघान । शुष्णं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषां प्राणिनां स्वधयान्नेन मंदंतं मोदमानं सर्वप्राणिनामन्नं
> स्वयमेव भुंजानं मिहः सेचनसमर्थस्य मेघस्य नपातं पातारं रक्षितारं । अत्र
> नपाच्छब्दः पातरि वर्तते । प्राणो वै तनूनपात्स हि तन्नः पाति । ऐ. ब्रा. २-४ । इति
> ब्राह्मणं । सुवृथं प्रवृद्धं तमोगां तमोऽंधकारं गच्छंतं त्यं चित्तं च वृत्रं
> निजघानेति शेषः । वृषप्रभर्मा वर्षणशीलस्य मेघस्य प्रहर्ता वज्री वज्रवानिंद्रो
> वज्रेण स्वकीयेनायुधेन दानवस्य दनुजस्य भामं । अत्र क्रोधवाचिभामशब्देन
> क्रोधादुत्पन्नः शुष्णासुरो लक्ष्यते । तं शुष्णासुरं नि जघान । हतवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, who strikes the raining cloud, struck down with his own weapon that Vṛtra as well, who rejoiced in the food (स्वधया (*svadhayā*)) of these creatures, enjoying by himself the food of all creatures, the नपातं (*napātaṃ*) (protector, guardian) of the cloud (मिहः (*mihaḥ*)) able to sprinkle; here the word napāt has the sense of protector. He is सुवृथं (*suvṛthaṃ*), well grown, and तमोगां (*tamogāṃ*), going in darkness. To this he adds the Brāhmaṇa: प्राणो वै तनूनपात्स हि तन्नः पाति (*prāṇo vai tanūnapātsa hi tannaḥ pāti*) (Ai. Brā. 2-4). The word भामं (*bhāmaṃ*), which denotes anger, here indicates the asura Śuṣṇa, born of the anger of the Dānava, the son of Danu; Indra struck down that Śuṣṇa.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—which belongs to the creatures
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—with food
- मदंतं (*madaṃtaṃ*)—who was rejoicing
- मिहः (*mihaḥ*)—of the cloud
- नपातं (*napātaṃ*)—the protector
- सुवृथं (*suvṛthaṃ*)—who had grown marvellously
- तमोगां (*tamogāṃ*)—who moves in darkness
- दानवस्य (*dānavasya*)—of Vṛtrāsura
- भामं (*bhāmaṃ*)—the one born of anger
- त्यं चित् शुष्णं (*tyaṃ cit śuṣṇaṃ*)—and the famous asura Śuṣṇa
- वृषप्रभर्मा (*vṛṣaprabharmā*)—who split the rain-making cloud
- वज्री (*vajrī*)—and who holds the thunderbolt, Indra
- वज्रेण (*vajreṇa*)—with his thunderbolt
- नि जघान (*ni jaghāna*)—destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who breaks the cloud and holds the thunderbolt, destroyed with his thunderbolt the asura named Śuṣṇa, who consumed by himself all the food due to creatures and rejoiced in it, who was the protector of the cloud, who had grown marvellously, who moved in darkness, and who was born of the anger of Vṛtrāsura.

### Printed p. 232

##### English translation
The wielder of the thunderbolt, the render of the rain-cloud, has destroyed with his bolt the mighty Sushna, the wrath-born ( son ) of the Danava, the walker in darkness, the protector of the showering cloud, exhilarating himself with the food of these (living creatures).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्यं चि॑दस्य॒ क्रतु॑भि॒र्निष॑त्तमम॒र्मणो॑ वि॒ददिद॑स्य॒ मर्म॑ ।  
> यदीं॑ सुक्षत्र॒ प्रभृ॑ता॒ मद॑स्य॒ युयु॑त्संतं॒ तम॑सि ह॒र्म्ये  
> धाः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्यं । चित् । अस्य । क्रतुभिः । निसत्तं । अमर्मणः । विदत् । इत् । अस्य । मर्म ।  
> यत् । ईं । सुक्षत्र । प्रभृता । मदस्य । युयुत्संतं । तमसि । हर्म्ये । धाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमर्मणो मर्महीनमात्मानं मन्यमानस्यास्य वृत्रस्य निषत्तं निषण्णं
> त्यं चित् त्यत्तदेव ॥ लिंगव्यत्ययः ॥ मर्म प्राणस्थानं । यत्र स्थाने विद्धो
> म्रियते तन्मर्मेत्युच्यते । अस्य वृत्रस्य क्रतुभिः प्रज्ञानैर्हे इंद्र त्वं विददित् ।
> अज्ञासीरेव । यद्यदा हे सुक्षत्र सुबलेंद्र त्वं मदस्य मादकस्य सोमस्य प्रभृता
> प्रभृतौ संभरणे सति युयुत्संतं योद्दुमिच्छंतमीमेनं वृत्रं हर्म्ये हारके
> तमसि धाः नृदधाः । वृत्र इंद्रस्य भयात्तमसि प्राविशदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: Of this Vṛtra, who thought himself without a vital spot (अमर्मणो (*amarmaṇo*)), the hidden निषत्तं (*niṣattaṃ*) vital spot (the word त्यं चित् (*tyaṃ cit*) stands for that same, with a change of gender). A vital spot (मर्म (*marma*)) is the seat of life: the place where, when pierced, one dies. O Indra, you knew it (विददित् (*vidadit*)) through the knowledge (क्रतुभिः (*kratubhiḥ*)) of this Vṛtra. When, O Sukṣatra, strong Indra, on the taking up (प्रभृता (*prabhṛtā*)) of the intoxicating Soma, you placed Vṛtra, who wished to fight, in the carrying-off darkness (हर्म्ये हारके तमसि (*harmye hārake tamasi*)): the meaning is that Vṛtra entered the darkness through fear of Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमर्मणः (*amarmaṇaḥ*)—of Vṛtrāsura, who had understood that there was no (dangerous) place in his body for killing him (you, O Indra)
- निषत्तं (*niṣattaṃ*)—which was hidden
- मर्म (*marma*)—the vulnerable spot
- त्यं चित् (*tyaṃ cit*)—that very one which there was
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Vṛtra
- क्रतुभिः (*kratubhiḥ*)—through his deeds
- विदत् इत् (*vidat it*)—you found out indeed
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सुक्षत्र (*sukṣatra*)—O Indra, of great strength
- मदस्य (*madasya*)—the Soma which causes joy
- प्रभृता (*prabhṛtā*)—after you had drunk
- हर्म्म्ये (*harmmye*)—which robs of sight (in which one cannot see)
- तमसि (*tamasi*)—in the darkness
- युयत्संतं (*yuyatsaṃtaṃ*)—Vṛtra, who was getting ready to fight
- धाः (*dhāḥ*)—you made fall down

### Printed p. 233

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you came to know, through the very deeds of Vṛtrāsura, who boasted that there was no vulnerable spot in him by which he could be killed, that dangerous spot of his. O mighty Indra, after you had drunk the Soma that causes joy, you thrust down Vṛtra, who was making ready for battle in the dense darkness in which nothing could be seen.

##### English translation
You have discovered, Indra, by his acts, the secret vital part of him who thought himself invulnerable, when, powerful Indra, in the exhilaration of the Soma, you have detected him preparing for combat in his dark abode.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्यंचि॑दि॒त्था क॑त्प॒यं शया॑नमसू॒र्ये तम॑सि वावृधा॒नं ।  
> तं चि॑न्मंदा॒नो वृ॑ष॒भः सु॒तस्यो॒च्चैरिंद्रो॑ अप॒गूर्या॑  
> जघान ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्यं । चित् । इत्था । कत्पयं । शयानं । असूर्ये । तमसि । ववृधानं ।  
> तं । चित् । मंदानः । वृषभः । सुतस्य । उच्चैः । इंद्रः । अपगूर्य । जघान ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुतस्याभिषुतेन सोमेन मंदानो मोदमानो वृषभः कामानां
> वर्षितेंद्र उच्चैरूर्ध्वमपगूर्य वज्रमुद्यम्य तं चित्तमेव वृत्रासुरं
> जघान । अवधीत् । कीदृशं । इत्थामुत्रांतरिक्षलोके कत्सयं । कत्सुखकरं पयो
> यस्य तं । शयानमप्पु शयनं कुर्वंतमसूर्ये सूर्यरहिते तमस्यंधकारे
> ववृधानं वर्धमानं । त्यं चिदिति पुनर्वचनं पूरणार्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the showerer of desires, delighted by the Soma that has been pressed (सुतस्य (*sutasya*)), raised his thunderbolt aloft and slew that very Vṛtrāsura. Sāyaṇa describes him: इत्था (*itthā*) means "in the atmospheric world"; कत्सयं (*katsayaṃ*) means one whose water (पयो (*payo*)) gives pleasant ease; शयानं (*śayānaṃ*) means one lying down in the waters; असूर्ये (*asūrye*) means in the sunless तमसि (*tamasi*), that is, in darkness; ववृधानं (*vavṛdhānaṃ*) means one who was growing. The repetition in त्यं चित् (*tyaṃ cit*) is only for completion.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—from the drinking of the desired Soma
- मंदानः (*maṃdānaḥ*)—one who is delighted
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the showerer of desires
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- उच्चैः अपगूर्य (*uccaiḥ apagūrya*)—having lifted up his thunderbolt
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in the atmospheric world
- कत्पयं (*katpayaṃ*)—one who dwells in the pleasant water
- शयानं (*śayānaṃ*)—one who lay sleeping in the atmosphere
- आसूरै (*āsūrai*)—sunless
- तमसि (*tamasi*)—in the darkness
- नवृधानं (*navṛdhānaṃ*)—one who had grown
- त्यं (*tyaṃ*)—the famous one
- तं चित् (*taṃ cit*)—that Vṛtrāsura
- जघान (*jaghāna*)—he slew

### Printed p. 234

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, delighted by the drinking of the pressed Soma and the showerer of desires, lifted up his thunderbolt and slew Vṛtrāsura, who had lain sleeping in the atmosphere in the midst of pleasant water and had grown in the sunless darkness.

##### English translation
Indra, the showerer (of benefits) exhilarated by the effused juices, uplifting (his thunderbolt), has slain him enjoying the dews of the fiirmament sleeping (amidst the waters), and thriving in sunless darkness.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उद्यदिंद्रो॑ मह॒ते दा॑न॒वाय॒ वध॒र्यमि॑ष्ट॒ सहो॒  ॑
> अप्रतीतं ।  
> यदीं॒ वज्र॑स्य॒ प्रभृ॑तौ द॒दाभ॒ विश्व॑स्य जं॒तोर॑ध॒मं च॑कार ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । यत् । इंद्रः । महते । दानवाय । वधः । यमिष्ट । सहः । अप्रतिइतं ।  
> यत् । ईं । वज्रस्य । प्रभृतौ । ददाभ । विश्वस्य । जंतोः । अधमं । चकार ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदेंद्रो महते प्रभूताय दानवाय वृत्रासुराय सहः शत्रूणामभिभवितृ अप्रतीतं केनाप्यप्रतिगतं वधर्वज्रमुद्यमिष्ट उदयच्छत् । यद्यदा
> वज्रस्य प्रभृतौ प्रहृतौ प्रहरणे सति ॥ हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वं ॥ ईमेनं वृत्रं
> ददाभ अहिंसीत् तदा विश्वस्य सर्वस्य जंतोः प्राणिनोऽधमं नीचं चकार ।
> अकरोत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When Indra raised his thunderbolt (वधर्वज्रमुद्यमिष्ट (*vadharvajramudyamiṣṭa*)), which overpowers enemies and which nobody has withstood, against the great and mighty Dānava, Vṛtrāsura, and when, at the hurling of the thunderbolt, he injured this Vṛtra, then he made him the lowest, the meanest, of every living creature.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- महते (*mahate*)—of great strength
- दानवाय (*dānavāya*)—against Vṛtra, the Asura
- सहः (*sahaḥ*)—that which withstands enemies
- अप्रतीतं (*apratītaṃ*)—that which cannot be turned back

### Printed p. 235

- वधः (*vadhaḥ*)—the thunderbolt
- उत् यमिष्ट (*ut yamiṣṭa*)—he hurled, (and)
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वज्रस्य (*vajrasya*)—of the thunderbolt
- प्रभृतौ (*prabhṛtau*)—when it was hurled
- ईं (*īṃ*)—Vṛtra
- ददाभ (*dadābha*)—he injured (then him)
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of all
- जंतोः (*jaṃtoḥ*)—than creatures
- अधमं (*adhamaṃ*)—so as to go down below
- चकार (*cakāra*)—he made

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When Indra hurled his thunderbolt, which withstands enemies and cannot be turned back, against Vṛtra, the mighty Asura, Vṛtra was grievously injured. Immediately he was thrust down into a region lower than all creatures.

##### English translation
When Indra raised his powerful irresistible weapon against the mighty Danava, when he struck him with the blow of the thunderbolt, he made him the lowest of all creatures.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्यं चि॒दर्णं॑ मधु॒पं शया॑नमसि॒न्वं व॒व्रं मह्याद॑दु॒ग्रः ।  
> अ॒पाद॑म॒त्रं म॑ह॒ता व॒धेन॒ नि दु॑र्यो॒ण आ॑वृणङ्मृ॒ध्रवा॑चं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्यं । चित् । अर्णं । मधुपं । शयानं । असिन्वं । वव्रं । महि । आदत् । उग्रः ।  
> अपादं । अत्रं । महता । वधेन । नि । दुर्योणे । अवृणक् । मृध्रवाचं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उग्र उद्धूर्णबल इंद्रो महि महांतं त्यं चित्तमेव वृत्रमादत् ।
> आददौ । प्रत्यग्रहीत् । कीदृशं । अर्णं गंतारं जलं मेघं वावृत्य शयानं
> शयनं कुर्वंतं । स्थितवंतमित्यर्थः । मधुपं मधुनोंभसः पातारं पालयितारमसिन्वं सपत्नानामवक्षेप्तारं ॥ अस्यतेरिदं रूपं ॥ वव्रं वृण्वंशं सर्वम.
> प्याच्छादयंतं । स इमाल्लोकानवृणोत्तद्वृत्तस्य वृत्रत्वं । तै. सं. २-५-२-२ ।
> इति हि तैत्तिरीयकं । तदनंतरमिंद्रो दुर्योणे संगामे महता प्रभूतेन

### Printed p. 236

> वधेन वज्रेणापादं पादरहितममत्रममात्रं परिमाणरहितं मृध्रवाचं हिंसितवागिंद्रियं । जृंभाभिभूतमित्यर्थः । वृत्रं नृवृणक् । नितरामहिंसीत् । तस्माज्जंजभ्यमानादग्नीषोमो निरक्रामतां प्राणापान् वा एनं तदजहितां । तै. सं.
> २-५-२-४ । इति हि तैत्तिरीयकं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The fierce Indra, of overpowering strength, seized that very Vṛtra, the great one. Sāyaṇa glosses the epithets: अर्णं (*arṇaṃ*) is one who goes, or water, or a cloud, having enveloped which he lay (शयानं (*śayānaṃ*)), that is, remained there; मधुपं (*madhupaṃ*) is the drinker and protector of the sweet water; असिन्वं (*asinvaṃ*) is one who casts down his rivals; वव्रं (*vavraṃ*) is one who covers everything. He quotes the Taittirīya: "He covered these worlds; hence Vṛtra is Vṛtra" (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-2-2). After that, Indra in the battle (दुर्योणे (*duryoṇe*)), with his great and abundant weapon, the thunderbolt, utterly slew Vṛtra, who was footless, measureless, and whose faculty of speech was injured, that is, who was overcome by yawning. Sāyaṇa quotes the Taittirīya again: from him, as he was yawning, Agni and Soma departed, and the in-breath and the out-breath left him then (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-2-4).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—Indra, of terrible strength
- अर्णं (*arṇaṃ*)—one who goes about enveloping the waters
- शयानं (*śayānaṃ*)—one who lies in the atmosphere
- मधुपं (*madhupaṃ*)—the protector of the water
- असिन्वं (*asinvaṃ*)—one who defeats his enemies and throws them down
- वव्रं (*vavraṃ*)—one who has the power to envelop everything
- महि (*mahi*)—one of great power
- त्यं चित् (*tyaṃ cit*)—that very Vṛtra (when)
- आदत् (*ādat*)—he seized, then
- दुर्योणे (*duryoṇe*)—in battle
- महता (*mahatā*)—with the abundant
- वधेन (*vadhena*)—thunderbolt
- अपादं (*apādaṃ*)—the footless
- अत्रं (*atraṃ*)—the measureless
- मृध्रवाचं (*mṛdhravācaṃ*)—the one whose speech is harmful, Vṛtrāsura
- नि अवृणक् (*ni avṛṇak*)—he injured completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the fierce Indra seized that very Vṛtra, who goes about enveloping the waters, who lies in the atmosphere, who is the protector of the water, who defeats his enemies and throws them down, and who has the power to envelop everything, then in the battle he injured Vṛtra completely with his thunderbolt of mighty form, Vṛtra who was footless, measureless and of harmful speech.

##### English translation
The fierce Indra seized upon him, that vast moving (Vritra), when slumbering, (after) having drunk the Soma, subduing (his foe-), and envelop- ing (the world), and then slew him with his great weapon in battle, footless, measureless, speechless.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> को अ॑स्य॒ शुष्मं॒ तवि॑षीं वरात॒ एको॒ धना॑ भरते॒ अप्र॑तीतः ।  
> इ॒मे च॑दस्य॒ ज्रय॑सो॒ नु दे॒वी इंद्र॒सौज॑सो भि॒यसा॑  
> चहाते ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कः । अस्य । शुष्मं । तविषीं । वराते । एकः । धना । भरते । अप्रतिइतः ।  
> इमे इति । चित् । अस्य । ज्रयसः । नु । देवी इति । इंद्रस्य । ओजसः । भियसा ।  
> जिहाते इति ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्येंद्रस्य संबंधिनीं शुष्मं शोषणीं तविषीं बलं को वराते । निवारयेत् ॥ शुष्मशब्दस्य स्त्रीलिंगविशेषणत्वेऽपि नियतलिंगत्वात्पुल्लिंगत्वमेव ॥ अप्रतीतः

> हरते वा । देवी देव्या द्योतमाने इमे चिदेव द्यावापृथिव्यौ ज्रयसो
> वेगवतोऽस्येंद्रस्य संबंधिन ओजसो बलवादुद्भूतेन भयसा भयेन नु क्षिप्रं
> जिहाते । गच्छतः । चलत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Who can hold back the withering (शोषणीं (*śoṣaṇīṃ*)) strength of this Indra? Indra, whom nobody has withstood, alone and unaided, carries off (or seizes) the riches of his enemies. These two shining ones, heaven and earth, move swiftly through the fear that arises from the strength of the swift Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*)—that destroys enemies
- तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*)—the strength
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who indeed
- वराते (*varāte*)—can obstruct?
- अप्रतीतः (*apratītaḥ*)—Indra, who has never been repelled
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—alone, unaided
- धना (*dhanā*)—the riches of enemies
- भरते (*bharate*)—he carries
- देवी (*devī*)—the two divine beings
- इमे चित् (*ime cit*)—even these heaven and earth
- ज्रयसः (*jrayasaḥ*)—swift
- अस्य इंद्रस्य (*asya iṃdrasya*)—of this Indra
- ओजसः (*ojasaḥ*)—of the strength
- भयसा नु (*bhayasā nu*)—through fear
- जिहाते (*jihāte*)—they move

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Who can obstruct the enemy-destroying strength of this Indra? Indra, whom nobody has repelled, carries off the riches of his enemies, alone and unaided. Even these two divine beings, heaven and earth, move through fear of the strength of the swift Indra.

##### English translation
Who may resist the withering might of that Indra : he, single and irresistible, carries off the riches (of the enemy) : these two divine (beings, heaven and earth), proceed swiftly through fear of the strength of the quick-moving Indra.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न्य॑स्मै दे॒वी स्वधि॑तिर्जिहीत॒ इंद्रा॑य गा॒तुरु॑श॒तीव॑ येमे ।  
> सं यदोजो॑ यु॒वते॒ विश्व॑माभि॒रनु॑ स्व॒धान्ने॑ क्षि॒तयो॑  
> नमंत ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । अस्मै । देवी । स्वधितिः । जिहीते । इंद्राय । गातुः । उशतीऽइव । येमे ।  
> सं । यत् । ओजः । युवते । विश्वं । अभिः । अनु । स्वधाऽन्ने । क्षितयः । नमंत ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वधितिः स्वधृतिः स्वेन धृता देवी द्योतमाना द्यौरस्मा इंद्राय नि जिहीते ।
> नीचत्वेन याति । गातुर्भूमिरुशतीव कामयमाना योषिदिवेंद्राय येमे ।
> आत्मानं नियच्छति । यथेष्टमात्मानं नियोक्तुं योग्या भवतीत्यर्थः । यद्यदेंद्रो विश्वं समस्तमोजो बलमाभिः प्रजाभिः सं युवते संयोजयति ।
> इंद्रः स्वकीयं बलं सर्वासु प्रजासु निहितवानित्यर्थः । अनु अनुकूल्येन वर्तमानाः क्षितयो मनुष्याः । क्षितय इति मनुष्यनामैतत् । स्वधान्ने बलवत
> इंद्राय नमंत । संनमंति । प्रह्वीभवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

स्वधितिः (*svadhitiḥ*) means "held by herself": the shining Heaven bows down to Indra, that is, goes down in lowliness. गातुः (*gātuḥ*), the Earth, like a woman full of desire, holds herself in check for Indra; that is, she becomes fit to be disposed of as he pleases. When Indra joins all his strength with these creatures, that is, when Indra has placed his own strength in all the creatures, then the people (क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*) is a name for men), following in accord with him, bow down to the mighty Indra, स्वधान्ने (*svadhānne*); they bow and become humble.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वधितिः (*svadhitiḥ*)—she who sustains herself by her own power
- देवी (*devī*)—the radiant presiding deity of the heavenly world
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—toward Indra
- नि जिहीते (*ni jihīte*)—she is submissive
- गातुः (*gātuḥ*)—the Earth
- उशतीव (*uśatīva*)—like a woman full of love
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's companionship
- येमे (*yeme*)—she surrenders (her self)
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—strength
- अभिः (*abhiḥ*)—with all the creatures
- सं युवते (*saṃ yuvate*)—he unites (then)
- अनु (*anu*)—those who act according to Indra's wish
- क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*)—men
- स्वधाम्ने (*svadhāmne*)—to the mighty Indra
- नमंत (*namaṃta*)—they bow humbly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The radiant presiding deity of the heavenly world, who sustains herself by her own power, is submissive to Indra. The Earth, like a woman full of love, surrenders herself to Indra's companionship.

### Printed p. 239

When Indra unites all his strength with all the creatures, then all men, who follow Indra's wish, bow humbly to the mighty Indra.

##### English translation
The divine, self-sustaining (heaven) comes to him ; the moving (earth), like a loving (wife), resigns herself to Indra : when he shares all his vigour with these (his people), then in due succession, men offer reverence to the potent Indra.

> दोषा क्षपायां वस्तोर्वासरे च हवमानासः स्तुवंत आशसः कामानां शुसमाना मे मदीयाः प्रजा नविष्ठमतिशयेन स्तुत्यं तमिंद्रं जगृभ्रे । गृह्णंतु ।
> स्वीकुर्वंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, I, the seer of the mantra, hear of you alone as the chief among all men, from the foremost of the seers. He describes him: सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*), the protector of the good; पांचजन्यं (*pāṃcajanyaṃ*), one who is beneficial to the five peoples, that is, to men; born, and glorious. Praising him by night (दोषा (*doṣā*)) and by day (वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)), desiring their wishes, my people have taken hold of that Indra, the most praiseworthy; let them accept him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*)—protector of the good
- पांचजन्यं (*pāṃcajanyaṃ*)—beneficial to the five kinds of people
- जातं (*jātaṃ*)—born
- यशसं (*yaśasaṃ*)—glorious
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- जनेषु (*janeṣu*)—among all men

### Printed p. 240

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एकं नु (*ekaṃ nu*)—as the most excellent, the chief one
- शृणोमि (*śṛṇomi*)—I have heard
- दोषा (*doṣā*)—at night
- वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)—by day
- हवमानासः (*havamānāsaḥ*)—those who praise (you)
- आशासः (*āśāsaḥ*)—those who pray for their desired ends
- मे (*me*)—my sons and others
- नविष्ठं (*naviṣṭhaṃ*)—exceedingly praiseworthy
- तं इंद्रं (*taṃ iṃdraṃ*)—that Indra
- जगृभ्रे (*jagṛbhre*)—may they accept

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, I have heard of you, the protector of the good, who were born beneficial to the five kinds of people and are endowed with fame, as the most excellent chief among all men. May my sons and others, who praise you day and night and pray for their desired ends, accept that Indra, who is exceedingly praiseworthy.

##### English translation
Verily I hear of you as chief amongst men, the protector of the good friendly to the five classes of beings, the begotten, the renowned ; may my (progeny), representing (their wishes), and uttering his praises night and, day, propitiate the glorified Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पांचजन्यं (*pāṃcajanyaṃ*)—गंधर्वा अप्सरसो देवा असुरा रक्षांसि पंचजनाः । निषादपंच माश्चत्वारो वर्णा वा । (*gaṃdharvā apsaraso devā asurā rakṣāṃsi paṃcajanāḥ | niṣādapaṃca māścatvāro varṇā vā |*). Sāyaṇa explains that the five groups are the Gandharvas, the Apsarases, the gods, the Asuras and the Rākṣasas together; or else the four classes of people (varṇas) together with the fifth group, the Niṣādas, that is, the hunters. There are differences of opinion in this classification. The author of the Nirukta has not stated his own view, but has only cited the opinions of others.

पंचजना ( मम होत्रं जुषध्वं ) गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः । (*paṃcajanā ( mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ ) gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsītyeke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ paṃcama ityaupamanyavaḥ |*) (Ni. 3-8)

That is, some say that the five kinds of people are the Gandharvas, the ancestors, the gods, the Asuras and the Rākṣasas; Upamanyu and others hold that the four classes of people beginning with the Brāhmaṇas, together with the fifth group called the Niṣādas, are the five peoples. Thus he has stated only the opinions of others.

Formerly, when all the gods addressed Agni and prayed that he should accept the oblation offered in the sacrifice for them and distribute it to all, Agni agreed and said:

तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुरा अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं । (*tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurā abhi devā asāma | ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4).

### Printed p. 241

The author of the Bṛhaddevatā cites this sentence, in which the answer is given that the five peoples should enjoy this oblation, and discusses it, showing the differences of opinion about who the five peoples are. In the śloka

प्रत्युवाचाथ तानग्निर्विश्वेदेवा यदूच मां । तत्करिष्ये जुषंतां तु होत्रं पंचजना मम ॥ (*pratyuvācātha tānagnirviśvedevā yadūca māṃ | tatkariṣye juṣaṃtāṃ tu hotraṃ paṃcajanā mama ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-66)

he states the answer that Agni gave to the gods, and then explains the word pañcajana:

शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः । उत्तरो दक्षिणश्चाग्निरेते पंचजनाः स्मृताः ॥ (*śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaśca putro gṛhapateśca yaḥ | uttaro dakṣiṇaścāgnirete paṃcajanāḥ smṛtāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-67)

That is, the fire at the entrance of the hall, the Āhavanīya fire that has been led forth, the Gārhapatya fire that is like a son of the sacrificer, and the southern and northern fires: these five kinds of fire are held to be the five groups, according to traditional usage. This is one opinion. Moreover:

मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गंधर्वोरगराक्षसाः । गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ (*manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ | gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-68)

According to the first opinion the serpents and Rākṣasas form one group; in the second the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas form one group.

यास्कौपमन्यनावेतानाहतुः पंच वै जनान् । निषादपंचमान्वर्णा मन्यते शाकटायनः ॥ (*yāskaupamanyanāvetānāhatuḥ paṃca vai janān | niṣādapaṃcamānvarṇā manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 76-69)**NOTE**

In this verse the author of the Bṛhaddevatā says that Yāska's opinion is the first. But in the Nirukta the opinions of others are stated, and Yāska's own opinion is not stated definitively. Probably he too accepted that one.

ऋत्विजो यजमानं च शाकपूणिस्तु मन्यते । (*ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇistu manyate |*) (Bṛ. De. 7-20)**NOTE**

The opinion of Śākapūṇi is that the four priests, the hotṛ and the others, together with the sacrificer make five groups.

चक्षुः श्रोतं मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः । गंधर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा ॥ सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयंते हैतरेयके । (*cakṣuḥ śrotaṃ mano vāk ca prāṇaścetyātmavādinaḥ | gaṃdharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitarastathā ‖ sarpāśca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyaṃte haitareyake |*)

### Printed p. 242

The opinion of those who speak of the Self is that these five, the eye, the ear, the mind, speech and breath, are the five peoples. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa explains them as the Gandharvas and the others (Ai. Brā. 3-31-5). Differences of opinion are cited also in the explanation of the Bṛhaddevatā, where it is said that Agni gave the gods the answer that such five peoples should enjoy the oblation.

The words पंच जनाः (*paṃca janāḥ*) and पंचकृस्टीः (*paṃcakṛsṭīḥ*) occur in many places in the Ṛgveda:

तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुरा अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं ॥ (*tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurā abhi devā asāma | ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4)

पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषंतां गोजाता उत ये यज्ञियासः । (*paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣaṃtāṃ gojātā uta ye yajñiyāsaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-5)

सद्यश्चिद्यः शवसा पंचकृष्णी सूर्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान ॥ (*sadyaścidyaḥ śavasā paṃcakṛṣṇī sūrya iva jyotiṣāpastatāna ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-178-3)

In his Nirukta Yāska has explained the words पंचजनाः (*paṃcajanāḥ*) and पंचकृष्टीः (*paṃcakṛṣṭīḥ*) in these ṛks in the following way:

पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः । निषादः कस्मान्निषदनो भवति निषण्णमस्मिन् पापकमिति नैरुक्ताः (*paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsītyeke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ paṃcama ityaupamanyavaḥ | niṣādaḥ kasmānniṣadano bhavati niṣaṇṇamasmin pāpakamiti nairuktāḥ*)

That is, some say that the five peoples are the Gandharvas, the ancestors, the gods, the Asuras and the Rākṣasas. The opinion of Upamanyu and others is that the four classes of people beginning with the Brāhmaṇas, together with the people of the hunter caste called Niṣāda, make the five kinds of people (Sāyaṇa has approved this). The Nirukta-writers say that Niṣādas are those who kill animals, or that they are called Niṣāda because sin has settled in them. Besides this, there may have been five principal tribes at that time. The poet may have kept this very opinion in mind and said पंच क्षितीनां (*paṃca kṣitīnāṃ*). In any case it is clear that there was a difference of opinion on this matter even in the time of Yāska, the author of the Nirukta.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा हि त्वामृ॑तु॒था या॒तयं॑तं म॒घा विप्रे॑भ्यो॒ दद॑तं  ॒॑
> शृणोमि ।  
> किं ते॑ ब्र॒ह्माणो॑ गृहते॒ सखा॑यो॒ ये त्वा॒या नि॑द॒धुः  ॑
> काममिंद्र ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । हि । त्वां । ऋतुथा । यातयंतं । मघा । विप्रेभ्यः । ददतं । शृणोमि ।  
> किं । ते । ब्रह्माणः । गृहते । सखायः । ये । त्वाया । निदधुः । कामं । इंद्र ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एवैवमुक्तप्रकारेण हि ऋतुथा काले काले यातयंतं जंतून्सेरयंतं हे इंद्र त्वां विप्रेभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यो मघा मघानि धनानि ददतं यच्छंतं
> शृणोमि । निशामयामि । एतनृष्यैव प्रतिभाति । हे इंद्र त्वाया त्वयि ये
> स्तोतारः कामं स्वकीयाभिलाषं निदधुः न्यक्षिपन् ब्रह्माणो बृहंतस्ते त्वदीयाः
> सखायः स्तोतारः किं गृहते । त्वत्तः किं गृष्णंते । ऋषिः स्वकीयाभिलाषप्राप्तिविलंबनादेवमुक्तवानित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the manner just stated, O Indra, I hear of you as one who from time to time, in the proper seasons, sets creatures in motion (यातयंतं (*yātayaṃtaṃ*)) and gives wealth (मघा (*maghā*)) to the praisers, the learned singers (विप्रेभ्यः (*viprebhyaḥ*)). "I hear" means "I perceive"; this is how it strikes the seer himself. O Indra, the praisers who have placed their own desire in you, the great ones (ब्रह्माणो (*brahmāṇo*) means "great"), your friends, the praisers: what do they obtain from you? The seer spoke in this way because the fulfilment of his own wish was delayed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) एव (*eva*)—in this manner
- ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*)—in the respective seasons
- यातयंतं (*yātayaṃtaṃ*)—one who impels people (to their respective rites)
- विप्रेभ्यः (*viprebhyaḥ*)—to the praisers
- मघा (*maghā*)—wealth
- ददतं (*dadataṃ*)—one who gives
- त्वा (*tvā*)—concerning you
- शृणोमि (*śṛṇomi*)—I have heard (from those who know) (O Indra)
- त्वाया (*tvāyā*)—in you
- ये (*ye*)—which of your praisers
- कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—their desired ends
- निदधुः (*nidadhuḥ*)—place
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—those of great nature
- ते (*te*)—your kinsmen
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—the praisers
- किं गृह्णते (*kiṃ gṛhṇate*)—what can they obtain (from you)?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, I have heard from those who know about you, who constantly impel people at the respective seasons to the respective rites and who give wealth to the praisers.

### Printed p. 244

What can those praisers of yours obtain from you, who place their desired ends in you, who know the great truth and are your kinsmen?

##### English translation
I hear of you influencing (creatures) according to the season, and giving riches to the pious ; but what do your devoted friends ( obtain ), who have entrusted their desires, Indra, to you ?

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणामात्येन विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये चतुर्थाष्टके प्रथमोऽध्यायः ॥ (*iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇāmātyena viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye caturthāṣṭake prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ ‖*) समाप्तिः (*samāptiḥ*) ओं तत्स्यत् (*oṃ tatsyat*)

Here ends the first adhyāya, in the fourth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and with a Kannada translation.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖*) शुभं भूयात् (*śubhaṃ bhūyāt*) मंगळं (*maṃgaḷaṃ*)

Om. Obeisance to Śrī Mahāgaṇapati.

वागीशादाः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे ! यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame ! yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)

यस्य निश्यसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśyasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*)

वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*)

**Introduction**

Fourth Aṣṭaka, second Adhyāya.

Fifth Maṇḍala, thirty-third Sūkta.

**Prefatory note**

In this section, the second adhyāya of the fourth aṣṭaka, there are in all 14 sūktas, from the 33rd sūkta to the 46th sūkta of the fifth maṇḍala. This section can be roughly divided into two parts. First, ऐंद्राणि द्वादश (*aiṃdrāṇi dvādaśa*) (Bṛ. De. 5-27): the twelve Aindra sūktas from the 29th sūkta to the 40th sūkta of the 5th maṇḍala. Of these, 8 sūktas of the present adhyāya are included, that is, up to the 40th sūkta. Second,

को नु वां वैश्वदेवानि एकादश पराण्यतः । (*ko nu vāṃ vaiśvadevāni ekādaśa parāṇyataḥ |*) (Bṛ. De. 5-36)

the eleven Vaiśvadeva sūktas in all, from the 41st sūkta, which begins with को नु वां (*ko nu vāṃ*), to the 51st sūkta. Of these, 6 sūktas of the present adhyāya are included. That is, 8 Aindra sūktas and

### Printed p. 246

the remaining 6 Vaiśvadeva sūktas: this is the rough division. But in these same sūktas other deities who are to be praised incidentally are also included. It is therefore necessary to examine how many such occasions there are in the Aindra sūktas, and who the deities are that are included occasionally in the Vaiśvadeva sūktas. If the Aindra sūktas are explained first,

यत्वा सूर्येति चात्रीणां पंचर्चे कर्म कीर्त्यते । (*yatvā sūryeti cātrīṇāṃ paṃcarce karma kīrtyate |*) (Bṛ. De. 5-28)

in the five mantras (5-40-5 to 9), beginning with the mantra यत् त्वा सूर (*yat tvā sūra*), the work of Atri is praised. This episode stands in the midst of the Aindra sūktas. Although the subject makes known the greatness of Atri's work, praise of Indra is mixed with it, and so it may be said that praise of Indra runs through it as well. Sentences such as इंद्र माया अवाहन् (*iṃdra māyā avāhan*) (5-40-6) make this clear. The gist of this section is that when Sūra was hidden by Svarbhānu, through the efforts of Indra and the efforts of Atri Svarbhānu was destroyed, and the light of Sūra was able to spread over the whole world. The greatness of Atri has been told in the introduction at the beginning of the fifth maṇḍala; there is no need to describe it here. Only the present context is briefly stated.

Svarbhānu is the son of an Asura. When he hid Sūra and obstructed his light, Indra and Atri destroyed him: this is the description of the present context. But this occasion is described in one way in one place and in another way in another. For example:

सुवर्भानुरासुरस्सूर्यं तमसाविध्यत्तस्मै देवाः प्रायश्चित्तिमैच्छन्तस्य यत्प्रथमं तमोऽपाघ्नन्ता कृष्णा विरभवद्यद्दितीयग्ं सा फल्गुनी यतृतीयग्ं सा वलक्षी यथद्यस्थादपाकृंतन्ता निर्वशा समभवत्ते देवा देवा अब्रुवन् देवपशुर्वा अयग्ं समभूत् ॥ (*suvarbhānurāsurassūryaṃ tamasāvidhyattasmai devāḥ prāyaścittimaicchantasya yatprathamaṃ tamo 'pāghnantā kṛṣṇā virabhavadyadditīyagṃ sā phalgunī yatṛtīyagṃ sā valakṣī yathadyasthādapākṛṃtantā nirvaśā samabhavatte devā devā abruvan devapaśurvā ayagṃ samabhūt ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-2-2)

Svarbhānu, the son of an Asura, once caused Sūra to be covered with darkness. The gods then tried to remove it. As soon as they had destroyed half of that darkness, a black cloud came into being. From the second half the origin of a shining cloud came about. From the third it became of white colour. What was cut off from the upper part of the bone came to be transformed into a barren animal. Then all the gods together discussed: "This has become an animal of the gods; to whom shall we offer it?" And so on: in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā it is described

### Printed p. 247

But here there is no statement that either Atri or Indra destroyed Svarbhānu and made the sun shine. Explaining this same occasion, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa states as follows:

स्वर्भानुर्ह वा असुरः सूर्यं तमसा विव्याध । स तमसा विद्धो न व्यरोचत तस्य सोमारुद्रादेवैतत्तमोऽपाहताग्ं स एषोऽपहतपाप्मा तपति ॥ (*svarbhānurha vā asuraḥ sūryaṃ tamasā vivyādha | sa tamasā viddho na vyarocata tasya somārudrādevaitattamo 'pāhatāgṃ sa eṣo 'pahatapāpmā tapati ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 5-3-2-2)

The Asura Svarbhānu once covered the sun with darkness. Then the sun, enveloped in darkness, did not shine. Then, after Soma and Rudra both had destroyed that darkness, the sun began to shine, it is said. Here too there is no praise of Atri's help.

Therefore only in the Ṛk-saṃhitā (5-40-5 to 9) is it stated that the great seer Atri became the cause of Svarbhānu's destruction. Showing a spiritual tradition in this endeavour:

स्वर्भानोरध यदिंद्र माया अवो दिवो वर्तमाना अवाहन् । गूह्लं सूर्यं तमसापव्रतेन तुरीयेण ब्रह्मणाविंददत्रिः ॥ (*svarbhānoradha yadiṃdra māyā avo divo vartamānā avāhan | gūhlaṃ sūryaṃ tamasāpavratena turīyeṇa brahmaṇāviṃdadatriḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-6)

यत्त्वा सूर्य स्वर्भानुस्तमसाविध्यदासुरः । अक्षेत्रविद्यधा मुग्धो भुवनान्यदीधयुः ॥ (*yattvā sūrya svarbhānustamasāvidhyadāsuraḥ | akṣetravidyadhā mugdho bhuvanānyadīdhayuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-5)

It is said that Atri destroyed this darkness, which was of the nature of illusion, by means of the fourth mantra. What the spiritual meaning is in this context has been stated earlier, in the special topics on the mantra Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-10. After this praise of Atri there again follow mantras praising the qualities of Indra.

**Deities incidentally praised in the Vaiśvadeva sūktas**

Sūktas 41 to 46 of the fifth maṇḍala.

Who the Viśvadevas are, whether a single group or the whole assembly of deities that includes all the gods, will be discussed later, in the introduction preceding the 41st sūkta of the fifth maṇḍala (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5. 41). Even if one accepts the view that in the Vaiśvadeva sūktas the assembly of specified deities is something separate, even then, besides the deities of that group, other deities who are praised incidentally are also included in those sūktas. On the question who these incidental deities are, there is a whole section in the Bṛhaddevatā. This subject will be explained in detail later. At present it will be stated only who the deities are that are praised incidentally. Beginning with सप्तर्षयो वसवश्चापि देवाः (*saptarṣayo vasavaścāpi devāḥ*) (Bṛ. De. 8-125) and so on, the Bṛhaddevatā names these incidental deities and concludes with निपातिनो वैश्वदेवेषु सर्वॆ (*nipātino vaiśvadeveṣu sarvè*) (8-128). Who are they?

### Printed p. 248

The seven seers, the Vasus, the divine Atharvans**NOTE**, the Bhṛgus, Soma, Sūra, Pathyāsvasti, Heaven and Earth, Kuhū, Gungū, Aditi, Dhenu, Aghnyā, Asunīti, Iḷā, Āstaru, Vidhātṛ, Anumati, the assembled Aṅgirases, Vaiśvānara, Suparṇa, Vivasvat, Prajāpati, Dyau, Sudhasvana, Nagohya, Apāṃ Napāt, Aramyan, Vātajūti, Iḷaspati, Rathaspati, the Ṛbhus, Parjanya, the mountains, Gnā, Dakṣa, Bhaga, the wives of the gods, the deities of the directions, the Ādityas, the Rudras, the ancestors and the Sādhyas (Bṛ. De. 8-125 to 128).

If all the deities in this assembly are incidental deities, it also becomes laborious to settle who the constant deities are. Deities such as Agni, Soma and Bṛhaspati are regularly praised in the Vaiśvadeva sūktas. In indicating the deities included in this section, that is, in sūktas 41 to 46, the Bṛhaddevatā has named only some deities. It is therefore a question whether all the deities specified there can be taken as the incidental deities of these sūktas. Secondly, Yāska and others have shown a diversity of opinion also on which deity exactly is praised in some mantras. How is that?

प्र सुष्टुतिः स्तनयंतं रुवंतमिळस्पतिं जरितर्नूनमश्याः । यो अब्बिमा उदनिमा इयर्ति प्र विद्युता रोदसी उक्षमाणः ॥ (*pra suṣṭutiḥ stanayaṃtaṃ ruvaṃtamiḷaspatiṃ jaritarnūnamaśyāḥ | yo abbimā udanimā iyarti pra vidyutā rodasī ukṣamāṇaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-42-1)

In this mantra there is praise of Iḷaspati. There is no exact opinion at all about who this Iḷaspati is. Sāyaṇa has explained it as इळः अन्यस्य उदकस्य ना पतिं स्वामिनु (*iḷaḥ anyasya udakasya nā patiṃ svāminu*) (Parjanya), the lord of food or of water, all**NOTE**. This is one opinion. The opinion**NOTE** is stated in the Bṛhaddevatā in this way:

तमु ष्टुहीति रौद्री तु प्र सुष्टुतिरिति त्वृचि । शौनकादिभिराचार्यैर्देवता बहुधेरिता । इळस्पतिं शाकपूणिः पर्जन्याग्नी तु गालवः ॥ यास्कस्तु पूषणं मेने स्तुतमिंद्रं तु शौनकः । वैश्वानरं भागुरिस्तु मारुत्येष समाश्विना । (*tamu ṣṭuhīti raudrī tu pra suṣṭutiriti tvṛci | śaunakādibhirācāryairdevatā bahudheritā | iḷaspatiṃ śākapūṇiḥ parjanyāgnī tu gālavaḥ ‖ yāskastu pūṣaṇaṃ mene stutamiṃdraṃ tu śaunakaḥ | vaiśvānaraṃ bhāguristu mārutyeṣa samāśvinā |*) (Bṛ. De. 5-38 to 40)

In the mantra quoted above, Śaunaka and others have shown various kinds of opinion about who the specified deity is. Śākapūṇi called it Iḷaspati. Gālava said Parjanya and Agni**NOTE**. Yāska said Pūṣan. Śaunaka held that it is Indra. Bhāguri said Vaiśvānara. In this way there is a diversity of opinion. Similarly,

### Printed p. 249

तं प्रत्नथा पूर्वथा विश्वथेमथा ज्येष्ठतातिं बर्हिषदं स्वर्विदं । प्रतीचीनं वृजनं दोहसे गिराशुं जनयंतमनु मासु वर्धसे ॥ (*taṃ pratnathā pūrvathā viśvathemathā jyeṣṭhatātiṃ barhiṣadaṃ svarvidaṃ | pratīcīnaṃ vṛjanaṃ dohase girāśuṃ janayaṃtamanu māsu vardhase ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-44-1)

In this mantra Sāyaṇa has taken तं इंद्रं (*taṃ iṃdraṃ*) as Indra**NOTE**. But the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā have not stated definitely which deity is praised in this mantra, and have shown many alternatives.

तं प्रत्नथेति सौमी ना दैन्यैंद्री ना प्रजापतेः । परोक्षनैश्वदेवं तदाह कौषीतकिः स्वयं ॥ (*taṃ pratnatheti saumī nā dainyaiṃdrī nā prajāpateḥ | parokṣanaiśvadevaṃ tadāha kauṣītakiḥ svayaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 5-44)

In the mantra तं प्रत्यथा (*taṃ pratyathā*) the deity indicated may be included (in the group), or it may be some other particular deity, or it may be Indra. If it is none of these, Prajāpati himself may be the one indicated: thus in the first half alternative meanings are stated. In the second half, stating the opinion of the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa, the verse cites the sentence spoken by Kauṣītaki that in this mantra the Viśvedevas**NOTE** are indicated indirectly (Kau. Brā. 24-9)**NOTE**.

Thus, when there is no exact opinion even about the deity specified in many mantras, it becomes laborious to determine, in the present section (5-41 to 46), which are the constant deities that belong to the Vaiśvadeva group and which are the incidental deities**NOTE**.

## Sūkta 33 (Maṇḍala 5)

The thirty-third sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्रात्रेः पंचमे मंडले तृतीयेऽनुवाके द्वादश सूक्तानि । तत्र महि
> मह इति दशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं प्रजापतिपुत्रस्य संवरणस्यार्षं । इंद्रो देवता ।
> त्रिष्टुप् छंदः । महि दश प्राजापत्यः संवरण इत्यनुक्रांतु । विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the fifth maṇḍala, in the third anuvāka of Atri's hymns, there are twelve sūktas. Among them the first sūkta, महि मह (*mahi maha*), has ten ṛks. Its seer is Saṃvaraṇa, son of Prajāpati; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says: महि दश प्राजापत्यः संवरण (*mahi daśa prājāpatyaḥ saṃvaraṇa*). The use in ritual is laiṅgika (determined by indication).

In the third anuvāka of this fifth maṇḍala, which was seen by three seers, there are twelve sūktas. Among them the sūkta महि महे (*mahi mahe*) is the first. It has ten ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Saṃvaraṇa, son of Prajāpati; Indra is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: महि दश पाजापत्यः संवरणः (*mahi daśa pājāpatyaḥ saṃvaraṇaḥ*). The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

### Printed p. 250

Sūkta 33.

Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 33.

Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 2, Varga 1, 2.

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10.

Seer: Saṃvaraṇa Prājāpatya.

Deity: Indra.

Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> महि॑ म॒हे त॒वसे॑ दीध्ये॒ न्यनिंद्रा॑ये॒त्था त॒वसे॒ अत॑व्यान् ।  
> यो अ॑स्मै सुम॒तिं वाज॑सातौ स्तु॒तो जने॑ सम॒र्य॑श्चि॒केत॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महि । महे । तवसे । दीध्ये । न्यून् । इंद्राय । इत्था । तवसे । अतव्यान् ।  
> यः । अस्मै । सुमतिं । वाजसात् । स्तुतः । जने । समर्यः । चिकेत ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं संवरणोऽतव्यानत्यंतमिव दुर्बलः सन् महि महत् प्रभूतं
> स्तोत्रं महे महते तवसे बलवत इंद्रायेत्थेत्थं वक्ष्यमाणप्रकारेण दीध्ये ।
> दीपयामि । प्रकाशयामि ! किमर्थं । नृन् ॥ षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया ॥ मनुष्याणामस्मदीयानां तवसे बलाय । यद्वा । ननस्मद्विरोधिनामभिभवायेति शेषः ।
> तदर्थं तवसेऽस्मद्बलाय । यं इंद्रोऽस्मै जने जनाय संवरणाय वाजसात्
> संग्रामे वाजस्यान्नस्य वा लाभे निमित्ते सति स्तुतः सन् सुमतिं समर्यो मर्त्यैः
> स्तोतृभिः सहितो यद्वा सह म्रियमाणैर्युध्यमानैर्मरुदादिभिरथवा समरा
> र्हश्चिकेत जानाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Saṃvaraṇa, being exceedingly weak (अतव्यान् (*atavyān*) means "as it were extremely feeble"), recite (दीध्ये (*dīdhye*) means "I kindle, I make shine") in the manner to be stated an abundant praise (महि (*mahi*)) to Indra, the great and mighty one (महे (*mahe*), तवसे (*tavase*)). For what purpose? नृन् (*nṛn*) stands in the accusative in the sense of the genitive: for the strength of our men; or else, the ellipsis being supplied, for the overcoming of those who oppose us: for that purpose, for our strength. That Indra, when praised on the occasion of winning a battle or winning food (वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)), knows (चिकेत (*ciketa*)) favourable intent toward this person (अस्मै जने (*asmai jane*)), Saṃvaraṇa. समर्यः (*samaryaḥ*) means accompanied by mortal praisers; or accompanied by the Maruts and others who fight and die in the battle; or else, worthy of the battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अतव्यान् (*atavyān*)—I, who am extremely weak
- महे (*mahe*)—who is of great form
- तवसे (*tavase*)—and mighty
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—addressed to Indra
- न्यन् (*nyan*)—to men
- तवसे (*tavase*)—for giving strength
- इत्या (*ityā*)—in this manner
- महि (*mahi*)—the abundant praise
- दीध्ये (*dīdhye*)—I recite with brilliance

### Printed p. 251

- समरः (*samaraḥ*)—accompanied by the Maruts and others
- यः (*yaḥ*)—that same Indra who
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—in the battle fought for food
- स्तुतः (*stutaḥ*)—being praised
- अस्मै जने (*asmai jane*)—for me (named Saṃvaraṇa), on whom it is to be placed
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—the favourable mind
- चिकेत (*ciketa*)—he knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the sake of giving strength to all men, I, who am extremely weak, recite, in the manner to be stated, an abundant and brilliant praise addressed to Indra, who is of great form and mighty. Indra, accompanied by the Maruts and others, being praised in the battle fought for food, knows the favourable mind that is to be placed in me, who am named Saṃvaraṇa.

##### English translation
Feeble as I am, I offer praise to the great and vigorous Indra, for this purpose, (that he may grant) strength to (our) people : he who, associated with the Maruts, shews favour to this person when praised for the sake of sustenance.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स त्वं न॑ इंद्र धियसा॒नो अ॒र्कैर्हरी॑णां वृष॒न्योक्र॑मश्रेः ।  
> या इ॒त्था म॑घव॒न्ननु॒ जोषं॒ वक्षो॑ अ॒भि प्राय्यः स॑क्षि॒  ॑
> जनान् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । त्वं । नः । इंद्र । धियसानः । अर्कैः । हरीणां । वृषन् । योक्रं । अश्रेः ।  
> याः । इत्था । मघवन् । अनु । जोषं । वक्षः । अभि । प्र । अर्यः । सक्षि । जनान् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृषन् वर्षकेंद्र स प्रसिद्धस्त्वं नोऽस्मानियसानो ध्यायन् अर्कैरर्चनसाधनैः स्तोत्रैर्निमित्तभूतैर्हरीणां रथे नियोज्यानामश्वानां योक्रं

### Printed p. 252

> नियोजनरज्जुमश्रेः । आश्रयसि । याः ॥ लिंगव्यत्ययः ॥ यानर्कान् हे मघवन्
> इत्थेष्ठं जोषं प्रीतिमनु वक्षोऽवहः तैर्निमित्तैर्योक्रमश्रेरिति । तथा कृत्वार्योऽस्मदरीन् जनानभि अभिमुख्येन प्र प्रकृष्टं सक्षि । पराभव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, showerer, you, the famous one, thinking of us (ध्यायन् (*dhyāyan*)) by means of praises (अर्कै (*arkai*), the instruments of worship) as the cause, fasten (अश्रेः (*aśreḥ*) means "you resort to") the traces (योक्रं (*yokraṃ*), the yoking rope) of the horses (हरीणां (*harīṇāṃ*)) that are to be harnessed to the chariot. याः (*yāḥ*) is a change of gender: O Maghavan, with the praises with which you bring the desired delight (जोषं (*joṣaṃ*), love), for those reasons you fasten the traces. Having done so, overpower strongly, in front, the people who are our enemies (अर्यः (*aryaḥ*), जनान् (*janān*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy one
- वृषवन् (*vṛṣavan*)—O showerer of desires
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सः (*saḥ*)—the famous one
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- याः (*yāḥ*)—in which of our praises
- इत्या (*ityā*)—in this manner
- जोषं (*joṣaṃ*)—love
- अनु वक्षः (*anu vakṣaḥ*)—you have (such)
- अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)—being satisfied by our praises
- नः (*naḥ*)—us alone
- धियसानः (*dhiyasānaḥ*)—thinking (with a mind of favour)
- हरीणां (*harīṇāṃ*)—of the horses
- योक्रं (*yokraṃ*)—the bridle
- अश्रेः (*aśreḥ*)—you take hold of
- अरैः (*araiḥ*)—(for us) the hostile
- जनान् (*janān*)—people
- अभि (*abhi*)—all around
- प्र सक्षि (*pra sakṣi*)—overcome

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, showerer of desires, you, famous in the world, take great delight in our praises and, satisfied by them, thinking of us alone with a mind of favour, make your horses ready to come to us and take hold of their bridle. Overcome completely the people who are hostile to us.

##### English translation
You, Indra, medit ting upon us, fasten the traces of yours horses, (incited), showerer (of benefits), by those praises in which you take suitable delight, and therefore overcome (for us) hostile men.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न ते त॑ इंद्रा॒भ्य१॒ं॑स्मदृ॒ष्टायु॑क्तासो अब्र॒ह्मता॒ यदस॑न् ।  
> तिष्ठा॒ रथ॒मधि॒ तं व॑ज्रह॒स्ता र॒श्मिं दे॑व यमसे॒ स्वश्वः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । ते। ते । इंद्र । अभि । अस्मत् । ऋष्ट । अयुक्तासः । अब्रह्मता । यत् । असन् !  
> तिष्ठ । रथं । अधि । तं । वज्रहस्त । आ । रश्मिं । देव । यमसे । सुअश्वः ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 253

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋष्ट महन्निंद्र यत् येऽस्थदस्तत्तस्त्वद्भक्तेभ्योऽन्येऽयुक्तासस्त्वयासंयुक्ता आसन् आसन् अभवन् अब्रह्मता । ब्रह्म परिवृढं कर्म ! तद्रहितत्वात् ते
> नरास्ते त्वदीया न भवंति । अतोऽस्थद्यज्ञमभ्यागंतुं तं प्रसिद्धं रथमधि तिष्ठ ।
> हे वज्रहस्तेंद्र देव स्वश्वस्त्वं युं रथमारोढुं रश्मिं प्रग्रहमा यमसे नियमयिसि तमधि तिष्ठ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O mighty Indra, those others, different from your devotees, who are not joined with you are without *brahma* (अब्रह्मता (*abrahmatā*)). *Brahma* is the encompassing rite; being devoid of it, those men are not yours. Therefore, in order to come to our sacrifice, ascend that well-known chariot. O thunderbolt-handed Indra, divine one, well-horsed as you are, ascend the chariot whose rein you hold in check, in order to mount it.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋष्ट (*ṛṣṭa*)—O one of mighty form
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—those who are different from us
- आयुक्ता सः (*āyuktā saḥ*)—and have no devotion to you
- यत् असन् (*yat asan*)—whoever they are
- अब्रह्मणा (*abrahmaṇā*)—because they do not follow the Vedic path
- ते (*te*)—belonging to you
- न (*na*)—they do not become (therefore)
- वज्रहस्त (*vajrahasta*)—holder of the thunderbolt
- देव (*deva*)—divine Indra
- स्वश्वः (*svaśvaḥ*)—provided with excellent horses
- रश्मिं (*raśmiṃ*)—(of whichever chariot) the rein
- आ यमसेकैयल्लि (*ā yamasekaiyalli*)—you hold in your hand
- तं रथं (*taṃ rathaṃ*)—that same chariot
- अभि (*abhi*)—in order to come (to our sacrifice)
- अधि तिष्ठ (*adhi tiṣṭha*)—ascend and be seated

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra of mighty form, those who are different from us and have no devotion to you, whoever they are, do not belong to you, because they do not follow the Vedic path. Therefore, O Indra, holder of the thunderbolt and divine one, ascend that same chariot, to which you have yoked excellent horses and whose rein you hold in your hand, in order to come to our sacrifice.

##### English translation
Since, mighty Indra, those who, dffering from us, and not united with you through their lack of devotion, are not yours ; therefore, divine holder of the thunderbolt, you are possessed of excellent horses, ascend the car, whose reins you guide, (to come to our sacrifice).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒रू यत्त॑ इंद्र॒ संत्यु॒क्था गवे॑ च॒कर्थो॒र्वरा॑सु॒ युध्य॑न् ।  
> त॒त॒क्षे सूर्या॑य चि॒दोक॑सि॒ स्वे वृषा॑ स॒मत्सु॑ दा॒सस्य॒ नाम॑  
> चित् ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 254

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुरु । यत् । ते । इंद्र । संति । उक्ता । गवे । चकर्थ । उर्वरासु । युध्यन् ।  
> तत्तक्षे । सूर्याय । चित् । ओकसि । स्वे । वृषा । समत्सु । दासस्य । नाम । चित् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव यद्यदा स्वभूतानि पुरु पुरूणि बहून्युक्कोक्कानि शस्त्राणि
> संति तदोर्वरासु सस्योपेतासु भूमिषु निमित्तभूतासु गवे वृष्टुदकाय
> युध्यन् जलप्रतिबंधकान् संहरन् चकर्थ । करोषि भेदनं । कुत्रेति । सूर्याय
> सूर्यस्य स्वे स्वकीय ओकसि स्थाने । वृषा वर्षिता सन् ततक्षे । संपादयसि ।
> समत्सु संग्रामेषु दासस्य वृष्टि प्रतिबंधकर्तुरेतन्नामकस्यासुरस्य नाम चिन्नामापि ततक्षे । नाशयसीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, when your own many (पुरु (*puru*)) praises and recitations, that is, *śastras*, exist, then, fighting for the sake of rain-water (गवे (*gave*)) on fertile lands as the occasion, destroying those who obstruct the waters, you bring about the cleaving open (of the clouds). Where? In the sun's own dwelling-place, the place that is his own. Being the showerer, you accomplish it. In battles you destroy even the name of the Asura called Dāsa, the obstructor of rain; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- पुरू (*purū*)—very numerous
- उक्ता (*uktā*)—all the praises that take the form of *śastras*
- ते (*te*)—addressed to you alone
- संति (*saṃti*)—have become (for that reason)
- उर्वरासु (*urvarāsu*)—upon the earth full of plants
- गवे (*gave*)—in order to pour down rain
- युध्यन् (*yudhyan*)—fighting (with the enemies who obstruct the rain)
- चकर्थ (*cakartha*)—you have brought about (their destruction)
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you, the one who pours down rain
- समत्सु (*samatsu*)—when battle comes
- सूराय (*sūrāya*)—of the sun
- स्वी ओकसिचित् (*svī okasicit*)—in his own home (in the atmosphere itself)
- दासस्य (*dāsasya*)—of the Asura
- नामचित् (*nāmacit*)—the very name
- ततक्षे (*tatakṣe*)—you have destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, praises in the form of *śastras* have been composed in very great numbers and offered to you. All of them are addressed to you alone. For that reason, in order to pour down rain upon the earth full of plants, you have fought with the enemies who obstruct the rain and brought about their destruction. You, the sprinkler of rain, when battle came, destroyed the very name of the Asura in the atmosphere itself, which is the sun's own heaven.

##### English translation
Inasmuch, Indra, as many praises are yours, therefore, combating for the sake of (shedding) waters on fertile (lands), you have effected , the discomfiture of its obstructors); you, who are the showerer (of benefits , have on behalf of the sun, destroyed in his own dwelling, the very name of , the Asura, Dasa, in battle.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व॒यं ते त॑ इंद्र॒ ये च॒ नरः॒ शर्धो॑ जज्ञा॒ना या॒ताश्च॒  ॑
> रथाः ।  
> आस्माज्ज॑गम्यादहिशुष्म॒ सत्वा॒ भगो॒ न हव्यः॑ प्रभृ॒थेषु॒ चारुः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वयं । ते । ते । इंद्र । ये । च । नरः । शर्धः । जज्ञानाः । याताः । च । रथाः ।  
> आ । अस्मान् । जगम्यात् । अहिशुष्म । सत्वा । भगः । न । हव्यः । प्रभृथेषु । चारुः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ये च नरः कर्मणां नेतार ऋत्विग्यजमाना वयं स्मः ते वयं
> ते त्वदीयाः । किदृशा वयं । शर्धो बलं जज्ञाना उत्पादयंतः स्तुतिभिर्याताश्च होतुं त्वां प्राप्ताश्च रथा रंहणशीलाश्च । किंच हे अहिशुष्म । अहिरयनात् ।
> सर्वतो व्याप्तबलेंद्र त्वदनुग्रहाद्दव्यः स्तुत्यः प्रतिभटैराह्वातव्यो ना चारुः
> संगंता सत्वा भृत्यादिः प्रभृथेषु संग्रामेषु यज्ञेषु वास्माना जगम्यात् ।
> अगच्छेत् । भगो न भग इव हव्यश्चारुः । भगदेवो यथास्मत्सहाय आगच्छति तथा
> भृत्यादिरागच्छेदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, we who are the leaders of rites, the priests and the sacrificers, are yours. What are we like? We produce strength (शर्धो (*śardho*) means *bala*) by our praises, we have come to you in order to offer the oblation, and we are swift. Further, O Ahiśuṣma, Indra of all-pervading strength, by your favour let a follower, an attendant and the like (सत्वा (*satvā*)), who is praiseworthy, to be called upon by those who face the adversaries, and agreeable, a companion, come to us in the battles or in the sacrifices (प्रभृथेषु (*prabhṛtheṣu*)). Like Bhaga: as the god Bhaga comes as our helper, so may the attendant and the rest come; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—O Indra
- शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)—(your) strength
- जज्ञानाः (*jajñānāḥ*)—those who increase it (by our praises)
- याताश्च (*yātāśca*)—those who approach you
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—those who move swiftly to gain your presence
- ये वयं (*ye vayaṃ*)—we who
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—are the leaders of all rites
- ते (*te*)—such as we are
- ते (*te*)—are yours alone
- अहिशुष्म (*ahiśuṣma*)—O Indra, drier up of enemies
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—one of praiseworthy valour
- चारुः (*cāruḥ*)—and trusted
- सत्वा (*satvā*)—follower
- प्रभृथेषु (*prabhṛtheṣu*)—in battles
- भगो न (*bhago na*)—like Bhaga, as a helper
- आस्मान् (*āsmān*)—to our side
- आ जगम्यात् (*ā jagamyāt*)—may he come and join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we who increase your strength by our praises, who approach you alone, who strive only for the joy of your presence, and who are the leaders of all rites, such as we are, are indeed yours.

### Printed p. 256

O Indra, drier up of enemies, may a follower of praiseworthy valour and trusted, like Bhaga as a helper, come to our help in battles.

##### English translation
We, Indra, are yours, and yours are they who are the leaders ( of rites), promoters of (your), strength, and willing applicants (to you) : all-powerful Indra, may adherents worthy of commendation, and faithful, come to us, like Bhaga, in battles.

> दानं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पपृक्षेण्यं संपर्कार्हं पूज्यं वौजो बलं त्वे हि त्वयि खलु ।
> त्वदधीनमित्यर्थः । नृतमानो नृत्यन् अमर्तोऽमरणधर्मा स त्वं वसवान
> आच्छादयन् स्वतेजसा जगत् नृम्मानि नृमणानि द्रविणानि । वक्षमाणरय्यपेक्षया
> चशब्दः । एनीमेनवर्णां श्वेतवर्णां रयिं धनं दाः । देहि । अहं च अर्य
> ईश्वरस्य तुविमघस्य प्रभूतधनस्य च दानं प्र स्तुषे । सौमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, your strength (वौजो (*vaujo*)) is worthy of association and to be revered; it rests in you, that is, it depends on you. You, dancing, immortal, subject to no death, covering the world with your own splendour, give wealth (नृम्मानि (*nṛmmāni*) means riches); the word *ca* has regard to the wealth that is to be mentioned. Give the wealth that is tawny, that is, white in colour. And I praise the gift of the lord, the possessor of abundant wealth; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वे हि (*tve hi*)—residing in you

- पपृक्षेण्यं (*papṛkṣeṇyaṃ*)—is exceedingly praiseworthy and radiant
- नृतमानः (*nṛtamānaḥ*)—full of joy
- अमर्तः (*amartaḥ*)—free from the nature of death
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- वसवानः (*vasavānaḥ*)—covering the whole world with your splendour
- नृम्मानि (*nṛmmāni*)—riches
- एनीं (*enīṃ*)—shining
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give (I also)
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—the lord
- तुविमघस्य (*tuvimaghasya*)—of you who possess abundant wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the strength that resides in you is exceedingly praiseworthy and radiant. You, who are full of joy and free from the nature of death, covering the whole world with your splendour, give us riches and shining wealth. I also praise the gift of you who are the lord and possess abundant wealth.

##### English translation
Glorious, Indra, is your strength, exulting, immortal, and clothing (the world with light) : give us riches, and brilliant wealth, and I will greatly praise the munificence of the opulent lord.

> ददतः प्रयच्छतः सुषुतस्य सुष्त्वभिषुतस्य चारोर्मनोहरस्य मध्वः सोमस्य

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O heroic Indra, in this very way protect us, who praise you, the performers of rites and priests, with your protections. And further, in battle (वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)) take the covering form that envelops. Satisfy yourself, give delight to yourself, with the sweet Soma, well pressed and charming. The genitive here stands for the accusative: the meaning is "drink the Soma of the kind described". Or else the genitive stands for the instrumental: delight yourself with the drinking of the Soma of the kind described.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- एव (*eva*)—in one and the same way
- गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)—who praise you
- कारून् (*kārūn*)—and perform rites (or praises)
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—with your protections
- अव पाहि (*ava pāhi*)—protect
- उत (*uta*)—and
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—in battle
- त्वचं (*tvacaṃ*)—the form
- ददतः (*dadataḥ*)—that produces (for you a form that is a covering)
- सुषुतस्य (*suṣutasya*)—that is pressed out excellently
- चारोः (*cāroḥ*)—and charming
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of Soma (by drinking)
- पिप्रीहि (*piprīhi*)—become satisfied

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, protect us, who praise you in one and the same way and who carry out the rites, with your protections. And in battle become satisfied by drinking the Soma, which produces for you a covering form, which is excellently pressed out and charming.

##### English translation
Hero, Indra, with your protection defend us, praising and worshipping (you', and be propitiated (by drinking) of the well-effused and agree able Soma juice that yields 'a defensive) covering in combat.

> नु क्षिप्रं सष्टे । गच्छेयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: "Trasadasyu, Vidadha and Dhvanya, these three kings gave horses, wealth and cows to the seer; so the seer says." Further, त्ये (*tye*) means "those", and मा (*mā*) is the accusative in the sense of the dative: to me. रराणाः (*rarāṇāḥ*) means given. May the ten white, bright-coloured horses of this Trasadasyu, the royal seer sprung from the line of Girikṣita, son of Purukutsa, the impeller, possessed of gold, carry me, bring me (to the sacrifice). And with rites, that is, with the harnessing of the chariot and the like, or with sacrifices and the like, may I go quickly; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- मा (*mā*)—to me
- रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*)—given
- गैरिक्षितस्य (*gairikṣitasya*)—sprung from the lineage of Girikṣita
- पौरुकुत्सस्य (*paurukutsasya*)—son of Purukutsa
- सूरेः (*sūreḥ*)—composer of praises
- हिरणिनः (*hiraṇinaḥ*)—and wealthy
- अस्य त्रसदस्कोः (*asya trasadaskoḥ*)—belonging to this Trasadasyu
- श्येतासः (*śyetāsaḥ*)—of white colour
- त्ये दश (*tye daśa*)—these ten horses
- मा (*mā*)—me
- वहंतु (*vahaṃtu*)—may they carry (to the place of sacrifice)
- क्रतुभिः (*kratubhiḥ*)—with the rites
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- सश्चे (*saśce*)—may they bring me together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May these ten horses of white colour, belonging to Trasadasyu, sprung from the lineage of Girikṣita, son of Purukutsa, composer of praises and wealthy, carry me to the place of sacrifice. And may they bring us quickly together with the rites.

##### English translation
May those ten bright horses, the gift to me of the pious gold-possessing Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, of the race of Girikshita, convey me (to the sacrifice), and may I proceed quickly with the rites

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सहस्रा । मे । च्यवतानः । ददानः । आनूकं । अर्यः । वपुषे । न । आर्चत् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च तै श्वा वक्ष्यमाणा मारुताश्वस्य । मरुत्सदृशवेगाश्ववान्मरुताश्वः । तदपत्यस्य विदथस्यॆतन्नामकस्य राज्ञः शोणाः शोणवर्णाः क्रत्वामघासः
> क्रतुना कर्मणा शीघ्रगमनादिलक्षणेन माहनीया अश्वा रात् दाने विनियुक्ता
> मां वहंतीति शेषः । किंच सहस्रा सहस्राण्यपरिमितानि धनान्यर्यः पूज्यस्य मे ।
> चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी । पूज्याय मह्यं च्यवतानश्चावयन् ददानः प्रयच्छन् स
> आनूकमाभरणं च वपुषे स्वशरीरालंकारायार्चत् । प्रायच्छत् । नेति चार्थे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: And those (horses) to be mentioned: the horses of Vidatha, the king so named, son of Mārutāśva, one whose horses have a speed like that of the Maruts; tawny-coloured (शोणाः (*śoṇāḥ*)), made worthy of honour by a rite (क्रतुना (*kratunā*)) marked by swift going and the like, assigned at the gift, carry me; "carry me" is the remainder to be supplied. Further, the king gave countless thousands of riches to me, the venerable one (the genitive stands for the dative), causing them to fall to me as a gift; and he gave ornament for the adornment of my own body. The word *na* is in the sense of "and".**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- मारुताश्वस्य (*mārutāśvasya*)—of the son of Marutāśva
- विदथस्य (*vidathasya*)—belonging to the king named Vidatha
- शोणाः (*śoṇāḥ*)—golden-coloured
- क्रत्वामघासः (*kratvāmaghāsaḥ*)—those that have gained greatness through rites
- रात् (*rāt*)—(given to me) at the time of the gift
- तै (*tai*)—those horses
- मा (*mā*)—me (may they carry to the sacrifice) (and that same king)
- सहस्रा (*sahasrā*)—countless riches
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—venerable
- मे (*me*)—to me
- च्यवता (*cyavatā*)—wishing to give
- ददानः (*dadānaḥ*)—giving (together with them)
- वपुषे (*vapuṣe*)—for the adornment of the body
- आनुकं (*ānukaṃ*)—and ornament
- अर्चत् (*arcat*)—gave

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the horses given to me at the time of the gift by the king named Vidatha, son of Mārutāśva, golden-coloured and having gained greatness through rites, carry me to the sacrifice. The same king, in his affection for me, who am worthy of his respect, gave me countless riches and presented ornaments for the adornment of my body.

##### English translation
Or may those bay, well-actioned horses, the donation of Vidatha, the son of Marutashwa, (convey me) : or (may) the thousands (of treasure) which he was bestowing upon and giving to me, entitled to respect, and the ornaments which he presented (to decorate) the person, (contribute to the ceremony).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च तै ते वक्ष्यमाणा रायो ध्वन्यस्य ध्वन्यनामकस्य लक्षण्यस्य
> लक्ष्मणपुत्रस्य राज्ञः संबंधिनोऽश्वा मा जुष्टा मां प्राप्ताः सुरुचः शोभनदीप्तयो यताना वहमानाय यतमानाः । रायो मह्ना महत्वेन युक्ता
> रायः प्रयता दत्ताः सत्यः संवरणस्य ऋषेरपि ग्मन् । अपिगताः । प्राप्ता मद्गृहमिति शेषः । व्रजं न गावो गोष्ठं गाव इव । यद्वा । नेति चार्थे । गावश्च मम
> व्रजमपिग्मन् । अत्रैंद्रे सूक्ते प्रायेणैंद्रे मरुतो राजां च दानस्तुतॆयः ।
> अनु- २-२२ । इत्युक्तत्वाद्राज्ञां दानस्तुतिरविरुद्धा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: And those (horses) to be mentioned, belonging to the king Dhvanya, son of Lakṣmaṇa, have come to me, shining beautifully, striving to carry me. The riches endowed with greatness, given, have reached the house of the seer Saṃvaraṇa; "reached my house" is the remainder to be supplied. They are like cows going to a stall. Or else *na* is in the sense of "and": and cows also have reached my stall. In this Aindra sūkta, since it is said, "for the most part in Aindra (hymns) there are praises of gifts by the Maruts and by kings" (Anu. 2-22), a praise of the gifts of kings is not contradictory.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—or
- लक्ष्मण्यस्य (*lakṣmaṇyasya*)—of the son of Lakṣmaṇa
- ध्वन्यस्य (*dhvanyasya*)—named Dhvanya, the king who gave
- जुष्टाः (*juṣṭāḥ*)—those that have joined me
- सुरुचः (*surucaḥ*)—of resplendent brilliance
- यतानाः (*yatānāḥ*)—eager to carry me away
- त्ये (*tye*)—those horses
- मा (*mā*)—me (may they carry to the sacrifice) (and)
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—cows
- व्रजं न (*vrajaṃ na*)—as they hasten to and reach the stall
- प्रयताः (*prayatāḥ*)—given to me
- मह्वा (*mahvā*)—filled with greatness
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—riches
- संवरणस्य ऋषेः (*saṃvaraṇasya ṛṣeḥ*)—to the house of the seer named Saṃvaraṇa
- अपि ग्मन् (*api gman*)—may they go and reach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the horses given by the king named Dhvanya, son of Lakṣmaṇa, that have come into my possession, are radiant and are eager to carry me to the sacrifice, carry me to the sacrifice. As cows hasten to and reach their stalls, may the riches given to me, filled with greatness, go and reach the

### Printed p. 262

house of the seer named Saṃvaraṇa (my house).

##### English translation
Or may the bright and active steeds bestowed upon me by Dhwanya, the son of Lakshmana (bear me) : the riches, endowed with greatness, that have been presented, have passed ( to the dwelling) of the Rishi Samvarana, like cows to their stalls.

## Sūkta 34 (Maṇḍala 5)

The thirty-fourth sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अजातशत्रुमिति नवर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं प्राजापत्यस्य संवरणस्यार्षमैंद्रं ।
> नवमी त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुंबतपरिभाषया जगत्यः । अजातशत्रुं नव त्रिष्टुबंतमित्यनुक्रमणिका । विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: The second sūkta, अजातशत्रुमिति (*ajātaśatrumiti*), of nine ṛks, belongs to the seer Saṃvaraṇa Prājāpatya; its deity is Indra. The ninth ṛk is in Triṣṭubh; the rest are Jagatī by the convention on a sūkta that ends in Triṣṭubh.**NOTE** The Anukramaṇikā says: अजातशत्रुं नव (*ajātaśatruṃ nava*) (the sūkta is called nine ṛks ending in Triṣṭubh). The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Translation of the Anuvāda: This sūkta, Ajātaśatrum, is the second sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are nine ṛks in it. The seer of this sūkta is Saṃvaraṇa, son of Prajāpati; Indra is the deity; the ninth ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre and the remaining ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "Ajātaśatruṃ nava triṣṭubantam". The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Sūkta 31.**NOTE**

Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 34.

Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 2, Varga 3, 4.

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9.

Seer: Saṃvaraṇa Prājāpatya.

Deity: Indra.

Metre: 1-8, Jagatī, Triṣṭubh.

### Printed p. 263

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अजा॑तशत्रुम॒जरा॒ स्व॑र्व॒त्यनु॑ स्व॒धामि॑ता द॒स्ममी॑यते ।  
> सु॒नोत॑न॒ पच॑त॒ ब्रह्म॑वाहसे पुरुष्टु॒ताय॑ प्रत॒रं द॑धातन ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अजातशत्रुं । अजरा । स्वःवती । अनु । स्वधा । अमिता । दस्मं । ईयते ।  
> सुनोतन । पचत । ब्रह्मवाहसे । पुरुस्तुताय । प्रतरं । दधातन ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अजातशत्रुं । अनुत्पन्नाः शातयितारो यस्य तं । दस्मं शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितारमजराक्षिणा स्वर्वती स्वरणवत्यमितापरिमिता स्वधान्नं हविरन्वियते । अनुप्राप्नोति । तदर्थं हे ऋत्विजः सुनोतन । अभिषुणुत । पचत पुरोडाशादिकं ।
> कस्मै । ब्रह्मवाहसे ब्रह्मणः परिवृढस्य स्तोत्रस्य वाहकाय पुरुष्टुताय बहुभिः
> स्तु तायेंद्राय । प्रतरं प्रकृष्टतरं दधातन । धारयत स्वस्वोचितकर्म ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: *Ajātaśatru* is he whose destroyers are not born. *Dasma* is the one who casts down enemies. Food as oblation (स्वधान्नं (*svadhānnaṃ*)), undecaying, leading to heaven and unlimited, follows him, that is, reaches him. For that purpose, O priests, press out the Soma and cook the cakes and the rest. For whom? For Indra, the bearer of *brahma*, the all-encompassing praise, praised by many. Set in place your respective duties in the best manner.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अजरा (*ajarā*)—undecaying
- स्वर्वती (*svarvatī*)—leading to heaven
- अमिता (*amitā*)—and unlimited
- स्वधा (*svadhā*)—food in the form of oblation
- अजातशत्रुं (*ajātaśatruṃ*)—the one who has no enemy at all
- दस्मं (*dasmaṃ*)—and destroyer of enemies, the god
- अनु ईयते (*anu īyate*)—goes and reaches (O priests)
- सुनोतन (*sunotana*)—press out the Soma juice
- पचत (*pacata*)—cook the cakes and the rest
- ब्रह्मवाहसे (*brahmavāhase*)—who receives and bears the most excellent praises
- पुरुष्टुताय (*puruṣṭutāya*)—and is praised by many, to Indra
- प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)—in the most excellent manner
- दधातन (*dadhātana*)—perform (your respective) rites

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The food in the form of oblation, undecaying and unlimited, goes and reaches the god who has no enemy and destroys enemies. O priests, press out the Soma juice. Cook the cakes and the rest. Perform your respective rites in the most excellent manner, addressing Indra, who receives and bears the most excellent praises and is praised by many.

### Printed p. 264

##### English translation
The undecaying, heaven-conferring, unlimited (sacrificial) food, goes to the tamer (of enemies), whose adversaries are unborn : therefore (priests), pour out (the libation), dress (the cakes and butter), diligently discharge (your offices) to him who is the accepter of prayer, who is glorified by many.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: Maghavan, who filled his own belly all round with Soma, was exhilarated, that is, satisfied, by drinking the sweet-flavoured Soma (अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)). - यमत् (*yamat*)—raised and held

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who fills his belly completely with Soma juice, was satisfied by drinking the sweet Soma juice. Immediately thereafter, desiring to kill the Asura named Mṛga, he raised and held in his hand the thunderbolt weapon, which has thousands of edges and is destructive.

##### English translation

> उच्यते । अहनि रात्रौ च सोमं सुनोति स भवति द्युमान् दीप्तिमान् ॥ अहेति
> विनिग्रहार्थियः । किंच शक्रः शक्तोऽयमिंद्रस्ततनुष्टिं । ततं धर्मसंततिं नुदति
> वष्टि कामयते कामानिति ततनुष्टिः । तं तनूशुभ्रं तनूः शुभ्रा शोभनीयालंकारादिभिर्यस्य तं । तादृशं स्वपोषकमयज्ञानमपोहति । अपरोऽपशब्दः
> पूरणार्थः । मघवा धनवान्यश्च कवासखः कुत्सितपुरुषसहायस्तमपोहतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: The sacrificer who, for this Indra, in the *phraṃsa*, which is a name for the day (the juices are taken in it), or else the one who, in the *ūdhan*, the night: what is more swollen and raised is called *ūdhas*; since night is like the udder in giving moisture and sap, night too is called *ūdhas*. He who presses Soma by day and by night becomes radiant. The word *aha* is in the sense of restraint. Further, this capable Indra drives away the *tatanuṣṭi*, that is, one who thrusts aside the continuity of dharma and desires desires. He also drives away such a one, whose body is resplendent with ornaments and the like, who nourishes only himself and does not perform sacrifice; the second *apa* is for completion. And he drives away the wealthy man who is the friend of base men.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—addressing Indra
- फ्रंसे (*phraṃse*)—by day
- उत वा (*uta vā*)—or
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whoever
- ऊधनि (*ūdhani*)—also in the night
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice (to offer it)
- सुनोति (*sunoti*)—presses (he)
- द्युमान् (*dyumān*)—radiant
- भवति (*bhavati*)—becomes
- शक्रः (*śakraḥ*)—Indra
- ततनुष्टिं (*tatanuṣṭiṃ*)—one who, without devotion to god, is proud only of his offspring
- तनूशुभ्रं (*tanūśubhraṃ*)—and proud only of his own body, one fallen from rites
- अप ऊहति (*apa ūhati*)—rejects
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whoever
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—though wealthy
- कवासखः (*kavāsakhaḥ*)—is a friend of wicked people (he rejects him too)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those sacrificers who press out and offer Soma juice to Indra by day and by night become radiant. Indra rejects those who, without devotion to god, nurse an unworthy pride in their offspring alone and in their own bodies alone, and those who, though wealthy, are friends of wicked people.

##### English translation
He who pours out the libation to that Indra, by day or by night, undoubtedly becomes illustrious : Shakra disregards the man who is proud of his descendants and vain of his person, and who, though wealthy, is the friend of the base.
