> वस्वः । आकरः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शक्रो शक्तोऽयं यस्यायज्वनः पितरमवधीत् हतवान् । यस्य च
> मातरमवधीत् । यस्य च भ्रातरं अतोऽस्मादयज्जनः सकाशान्नेषते । न बिभेति
> न गच्छति वा । किंत्वस्य प्रयता दत्तानि हवींषि वेतीदु । कामयत एव । अयज्ञानं
> शिक्षयित्वा नियोजयतीत्यर्थः । यतंकरो यमनकर्ता वस्वो वसुनो धनस्याकर
> आभिमुख्यकर्ता यः किल्बिषात्पित्रादिवधयुक्तान्नेषते न चलति न बिभेति वा । इंद्रस्यास्तोत्थणां हतरिंद्रो यतीन् सालावृकेभ्यः प्रायच्छत् अंतरिक्षे पौलोमान्पृथिव्यां कालकांज्यानरुन्मुखान्तीन् सालावृकेभ्यः प्रायच्छमित्यादि श्रुतिषु प्रसिद्धा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: This Indra, the capable one, has slain the father of a certain non-sacrificer, and also his mother and his brother; yet he does not fear this non-sacrificer nor go away from him. Rather he desires the oblations offered by him: having instructed the non-sacrificer, he engages him in the rite; that is the meaning. *Yataṃkara* is the regulator; *ākara* of wealth is the one who brings wealth toward the sacrificer. Indra neither moves away from nor fears the sin consisting in the killing of a father and the like. Passages in the śrutis, such as "Indra gave the ascetics to the wolves; in the atmosphere the Paulomas, on the earth the Kālakāñjas", are well known.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शक्रः (*śakraḥ*)—Indra
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of whichever man
- पितरं (*pitaraṃ*)—the father
- अवधीत् (*avadhīt*)—has slain
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of whom
- मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—the mother (has slain)
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of whom
- भ्रातरं (*bhrātaraṃ*)—the brothers (has slain)
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—from all these people
- न ईषते (*na īṣate*)—he is not afraid
- अस्य (*asya*)—from such persons
- प्रयता (*prayatā*)—the oblations offered
- वेतीदु (*vetīdu*)—he surely desires and accepts
- यतंकरः (*yataṃkaraḥ*)—who teaches the rules of rites
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—of wealth
- आकरः (*ākaraḥ*)—the support, Indra
- किल्पिषात् (*kilpiṣāt*)—from the sinful deeds of those who do not follow the Veda
- न ईषते (*na īṣate*)—is not frightened

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra is not afraid of a man whose father, mother or brother he has slain for their sinful deeds. Or, if that man offers an oblation in the proper way, he accepts it without rejecting it. Indra, who teaches the rules of rites and is the support of wealth, is not frightened by the sinful deeds of those who do not follow the Veda.

##### English translation
Shakra does not turn away from him whose father, whose mother, whose brother he has slain, but is willing to accept his offerings : the regulator (of acts), the bestower of riches, does not turn away from iniquity.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । पंचभिः । दश्यभिः । वष्टि । आरभं । न । असुन्वता । सचते । पुष्यता । चन ।  
> जिनाति । वा । इत् । अमुया । हंति । वा । धुनिः । आ । देवयुं । भजति ।  
> गोमति । व्रजे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिंद्रः पंचभिर्दशभिर्वा सहायैरारभमारंभं शत्रुहननायालंबनं
> न वष्टि । साहाय्यं नापेक्षत इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । अमुमिंद्रं पंचभिर्दशभिर्वा
> यज्ञादन्यैरुषायैरारभमारब्धु मुद्योगं कर्तुं न वष्टि । न कामयते। असुन्वताभिषवमकुर्वता सह पुष्यता चन बंध्वादीनपोषयतापि न सचते। न संगच्छते।
> असुन्वंतमभिषवमकुर्वाणमयष्टारमपुष्कंतं च न प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः । न केवलमप्राप्तिमात्रं किंतु जिनाति वा । नाशब्दश्चार्थे । जिनाति च : बाधते । इदिति
> पूरणः । हंति नामुयामुमयष्टारु धुनिः कंपकः शत्रूणां । देवयुं
> देवमिंद्रं कामयमानं यजमानं गोमति व्रज आ भजति । योजयतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: This Indra does not desire (न वष्टि (*na vaṣṭi*)) to begin an undertaking, a support for slaying enemies, with five or ten helpers; he does not look for help; that is the meaning. Or else: he does not desire, does not wish, to make an effort towards that undertaking by means other than the sacrifice, five or ten. He does not associate even with one who does not press the Soma and does not nourish his dependants; that is, he does not reach one who does not press, does not sacrifice and does not nourish. Not only does he not reach him; he also overcomes him: the word *na* is in the sense of "and": he oppresses and slays that non-sacrificer. The word *it* is for filling out. *Dhuni* is the shaker of enemies. The sacrificer who desires the god Indra he joins to a stall rich in cows; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- आरभं (*ārabhaṃ*)—for an effort that restrains enemies
- पंचभिः (*paṃcabhiḥ*)—with five persons
- दशभिः (*daśabhiḥ*)—or with ten persons
- न वष्टि (*na vaṣṭi*)—he does not look for help
- असुन्वता (*asunvatā*)—with a man who does not press Soma (for the sacrifice)
- पुष्यता चन (*puṣyatā cana*)—and does not nourish his relations and the like
- न सचते (*na sacate*)—he does not associate (not only that)
- जिनाति वा (*jināti vā*)—he oppresses him
- हंति वा (*haṃti vā*)—or slays him
- अमु (*amu*)—such a one fallen from rites
- धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*)—Indra, who terrifies
- देवयुं (*devayuṃ*)—the sacrificer who longs for and worships Indra and the other gods for help
- गोमति (*gomati*)—full of cows
- वज्रे (*vajre*)—together with the stall
- आ भजति (*ā bhajati*)—he joins

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra does not look for the help of any company, whether five persons or ten, in his effort to destroy enemies. He does not associate at all with a man who does not press Soma for the sacrifice and does not nourish his relations and the like.

### Printed p. 269

Moreover, he oppresses him, or slays him. Indra, who terrifies such a man fallen from rites, provides stalls full of cows for the sacrificers who worship Indra and the other gods.

##### English translation
He desires not (association in) enterprises with five or with ten ; he associates not with the man who does not present libations ; and cherishes not ( his dependants ) : nay, the terrorier (of foes) punishes him, but he places the devout man in a pasturage stocked with cattle.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुमृतौ संग्रामे वित्वक्षणो विशेषेण तनूकर्ता शत्रूणां तदर्थं चक्रमासजो रथचक्रस्यासंजयितासुन्वतोऽयजमानस्य विषुणः पराङ्मुखः सुन्वतो
> यजमानस्य वृधो वर्धयितेंद्रो विश्वस्य दमिता शिक्षयिता विभीषणो भयजनक
> आर्यः स्वामी यथावशं यथेच्छं दासं दासकर्माणं जनं नयति स्ववशं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: Indra, who in battle especially thins out the enemies, and for that purpose sets in motion the wheel of his chariot, turns away from the sacrificer who does not press Soma, the non-sacrificer, and is the increaser of the sacrificer who presses. Indra, the tamer, that is, the instructor, of all, causing fear, the lord, leads at his will the servant, the person who does a servant's work, under his own control.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समृतौ (*samṛtau*)—in battle
- विश्वक्षणः (*viśvakṣaṇaḥ*)—who makes the strength of enemies decay
- चक्रमासजः (*cakramāsajaḥ*)—and for that purpose makes his chariot wheel run swiftly
- असुन्वतः (*asunvataḥ*)—from the man who does not press

### Printed p. 270

- विषुणः (*viṣuṇaḥ*)—who turns away
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—to the sacrificer who presses Soma for the sacrifice
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—the increaser
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of the whole world
- दमिता (*damitā*)—the instructor
- विभीषणः (*vibhīṣaṇaḥ*)—the one who causes fear
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—and lord
- यथावशं (*yathāvaśaṃ*)—as he pleases
- दासु (*dāsu*)—servants
- नयति (*nayati*)—he brings under his own control

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who makes the strength of enemies decay in battle, and for that purpose makes his chariot wheel run swiftly, who turns away from the man who does not press Soma and increases the sacrificer who presses Soma for the sacrifice, is the instructor of the whole world, the terrifier and the lord, and brings servants under his own control as he pleases.

##### English translation
Thinning (his enemies) in battle, and accelerating the wheels (of his car), he turns away from him who offers no libation, and augments (the prosperity of) the offerer : Indra, the subduer of all, the formidable, the lord, conducts the Dasa at his pleasure.

> यजमानाय वि भजति सूनरु शोभनमनुष्यं वसु धनं । अयष्टुर्धनमाकृष्य
> यष्टे प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः । न केवलं वणिग्धनप्रदानमात्रं किंतु पुरु पुरुणि दुर्गॆ
> चन दुःखेन गंतव्य आपद्यपि विश्वः सर्वोऽपि दातृजन आ द्रियते । आस्थाप्यते ।
> यो जनोऽस्येंद्रस्य तनिषीं बलमचुक्रुदत् विहिताकरणादिना तस्य पणेरजतीति
> पूर्वशेषः । यद्वा । योऽस्य तनिषीमचुक्रुदत् स सर्वोऽपि जनो दुर्गॆ
> चनाध्रियत इंद्रेण ॥ चनेत्येकपदमध्येतृसंप्रदायप्राप्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: This Indra goes, like a trader to a miser who gives nothing, to steal his wealth or food; he goes fully, and having taken it he distributes it to the sacrificer who gives oblations: fine wealth, rich in men. Having drawn away the wealth of the non-sacrificer, he gives it to the sacrificer; that is the meaning. Not only is it a giving of a trader's wealth: even in a danger hard to get through, every giving person is supported. Of the man who has angered the might of Indra by not doing what is prescribed, Indra goes to steal the wealth; this is the remainder to be supplied from before. Or else: every man who has angered his might is not supported by Indra even in a hard place. The word *cana* is a single word, received through the tradition of the reciters.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Indra
- पणेः (*paṇeḥ*)—of the miser who gives nothing
- भोजनं (*bhojanaṃ*)—the wealth of food
- मुषे (*muṣe*)—to steal
- सं अजति (*saṃ ajati*)—he strives
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblations
- सूनरं (*sūnaraṃ*)—beneficial to men
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- वि भजति (*vi bhajati*)—he provides
- यः जनः (*yaḥ janaḥ*)—whatever man
- अस्य (*asya*)—of Indra
- तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*)—the might
- अचुक्रुधत् (*acukrudhat*)—provokes by disrespect
- विश्वः (*viśvaḥ*)—all such people
- पुरु (*puru*)—very great
- दुर्गे चन (*durge cana*)—in distress
- आ ध्रियते (*ā dhriyate*)—are placed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra strives to steal the food-wealth of a miser who gives nothing. He provides wealth beneficial to men to the sacrificer who offers oblations. All people who provoke the might of Indra by disrespect have to share in very great distress.

##### English translation
He proceeds to plunder the wealth of the ( avaricious ), and bestows the riches that are prized by man upon the donor (of the libation) : every man is involved in great difficulty who provokes the might of Indra to wrath.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सं यज्जना॑ सु॒धना॑ वि॒श्वश॑र्धसा॒ववे॒दिंद्रो॑ म॒घवा॒ गोषु॑  ॒॑
> शु॒भ्रिषु॑ ।

### Printed p. 272

> युजं ह्यगन्यमकृत प्रवेपन्युदीं गव्यं सृजते सत्वभिर्धुनिः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । यत् । जनौ । सुधन् । विश्वशर्धसौ । अनेत् । इंद्रः । मघवा । गोषु ।  
> शुभ्रिषु ।  
> युजं । हि । अन्यं । अकृत । प्रवेपनी । उत् । ईं । गव्यं । सृजते । सत्वभिः ।  
> धुनिः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समवेत्संजानाति यद्यदा जनौ परस्परं प्रतिद्वंद्विनौ सुधनौ शोभनधनौ
> विश्वशर्धसौ व्याप्तबलौ बहूत्साहौ वा मघवा धनवानिंद्रो गोषु शुभ्रिषु
> शोभनासु गोषु निमित्तभूतासु अन्यं यष्टारं युजं सहायमकृत कृतवान्
> प्रवेपनी शत्रूणां प्रवेपनवान् । ईमस्मै गव्यं गोसमूहमुत्सृजते सत्वभिर्मरुद्धिः सह धुनिर्मेघानां कंपयिता । इंद्रो यजमानमयजमानं वा
> यं जानाति गोनिमित्तं ज्ञात्वा यज्जने गोसमूहं प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: Indra discerns when two persons, rivals of each other, rich, of pervading strength or of great zeal, are in contest over shining cows; Maghavan, the wealthy Indra, makes the other, the sacrificer, his ally on account of the cows. *Pravepanī* is the one who makes his enemies tremble. For him, together with the Maruts, he lets loose a herd of cows, he, the shaker of the clouds. Whomever Indra recognises as sacrificer or non-sacrificer, having known him in the matter of the cows, he gives the herd of cows to the sacrificing man; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवा (*maghavā*)—wealthy
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- शुभ्रिषु (*śubhriṣu*)—for the sake of the shining
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—cows (who fight)
- सुधना (*sudhanā*)—those who possess wealth
- विश्वशर्धसौ (*viśvaśardhasau*)—and are of exceedingly great strength
- जनौ (*janau*)—among rivals
- सं आवेत् (*saṃ āvet*)—discerns and knows (who is the sacrificer and who is not), then
- प्रवेपनी (*pravepanī*)—causing fear in the enemy
- अन्यं (*anyaṃ*)—to the sacrificer
- युजं (*yujaṃ*)—help
- अकृत (*akṛta*)—he gives
- सत्वभिः (*satvabhiḥ*)—together with the Maruts
- धुनि: (*dhuni:*)—Indra, who makes the clouds move
- ईं (*īṃ*)—to such a sacrificer
- गव्यं (*gavyaṃ*)—a herd of cows
- उत्सृजते (*utsṛjate*)—he creates

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wealthy Indra fights for the sake of shining cows. As soon as he discerns, among rival persons who are rich and of exceedingly great strength, who is the sacrificer and who is not, he causes fear in the enemy and helps the sacrificer. Indra, who makes the clouds move together with the Maruts, creates a herd of cows for such a sacrificer.

### Printed p. 273

##### English translation
When Indra, the possessor of opulence, discriminates between two men, both wealthy, and exerting themselves (against each other) for the sake of valuable cattle, he takes one of them as his associate, causing (his adversaries) to tremble, and the agitator (of the clouds), together with the Maruts, bestows upon him herds of cattle.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒ह॒स्र॒सामान्यि॑वेशं गृणीषे॒ शत्रि॑मग्न उप॒मां के॒तुम॒र्यः ।  
> तस्मा॒ आपः॑ सं॒यतः॑ पीपयंत॒ तस्मि॑न् क्ष॒त्रमनु॑वत्त्वे॒षम॑स्तु ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सहस्रसां । आग्निऽवेशं । गृणीषे । शत्रिं । अग्ने । उपमां । केतुं । अर्यः ।  
> तस्मै । आपः । संयतः । पीपयंत । तस्मिन् । क्षत्रं । अमवत् । त्वेषं । अस्तु ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निवेशिसुतं शत्रिमसंख्यातधनप्रदं । आशास्त्र ऋषिरंत्यर्चा प्रजापतिसुतः
> सुधीः ॥ अर्योऽहं सहस्रसामपरिमितधनप्रदमाग्नि वेशिमग्निवेशिसुतं शत्रिमेतन्नामकं राजर्षि० गृणीषे । गृणे । सौमि । हे अग्ने अंगनादिगुणविशिष्टेंद्र ।
> कीदृशं तं । उपमामुपमानभूतं केतुं प्रज्ञापकं । प्रख्यातमित्यर्थः । तस्मा
> आपः संयतः सम्यक् गच्छंत्यः पीपयंत । प्यायंतां । तस्मिन्राज्ञि क्षत्रं धनममवद्बलसहितं त्वेषं दीप्तमस्त्विति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa begins with a verse: Śatri, the son of Agniveśa, is the giver of countless wealth; the seer of the last ṛk is Āśāstra, the wise son of Prajāpati. He then explains: I, Arya, praise (गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*) is used for "I praise") the royal sage named Śatri, the son of Agniveśa, the giver of a thousand, that is, of immeasurable wealth. "O Agni" is addressed to Indra, who has the qualities of Agni and the others.**NOTE** Of what kind is that king? He is a model (उपमां (*upamāṃ*)), a *ketu*, that is, one who makes known; the meaning is "famous". For him may the waters, flowing well together, swell, that is, increase; and in that king may *kṣatra*, that is wealth, accompanied by strength, and brilliant, be.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—I, the venerable one
- उपमां (*upamāṃ*)—a model person (for the sacrificers)
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—famous
- सहस्रसां (*sahasrasāṃ*)—the giver of immeasurable wealth
- अग्निवेशिं (*agniveśiṃ*)—the son of Agniveśa
- शत्रिं (*śatriṃ*)—the royal sage named Śatri
- गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*)—I praise
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—for that king
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- संयतः (*saṃyataḥ*)—gathering together
- पीपयंत (*pīpayaṃta*)—may they satisfy
- तस्मिन् (*tasmin*)—in that king
- क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*)—wealth
- अनवत् (*anavat*)—accompanied by strength
- त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)—and brilliant
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it gather

### Printed p. 274

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, I, the venerable one, praise the royal sage named Śatri, the son of Agniveśa, a model person for all sacrificers, famous, and the giver of immeasurable wealth. For that king may all the waters, gathering together, give satisfaction. In that king may wealth, accompanied by strength and brilliant, gather.

##### English translation
I, Arya, Agni, praise Satri, the son of Agnivesha, the bestower of thousands, a type for comparison : may the collected waters yield him abundance ; may wealth, and strength, and glory be upon him

## Sūkta 35 (Maṇḍala 5)

The thirty-fifth sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्ते साधिष्ठ इत्यष्टर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं । अंगिरोगोत्रः प्रभूवसुर्नाम
> ऋषिः । अंत्या पंक्तिः । पंक्त्यंतपरिभाषया शिष्टा अनुष्टुभः । इंद्रो देवता ।
> यस्तेऽष्टौ प्रभूवसुरांगिरसः पंक्त्यंतमित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो
> लैंगिकः ॥ आभिप्लविकेषूक्ष्येषु तृतीयसवन आद्यस्तृचोऽच्छावाकस्य वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । यस्ते साधिष्ठोऽवसे पुरां भिंदुर्युवा कविः । आ: ७-८ ।
> इति ॥ द्वितीयतृतीययोः स्वरसान्नोश्चाद्यौ तृचावनुरूपौ । यस्ते साधिष्ठोऽवस इति षळनुष्टुभः । आ. ८-५ । इति हि सूत्रितं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: The third sūkta, यस्ते साधिष्ठ (*yaste sādhiṣṭha*), has eight ṛks. The seer is the Aṅgirasa Prabhūvasu. The last ṛk is in Paṅkti; the remaining ones are Anuṣṭubh by the convention on a Paṅkti ending. The deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā says: यस्तेऽष्टौ प्रभूवसुरांगिरसः पंक्त्यंतमित्यनुक्रांतं (*yaste 'ṣṭau prabhūvasurāṃgirasaḥ paṃktyaṃtamityanukrāṃtaṃ*). The use of the sūkta in ritual is laiṅgika. In the Ābhiplavika Ukthya sacrifices, at the third pressing, its first ṛk-triad is the optional Anurūpa of the Acchāvāka priest. It is stated in the sūtra: यस्ते साधिष्ठोऽवसे पुरां भिंदुर्युवा कविः (*yaste sādhiṣṭho 'vase purāṃ bhiṃduryuvā kaviḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-8). Further, in the second and third Svarasāman, the first two triads are the Anurūpa triads: यस्ते साधिष्ठोऽवस इति षळनुष्टुभः (*yaste sādhiṣṭho 'vasa iti ṣaḷanuṣṭubhaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-5), as is stated in the sūtra.

Translation of the Anuvāda: This sūkta, Yaste sādhiṣṭhaḥ, is the third sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are eight ṛks in it. The seer of this sūkta is Prabhūvasu, born in the family of the seer Aṅgiras; Indra is the deity; the last ṛk of this sūkta is in the Paṅkti metre and the remaining ṛks are in the Anuṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "Yaste'ṣṭau prabhūvasurāṅgirasaḥ paṅkty-antam". The use in ritual is laiṅgika. In the Ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, at the time of the third pressing, the first triad (three ṛks) of this sūkta is to be recited by the priest called Acchāvāka as an optional Anurūpa triad, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, "Yaste sādhiṣṭho'vase purāṃ bhinduryuvā kaviḥ" (Ā. 7-8). When the second and third Svarasāman mantras are recited, the first and second triads of this sūkta (ṛks 1-3 and 4-6) are to be recited as Anurūpa triads, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, "Yaste sādhiṣṭho'vasa iti ṣaḷanuṣṭubhaḥ" (Ā. 8-5).

### Printed p. 275

Sūkta 35.

Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 35.

Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 2, Varga 5, 6.

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8.

Seer: Prabhūvasu Āṅgirasa.

Deity: Indra.

Metre: 1-7, Anuṣṭubh; 8, Paṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्ते॒ साधि॒ष्ठोऽव॑स॒ इंद्र॒ क्रतु॒ष्टमा भ॑र ।  
> अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ चर्षणी॒सहं॒ सस्निं॒ वाजे॑षु दु॒ष्टरं॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । ते । साधिष्ठः । अवसे । इंद्र । क्रुतुः । तं । आ । भर ।  
> अस्मभ्यं । चर्षणीसहं । सस्निं । वाजेषु । दुस्तरं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव यः साधिष्ठोऽतिशयेन साधकः क्रतुरुक्तलक्षणं कर्म प्रज्ञा
> नास्ति तं क्रतुं नोऽवसेऽस्मद्रक्षणायास्मभ्यमा भर । आहर । कीदृशं तं । चर्षणीसहं सर्वेषां मनुष्याणामभिभवितारं सस्निं संस्कृतं शुद्धं वाजेषु संग्रामेषु
> दुष्टरमन्वैरनभिभाव्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, whatever act of yours, called *kratu*, is most accomplishing, that is, accomplishes to the highest degree, or the wisdom (*prajñā*)**NOTE**, that *kratu* bring to us for our protection. Of what kind is it? It overpowers all men (चर्षणीसहं (*carṣaṇīsahaṃ*)), it is *sasni*, that is refined and pure, and in battles it is hard to cross, that is, it cannot be overcome by others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- साधिष्ठः (*sādhiṣṭhaḥ*)—most effective in accomplishing
- क्रतुः (*kratuḥ*)—which is the act
- चर्षणीसहं (*carṣaṇīsahaṃ*)—which confronts enemy people
- सस्निं (*sasniṃ*)—which is pure
- वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—in battles
- दुष्टरं (*duṣṭaraṃ*)—which cannot be withstood by enemies
- तं (*taṃ*)—that well-known act
- अस्मभ्यं अवसे (*asmabhyaṃ avase*)—for our protection
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—obtain and perfect it (make it manifest)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whichever act of yours is most effective in accomplishing, bring for our protection that act which confronts enemy people, is pure, cannot be withstood by enemies in battles, and is well known: obtain it and perfect it.

### Printed p. 276

##### English translation
Perfect for our protection, Indra, that your act which is most effective ; whch is the subduer of men ; holy, and difficult to be encountered in battles.**NOTE**

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दिं॑द्र ते॒ चत॑स्रो॒ यच्छू॑र॒ संति॑ ति॒स्रः ।  
> यद्वा॒ पंच॑ क्षिती॒नामव॒स्तत्सु न॒ आ भ॑र ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । इंद्र । ते । चतस्रः । यत् । शूर । संति । तिस्रः ।  
> यत् । वा । पंच । क्षितीनां । अवः । तत् । सु । नः । आ । भर ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव यत् या ऊतयश्चतस्रश्चतुर्सु वर्णेषु संश्रिताः संति
> याश्च हे शूर तिस्रस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वर्तमानाः । यद्वा । नाशब्दश्चार्थे । यद्याश
> पंच क्षितीनां पंचजनसंबंधिन्य ऊतयः संति तत्सर्वमवो रक्षणं सु सुषु
> नोऽस्मभ्यमा भर । आहरेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, those protections of yours that are four, abiding in the four castes, and, O hero, those that are three, existing in the three worlds; or else, the word *nā* is in the sense of "and",**NOTE** and whichever protections there are that belong to the five peoples, all that protection (अवः (*avaḥ*)) bring well (*su*, "excellently") to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- यत् (*yat*)—which protections
- चतस्रः (*catasraḥ*)—together with the people of the four castes
- संति (*saṃti*)—are
- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant one
- यत् (*yat*)—which protections
- तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—can pervade the three worlds
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—and moreover
- पंच क्षितीनां (*paṃca kṣitīnāṃ*)—are protective of the five kinds of people, gods, Gandharvas and the rest
- तत् अवः (*tat avaḥ*)—all those acts of protection
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- नः (*naḥ*)—for our welfare
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, those protections of yours that are together with the people of the four castes, those that can pervade the three worlds, and moreover those that are protective of the five kinds of people, gods, Gandharvas and the rest, all those acts of protection obtain exceedingly for our welfare.

### Printed p. 277

##### English translation
Whatever protections, Indra, may be yours, whether four, or hero, three or those accorded to the five (classes) of men, bestow them freely upon us.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ तेवो॒ वरे॑ण्यं॒ वृषं॑तमस्य हूमहे ।  
> वृष॑जूति॒र्हि ज॑ज्जि॒ष आ॒भूभि॑रिंद्र तु॒र्वणिः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ते । अवः । वरेण्यं । वृषन्सतमस्य । हूमहे ।  
> वृषजूतिः । हि । जज्ञिषे । आभूभिः । इंद्र । तुर्वणिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वृषंतमश्य फलानां वर्षकतमस्य ते तवावो रक्षणं गमनं
> ना वरेण्यं वरणीयमा हूमहे । आह्वयामः । हे इंद्र वृषजूतिर्वर्षणगमनस्तुर्वणिस्तूर्णवनिर्हिंसको ना त्वमाभूमिः सर्वतो भवद्भिव्याप्तैर्मरुद्धिः
> सहावो हि जज्जिषे । उत्पादयसि खलु । तेऽव आह्वयाम इति । यद्वा । वृषगमनः
> सन्यस्माद्यज्ञमागत्य फलं जज्जिषे तस्मात्तेऽवो हूमह इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, of you, the one who showers fruits most abundantly, we call upon the desirable, that is, the choice-worthy, protection (*avas*, protection or going).**NOTE** O Indra, you whose going is that of rain (*vṛṣajūti*), swift-conquering and destroying (*turvaṇi*), you indeed produce that protection with the Maruts who pervade on all sides; therefore we call upon your protection. Or else: because you, whose going is like rain, come to the sacrifice and are born for its fruit, therefore we call upon your protection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृषजूतिः (*vṛṣajūtiḥ*)—the distributor of rain
- तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*)—and the one who quickly destroys enemies, you
- अभूभिः (*abhūbhiḥ*)—with the all-pervading Maruts
- जज्जिषे हि (*jajjiṣe hi*)—such protections as you produce
- वृषंतमस्य (*vṛṣaṃtamasya*)—of you who rain down fruit
- ते (*te*)—your
- वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*)—highly esteemed
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection
- आ हूमहे (*ā hūmahe*)—we pray for

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who distribute rain and quickly destroy enemies, we pray for that highly esteemed protection of you, who rain down fruit, such protections as you produce together with the all-pervading Maruts.

### Printed p. 278

##### English translation
We invoke the desirable protection of you, the most liberal showerer (of benefits); that (protection) which you, the distributor of rain, the quick destroyer (of foes), grant (associated) with the present (Maruts).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृषा॒ ह्यसि॒ राध॑से जज्ञि॒षे वृष्टि॑ ते॒ शवः॑ ।  
> स्वक्ष॑त्रं ते धृ॒षन्मनः॑ सत्रा॒हमिं॑द्र॒ पौंस्यं॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषा । हि । असि । राधसे । जज्जिषे । वृष्टि । ते । शवः ।  
> स्वक्षत्रं । ते । धृषत् । मनः । सत्राहं । इंद्र । पौंस्यं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र राधसे यजमानानां समृद्धये वृषा ह्यसि । फलस्य वर्षकोऽसि
> खलु । यद्वा । वृषा खल्वसि । राधसे धनार्थं जज्जिषे । उत्पद्यसे । ते शवो बलं
> वृष्णि वर्षितृ । ते मनः स्वक्षत्रं स्वायत्तबलं धृषत् धर्षकं विरोधिनां । हे इंद्र
> ते पौंस्यं पुंस्त्वं सत्राहं संघहंतृ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, for the prosperity of the sacrificers you are a showerer; you are indeed the one who rains down fruit. Or else: you are a showerer, born for wealth. Your strength (*śavas*) is rain-giving. Your mind is *svakṣatra*, with strength dependent on itself, and *dhṛṣat*, overbearing towards adversaries. O Indra, your manhood is *satrāha*, the destroyer of hosts together.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—as the one who showers desires
- असि हि (*asi hi*)—you are
- राधसे (*rādhase*)—for the prosperity in wealth (of the sacrificer)
- जज्जिषे (*jajjiṣe*)—you are born
- ते (*te*)—your
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—strength
- वृष्टि (*vṛṣṭi*)—pours down the desired objects
- ते (*te*)—your
- स्वक्षत्रं (*svakṣatraṃ*)—of self-possessed strength**NOTE**
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind
- धृषत् (*dhṛṣat*)—is overbearing towards enemies
- पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)—your manly power
- सत्राहं (*satrāhaṃ*)—is such as to destroy (enemies) in a mass

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are a showerer of desires. You are born for the prosperity of the sacrificer in wealth. Your strength pours down the desired objects. Your mind, which has self-acquired strength, is overbearing towards enemies. Your manly power is such as to destroy enemies in a mass.

### Printed p. 279

##### English translation
You are the showerer (of benefits) ; you are born to (bestow) riches ; your strength rains (blessings) ; your self-invigorated mind is the restrainer (of adversaries) ; your manhood, Indra, is the destroyer of multitudes.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं तमिं॑द्र॒ मर्त्य॑ममित्र॒यंत॑मद्रिनः ।  
> स॒र्व॒र॒था श॑तक्रतो॒ नि या॑हि शवसस्पते ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । तं । इंद्र । मर्त्यं । अमित्रयंतं । अद्रिनः ।  
> सर्वऽरथा । शतक्रतो इति शतक्रतो । नि । याहि । शवसः । पते ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं तममित्रयंतं शत्रुत्वमाचरंतं शत्रुं वेच्छंतं मर्त्यं हे
> अद्रिवो वज्रवन्निंद्र सर्वरथा सर्वत्र व्याप्तेन रथेन ॥ सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः ॥ हे
> शतक्रतो हे शवसस्पते बलस्य पालकेंद्र नि याहि । नितरां गच्छाभिभवितुं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, against that mortal who behaves as an enemy, or who desires an enemy; O wielder of the thunderbolt (*adrivaḥ*); with a chariot that pervades everywhere (*sarvarathā*); O Śatakratu; O lord of strength (*śavasaspate*), protector of strength, Indra: go against him (*ni yāhi*), that is, go down upon him in order to overcome him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O bearer of the thunderbolt
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O doer of many acts
- शवसस्पते (*śavasaspate*)—O protector of strength
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सर्वरथा (*sarvarathā*)—with a chariot that pervades everywhere
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अमित्रयंतु (*amitrayaṃtu*)—who behaves like an enemy
- तं मर्त्यं (*taṃ martyaṃ*)—to confront that man
- नि याहि (*ni yāhi*)—set out and oppose him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, doer of many acts, protector of strength, set out with your chariot that pervades everywhere, to confront men who behave like enemies.

##### English translation
Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, rider in an all-pervading car, object of many rites, and lord of strength, proceed against the mortal who entertains hostility towards you.

### Printed p. 280

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वामिद्वृ॑त्रहंतम॒ जना॑सो वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः ।  
> उ॒ग्रं पू॒र्वीषु॑ पू॒र्व्यं हवं॑ते॒ वाज॑सातये ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वां । इत् । वृत्रहन्ऽतम । जनासः । वृक्तबर्हिषः ।  
> उग्रं । पूर्विषु । पूर्व्यं । हवंते । वाज्यसातये ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहंतमातिशयेन वृत्राणां हंतरिंद्र त्वामित्वामेव जनासो जना
> वृक्तबर्हिष आच्छादितदर्भाः । प्रवृत्तयज्ञा इत्यर्थः । उग्रमुद्गूर्णबलं पूर्वीषु
> बह्वीषु प्रजासु मध्यॆ पूर्व्यं पुरातनं संतं वाजसातये संग्रामाय हवंते ।
> आह्वयंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, greatest slayer of Vṛtras, you alone do the people whose sacred grass is spread (वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*), that is, who have covered the darbha grass; the meaning is that they have set the sacrifice going) call to the battle (वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*), that is, for the fight). You are fierce, of uplifted strength, and ancient among the many peoples.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहंतनु (*vṛtrahaṃtanu*)—O Indra, destroyer of Vṛtra
- पूर्वीषु (*pūrvīṣu*)—among many men
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—who are of exceeding strength
- पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*)—and ancient
- त्वामित् (*tvāmit*)—you alone
- वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*)—who prepare seats of darbha grass to provide you a seat
- जनासः (*janāsaḥ*)—people
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for help in battle
- हवंते (*havaṃte*)—call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, destroyer of Vṛtra, you who are of exceeding strength and ancient among many men, you alone do those men who prepare seats of darbha grass for you and make ready the sacrifice call, desiring help in battle.

##### English translation
Slayer of Vritra, men with clipped sacred grass invoke you, who are fierce and foremost among many, for aid in battle.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्माक॑मिंद्र दु॒ष्टरं॑ पुरो॒यावा॑नमा॒जिषु॑ ।  
> स॒यावा॑नं॒ धने॑धने वाज॒यंत॑मवा॒ रथं॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्माकं । इंद्र । दुस्तरं । पुरःऽयावानं । आजिषु ।  
> स्ययावानं । धनेऽधने। वाजयंतं । अव । रथं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अस्माकं रथं रंहणस्वभावं ना पुत्रमव । रक्ष । कीदृशं रथं ।
> दुष्टरं दुःखेन तरणीयमाजिसु संग्रामेषु पुरोयावानं पुरतो मिश्रयितारं सयावानमनुचरैः सह गंतारं धने धने सर्वेषु धनेषु वाजयंतं
> संग्रामं धनं वेच्छंतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, protect our chariot, whose nature is to rush on.**NOTE** Of what kind is the chariot? It is hard to cross, that is, to be got over only with difficulty, in battles; it goes in front (पुरोयावानं (*puroyāvānaṃ*), that is, it mingles in front); it goes together with followers; in every kind of wealth it seeks battle and wealth (वाजयंतं (*vājayaṃtaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- दुष्टरं (*duṣṭaraṃ*)—which others can hardly stop
- आजिषु (*ājiṣu*)—in battles
- पुरोयावानं (*puroyāvānaṃ*)—which moves about in the forefront
- सयावानं (*sayāvānaṃ*)—which moves along with followers
- धनेधने (*dhanedhane*)—again and again, to gather wealth
- वाजयंतं (*vājayaṃtaṃ*)—and which desires battle
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—chariot
- अव (*ava*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, protect our chariot, which others can hardly stop, which moves boldly in the forefront in battles, moves along with followers, and again and again desires battle for the sake of gaining wealth.

##### English translation
Defend, Indra, our chariot, difficult (to be stopped), mingling foremost in combats, followed by attendants. and eagerly striving for repeated spoil.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मनामहे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्माकं । इंद्र । आ । इहि । नः । रथं । अव । पुरंs ध्या ।  
> वयं । शविष्ठ । वार्यं । दिवि । श्रवः । दधीमहि । दिवि । स्तोमं । मनामहे ॥८॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अस्माकमस्मदीय एव सन् एहि । आगच्छ । अगत्य च पुरंध्या शोभनबुद्धा नोऽस्माकु रथमव । रक्ष । वयं च हे शविष्ठ अतिशयेन बलवन् त्वदनुग्रहाद्वार्यं वरणेयं श्रवोऽन्नं कीर्तिं वा दिवि द्योतमाने त्वयि दधीमहि ।
> स्थापयामः । तथा दिवि त्वयि स्तोमं स्तोत्रं मनामहे । करवामह इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, come to us, being truly ours; and having come, protect our chariot with good understanding (पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*)). And we, O Śaviṣṭha, most mighty one, by your favour place the desirable (वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)) food or fame (श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)) in you who shine; likewise we make (मनामहे (*manāmahe*)) praise in you who shine; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—to us
- एहि (*ehi*)—be pleased to come
- पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*)—with a favouring understanding
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—chariot
- अव (*ava*)—protect
- शविष्ठ (*śaviṣṭha*)—O Indra, most powerful
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)—desired
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food
- दिवि (*divi*)—in you who shine
- दधीमहि (*dadhīmahi*)—we place
- दिवि (*divi*)—addressed to you who are divine
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—praise
- मनामहे (*manāmahe*)—we recite and offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, be pleased to come to us. Protect our chariot with a favouring understanding. O most powerful Indra, in you who shine we place the most desired**NOTE** food. Addressing you, who are divine, we also recite and offer praise.

### Printed p. 283

##### English translation
Come, Indra, to us ; defend by your providence our car : we contemplate in you who, most mighty one, are divine, all desirable vigour : (to you), who are divine, we offer praise.

## Sūkta 36 (Maṇḍala 5)

The thirty-sixth sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स आ गमदिति षडृचं चतुर्थं सूक्तं ॥ अंगिरसः प्रभूवसुर्ऋषिः । तृतीया
> जगती शिष्टा अनुक्तत्वात् त्रिष्टुभः । इंद्रो देवता । अनुक्रांतं च । स आ गमत्
> षट् तृतीया जगतीति ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: The fourth sūkta, स आ गमदिति (*sa ā gamaditi*), has six ṛks. The seer is the Aṅgirasa Prabhūvasu. The third ṛk is in Jagatī; the remaining ones are Triṣṭubh, because no other metre is stated. The deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā also says: स आ गमत् षट् तृतीया जगतीति (*sa ā gamat ṣaṭ tṛtīyā jagatīti*). The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Translation of the Anuvāda: This sūkta, Sa ā gamat, is the fourth sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are six ṛks in it. The seer of this sūkta is Prabhūvasu, born in the line of the seer Aṅgiras. Indra is the deity. The third ṛk of this sūkta is in the Jagatī metre and the remaining ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "Sa ā gamat ṣaṭ tṛtīyā jagatī". The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Sūkta 36.

Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 36.

Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 2, Varga 7.

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6.

Seer: Prabhūvasu Āṅgirasa.

Deity: Indra.

Metre: 1, 2, 4-6, Triṣṭubh; 3, Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स आ ग॑म॒दिंद्रो॒ यो वसू॑नां॒ चिके॑त॒द्दातुं॒ दाम॑नो  ॒
> रयीणां ।  
> ध॒न्व॒च॒रो न वंस॑गस्तृषा॒णश्च॑कमा॒नः पि॑बतु दु॒ग्धमं॒शुं ॥१॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । आ । गमत् । इंद्रः । यः । वसूनां । चिकेतत् । दातुं । दामनः । रयीणां ।  
> धन्वचरः । न । वंसगः । तृषाणः । चकमानः । पिबतु । दुग्धं । अंशुं ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 284

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स इंद्रोऽस्मद्यज्ञं प्रत्या गमत् । आगच्छतु । यो देवो वसूनां धनानां ।
> कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ वसूनि धनानि चिकेतत् जानाति प्रदातुं । स कीदृशः । दामनो
> दाता दानमना वा रयिणां धनानां । गमने दृष्टांतः । धन्वचरो न धनुषा
> सह संचरन् धानुष्क इव वंसगो वननीयगमनस्तृषाणोऽत्यंतं तृषितश्चकमानः
> कामयमानश्च सन् दुग्धमभिषुतमंशुं सोमं पिबतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: May that Indra come to our sacrifice, the god who knows how to give wealth. What kind is he? He is the giver of riches, or one whose mind is set on giving. As an illustration of his coming: like a bowman (धन्वचरो (*dhanvacaro*), one who moves about with a bow), whose going is lovely (वंसगः (*vaṃsagaḥ*)), exceedingly thirsty and desirous, may he drink the pressed (दुग्धं (*dugdhaṃ*)) Soma, the *aṃśu*.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—wealth
- दातुं (*dātuṃ*)—to distribute to the sacrificers
- चिकेतत् (*ciketat*)—knows (and)
- रयीणां (*rayīṇāṃ*)—of riches
- दामनः (*dāmanaḥ*)—is the giver
- सः इंद्रः (*saḥ iṃdraḥ*)—that Indra
- धन्वचरो न (*dhanvacaro na*)—like a warrior bearing a bow
- आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)—may he come to our sacrifice
- वंसगः (*vaṃsagaḥ*)—of attractive going
- तृषाणः (*tṛṣāṇaḥ*)—thirsty
- चकमानः (*cakamānaḥ*)—and desirous (of drinking Soma)
- दुग्धं (*dugdhaṃ*)—pressed
- अंशुं (*aṃśuṃ*)—Soma
- पिबतु (*pibatu*)—may he drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Indra who knows that wealth is to be distributed to the sacrificers come to our sacrifice like a warrior bearing a bow. Of attractive going, thirsty and desirous of drinking Soma, may he drink the Soma juice.

##### English translation
May that Indra who is the donor of wealth, who knows ( how ) to distribute riches, come (to our sacrifice) marching boldly like a warrior ; and may he, being thirsty, and desirous (of the draught), drink of the effused Soma juice.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ ते॒ हनू॑ हरिवः शूर॒ शिप्रे॒ रुह॒त्सोमो॒ न पर्व॑तस्य पृ॒ष्ठे ।  
> अनु॑ त्वा राज॒न्नर्व॑तो॒ न हि॒न्वन् गी॒र्भिर्म॑देम पुरुहूत॒  ॑
> विश्वे ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 285

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ते । हनू इति । हरिऽवः । शूर । शिप्रे इति । रुहत् । सोमः । न । पर्वतस्य ।  
> पृष्ठे ।  
> अनु । त्वा । राजन् । अर्वतः । न । हिन्वन् । गीभिः । मदेम । पुरुहूत ।  
> विश्वे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र हे हरिवो हरिभ्यां तद्वन् शूर ते तव हनू हननसाधने । यद्यप्ययं शिप्रावचनस्तथापि पुनः शिप्राभिधानाद्गौणोऽवगंतव्यः । उक्तरूपे संहते
> वा शिप्रे आ रुहत् आरोहतु प्राप्नोतु सोमोऽस्मद्दत्तः । पर्वतस्य पृष्ठे न
> रुहत् । नारोहति । तत्र न तिष्ठतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । नशब्दः पुरस्तात्पयुक्तोऽप्यत्रोपमार्थः । पर्वतस्य पृष्ठ उपरिप्रदेशे सोमो न । तत्र यथा विस्रंभेण
> प्रसरत्ति-तद्वत् । हे राजन् राजमानेंद्र त्वा त्वामनु त्वया सह ॥ तृतीयार्थ
> इत्यनोः कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वं ॥ विश्वे वयमर्वतो नाश्वानिव तृणादिभिर्गिर्भिः
> स्तुतिभिर्हिन्वन् हिन्वंतस्त्वां प्रीणयंतः संतो मदेम । हृष्येम ॥ हे पुरुहूत
> बहुप्रकारं बहुभिर्वाहूतेंद्र ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, O possessor of bay horses, O hero, these two jaws of yours (हनू (*hanū*)) are the instruments of striking. Although this word has the sense of *śipra*, yet because *śipra* is named again, it is to be understood in a secondary sense.**NOTE** Into the two *śipras*, of the stated form or joined together, may the Soma given by us climb, that is, reach. It does not climb on the back of a mountain, that is, it does not stay there. Or else, the word *na*, although used earlier, has here the sense of comparison: as Soma moves about with confidence on the upper part, the back, of a mountain, so it does here. O shining king Indra, with you (त्वा (*tvā*) अनु (*anu*)) we all, pleasing you with our praises (*girbhiḥ*), as one delights horses (अर्वतो (*arvato*)) with grass and the like, would rejoice, that is, be glad. O Puruhūta, Indra, called in many ways or by many.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O one yoked with horses
- शूर (*śūra*)—and O hero, Indra
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—may Soma
- पर्वतस्य (*parvatasya*)—of a mountain
- पृष्ठे न (*pṛṣṭhe na*)—as one climbs the summit
- हनू (*hanū*)—which are the instrument of striking (enemies)
- ते शिप्रे (*te śipre*)—into your jaws
- आ रुहत् (*ā ruhat*)—climb (and join)
- राजन् (*rājan*)—O lord
- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—and O Indra, called by many
- अर्वतो न (*arvato na*)—as one pleases horses with grass and the like
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with our praises
- हिन्वन् (*hinvan*)—gladdening you
- त्वा अनु (*tvā anu*)—with you
- विश्वे मदेम (*viśve madema*)—we all shall rejoice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are yoked with horses and are a hero, may Soma climb up and fill your jaws, the instrument of striking enemies, as one climbs the summit of a mountain. O Indra, lord, called by many, gladdening you with our praises as one pleases horses with grass and the like, we all shall rejoice with you.

### Printed p. 286

##### English translation
Hero, lord of horses, may the the Soma ascend to your destructive jaw, as if to the summit of a mountain : may we all, royal Indra, who are invoked of many, give pleasure to you with our hymns, as to horses with fodder.

> रथा॒दधि॑ त्वा जरि॒ता स॑दावृध कु॒विन्नु स्तो॑षन्मघवन्नुरू॒वसुः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

> पुरुर्वसुः ॥ २ ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुरुहूत बहुभिराहूत हे अद्रिवो वज्रवन्निंद्र मे मनोऽमतेरिद्दारिद्रादस्तोतुर्वा सकाशाद्भिया भीत्या वेपते । कंपते । वृत्तं चक्रं न भूमौ
> वर्तमानं चक्रमिव । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्रथादध्युपरि स्थितं त्वा त्वां हे सदावृध
> सर्वदा वर्धमान हे मघवन्निंद्र जरिता स्तोता पुरूवसुरहमृषिः कुविद्बहु नु
> क्षिप्रं स्तोषत् । स्तोष्यति । स्तूयात् ॥ अत्र कुविच्छब्दयोगेऽप्याख्यातस्य बहुलग्रहणान्निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Puruhūta, called by many, O Adrivas, Indra armed with the thunderbolt, my mind trembles with fear, that is, shakes, from poverty (मनोऽमतेरिद्दारिद्रादस्तोतुर्वा (*mano 'materiddāridrādastoturvā*) is read here as "from poverty, or from one who does not praise"),**NOTE** like a wheel rolling on the ground. Because this is so, O ever-growing one (सदावृध (*sadāvṛdha*)), O Maghavan Indra, I, the praiser, the seer Puruvasu, will quickly and abundantly (कुविद्बहु नु क्षिप्रं (*kuvidbahu nu kṣipraṃ*) is his gloss of *kuvit* and *nu*) praise you, who stand above the chariot.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—who are called by many
- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—and who hold the thunderbolt
- मे (*me*)—my
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind
- अमशेः (*amaśeḥ*)—of poverty
- भिया (*bhiyā*)—through fear

### Printed p. 287

- वृत्तं (*vṛttaṃ*)—which is rolling on the ground
- चक्रं न (*cakraṃ na*)—like a wheel
- वेपते (*vepate*)—trembles
- सदावृध (*sadāvṛdha*)—who always grow
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—and are wealthy, O Indra
- रथादधि (*rathādadhi*)—who stand on the chariot
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- जरिता (*jaritā*)—the praiser
- पुरूवसुः (*purūvasuḥ*)—named Puruvasu, I
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—in many ways
- नु (*nu*)—and quickly
- स्तोषत् (*stoṣat*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, called by many and holding the thunderbolt, my mind trembles through fear of poverty like a wheel rolling on the ground. O Indra, who always grow and are wealthy, I, the praiser named Puruvasu, praise you, who stand on the chariot, in many ways and quickly.

##### English translation
Wielder of the thunderbolt, the invoked of many, my mind trembles through dread of poverty like a whirling wheel : Maghavan, ever prosperous, may your worshipper, Puruvasu, praise you promptly and abundantly, seated in your chariot.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एष जरिता गरिता स्तोता ग्रावेवाभिषवाश्मेव । स यथा रसं जनयति तद्वत्
> हे इंद्र ते तुभ्यं वाचं स्तुतिमियर्ति । प्रेरयतीत्यर्थः । बृहन्महत्प्रभूतं
> फलमाशुषाण आशु संभक्ता सन् हे मघवन् सव्येन हस्तेन रायो धनानि प्र
> यंसि । प्रयच्छसि । दक्षिणिद्दक्षिणेनापि प्र यंसीति शेषः । मा वि वेनः । विगतकामं
> मा कार्षिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: This praiser, like the pressing stone (ग्रावेव (*grāveva*)), which produces the juice, sends forth (इयर्ति (*iyarti*), that is, urges on) praise to you, O Indra, quickly obtaining great, abundant fruit. O Maghavan, with the left hand you give riches (प्र यंसि (*pra yaṃsi*), that is, you give); the remainder is to be supplied thus: with the right hand also you give. Do not disappoint him (मा वि वेनः (*mā vi venaḥ*)): do not make him bereft of desire.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- एषः जरिता (*eṣaḥ jaritā*)—this praiser
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—abundant
- आशुषाणः (*āśuṣāṇaḥ*)—looking for fruit
- ग्रावेव (*grāveva*)—as the stone that presses Soma produces the juice
- ते (*te*)—which praises you
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—praise
- इयति (*iyati*)—produces
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- सव्येन (*savyena*)—with the left hand
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—riches
- प्र यंसि (*pra yaṃsi*)—you give
- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O Indra, yoked with horses
- दक्षिणित् (*dakṣiṇit*)—with the right hand also
- प्र (*pra*)—give (generously)
- मा वि वेनः (*mā vi venaḥ*)—do not hold back from giving

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, this praiser, looking for abundant fruit, brings forth praise of you, as the stone that presses Soma brings out the juice. O wealthy Indra, you give riches with the left hand; in the same way, O Indra yoked with horses, give with the right hand also. Give generously; do not hold back from giving.

##### English translation
This your adorer, Indra, like the stone (that express the Soma juice), urges praise to you, participating in the great (reward): you bestow, Maghavan, riches with your left hand, you bestow them, lord of horses, with the right : be not reluctant.

> स नो॒ वृषा॒ वृष॑रथः सुशिप्र॒ वृष॑क्रतो॒ वृषा॑ वज्रि॒न्भरे॑ धाः ॥

> सर् । नः । वृषा । वृषरथः । सुशिप्र । वृषक्रतो इति वृषक्रतो । वृषा । वज्रिन् ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वा त्वां वृषा वर्षित्री द्यौर्द्योतयित्रि स्तुतिः ॥ द्योततेर्दीव्यतीर्वा स्तुत्यर्थस्येदं रूपं ॥ वृषणं कामानां वर्षकं त्वां वर्धतु ।
> वर्धयतु । वृषा त्वं वृषभ्यां सेक्तृभ्यां हरिभ्यां वहसे । यज्ञं प्रत्युह्यसे ।
> सुशिप्र शोभनहनो वृषक्रतो वर्षणकर्मन् हे वज्रिन् वज्रयुक्तेंद्र स त्वं
> वृषा वृषरथश्च सन् नोऽस्मान् भरे संग्रामे भरणवति यज्ञे वा धाः । धारय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, may praise, which rains and illumines (द्यौः (*dyauḥ*), a form of the root meaning "to shine" or "to play", used in the sense of praise), increase you, the showerer of desires. You, the showerer, are borne to the sacrifice by the two showering (that is, sprinkling) bay horses. O Suśipra, of fine jaws, O you of showering deeds, O wielder of the thunderbolt, Indra, being such a showerer with a showering chariot, uphold (धाः (*dhāḥ*), that is, support) us in battle, or in the sacrifice that bears us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—this praise, which gives satisfaction (O Indra)
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—and which shines
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—who rain down desires
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वर्धतु (*vardhatu*)—may it make grow
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you who rain down desires
- वृषभ्यां (*vṛṣabhyāṃ*)—which have the power to sprinkle
- हरिभ्यां (*haribhyāṃ*)—by the horses
- वहसे (*vahase*)—are borne
- सुशिप्र (*suśipra*)—who have fine cheeks
- वृषक्रतो (*vṛṣakrato*)—who have deeds that grant desires
- वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)—O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—who have the power to sprinkle
- वृषरथः (*vṛṣarathaḥ*)—and have a chariot that grants desires
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- भरे (*bhare*)—in battle
- धाः (*dhāḥ*)—uphold (protect)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may this praise, which gives satisfaction and shines, make you, the rainer of desires, grow. You, the rainer of desires, are borne by horses that have the power to sprinkle. O Indra, who have fine cheeks, deeds that grant desires, and who hold the thunderbolt, you who have the power to sprinkle and a chariot that grants desires, protect us in battle.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: This is a praise of the gift of King Śrutaratha. The king who is rich in food, Śrutaratha, gave (अदिष्ट (*adiṣṭa*)) two red (रोहितौ (*rohitau*)) swift horses (वाजिनौ (*vājinau*)), joined with three hundreds, of the stated number, of cows, that is, of wealth.**NOTE** To him, the ever-youthful (यूने (*yūne*): one who mixes with all everywhere, or who is always young), to this Śrutaratha, may all peoples (क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*)), in service (दुवोया (*duvoyā*), that is, in attendance), bow together, that is, be submissive and serve. "O Maruts" is an address to the Maruts, the helpers of Indra.

## Sūkta 37 (Maṇḍala 5)

The thirty-seventh sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सं भानुनेति पंचर्चं पंचमं सूक्तमत्रेरार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । सं
> भानुना पंचात्रिरित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: The fifth sūkta, सं भानुनेति (*saṃ bhānuneti*), has five ṛks; its seer is Atri, its metre is Triṣṭubh and its deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā says: सं भानुना पंचात्रिरित्यनुक्रमणिका (*saṃ bhānunā paṃcātrirityanukramaṇikā*). The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Translation of the Anuvāda: This sūkta, Saṃ bhānunā, is the fifth sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are five ṛks in it. The seer of this sūkta is Atri; Indra is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "Saṃ bhānunā pañcātriḥ". The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Sūkta 37.

Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 37.

Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 2, Varga 8.

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5.

Seer: Atri.

Deity: Indra.

Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

> तस्मा॒ अमृ॑ध्रा उ॒षसो॒ व्यु॑च्छा॒न्य इंद्रा॑य सु॒नवा॒मेत्याह॑ ॥

> तस्मै । अमृध्राः । उषसः । वि । उच्छान् । यः । इंद्राय । सुनवाम । इति । अह॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूरस्य भानुना तेजसा सहाजुह्वानः सर्वत्र हूयमानः ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः । धृतपृष्ठः प्रदीप्तज्वालो धृतयुक्त पृष्ठप्रदेशो वा स्वंचाः स्वंचनोऽग्निः सं यतते । सम्यक् प्रयत्नं करोति। उदयकाले ह्यग्नयः प्रज्वाल्यंते ।
> तस्मात्कारणाद्यो यजमान इंद्राय सुनवामेत्याह ब्रूतेऽध्वर्युं प्रति तस्मै
> यजमानायामृध्रा अहिंसिता उषसो व्युच्छान् । व्युच्छंतु । उदयकालेऽग्निः
> प्रज्वालितस्तस्मात्सोमयागं कुर्म इति यो ब्रूते तस्यॆ सुदिनानि भवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: Together with the radiance (bhānu), that is, the brilliance, of the sun, Agni, who is invoked everywhere (the agent-suffix is used here in the passive sense), who has blazing flames or whose back is joined with ghee (*dhṛtapṛṣṭha*), and who is of good motion (*svañcāḥ*), makes a proper effort, for fires are kindled at the time of sunrise. For that reason, the sacrificer who says to the adhvaryu, "Let us press Soma for Indra" — for that sacrificer may the unharmed dawns shine forth. The meaning is that good days come to him who says, "At sunrise the fire is kindled; therefore we perform the Soma sacrifice."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धृतपृष्ठः (*dhṛtapṛṣṭhaḥ*)—having blazing flames
- स्वंचाः (*svaṃcāḥ*)—of beautiful motion
- आजुह्वानः (*ājuhvānaḥ*)—he who is invoked everywhere, Agni
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- भानुना (*bhānunā*)—with the radiance
- संयतते (*saṃyatate*)—joins and becomes one (or: vies with the splendour of the sun and shines)
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sacrificer
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- सुनवाम (*sunavāma*)—let us press Soma (for offering to Indra)
- इति (*iti*)—thus
- आह (*āha*)—says
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—for that sacrificer
- अमृध्राः (*amṛdhrāḥ*)—unharmed
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—the dawns
- व्युच्छान् (*vyucchān*)—may they appear and shine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who has blazing flames, who is of good motion and who is invoked everywhere, vies by his own radiance with the splendour of the sun. For the sacrificer who, urging Indra, says, "Let us press Soma for offering to Indra," may the unharmed dawns appear and shine.

### Printed p. 293

##### English translation
The piously worshipped (Agni), when invoked, glistening with the oblation, vies with the splendour of the sun : may the dawns rise innoxious to him who says, let us offer oblations to Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धृतपृष्ठः (*dhṛtapṛṣṭhaḥ*)—प्रदीप्तज्वालो धृतयुक्तपृष्ठप्रदेशो वा (*pradīptajvālo dhṛtayuktapṛṣṭhapradeśo vā*). Because ghee is offered into the fire, the meaning is that Agni shines with sharp and brilliant flames. It is customary to praise the Agni that blazes through oblations and the like by the word dhṛtapṛṣṭha.

स्वंचाः (*svaṃcāḥ*)—On this word Yāska has given the explanation: स्पंचाः सु अंचनः । आजुह्वानो धृतपृष्ठः स्पंचाः इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*spaṃcāḥ su aṃcanaḥ | ājuhvāno dhṛtapṛṣṭhaḥ spaṃcāḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati*) (Ni. 5-7). Since añcana means motion, svañcāḥ means one who has beautiful motion. If it be asked whether Agni has motion: the fire is churned in the araṇis, and from that place is brought to the fire-pit called Āhavanīya on the northern altar and established there. This rite is called Āgnyānayana or Agnipraṇayana. It is performed with injunction and with mantras. It is the most important of the auxiliary rites at the beginning of the sacrifice. To indicate this, he is here praised as svañcāḥ, one of beautiful motion.

सूर्यस्य भानुना आजुह्वानः सं यतते (*sūryasya bhānunā ājuhvānaḥ saṃ yatate*)—In the morning, when the sun rises, the priests kindle the fire and make it blaze. Since that fire, blazing and burning, shines very brightly, the idea is suggested that Agni, invoked together with the radiance of the sun that is just rising, shines like the radiance of the sun.

यः इंद्राय सुनवाम इति आह तस्मै अमृध्रा उषसः व्युच्छान् (*yaḥ iṃdrāya sunavāma iti āha tasmai amṛdhrā uṣasaḥ vyucchān*)—Whatever sacrificer expresses the wish that in the sacrifice performed in the morning Soma juice be pressed and offered for Indra, in his case may the Dawn deities be pleased, and may that day of the sacrifice turn out for the sacrificer a sudina, that is, a good day that brings about the favour of Indra and Agni. This intention is expressed here.

> समिद्दाग्निः प्रदीप्ताग्निः स्तीर्णबर्हिः प्रस्तृतदर्भोऽयं यजमानो
> वनवत् । संभजते । युक्तग्रावा नियुक्ताभिषवपाषाणः सुतसोमोऽभिषुतसोमो
> जराते । जरति । स्तौति । यस्याध्वर्योर्ग्रावाणोऽभिषवसाधना इषिरमेषणीयं
> गमनशीलं वा शब्दं वदंति सोऽध्वर्युर्हविषा सहानायत् सिंधुं । पन्नेजनीरवगच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: He whose fire is kindled (*samiddhāgni*) and whose sacred grass is spread out (*stīrṇabarhiḥ*), this sacrificer, worships (*vanavat*, he serves). He who has the pressing stones fitted in place (*yuktagrāvā*) and whose Soma is pressed (*sutasoma*) praises (*jarāte* means "he praises"). The adhvaryu, whose pressing stones, the instruments of pressing, utter a desirable or moving sound (*iṣira*, that which is to be wished for, or that which has motion), that adhvaryu goes down with the oblation to the stream (*sindhu*), that is, to the waters called pannejanī.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समिद्दाग्नि (*samiddāgni*)—he who has a kindled fire
- स्तीर्णबर्हिः (*stīrṇabarhiḥ*)—the sacrificer who has sacred grass spread widely for a seat
- वनवत् (*vanavat*)—offers worship
- युक्तग्रावा (*yuktagrāvā*)—he who holds the stone for pressing out the juice
- सुतसोमः (*sutasomaḥ*)—the sacrificer (or priest) who has pressed Soma
- जराते (*jarāte*)—praises
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which adhvaryu
- ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*)—the stones
- इषिरं (*iṣiraṃ*)—a moving sound
- वदंति (*vadaṃti*)—indicate
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with the oblation
- सिंधुं (*siṃdhuṃ*)—to the river
- अपायत् (*apāyat*)—descends (for the preliminary rite) **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer who has a kindled fire and sacred grass spread widely for the seat offers worship. The sacrificer, or the priest, who holds the stone for pressing out the juice and has the pressed Soma praises. The adhvaryu whose pressing stones indicate a moving sound goes down with the oblation to the river for the preliminary rite.

### Printed p. 295

##### English translation
He whose fire is kindled, whose sacred grass is strewn, offers worship : he whose stone is uplifted, whose Soma juice is effused, offers praise : the priest, of whom the stones utter the sounds of bruising, descends with the oblation (for previous ablution) to the stream.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

समिद्दाग्निः स्तीर्णबर्हिषः वनवत् युक्तग्रावा सुतसोमः (*samiddāgniḥ stīrṇabarhiṣaḥ vanavat yuktagrāvā sutasomaḥ*)—All these qualifying words describe the preparations that the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice has made for it. That is, the sacrificer, after sunrise in the morning, in order to perform the sacrifice, together with the priests and according to the rules performs the auxiliary rites such as the churning of the fire and the Agnipraṇayana, establishes the fire on the northern altar and kindles it with fuel and other materials so that he may offer oblations in it: this meaning is suggested by the word समिद्दाग्निः (*samiddāgniḥ*). Then the deities, invoked by Agni (or by the Hotṛ) and coming to the place of sacrifice, need a place to sit; for this he spreads darbha grass cut level, layer upon layer, that is, one layer upon another and a third upon that, in three layers. It is the custom to lay three layers in this way so that the seat is soft for those who sit. The idea that the sacrificer has prepared such a seat for the deities is expressed by the word स्तीर्णबर्हिः (*stīrṇabarhiḥ*). After this the priests, the adhvaryu and others, take stones in their hands, crush the Soma creepers and press out the juice. That the stones are made ready for this pressing of Soma, and that Soma is pressed out with them, is understood from the words यक्तग्रावा (*yaktagrāvā*) and सुतसोमः (*sutasomaḥ*). All these, that is, the kindling of the fire, the invocation of the deities, the spreading of the seat and the pressing of Soma, are preparations to be made at the start of the sacrifice as auxiliary rites. The matter that the sacrificer has made them and is ready to perform the sacrifice is indicated in the first half of this Ṛk.

In the second half the beginning of the sacrifice is described in detail: the word जराते (*jarāte*) shows that the sacrificer or the Hotṛ has begun to praise the deities; ग्रावाणः यस्य इषिरं नदंति (*grāvāṇaḥ yasya iṣiraṃ nadaṃti*) shows that the stones that crush the Soma, busy in the work of pressing, are pressing out the Soma juice with an audible sound; and the sentence अध्वर्युः हविषा सिंधुं अव आयत् (*adhvaryuḥ haviṣā siṃdhuṃ ava āyat*) describes that the adhvaryu and others are engaged in their respective duties.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: This bride, the wife of Indra, desiring her husband, that is, wishing for her beloved who has set out for the sacrifice, follows him. The Indra who brings this chief queen (*mahiṣī*), who is *iṣirā*, that is, endowed with motion: of this Indra the chariot comes hither, facing us. It desires food (*śravasyāt*), it sounds loudly (*ghoṣāt*, it cries out, makes a noise), and it rolls around, that is, brings all around, more than before, thousands of riches. Or else the two verbs are to be taken as meaning "it desires food and it would sound."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- इषिरां (*iṣirāṃ*)—his companion
- ईं महिषीं (*īṃ mahiṣīṃ*)—his chief queen
- वहते (*vahate*)—brings along (his wife)
- इयं वधूः (*iyaṃ vadhūḥ*)—this wife
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—her husband Indra
- इच्छंती (*icchaṃtī*)—wishing that he should go toward the sacrifice
- एति (*eti*)—follows him and goes
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this same Indra
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—the chariot
- आ (*ā*)—all around
- श्रवस्यात् (*śravasyāt*)—wishes food (for the sacrificer)
- आ च घोषात् (*ā ca ghoṣāt*)—makes sound all around
- पुरु (*puru*)—exceedingly
- सहस्रा (*sahasrā*)—immeasurably
- परि (*pari*)—all around
- वर्तयते (*vartayate*)—provides (the wealth)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wife of the Indra who brings his companion, his chief queen, wishing that her husband Indra should go toward the sacrifice, follows him. The chariot of that same Indra wishes food for the sacrificer all around and makes sound all around. It provides all around wealth that is exceedingly abundant and immeasurable.

### Printed p. 297

##### English translation
The bride (of Indra), devoted to her lord, attends, him (to the rite), who thus brings (with him) his accompanying queen : may his car convey to us ample food; may it sound loudly ; may it scatter around many thousands (of riches).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk there is a description of Indra's wife following Indra, sitting with Indra in the chariot, and coming to the place of sacrifice. Ordinarily, in sacrifices and the like, it is the custom to invite Indra alone for the drinking of Soma. But in this Ṛk the meaning is implied that Indra and his wife Indrāṇī come in a chariot that is able to give food and the like, that makes a sound by the turning of its wheels as it moves, and that gives wealth and the like without number to those who worship Indra.

महिषी (*mahiṣī*)—The word mahiṣa is read among the names for "great" (Ni. 2-13) and indicates the sense "large, of great form". Therefore the word mahiṣī can be given the senses "worshipful, excellent".

वधूः (*vadhūḥ*)—The word vadhū is read among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24). Ordinarily the word vadhū is customarily used in the sense of a woman who has a young husband and is married. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न स राजा॑ व्यथते॒ यस्मि॒न्निंद्र॑स्ती॒व्रं सोमं॒ पिब॑ति॒ गोस॑खायं ।  
> आ स॑त्त्व॒नैरज॑ति॒ हंति॑ वृ॒त्रं क्षेति॑ क्षि॒तीः सु॒भगो॒ नाम॒ पुष्य॑न् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । सः । राजा । व्यथते । यस्मिन् । इंद्रः । तीव्रं । सोमं । पिबति । गोऽसखायं ।  
> आ । सत्त्वनैः । अजति । हंति । न तं । क्षेति । क्षितीः । सुभगो । नाम । पुष्यन् ॥ ८ ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ । सत्वनैः । अजति । हंति । वृत्रं । क्षेति । क्षितीः । सुभगः । नाम । पुष्यन् ॥ ४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The block gives only a word-by-word line of the second half of the Ṛk, with the number 4, and no explanation by Sāyaṇa. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 298

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स राजा न व्यथते । व्यथितो न भवति । यस्मिन्राजनि तदीये यज्ञ इंद्रस्तीव्रं मदजनकं सोमं पिबति गोसखायं । विकारे प्रकृतिशब्दः क्षीरादिमिश्रणवंतं । स राजा सत्वनैः सत्वभिरनुचरैरा सर्वतोजति । गच्छति । हुति च वृत्रं पापं
> वैरिणं वा । क्षेति गच्छति क्षितीः प्रजाः । अथवा क्षितीर्निवासान्निवसते । सुभगः
> शोभनसुखो नाम नामकं धनमिंद्रस्य स्तोत्रं वा पुष्यन् पोषयन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: That king is not afflicted; he does not become troubled, in whose realm, that is, in whose sacrifice, Indra drinks the sharp, intoxicating Soma. The word *gosakhāyam* is a case of using the name of the original substance for its product: it means Soma mixed with milk and the like. That king, with his *satvans*, that is, with his attendants, goes about everywhere. He also destroys Vṛtra, that is, sin, or else the enemy. He dwells among the *kṣitīḥ*, the subjects; or else *kṣitīḥ* are dwellings, and he dwells in dwellings. *Subhaga* means one of fair happiness; *nāma* means the name, that is, wealth, or a hymn of praise of Indra; *puṣyan* means nourishing it. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in whose sacrifice, that of which king
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- तीव्रं (*tīvraṃ*)—intoxicating
- गोसखायं (*gosakhāyaṃ*)—mixed with milk
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- पिबति (*pibati*)—drinks
- स राजा (*sa rājā*)—that king
- न व्यथते (*na vyathate*)—does not become afflicted
- सत्वनैः (*satvanaiḥ*)—with his attendants
- आ (*ā*)—all around (fearlessly)
- अजति (*ajati*)—can move about
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the enemy
- हुति (*huti*)—destroys
- सुभगः (*subhagaḥ*)—enjoying excellent happiness
- नाम (*nāma*)—the name of Indra
- पुष्यन् (*puṣyan*)—praising
- क्षितीः (*kṣitīḥ*)—his subjects
- क्षेति (*kṣeti*)—makes them dwell happily

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The king in whose sacrifice Indra drinks the intoxicating Soma juice mixed with milk is not afflicted. With his attendants he can move about everywhere without fear of enemies. He destroys his enemies. And while he himself enjoys excellent happiness, praising the divine names of Indra, he also carries on the government in such a way that his subjects live well.

##### English translation
That prince suffers no evil in whose realm Indra drinks the sharp Soma juice mixed with milk : attended by faithful (followers), he moves (in all directions) : he destroys his enemy, he protects his subjects : enjoying prosperity, he cherishes the name of (Indra).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गोसखायं (*gosakhāyaṃ*)—क्षीरादिमिश्रणवंतं (*kṣīrādimiśraṇavaṃtaṃ*). Here the word *go* is used to denote milk. The meaning is Soma juice mixed with milk. There is also the practice of purifying the Soma juice and drinking it just so, without mixing anything with it; such Soma is called *tīvra*. And in order to make the Soma juice tasty, substances such as milk, curds and flour are mixed with it. These

### Printed p. 299

substances are called *āśira* substances. Soma juice mixed with milk is called *gavāśira*, Soma juice mixed with curds *dadhyāśira*, and Soma juice mixed with flour *yavāśira*. In the present Ṛk it is stated that Indra drinks the Soma juice mixed with milk, called *gavāśira*.

The fruits that come to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice when Indra is satisfied by the drinking of Soma are described in this Ṛk. The king in whose sacrifice Indra, invited and arrived, drinks the Soma juice offered by the priests so as to be satisfied, suffers no kind of sorrow. Many attendants, servants and others, resort to him. He overcomes his enemies in battle, enjoys many kinds of happiness, and protects his subjects so that they live happily. Thus the greatness of Indra's Soma-drinking is described in this Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पुष्प्या॒त् क्षेमे॑ अ॒भि योगे॑ भवात्यु॒भे वृत्॑ संय॒ुती सं  ॑
> जयाति ।  
> प्रि॒यः सूर्ये॑ प्रि॒यो अ॒ग्ना भ॑वाति॒ य इंद्रा॑य सु॒तसो॑मो॒ ददा॑शत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुष्यात् । क्षेमे । अभि । योगे । भवाति । उभे इति । वृतौ । संयती इति संयती । सं । जयाति ।  
> प्रियः । सूर्ये । प्रियः । अग्ना । भवाति । यः । इंद्राय । सुतसोमः ।  
> ददाशत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुष्यात् पोषयेद्बंध्वादीन् । क्षेमे प्राप्तस्य धनस्य रक्षणे योगेऽलब्धस्य
> प्राप्ता चाभि भवाति । भवति । अभीत्यनर्थको धात्वर्थानुवादी वा । प्रभुर्भवती-

### Printed p. 300

> त्यर्थः । तथोभे वृत् वर्तमाने संयती नियते अहोरात्रे सं जयाति ।
> सम्यक् जयति । ते सुखकरे स्यातामित्यर्थः । किंच स प्रियो भवति सूर्ये तथाग्नाग्नौ प्रियो भवति य इंद्राय सुतसोमो ददाशत् सोमं ददाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: *Puṣyāt* means that he would nourish his kinsmen and others. *Kṣeme* means in the protection of wealth already obtained; *yoge* means in the acquiring of what has not been obtained; he becomes (*abhi bhavāti* means *bhavati*; the word *abhi* is either without meaning or repeats the sense of the root) the master of both; this is the meaning, that he becomes lord. Likewise he conquers well the two, day and night, which are present and regulated; the meaning is that they would be happy for him. Further, he who gives Soma to Indra, that is, offers the pressed Soma, becomes dear in the sun and likewise dear in Agni.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—whoever
- सुतसोमः (*sutasomaḥ*)—pressing out Soma juice
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- ददाशत् (*dadāśat*)—offers it (he)
- पुष्यात् (*puṣyāt*)—nourishes (his kinsmen and friends)
- क्षेमे (*kṣeme*)—in the protection of wealth
- योगे (*yoge*)—in the obtaining of new wealth
- अभि भवाति (*abhi bhavāti*)—becomes capable
- उभे वृता (*ubhe vṛtā*)—in the past, present and future (always) **NOTE**
- संयुती (*saṃyutī*)—in day and night of regulated course
- सं जयाति (*saṃ jayāti*)—wins complete victory
- सूर्ये (*sūrye*)—to the sun
- प्रियः भवति (*priyaḥ bhavati*)—becomes dear
- अग्ना (*agnā*)—to Agni
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—becomes dear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Whoever presses out Soma juice and offers it to Indra nourishes his kinsmen and friends. He becomes capable of protecting the wealth he has and of obtaining new wealth. In the past, the future and the present, and in the days and nights of regulated course, he wins complete victory. He becomes dear to the sun and to Agni.

##### English translation
He cherishes (his kin) ; he (reigns) in welfare and prosperity ; he is victorious in present and continuous ( time ) : dear is he to the sun, dear to Agni, who, with prepared libation, offers it to Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As said in the previous Ṛk, in this Ṛk too the great nature of Indra's Soma-drinking and the fruits that come from it are described. But here no particular person is indicated by the word king. It can apply to any man who performs a sacrifice.

## Sūkta 38 (Maṇḍala 5)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उरोष्ट इति पंचर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तमत्रेरार्षमानुष्टुभमैंद्रं । उरोरानुष्टुभमित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: The sixth sūkta, उरोष्ट इति (*uroṣṭa iti*), has five ṛks; its seer is Atri, its metre is Anuṣṭubh and its deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā says: उरोरानुष्टुभमित्यनुक्रांतं (*urorānuṣṭubhamityanukrāṃtaṃ*). The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Translation of the Anuvāda: This sūkta, उरोष्टे (*uroṣṭe*), is the sixth sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are five ṛks in it. The seer of this sūkta is Atri; Indra is the deity; the metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: उरोरानुष्टुभं (*urorānuṣṭubhaṃ*). The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Sūkta: Khila. **NOTE**

Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 38.

Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 2, Varga 9.

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5.

Seer: Atri.

Deity: Indra.

Metre: Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒रोष्ट॑ इंद्र॒ राध॑सो वि॒भ्वी रा॒तिः श॑तक्रतो ।  
> अधा॑ नो विश्वचर्षणे द्यु॒म्ना सु॑क्षत्र मंहय ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उरोः । ते । इंद्र । राधसः । विभ्वीरातिः । शतक्रतो इति शतक्रतो ।  
> अध । नः । विश्वचर्षणे । द्युम्ना । सुक्षत्र । मंहय ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र शतक्रतो बहुकर्मन् ते तवोरोः प्रभूतस्य राधसो धनस्य
> रातिर्दानं विभ्वी महती । अधातः कारणात् नोऽस्मभ्यं हे विश्वचर्षणे सर्वॆस्य

### Printed p. 302

> द्रष्टः सुक्षत्र शोभनधनेंद्र । क्षत्रमिति धननाम । द्युम्ना द्युम्नानि धनानि मंहय ।
> प्रयच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra of a hundred acts, that is, of many deeds, the gift of your abundant wealth is great. For that reason, to us, O all-seeing one, O Indra of excellent wealth (*kṣatra* is a name for wealth), bestow riches (*dyumna* means wealth); *mamhaya* means give.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O doer of many deeds
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- उरोः (*uroḥ*)—abundant
- राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)—of wealth
- रातिः (*rātiḥ*)—the gift
- विभ्वी (*vibhvī*)—exceedingly great
- अध (*adha*)—therefore
- विश्वचर्षषे (*viśvacarṣaṣe*)—all-beholder
- सुकृत्र (*sukṛtra*)—possessor of excellent wealth, O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*)—the wealth of riches
- मंहय (*maṃhaya*)—bestow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, doer of many deeds, the gift of your abundant wealth is of great glory. Therefore, O Indra, all-beholder and possessor of excellent wealth, bestow wealth and riches upon us.

##### English translation
Indra of many exploits, liberal is the distribution of your abundant riches: therefore, all-beholder, possessor of excellent wealth, bestow upon us opulence.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—बहुकर्मन् (*bahukarman*). One who has done many deeds; that is, one who has done many daring deeds that cannot be done by anyone else, such as the slaying of Vṛtra. Such is the intention. Here the word *śata* must be understood as "many". The word *kratu* means deed, a daring act. A daring act that can be done by the use of strength, valour and courage is called *kratu*, and because Indra has done many such deeds, the calling of Indra also by the word *śatakratu* is specially in use in the Ṛgveda.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदी॑मिंद्र श्र॒वाय्य॒मिषं॑ शविष्ठ दधि॒षे ।  
> प॒प्र॒थे दी॑र्घ॒श्रुत्त॑मं॒ हिर॑ण्यवर्ण दु॒ष्टरं॑ ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 303

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । ईं । इंद्र । श्रवाय्यं । इषं । शविष्ठ । दधिषे ।  
> पप्रथे । दीर्घश्रुत्तमं । हिरण्यवर्ण । दुस्तरं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र शविष्ठ अतिशयेन बलवन् यदिषमन्नं श्रवाय्यं श्रवणीयमीं
> सर्वतो दधिषे धारयसि ददासि ना ॥ इषशब्दो नपुंसकलिंगोऽप्यस्ति ॥ हे हिरण्यवर्णेंद्र तदन्नं पप्रथे । प्रथते । कथं । दीर्घश्रुत्तममतिदूरश्रवणीयतमं ।
> सर्वत्र कीर्त्यमित्यर्थः । दुष्टरमनभिभाव्यमुक्तलक्षणं प्रथते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, O most mighty, the food (*iṣa*) that is *śravāyya*, that is, worthy of being heard, you hold on all sides and give. The word *iṣa* also occurs in the neuter gender. **NOTE** O golden-hued Indra, that food spreads. How? Most widely heard, that is, to be celebrated everywhere. It spreads as unconquerable, having the stated character.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शविष्ठ (*śaviṣṭha*)—most mighty
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—even if
- श्रवाय्यं (*śravāyyaṃ*)—exceedingly well known
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- ईं (*īṃ*)—everywhere
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you hold
- हिरण्यवर्ण (*hiraṇyavarṇa*)—O Indra of golden-coloured form
- दुष्टरं (*duṣṭaraṃ*)—that to obtain that food is very difficult
- दीर्घश्रुत्थमं (*dīrghaśrutthamaṃ*)—so as to be heard everywhere
- पप्रथे (*paprathe*)—it is renowned

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O most mighty Indra, it is known to everyone that you hold food that is very well known and abundant. Yet, O golden-hued Indra, it is so renowned as to be heard everywhere that obtaining that food is a very laborious task.

##### English translation
Although, most mighty Indra, you possess well-known abundance (of food), yet golden-hued (deity) it is most notoriously reported as difficult (to be procured).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ईं (*īṃ*)—The word *īm* is well known as a particle (*nipāta*). On this word Yāska says: अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रंथेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छंति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्विति ॥ (*atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu graṃtheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchaṃti padapūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidviti ‖*) (Ni. 1-9)

### Printed p. 304

That is, the particles *kam*, *ī*, *it*, *u* have no definite meaning of their own. It is said that these words are used in prose works for completing the sentence, and in metrical Ṛks and the like for completing the pāda. The pādas of metres (a pāda is a part of the metre, generally a quarter) must have a fixed number of syllables. In some cases, when a pāda is short by one syllable, one of these particles is used to fill out the pāda; therefore it is said that these particles are used for completing the words. Besides this, another kind of meaning may also result. Here the word *īm* has the sense "everywhere, on all sides". In some places the sense of the word *eva* is also given, and so on.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शुष्मा॑सो॒ ये ते॑ अद्रिवो मे॒हना॑ केत॒सापः॑ ।  
> उ॒भा दे॒वाव॒भिष्ट॑ये दि॒वश्च॒ ग्मश्च॑ राजथः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुष्मासः । ये । ते । अद्रिवः । मेहना । केतसापः ।  
> उभा । देवौ । अभिष्टये । दिवः । च। गृः । च । राजथः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अद्रिवो वज्रवन्निंद्र ते त्वदीया ये शुष्मासो बलभूता मरुतः
> संति । कीदृशास्ते । मेहना मंहनीयाः केतसापः प्रज्ञापकं कर्मांतरिक्षं वा
> स्पृशंतः । उभौ देवौ त्वं च मरुत्समूहश्चेत्सु भौ युवां दिवश्च द्युलोकात्
> ग्मश्च भूमेः सकाशादभिष्टयेऽभितो गमनाय राजथः । ईशाथे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, those *śuṣmas* of yours, that is, the Maruts who are your strength, are such as are *mehanā*, worthy of praise, and *ketasāpaḥ*, touching the rite that makes known, or touching the sky. Both gods, you and the host of the Maruts **NOTE**, rule from heaven and from earth, for going on all sides; *rājathaḥ* means "you two rule".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt
- मेहना (*mehanā*)—worthy of worship
- केतसापः (*ketasāpaḥ*)—having rites that make known
- ते (*te*)—to you
- शुष्मासः (*śuṣmāsaḥ*)—givers of strength
- ये (*ye*)—whichever Maruts there are (they)
- उभा देवौ (*ubhā devau*)—you and the host of the Maruts, who are of divine nature
- दिवश्च (*divaśca*)—from the world of heaven
- ग्मश्च (*gmaśca*)—and from the earth
- अभिष्टये (*abhiṣṭaye*)—to come to this place of sacrifice **NOTE**
- राजथः (*rājathaḥ*)—you shine as lords

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, the Maruts who are worthy of worship, who have rites that make known and who give you strength, and you together with them, you who are of divine nature, being in the highest station, shine as lords of all heaven and earth.

### Printed p. 305

##### English translation
Wielder of the thunderbolt, yours are the strong (Maruts), who are adorable, and whose exploits are renowned : both divinities, you and they) rule at pleasure over heaven and earth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—The word *adri* is stated among the names of the thunderbolt, among the names of the cloud (Ni. 2.2) and among the names of the mountain. *Adri* means the stone called *grāvā* that crushes the Soma plant.

मेहना (*mehanā*)—On this word Yāska stated the meaning "*mehanā* is *maṃhanīya*", that is, worthy of worship, and in support of it gave as an example the Ṛk beginning यदिंद्र चित्र (*yadiṃdra citra*).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒तो नो॑ अ॒स्य कस्य॑ चि॒द्दक्ष॑स्य॒ तव॑ वृत्रहन् ।  
> अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ नृ॒म्लमा भ॑रा॒स्मभ्यं॑ नृमणस्यसे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उतो इति । नः । अस्य । कस्य । चित् । दक्षस्य । तव । वृत्तहन् ।  
> अस्मभ्यं । नृम्णं । आ । भर । अस्मभ्यं । नृमनस्यसे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतो अपि च हे वृत्रहन्निंद्र नोऽस्मभ्यं कस्य चिदनिर्देश्यस्य दक्षस्य प्रवृद्धस्य
> दातुर्वास्य तव स्वभूतेभ्योऽस्मभ्यं । पुनःश्रुतिरादरार्था । नृण्नं नृमणु धनमा
> भर । आहर । हे इंद्र यतस्त्वमस्मभ्यं नृमणस्यसे धनमिच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: And also, O Vṛtra-slayer Indra, to us, who are your own, bring (*ā bhara* means "fetch") the wealth (*nṛmṇa* is wealth) of some unspecified person who is *dakṣa*, that is, grown great, or a giver; the repetition of "to us" is for emphasis. O Indra, since you desire wealth for us (*nṛmaṇasyase* means "you wish wealth").

O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, bring to us, who belong to you, the wealth of someone abounding in wealth. You certainly wish that wealth be obtained by us.

नृम्मं (*nṛmmaṃ*)—The word *nṛmṇa* is read among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शतक्रतो इंद्र ते तवाभिरभिष्टिभिरभिगमनैर्नु शीघ्रं समृद्धा भवेमेति
> शेषः । हे इंद्र तव शर्मन् शर्मणि सुखी सति सुगोपाः स्याम ! भवेम । हे
> शूर तव शर्मणि सुगोपाः शोभनरक्षणाः स्याम । भवेम । पुनरुक्तिरादरार्था ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra of a hundred acts, by your approaches (*abhiṣṭi* means going towards), may we quickly become prosperous; the verb "may we become" is what is to be supplied. O Indra, being happy in your shelter (*śarman*), may we be well protected, may we be. O hero, in your shelter may we be well protected, that is, well guarded; may we be. The repetition is for emphasis.
