> इति संबंधः । किमर्थं । राय एषे धनानि प्राप्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I worship, that is, I praise, you, who have many to nourish, the leaders of food and rites.**NOTE** Who are you? He says: Vāstoṣpati and Tvaṣṭṛ, whom I, delighting with praises and the like, or giving oblations, worship; the giver of wealth, who goes together with the other gods and gratifies them, the Dhiṣaṇā, that is Speech, the goddess of speech.**NOTE** These words, standing in the first case, are used in the sense of the second case. The construction is: I worship, together with salutations, the speech so described, the lords of the forest and the herbs. For what purpose? To obtain riches, that is, to attain wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*)—I who recite praise and the like
- पोष्यावतः (*poṣyāvataḥ*)—who nourish many people
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—and who carry out rites such as sacrifices
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you (that is)
- वास्तोष्पतिं (*vāstoṣpatiṃ*)—the deity named Vāstoṣpati
- त्वष्टारं (*tvaṣṭāraṃ*)—Tvaṣṭṛ
- धन्या (*dhanyā*)—the giver of wealth
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—who has equal affection with the other gods
- धिषणा (*dhiṣaṇā*)—the goddess of speech
- वनस्पतीन् (*vanaspatīn*)—the deities presiding over trees, or the trees
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the herbs, such as trees and creepers,

### Printed p. 374
  or the deities that preside over them
- रायः एषे (*rāyaḥ eṣe*)—for the obtaining of wealth
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with salutations or with praises
- अर्चे (*arce*)—I worship or I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I who recite praises worship you, who nourish people and lead rites such as sacrifices: that is, the deity named Vāstoṣpati; the goddess of speech, the giver of wealth, who is affectionate together with the other gods; and the trees, the creepers and the climbers, or the deities who preside over them, with recitation of praises, salutations and the like, for the obtaining of wealth.

##### English translation
I glorify you, leaders (of rites), cherishers (of many), gratifying (with oblations, you) Twashtri the lord of foundations, and the goddess of speech, bestower of opulence, and sharer in the satisfaction (of the other divinities); also the lords of the forest, and the herbs, that I may obtain riches.
#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तु॒जे न॒स्तने॒ पर्व॑ताः संतु॒ स्वैत॑वो॒ ये वस॑वो॒ न वी॒राः ।  
> प॒नि॒त आ॒प्त्यो य॑ज॒तः सदा॑ नो॒ वर्धा॑न्नः॒ शंसं॒ नर्यो॑  ॒॑
> अभिष्टौ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तुजे । नः । तने । पर्वताः । संतु । स्वएतवः । ये । वसवः । न । वीराः ।  
> पनितः । आप्त्यः । यजतः । सदा । नः । वर्धात् । नः । शंसं । नर्यः । अभिष्टौ ॥९॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पर्वताः पर्ववंतः पूरणवंतो ना मेघास्तने विस्त्रते तुजे दाने ।
> यद्वा । तनेति पुत्रनाम ॥ षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी ॥ पुत्रस्य दान इत्यर्थः । अथवा
> नस्तुजे पुत्रे तने तत्पुत्रे च स्वैतवः शोभनगमनाः संतु । भवंतु । कीदृशास्ते ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The पर्वताः (*parvatāḥ*) are those having joints, that is, full ones: the clouds. तने (*tane*) means extended; तुजे (*tuje*) means in giving. Or else: तने (*tane*) is a name for son, and the fourth case stands in the sense of the sixth: the meaning is in the giving of a son. Or again: may they be of good going, in our तुजे (*tuje*), our son, and in तने (*tane*), his son. What are they like?

### Printed p. 375

> ये वसवो जगतो वासयितारो वीरा न वीरा इव । किंच पनितः स्तुत आप्त
> आप्तव्यः सर्वैर्यजतो यजनीय आदित्यः सदा सर्वदा नः शंसमस्माकं स्तुतिं
> नर्यो नरेभ्यो हितो देवोऽभिष्टावभित एषणेऽभिगमने वा सति वर्धात् ।
> वर्धयेत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They are the Vasus, who make the world dwell, like heroes. Moreover, the Āditya, praised, to be obtained by all, adorable, beneficial to men, may always increase our praise, that is, make it grow, when there is longing or approach on every side.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which clouds
- वीरा न (*vīrā na*)—like heroes
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—such as give the world its dwelling
- पर्वताः (*parvatāḥ*)—the clouds
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- तने (*tane*)—very extensive
- तुजे (*tuje*)—for the giving (of water)
- स्वैतवः (*svaitavaḥ*)—of excellent motion
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—may they be
- पनितः (*panitaḥ*)—praised by all
- आप्त्यः (*āptyaḥ*)—easily attained by all
- यजतः (*yajataḥ*)—worthy of worship, the Āditya
- नर्यः (*naryaḥ*)—beneficial to all men
- अभिष्टा (*abhiṣṭā*)—while he pervades all around
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- शंसं (*śaṃsaṃ*)—praise
- वर्धात् (*vardhāt*)—may he increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May those clouds which, like heroes, give the world its dwelling, move excellently so as to give us water in great abundance. May the Āditya, praised by all, easily attained by all, worthy of worship, beneficial to all men, increase our praise while he pervades all around.

##### English translation
May the Parvatas be (bountiful) to us in liberal donations; may they be favourable (to us) who are the establishers (of the world) like heroes; may the adored and adorable (deity), who is accessible (to all), who is friendly to man, ever grant us increase, being propitiated by our praise.
#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृष्णो॑ अस्तोषि भू॒म्यस्य॒ गर्भं॑ त्रि॒तो नपा॑तम॒पां सु॑वृ॒क्ति ।  
> गृ॒णी॒ते अ॒ग्निरे॒तरी॒ न शू॒ष्यैः शो॒चिष्के॑शो॒ नि रि॑णाति॒ वना॑ ॥१०॥

### Printed p. 376

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृष्णः । अस्तोषि । भूम्यस्य । गर्भं । त्रितः । नपातं । अपां । सुवृक्ति ।  
> गृणीते । अग्निः । एतरि । नः । शूषैः । शोचिःकेशः । नि । रिणाति । वना ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भूम्यस्य । भूमिरंतरिक्षं । तदर्हस्य । तादृशस्य वृष्णो वर्षकस्य पर्जन्यस्य
> अथवा भूम्यो भूमेरेवार्हः तदुचितवृष्टि प्रदानात् । तादृशस्य मेघस्य गर्भं
> गर्भस्थानीयमपां नपातं रक्षकं वैद्युतमग्निं सुवृक्ति । स्तोत्रकर्मैतत् ।
> शोभनपापादिवर्जनवता स्तोत्रेणास्तोषि । स्तुतवानहं । स त्रितस्तीर्णतमस्त्रिषु
> स्थानेष्टन्येषु त्रित्वापन्नेषु तायमानोऽग्निरेतरि गंतरि मयि शूषैः सुखकरै
> रश्मिभिर्न गृणीते । न गरणं कुरुते । न क्रुद्यतीत्यर्थः । किंतुशोचिष्केशः प्रदीप्तरश्मिः
> सन् वना वनानि नि रिणाति । हिनस्ति । दहतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

भूम्यस्य (*bhūmyasya*): भूमि (*bhūmi*) is the firmament; भूम्यस्य (*bhūmyasya*) means worthy of it. Of such a rain-giving Parjanya, or: भूम्यो (*bhūmyo*) means worthy of the earth alone, because he gives rain fitting to it. Of such a cloud, the embryo, that stands in the place of the womb, the protector of the waters, the lightning-fire, सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*), a word of praise: with praise that has avoided sin and the like, I have praised him. That Trita, who has crossed over most, who is preserved in the three places, the others having become threefold,**NOTE** Agni, does not गृणीते (*gṛṇīte*), that is, does not roar, with comfort-giving rays, at me, who go to him: that is, he does not become angry. But, with blazing rays as his hair, he नि रिणाति (*ni riṇāti*) the forests, that is, harms them: the meaning is that he burns them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भूम्यस्य (*bhūmyasya*)—of him who dwells in the firmament
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—and who causes rain, to Parjanya
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—who is as an embryo
- अपां नपातं (*apāṃ napātaṃ*)—the protector of the waters, the lightning-fire
- सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*)—by well-composed praise
- अस्तोषि (*astoṣi*)—I have praised
- त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)—who is in the three places, the earth and the rest
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- एतरि (*etari*)—upon me, who go near him
- शूषैः (*śūṣaiḥ*)—with comfort-giving rays
- न गृणीते (*na gṛṇīte*)—does not show anger (but)
- शोचिष्केशः (*śociṣkeśaḥ*)—having blazing rays
- वना (*vanā*)—the forests
- नि रिणाति (*ni riṇāti*)—he burns

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have praised, with well-composed praise, the lightning-fire, who dwells in the firmament, is as an embryo to the rain-giving Parjanya and is the protector of the waters. Agni, who is in the three places, the earth and the rest, does not show anger with his comfort-giving rays at me, who approach him with devotion. But, with blazing rays as his hair, he burns all the forests.

##### English translation
I glorify with unqualified praise the embryo of the earth-fertilizing rain, the grandson of the waters, Agni, who is threefold, who rages (upon

### Printed p. 377
me) not, when travelling, with (his) withering rays, but, bright-haired. consumes the forests.
#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क॒था म॒हे रु॒द्रिया॑य ब्रवाम॒ कद्रा॒ये चि॑कि॒तुषे॒ भगा॑य।  
> आप॒ ओष॑धीरु॒त नो॑ऽवंतु॒ द्यौर्वना॑ गि॒रयो॑ वृ॒क्षके॑शाः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कथा । महे । रुद्रियाय । ब्रवाम । कत् । राये । चिकितुषे । भगाय ।  
> आपः । ओषधीः । उत । नः । अवंतु । द्यौः । वना । गिरयः।वृक्षकेशाः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयमत्रयः कथा केन प्रकारेण महे महते रुद्रियाय रुद्रपुत्राय
> मरुद्धणाय ब्रवाम स्तुतीः । कत् किं च स्तोत्रं राये धनलाभाय चिकितुषे
> सर्वं जानते भगाय्कॆतन्नामकाय देवाय ब्रवाम । उतापि चापोऽद्भवता
> ओषधीरोषधयो द्यार्द्यदेवता वना वनानि गिरयो वृक्षकेशाः । वृक्षा एव केशस्थानीया येषां ते । एता उक्ता देवता नोऽस्मानवंतु । रक्षंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, the Atris: in what manner shall we speak praises to the great रुद्रियाय (*rudriyāya*), the son of Rudra, the host of the Maruts? And what praise shall we speak, for the gaining of wealth, to the all-knowing deity named Bhaga? Moreover, may the waters, the herbs, Dyu the deity of heaven, the woods, and the mountains whose tresses are trees, that is, those whose hair is the trees themselves, these deities named, protect us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राये (*rāye*)—so that wealth may come to us
- महे (*mahe*)—worthy of worship
- रुद्रियाय (*rudriyāya*)—to the host of the Maruts, the sons of Rudra
- कथा (*kathā*)—in what manner
- ब्रवाम (*bravāma*)—shall we offer praise?
- चिकितुषे (*cikituṣe*)—all-knowing
- भगाय (*bhagāya*)—to Bhaga
- कत् (*kat*)—what praise shall we recite?
- उत (*uta*)—and
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the deities of the waters
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the herbs
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the deity presiding over the heaven
- वृक्षकेशाः (*vṛkṣakeśāḥ*)—having trees for hair
- गिरयः (*girayaḥ*)—the mountains
- वना (*vanā*)—the woods
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*)—may they protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In what manner shall we offer praise to the worshipful host of the Maruts, the sons of Rudra, so that wealth may come to us? What praise shall we recite to the all-knowing Bhaga? And

### Printed p. 378
the deities of the waters, the herbs, the deity presiding over the heaven, and the mountains and woods that have trees for hair, may they protect us.

##### English translation
How can we offer (fit praise) to the mighty posterity of Rudra, or to the all-knowing Bhaga, for (the sake of obtaining) riches? may the waters, may the plants, protect us, and the heaven, the woods, and the mountains, whose tresses are trees.
#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शृ॒णोतु॑ न ऊ॒र्जां पति॒र्गिरः॒ स नभ॒स्तरी॑या इषि॒रः परि॑ज्मा।  
> शृ॒ण्वंत्वापः॒ पुरो॒ न शु॒भ्राः परि॒ स्रुचो॑ बबृहा॒णस्याद्रॆः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शृणोतु । नः । ऊर्जां । पतिः । गिरः । सः । नभः । तरीयान् । इषिरः । परिज्मा ।  
> शृण्वंतु । आपः । पुरः । न । शुभ्राः । परि । स्रुचः । बबृहाणस्य । अद्रेः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्माकं गिरः स्तुतीः शृणोतु । कः । ऊर्जां बलानां पतिर्वायुः ।
> अथवा ऊर्जामन्नानां पतिः । प्राणोपाधिकस्य वायोः कृत्सात्तत्वं प्रसिद्धं ।
> श्रुतिश्च भवति । प्राणस्यान्नमिदं सर्वं प्रजापतिरकल्पयत् । मनु. ५-२८ । इति । स
> नभो नभसि चारी तरीयान् तरितव्य इषिरो गमनशीलः परिज्मा परितो गंता ।
> किंचापः शृण्वंतु गिरः । कीदृश्यस्ताः । पुरो न पुराणीव शुभ्रा दीप्ता बबृहाणस्य
> वर्धमानस्याद्रेर्मघस्य ना पर्वतस्य वा परि परितः स्पुचः सरणशीलाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the lord of strengths, Vāyu, hear our praises. Or else: the lord of ऊर्जामन्नानां (*ūrjāmannānāṃ*), of foods. That Vāyu, under the limitation of breath, is the eater of all is well known,**NOTE** and there is the Śruti: प्राणस्यान्नमिदं सर्वं प्रजापतिरकल्पयत् (*prāṇasyānnamidaṃ sarvaṃ prajāpatirakalpayat*) (Manu. 5-28). He moves in the sky, is तरीयान् (*tarīyān*), to be crossed over, इषिरः (*iṣiraḥ*), given to motion, परिज्मा (*parijmā*), one who goes all round. Moreover, may the waters hear the praises. What are they like? Bright, shining like cities, flowing all round, of the growing mountain or cloud.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नभः (*nabhaḥ*)—in the firmament
- तरीयान् (*tarīyān*)—who moves about
- इषिरः (*iṣiraḥ*)—who is (always) in motion
- परिज्मा (*parijmā*)—who pervades all around
- ऊर्जां (*ūrjāṃ*)—of all powers
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—the lord
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Vāyu
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—praises
- शृणोतु (*śṛṇotu*)—may he hear
- बबृहाणस्य (*babṛhāṇasya*)—**NOTE**

### Printed p. 379
  very lofty and grown
- अद्रेः (*adreḥ*)—of the mountain
- परि (*pari*)—around
- स्रुचः (*srucaḥ*)—flowing
- पुरो न (*puro na*)—like cities
- शुभ्राः (*śubhrāḥ*)—shining
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- शृण्वंतु (*śṛṇvaṃtu*)—may they hear (our praises)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Vāyu, who moves in the firmament, is always in motion, pervades all around and is lord of all powers, hear our praises. May the waters also, which flow around the exceedingly lofty mountain and shine like cities, hear our praises.

##### English translation
May the lord of vigour, (Vayu), hear our prayers; he who traverses the firmament, the circumambient: may the waters hear, bright as cities, flowing round the towering mountains.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒दा चि॒न्नु म॑हांतो॒ ये व॒ एवा॒ ब्रवा॑म दस्मा॒ वार्यं॒  ॑
> दधानाः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

My praise is placed, that is, laid down, offered, on the ground at every step, at each time. And that praise, being powerful, with its protections, becomes the warder-off of troubles that come upon us; the word वा (*vā*) is in the sense of "and". May the mother, the maker of all, great, worthy of worship, the essence, the Earth, attend our praise; or else, being praised, may she attend to us. The word स्मत् (*smat*) expresses praise: by reason of the praises of the wise praisers, that is, pleased by acquaintance with them, may she be straight-handed, that is, with a hand favourable to us, and a giver of good gifts.

- वायुभिः (*vāyubhiḥ*)—with protections

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From time to time our praise is offered. That same praise, being powerful, becomes with its protections the remover of troubles. May the Earth, the maker of all, great and full of essence, attend to our praise (hear it). Pleased by the praises of the praisers, may she be of a hand favourable to us and of a beneficial gift.

##### English translation
My praise has been continually proffered as a protectress, powerful with (the means of) preservation: may the maternal and venerable earth accept our (praises), and, (pleased) with her pious (worshippers) be (to us) straight-handed, and the giver of good.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In what manner shall we serve, that is, wait upon, with praise or with food, the Maruts of good gifts? In the manner thus being carried out, with a speech addressed to them as the occasion, how shall we serve those Maruts? The sense is that they are hard to propitiate. How are they possessors of excellent food, in me whose praise is an utterance that goes towards them? Or else: when there is praise from me, who have excellent food, in what manner shall we serve the Maruts? The repetition is for respect. May the god Ahirbudhnya not set us to the harmful one, that is, not establish us there; may that god be ours, the slayer of enemies.

- उपमातिवनिः (*upamātivaniḥ*)—the slayer of enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

With what praise shall I worship the Maruts, who are exceedingly generous? Or: when I am ready with the most excellent praise, in what manner shall I make them recipients of the excellent oblation? May the god Ahirbudhnya not give us up to the harmful enemy. May he be the slayer of our enemies.

##### English translation
How may be (duly) worship the liberal (Maruts) with praise, how adore the Maruts with present praise in a fitting manner, the glorious Maruts with present praise? may Ahirbudhnya contrive not for our harm ; may he be the destroyer (of our enemies).

### Printed p. 385

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Nirukta-writers regard the deity named Ahirbudhnya as a deity of the middle region (antarikṣa). The word *ahi* ordinarily means a serpent; it is read among the names of the cloud and also among the names of water (Ni. 2-21; 2-24). But when the nature of the deity Ahirbudhnya is to be stated, what connection is there between the cloud and water? And what is the reason that this deity bears this name? These questions must be examined.

For the word *ahi* alone, the Nirukta-writers give the derivation अहिः अयनात् एति अंतरिक्षे (*ahiḥ ayanāt eti aṃtarikṣe*), that is, because it moves about in the middle region, the cloud is the meaning of *ahi*; and then अयमपीतरोऽहिरेतस्मादेव निर्ह्रसित उपसर्ग आहंतीति । (*ayamapītaro 'hiretasmādeva nirhrasita upasarga āhaṃtīti |*): in the sense of a serpent too the derivation is the same. But the meaning "one that strikes with its hood" is also possible; (आहंत्यसौ भोगेन इत्यादिः (*āhaṃtyasau bhogena ityādiḥ*), Durga), so they have explained another meaning as well. In the same context they cite the mantra

दासपत्नीरहिगोपा अतिष्ठन्निरुद्धा आपः पणिनेव गावः (*dāsapatnīrahigopā atiṣṭhanniruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32.11)

and explain the word अहिगोपाः (*ahigopāḥ*) there as "those who guard the clouds". That is, here the word *ahi* means Vṛtra. But the word *ahi* is also used in the sense of a particular deity. For example—

उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यो ३ मयस्कः शिशुं न पिप्युषीव वेति सिंधुः । येन नपातमपां जुनाम मनोजुवो वृषणो यं वहंति ॥ (*uta no 'hirbudhnyo 3 mayaskaḥ śiśuṃ na pipyuṣīva veti siṃdhuḥ | yena napātamapāṃ junāma manojuvo vṛṣaṇo yaṃ vahaṃti ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-186-5)

Here Sāyaṇa has explained the word *ahi* as meaning a particular deity, and has shown the derivation अहिः अंतरिक्षगामी अहंता ना अहीनो वा अहन्यमानो ना एतन्नामको देवः (*ahiḥ aṃtarikṣagāmī ahaṃtā nā ahīno vā ahanyamāno nā etannāmako devaḥ*). The nature of this derivation was explained earlier, when the purport of this cited Ṛk was set out. And the word बुध्नः (*budhnaḥ*) here is to indicate the place of this deity: बुध्नं अंतरिक्षं तदर्हतीति बुध्नः अंतरिक्षचारी एतन्नामको देवः । (*budhnaṃ aṃtarikṣaṃ tadarhatīti budhnaḥ aṃtarikṣacārī etannāmako devaḥ |*). The purport is: the deity of this name who moves in the middle region. What the individual nature of this deity who moves in the middle region is, is the chief matter to be examined. The Nirukta-writers have stated the derivation of this word thus:

अहिर्बुध्न्यः । योऽहिः स बुध्यो बुध्नमंतरिक्षं । तन्निवासात् । (*ahirbudhnyaḥ | yo 'hiḥ sa budhyo budhnamaṃtarikṣaṃ | tannivāsāt |*) (Ni. 10-44)

### Printed p. 386

*Budhna* means the middle region. How so? बुद्धमंतरिक्षं बद्धा अस्मिन् ; धृता आप इति ना । इदमपीतरद्बुध्नमेतस्मादेव । बद्धा अस्मिन् धृताः प्राणा इति । (*buddhamaṃtarikṣaṃ baddhā asmin ; dhṛtā āpa iti nā | idamapītaradbudhnametasmādeva | baddhā asmin dhṛtāḥ prāṇā iti |*).**NOTE** Because it holds the waters, the middle region is called *budhna*. In the present context, the Nirukta-writers have shown only the deity's place of abode, namely that this deity is called Ahirbudhnya because he dwells in the middle region; they have not stated the individual nature of this deity. But first it must be examined whether any particulars on this matter are found in the passages of the Ṛk-saṃhitā.

अब्बा मुक्कैरहिं गृणीषे बुद्धे नदीनां रर्जसु षीदन् । मा नोऽहिर्बुध्यो रिषे धान्मा यज्ञो अस्य स्रिधदृतायोः ॥ (*abbā mukkairahiṃ gṛṇīṣe buddhe nadīnāṃ rarjasu ṣīdan | mā no 'hirbudhyo riṣe dhānmā yajño asya sridhadṛtāyoḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-16, 17)

In these mantras there is a prayer to the god Ahirbudhnya. In the first of them the nature of this god is described to some extent: the poet resolves, "I praise the *ahi*, who is born in the waters and abides in the middle region." Sāyaṇa has explained the purport here as अहिश्चासौ बुध्न्यश्चेत्यहिर्बुध्न्योऽग्निः (*ahiścāsau budhnyaścetyahirbudhnyo 'gniḥ*), that is, the *ahi*-nature contained in Budhnya is a quality of the god Agni. The epithet *ahi* is applied to Vṛtra just as it is to Agni. In many contexts the word *ahi* means Vṛtra. But in

हिरण्यकेशो रजसो विसारेऽहिर्धुनिर्नात इव ध्रूजीमान् । (*hiraṇyakeśo rajaso visāre 'hirdhunirnāta iva dhrūjīmān |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-79-1)

and similar places the word *ahi* has been explained as "the striker". Agni is described as the one who makes the clouds tremble (*dhuniḥ*) and the one who splits the clouds asunder. In this way the word *ahi* shows the qualities of Agni as it shows the qualities of Vṛtra. But the purport of another word that shows a special quality of Agni must also be chiefly noted.

स जायत प्रथमः पस्त्यासु महो बुद्धे रजसो अस्य योन् । अपादशीर्षा गुहमानो अंतायो युवानो वृषभस्य नीळे ॥ (*sa jāyata prathamaḥ pastyāsu maho buddhe rajaso asya yon | apādaśīrṣā guhamāno aṃtāyo yuvāno vṛṣabhasya nīḷe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-1-11)

Agni, who is without feet and without head, lies hidden in the *budhna* of the middle region, that is, in the corner beyond the range of sight. Such descriptions occur only as synonyms of Agni. From these examples it is also understood that the epithets *ahi*, Vṛtra and Apāṃ Napāt are common to both Agni and Vṛtra.

### Printed p. 387

Moreover, this deity Ahirbudhnya is described as ordinarily associated with the deities अज एकपात् (*aja ekapāt*), अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) and Savitṛ. There are also contexts in which he is praised separately. It is clear that all these deities are variant forms of Agni or of Sūrya. One may also say that they are deities of the middle region. That अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) is used as an epithet of the deity Ahirbudhnya is likewise stated in the mantra Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-16 cited above. There the word अब्ब (*abba*) also shows the special nature of this deity. It would not be wrong to give one and the same meaning to both अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) and अब्ब (*abba*). (That Agni is "born of water" because he is produced from the lotus leaf will be stated later, in the special topics of the mantra 6-16-13.) In the manner in which the word *ahirbudhnya* shows the special quality of Agni, that is, of the Agni of the middle region, in that same manner it also shows the special quality of Vṛtra, the chief of the Asuras; so the question is how one epithet can describe the special qualities of the opposite forms, gods and non-gods (Devas and Asuras). It may be examined that there are a few more such examples, like this one.

In the mantra cited above, हिरण्यकेशो रजसः (*hiraṇyakeśo rajasaḥ*) (1-79-1), the epithet धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*) which describes the nature of Agni also shows a quality of an Asura. Moreover, this word is itself the name of an Asura. For example,

त्वं नृभिर्नृमणो देववीत् भूरीणि वृत्रा हरश्व हंसि । त्वं नि दस्युं चुमुरिं धुनिं चास्वापयो दभीतये सुहंतु ॥ (*tvaṃ nṛbhirnṛmaṇo devavīt bhūrīṇi vṛtrā haraśva haṃsi | tvaṃ ni dasyuṃ cumuriṃ dhuniṃ cāsvāpayo dabhītaye suhaṃtu ‖*) (Puṃ. Saṃ. 7-19-4)**NOTE**

In this mantra *dhuni* stands as the name of an Asura. The same point is shown by the mantra इंद्रो धुनिं च चुमुरिं च दंभयन् (*iṃdro dhuniṃ ca cumuriṃ ca daṃbhayan*) (10-113.9). In 1.174-9 धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*) is an epithet of Indra himself. Thus it cannot be improper that one and the same word, according to the context, should be an epithet describing the nature of persons of two groups, the gods and the Asuras. In the present case, if the word Ahirbudhnya is an epithet of a deity, then it must be examined which deity's individual nature it describes. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa the nature of this deity is described thus—

तासु ना अहिना बुद्ध्येन परोक्षात्तेजोऽदधादेष ह वा अहिबुध्यो यदग्नि गार्हपत्योऽग्निनैवासु तद्गार्हपत्येन परोक्षात्तेजो दधाति । (*tāsu nā ahinā buddhyena parokṣāttejo 'dadhādeṣa ha vā ahibudhyo yadagni gārhapatyo 'gninaivāsu tadgārhapatyena parokṣāttejo dadhāti |*) (Ai. Brā. 3-36)

### Printed p. 388

In this sentence *ahirbudhnya* is explained as the Gārhapatya fire. Explaining the same view further, Sāyaṇa has said in his commentary:

अहिना बुध्येन अहिशब्दबुध्यशब्दद्वयनामकाग्नि विशेषेण परोक्षात् परोक्षरूपेण तेजोऽदधात् । यो गार्हपत्योऽग्निरस्ति एष एवाहिशब्देन बुध्यशब्देनाभिहितः ॥ (*ahinā budhyena ahiśabdabudhyaśabdadvayanāmakāgni viśeṣeṇa parokṣāt parokṣarūpeṇa tejo 'dadhāt | yo gārhapatyo 'gnirasti eṣa evāhiśabdena budhyaśabdenābhihitaḥ ‖*) (Sā. Bhā.)**NOTE**

The two words *ahi* and *budhya* are both names of Agni. By the help of this Agni, brilliance is spread among the people. The very Gārhapatya fire that exists is denoted by the word *ahi* and by the word *budhya*. Moreover, the invisibility of this god is also indicated; the word *budhya* shows this invisibility. This invisibility is shown by the sentence cited above (4-1-11), अपादशीर्षा गुहमानो अंता (*apādaśīrṣā guhamāno aṃtā*). Though he is invisible, he is praised as spreading visible radiance among the people. Because Agni is footless, headless and hiding, it would not be wrong to say that he is denoted by the word *budhya*. This same invisibility and *budhya*-nature of Agni are described in many places. In all such contexts it is understood that the description is of Agni in the form of Sūrya. For example—

द्विमाता होता विधथेषु सम्राळन्वग्रं चरति क्षेति बुद्धः । प्र रण्यानि रण्यवाचो भरंते महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥ (*dvimātā hotā vidhatheṣu samrāḷanvagraṃ carati kṣeti buddhaḥ | pra raṇyāni raṇyavāco bharaṃte mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-55-7)

Here there is a description of Agni. But in explaining the sentence बुद्ध्यः चरति (*buddhyaḥ carati*), क्षेति (*kṣeti*), Sāyaṇa has said सूरभूतः तत्र वर्तते (*sūrabhūtaḥ tatra vartate*): having become Sūrya, he moves in the middle region; in the form of Agni he dwells on the earth. When this same Sūrya is hidden in a cave, he also becomes denoted by the word *ahi*.

सूर‍्यं न दस्रा तमसि क्षियंतं (*sūryaṃ na dasrā tamasi kṣiyaṃtaṃ*) (1-117-5); गूळ्हं सूर‍्यं तमसापव्रतेन (*gūḷhaṃ sūryaṃ tamasāpavratena*) (5-40-6). These sentences state the invisibility of Sūrya. This same Sūrya, who is hidden in the cave, may also be denoted by the word *ahi*.

गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्मप्पपीवृतं मायिनं क्षियंतं । उतो अपो द्यां तस्तभ्वांसमहन्नहिं शूर वीर्येण ॥ (*guhā hitaṃ guhyaṃ gūḷmappapīvṛtaṃ māyinaṃ kṣiyaṃtaṃ | uto apo dyāṃ tastabhvāṃsamahannahiṃ śūra vīryeṇa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-5)

### Printed p. 389

Here the manner in which Indra slew the *ahi* hidden in the cave is described. Here all the epithets गुहाहितं (*guhāhitaṃ*), गुह्यं (*guhyaṃ*), गूळं (*gūḷaṃ*) and the rest are just like the description of Sūrya given in the mantra 5 40-6, गूळं सूर्‍यं (*gūḷaṃ sūryaṃ*) and so on. Here the epithets अपीवृतं (*apīvṛtaṃ*), अपव्रतेन (*apavratena*) and so on indicate the Vṛtra-nature of Sūrya or Agni, who is hidden in the cave or is *budhya*. The description of Agni in the mantra 4-1-11 cited above, गुहमानो अंता (*guhamāno aṃtā*), also shows the same point. That is, if the word Ahirbudhnya is explained as Sūrya or Agni hidden in the cave, then one may say that the *ahi*-nature and the Vṛtra-nature are attributed to him. If it is asked what Vedic authority there is for explaining it in this way, the answer is that Vedic sentences themselves can be shown as the proof.

अहन्वत्रमृचीषम और्णवाभमहीशुवं । हिमेनाविध्यदर्बुदं ॥ (*ahanvatramṛcīṣama aurṇavābhamahīśuvaṃ | himenāvidhyadarbudaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-22-26)

आदीं शवस्यब्रवीदौर्णनाभमहीशुवं । ते पुत्र संतु निष्टुरः ॥ (*ādīṃ śavasyabravīdaurṇanābhamahīśuvaṃ | te putra saṃtu niṣṭuraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-77-2)

In these and similar sentences Vṛtra has the epithet और्णवाभ (*aurṇavābha*). In explaining the meaning of this same epithet in the mantra Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-18, Sāyaṇa has stated the purport: और्णः ऊर्णनाभिः । तदाभं तत्सदृशमित्यर्थः । ततः तमोरूपस्य हननात् । (*aurṇaḥ ūrṇanābhiḥ | tadābhaṃ tatsadṛśamityarthaḥ | tataḥ tamorūpasya hananāt |*), that is, "like a weaver-insect (spider)", that is, "of the nature of darkness". In the Brāhmaṇas and other works, Ūrṇāyu is a Gandharva. (Sūrya too is praised as a Gandharva in the Saṃhitās and other works.) Moreover,

अग्ने विश्वेभिः स्वनीक देवैरूर्णावंतं प्रथमः सीद योनिं । कुलायिनं धृतवंतं सवित्रे यज्ञं नय यजमानाय साधु ॥ (*agne viśvebhiḥ svanīka devairūrṇāvaṃtaṃ prathamaḥ sīda yoniṃ | kulāyinaṃ dhṛtavaṃtaṃ savitre yajñaṃ naya yajamānāya sādhu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-15-16)

Here the altar, the womb of Agni, is praised with the epithet ऊर्णवंतं (*ūrṇavaṃtaṃ*). One may say that there is no difference in purport between ऊर्णवंतं (*ūrṇavaṃtaṃ*) here and the epithet और्णवाभं (*aurṇavābhaṃ*). Such epithets also show the spiritual nature of Sūrya or Agni who is hidden in the cave. How? Thus:

अमी ये सप्त रश्मयस्तत्रा मे नाभिरातता । (*amī ye sapta raśmayastatrā me nābhirātatā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-9)

The description that "my navel grew spread out in these seven rays of the sun, which are in the form of the seven vital breaths"—this description

### Printed p. 390

स यथोर्णनाभिस्तंतुनोच्चरेद्यथाग्नेः क्षुद्रा विस्फुलिंगा व्युच्चरंति एवमेवास्मादात्मनः सर्वे प्राणाः सर्वे लोकाः सर्वे देवाः सर्वाणि भूतानि व्युच्चरंति........प्राणा वै सत्यं तेषामेष सत्यं ॥ (*sa yathorṇanābhistaṃtunoccaredyathāgneḥ kṣudrā visphuliṃgā vyuccaraṃti evamevāsmādātmanaḥ sarve prāṇāḥ sarve lokāḥ sarve devāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni vyuccaraṃti........prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣāmeṣa satyaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 2-1-20)

If it is compared with this description, that as small sparks go forth from fire and as threads go forth from the spider, so from this Self all the vital breaths come into being, then a likeness may be stated between the navel of Sūrya (or of Agni) and the navel of the Self. The extension of the seven threads of Sūrya in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164.5 was explained at length earlier. In the Kauṣītakī Brāhmaṇa Sūrya is compared to a spider (19.3). Therefore the purport is: when Sūrya, or Agni in the form of Sūrya, does not shine forth his rays but lies dormant, he is marked with the name Vṛtra; when he makes his rays shine, he is called a god. The same view is stated in the Śatapatha and other Brāhmaṇas by such sentences as

तदसानादित्य इमांल्लोकान्सूत्रे समापयते तद्यत्तूत्रं (*tadasānāditya imāṃllokānsūtre samāpayate tadyattūtraṃ*) (Śa. Brā. 8-7-3-10)

This same Sūrya, or Agni in the form of Sūrya, has two states: one the awakened state, the other the state of deep sleep. How so? Thus:

अतृप्नवंतं वियतमबुध्यमानं सुषुपाणमिंद्र । (*atṛpnavaṃtaṃ viyatamabudhyamānaṃ suṣupāṇamiṃdra |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-19-3)

Here the epithets अबुध्यं (*abudhyaṃ*) and सुषुपाणं (*suṣupāṇaṃ*) are noteworthy. In a time without awareness, that is, without light, these epithets show the nature of the *ahi*. For Sūrya as for Agni, the two states, the time of sleep and the time of waking, are well known in the Saṃhitās and other works.

तदिंद्र प्रेव वीर्यं चकर्थ यत्ससंतं वज्रेणाबोधयोऽहिं । (*tadiṃdra preva vīryaṃ cakartha yatsasaṃtaṃ vajreṇābodhayo 'hiṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-183-7)

"O Indra, you struck the intoxicated Vṛtra with the thunderbolt and woke him by your valour"; such sentences show the sleeping state and the waking state of Sūrya. In the same way, sentences such as उषर्बुधः (*uṣarbudhaḥ*) and अबोध्यग्निः (*abodhyagniḥ*) (5-1.1; 4-23-7) show the sleeping state and the waking state of Agni. Therefore, in the sleeping state, either for Sūrya or for Agni, there is the *ahi*-nature or Vṛtra-nature; in the awakened state, godhood. In the same way,

### Printed p. 391

अपादहस्तो अपृतन्यदिंद्रमास्य वज्रमधि सानौ जघान । (*apādahasto apṛtanyadiṃdramāsya vajramadhi sānau jaghāna |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-7)

सहदानुं पुरुहूत क्षियंतमहस्त मिंद्र सं पिणक्कुणारुं । (*sahadānuṃ puruhūta kṣiyaṃtamahasta miṃdra saṃ piṇakkuṇāruṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-8)

In these and similar sentences, the epithets आपात् (*āpāt*), अहस्त (*ahasta*) and the like, which are well known as describing particular Asuras such as Vṛtra and Ahivṛtra, are without doubt also descriptions of Sūrya.

गुहा शिरो निहितमृधगक्षी असिन्वन्नत्ति जिह्वया वनानि । अत्राण्यस्मै पड्भिः सं भरंत्युत्तानहस्ता नमसाधि विक्षु ॥ (*guhā śiro nihitamṛdhagakṣī asinvannatti jihvayā vanāni | atrāṇyasmai paḍbhiḥ saṃ bharaṃtyuttānahastā namasādhi vikṣu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-79-2)

In these and similar sentences the descriptions गुहा शिरो निहितं (*guhā śiro nihitaṃ*) are the same as the descriptions बुद्धे रजसः (*buddhe rajasaḥ*).

The authorities cited above explain the nature of Ahirbudhnya. The purport is that Agni acquires the state of Ahirbudhnya at the time when he lies asleep in a hidden region of the middle region. The purport of the sentence in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, which describes the Gārhapatya fire that possesses invisibility as the god Ahirbudhnya, is the same.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इति चिन्नु प्रजायै पशुमत्यै देवासो वनते मर्त्यो न  
> आ देवासो वनते मर्त्यो नः ।  
> अत्रा॑ शि॒वां त॒न्नो॑ धा॒सिम॒स्या ज॒रां चि॑न्मे॒ निर्य॑तिर्जग्रसीत॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इति । चित् । नु । प्रजायै । पशुमत्यै । देवासः । वनते । मर्त्यः । वः । आ ।  
> देवासः । वनते । मर्त्यः । वः ।  
> अत्र । शिवां । तन्वः । धासिं । अस्याभिजरां । चित् । मे । निःऋतिः । जग्रसीत ॥ १७ ॥

### Printed p. 392

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवासो देवा वो युष्मानिति चिदित्थमेव नु क्षिप्रं प्रजायै पशुमत्यै
> पशुसहितायापत्याय वनते भजते मर्त्यो मनुष्यो यजमानः । आ देवास इति
> पुनरुक्तिरादरार्था । अत्रास्मिन्यज्ञे शिवां धासिमन्नं मे ममास्यास्तन्वो देवैरनुगृहीतस्य पुत्रस्य करोतु निर्ऋतिर्देवता । जरां चिज्जरां च जग्रसीत । ग्रसतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses देवासः (*devāsaḥ*) as "O gods" and वः (*vaḥ*) as "you". Thus, indeed, and quickly, the mortal, the sacrificer, worships (वनते (*vanate*)) for offspring accompanied by cattle (पशुमत्यै (*paśumatyai*) प्रजायै (*prajāyai*)). The repetition in आ देवास (*ā devāsa*) is for the sake of respect. In this sacrifice, may the deity Nirṛti make good food for me, for this body, a son favoured by the gods. And may she swallow up (ग्रसतु (*grasatu*)) old age.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—O gods
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—the human being
- वः चित् (*vaḥ cit*)—you
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- पशुमत्यै (*paśumatyai*)—accompanied by cattle
- प्रजायै (*prajāyai*)—for the wealth of progeny
- वनते (*vanate*)—worships
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—O gods
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—that same human being
- वनते (*vanate*)—(surely) worships
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this sacrifice
- निर्ऋतिः (*nirṛtiḥ*)—the god Nirṛti
- मे (*me*)—my
- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—for the protection of this body
- शिवां धासिं (*śivāṃ dhāsiṃ*)—the most excellent food
- तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)—may she produce
- जरांचित् (*jarāṃcit*)—decay
- जग्रसीत (*jagrasīta*)—may she remove

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, the human being worships you without fail for the wealth of progeny together with cattle; he is bound to worship you. On this occasion may the god Nirṛti increase the excellent food needed for the nourishment of this body of mine. May she see to it that our body does not waste away through old age.

##### English translation
The mortal (sacrificer) worships you, gods, at all times for progeny and cattle : verily, gods, the mortal worships you: may Nirriti, on this occasion, sustain my body with solutary food, and keep off decay.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the present mantra Nirṛti is regarded as a particular deity. Sāyaṇa has explained it as meaning a deity. And the sacrificer prays that she should do him a favour. Such contexts are rare. Nirṛti is ordinarily known as a deity who causes harm. In the present case a good result is expected from that deity. It is therefore necessary to know what the true nature of this deity is.

The Nirukta-writers have read the word निर्यति (*niryati*) among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5).**NOTE** Afterwards, showing the derivation of this word,

### Printed p. 393

इमान्येकविंशतिः पृथिवीनामधेयान्यनुक्रांतानि । तत्र निर्यतिर्निरमणादृच्छतेः कृच्छ्रापत्तिरितरा सा पृथिव्या संदिह्यते । तयोर्विभागः ॥ (*imānyekaviṃśatiḥ pṛthivīnāmadheyānyanukrāṃtāni | tatra niryatirniramaṇādṛcchateḥ kṛcchrāpattiritarā sā pṛthivyā saṃdihyate | tayorvibhāgaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 2-7)

This word may be formed from two roots. If it is formed first from the root *ram*, then निरमणात् (*niramaṇāt*): निविष्टानि रमंते अस्यां भूतानीति निर्ऋतिः पृथिवी (*niviṣṭāni ramaṃte asyāṃ bhūtānīti nirṛtiḥ pṛthivī*); because all beings that rest on the earth experience delight from the earth, the earth has the name Nirṛti. Secondly, from ऋच्छतेः (*ṛcchateḥ*): इतरा कृच्छ्रापत्तिः । दुःखसंज्ञिका । निर्ऋतिः पाप्मा । (*itarā kṛcchrāpattiḥ | duḥkhasaṃjñikā | nirṛtiḥ pāpmā |*); because she causes sorrow, the goddess Nirṛti is a producer of sin. But here, समान नामधेयत्वात् समानश्रुतित्वं पृथिव्या संदिह्यते (*samāna nāmadheyatvāt samānaśrutitvaṃ pṛthivyā saṃdihyate*); having shown in this way the two derivations of this word, he then says that the meaning of the word is to be stated according to the context, that when the meaning "earth" is intended one must not take it as "mother of sin", and when the second purport is intended one must not take it as "earth".

Durgācārya has explained it in two ways: 1) एका निविष्टानां भूतानां रमयित्री (*ekā niviṣṭānāṃ bhūtānāṃ ramayitrī*), one who gives delight to all beings; 2) एका पुनः कृच्छ्रमापादयित्री (*ekā punaḥ kṛcchramāpādayitrī*), another who gives sorrow. In this context the Nirukta-writers

य ईं चकार न सो अस्य वेद य ईं ददर्श हिरुगिन्नु तस्मात् । स मातुर्योना परिवीतो अंतर्बहुप्रजा निर्ऋतिमा विवेश ॥ (*ya īṃ cakāra na so asya veda ya īṃ dadarśa hiruginnu tasmāt | sa māturyonā parivīto aṃtarbahuprajā nirṛtimā viveśa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-32)

cite this mantra and explain the meaning of the word *nirṛti*. In the cited mantra, in stating his explanation of the word *nirṛti*, Sāyaṇa first gives his own view, which differs from that of the Nirukta-writers, and explains it as sorrow; afterwards he also gives the view of the Nirukta-writers and explains it as the earth, the means of sorrow. But it appears that the view of the Nirukta-writers is that whenever the meaning "earth" is intended, it must be explained as a means of delight. But the use of the word *nirṛti* appears for the most part to concern an inauspicious deity. One or two of these may be taken as examples and their purport examined.

मो षु णः परापरा निर्युतिर्दुर्हणा वधीत् । पदीष्टतृष्णया सह ॥ (*mo ṣu ṇaḥ parāparā niryutirdurhaṇā vadhīt | padīṣṭatṛṣṇayā saha ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.38-6)

### Printed p. 394

Here the word *nirṛti* is explained as a deity of the demon class. The prayer is that this deity of demonic form may not do us harm. In such contexts, powers that cause calamity, such as famine and greed, are indicated as the deity. In sum, it may be explained as the presiding deity of sin.

Showing the purport of this word, the scholar Max Muller has stated his view thus:

"One of the meanings of निर्यति (*niryati*) is sin. It is derived from the same root which yielded ऋत (*ṛta*) in the sense of right. निर्यति (*niryati*) was conceived, it would seem, as going away from the Path of right. It was personified as a power of destruction and evil," (Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 32, p. 88)

Among the many meanings of the word *nirṛti*, the meaning "sin" is the most frequent. The word *nirṛti* is formed from the same root from which the word *ṛta* is formed. The word *ṛta* means the straight path, truth. That which is without straightness and without truth is the meaning of the word *nirṛti*. To conceive the states of sin and destruction as embodied is the knowledge of the nature of the deity Nirṛti.**NOTE** There is a rule that certain rites must be performed to escape from the influence of this deity, who is full of sin and causes sorrow. When these rules are stated, the nature of this deity is stated along with them. For example, only a few passages may be examined here.

अथातो नैऋतीर्हरंति । एतद्वै देवा गार्हपत्यं चित्वा समारोहन्नयं वै लोको........समारोहंस्ते तम एवानतिदृश्यमपश्यन् ॥ (*athāto naiṛtīrharaṃti | etadvai devā gārhapatyaṃ citvā samārohannayaṃ vai loko........samārohaṃste tama evānatidṛśyamapaśyan ‖*) (Śa. Bhā. 7. 2. 1-1)**NOTE**
(Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-1)

These are the mantras recited while the bricks named Nirṛti are laid. When the gods had built the Gārhapatya fire-altar and were ready to ascend it, they were enveloped in pitch darkness on this Gārhapatya, which has the form of the earth, and could see nothing.

तेऽब्रुवन् । उप तज्ञानीत यथेदं तमः पाप्मानमपहनामहा इति तेऽब्रुवंश्चतयध्वमिति ॥ (*te 'bruvan | upa tajñānīta yathedaṃ tamaḥ pāpmānamapahanāmahā iti te 'bruvaṃścatayadhvamiti ‖*)

"We must think how we are to cross this darkness. All of you meditate, seeking a means of destroying it." When this was said, the knowledge came to them that the fire-altar must be built.

ते चेतयमानाः । एता इष्टका अपश्यन्नैर्य्यतीस्ता उपादधत ताभिस्तत्तमः पाप्मानमपाघ्नत पाप्मा वै निर्ऋतिः तद्यदेताभिः पाप्मानं निर्ऋतिमपाघ्नत ॥ (*te cetayamānāḥ | etā iṣṭakā apaśyannairyyatīstā upādadhata tābhistattamaḥ pāpmānamapāghnata pāpmā vai nirṛtiḥ tadyadetābhiḥ pāpmānaṃ nirṛtimapāghnata ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-3)

### Printed p. 395

Meditating, they found the bricks named Nirṛti. Then by building them they destroyed the darkness and Nirṛti, who has the form of sin. Nirṛti is the mass of sin in the form of destruction. By the building of the bricks named Nirṛti this sin is destroyed. In this way and the like the nature of this deity is described. But in order to escape the destructive influence of this deity, worship must be offered even to this deity.

असुन्वंतमयजमानमिच्छेति । यो वै न सुनोति न यजते तं निर्ऋतिऋच्छति स्तेनस्येत्यामन्विहि तस्करस्येति .... .... .... .... यथा स्येनतस्करः प्रलायमेत्यॆ वं प्रलायनि:हि .... .... .... .... नमो देवि निर्ऋते तुभ्यमस्त्विति नमस्कारेणैवैनामपहते ॥ (*asunvaṃtamayajamānamiccheti | yo vai na sunoti na yajate taṃ nirṛtiṛcchati stenasyetyāmanvihi taskarasyeti .... .... .... .... yathā syenataskaraḥ pralāyametyè vaṃ pralāyani:hi .... .... .... .... namo devi nirṛte tubhyamastviti namaskāreṇaivaināmapahate ‖*) (Śa. Prā. 7 2.1.9)**NOTE**

"O goddess Nirṛti, strike the one who does not press the Soma for the sacrifice and does not offer the oblation in the sacrifice. O goddess, follow the very path the thief takes, and hide as he hides. Approach the one who is not a sacrificer and strike him. O goddess, homage to you"; saying this and making obeisance, he sends that goddess out.

नमः सु ते निर्ऋते तिग्मत्तेज इति । तिग्मत्तेजा वै निर्ऋतिस्तस्याएतन्नमस्करोत्ययस्मयं विच्यता बंधमेतमित्ययस्मयेन ह वै तं बंधेन निर्ऋतिर्बध्नाति .... .... .... .... ॥ (*namaḥ su te nirṛte tigmatteja iti | tigmattejā vai nirṛtistasyāetannamaskarotyayasmayaṃ vicyatā baṃdhametamityayasmayena ha vai taṃ baṃdhena nirṛtirbadhnāti .... .... .... .... ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-19)

"Homage to you, O Nirṛti of sharp brilliance. Indeed your power is very keen and radiant. Loosen this bond of mine in the form of an iron rod." For Nirṛti binds the man with whom she is displeased with hard iron rods (pierces him).

यस्यास्ते घोर आसज्जु होमीति । घोरा वै निर्ऋतिस्तस्या एतदासञ्जुहोति यत्तद्देवत्यं कर्म करोत्येषां बंधानामवसर्जनायेति यैर्बंधैर्बद्धो भवति यां त्वा जनो भूमिरिति प्रमंदत इतीयं वै भूमिरस्स्यां वै स भवति यो भवति निर्ऋतिं त्वाहं परिवेद विश्वत इति निर्ऋतिरिति त्वाहं परिवेद सर्वत इत्येतदियं वै निर्ऋतिरियं वै तं निरर्पयति यो निर्ऋच्छति................आमंत्रितो हिनस्ति ॥ (*yasyāste ghora āsajju homīti | ghorā vai nirṛtistasyā etadāsañjuhoti yattaddevatyaṃ karma karotyeṣāṃ baṃdhānāmavasarjanāyeti yairbaṃdhairbaddho bhavati yāṃ tvā jano bhūmiriti pramaṃdata itīyaṃ vai bhūmirassyāṃ vai sa bhavati yo bhavati nirṛtiṃ tvāhaṃ pariveda viśvata iti nirṛtiriti tvāhaṃ pariveda sarvata ityetadiyaṃ vai nirṛtiriyaṃ vai taṃ nirarpayati yo nirṛcchati................āmaṃtrito hinasti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-11)

### Printed p. 396

"O goddess Nirṛti, you are of terrible form": having praised her thus, in performing the rite of the deity he offers the oblation in her mouth. If he offers it saying "O goddess, this is for the release of your bond", the sacrificer is freed from whatever bond he is bound by. "O goddess, the sacrificers address you as the earth; but I know you only as all-pervading." What is said here is also true. The earth rejects and thrusts far away the sacrificer who is blameworthy. If, as said above, worship is offered to Nirṛti, the sacrificer's release from bondage comes about.

नोपस्पृशति । पाप्मा वै निर्ऋतिर्नेत्पास्मना सग्गस्पृशा इति न सादयति प्रतिष्ठा वै सादनं नेत्वाप्मानं प्रतिष्ठापयानीति .... .... .... ॥ (*nopaspṛśati | pāpmā vai nirṛtirnetpāsmanā saggaspṛśā iti na sādayati pratiṣṭhā vai sādanaṃ netvāpmānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayānīti .... .... .... ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-12)

The sacrificer does not touch the bricks named Nirṛti. Nirṛti has the form of sin; therefore, if he touches them, contact with sin results. Nor does he set them up; if he set them up, it would be as if he established in his own house Nirṛti herself, who has the form of sin. — In this way and the like, in order to escape the sin-filled and sorrow-causing influence of Nirṛti, who is of an inauspicious nature, he regards her as a particular deity, worships her and sends her out (नमस्कारेणैवैनामपहते (*namaskāreṇaivaināmapahate*)). Thus there is a description of Nirṛti's nature. Even though Nirṛti is said to have the form of the earth, for some people the earth becomes a giver of delight; then the derivation of this word is from the root *ram*. For others the earth is a sharer of sorrow; then the derivation is from the root *ṛ*. Although at times an identity between the earth and this deity is shown, on many occasions she is regarded as a deity different from the earth.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the gods as Vasus, "those who cause to dwell", and speaks of "that well-known good thought (sumati) of yours", that is, a means of good thinking; growth of thought comes from food, and it is well known in passages such as अन्नेन मतिवृद्धिरन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः । (*annena mativṛddhirannamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ |*) (Chā. U. 6. 5. 4) that "the mind, dear one, is made of food". "Invigorating" means strength-giving, and the इषं (*iṣaṃ*) is food, a means of seeking, of the nature of milk, curds and the like. May we obtain it, may we reach it, through praise (शसा (*śasā*)) from the cow. May that goddess come to us for our good, for happiness; गम्याः (*gamyāḥ*) means "may she come", "may she approach". The deity is further qualified: सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*), of good gifts; मृळयंती (*mṛḷayaṃtī*), making us happy; द्रवंती (*dravaṃtī*), hastening, coming towards us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O you who are of divine nature
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—O Vasus
- शसा (*śasā*)—as the fruit of our praises
- गोः (*goḥ*)—from that cow
- वः (*vaḥ*)—which is to be (kept) with regard to you
- तां (*tāṃ*)—that famous
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—conducive to an excellent state of mind
- ऊर्जयंतीं (*ūrjayaṃtīṃ*)—producing strength of the body
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food of the nature of milk and the like
- आश्याम (*āśyāma*)—may we obtain
- सा देवी (*sā devī*)—that goddess
- सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*)—endowed with excellent gifts
- मृळयंती (*mṛḷayaṃtī*)—giving us happiness
- द्रवंती (*dravaṃtī*)—eager to come to us
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—for the good
- प्रति गम्याः (*prati gamyāḥ*)—may she come towards us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vasus, divine beings, the food of milk and the like, to be obtained from that cow, is conducive to the pure state of mind that we must keep with regard to you, and is a producer of nourishment for our body. As the fruit of our praise may we obtain that food. And may that goddess, who is endowed with excellent gifts, who is a giver of happiness to us, and who is eager to favour us, come towards us for our good.

##### English translation
Divine Vasus, may we obtain from the adorable cow invigorating and mind-sustaining food : may that liberal and benignant goddess, hastening (hither), come for our felicity.

> कं । आयोरायुं मनुष्यं यजमानं । केन । प्रभृथस्य तेजसो वोदकस्य ना
> दानेन । प्रभृथस्य तेजसो वोदकस्यॆति निरुक्तं । ११-४९. । अथवा प्रभृथस्य प्रभरणवत
> आयोर्यज्ञमभ्यूर्व्वानाच्छादयंती ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Iḷā, the earth, the creator of the herd (the host of cows), praise us. Or, as they say, Iḷā is the daughter of Manu, who has taken the form of a cow. Or else Iḷā is the Mādhyamikā Vāc, the creator of the host of Maruts. Or Urvaśī is the Mādhyamikā Vāc. May she praise with the rivers, with the Gaṅgā and the others. The word स्मच्छब्दः (*smacchabdaḥ*) is said to be a word of praise: may she proclaim excellence. Or else Urvaśī, of abundant brilliance, uttering, praising our rite, covering (the sacrificer): whom? Āyu, the man, the sacrificer. By what? By प्रभृथस्य (*prabhṛthasya*), by brilliance or by water, by giving; the Nirukta (11-49) says that प्रभृथस्य तेजसो वोदकस्यॆति (*prabhṛthasya tejaso vodakasyèti*). Or else प्रभृथस्य (*prabhṛthasya*) means "of him who carries offerings forward", covering the sacrifice of Āyu.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यूधस्य (*yūdhasya*)—to the host of cows
- माता (*mātā*)—the mother
- इळा (*iḷā*)—the goddess Iḷā
- उर्वशी (*urvaśī*)—and Urvaśī (माध्यमिका वाक् (*mādhyamikā vāk*))
- नदीभिः (*nadībhiḥ*)—together with the Gaṅgā and the other rivers
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अभि गृणातु (*abhi gṛṇātu*)—may she favour
- वा (*vā*)—moreover
- बृहद्दिवा (*bṛhaddivā*)—of exceeding brilliance
- उर्वशी (*urvaśī*)—Urvaśī
- गृणाना (*gṛṇānā*)—praising our rites
- आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—the sacrificer
- प्रभृथस्य (*prabhṛthasya*)—by the spreading of brilliance
- अभ्यूर्वाना (*abhyūrvānā*)—covering (may she be gracious)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the goddess Iḷā, the mother of the host of cows, and Urvaśī, together with the Gaṅgā and the other rivers, favour us. Moreover, may Urvaśī, of exceeding brilliance, be gracious, praising our rites and covering the sacrificer by the spreading of brilliance.

## Sūkta 42 (Maṇḍala 5)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र शंतमेत्यष्टादशर्चं दशमं सूक्तं भौमस्यात्रेरार्षं त्रैष्टुभं । पूर्वसूक्ते वै तदित्युक्तत्वादिदमपि वैश्वदेवं । तमु ष्टुहीत्येकादशी रुद्रदेवत्या ।
> सप्तदश्येकपदैतयोरुपांत्यैकपदेत्यनुक्रमिष्यमाणत्वात् । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । प्र
> शंतमा द्वौनैकादशी रौद्रीति । विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the sūkta beginning प्र शंतमा (*pra śaṃtamā*) has eighteen Ṛks and is the tenth sūkta. Its seer is Atri of the Bhauma line (भौमस्यात्रेरार्षं (*bhaumasyātrerārṣaṃ*)), the metre is Triṣṭubh, and, since the preceding sūkta was said to be Vaiśvadeva, this one too is Vaiśvadeva (addressed to the Viśvedevas). The eleventh Ṛk, तमु ष्टुही (*tamu ṣṭuhī*), has Rudra as its deity. The seventeenth is of one pāda, since the Anukramaṇikā is going to say so. The Anukramaṇikā here says that प्र शंतमा (*pra śaṃtamā*) is the sūkta in which, with the eleventh two short, the Ṛk is Raudra. The use (viniyoga) is by indication (laiṅgika).

Anuvāda: This sūkta प्र शंतमा (*pra śaṃtamā*) is the tenth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has eighteen Ṛks. Atri is the seer of this sūkta; the metre is Triṣṭubh; as in the preceding sūkta, the Viśvedevas are the deity; the eleventh Ṛk of this sūkta, तमुष्टिहि (*tamuṣṭihi*), is addressed to Rudra; the seventeenth Ṛk is in the metre called Ekapadā. In the Anukramaṇikā the statement द्व्यूनैकादशी दौद्रीति (*dvyūnaikādaśī daudrīti*) is made;**NOTE** the use is by indication.

- Sūkta 42
- Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 42
- Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 2, Vargas 17, 18, 19
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 18
- Seer: अत्रिः (*atriḥ*)
- Deity: Ṛks 1-10, 12-18 विश्वेदेवाः (*viśvedevāḥ*); 11 रुद्रः (*rudraḥ*)
- Metre: Ṛks 1-16, 18 त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*); 17 एकपवा (*ekapavā*)**NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र शंत॑मा॒ वरु॑णं॒ दीधि॑ती॒ गीर्मि॒त्रं भग॒मदि॑तिं नू॒नम॑श्याः ।  
> पृष॑द्योनिः॒ पंच॑होता शृणो॒त्वतू॑र्तपंथा॒ असु॑रो  ॒
> मयोभुः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 401

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । शंतमा । वरुणं । दीधिती । गीः । मित्रं । भगं । अदितिं । नूनं । अश्याः ।  
> पृषत्ऽयोनिः । पंचहोता। शृणोतु । अतूर्तऽपंथाः । असुरः । मयःऽभुः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र शंतमात्यंतं सुखकरी गीः स्तुतिरूपा, वाग्वरुणं मित्रं भगमदितिं च
> दीधिती दीधित्या कर्मणा हविष्पक्षेपणात्मकेन सह नूनमवितथं प्राश्याः ।
> प्राप्नोतु । किंच पृषद्योनिः पृषद्वर्णांतरिक्षस्थः पंचहोता पंचविधस्य प्राणापानादिहोमस्य साधको वायुः । यद्वा । पंचहोतेति वायोर्नाम । वायुः
> पंचहोता स प्राण इति हि श्रुतेः । स चातूर्तपंथा अहिंसितगतिरसुरः प्राणस्य दाता
> मयोभुः सुखस्यास्पदभूतः । एवमुक्तलक्षणो वायुः शृणोतु स्तोत्रमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the speech of praise, most happiness-giving, together with the दीधिती (*dīdhitī*), the rite consisting of casting in the oblation, surely and without fail reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Bhaga and Aditi. Moreover, पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) is he who dwells in the middle region of dappled colour; पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*) is Vāyu, the accomplisher of the fivefold homa of the breaths prāṇa, apāna and the rest. Or else पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*) is a name of Vāyu, for the śruti says that Vāyu is the five-fold hotṛ and he is the breath. He is अतूर्तपंथाः (*atūrtapaṃthāḥ*), of unharmed course, असुरः (*asuraḥ*), the giver of the breath, मयोभुः (*mayobhuḥ*), the abode of happiness. May Vāyu, of the nature so described, hear the praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शंतमा (*śaṃtamā*)—most happiness-giving
- गीः (*gīḥ*)—the speech in the form of (our) praise
- दीधिती (*dīdhitī*)—joined with rites such as the giving of the oblation
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—Mitra
- भगं (*bhagaṃ*)—Bhaga
- अदितिं (*aditiṃ*)—Aditi
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—surely
- प्र अश्याः (*pra aśyāḥ*)—may it go and reach
- पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*)—he whose own place is the middle region, of variegated colours
- अतूर्तपंथाः (*atūrtapaṃthāḥ*)—he whose going is unimpeded
- असुरः (*asuraḥ*)—the giver of life
- मयोभुः (*mayobhuḥ*)—the bestower of happiness
- पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*)—Vāyu, the accomplisher of the fivefold homa consisting of prāṇa, apāna and the rest
- शृणोतु (*śṛṇotu*)—may he hear our praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May our most happiness-giving praise, joined with rites such as the giving of the oblation, surely go and reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Bhaga and Aditi. May Vāyu, whose own abode is the middle region of variegated colours, whose going is unimpeded, the giver of life, the bestower of happiness, the accomplisher of the fivefold homa consisting of prāṇa, apāna and the rest, hear our praise.

##### English translation
May our most animating praise, together with our offerings, successfully attain Varuna, Mitra, Bhaga and Aditi: may the ministrant

### Printed p. 402

of the five (vital airs, Vayu), the dweller in the dappled (firmament), he whose path is unimpeded, who is the giver of life, the bestower of happiness, hear.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पृषद्योनिः पंचहोता (*pṛṣadyoniḥ paṃcahotā*)

The two words पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) and पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*) both describe the nature of Vāyu. Because he dwells in the middle region of dappled hue, Vāyu is called पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*). There is also the synonymous name पृश्निगर्भ (*pṛśnigarbha*). This is the purport of the first epithet. Secondly, for पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*) the explanation पंचविधस्य प्राणापानादिहोमस्य साधको वायुः (*paṃcavidhasya prāṇāpānādihomasya sādhako vāyuḥ*) is given: it is explained as Vāyu, the accomplisher of the fivefold homa in the form of prāṇa, apāna and the rest. It must be examined which natures of Vāyu these two epithets show. First,

पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*):— अथातो मध्यस्थाना देवताः । तासां वायुः प्रथमगामी भवति (*athāto madhyasthānā devatāḥ | tāsāṃ vāyuḥ prathamagāmī bhavati*) (Ni. 10.1). The Nirukta-writers have indicated Vāyu's place thus: among the deities of the middle region the first place belongs to Vāyu; he is the "first-going". There is a difference between merely "dwelling in the middle region" and पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) or पृश्निगर्भ (*pṛśnigarbha*). The epithet पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) also indicates Vāyu's right to enjoy the sacrifice.

अथ नमो नायवेंतरिक्ष्षिते लोकक्षिते (*atha namo nāyaveṃtarikṣṣite lokakṣite*) (Bhā. U. 9-24-9)**NOTE**

The enjoyment of the sacrifice stated in such sentences is what is indicated in the present mantra. It is from this very place that he is the one to whom offerings are made, as is stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa thus:

तान्वायुरब्रवीत् । उपाहमायानीति केनेति दिग्भिरिति तथेति दिश्याभिर्ह तदुवाच तस्माद्वितीयाय्कॆ स्वयमातृणाया अनंतर्हिता दिश्या उपधीयंते तस्मादंतरिक्षादनंतर्हिता दिशोऽनंतर्हितो वायुरनंतर्हितो हैष एताभिरुपैत् ॥ (*tānvāyurabravīt | upāhamāyānīti keneti digbhiriti tatheti diśyābhirha taduvāca tasmādvitīyāykè svayamātṛṇāyā anaṃtarhitā diśyā upadhīyaṃte tasmādaṃtarikṣādanaṃtarhitā diśo 'naṃtarhito vāyuranaṃtarhito haiṣa etābhirupait ‖*) (Śa. Bā. 6-2-3)**NOTE**

The layer of the second storey itself appeared in the form of the middle region. "I shall ascend there," said Vāyu. Then he joined the bricks of the layer. Then they were not separated from the middle regions. Then

### Printed p. 403

Vāyu too came to have a permanent connection with the middle region, which is of the form of a brick, and so on; thus it is stated that his standing in the middle region itself produced his fitness for the sacrifice. While describing the nature of Vāyu at the time of the brahmodya it is said,

वायुर्गृहपतिरिति हैक आहुः सोंतरिक्षलोकस्य गृहपतिः । (*vāyurgṛhapatiriti haika āhuḥ soṃtarikṣalokasya gṛhapatiḥ |*)

and so on; thus it is stated that the lordship of the household fire (gārhapatya) of the middle world is the office of Vāyu. Although in this way the topic पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) points out the place of Vāyu, saying that the middle region itself is the womb (the place) of Vāyu, yet in some passages it is clearly stated that heaven and earth, both of them, are the causes of Vāyu's origin. For example:

राये नु यं यज्ञ तू रोदसीमे राये देवी धिषणा धाति देवं ॥ (*rāye nu yaṃ yajña tū rodasīme rāye devī dhiṣaṇā dhāti devaṃ ‖*)
(Saṃ. Saṃ. 7-90-2)**NOTE**

In sentences of this kind, heaven and earth are said to have caused Vāyu to be born, and so the quality of being the womb of Vāyu is a common feature of the two worlds. The sentences प्राणाद्वायुरजायत (*prāṇādvāyurajāyata*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-13), "from the breath of the Supreme Person the birth of Vāyu took place", are sentences that point to the quality of being a "five-fold priest" in Vāyu, which is indicated by the word पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*), the second epithet in the present mantra. The connection that the five breaths, indicated by the word pañcahotṛ, have with Vāyu, and Vāyu's lordship over the middle region, are stated together in one and the same context in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as follows.

स यः स वैश्वानरः । अंतरिक्षमेव विश्वं । वायुर्नरः ॥ (*sa yaḥ sa vaiśvānaraḥ | aṃtarikṣameva viśvaṃ | vāyurnaraḥ ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 9-3-1.3)

The middle region itself is the universe (viśva). Since Vāyu is the lord of the middle region, he too has the repute of being Vaiśvānara. Moreover, if the influence of Vāyu is to be described further,

इदमेवांतरिक्षं । तस्मादेतदलोमकमलोमकमिव ह्यंतरिक्षं तदेतद्विश्वं प्राण एव वायुः स नरः स मध्येनास्य भवति मध्यॆ न ह्यंतरिक्षस्य वायुः ॥ (*idamevāṃtarikṣaṃ | tasmādetadalomakamalomakamiva hyaṃtarikṣaṃ tadetadviśvaṃ prāṇa eva vāyuḥ sa naraḥ sa madhyenāsya bhavati madhyè na hyaṃtarikṣasya vāyuḥ ‖*)
(Ka. Brā. 9-3-15)**NOTE**

This middle part of the Universal Person is the middle region itself. It is without hair. For this part of the Universal Self, Vāyu is the form of breath; he is the Man (nara). This Vāyu is the lord of the middle world. Sentences such as these declare the nature and the authority of Vāyu.

### Printed p. 404

अथ विश्वज्योतिषमुपदधाति । वायुर्वै मध्यमा विश्वज्योतिर्वायुर्ह्येवांतरिक्षलोके विश्वं ज्योतिर्वायुमेवैतदुपदधाति तामनंतर्हितां दिश्याभ्य उपदधाति दिक्षु तद्वायुं दधाति तस्मात्सर्वासु दिक्षु वायुः ॥ (*atha viśvajyotiṣamupadadhāti | vāyurvai madhyamā viśvajyotirvāyurhyevāṃtarikṣaloke viśvaṃ jyotirvāyumevaitadupadadhāti tāmanaṃtarhitāṃ diśyābhya upadadhāti dikṣu tadvāyuṃ dadhāti tasmātsarvāsu dikṣu vāyuḥ ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 8-3-2-1)

When the bricks named Viśvajyotis are laid, there is this praise of Vāyu. The Viśvajyotis of the middle part is Vāyu. Vāyu is the light that illumines the world. Since it reflects all the directions and the intermediate directions, it is an all-pervading form of radiance. It also has the power of producing universal vitality. For this Vāyu, who is of the form of the universal light, the middle region is merely the place of origin; the existence of this Vāyu is all-pervading.

वायुर्वाव धर्त्तं चतुष्टोमः स आभिश्चतसृभिर्दिग्भिः स्तुते तद्यत्तमाह धर्त्तमिति प्रतिष्ठा नै धर्त्तं वायुरु सर्वेषां भूतानां प्रतिष्ठा तदेव तद्रूपमुपदधाति स वै वायुमेव प्रथममुपदधाति वायुमुत्तमं वायुनैव तदेतानि सर्वाणि भूतान्युभयतः परिगृह्णाति ॥ (*vāyurvāva dharttaṃ catuṣṭomaḥ sa ābhiścatasṛbhirdigbhiḥ stute tadyattamāha dharttamiti pratiṣṭhā nai dharttaṃ vāyuru sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ pratiṣṭhā tadeva tadrūpamupadadhāti sa vai vāyumeva prathamamupadadhāti vāyumuttamaṃ vāyunaiva tadetāni sarvāṇi bhūtānyubhayataḥ parigṛhṇāti ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 8-4-1-26)

Thus is the praise of Vāyu by the hymn that is a part of the Catuṣṭoma. If the Catuṣṭoma is the supporter of all sacrifices, then Vāyu is this Catuṣṭoma. Therefore Vāyu is the supporter of all sacrifices. Because he keeps bestowing, from all directions, the gift in the form of praise, Vāyu is the supporter of the sacrifice from every direction. Moreover he is the foundation of all beings and their support as well. In this way the importance of Vāyu in the sacrifice is praised.

Pañcahotā:

In the present mantra, one must examine what personal quality is praised by the epithet पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*), "the accomplisher of the offering in the form of the five breaths". Because he gives vitality to all living beings, Vāyu is praised in many places as the lord of the breath. He is the support, the shelter and the prop even of the primal deities Agni, Āditya and Soma, who give vitality to all beings. He is of the form of the breath of the universe. How is that? Thus:

वायुर्वाव संवर्गो यदा वा अग्निरुद्वायति वायुमेवाप्येति यदा सूर्योऽस्तमेति वायुमेवाप्येति यदा चंद्रोऽस्तमेति वायुमेवाप्येति ॥ (*vāyurvāva saṃvargo yadā vā agnirudvāyati vāyumevāpyeti yadā sūryo 'stameti vāyumevāpyeti yadā caṃdro 'stameti vāyumevāpyeti ‖*)
(Kṛ. 70. 2-5.)**NOTE**

### Printed p. 405

In the world Vāyu takes into his own power all things. When fire blazes up and becomes quiet, and after the sun has set, and after the moon has set, they join Vāyu alone and become one with him there.

शौ वा ऐश् द्वै संवर्गौ वायुरेव देवेषु प्राणः प्राणेषु ॥ (*śau vā aiś dvai saṃvargau vāyureva deveṣu prāṇaḥ prāṇeṣu ‖*)
(Cha. 32, 3-5-4)**NOTE**

Among the "gatherers" of the world (those that take everything into themselves) there are chiefly only two that draw the breath: among the gods, Vāyu, and among the fivefold breaths, the breath. Vāyu and the breaths are not different principles.

वायुः प्राणो भूत्वा नासिके प्राविशत् । (*vāyuḥ prāṇo bhūtvā nāsike prāviśat |*)
(Ka. 3. 2. 4)**NOTE**

Thus it is described: Vāyu, becoming breath, entered the nostrils. The following sentences explain that the five breaths too are the five-fold transformations of Vāyu. Moreover, they state the connection that the offering in the form of breath has with Vāyu.

तस्य व्युष्टिवाहनोऽश्वरथो दक्षिणा । त्रयोऽश्वा द्वौ सव्यष्टसारथी ते पंचप्राणा यो वै प्राणः स वातस्तद्यते तस्य कर्मण एषा दक्षिणा तस्मात्पंचवातीयं नाम ॥ (*tasya vyuṣṭivāhano 'śvaratho dakṣiṇā | trayo 'śvā dvau savyaṣṭasārathī te paṃcaprāṇā yo vai prāṇaḥ sa vātastadyate tasya karmaṇa eṣā dakṣiṇā tasmātpaṃcavātīyaṃ nāma ‖*)
(6. 75. 7-7-6-7)

This is the explanation of the offering of oblations named Pañcavātīya. Here, what are the five oblations? They are three horses, a warrior, and a charioteer. The five breaths are these three horses, the warrior and the charioteer. These five breaths are the fivefold transformations of Vāyu. Therefore, since he is the accomplisher of the sacrifice by the oblations that are his own five forms, a kind of five-fold priesthood is established through this Pañcavātīya quality. Besides this, the five-fold priesthood has a spiritual meaning as well. The explanation below contains both purports, the one concerning the deities and the one concerning the self, and it also makes clear the five-fold priesthood of Vāyu.

प्राणो वै वायुः । प्राणोग्निस्तस्येमा इष्टका । यः प्राणो व्यानोऽपानः समान उदानः ॥ (*prāṇo vai vāyuḥ | prāṇognistasyemā iṣṭakā | yaḥ prāṇo vyāno 'pānaḥ samāna udānaḥ ‖*)
(Maitryupaniṣad 6-33)

From one point of view the Gārhapatya fire is in the form of the year, which consists of the five seasons. From another point of view this same Gārhapatya is in the form of Vāyu, which consists of the five breaths. Prāṇa, apāna, vyāna,

### Printed p. 406

udāna and samāna, the five breaths so named, are the bricks of this Vāyu in the form of the Gārhapatya. It is described that Vāyu, the accomplisher of this offering in the form of the five breaths, has the five-fold priesthood.

Besides this, how Vāyu, comprising these five breaths, is the accomplisher of the offering in the sacrifice that consists of the realisation of the Self is thus: the description of this offering of a spiritual nature is as follows.

तस्य ह ना एतस्य हृदयस्य पंच देवसुषयः स योऽस्य प्राज्‌सुषि स प्राणस्तच्चक्षुः स आदित्यस्तदेतत्तेजोऽन्नाद्यमित्युपासीत तेजस्व्यन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*tasya ha nā etasya hṛdayasya paṃca devasuṣayaḥ sa yo 'sya prājsuṣi sa prāṇastaccakṣuḥ sa ādityastadetattejo 'nnādyamityupāsīta tejasvyannādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Chā. U. 3-13-1)

In the heart of a person there are five paths to the sacrifice that is the realisation of Brahman. Among these, the door of the eastern direction is the breath. That is the eye, and that is the sun. One should meditate upon that radiance as food. One who knows this truth becomes radiant and an eater of food.

अथ योऽस्य दक्षिणः सुषिः । स व्यानस्तच्छोत्रं स चंद्रमास्तदेतच्छिश्च यशश्चेत्युपासीत श्रीमान् यशस्वी भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*atha yo 'sya dakṣiṇaḥ suṣiḥ | sa vyānastacchotraṃ sa caṃdramāstadetacchiśca yaśaścetyupāsīta śrīmān yaśasvī bhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Bhā. U. 3-13-2)**NOTE**

The path of the southern direction is vyāna. That is the ear and the moon. The worshipper should meditate upon it as fame and as wealth. One who knows this truth becomes wealthy and famous.

अथ योऽस्य प्रत्यज् सुषि: सोऽपानः सा वाक् सोऽग्निस्तदेतद्ब्रह्मवर्चसमन्नाद्य मित्युपासीत ब्रह्मवर्चस्यन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद । (*atha yo 'sya pratyaj suṣi: so 'pānaḥ sā vāk so 'gnistadetadbrahmavarcasamannādya mityupāsīta brahmavarcasyannādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda |*)
(Bhā. U. 3-13-3)**NOTE**

The path of the western direction is apāna. That is speech and fire. The worshipper should meditate upon it as the knowledge of Brahman, which is the cause of the brilliance of Brahman, and as food. One who knows this truth becomes possessed of the brilliance of Brahman and an eater of food.

अथ सोऽस्योदज्‌सुषिः स समानस्तन्मनः स पर्जन्यस्तदेतत्कीर्तिश्च व्युष्टिश्चेत्युपासीत कीर्तिमान्व्युमान्भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*atha so 'syodajsuṣiḥ sa samānastanmanaḥ sa parjanyastadetatkīrtiśca vyuṣṭiścetyupāsīta kīrtimānvyumānbhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Bhā. U. 3-13-2)**NOTE**

Samāna is the path of the northern direction. That is the mind-principle and is of the nature of Parjanya. That is fame and beauty. One who knows this truth becomes famous and powerful.

### Printed p. 407

अथ योऽस्योर्ध्वः सुषिः स उदानः स वायुः स आकाशस्तदेतदोजश्च महश्चेत्युपासीतौजस्वी महस्वान्भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*atha yo 'syordhvaḥ suṣiḥ sa udānaḥ sa vāyuḥ sa ākāśastadetadojaśca mahaścetyupāsītaujasvī mahasvānbhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Chā. U. 3-13-5)

Udāna is the door of the upper part. That is Vāyu and that is space. The worshipper should meditate upon it as vigour and as strength. One who knows this becomes vigorous and strong.

ते वा एते पंच ब्रह्मपुरुषाः स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपाः एतानेवं पंच .... .... .... .... स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपान्वेद ॥ (*te vā ete paṃca brahmapuruṣāḥ svargasya lokasya dvārapāḥ etānevaṃ paṃca .... .... .... .... svargasya lokasya dvārapānveda ‖*)
(Bhā. U. 3-13-6)**NOTE**

These five divisions of Vāyu, of the nature of breath, are the door-keepers of the Person who is Brahman. One who knows this truth attains union with Brahman; thus the spiritual five-fold priesthood is described. Śaṅkarācārya, explaining this in his commentary, has explained it with sentences such as प्राणाय स्वाहेति हुतं हविः सर्वमेतत्तर्पयतीति (*prāṇāya svāheti hutaṃ haviḥ sarvametattarpayatīti*) (Chā. U. Śa. Bhā. 3-13.1)**NOTE**.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रति॑ मे॒ स्तोम॒मदि॑तिर्जगृभ्यात्सू॒नुं न मा॒ता हृद्यं॑  ॒॑
> सुशेवं ।  
> ब्रह्म॑ प्रि॒यं दे॒वहि॑तं॒ यदस्त्व॒हं मि॒त्रे वरु॑णे॒ यन्म॑यो॒भु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रति । मे । स्तोमं अदितिः । जगृभ्यात् । सूनुं । न । माता । हृद्यं । सुशेवं ।  
> ब्रह्म । प्रियं । देव्यहितं । यत् । अस्ति । अहं । मित्रे । वरुणे । यत् ।  
> मयःभु ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 408

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मे मदीयं स्तोमं स्तोत्रमदितिर्देवता प्रति जगृभ्यात् । प्रतिगृह्णातु ।
> सूनुं न माता स्वतनुजं जननीव । सा यथा प्रतिगृह्यालिंग्य परितुष्यति तद्वदित्यर्थः ।
> कीदृशं तं । हृद्यं हृदयंगमं सुशेवं शोभनसुखकरं । एतद्वयं साधारणं ।
> किंच ब्रह्म मंत्रजातं प्रियं प्रियकरु देवहितं देवैः प्राप्यं यदस्ति यद्ब्रह्म
> मयोभु सुखसाधनं तदहं मित्रे वरुणे च प्रापयामिोति शेषः । यद्वा । मित्रे
> वरुणे चाहोरात्राभिमानिदेवयोर्यदुक्तलक्षणं ब्रह्म परिवृढं यज्ञादिरूपं
> कर्मास्ति तदहं धारयामिोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa takes the word मे (*me*) as "mine" and says that the deity Aditi is to accept my praise (stoma, stotra). "As a mother her own son": as a mother, having received her son and embraced him, is pleased, so may she be, this is the meaning. What kind of praise is it? It is heart-going (हृद्यं (*hṛdyaṃ*)) and gives good happiness (सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*)); these two qualities are common to the praise. Further, the brahma, the mass of mantras, which is pleasing, dear to the gods and attainable by the gods, which is a means of happiness: that I convey to Mitra and Varuṇa, "I convey" being the word to be supplied. Or else: of Mitra and Varuṇa, the presiding deities of day and night, there is the brahma of the stated character, the great rite in the form of sacrifice and so on, and that I uphold.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- माता (*mātā*)—the mother
- सूनं न (*sūnaṃ na*)—as (she) lovingly embraces her own child**NOTE**
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi
- मे (*me*)—my
- हृद्यं (*hṛdyaṃ*)—the pleasing
- सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*)—the auspicious
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—praise
- प्रति जगृभ्यात् (*prati jagṛbhyāt*)—may she accept
- यत् ब्रह्म (*yat brahma*)—which mantra
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—is affection-producing
- देवहितं (*devahitaṃ*)—beneficial to the gods
- अस्ति (*asti*)—is
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- मयोभु (*mayobhu*)—is the giver of happiness, that mantra
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- मित्रे (*mitre*)—addressing Mitra
- वरुणे (*varuṇe*)—addressing Varuṇa (I offer)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a mother lovingly embraces her child, may Aditi lovingly accept my praise, which is pleasing and auspicious. The mantra that is affection-producing, beneficial to the gods and giver of happiness, that mantra I offer, addressing Mitra and Varuṇa.**NOTE**

##### English translation
May Aditi accept my affectionate and devoted praise, as a mother (the endearments of) a son; the pleasing, delightful prayer that is approved of by the gods I address to Varuna and Mitra.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उदी॑रय क॒वित॑मं कवी॒नामु॒नत्तै॑नम॒भि मध्वा॑ घृ॒तेन॑ ।  
> स नो॒ वसू॑नि॒ प्रय॑ता हि॒तानि॑ चं॒द्राणि॑ दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता सु॑वाति ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ईरय । कवितमं । कवीनां । उनत्त । एनं । अभि । मध्वा । धृतेन ।  
> सः । नः । वसूनि । प्रयता । हितानि । चंद्राणि । देवः । सविता । सुवाति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उदीरयेत्येष्टैकादशिने सावित्रे पशौ वपायज्या । सूत्रितं च । उदीरय
> कवितमं कवीनां भगं धियं वाजयंतः पुरंधिमिति द्वे । आ ३-७. । इति ॥
> अनया सविता च स्तूयते । हे ऋत्विजः कवीनां कवितमं क्रांतदर्शिनममुं
> पुरोवर्तिनमग्निं सवितारं वोदीरय । ऊर्ध्व० प्रापयत । हर्षयतेत्यर्थः । एनं
> देवं मध्वा मधुरेण सोमरसेन धृतेन चाभ्यनत्त । अभिषिंचत । तर्पयतेत्यर्थः ।
> स सविता देवो नोऽस्मभ्यं वसूनि निवासयोग्यानि गवादिधनानि प्रयता प्रयतानि
> हितानि चंद्राण्याह्लादकानि हिरण्यानि सुवाति । प्रयच्छत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Ṛk beginning उदीरय कवितमं कवीनां भगं धियं वाजयंतः पुरंधिमिति द्वे । (*udīraya kavitamaṃ kavīnāṃ bhagaṃ dhiyaṃ vājayaṃtaḥ puraṃdhimiti dve |*) is the vapā-yājyā at the animal sacrifice to Savitṛ in the rite named in the glued word उदीरयेत्येष्टैकादशिने (*udīrayetyeṣṭaikādaśine*)**NOTE**, and the sūtra says so: "'Udīraya kavitamaṃ kavīnām' and 'bhagaṃ dhiyaṃ vājayantaḥ puraṃdhim', two verses" (Ā. 3-7). By this Ṛk Savitṛ is praised. O priests, rouse this Agni, or Savitṛ, who stands before you, the most far-seeing (kavitama, "of penetrating vision") of the poets; carry him upward, that is, gladden him. Anoint this god with sweet Soma juice and with ghee; that is, satisfy him. May that god Savitṛ give us wealth (vasūni, fit for dwelling, such as cattle and the like), well offered (prayatā, prayatāni), beneficial, delightful (candrāṇi, āhlādaka) gold; this is the meaning of "may he give" (suvāti).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कवीनां (*kavīnāṃ*)—among poets
- कवितमं (*kavitamaṃ*)—the most excellent poet, Savitṛ
- उदीरय (*udīraya*)—gladden
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this god
- मध्वा (*madhvā*)—with sweet Soma juice
- घृतेन च (*ghṛtena ca*)—and with ghee
- अभि उनत्त (*abhi unatta*)—satisfy
- सः सविता (*saḥ savitā*)—that same god Savitṛ
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- प्रयता (*prayatā*)—complete
- हितानि (*hitāni*)—beneficial
- चंद्रानि (*caṃdrāni*)—delightful**NOTE**
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—wealth
- सुवाति (*suvāti*)—may he give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, gladden the god Savitṛ, the most excellent of poets. Satisfy this god with sweet Soma juice. May that same god Savitṛ give us wealth that is complete, beneficial and delightful.

### Printed p. 410

##### English translation
Celebrate, (priests), the most prophetic of the prophets; imbue him with the sweet libation, and may the divine Savitri bestow upon us ample beneficial, and delightful riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk beginning with the word उदीरय (*udīraya*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra in the vapā-offering made in the animal sacrifice to the deity called Ekādaśī Savitṛ**NOTE**, as is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra उदीरय कवितमं कवीनां भगं धियं वाजयंतः पुरंधिमिति द्वे (*udīraya kavitamaṃ kavīnāṃ bhagaṃ dhiyaṃ vājayaṃtaḥ puraṃdhimiti dve*) (Ā. 3-7).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> समिं॑द्र णो॒ मन॑सा नेषि॒ गोभिः॒ सं सू॒रिभि॑र्हरिवः॒ सं स्व॒स्ति ।  
> सं ब्रह्म॑णा दे॒वहि॑तं॒ यदस्ति॒ सं दे॒वानां॑ सुम॒त्या य॒ज्ञिया॑नां ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । इंद्र । नः । मनसा । नेषि । गोभिः । सं । सूरिभिः । हरिवः । सं । स्वस्ति ।  
> सं । ब्रह्मणा । देव्यहितं । यत् । अस्ति । सं । देवानां । सुमत्या । यज्ञियानां ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र नोऽस्मान्मनसा प्रकृष्टेन चेतसा गोभिः सह सं नेषि । नयसि ।
> अस्मान् गाः प्रापयसीत्यर्थः । एवं सर्वत्र । हे हरिवो हरिभ्यां तद्वन्निंद्र सूरिभिर्मेधाविभिः पुत्रैर्यृत्विग्निर्वा सं नेषि । तथा स्वस्ति स्वस्तिभिः क्षेमैः सं नेषि । ब्रह्मणा
> प्रभूतेनान्नेन सं नेषि । यदन्नं देवहितमस्ति तेन । किंच यज्जियानां यज्ञार्हाणां देवानां सुमत्यानुग्रहबुद्ध्या सं नेषि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you lead us (सं नेषि (*saṃ neṣi*)) with a mind, that is, with an excellent thought, together with cows; that is, you bring cows to us. In the same way the verb is to be supplied everywhere. O Harivat, that is, Indra, who has the two bay horses, you lead us with the wise (सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)), that is, with sons or with priests**NOTE**; likewise with blessings (स्वस्ति (*svasti*)), that is, with well-being, you lead us. With brahma, that is, with abundant food, you lead us: with the food which is beneficial to the gods. Further, you lead us with the good will (सुमत्या (*sumatyā*)), that is, with the thought of favour, of the gods who are worthy of sacrifice.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, with your mind full of favour, unite us with cows, with wise sons, and with abundant food that is beneficial also to the gods. And cause the thought of favour of the gods who are worthy of sacrifice to be upon us.

With a (willing) mind, Indra, you associate us with cattle, with pious (priests) and, lord of steeds, with prosperity, with (sacrificial) food that is agreeable to the gods, and with the favour of the adorable deities.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र लिंगोक्ता देवताः । भगो देवः सविता च रायो धनस्य स्वाम्यंशस्वष्टा वृत्रस्य हंतेंद्रश्च एते देवा धनानां संजितः सम्यग्जेतार ऋभुक्षा ऋभुर्वाजश्च उत वापि च पुरंधिः बहुधीः । विभोच्यते । एते चामृतासोऽमृता
> अमरणधर्माणो भगादिदेवास्तुरासोऽस्मद्यज्ञं प्रति त्वरमाणाः संतो नोऽस्मानवंतु । रक्षंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here the deities are stated by their gender. Bhaga, the god Savitṛ, the master of wealth, Aṃśa, and स्वष्टा (*svaṣṭā*)**NOTE**, and Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra: these gods are the conquerors of riches, that is, those who rightly conquer them; Ṛbhukṣan, that is, Ṛbhu, and Vāja, and also Purandhi, that is, one of much wisdom, who is called Vibhu. And these gods, Bhaga and the others, being immortal, of the nature of not dying, hastening toward our sacrifice, may protect us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the divine
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—Bhaga
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—the master of wealth
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ
- अंशः (*aṃśaḥ*)—Aṃśa
- वृत्रस्य (*vṛtrasya*)—the slayer of Vṛtra
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—over riches
- संजितः (*saṃjitaḥ*)—who have obtained mastery
- ऋभुक्षाः (*ṛbhukṣāḥ*)—Ṛbhu
- वाजः (*vājaḥ*)—Vāja
- उत (*uta*)—and also
- पुरंधिः (*puraṃdhiḥ*)—Vibhvan, of many kinds of wisdom
- अमृतासः (*amṛtāsaḥ*)—all the gods who are free from the nature of death
- तुरासः (*turāsaḥ*)—being eager to come to our sacrifice
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*)—may protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Bhaga, Savitṛ the master of wealth, Aṃśa, Indra the slayer of Vṛtra, Ṛbhu, Vāja and Vibhvan, who have obtained mastery over riches, and all the gods who are free from the nature of death, being eager to come to our sacrifice, may protect us.

##### English translation
May the divine Bhaga, Savitri, the lord of wealth, Ansa, Indra (the slayer) of vritra, (all) the conquerors of riches, Ribhukshin, Vaja and also Purandhi, immortals, hastening (to our sacrifice) preserve us.
