> न ते॒ पूर्वे॑ मघव॒न्नाप॑रासो॒ न वी॒र्यं१॒॑१ नूत॑नः॒ कश्च॒नाप॑ ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 413

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मरुत्वतः । अप्रतिइतस्य । जिष्णोः । अजूर्यतः । प्र । ब्रवाम । कृतानि ।  
> न । ते । पूर्वे । मघवन् । न । अपरासः । न । वीर्यं । नूतनः । कः । चन ।  
> आप ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयं यजमाना मरुत्वतो मरुद्धिस्तद्वत इंद्रस्य कृतानि कर्माणि प्र
> ब्रवाम । प्रख्यापयाम । कीदृशस्य तस्य । अप्रतीतस्याप्रतिगतस्य युद्धेऽपलायमानस्य । न केवलं तावन्मात्रं । जिष्णोर्जयनशीलस्याजूर्यतोऽजीर्यमाणस्य ।
> सर्वदा यून इत्यर्थः । अथ प्रत्यक्षेणोच्यते । हे मघवन्निंद्र ते तव वीर्यं
> पराक्रमं पूर्वे पुरातनाः पुरुषा नापुः । नापरासोऽपरेऽपि नापुः । किं बहुना ।
> नूतनः कश्चनाश्चर्यभूतो यः कोऽपि वीर्यं नाप । न प्राप्नोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, the sacrificers, proclaim, that is, make known, the deeds of Indra, who is possessed of the Maruts (मरुत्वतो (*marutvato*)). What kind of Indra is he? He is unopposed (अप्रतीतस्य (*apratītasya*)), that is, one who has not retreated, who does not run away in battle. And not only that: he is victorious (जिष्णोः (*jiṣṇoḥ*)), that is, by nature a conqueror, and unageing (अजूर्यतः (*ajūryataḥ*)), that is, one who does not grow old, always young. Now it is said directly: O Maghavan Indra, the ancient men did not attain your valour, that is, your prowess; the later ones did not attain it either. What more is there to say? Whoever is new, a marvel, whoever he may be, does not attain valour.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अप्रतीतस्य (*apratītasya*)—of the unopposed
- जिष्णोः (*jiṣṇoḥ*)—the victorious
- अजूरतः (*ajūrataḥ*)—the undecaying**NOTE**
- मरुत्वतः (*marutvataḥ*)—Indra, who is with the Maruts
- कृतानि (*kṛtāni*)—deeds
- प्र ब्रवाम (*pra bravāma*)—we praise
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, the possessor of wealth
- ते (*te*)—your
- वीर्यं (*vīryaṃ*)—prowess
- पूर्वे (*pūrve*)—none of the earlier ones
- न (*na*) (आपुः (*āpuḥ*))—had attained
- अपरासः (*aparāsaḥ*)—none of those after them
- न (*na*)—attained
- नूतनः कश्चन (*nūtanaḥ kaścana*)—any among the moderns
- न आप (*na āpa*)—cannot attain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We praise the heroic deeds of Indra, who is unopposed, victorious, undecaying and always in the company of the Maruts. O Indra, possessor of wealth, none of those who came before attained your prowess. None of those who came after attained it. None among the moderns can attain it.

##### English translation
We celebrate the exploits of Marutwat, the unrecoiling, the victorious, the undecaying: neither the ancients, Maghavan, nor their successors, have attained your prowess, nor has any one recent attained it.

> उप॑ स्तुहि प्रथ॒मं र॑त्न॒धेयं॒ बृह॒स्पतिं॑ सनि॒तारं॒ धना॑नां  
> यः शंस॑ते स्तुव॒ते शंभ॑विष्यः पुरू॒वसु॑रा॒गम॒ज्योहु॑वानं ॥

> यः । शंसते । स्तुवते । शंभविष्यति । पुरुवसुः । आगमत् । जोहुवानं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अंतरात्मन् त्वं प्रथमं मुख्यं । प्रकृष्टतममित्यर्थः । रत्नधेयं रमणीयधनदातारं धनानां हनिर्लक्षणानां सनितारं संभक्तारं । अथवा रत्नशब्देन
> मणिमुक्तादयो गृहीता इह धनशब्देन गवादयः । गनादिदातारं बृहस्पतिं
> बृहतो मंत्रस्य पतिं स्वामिनं देवमुप स्तुहि । यो देवः शंसते शस्त्रैः स्तुवतॆ ।
> सामभिर्यजमानाय शंभविष्ठः सुखस्य भावयित्कृतमो भवति । यश्च जोहुवानमाह्वयंतं यजमानं पुरूनसुः प्रभूतधनः सन्नागमत् आगच्छति तमुप स्तुहि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O inner self, you praise (उप स्तुहि (*upa stuhi*)) the god Bṛhaspati. He is first (प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)), that is, chief, the most excellent; the giver of delightful wealth (रत्नधेयं (*ratnadheyaṃ*)); the distributor, the one who apportions, of riches that are of the nature of oblations**NOTE**. Or else: by the word ratna jewels, pearls and the like are meant, and here by the word dhana cows and the like; he is the giver of cows and the like. Bṛhaspati is the lord, the master, of the great mantra. Praise that god who praises the sacrificer with the śastras and extols him with the sāmans, who is the greatest producer of happiness (शंभविष्ठः (*śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ*)), and who, being rich in abundant wealth, comes to the sacrificer who calls upon him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O inner self)
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- शंसते (*śaṃsate*)—who praises with the śastra mantras
- स्तुवते (*stuvate*)—to the sacrificer who extols with the sāmans and the like
- शंभविष्ठः (*śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ*)—the giver of happiness; and he who
- चोहुवानं (*cohuvānaṃ*)—to the sacrificer who prays that he may come to his help**NOTE**
- पुरूनसुः (*purūnasuḥ*)—possessed of abundant wealth**NOTE**
- आगमत् (*āgamat*)—comes, such a one
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—the best of all
- रत्नधेयं (*ratnadheyaṃ*)—the giver of jewels and other riches**NOTE**
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—of the wealth of oblation-food and the like
- सनितारं (*sanitāraṃ*)—the distributor
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- उप स्तुहि (*upa stuhi*)—praise with hymns

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O inner self, praise and extol Bṛhaspati, who gives happiness to the sacrificer who praises with the śastras and the like and extols with the sāmans and the like, who comes bringing abundant wealth to the sacrificer who prays to him for help, who is the best of all, the giver of riches such as jewels, and the distributor of the wealth of oblation-food and the like.

### Printed p. 415

##### English translation
Glorify the first donor of precious treasure, Brihaspati, the distributer of riches, the bestower of great happiness upon him who recites or chants (his praise), who comes laden with ample wealth to his invoker.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मघवानो धनवंतः सुवीराः शोभनपुत्राश्च भवंति । ये त्वदनुगृहिता अश्वदा
> बहूनामश्वानां दातारः संति । उत वाथवा गोदाः संति । ये च वस्त्रदाः सुभगाः
> शोभनधनाः संति तेषु सर्वॆषु रायो धनानि संभवंत्विति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Bṛhaspati, the sacrificers who are united with your protections (तवोतिभी (*tavotibhī*)), who are unharmed, wealthy and have good sons, that is, good heroes. Those who, favoured by you, are givers of many horses; or else givers of cows; and those who are givers of clothing and are fortunate, that is, possessed of good wealth: among all of these let riches, that is, wealth, come to be; "let come to be" is the word to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*)—O Bṛhaspati
- तव ऊतिभिः (*tava ūtibhiḥ*)—with your protections
- सचमानाः (*sacamānāḥ*)—the sacrificers who are united
- अरिष्टाः (*ariṣṭāḥ*)—unharmed (by enemies)
- मघवानः (*maghavānaḥ*)—possessed of wealth
- सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*)—and united also with excellent sons and the like
- ये सुभगाः (*ye subhagāḥ*)—whoever have obtained the wealth of your favour
- अश्वदाः (*aśvadāḥ*)—givers of horses
- उत वा (*uta vā*)—or else
- गोदाः (*godāḥ*)—givers of cows, and
- ये (*ye*) (च (*ca*))—who
- वस्त्रदाः (*vastradāḥ*)—givers of clothing
- संति (*saṃti*)—are
- तेषु (*teṣu*)—among such
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—let riches abound

### Printed p. 416

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bṛhaspati, the sacrificers who are united with your protections are unharmed by enemies, possessed of wealth and endowed with excellent sons and the like. Among all such as, having obtained the wealth of your favour, are givers of horses, givers of cows and givers of clothing, let riches abound.

##### English translation
Associated, Brihaspati, with your protections, (men) are unharmed (by foes), and become opulent and blessed with descendants: may wealth devolve on those who are generous, and givers of horses, of cows, of clothes.

> न उक्षैः ।  
> अप॑व्रतान्प्रस॒वे वा॑वृथ॒ान्‌ब्र॑ह्म॒द्विषः॒ सूर्या॑द्यावयस्व ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विसर्माणं । कृणुहि । वित्तं । एषां । ये । भुंजते । अपृणंतः । नः । उक्षैः ।  
> अपव्रतान् । प्रसवे । ववृधानान् । ब्रह्मद्विषः । सूर्यात् । यवयस्व ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषां वक्ष्यमाणानां वित्तं धनं विसर्माणं विसरणशीलं कृणुहि । कुरु । हे
> ब्रह्मणस्पते । एषामित्युक्तं केषामित्याह । ये भुंजतेऽपृणंतोऽप्रयच्छंतः ।
> केभ्यः । उक्थैः स्तुतिप्रतिपादकैः शस्त्रैर्विशिष्टेभ्यो नोऽस्मभ्यं । तानपव्रतानपगतकर्मणः प्रसव उत्पत्तिमति मनुष्यलोके ववृधानान् वर्धमानान ब्रह्मद्विषो
> ब्राह्मणद्वेष्टन्मंत्रद्वेष्टन् ना सूर्याद्यावयस्व । पृथक्कुरु । अंधकारे
> स्थापयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Make the wealth of these who are about to be named (एषां (*eṣāṃ*)) scattering, that is, of a nature to disperse (विसर्माणं (*visarmāṇaṃ*)), O Brahmaṇaspati**NOTE**. Of whom does he say "of these"? Of those who enjoy without giving, that is, without bestowing: on whom? On us, who are distinguished by the ukthas, the śastras which convey praise. Make dispersing the wealth of those who are devoid of rites (अपव्रतान् (*apavratān*)), that is, whose works have gone astray, who are prospering in the world of men, the place of birth, who are haters of brahma, that is, haters of Brāhmaṇas and haters of mantras. Separate them from the sun; put them apart, that is, place them in darkness.

### Printed p. 417

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Bṛhaspati)
- उक्थैः (*ukthaiḥ*)—who praise with the śastra and other mantras
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- ये (*ye*)—who
- अपृणंतः (*apṛṇaṃtaḥ*)—without giving
- भुंजते (*bhuṃjate*)—enjoy (all wealth) themselves
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of such greedy people
- वित्तं (*vittaṃ*)—the wealth
- विसर्माणं (*visarmāṇaṃ*)—so that it scatters
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—make
- आपव्रतान् (*āpavratān*)—who are without Vedic rites**NOTE**
- प्रसवे (*prasave*)—in the world of men
- ववृधान् (*vavṛdhān*)—while prospering
- ब्रह्मद्विषः (*brahmadviṣaḥ*)—those fallen from the rites, who despise the mantras and the like without knowing their greatness
- सूर्यात् (*sūryāt*)—from the sun
- यवयस्व (*yavayasva*)—separate

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bṛhaspati, make the wealth of those greedy rich men who, without giving to us, who are distinguished by praise with śastras and the like, enjoy all wealth themselves, scatter and disperse. Those who, while prospering in the world of men, are devoid of Vedic rites and despise the mantras and the like without knowing their greatness, those who have fallen from the rites: separate them from the sun, that is, place them in pitch darkness, where there is no light of the sun.**NOTE**

##### English translation
Render transitory the riches of those who partake of enjoyment without giving satisfaction (to those who are eminent) by holy hymns: put apart from the sun, those who perform not sacred rites, and who, though prospering in their posterity, are the adversaries of prayer.

#### Ṛk 10

> य ओह॑ते र॒क्षसो॑ दे॒ववी॑तावच॒क्रेभि॒स्तं म॑रुतो॒ निया॑त ।  
> यो वः॒ शमीं॑ शशमा॒नस्य॒ निंदा॑त्तु॒च्छ्यान्मामा॑न्करते  ॒
> सिष्टिदानः ॥ १० ॥

> यः । ओहते । रक्षसः । देव्यवीत् । अचक्रेभिः । तं । मरुतः । नि । यात ।

> यः । वः । शमीं । शशमानस्य । निंदात् । तुच्छ्यान् । कामान् । करते ।  
> सिस्विदानः ॥ १८ ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो यजमानो रक्षसो बलिनो राक्षसानोहते प्रापयति देवनीत् ।
> देवानां नीतिः प्राप्तिर्भक्षणं ना यत्र स तथोक्तः । तस्मिन्यज्ञे । अन्यथानुष्ठानादिनासुरं करोतीत्यर्थः । तं यजमानमचक्रेभिरचक्रै रथैर्हे मरुतो नि यात ।
> नितरां प्रापयतांधकारं । यद्वा । अचक्रेभिरिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । चक्रशब्देनांगान्युच्यंते । पुनःपुनरंगरहितैः केवलैरेव प्रधानैरोहते प्रापयति । सांगं हि
> कर्म देवानभ्येति । यश्च वो युष्माकं शमीं कर्म स्तुतिलक्षणं शशमानस्य मम
> संबंधि निंदात् निंदेत् वैदिकं ज्योतिष्टोमादिरूपं कर्म निंदति स्वयं च
> तुच्छान्नश्वरान् कामान् कृष्यादिजनितभोगान् करते कुरुते सिष्टिदानः स्विद्यन्नात्मानं क्लेशयन् । अथवा युष्मासु कमनीयान्भोगान् तुच्छान् करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer who brings (ओहते (*ohate*)) the powerful rākṣasas into the sacrifice called देवनीत् (*devanīt*), that is, the sacrifice in which there is the going of the gods, their arrival, their partaking**NOTE**, and who makes it demoniac by performing it wrongly and the like: that sacrificer, O Maruts, drive down with chariots without wheels (अचक्रेभिः (*acakrebhiḥ*)) into darkness. Or else: अचक्रेभिः (*acakrebhiḥ*) is to be construed with what goes before; by the word "wheel" the limbs of the rite are meant; he brings it again and again with only the principal parts, without the limbs; whereas a rite with its limbs reaches the gods. And whoever of you reviles the rite of praise (शमीं (*śamīṃ*)) belonging to me who am praising, that is, reviles the Vedic rite such as the Jyotiṣṭoma and the like, and himself pursues futile and perishable desires, enjoyments born of ploughing and the like, sweating, that is, tormenting himself. Or else: he makes the desirable enjoyments among you worthless.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sacrificer
- देवनीत् (*devanīt*)—in the sacrifice that proceeds for the satisfaction of the gods
- रक्षसः (*rakṣasaḥ*)—the demons
- ओहते (*ohate*)—brings together
- तं (*taṃ*)—that sacrificer
- अचक्रेभिः (*acakrebhiḥ*)—with chariots without wheels
- नि यात (*ni yāta*)—push into darkness
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- वः (*vaḥ*)—addressed to you
- शमीं (*śamīṃ*)—while performing a rite accompanied by praise
- शशमानस्य (*śaśamānasya*)—me, who praise (you) (or those who belong to me)
- निंदात् (*niṃdāt*)—reviles, (he)
- सिष्टिदानः (*siṣṭidānaḥ*)—exposing himself to affliction and pouring out sweat
- तुच्छान् (*tucchān*)—vain
- कामान् (*kāmān*)—desires for enjoyment
- करते (*karate*)—imagines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, the sacrificer who brings demons into the sacrifice that proceeds for the satisfaction of the gods, push that sacrificer into darkness with chariots without wheels. The one who reviles me, who offer praise to you by performing a rite directed to you, or those who belong to me, he, exposing himself merely to affliction and pouring out sweat, imagines these desires for enjoyment that are of no worth.

### Printed p. 419

##### English translation
Send, Maruts, into darkness, with (cars) devoid of wheels, the man who invites the Rakshasas to the food of the gods; (him also) who reviles me when offering praise to you : whilst sweating, he toils (to realize) vain desires.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमु॑ ष्टुहि॒ यः स्ति॒षुः सु॒धन्वा॒ यो विश्व॑स्य॒ क्षय॑ति बेष॒जस्य॑ ।  
> यक्ष्वा॑ म॒हे सौ॑मन॒साय॑ रु॒द्रं नमो॑भिर्दे॒वमसु॑रं  
> दुवस्य ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । ऊं इति । स्तुहि । यः । सुइषुः । सुधन्वा । यः । विश्वस्य । क्षयति । भेषजस्य ।  
> यक्ष्व । महे । सौमनसाय । रुद्रं । नमभिः । देवं । असुरं । दुवस्य ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आत्मन् तमु तमेव रुद्रं स्तुहि । स्तुतिं कुरु । यः स्विसु: शोभनवाणः
> सुधन्वा च । विरोधिहंतृत्वात्तुष्टुत्वं । यश्च विश्वस्य भेषजस्याषधस्य क्षयति ईश्वरो
> भवति । शारीरस्य सांसारिकस्य वा रिष्टस्य शमनायेश्वरस्य व्यतिरिक्तसौषधस्याभावाद्भिषक्तमत्वाच्चास्य भेषजस्वामित्वं । भिषक्तमं त्वा भिषजां शृणोमि । ऋग्वे २.३३-४. ।
> इत्यादिश्रुतेः । किंच तमेव रुद्रं दुःखात्तत्साधनाद्दुरिताद्वा मोचयितारं देवं
> यक्ष्व यज च महे महते सौमनसाय सुमनस्वाय । ईश्वराराधनाच्चित्तशांतिः
> प्रसिद्धा । किंच नमोभिर्हविर्भिर्नमस्कार्वैर्वा देवं द्योतमानमसुरं प्रकृष्वासुं । बलवंतमित्यर्थः । यद्वा । प्राणदातारु रुद्रं दुवस्य । परिचरेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O self, praise that very Rudra; make praise. He who has a good arrow (स्विसु: (*svisu:*))**NOTE** and a good bow; his praiseworthiness is due to his killing of opponents. And he who is lord of all medicine, that is, of all herbs: for the allaying of bodily or worldly ailment, since there is no remedy apart from the Lord and since he is the best of physicians, his lordship over medicine is established, as the śruti says, भिषक्तमं त्वा भिषजां शृणोमि । (*bhiṣaktamaṃ tvā bhiṣajāṃ śṛṇomi |*) (Ṛgve. 2.33-4)**NOTE**, and so on. Further, worship that Rudra, the god who delivers from suffering or from the evil that causes it, for great (महे (*mahe*)) good-mindedness; peace of mind from worship of the Lord is well known. Further, with salutations or with oblations, attend upon the shining god, the asura, that is, one of excellent life, the mighty one; or else: attend upon Rudra, the giver of breath.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Rudra
- स्विषुः (*sviṣuḥ*)—has an excellent arrow
- सुधन्वा (*sudhanvā*)—and has a bow that is effective
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of all
- भेषजस्य (*bheṣajasya*)—of the herbs as well

### Printed p. 420

- क्षयति (*kṣayati*)—is the lord; such a one
- तमु (*tamu*)—that very Rudra
- स्तुहि (*stuhi*)—praise
- रुद्रं (*rudraṃ*)—addressing that same Rudra
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- सौमनसाय (*saumanasāya*)—for the gain of an excellent state of mind
- यक्ष्य (*yakṣya*)—perform the sacrifice
- असुरं (*asuraṃ*)—the mighty
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—that same god
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with salutations
- दुवस्य (*duvasya*)—worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praise that Rudra who has an excellent arrow and an effective bow, who is the lord of all herbs. Perform the sacrifice addressed to that same Rudra for the gain of a great and excellent state of mind, and worship that same mighty god with salutations.

##### English translation
Praise him who has the sure arrow, the strong bow, who presides over all sanitary drugs; worship Rudra for a comprehensive and sound understanding; adore the powerful divinity with prostrations.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विभ्वत॒ष्टाः ।

> सरस्वती । बृहत्दिवा । उत । राका । दशस्यंतीः । वरिवस्यंतु । शुभ्राः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र लिंगोक्तदेवताः । दमूनसो दानमनसो दांतमनसो वापसश्चमसाश्वरथगवादिशोभनकर्मवंतः ॥ मत्त्वर्थो लुप्यते ॥ आत एव सुहस्ताः कुशलहस्ता

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here the deities are named by their gender. The word दमूनसो (*damūnaso*) means those of a giving mind or of a controlled mind; or else those who are अपसः (*apasaḥ*), doers of good work in making cups, chariots, cows and the like; the suffix of possession is dropped. For that very reason they are सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*), skilful of hand,

### Printed p. 421

> ये संति त ऋभवो वृष्णो वर्षकस्येंद्रस्य पत्निः पत्न्यः पालयित्यो नद्यो
> नदनशीला गंगाद्या निभ्वतष्टा ऋभूणां मध्यमेन कृताः सरस्वत्येतन्नामिका नदी
> वाग्देवी वा बृहद्दिवा प्रभूतदीप्तिरुतापि च राका देवी च दशस्यंतीर्दशस्यंत्यः
> कामान्प्रयच्छंत्यः शुभ्रा दीप्ताः ताश्च वरिवस्यंतु । अस्मभ्यं धनमिच्छंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

those who are such, the Ṛbhus; and the wives, that is, the protectresses, of the showerer, that is, of Indra the rain-giver; the rivers, those that roar, Gaṅgā and the others, made by the middle one of the Ṛbhus; Sarasvatī, the river of that name or the goddess of speech; Bṛhaddivā, of abundant radiance; and also the goddess Rākā; they who grant desires, the radiant; and may they favour us, that is, wish wealth for us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दमूनसः (*damūnasaḥ*)—of a giving mind
- अपसः (*apasaḥ*)—possessed of excellent work such as the making of cups
- सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*)—possessed of hands fit for skilful work
- ये (*ye*)—whichever Ṛbhus there are, those
- वृष्ण (*vṛṣṇa*)—of Indra, the showerer of desires
- पत्निः (*patniḥ*)—the wives
- विभृतष्टाः (*vibhṛtaṣṭāḥ*)—fashioned by Vibhu
- नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)—the rivers
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—Sarasvatī
- उत (*uta*)—and
- बृहद्दिवा (*bṛhaddivā*)—shining exceedingly
- राका (*rākā*)—the goddess Rākā
- दशस्यंतीः (*daśasyaṃtīḥ*)—supplying our desired objects
- शुभ्राः (*śubhrāḥ*)—being radiant
- वरिवस्यंतु (*varivasyaṃtu*)—may they bless us that we may gain wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Ṛbhus who are of giving mind, who are doers of excellent work such as the making of cups, who have hands fit for skilful work; the wives of Indra, the showerer of desires; the rivers fashioned by Vibhu; Sarasvatī; and the goddess Rākā, who shines exceedingly: may they too, supplying our desired objects and being radiant, bless us that we may gain wealth.

##### English translation
May the dexterous-handed, humble-minded artisans (of the gods, the Ribhus; may the wives of the showerer (Indra); may the rivers carved out by Vibhu; may Saraswathi and the brilliant Raka, the illustrious granters of desires, be willing to grant us riches.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सु सुष्टु प्र भरे प्रकर्षेण संपादयामि महे महते सुशरणाय शोभनरक्षकायेंद्राय पर्जन्याय वा सुसुखाय वा । किं । मेधां मतौ धीयमानां
> गिरं स्तुतिं । कीदृशीं । नव्यसीं नवतरामतिशयेन स्तुत्यां वा जायमानामिदानीमुत्पद्यमानां । नूतनामित्यर्थः । य इंद्रः पर्जन्यो वा आहना आहंता सेक्ता
> दुहितुर्दुहितृस्थानीयायाः पृथिव्या हिताय वक्षणासु नदीषु रूपा रूपाणि
> मिनानः कुर्वाण इदमुदकं नोऽस्मभ्यमकृणोत् करोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I bring forth well, that is, I prepare excellently, for the great one, the good protector, Indra or Parjanya, or the giver of good happiness, a praise held in the mind (मेधां (*medhāṃ*)), a hymn. Of what kind? New, that is, very recent, or very praiseworthy, and being born, that is, produced now: new, that is the meaning. Indra or Parjanya, who is the striker, that is, the sprinkler, for the good of the daughter, that is, the earth, who stands in the place of a daughter, making forms in the rivers, has made this water for us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- आहनाः (*āhanāḥ*)—as the one who pours out rain
- दुहितुः (*duhituḥ*)—of this earth, his daughter (for her good)
- वक्षणासु (*vakṣaṇāsu*)—in the rivers
- रूपा (*rūpā*)—forms of streams
- मिनानः (*minānaḥ*)—producing
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this water
- नः (*naḥ*)—for our good
- अकृणोत् (*akṛṇot*)—made
- महे (*mahe*)—who is great
- सुशरणाय (*suśaraṇāya*)—and the giver of an excellent refuge, to such Indra
- नव्यसीं (*navyasīṃ*)—new
- जायमानां (*jāyamānāṃ*)—just now made
- मेधां (*medhāṃ*)—and of the nature of meditation
- गिरं (*giraṃ*)—praise
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- प्र भरे (*pra bhare*)—I fashion, to offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra who, pouring out rain, for the good of the earth, his daughter, and producing forms of streams in the rivers, has made this water for our good: to offer to that great one, the giver of an excellent refuge, I fashion exceedingly a praise that is new, just now born, and of the nature of meditation.

### Printed p. 423

##### English translation
To the great protector, (Indra), I offer devoutly pious praise, new and originated (at this time): to him, the showerer, who for his daughter (earth). giving form to the rivers, has provided this water for our (use).
#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो अ॑ब्बि॒मा उ॑दनि॒मा इय॑र्ति॒ प्र वि॒द्युता॒ रोद॑सी उ॒क्षमा॑णः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र पर्जन्यः स्तूयते । सुष्टुतिः शोभना स्तुतिः स्तनयुतं गर्जंतं रुवंतं
> वर्षणजनितं शब्दं कुर्वाणमिळोऽन्नस्योदकस्य ना पतिं स्वामिनं हे जरितः स्तोतस्त्वदीया स्तुतिर्नूर्नं प्राश्याः । प्रकर्षेण वाप्नोतु । यश्च पर्जन्योऽब्बिमान् ।

> द्यावापृथिव्यावुक्षमाणः सिंचन् प्रेयर्ति गच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here Parjanya is praised. Sāyaṇa takes the verse thus: O worshipper, let your excellent praise surely reach, that is, attain in full measure, Parjanya, who thunders and roars, making the sound that is produced by raining, the lord of Ilā, that is, of food and of water. And that Parjanya who possesses the abbimān, the waters, that is, the clouds, and is full of water, goes forth sprinkling the two worlds, heaven and earth, with lightning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जरितः (*jaritaḥ*)—O worshipper
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Parjanya
- अब्दिमान् (*abdimān*)—who keeps the clouds under his own control
- उदनिमान् (*udanimān*)—who is possessed of water (and)
- विद्युता (*vidyutā*)—by lightning
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- उक्षमाणः (*ukṣamāṇaḥ*)—making them illumined
- प्र इयर्ति (*pra iyarti*)—moves about

### Printed p. 424
- स्तनयंतं (*stanayaṃtaṃ*)—one who thunders such
- रुवंतं (*ruvaṃtaṃ*)—producer of the sound that sprinkles rain
- इळः (*iḷaḥ*)—of food (or of water)
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—the lord, the god Parjanya
- सुष्टुतिः (*suṣṭutiḥ*)—your excellent praise
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—quickly
- प्र अश्याः (*pra aśyāḥ*)—go and reach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O worshipper, may your excellent praise go quickly and reach that Parjanya, the lord of food, who keeps all the clouds under his own control, who is full of water, who by his lightning makes heaven and earth shine, and who moves about thundering.

##### English translation
May your pious praise, oh worshipper, assuredly reach the thundering, roaring lord of Ila, who, impelling the clouds and distributing the rain, proceeds, illuminating the heaven and earth with lightning.

> मिश्रणेच्छून्वा उदुन्नतमत्यधिकमश्याः । व्याप्नुहि हे मनः । कामः संकल्पो राये
> धनार्थं मा मां स्वस्त्यविनश्वरं हवते । आह्वयति । प्रेरयतीत्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं
> तस्मात्पृषदश्वान्पृषद्वर्णाश्चोपेतानयासो यज्ञगंत्यनुपोपेत्यस्तुहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May this hymn, produced by me, reach the Maruts' might, turning towards it. Having praised them as a group, he now speaks of them as individuals: they are the sons of Rudra (their sonship to Rudra has been stated again and again), and they are youthful, or else desirous of union. The word for "up" is to be taken as "exceedingly": reach, O mind, exceedingly. Desire, that is, resolve, calls me, that is, impels me, towards wealth and towards imperishable well-being. Since this is so, approach and praise the Maruts who have spotted horses, that is, spotted in colour, and who go to the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रुद्रस्य (*rudrasya*)—of Rudra
- सूनून् (*sūnūn*)—the sons
- युवन्यून् (*yuvanyūn*)—and very youthful
- मारुतं (*mārutaṃ*)—of the Maruts
- शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)—the host
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—produced by me
- स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)—this hymn
- अच्छ (*accha*)—towards them
- उत् आश्याः (*ut āśyāḥ*)—may it go and reach, so as to be pleasing
- कामः (*kāmaḥ*)—my mental resolve
- राये (*rāye*)—being desirous of wealth
- मा (*mā*)—me
- स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—on an auspicious path
- हवते (*havate*)—impels
- पृषदश्वान् (*pṛṣadaśvān*)—those who ride horses of variegated colour
- आयासः (*āyāsaḥ*)—and who are going to the sacrifice, the gods
- उप (*upa*)—approaching
- स्तुहि (*stuhi*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this hymn, produced by me, go and reach the host of the Maruts, the sons of Rudra and very youthful, turning towards them and so as to be pleasing to them. My mental resolve, being desirous of wealth, impels me on an auspicious path alone. Approach and praise the gods who ride variegated horses and are going to the sacrifice.

##### English translation
May this hymn reach up to the presence of the might of the Maruts, the youthful sons of Rudra: the desire of riches incites me to holiness : glorify those who go to sacrifice on spotted steeds.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May this hymn, this praise, reach the deities beginning with Earth. For what purpose? For wealth. May every god, each and every deity, be easily invoked for me, that is, readily called. May Earth, the mother, the maker of all (or else, since Atri is earth-born, in a special sense the mother), not place us in ill-thought, that is, not establish us there.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषः स्तोमः (*eṣaḥ stomaḥ*)—this praise made by me

- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—for me
- सुहवो भूतु (*suhavo bhūtu*)—may be prayed to and called in an excellent manner
- माता (*mātā*)—the maker of the world
- पृथीवी (*pṛthīvī*)—Earth
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- दुर्मत् (*durmat*)—with ill-thought
- मा धात् (*mā dhāt*)—may she not place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This praise, made by me, for the sake of wealth, may go and reach in an excellent manner the deity Earth, the deity of the mid-region, the deities of the forest trees and the deities of the herbs.

### Printed p. 427
May every single deity be prayed to and called by me in an excellent manner. May Earth, the maker of the world, not join us with ill-thought.

##### English translation

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We would come together with the Aśvins' protection, which is new, that is, not experienced before by others; which is joy-producing, that is, brings about happiness; and which is well-leading, that is, has good guidance. O immortals, deathless Aśvins, bring us wealth, that is, make it reach us; bring also sons of good valour; bring also all good fortunes.

- सुप्रणीती (*supraṇītī*)—and excellently guiding
- अवसा (*avasā*)—together with protection
- सं गमेम (*saṃ gamema*)—may we be joined

- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- आ वहतं (*ā vahataṃ*)—bring
- आ उत (*ā uta*)—and further
- वीरान् (*vīrān*)—heroic sons
- आ (*ā*)—bring
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- सौभगानि (*saubhagāni*)—good fortunes
- आ (*ā*)—bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Together with protection that is new, never experienced before by anyone, joy-producing and excellent, may we always be possessed of them. O Aśvin deities, free from the nature of death, bring us wealth, heroic sons and all good fortunes.

##### English translation
May we ever be participant of the unprecedented, joy-conferring and well-guided protection of the Aswins: bring to us, immortal (Aswins,) riches, male progeny, and all good things.

## Sūkta 43 (Maṇḍala 5)
The forty-third hymn.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ धेनव इति सप्तदशर्चमेकादशं सूक्तमत्रेरार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वैश्वदेवं ।
> अत्रानुक्रमणिका । आ धेनवस्त्रोन्यतयोरुपांत्यैकपदेति ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥
> अपोनप्रीय एकधनासु हविर्धानं प्रति नीयमानास्वाद्यानुवचनीया । सूत्रितं
> च । आ धेनवः पयसा तूर्णार्थाः समन्या यंत्युप यंत्यन्याः । आ. ५. १. । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning आ धेनवः (*ā dhenavaḥ*) has seventeen Ṛks and is the eleventh sūkta. Its seer is Atri, its metre Triṣṭubh and its deity the Viśvedevas. For the Anukramaṇikā he cites the words on the penultimate Ṛk being of one pāda. The use is by indication (laiṅgika): at the Aponaptrīya offering, when the Ekadhanā waters are being led towards the Havirdhāna, the first Ṛk is to be recited as the Anuvacanīya. He supports this with the sūtra आ धेनवः पयसा तूर्णार्थाः समन्या यंत्युप यंत्यन्याः । (*ā dhenavaḥ payasā tūrṇārthāḥ samanyā yaṃtyupa yaṃtyanyāḥ |*) (Ā. 5. 1).
Anuvāda: This sūkta आ धेनवः (*ā dhenavaḥ*) is the eleventh sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has seventeen Ṛks. Atri is the seer of this sūkta; the Viśvedevas are the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said आ धेनवस्त्रूनैतयोरुपांत्यैकपदा (*ā dhenavastrūnaitayorupāṃtyaikapadā*). The use is by indication. At the Aponaptrīya sacrifice, when the Ekadhanā waters are carried to the Havirdhāna, the cart for bringing Soma, the first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra आ धेनवः पयसा तूर्णर्थाः समन्यायंत्युप यंत्यन्याः (*ā dhenavaḥ payasā tūrṇarthāḥ samanyāyaṃtyupa yaṃtyanyāḥ*) (Ā. 5-1).

- Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 43
- Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 2, Vargas 20, 21, 22

- Seer: Atri
- Deity: the Viśvedevas
- Metre: Ṛks 1-15, 17 Triṣṭubh; 16 Ekapadā

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ धे॒नवः॒ पय॑सा॒ तूर्ण॑र्था॒ अम॑र्धंती॒रुप॑ नो यंतु॒  ॑
> मध्वा ।  
> म॒हो रा॒ये बृ॑ह॒तीः स॒प्त विप्रो॑ मयो॒भुवो॑ जरि॒ता  ॑
> जोहवीति ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 430

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । धेनवः । पयसा । तूर्णिS अर्थाः । अनुर्धंतीः । उप । नः । यंतु । मध्वा ।  
> महः । राये । बृहतीः । सप्त । विप्रः । मयःसभुवः । जरिता । जोहवीति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धेनवः प्रीणयित्र्यो नद्यो मध्वा मधुरेण पयसा रसेन सहितास्तूर्ण्यर्थास्वरमाणगमनाः । अर्थोऽर्तॆः । नि १. १८. । इति यास्कः । अमर्धंतीरहिंसंत्यः सत्यो नोऽस्नानुपा यंतु । उपागच्छंतु । तदर्थ० महो महते राये
> धनाय बृहतीर्महतीः सप्त सर्पणस्वभावाः सप्तसंख्याका इमं मे गंगे । ऋग्वे
> १०. ७५. ५ । इति मंत्रोक्ता गंगाद्या ना । तत्र हि प्राधान्येन सप्तैवोक्ताः ।
> मयोभुवः सुखस्य भावयित्रिर्विप्रो विशेषेण प्रीणयिता जरिता स्तोता जोहवीति।
> आह्वयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The dhenus, the nourishing ones, are the rivers, accompanied by sweet milk, that is, sweet essence; they are swift in motion, for Yāska says that artha means going (Ni. 1. 18). Being unharming, may they come near to us. For the sake of great wealth they are the great ones, the seven, seven in number and of a flowing nature: the Gaṅgā and the others spoken of in the mantra इमं मे गंगे (*imaṃ me gaṃge*) (Ṛgve. 10. 75. 5)**NOTE**, where seven only are mentioned as the principal ones. They are mayobhuvaḥ, bringers of happiness. The vipra, the one who especially gratifies, the worshipper, the praiser, invokes them, calls them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—the rivers, which give satisfaction
- मध्वा (*madhvā*)—sweet
- पयसा (*payasā*)—together with water
- तूर्णार्थाः (*tūrṇārthāḥ*)—flowing swiftly
- अमर्धंतीः (*amardhaṃtīḥ*)—and not harming in any way
- नः उप (*naḥ upa*)—near to us
- आ यंतु (*ā yaṃtu*)—may they flow and come
- महे (*mahe*)—great**NOTE**
- राये (*rāye*)—for wealth
- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—of great nature
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number, the Gaṅgā and the rest
- मयोभुवः (*mayobhuvaḥ*)—and giving happiness, the rivers
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise
- जरिता (*jaritā*)—the praiser
- जोहवीति (*johavīti*)—invokes, calls with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the rivers, which give satisfaction to all men, come flowing near to us together with sweet water, flowing swiftly and not harming in any way. I, who am wise and a praiser, invoke with prayer the rivers, which are of great nature, seven in number, the Gaṅgā and the rest, and givers of happiness.

##### English translation
May the milch cows, quick-moving, doing no harm, come to us, (laden) with their sweet fluid; the wise worshipper invokes the seven-vast and joy-diffusing (rivers) for the sake of ample riches.

### Printed p. 431

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Rākā: Sāyaṇa has said earlier (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2.32-4)**NOTE** that Rākā means the full-moon day, which has a complete moon. The author of the Nirukta, explaining this word, says:
राका रातेर्दानकर्मणः (हविदाननिमित्तं हि सा) (*rākā rāterdānakarmaṇaḥ (havidānanimittaṃ hi sā)*)
(Ni. 11-30)
that is, the name Rākā is well known as formed from the root rā, which has the meaning of giving.
राका वाक् सरमाप्ताश्च भृगवोऽघ्ना श्य सरस्वती । (*rākā vāk saramāptāśca bhṛgavo 'ghnā śya sarasvatī |*)
(Bṛ. Ve. 1-28)**NOTE**
From the Bṛhaddevatā text it is known that the particular deities Rākā, Vāc and the like belong to the Indra-world, the atmosphere. This deity is praised as one whose gift is accompanied by an exceedingly generous mind. Some statements show also that she is the sister of the gods and is as worthy of worship as the gods. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, at the time of laying down the worship of Rākā, a doubt arises and there is also an answer to it. On that occasion Sāyaṇa has explained as follows:
संपूर्णचंद्रमंडलयुक्ता पौर्णमासी राका । तदभिमानिदेवतायाः प्रतिपादिका ऋगपि राकेत्युच्यते । सेयं राका देवानां जामी नाम भगिनी ॥ (*saṃpūrṇacaṃdramaṃḍalayuktā paurṇamāsī rākā | tadabhimānidevatāyāḥ pratipādikā ṛgapi rāketyucyate | seyaṃ rākā devānāṃ jāmī nāma bhaginī ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. Sā. Bhā. 3-37)**NOTE**
The full-moon day that has the complete lunar disc is designated by the name Rākā. The Ṛk that praises the deity presiding over her is also well known by the name Rākā. He has explained the sense of the Brāhmaṇa sentence thus: this deity is worshipped as the sister of all the gods. In this connection a doubt arises about the order of worship of this deity. It is this:
तदाहू राकां पूर्वां शंसेच्चा मै वै पूर्वपेयमिति ॥ (*tadāhū rākāṃ pūrvāṃ śaṃseccā mai vai pūrvapeyamiti ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 3-37)
In this sentence the idea is expressed that to Rākā, the sister of the gods, worship that comes before that of the wives of the gods should be offered. But this injunction is the sentence of the prima facie view. पूर्वपेयं प्रथमतः सोमपानं युक्तमिति पूर्वपक्षः (*pūrvapeyaṃ prathamataḥ somapānaṃ yuktamiti pūrvapakṣaḥ*) (Sā. Bhā.). The next sentence refutes this prima facie view and states the established conclusion that the drinking of Soma that comes before is prescribed for the wives of the gods, rather than for Rākā.

### Printed p. 432
तत्तन्नादृत्यं देवानामेव पत्निः पूर्वाः शंसेत् । (*tattannādṛtyaṃ devānāmeva patniḥ pūrvāḥ śaṃset |*)
It states the answer, to the effect that the drinking that comes before belongs to the wives of the gods, and that the wife, rather than the sister, is the first one worthy of worship. Therefore, since Rākā is the sister of the gods, she does not get the first place that falls to the wives of the gods.
समानोदर्रा स्वसा अन्नोदरय्यै जायाया अनुजीविनी जीवति ॥ (*samānodarrā svasā annodarayyai jāyāyā anujīvinī jīvati ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 3-37)
It states clearly that, although a sister is born of the womb of one and the same mother, she lives following the wife, who is of another womb, and therefore hers is the second place. Afterwards, while praising Rākā, he enjoins that the worship of Rākā be offered, reciting the mantras beginning राकामहं यास्ते राके (*rākāmahaṃ yāste rāke*), after the passage
राकां शंसति राका ह वा एतां पुरुषस्य सेविनीं सीव्यति यैषा ...... ...... ॥ (*rākāṃ śaṃsati rākā ha vā etāṃ puruṣasya sevinīṃ sīvyati yaiṣā ...... ...... ‖*)
He also states that the mantra that praises Rākā too has the name Rākā. He also praises this same goddess Rākā as one who, taking a most prominent place in the work of the sacrifice, becomes a helper of the sacrificer. At sacrificial times the help of the metres is indispensable. He states this deity to be of the form of a metre.
अनुमत्यै चरुं यानुमतिः सा गायत्री । राकायै चरुं या राका सा त्रिष्टुप् । सिनीवालै चरुं या सिनीवाली सा जगती । कुह्वै चरुं या कुहूः सा अनुष्टुप् । एतानि वाव सर्वाणि च्छंदांसि गायत्रं त्रैष्टुभं जागतमानुष्टुभमन्वन्यान्येतानि हि यज्ञे प्रतमामिव क्रियंते । (*anumatyai caruṃ yānumatiḥ sā gāyatrī | rākāyai caruṃ yā rākā sā triṣṭup | sinīvālai caruṃ yā sinīvālī sā jagatī | kuhvai caruṃ yā kuhūḥ sā anuṣṭup | etāni vāva sarvāṇi cchaṃdāṃsi gāyatraṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ jāgatamānuṣṭubhamanvanyānyetāni hi yajñe pratamāmiva kriyaṃte |*)
(I. Bra., 3-47)**NOTE**
Since the help of the metres is indispensable to the series of sacrificial acts, the deities beginning with Anumati themselves reflect those metres. Anumati is of the form of the Gāyatrī; the goddess Rākā is of the nature of the Triṣṭubh. Sinīvālī is of the form of the Jagatī. The goddess Kuhū is of the nature of the Anuṣṭubh. These are praised as the ones that attain abundance and excess in the sacrifice. Because these, being of the form of metres, are helpful to the sacrifice, they also assist in the works of Prajāpati in regulating the universe. How is that? It is thus:
स यः स धातायमेव स धात्रः । द्वादशकपालः पुरोडाशो द्वादशकपालो द्वादशमासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सरः प्रजापतिः प्रजापतिर्धाताथ यत्तद्दिशां परमं त्रांतमेतानि तानि पूर्वाणि हवींष्यनुमत्यै चरू राकायैचरुः सितीनाल्यै चरुः कुह्वै चरुः .... .... .... ॥ (*sa yaḥ sa dhātāyameva sa dhātraḥ | dvādaśakapālaḥ puroḍāśo dvādaśakapālo dvādaśamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatirdhātātha yattaddiśāṃ paramaṃ trāṃtametāni tāni pūrvāṇi havīṃṣyanumatyai carū rākāyaicaruḥ sitīnālyai caruḥ kuhvai caruḥ .... .... .... ‖*)
(Pra. Pra. 7-5-1-38)**NOTE**

### Printed p. 433
The offering of oblation follows that work of Prajāpati which is of the form of the Creator (Dhātṛ) and the Supporter. Since Prajāpati is of the form of the year, cakes are to be baked on twelve potsherds, following the twelve divisions that are the parts of the year. On this occasion the deities named Anumati, Rākā, Sinīvālī and Kuhū are always to be worshipped and satisfied with oblations. These deities, Rākā and the rest, give stability in the various regions to the works of Prajāpati that support the universe.
ता ना एता देव्यः । दिशो ह्येताश्चंदागांसि वै दिशश्चंदागांसि देव्योऽथैष कः प्रजापतिस्तद्यद्देव्यश्च कश्च तस्माद्देविकाः पंच भवंति पंच हि दिशः ॥ (*tā nā etā devyaḥ | diśo hyetāścaṃdāgāṃsi vai diśaścaṃdāgāṃsi devyo 'thaiṣa kaḥ prajāpatistadyaddevyaśca kaśca tasmāddevikāḥ paṃca bhavaṃti paṃca hi diśaḥ ‖*)
(Ca. Ba. 9.5-1.-39)**NOTE**
Rākā, Sinīvālī and these deities are the four regional deities of the universe. Therefore they are the regulators of the universe. They themselves are of the form of metres. Therefore they are helpers of the sacrificial work that is useful for the business of the universe. They assist the world-nourishing work of Prajāpati, who is called Ka. These are goddesses. Since these goddesses are joined together with Prajāpati, who is of the form Ka, the usage Devikāḥ for all of them together is stated, so the praise of Rākā and the other deities runs. Therefore, although in the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa the deity Rākā has a somewhat lower place than the wives of the gods, in other places the influence of this deity is celebrated to the highest degree. That the help of these goddesses is quite necessary for the continuous growth of the progeny of the world is praised in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. The very goddesses whom it addresses as Devikāḥ because of their world-nourishing power are the ones whom a man desiring offspring should worship.
देविकाः ऎंब व्यवहारवु ऎंबुदागि राका मुंताद देवतॆगळ प्रशंसॆयिदॆ. आदुदरिंद, ऐतरेय ब्राह्मणवाक्यदल्लि राका देवतॆगॆ, देवपत्नियरिगिंतलू कॊंच अपकृष्टवाद स्थानविद्दरू उळिदॆडॆ गळल्लि ई देवतॆय प्रभाववन्नु अत्यतिशयवागि कॊंडाडिदॆ. विश्वद प्रजासंततियु अनुसूतवागि वृद्धियागलु ई देवियर सहायवु अत्यावश्यवॆंबंशवन्नु तैत्तिरीयसंहितॆयल्लि प्रशंसिसिदॆ. याव ई देवियरन्नु अवर जगत्पोषकशक्तिगागि देविकाः ऎंदु संबोधिसिदॆयो, अवरन्ने संतति कामनाद पुरुषनु आराधिसबेकु. देविका निर्वपेत्सजाकामश्चंदाग्‌ंसि वै देविकाश्चंदाग्ंसीव खलु वै प्रजाश्चंदोभिरेवास्मै प्रजाः प्र जनयति प्रथमं धातारं करोति मिथुनी एव तेन करोत्यन्वेवास्मा अनुमतिर्मन्यते राते राका प्र सिनीवाली जनयति .... .... .... देविकाश्चंदाग्ंसिवि ॥ (*devikāḥ èṃba vyavahāravu èṃbudāgi rākā muṃtāda devatègaḷa praśaṃsèyidè. ādudariṃda, aitareya brāhmaṇavākyadalli rākā devatègè, devapatniyarigiṃtalū kòṃca apakṛṣṭavāda sthānaviddarū uḷidèḍè gaḷalli ī devatèya prabhāvavannu atyatiśayavāgi kòṃḍāḍidè. viśvada prajāsaṃtatiyu anusūtavāgi vṛddhiyāgalu ī deviyara sahāyavu atyāvaśyavèṃbaṃśavannu taittirīyasaṃhitèyalli praśaṃsisidè. yāva ī deviyarannu avara jagatpoṣakaśaktigāgi devikāḥ èṃdu saṃbodhisidèyo, avaranne saṃtati kāmanāda puruṣanu ārādhisabeku. devikā nirvapetsajākāmaścaṃdāgṃsi vai devikāścaṃdāgṃsīva khalu vai prajāścaṃdobhirevāsmai prajāḥ pra janayati prathamaṃ dhātāraṃ karoti mithunī eva tena karotyanvevāsmā anumatirmanyate rāte rākā pra sinīvālī janayati .... .... .... devikāścaṃdāgṃsivi ‖*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 3-4-9-1)
A man desiring offspring should offer oblation to Rākā and the other goddesses. These deities are of the form of metres. Offspring too grows in the form of metres. Therefore Rākā and the others, who are of the form of mothers, are the cause of the origin of the metres, who are of the form of sons. Dhātṛ alone is the husband. After conjugal relation has been entered into with Anumatī, Rākā,

### Printed p. 434
these (goddesses), the birth of offspring takes place. Therefore the worship of these Devikās is prescribed. Not only the wealth of progeny, but also he who wishes for wealth of cattle should follow this order of worship.
पशवश्चंदोभिरेवास्कै पशून् प्रजनयति ॥ (*paśavaścaṃdobhirevāskai paśūn prajanayati ‖*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 3-4-9-2)
This point is stated by sentences of this kind. Stating that these four Devikās are four forms of the moon, it describes their forms in this way.
पूर्वपक्षो राकापरपक्षः कुहूरमावास्या सिनीवाली पौर्णमास्यनुमतिच्चंद्रमा धाता .... । (*pūrvapakṣo rākāparapakṣaḥ kuhūramāvāsyā sinīvālī paurṇamāsyanumaticcaṃdramā dhātā .... |*)
(Kṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-9-6)**NOTE**
The goddess Rākā is the first fortnight. The goddess Kuhū is the second fortnight. Sinīvālī is the night of the new moon. Anumati is the night of the full moon. Dhātṛ is the moon. In the form of wives of this moon, who is of the form of Dhātṛ, they are helpers in the manifestation and nourishment of the works of the world's business. In the present mantra the praise of Rākā, who has such influence, is recited, and the order of worship of this deity is laid down.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ सु॑ष्टु॒ती नम॑सा वर्त॒यध्यै॒ द्यावा॒ वाजा॑य पृथि॒वी  ॑
> अमृध्रे ।  
> पि॒ता मा॒ता मधु॑वचाः सु॒हस्ता॒ भरे॑भरे नो य॒शसा॑वविष्टां ॥ २ ॥

> आ । सुस्तुती । नमसा । वर्तयध्यै । द्यावा । वाजाय । पृथिवी इति । अमृध्रे  
> इति ।  
> पिता । माता । मधुवचाः । सुहस्ता । भरेऽभरे । नः । यशसौ । अविष्टां ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 435

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं सुष्टुती सुष्टुत्या शोभनस्तोत्रेण नमसा हविषा चामृद्रे हिंसारहिते
> द्यावा पृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यावा वर्तयध्यै । आवर्तयितुमिच्छामि वाजायानार्थं ।
> अन्नं वै वाज इति हि श्रुतिः । पिता पालयित्रि द्यौर्माता निर्मात्री पृथिवी मधुवचाः
> प्रियवचना सुहस्ताभिमतदानेन शोभनहस्ता । एते उभयविशेषणे । यशसौ
> यशोयुक्तौ द्यावापृथिव्यौ भरे भरे सर्वॆषु संग्रामेषु यज्ञेषु वा
> नोऽस्मानविष्टां । रक्षतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I wish to bring hither the unharmed heaven and earth, with excellent praise and with oblation, for the sake of vāja, that is, food: the Śruti says अन्नं वै वाज इति (*annaṃ vai vāja iti*). The father is the protector, Heaven; the mother is the maker, Earth. They are sweet of speech, that is, of kind words, and good of hand through giving what is desired. These two are epithets of both. May the glorious heaven and earth protect us in every battle or sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुष्टुती (*suṣṭutī*)—with most excellent praise
- नवसा (*navasā*)—and together with oblation**NOTE**
- अमृध्रे (*amṛdhre*)—the unharmed
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- वाजाय (*vājāya*)—for the sake of food
- आ वर्तयध्यै (*ā vartayadhyai*)—I approach
- पिता (*pitā*)—the protectors of the world
- माता (*mātā*)—the mothers of the world
- मधुवचाः (*madhuvacāḥ*)—with pleasant speech
- सुहस्ता (*suhastā*)—with hands that give liberally
- यशसौ (*yaśasau*)—and endowed with renown, heaven and earth
- भरे भरे (*bhare bhare*)—in every battle
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अविष्टां (*aviṣṭāṃ*)—may they protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Endowed with most excellent praise and with oblation, I approach heaven and earth for the sake of food. May heaven and earth, the protectors of the world and mothers of the world, of pleasant speech, of liberally giving hands and endowed with renown, protect us in every battle.

##### English translation
(I purpose) to approach with pious praise, and with oblations, for (the sake of) the uninjured heaven and earth: may the paternal (heaven), and the sweet-spoken, free-handed, maternal (earth), both enjoying renown, defend us in every battle.
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध्व॑र्यवश्चकृ॒वांसो॒ मधू॑नि॒ प्र वा॒यवे॑ भरत॒ चारु॑शु॒क्रं ।

> होतेव नः प्रथमः पाह्कस्य देव मध्वो ररिमा ते  
> मदाय ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध्वर्यवः । चकृनांसः । मधूनि । प्र । वायवे । भरत । चारु । शुक्रं ।  
> होता इव । नः । प्रथमः । पाहि । अस्य । देव । मध्वः । ररिम । ते । मदाय ॥३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यवोऽध्वरं युंजाना मधुनि मधुररसानि सोमाज्यादीनि
> चकृवांसः कुर्वाणा यूयं वायवे प्रथमं प्र भरत प्रकर्षण संपादयत
> चारु चरणीयं शुक्रं दीप्तं सोमं । हे वायो त्वं च होतेव होता यथा
> प्रथमं पिबति तद्वन्नोऽस्मदर्थमस्यामुं सोमं प्रथम इतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वं
> पाहि । पिब । हे देव वायो मध्यो मधुरं सोमरसं ते मदाय ररिम ।
> ददाम । वायोः पूर्वपानमसकृत्प्रपंचितं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Adhvaryus, who yoke the sacrifice and have prepared sweet things, Soma, ājya and the like, offer forth first to Vāyu the lovely, bright Soma. And you, O Vāyu, as the Hotṛ drinks first, so drink first for us this Soma, before the other gods. O god Vāyu, we give the sweet Soma-juice for your exhilaration. Vāyu's drinking first has been set forth again and again.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*)—O Adhvaryus
- मधूनि (*madhūni*)—sweet Soma-juices
- चकृवांसः (*cakṛvāṃsaḥ*)—you who prepare (first)
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—for Vāyu
- चारु (*cāru*)—and lovely
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—and bright Soma
- प्र भरत (*pra bharata*)—offer in an exceeding manner
- देव (*deva*)—O Vāyu, who are divine
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—the sweet Soma-juice
- ते (*te*)—your
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for the delight
- ररिम (*rarima*)—we offer
- नः (*naḥ*)—offered by us
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma-juice
- होतेव (*hoteva*)—as the Hotṛ drinks before all
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—you yourself first, before the other gods
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adhvaryus, you who prepare sweet Soma-juices, offer first to Vāyu, in an exceeding manner, the lovely and bright Soma. O divine Vāyu, we offer you sweet Soma-juice for your delight,

### Printed p. 437
this Soma-juice offered by us: as the Hotṛ drinks before all, so do you drink first, before the other gods.

##### English translation
Priests, who are preparing (the libation), first offer to Vayu the delightful and brilliant (Soma); and you, divine Vayu, like the Hotri, first drink of this sweet juice, (which) we offer for your exhilaration.
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दश॒ क्षिपो॑ युंजते बा॒हू अद्रिं॒ सोम॑स्य॒ या श॑मि॒तारा॑  ॒॑
> सुहस्ता ।  
> मध्वो॒ रसं॑ सु॒गभ॑स्तिर्गिरि॒ष्ठां चनि॑श्चदद्दु दुहे शु॒क्रमं॒शुः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दश । क्षिपः । युंजते । बाहू इति । अद्रिं । सोमस्य । या । शमितारा । सुहस्ता ॥  
> मध्वः । रसं । सुगभस्तिः । गिरिस्थां । चनिश्चदत् । दुदुहे । शुक्रं । अंशुः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्राभिषवस्य प्रतिपाद्यमानत्वात्सोमो देवता । यद्वा ऐंद्री । अद्रिमभिषवग्रावाणं दश क्षिपो दशसंख्याकाः क्षेप्रोऽंगुलयो युंजते । गृण्णंति । यद्वा ।
> परस्परं युक्ता भवंति । बाहू अप्यध्वर्युसंबंधिनावद्रिं युंजाते । या यौ
> सुहस्ता शोभनहननौ सोमस्य शमितारावभिषोतारौ तौ बाहू युंजाते । मध्यो
> मधुरस्य सोमस्य रसं गिरिष्ठां गिरिस्थायिनं गिरिवदुन्नतप्रदेशस्थितं वा सुगभस्तिः
> शोभनांगुलिरध्वर्युश्चनिश्चददाह्लादयन् ॥ चदि आह्लादन इत्यस्माद्यज्लु किछांदसं
> रूपं ॥ दुदुहे । दोग्धि । स चांशुः शुक्रं निर्मलं रसं दुदुहे । दुग्धे ।
> यद्वैकं वाक्यं । अंशुर्व्याप्तः सुगभस्तिः सुहस्तोऽध्वर्युर्मध्यो रसं दुदुहे ।
> दोग्धि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Since the pressing is what is set forth here, Soma is the deity; or else it is Aindrī (addressed to Indra). The ten kṣipaḥ, the ten fingers, seize the pressing-stone; or else they are joined one to another. The two arms too, belonging to the Adhvaryu, seize the stone: the two that are of good hand and are the pressers of the Soma. The Adhvaryu of good fingers, gladdening, the juice of the sweet Soma that dwells on the mountain, or that stands on a high place like a mountain, milks it out. And the aṃśu (the Soma plant) yields its pure, clear juice. Or else it is one sentence: the pervading Soma plant, the Adhvaryu of good hands, milks the sweet juice.

### Printed p. 438

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दश क्षिपः (*daśa kṣipaḥ*)—the ten fingers, (and)
- या (*yā*)—which
- सुहस्ता (*suhastā*)—being of excellent hands
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—of the Soma-juice
- शमितारा (*śamitārā*)—are the instruments of pressing, such
- बाहू (*bāhū*)—the arms (of the Adhvaryus)
- अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)—the pressing-stone
- युंजते (*yuṃjate*)—seize
- सुगभस्तिः (*sugabhastiḥ*)—the Adhvaryu, with excellent fingers
- गिरिष्ठां (*giriṣṭhāṃ*)—that dwells in the mountain region
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of the sweet
- रसं (*rasaṃ*)—the juice
- चनिश्चदत् (*caniścadat*)—presses out
- अंशुः (*aṃśuḥ*)—the Soma plant also
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—the clear juice
- दुदुहे (*duduhe*)—pours out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The arms of the Adhvaryus, which are of excellent hands and are the instruments for pressing the Soma-juice, and their ten fingers, seize the pressing-stone. The Adhvaryu of excellent fingers presses out the sweet Soma-juice that dwells in the mountain region. The Soma plant too pours out the clear juice.

##### English translation
The ten expressers of the juice, (the fingers) and the two arms of the priest, which are the dexterous immolators of the Soma, take hold of the stone; the exulting, skilful-fingered (priest) milks the mountain-born juice of the sweet Soma, and that Soma (yields its) pure juice.
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> असा॑वि ते जुजुषा॒णाय॒ सोमः॒ क्रत्वे॒ दक्षा॑य बृह॒ते  ॑

> हरी इति । रथे । सुधुरा । योगे । अर्वाक् । इंद्र । प्रिया । कृणुहि । हूयमानः । ५ ॥

> तं रथमर्वागस्मदभिमुखं कृणुहि । कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, for you, who delight in it and partake of it, Soma has been pressed. For what? For kratu, for work such as the slaying of Vṛtra; for dakṣa, strength; and for great exhilaration. Since this is so, O Indra, being invoked, yoke to the chariot, which is fit for yoking, your two beloved bay horses, fastened to the good yoke, and make that chariot face us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) दक्षाय (*dakṣāya*)—for the increase of your strength
- बृहते (*bṛhate*)—and for abundant
- मदाय (*madāya*)—delight
- जुजुषाणाय (*jujuṣāṇāya*)—and for satisfaction
- क्रत्वे (*kratve*)—and for the sake of an extraordinary work
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- ते (*te*)—towards you
- असावि (*asāvi*)—has been pressed
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- हूयमानः (*hūyamānaḥ*)—as soon as you are prayed to by us
- सुधुरा (*sudhurā*)—that bear an excellent load
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—and are dear
- हरी (*harī*)—your horses
- रथे (*rathe*)—to your chariot
- योगे (*yoge*)—having yoked them (that chariot)
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—facing us
- कृणु हि (*kṛṇu hi*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, Soma has been pressed towards you for the increase of your strength, for abundant delight, for satisfaction and for the sake of an extraordinary work. O Indra, as soon as you are prayed to by us, yoke your dear horses, which bear an excellent load, to your chariot, and make that chariot face us.

##### English translation
The soma has been effused, (Indra), for your gratification, for (giving you) strength in action, and for your great exhilaration : therefore, Indra

### Printed p. 440
when invoked by us, put to your car, your two beloved, docile, well trained horses and come down.
#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नो॑ म॒हीम॒रम॑तिं स॒जोषा॒ ग्नां दे॒वीं नम॑सा रा॒तह॑व्यां।  
> मधो॒र्मदा॑य बृह॒तीमृ॑त॒ज्ञा माग्ने॑ वह प॒थिभि॑र्देव॒यानैः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । महीं । अरमतिं । सजोषाः । ग्नां । देवीं । नमसा । रातहव्यां ।  
> मधोः । मदाय । बृहती । ऋत्यज्ञां । आ । अग्ने । वह । पथिभिः । देव्ययानैः ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्राग्निं संबोध्य ग्नादेवताया आवाह्यत्वादस्याग्निर्ग्ना वा देवता । हे
> अग्ने सजोषा अस्माभिः सह प्रीयमाणस्त्वं ग्नां देवीं सर्वैर्गंतव्यामेतन्ना
> मिकां देवतां । मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणां । नि. ३-२१. । इति यास्कः । नोऽस्मदर्थं
> देवयानैर्देवैर्गंतवैः पथिभिर्मार्गैरा अभिमुखमा वह । कीदृशीं । महीं
> महतीमरमतिमा समंताद्रममाणां सर्वत्र गंत्रीं ना नमसा स्तोत्रेण सह
> रातहव्यां । रातं दत्तं दानाय संकल्पितं हव्यं यस्यास्तां । दत्तहविष्कामित्यर्थः ।
> किमर्थं । मधोर्मधुरस्य सोमस्य मदाय । पुनः कीदृशीं । बृहतीं प्रवृद्धा
> मृतज्ञां यज्ञमभिजानतीं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here Agni is addressed, but since the goddess Gnā is to be invoked, the deity of this Ṛk is Agni or Gnā. O Agni, being pleased together with us, bring for us the goddess Gnā, the deity so named, to whom all go (Yāska: मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणां (*menā gnā iti strīṇāṃ*), Ni. 3-21), by the paths that the gods travel, facing us. What is she like? Great, aramati, that is, moving about everywhere and going everywhere, together with praise; rātahavyā, she whose oblation has been given, set apart for giving, that is, desirous of the oblation given; and for what purpose? For the exhilaration of the sweet Soma. Again, what is she like? Great, grown, ṛtajñā, knowing the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—having the same regard towards us
- महीं (*mahīṃ*)—great
- अरमतिं (*aramatiṃ*)—all-pervading
- नमसा (*namasā*)—joined with praise
- रातहव्यां (*rātahavyāṃ*)—one to whom oblation has been offered
- बृहतीं (*bṛhatīṃ*)—grown
- ऋतज्ञां (*ṛtajñāṃ*)—knowing the nature of the sacrifice**NOTE**

### Printed p. 441

- ग्नां देवीं (*gnāṃ devīṃ*)—the goddess named Gnā
- मधोः (*madhoḥ*)—of the sweet
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for the gain of exhilaration (of the drinking of Soma)
- देवयानैः पथिभिः (*devayānaiḥ pathibhiḥ*)—by the paths on which the gods travel
- नः आ आ वह (*naḥ ā ā vaha*)—bring facing us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, having the same regard towards us, bring facing us, by the paths on which the gods travel, the goddess named Gnā, who is great, all-pervading, joined with praise, one to whom oblation has been offered, grown, and knowing the nature of the sacrifice, for the gain of the exhilaration of drinking the sweet Soma.

##### English translation
Agni, being well pleased with us, bring to us, by paths frequented by the gods, the divine (female) Gna mighty and omnipresent, to whom oblations are offered with reverence, who is vast and cognizant of rites, to partake of the exhilaration of the sweet Soma.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अं॒जंति॒ यं प्र॒थयं॑तो॒ न विप्रा॑ व॒पावं॑तं॒ नाग्निना॒ तपं॑तः।  
> पि॒तुर्न पु॒त्र उ॒पसि॒ प्रेष्ठ॒ आ घ॒र्मो अ॒ग्निमृ॒तय॑न्नसादि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अंजंति । यं । प्रथयंतः । न । विप्राः । वपावंतं । न । अग्निना । तपंतः ।  
> पितुः । न । पुत्रः । उपसि । प्रेष्ठः । आ । घर्मः । अग्निं । ऋतयन् । असादि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रवर्ग्ये महावीरेऽज्यमानेऽंजंति यमित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । अंजंति यं
> प्रथयंतो न विप्रा इत्यज्यमाने । आ. ४-६ । इति ॥
> यं घर्म० महावीरं प्रथयंतो न ॥ नेति संप्रत्यर्थीयः । अस्तु पमार्थस्य संप्रत्यर्थे प्रयोगः ॥ इदानीं प्रथयंतो विप्रा मेधाविन ऋत्विजोऽध्व-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk beginning अंजंति यं (*aṃjaṃti yaṃ*) is used in the Pravargya, when the Mahāvīra (the vessel) is being anointed. The sūtra says so: "अंजंति यं प्रथयंतो न विप्रा इत्यज्यमाने (*aṃjaṃti yaṃ prathayaṃto na viprā ityajyamāne*)" (Ā. 4-6). "Yam" means the Gharma, the Mahāvīra. Sāyaṇa then speaks of the particle "na", saying that it is used in the sense of "now" (the text here is damaged and he adds a remark on its use in comparison). Now the priests, the Adhvaryu and others, the विप्राः (*viprāḥ*), wise ones, are spreading (the Gharma) **NOTE**.

### Printed p. 442

> र्य्वादयो वपावंतं न ॥ वपावंतं प्रवृद्धं पशुं यथाग्नौ तपंति तद्वदग्नि ना
> तपंतोंजंति । पितुर्न पुत्र उपसि प्रेष्ठः पितुरुपस्थे प्रियतमः पुत्र इव घर्मो
> महावीरः । यद्भ्र इत्यपतत्तद्धर्मस्य घर्मत्वं। तै. ऐ. ५.१.५. । इति हि श्रुतिः । स
> ऋतयन्यज्ञमिच्छन्नग्निमग्नावासादि । आसादितः । अत्र पितृपुत्रदृष्टांतः स्फोटादिराहित्येन सुखवासप्रख्यापनार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Vapāvantam na": as men roast over fire a fully fed animal, so the priests, heating the Gharma with fire, anoint it. "Pitur na putra upasi preṣṭhaḥ": the Gharma, the Mahāvīra, is like the dearest son in the lap of his father. A Śruti says: "यद्भ्र इत्यपतत्तद्धर्मस्य घर्मत्वं। (*yadbhra ityapatattaddharmasya gharmatvaṃ|*)" (Tai. Ai. 5.1.5) **NOTE**. He glosses ऋतयन् (*ṛtayan*) as desiring the sacrifice, and says that the Gharma has been seated in the fire. The example of father and son here is meant to declare that it sits there comfortably, free from the danger of bursting and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वपावंतं न (*vapāvaṃtaṃ na*)—as an animal with excellent fat, rich in marrow, is cooked in the fire
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the priests
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Gharma vessel
- अग्निना (*agninā*)—with fire
- तपंतः (*tapaṃtaḥ*)—heating
- प्रथयंतो न (*prathayaṃto na*)—as if making it known
- अंजंति (*aṃjaṃti*)—they adorn with ghee and other unguents
- घर्मः (*gharmaḥ*)—that same Gharma vessel (the Mahāvīra)
- प्रेष्ठः (*preṣṭhaḥ*)—dearest
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—son
- पितुः (*pituḥ*)—of the father
- उपसि न (*upasi na*)—as he sits lovingly on the lap
- ऋतयन् (*ṛtayan*)—desiring the performance of the sacrifice
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—in the fire
- आ असादि (*ā asādi*)—is seated comfortably (without fear of bursting)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The vessel of Gharma, which the priests adorn with ghee and other unguents in order to cook it in the fire, as one cooks an animal with excellent fat, rich in marrow, sits in the fire comfortably, without fear of bursting, desiring the performance of the sacrifice, like a dearest son sitting lovingly on the lap of his father.

##### English translation
The vessel which the priests, celebrating (it), supply with butter, as if roasting a marrow-yielding animal with fire, has been placed, desirous of the sacrifice, upon the fire, like a son upon the lap of his father.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the sacrifice called Pravargya, at the time of the rite called Mahāvīra, this Ṛk beginning अंजंति यं (*aṃjaṃti yaṃ*) is to be recited. This is set out by the aphorism of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, "अंजंति यं प्रथयंतो न विप्रा इत्यज्यमाने (*aṃjaṃti yaṃ prathayaṃto na viprā ityajyamāne*)" (Ā. 4.6).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अच्छाभिमुखमश्विनाश्विन् हुवध्या आह्वातुं गीरस्मदीया स्तुतिर्दूतो न
> दूत इवाह्वातेव गंतु । गच्छतु । गीर्विशेष्यते । मही पूज्या बृहती महती
> शंतमा सुखतमा । हे अश्विनौ मयोभुवा सुखस्य भावयितारौ सरथैकरथौ संतौ
> निधिं निहितं सोमनुरागभिमुखं यातं । गच्छतं । धुरं भारवाहिकां नाभिमाणिर्न
> कील इव । यथा निष्कीला नाभी रथं न निर्वहति तद्वत् युवाभ्यां वियुक्तः
> सोमो यागं न निर्वहतीति ज्ञापयितुमेवं दृष्टांतितं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अच्छा (*acchā*) means towards; "huvadhyai" means to invite; he addresses the Aśvins. Our praise (gīḥ), like a messenger, is to go towards them. The praise is described: मही (*mahī*), worthy of worship; बृहती (*bṛhatī*), great; "śantamā", most happy-making. मयोभुवा (*mayobhuvā*) means the two who cause happiness; सरथा (*sarathā*), the two being in one chariot; they are to come towards the Soma that has been deposited **NOTE**. "Dhuram" means the burden-bearing nave; "āṇir na" means like a linch-pin (kīla): just as a nave without a linch-pin does not carry the chariot, so Soma separated from the two of you does not carry the sacrifice through; the comparison is made to make this known.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मही (*mahī*)—worthy of worship
- बृहती (*bṛhatī*)—great
- शंतमा (*śaṃtamā*)—most happiness-giving
- गीः (*gīḥ*)—our praise
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvin gods
- हुवध्यै (*huvadhyai*)—to call
- दूतो न (*dūto na*)—like a messenger
- अच्छ (*accha*)—towards them
- गंतु (*gaṃtu*)—let it go (O Aśvin gods)
- धुरं (*dhuraṃ*)—bearing the burden
- नाभिं (*nābhiṃ*)—to the nave at the centre of the wheel
- आणिः न (*āṇiḥ na*)—as the very important pin is there (so you, most important to the sacrifice)
- गंतं (*gaṃtaṃ*)—come
- मयोभुवा (*mayobhuvā*)—being givers of happiness
- सरथा (*sarathā*)—(you) seated in the same chariot
- निधिं (*nidhiṃ*)—to the Soma placed here
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—facing
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—be gracious to come

### Printed p. 444

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May our praise, which is worthy of worship, great and most happiness-giving, go like a messenger towards the Aśvin gods to call them. O Aśvin gods, as the very important pin is at the nave of the wheel that bears the burden, so you, most important to the sacrifice, come. Be gracious to come, being givers of happiness to us and seated in the same chariot, towards the Soma placed here.

##### English translation
May this adoring, earnest, and gratifying praise go like a messenger to summon the Aswins hither: come, Aswins, givers of happiness, riding in one chariot, come down to the deposited (Soma), as the bolt (is essential) to the axle of the waggon.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, the seer, offer ("pra adikṣi") a hymn of homage, a "namas" utterance, to Pūṣan, the nourisher, who is "tavyas", of surpassing strength, and "turas", hastening, and to Vāyu of the said nature. The two, Pūṣan and Vāyu, by "rādhas", that is by the means of the oblation, are inciters of thoughts. Or else: राधसा (*rādhasā*) has the third case in the sense of the sixth,

> राधसो धनस्य मतीनां च चोदयितारौ । यौ च वाजस्यान्नस्य संग्रामस्य ना
> चोदयितारौ तौ देवावुतापि च त्मनात्मन्यनन्यप्रेरणायैव द्रवीणोदौ भवतमिति
> शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

so that they are the inciters of wealth and of thoughts; and those who incite food ("vāja") and battle, may those two gods also be, by their own impulse and without being urged by another, givers of wealth: "may you be" is what is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- या (*yā*)—those Pūṣan and Vāyu who both
- राधसा (*rādhasā*)—by reason of the food in the form of oblation
- मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)—of minds full of desire
- चोदितारा (*coditārā*)—are the inciters
- या (*yā*)—who
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—of food (are the inciters)
- उत (*uta*)—and moreover
- त्मन् (*tman*)—by their own impulse alone
- द्रविणोदौ (*draviṇodau*)—are givers of wealth
- तव्यसः (*tavyasaḥ*)—of surpassing strength
- तुरस्य (*turasya*)—of swift going
- पूष्णः उत वायोः (*pūṣṇaḥ uta vāyoḥ*)—addressed to the god Pūṣan and the god Vāyu
- नमउक्तिं (*namauktiṃ*)—praise accompanied by homage
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- प्र अदिक्षि (*pra adikṣi*)—offer in abundance

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I offer in abundance praise accompanied by homage, addressed to the god Pūṣan and the god Vāyu, who are of surpassing strength and of swift going: the two who, by reason of food in the form of oblation, are inciters of minds full of desire, who are inciters of food, and who moreover are, by their own impulse alone, givers of wealth.

##### English translation
I offer adoration to the powerful and rapid Pushan, and to (the powerful and rapid) Vayu, who are both instigators of the desire of wealth and of food, (who are both) distributors of riches.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञाग्ने हुवानोऽस्माभिराहूयमानः सन् विश्वान्मरुतः सर्वानपि स्तोत्रभाजो हविर्भाजश्च देवान् नामभिरिंद्रवरुणेत्यादिलक्षणैरा
> वक्षि । आवहसि । रूपेभिः सहस्राक्षवज्रहस्तत्वादिलक्षणै रूपैरा वक्षि । वहसि यज्ञं ।
> किंच हे मरुतो विश्वे सर्वे यूयं यज्ञमस्मदीयं यज्ञसंबंधि हनिर्वा
> जरितुः स्तोतुः संबंधिनीर्गिरः स्तुतिवचांसि सुष्टुतिं तत्साध्यां शोभनफलां स्तुतिं
> च ॥ अवयविन्याः स्तुतेरेकत्वादेकवचनं । अवयवानां बहुत्वादृहुवचनं ॥
> उक्ते यज्ञस्तुती अभिलक्ष्य गंत । आगच्छत । विश्वे च यूयमूती ऊत्या रक्षया
> च सह गंत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Jātavedas, Agni of born knowledge, being invoked by us, bring all the Maruts, that is all the gods who share in praise and in oblation, by their names such as Indra and Varuṇa, and bring them by their forms, such as being thousand-eyed or thunderbolt-handed; bring also the sacrifice. Further, O Maruts, all of you come to our sacrifice, or to the oblation connected with the sacrifice, to the गिरः (*giraḥ*), the words of praise belonging to the worshipper ("jaritṛ"), and to the good praise ("suṣṭuti") which they bring about, whose fruit is auspicious. The praise as a whole is one, hence the singular; its parts are many, hence the plural. Keeping in view the sacrifice and the praises just stated, come; and all of you come together with ऊती (*ūtī*), that is with protection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, of born knowledge
- हुवानः (*huvānaḥ*)—being entreated by us
- विश्वान् (*viśvān*)—all
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- नामभिः (*nāmabhiḥ*)—by their several personal names
- आ वक्षि (*ā vakṣi*)—bring
- रूपेभिः (*rūpebhiḥ*)—also by their several personal forms
- आ (*ā*) (the verb वक्षि (*vakṣi*) understood)—bring
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all of you
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—towards our sacrifice
- जरितुः (*jarituḥ*)—of the worshipper
- सुष्टुतिं (*suṣṭutiṃ*)—in the form of excellent praise
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—towards the words
- गंत (*gaṃta*)—be gracious to come
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all of you
- ऊती (*ūtī*)—with all your protections (be gracious to come)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of the nature of Jātavedas, being entreated by us, bring all the Maruts by their several personal names and by their several forms. O Maruts, all of you, together with all your protections, be gracious to come here, towards our sacrifice and having regard to the excellent praises.

##### English translation
Bring hither Jatavedas, who are invoked by us all, the Maruts, under their several names and forms : come, all you Maruts, with all your protect-ing faculties, to the sacrifice, the praises, and the adoration of the worshipper.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ नो दिव इत्येकादशी व्यूढे दशरात्रे नवमेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्रे सारस्वततृचे
> द्वितीया । सूत्रितं च । आ नो दिवो बृहतः पर्वतादा सरस्वत्यभि नो नेषि वस्यः ।
> आ. ८. ११ । इति ॥
> नोऽस्माकं य ज्ञं यजता यष्टव्या देवी सरस्वती दिवो द्योतमानाद्भुलोकादा गंतु । आगच्छतु । तथा बृहतो महतः पर्वतात्पर्ववतः पूरणवतः
> प्रीणनवतो वांतरिक्षान्मेघाद्वा सरस्वत्या गंतु । आगच्छतु । अनेन माध्यमिकी
> वागुच्यते ! यद्वैतद्दिव इत्यस्य विशेषणं । संति हि द्युलोकस्य त्रीणि पर्वाणि तिस्रो
> दिवः पृथिवीरित्यादि श्रुतेः । अस्मिन्पक्षे द्वितीय आकारः पूरणः । तदर्थं हवनमस्मदीयमाह्वानं देवी सरस्वती जुजुषाणा स्तुतिं सेवमाना धृताची धृतमुदकमंचती नोऽस्मदीयां शग्मां सुखकरीं वाचं स्तुतिमुशती कामयमाना सती
> शृणोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk, "आ नो दिवः (*ā no divaḥ*)", is the eleventh; in the Daśarātra called Vyūḍha, on the ninth day, in the Prauga-śastra, it is the second of the Sārasvata triplet. The sūtra says so: "आ नो दिवो बृहतः पर्वतादा सरस्वत्यभि नो नेषि वस्यः (*ā no divo bṛhataḥ parvatādā sarasvatyabhi no neṣi vasyaḥ*)" (Ā. 8. 11). The worshipful goddess Sarasvatī is to come to our sacrifice from heaven, the shining world; or, as a second explanation, from the great "parvata", which means that which has joints or fullness, or that which gives satisfaction, namely from the cloud of the atmosphere; by this the speech of the middle region is meant. Or else "great parvata" is an epithet of "heaven", since the heavenly world has three joints, as the Śruti says, "three are the heavens and the earths" and so on; on this view the second आ (*ā*) is the filling one. Therefore the goddess Sarasvatī, taking pleasure in our invocation, serving our praise, bringing water (ghee-water), and desiring our happiness-giving speech, our praise, is to hear it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यजता (*yajatā*)—worshipful
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—to the sacrifice
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the heavenly world
- आ गंतु (*ā gaṃtu*)—may she be gracious to come (or)
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—great
- पर्वतात् (*parvatāt*)—from the atmosphere
- आ (*ā*) (the verb गंतु (*gaṃtu*) understood)—may she be gracious to come
- देवी (*devī*)—Sarasvatī, who is of the nature of a deity
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—our praise in the form of prayer
- जुजुषाणा (*jujuṣāṇā*)—serving
- धृताती (*dhṛtātī*)—sprinkling water
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- शग्मां (*śagmāṃ*)—happiness-giving
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—praise
- उशती (*uśatī*)—desiring
- शृणोतु (*śṛṇotu*)—may she hear

### Printed p. 448

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the worshipful goddess Sarasvatī be gracious to come to our sacrifice either from the heavenly world or from the great atmosphere. May the goddess Sarasvatī, serving our praise in the form of prayer and sprinkling water, desiring our happiness-giving praise, listen to it with pleasure.

##### English translation
May the radiant Saraswati come to the sacrifice from the heavens or the spacious firmament : may the goddess, the showerer of water, propitiated by our invocation, and desirous of our gratifying praises, hear.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the time of reciting the Prauga-śastra mantras on the ninth day of the Daśarātra sacrifice called Vyūḍha, this Ṛk "आ नो दिवः (*ā no divaḥ*)" is to be recited as the second Ṛk in the triplet (a triplet is three Ṛks) whose deity is Sarasvatī. This is set out by the aphorism of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, "आ नो दिवो बृहतः पर्वतादा सरस्वत्यभि नो नेषि वस्यः (*ā no divo bṛhataḥ parvatādā sarasvatyabhi no neṣi vasyaḥ*)" (Ā. 8.11).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is addressed to Bṛhaspati. O priests, install in the house of our sacrifice the god Bṛhaspati, the lord of the great mantra. What sort of god? He is "vedhas", the maker of manifold things, "nīlapṛṣṭha", of glossy body, "bṛhat", great. Of such a god we, priests and sacrificers, **NOTE** are to perform service,

### Printed p. 449

> ग्यजमानाः सपेम । परिचरेम । स एव विशेष्यते । सादद्योनिं योन् सीदंतं
> दमे यागगृह आ सर्वतो दीदिवांसं दीप्यमानं हिरण्यवर्णमरुषमारोचमानं । अथवेयमाग्नेयि । बृहतः परिवृढस्य कर्णणः स्वामीति बृहस्पतिरग्निरुच्यते ।
> तथा नीलवर्णधूमपृष्ठत्वसदनसादनहिरण्यवर्णत्वादिलिंगैरप्यग्निरेव बृहस्पतिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

he alone is described further. "Sādadyoni" means sitting on his seat; in the "dame", the sacrificial house, shining all round, golden-hued, "aruṣa", brilliant. Or else this Ṛk is addressed to Agni: Agni is called Bṛhaspati, since he is lord of the great परिवृढस्य कर्णणः (*parivṛḍhasya karṇaṇaḥ*) **NOTE**. By the marks also, namely the blue-coloured smoky back, the sitting and the seating, the golden colour and so on, Agni alone is Bṛhaspati.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O priests) वेधसं (*vedhasaṃ*)—the creator
- नीलपृष्ठं (*nīlapṛṣṭhaṃ*)—one whose back is blue in colour

- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—the god Bṛhaspati
- सदने (*sadane*)—in our house of sacrifice
- आ सादयध्वं (*ā sādayadhvaṃ*)—install
- सादद्योनिं (*sādadyoniṃ*)—one who is seated on the sacrificial altar
- दमे (*dame*)—in the house of sacrifice
- आ (*ā*)—everywhere
- दीदिवांसं (*dīdivāṃsaṃ*)—shining
- हिरण्यवर्णं (*hiraṇyavarṇaṃ*)—of attractive golden colour
- अरुषं (*aruṣaṃ*)—brilliant
- सपेम (*sapema*)—let us worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, install in our house of sacrifice the god Bṛhaspati, the creator, whose back is blue in colour, of mighty form. Let us worship Bṛhaspati, who is seated on the sacrificial altar, shines everywhere in the house of sacrifice, is of an attractive golden colour and is brilliant.

##### English translation
(Priests) place the mighty Brihaspati, the creator, whose back is dark blue, in the chamber (of sacrifice): let us worship him who is seated in the interior of the mansion, everywhere shining, golden-hued, resplendent.

> सर्वैरोमभी रक्षणैः सह हुवान आहूयमानः । ग्ना गंत्रीर्ज्वाला ओषधीश्च वसानोऽमृध्रोऽहिंसितस्त्रिधातुशृंगस्त्रिप्रकारशृंगवदुन्नतलोहितशुक्लकृष्णवर्णज्वालो

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is addressed to Agni **NOTE**. May Agni come to our sacrifice: "dharṇasi", the upholder of all; बृहद्दिवः (*bṛhaddivaḥ*), of abundant radiance; रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*), delighting and granting desires; being invoked with all "omas", protections. ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*) are the moving flames, and he clothes himself in them and in the herbs; "amṛdhra", unharmed; "tridhātuśṛṅga", whose flames, like horns of three kinds, are tall and red, white and black; "vṛṣabha", the one who showers; वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*), the giver of food or the upholder of the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहद्दिवः (*bṛhaddivaḥ*)—of abundant radiance
- रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*)—full of delight
- ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*)—the moving flames
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the herbs
- वसानः (*vasānaḥ*)—wearing
- अमृधः (*amṛdhaḥ*)—unharmed
- त्रिधातुशृंगः (*tridhātuśṛṃgaḥ*)—possessed of flames which are red, white and black and are like horns
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the showerer of desires
- वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)—the giver of food
- धर्णसिः (*dharṇasiḥ*)—Agni, the upholder of the whole world
- विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*)—all
- ओमभिः (*omabhiḥ*)—together with the protections
- हुवानः (*huvānaḥ*)—as soon as he is entreated by us
- आ गंतु (*ā gaṃtu*)—may he be gracious to come to our sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni, who is of abundant radiance, full of delight, wears the moving flames and the herbs, is unharmed, has flames that are red, white and black and are like horns, is the showerer of desires, the giver of food and the upholder of the whole world, be gracious to come to our sacrifice, together with all his protections, as soon as he is entreated by us.

##### English translation
May the sustainer of all, (Agni), the greatly radiant, tho delighter, come, with all his protecting (faculties), when invoked; he who is clothed with flames and with plants; who is irresistible; who has horns of three colours; the showerer (of benefits), the accepter of oblations.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Āyu" means man, the sacrificer; विपन्यवः (*vipanyavaḥ*) is a name for praisers, the praisers, the Hotṛ priests and others, are रास्पिरासः (*rāspirāsaḥ*). रा (*rā*) is wealth, in the form of oblation; the ladles, the juhū and the others, touch it, and are रास्पा (*rāspā*); he who has them is रास्पि (*rāspi*); those who have them are रास्पिराः (*rāspirāḥ*). Such priests have gone to the bright, supreme place of the mother, the Earth, her maker, that is to the northern altar where the fire stands. For this purpose, "suśevya", what is good for happiness, the new-born child, वासे (*vāse*), for his dwelling, नमसा (*namasā*), with praise, the रातहव्याः (*rātahavyāḥ*), those who have given the oblation, that is who have offered the oblation, rub, cleanse. Here the example is आयवः (*āyavaḥ*), ordinary men; as they rub a child for his dwelling, so do these.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रास्पिरासः (*rāspirāsaḥ*)—those who hold the juhū ladle filled with the oblation
- आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—for the sacrificer, a man
- विपन्यवः (*vipanyavaḥ*)—the priests, who are praisers and performers of the offering
- मातुः (*mātuḥ*)—of the earth
- शुक्रे (*śukre*)—brilliant
- परमे पदे (*parame pade*)—to the region of the northern altar
- अग्मन् (*agman*)—have gone
- शिशुं (*śiśuṃ*)—the tender child
- आयवो न (*āyavo na*)—as they rub and caress it for its growth
- रातहव्याः (*rātahavyāḥ*)—the priests who have offered the oblation
- सुशेव्यं (*suśevyaṃ*)—one comfortably established
- शिशुं (*śiśuṃ*)—the one just born, Agni
- वासे (*vāse*)—for his increase
- नवसा (*navasā*)—with praise **NOTE**
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—rub (that is, nourish with love)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The priests, who hold the juhū ladle filled with the oblation and who are the praisers and performers of the offering for the sacrificer, a man, have gone to the brilliant region of the northern altar of the earth. As one rubs and caresses a tender child for its growth, so the priests who have offered the oblation rub, with praise, for his increase, Agni, who is comfortably established and just born; that is, they nourish him with love.

### Printed p. 452

##### English translation
The holders of the (sacrificial) ladles, the ministrant priests of the man (who institutes the rite), have repaired to the bright and most excellent place of the maternal (earth): offerers of the oblation, they foster the tender infant, (Agni), with worship, as people rub (the limbs of a child to promote his) existence.

> पू. मी. ६. १. २४ । अवशिष्टं गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

बृहत् (*bṛhat*) is abundant; "vayas" is food. O Agni, to you, the great, those धियाजुरः (*dhiyājuraḥ*), worn out by their rites, मिथुनासः (*mithunāsaḥ*), together with their wives, render service. The Śruti says, "Let husband and wife establish the fire" and so on. In the sixth chapter, the Adhikārādhyāya, it is established that the wife also has the right to the fire, and that this is together with the husband: Pū. Mī. 6.1.24 **NOTE**. The remainder has been dealt with.

- शुभ्यं (*śubhyaṃ*)—towards you **NOTE**

O Agni, the sacrificers, worn thin by their rites alone and accompanied by their wives, offer abundant food to you of mighty form and serve you. May every god also be entreated and called in an excellent manner for me. May the Earth, the maker of the world, not place us together with an evil mind.

##### English translation
Married pairs, worn by devout rites, jointly offer abundant sacrificial food, Agni, to you who are mighty: may each individual divinity be successfully invoked by me : let them not take us into unfavourable thought.
