## Sūkta 44 (Maṇḍala 5)

The forty-fourth hymn.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तं प्रत्नथेति पंचदशर्च० द्वादशं सूक्तं । अवत्सारो नाम ऋषिः स च
> कश्यपगोत्रः । यास्वक्षु सदापृणबाहुवृक्तादयः श्रुतास्तासु तेऽपि समुच्चीयंते । चतुर्दशीपंचदशौ त्रिष्टुभौ शिष्टा स्त्रिष्टुबंतपरिभाषया जगत्यः । विश्वे देवा
> देवता । अनुक्रांतं च । तं प्रत्नथा पंचोना काश्यपोऽवत्सारोऽन्ये च ऋषयोऽत्र गृष्टलिंगा द्वित्रिष्टुबंतमिति ॥ वाजपेयेऽतिरिक्कोष्ठ आदितस्त्रयोदशर्चः
> शंसनीया: । सूत्रितं च । तं प्रत्नथेति त्रयोदशानामेकां शिष्टाहूय दूरोहणं रोहेत् । आ. ९, ९. । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning तं प्रत्नथेति (*taṃ pratnatheti*) has fifteen Ṛks and is the twelfth sūkta. Its seer is Avatsāra, of the Kaśyapa gotra. In the Ṛks in which Sadāpṛṇa, Bāhuvṛkta and others are named, they too are included as seers. The fourteenth and fifteenth are Triṣṭubh; the rest are Jagatī, by the rule that the metre is Triṣṭubh at the end. The deity is the Viśvedevas. He cites the Anukramaṇikā: तं प्रत्नथा पंचोना काश्यपोऽवत्सारोऽन्ये च ऋषयोऽत्र गृष्टलिंगा द्वित्रिष्टुबंतमिति (*taṃ pratnathā paṃconā kāśyapo 'vatsāro 'nye ca ṛṣayo 'tra gṛṣṭaliṃgā dvitriṣṭubaṃtamiti*) **NOTE**. Use: in the Vājapeya, at the supplementary recitation वाजपेयेऽतिरिक्कोष्ठ (*vājapeye 'tirikkoṣṭha*) **NOTE**, the first thirteen Ṛks are to be recited. The sūtra says so: तं प्रत्नथेति त्रयोदशानामेकां शिष्टाहूय दूरोहणं रोहेत् (*taṃ pratnatheti trayodaśānāmekāṃ śiṣṭāhūya dūrohaṇaṃ rohet*) (Ā. 9, 9).

Anuvāda: This sūkta, तं प्रत्नथा (*taṃ pratnathā*), is the twelfth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has fifteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the one named Avatsāra, born in the Kaśyapa gotra; in whichever Ṛks of this sūkta the names of seers such as Sadāpṛṇa and Bāhuvṛkta are mentioned, they are the seers of those Ṛks; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the fourteenth and fifteenth Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Triṣṭubh metre, and the other Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: तं प्रत्नथा पंचोना काश्यपोऽवत्सारोऽन्ने च ऋषयोऽत्र दृष्टलिंगा द्वित्रिष्टुबंतं (*taṃ pratnathā paṃconā kāśyapo 'vatsāro 'nne ca ṛṣayo 'tra dṛṣṭaliṃgā dvitriṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). In the sacrifice called Vājapeya, in the recitation of the atirikta mantras **NOTE**, the first thirteen Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited; this is explained by the aphorism of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, तं प्रत्नथेति त्रयोदशानामेकां शिष्टाहूय दूरोहणं रोहेत् (*taṃ pratnatheti trayodaśānāmekāṃ śiṣṭāhūya dūrohaṇaṃ rohet*) (Ā. 9-9).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं प्र॒त्नथा॑ पू॒र्वथा॑ वि॒श्वथे॒मथा॑ ज्ये॒ष्ठता॑तिं बर्हि॒षदं॑  
> स्व॒र्विदं॑ ।  
> प्र॒ती॒ची॒नं वृ॒जनं॑ दोहसे गि॒राशुं जयं॑त॒मनु॒ यासु॒

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । प्रत्यथा । पूर्वथा । विश्वथा । इमथा । ज्येष्ठतातिं । बर्हिसदं ।  
> स्वःविदं ।  
> प्रतीचीनं । वृजनं । दोहसे । गिरा । आशुं । जयंतं । अनु । यासु । वर्धसे ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयमुत्तरा च द्वे ऐंद्रा वित्याहुः । तत्रोपपत्तिमेवाहुः । तं प्रत्नथेत्येषा
> शुक्रामंथिग्रहणे विनियुक्ता । ऐंद्रौ च शुक्रामंधिनौ । यदैंद्रं शंसति तेन
> शुक्रामंथिना उक्तवंतौ । ऐ ब्रा. ३. १. इति हि ब्राह्मणं । अध्वर्युसंप्रैषोऽपि
> भवति । प्रातःप्रातः सवस्य शुक्रवतो मधुश्चुत इंद्राय सोमान्प्रस्थितान्प्रेष्य ।
> शत. ब्रा. ४. २. १. २३. । इति । प्रशास्त्रप्रैषश्च भवति । होता यक्षदिंद्रं प्रातः
> प्रातः सावस्य । आ. ५. ५. । इत्यादि । प्रस्थिता इंद्राय सोमा इति याजा, चैंद्री ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He says that this Ṛk and the next are called Aindra, and that what follows is the ground for it. This Ṛk, तं प्रत्नथे (*taṃ pratnathe*), is used in the taking of the Śukra and Manthin cups, and the two cups Śukra and Manthin belong to Indra. The Brāhmaṇa says: यदैंद्रं शंसति तेन शुक्रामंथिना उक्तवंतौ (*yadaiṃdraṃ śaṃsati tena śukrāmaṃthinā uktavaṃtau*) (Ai. Brā. 3. 1). There is also the Adhvaryu's injunction: प्रातःप्रातः सवस्य शुक्रवतो मधुश्चुत इंद्राय सोमान्प्रस्थितान्प्रेष्य (*prātaḥprātaḥ savasya śukravato madhuścuta iṃdrāya somānprasthitānpreṣya*) (Śata. Brā. 4. 2. 1. 23) **NOTE**, and the injunction of the Praśāstṛ: होता यक्षदिंद्रं प्रातः प्रातः सावस्य (*hotā yakṣadiṃdraṃ prātaḥ prātaḥ sāvasya*) (Ā. 5. 5) and so on; and "प्रस्थिता इंद्राय सोमा (*prasthitā iṃdrāya somā*)" is the yājyā **NOTE**, and the Aindrī is इदं ते सोम्यं मधु (*idaṃ te somyaṃ madhu*) (Ā. 5. 5). Therefore both are Aindra.

> जयंतं सर्वमभिभवंतमिंद्रं गिरा स्तुत्या साधनेन दोहसे । धुक्ष सर्वदा
> सर्वान् कामान् । इत्यंतरात्मनः प्रैषः । यासु स्तुतिषु वर्धसे प्रवृद्धो भवसि
> वर्धयसि वेंद्रं यया स्तुत्येति । यास्विति व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Him, Indra: as the ancient sacrificers, those before us, all creatures, and the sacrificers living now obtained the fruit by praising Indra, so we also; and you also, O inner self, extract by praise, as the means, from Indra, the eldest, seated on the sacred grass, the all-knowing, the bestower of everything, turned towards us, वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*) being a name for strength, so he is the strong one, swift or all-pervading, victorious, overcoming everything; milk always all desires. This is the injunction addressed to the inner self. In whichever praises you grow, or make Indra grow by whichever praise: the plural यास्विति (*yāsviti*) is by interchange of number.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रत्नथा (*pratnathā*)—the ancient sacrificers
- पूर्वथा (*pūrvathā*)—our forefathers and others before us
- विश्वथा (*viśvathā*)—all sacrificers
- इमथा (*imathā*)—the great ones who are now living
- तं (*taṃ*)—that same Indra (they praised him and obtained their desired ends); (O inner self, you also)
- यासु (*yāsu*)—by which praises
- अनु वर्धसे (*anu vardhase*)—you make Indra grow and you also obtain the growth that is its fruit; such
- गिरा (*girā*)—by the means that takes the form of praise
- ज्येष्ठतातिं (*jyeṣṭhatātiṃ*)—the eldest of all
- बर्हिषदं (*barhiṣadaṃ*)—seated on the seat of darbha grass
- स्वर्विदं (*svarvidaṃ*)—all-knowing
- प्रतीचीनं (*pratīcīnaṃ*)—turned towards us
- वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)—strong
- आशुं (*āśuṃ*)—swift
- जयंतं (*jayaṃtaṃ*)—victorious Indra himself (worshipping him)
- दोहसे (*dohase*)—(from him) cause all your desired ends to rain down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The ancient sacrificers, our forefathers and others before us, all sacrificers and the great ones now living praised that same Indra and obtained their desired ends. O inner self, you also, with the means that takes the form of praise, by which praises you make Indra grow and so obtain the growth that is its fruit, worship that same Indra, who is the eldest of all, seated on the seat of darbha grass, all-knowing, turned towards us, strong, swift and victorious, and cause all your desired ends to rain down from him.

##### English translation
In like manner as the ancient (sages), those our predecessors, as all sages, and those of the present period, (have obtained their wishes by his praise), so do you by praise extract (my desires) from him who is the oldest

### Printed p. 458

and best (of the gods), who is seated on the sacred grass, who is cognizant of heaven, coming to our presence, vigorous, swift, victorious, for by such praises you exalt him.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk and the next are said to be addressed to Indra. The Ṛk तं प्रत्नथा (*taṃ pratnathā*) is used as a preliminary recitation at the time of the taking of the Śukra-Manthin cup. There is a statement of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that when one recites this Ṛk addressed to Indra, the mantras that are to be recited for the Śukra-Manthin cup are thereby recited: यद्येंद्रं शंसति तेन शुक्रामंथिना उक्तवंतौ (*yadyeṃdraṃ śaṃsati tena śukrāmaṃthinā uktavaṃtau*) (Ai. Brā. 3-1).

A little explanation is necessary here. In a sacrifice there is a custom of reciting the Prauga-śastra mantras for the increase of the sacrificer's food **NOTE**. In connection with these śastra mantras the mantras of nine cups are recited (a cup, graha, is a vessel for drinking Soma juice): the cups वायुग्रह (*vāyugraha*), इंद्रवायु ग्रह (*iṃdravāyu graha*), मैत्रावरुणग्रह (*maitrāvaruṇagraha*), आश्विनग्रह (*āśvinagraha*), शुक्रामंथिग्रह (*śukrāmaṃthigraha*), वैश्वदेवग्रह (*vaiśvadevagraha*), addressed to the deities named Sarasvatī and so on; there are nine cups, named उपांशु (*upāṃśu*), अंतर्याम (*aṃtaryāma*), वायव (*vāyava*), ऐंद्रवायव (*aiṃdravāyava*), मैत्रावरुण (*maitrāvaruṇa*), आश्विन (*āśvina*), शुक्र (*śukra*), आग्रयण (*āgrayaṇa*) **NOTE**. Among these the Ṛk तं प्रत्यथा (*taṃ pratyathā*) has its use in connection with the Śukra-Manthin cup. This Ṛk is also a praiṣa mantra that the Adhvaryu recites addressed to the Hotṛ. Since these matters belong to the Śrauta practice, we shall give further details on this when the Prauga-śastra mantras are explained later.

Besides this, in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa there is also an indication of the praiṣa mantra on this Ṛk: प्रातः प्रातःसवस्य शुक्रवतो मधुश्चुत इंद्राय सोमान्प्रस्थितान् प्रेष्य (*prātaḥ prātaḥsavasya śukravato madhuścuta iṃdrāya somānprasthitān preṣya*) (Śa. Brā. 4-2-1-23). That this Ṛk is to be recited also as a Praśāstṛ-praiṣa mantra is explained by the aphorism of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra होतायक्षदिंद्रं प्रातः प्रातस्सावस्य (*hotāyakṣadiṃdraṃ prātaḥ prātassāvasya*) (Ā. 5-5), and that it is to be recited addressed to Indra as the Prasthita-yājyā mantra by the aphorism of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra इदं ते सोम्यं मधु (*idaṃ te somyaṃ madhu*) (Ā. 5-5).

Yāska has given an etymology of this Ṛk: था इति च । तं प्रत्नथा पूर्वथा विश्वथेमथा । प्रत इव पूर्व इव विश्व इवेम इवेति अयमेततरोऽमुष्मात् । असावस्ततरोऽस्मात् । अमुथा यथासाविति वाख्यातं ॥ (*thā iti ca | taṃ pratnathā pūrvathā viśvathemathā | prata iva pūrva iva viśva ivema iveti ayametataro 'muṣmāt | asāvastataro 'smāt | amuthā yathāsāviti vākhyātaṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 459

Here, in order to explain also the meaning of the word or particle था (*thā*), Yāska has taken this very Ṛk as his example, and has explained what the particle था (*thā*) conveys in the words प्रत्नथा (*pratnathā*), पूर्वथा (*pūrvathā*), विश्वथा (*viśvathā*) and इमथा (*imathā*) that occur in this Ṛk. The meaning of अमुथा (*amuthā*) has already been given earlier: it means यथासौ (*yathāsau*), "like this". Here too the particle था (*thā*) must be given the meaning "like". In the word प्रत्नथा (*pratnathā*) the first part means ancient **NOTE**; therefore प्रत्नथा (*pratnathā*) means "like the ancients" or "as before". In the same way पूर्वथा (*pūrvathā*) means "like the former", विश्वथा (*viśvathā*) "like everything", इमथा (*imathā*) "like the present": such are the meanings of these words. Now, for the word अयं (*ayaṃ*) the explanation is "nearer than another object", that is, "this", "this object"; for that reason, when we point to an object that is near, we say अयं (*ayaṃ*), "this". In the same way, for the word असौ (*asau*) the explanation is अस्ततरः (*astataraḥ*), that is, "farther than this (than the object that is near)". Therefore, when we point to an object that is far away, we say असौ (*asau*), "that".

> चतुर्थी ॥ उपरस्य मेघस्य संबंधिन्यः सुदृशीः सुरोचमाना या आपः संति तासा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Indra: "O Indra, you who shine in heaven." He explains that the dative form of the word for "impeller" is used in the sense of the genitive (the Ṛk speaks of one who impels). The waters here are those connected with the cloud, beautiful and well shining, and the word for the quarters means all the directions; in the midst of them Indra is to be an impeller for the welfare of living beings, that is, for their finding refuge in them (the verb "be" is to be supplied).

### Printed p. 460

> मपां ककुभां सर्वासां दिशां मध्ये श्रिये प्राणिनां श्रयणाय प्रेरको भवेति
> शेषः । हे सुक्रतो शोभनवृष्टिप्रदानादिकर्मकेंद्र त्वं सुगोपाः प्राणिनां
> सुष्टु गोपायितासि । अतो न दभाय न दंभनाय वधाय प्राणिनां नासि । न
> प्रभवसि । त्वं च मायाभिरासुरीभिः परो मायाभ्यः परस्ताद्वर्तमानः । यस्मात्ते
> त्वदीयं नाम नामकं रूपमृते सत्यलोक आस आस्ते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues: "O Indra of good works, whose acts are such as the granting of excellent rain, you are the good protector of living beings; therefore you are not for harming or destroying them: you are not able to do so. And you stand beyond the demonic delusions, abiding above them; for your name, your designation and form, abides in the world of truth."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—in heaven
- विरोचमानः (*virocamānaḥ*)—you who shine
- उपरस्य (*uparasya*)—connected with the cloud
- सुदृशीः (*sudṛśīḥ*)—and attractive
- याः (*yāḥ*)—whichever waters there are, them
- ककुभां (*kakubhāṃ*)—in the interiors of all the quarters
- श्रिये (*śriye*)—for the welfare of living beings
- अचोदते (*acodate*)—you have impelled (to flow)
- सुकृतो (*sukṛto*)—O Indra, who have excellent deeds
- सुगोपाः असि (*sugopāḥ asi*)—you are the complete protector (of all beings)
- दभाय (*dabhāya*)—for their destruction (as a means)
- न (*na*)—(certainly) not
- मायाभिः (*māyābhiḥ*)—than the demonic delusions
- परः (*paraḥ*)—you are beyond them
- ते (*te*)—your
- नाम (*nāma*)—divine name
- ऋते (*ṛte*)—in the world of truth
- आस (*āsa*)—is established (is renowned)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who shine in heaven have impelled the waters that belong to the cloud and are attractive, so that they pervade the interiors of all the quarters and flow, and have brought welfare to all beings. O Indra of excellent deeds, you are the complete protector of all living beings; certainly you do not wish for their destruction. Your power surpasses the demonic delusions. Your divine name is established even in the world of truth.

##### English translation
You, (Indra), who are radiant in heaven, spread through the regions, for the good (of mankind) those the beautiful (waters) of the unyielding cloud : doer of good deeds, you are the preserver (of men), not (destined for their detriment : you are superior to all delusions ; your name abides in the world of truth.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सहःभरिः ।  
> प्रसर्र्णः । अनु । बर्हिः । वृषा । शिशुः । मध्यॆ । युवा । अजरः । विस्सुहा ।  
> हितः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयमाग्नेया होतृत्वयुवत्वादिलिंगैः । आयमग्निरत्यं सततमतनार्हं
> हविराज्यादिकं सचते । सेवते । कीदृशं हविः । सत् । सत्पलसाधनत्वाद्धविरपि सत् ।
> धातु च धारकं सर्वस्य । हूयमानस्य हविष आदित्यद्वारा वृष्टिसाधनत्वात् तया च
> वृष्ट्या प्रजोत्पत्तेर्धारकत्वं । तथा हि । अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते ।
> आदित्याज्ञायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः । मनु. ३. ७६. । इति । अरिष्टागातुरहिंसितगमनः । सति तस्य गमने यज्ञनिष्पत्ता फलसिद्धेररिष्टगमनत्वं । तदेवाह ।
> स खलु होता होमनिष्पादकः सहोभरिर्बलस्य भर्ता बर्हिरनु प्रसस्राणः
> प्रकर्षण सरन् वृषा वर्षकः फलस्य शिशुः स इव रक्षणीयोऽप्रौढो वा युवा
> सवत्र मिश्रयिताजरो जरारहितो विस्सुहा विस्सुहाणामोषधीनां मध्यॆ हितो
> निहितः स्थापितः । एवंभूतः सचते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this Ṛk is addressed to Agni, as the marks of being the Hotṛ priest, being a youth and the like show. This Agni partakes of the perpetual oblation, the ghee and the rest, that is fit to be offered continually. What kind of oblation? A good one: since it is the means of a good result, the oblation too is good. It is also the sustainer of all: the oblation poured into the fire is the means of rain through the sun, and through that rain creatures are born, so it is the sustainer. For so it is said: the offering properly cast into the fire reaches the sun; from the sun rain arises, from rain food, and from that creatures (Manu. 3. 76). Agni is of unharmed course, because when he moves the sacrifice is accomplished and its fruit obtained. Sāyaṇa then says the same thing again of him: he is the Hotṛ, the accomplisher of the offering; the bearer of strength; gliding forth over the sacred grass; the showerer, who rains down the fruit; a child, to be protected like one, or else immature; a youth, who mingles with everything; free from old age; and placed in the midst of the plants. Such a one partakes of the oblation. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरिष्टगातुः (*ariṣṭagātuḥ*)—of unharmed course
- होता (*hotā*)—accomplisher of the offering
- सहोभरिः (*sahobhariḥ*)—bearer of strength
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—showerer of desires
- शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*)—newly born

- युवा (*yuvā*)—youthful
- अजरः (*ajaraḥ*)—free from decay
- विस्तुहा (*vistuhā*)—of the plants
- मध्यॆ (*madhyè*)—in the midst
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—one who is established
- सः (*saḥ*)—Agni
- बर्हिः अनु (*barhiḥ anu*)—upon the seat of sacred grass
- प्रसर्त्राणः (*prasartrāṇaḥ*)—moving **NOTE**
- धातु (*dhātu*)—that which sustains all
- अत्यं च (*atyaṃ ca*)—and that which is to be offered continually
- सत् च (*sat ca*)—and that which gives a good result
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation
- सचते (*sacate*)—partakes of

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is of unharmed course, the accomplisher of the offering, the bearer of strength, the showerer of desires, newly born, youthful, free from decay, and established in the midst of the plants, moving upon the seat of sacred grass, partakes of the oblation that sustains all, that is to be offered continually, and that gives a good result.

##### English translation
He, (Agni), is associated with the perpetual oblation that is the true (source of good); the sustainer of all, he is of unrestricted movement, the offerer (of burnt-offerings), the cherisher of strength: gliding especially over the sacred grass, the showerer (of benefits) ; an infant, a youth, exempt from decay, whose place is among plants.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषा सौरी ना । एते रश्मयः सुयुजः सुष्टु परस्परं संयुक्ता यामन्यज्ञगमन इष्टय एषणाय नीचीः । नीचं गच्छंतीति शेषः । अमुष्मै यजमानाय
> यन्नो यम्या गमनार्हाः । अथवा यमो नियमितादित्यः । तस्य संबंधिनः ।
> ऋतावृधो यज्ञस्य वर्धयितारश्च । अयमादित्यः सुयंतुभिः सुगमनै: सर्वशास्यैः
> सर्वस्य शासकैरभीशुभी रश्मिभिः क्रिविः कर्ता नामानि नामकान्युदकानि प्रवणे निम्मे
> भूप्रदेशे मुषायति । मुष्णाति । आदत्त इत्यर्थः । अथवाग्निनावाह्यस्याग्नेरेतेऽश्वा
> इष्टये यज्ञगमनाय यामनि रथे सुयुजः प्रगच्छंति । शिष्टं समानं । क्रिविः क्रिविसदृशोऽग्निः प्रवणे न मानि हवींष्युक्तलक्षणाभिर्ज्वालाभिर्मुषायति । आदत्ते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this Ṛk is addressed to the sun **NOTE**. These rays are well joined with one another; at the going of the sacrifice, for its desire, they go downward (the verb is to be supplied). They are fit to go for this sacrificer. Or else the word for them refers to Yama, the restraining Āditya, and means those that belong to him; they are also the augmenters of the sacrifice. This Āditya, with these rays that go well and rule over all, is the doer: he takes the waters, the things so named, in the low ground; that is, he draws them to himself. Or else, Sāyaṇa gives another explanation: these are the horses of Agni, who is to be borne along by Agni, and for the sake of going to the sacrifice they proceed well yoked in the chariot; the rest is the same. Agni, like the active one, takes up the oblations with the flames of the kind described, in the low places **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वः एते (*vaḥ ete*)—these rays of yours
- सुयुजः (*suyujaḥ*)—well united with one another
- अमुष्मै (*amuṣmai*)—for this sacrificer
- यम्यः (*yamyaḥ*)—regulating, or belonging to Āditya
- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—augmenting the sacrifice
- यामन् (*yāman*)—in going to the sacrifice
- इष्टये (*iṣṭaye*)—being desirous
- नीचीः प्र (*nīcīḥ pra*)—(they) spread downward
- सुयंतुभिः (*suyaṃtubhiḥ*)—having excellent spreading
- सर्वशास्यैः (*sarvaśāsyaiḥ*)—governing the world
- अभीशुभिः (*abhīśubhiḥ*)—with these very rays
- क्रिविः (*kriviḥ*)—Āditya or Agni, who acts
- नामानि (*nāmāni*)—the waters, or the oblation
- प्रवणे (*pravaṇe*)—in your regions **NOTE**
- मुषायति (*muṣāyati*)—draws to himself

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These rays of the sun or of Agni, well united with one another, spread downward, augmenting the sacrifice for this sacrificer, and being desirous of going to the sacrifice. With these same rays, which have excellent spreading and govern the world, Āditya or Agni, who acts, draws to himself all the waters that are in your regions.

##### English translation
These well-combined rays (of the sun) are descending with intent to proceed on the path (of the sacrifice), amplifiers of the ceremony for this (its institutor) : operating with these swift-moving, all-regulating rays, he' (Aditya), steals the waters (that flow) in low places.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this Ṛk the commentator has explained the meaning in two ways, with reference to Āditya and with reference to Agni. Like the rays of the sun, the rays of the flame of fire also spread in every direction. The sun's

### Printed p. 464

rays draw up the waters that lie in low ground such as pits, that is to say, they make the water dry up. The rays of Agni, by means of the flame, draw up the oblations and other things offered in the sacrifice and carry them to the gods.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋजुगाथ शोभनस्तुतिकाग्ने तरुभिस्तरुविकारैर्ग्रह्यः सुतेगृभनुभिषुतेन
> रसेन गृहीतं वयाकिनं । कुत्सिता वयाः शाखा वयाका लताः । तद्वंतं सोमं
> चित्तगर्भासु चित्तग्राहिणेषु स्तुतिषु स्तुतिभिः सह संजर्भुराणो गृभन् गृण्णन्
> सुस्वरुः शोभनगमनः शोभनस्तुतिको वा त्वं धारवाकेषु । धारयंति वाकान्
> स्तोत्राणीति धारवाका ऋत्विग्यजमानाः । तेषु मध्यॆ शोभसे । किंचाध्वरे जीवः
> सर्वस्य जीवयिता पत्नीः पालयित्रिरोषधीर्ज्वाला ना अभि अभिमुखं वर्धस्व ।
> अभिवर्धय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Agni: "O Agni of straight and excellent praise." The Soma is described as taken up by the pressed juice, and as having creepers, for the word means bad branches, which are creepers; he refers to the Soma that has them **NOTE**. Agni, seizing and taking it up together with praises that charm the mind, being of good going or of good praise, shines among the holders of the praises, that is, among the priests and sacrificers who hold the utterances. Moreover, in the sacrifice, Agni is the life-giver of all; he is to grow towards the protecting herbs, the flames, and make them grow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋजुगाथ (*ṛjugātha*)—O Agni, who are worshipped with faultless praise
- तरुभिः (*tarubhiḥ*)—(filled) with vessels made of wood **NOTE**
- सुतेगृभं (*sutegṛbhaṃ*)—that which is pressed and consists of juice
- वयाकिनं (*vayākinaṃ*)—**NOTE**

### Printed p. 465

- the Soma
- चित्तगर्भासु (*cittagarbhāsu*)—with praises that attract the mind
- संजर्भुराणः (*saṃjarbhurāṇaḥ*)—accepting
- सुस्वरुः (*susvaruḥ*)—having an excellent spreading
- धारवाकेषु (*dhāravākeṣu*)—among the priests and others who recite the praises
- शोभसे (*śobhase*)—you shine
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- जीवः (*jīvaḥ*)—as the giver of life to all
- पत्निः (*patniḥ*)—the protecting flames
- अभि वर्धस्व (*abhi vardhasva*)—cause them to increase fully

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who are worshipped with faultless praise, you accept the Soma, which is filled into the vessels (grahas) made of wood and is pressed and of the nature of juice, together with praises that attract the mind, and having an excellent spreading you shine among the priests and others who recite the praises. As the giver of life to all in the sacrifice, cause the protecting flames to increase fully.

##### English translation
Object of honest eulogium, (Agni), you shine amongst the reciters of your praises when the Soma is received at its effusion by the wooden (cups), and you accepting (the beverage), are animated by the heart-affecting (praises) : giver of life, increase in the sacrifice your protecting flames.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या॒दृगे॒व ददृ॑शे ता॒दृगु॑च्यते॒ सं छा॒यया॑ दधिरे सि॒द्धया॒प्सा ।  
> म॒हीम॒स्मभ्य॑मुरु॒षामु॒रु ज्रयो॑ बृ॒हत्सु॒वीर॒मन॑पच्युतं॒ सहः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यादृक् । एव । ददृशे । तादृक् । उच्यते । सं । छायया । दधिरे । सिद्धया ।  
> अप्सु । आ ।

### Printed p. 466

> महीं । अस्मभ्यं । उरुसां । उरु । ज्रयः । बृहत् । सुवीरं । अनपच्युतं ।  
> सहः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषा वैश्वदेवी । यादृगेव ददृशे यादृग्रूपमेव दृश्यते तादृगुच्यते ।
> तादृग्रूपमेवोच्यते । यथादृष्टमेव स्तूयते न तु परवचनप्रत्ययेन ।
> यस्माच्छायया दीप्त्या सिद्धर्या साधिकया सहाप्सु व्यापकासु स्तुतिषु अप्पेव
> वा आ सं दधिरे सम्यग्दारयंति स्वीयं रूपं स्तुतिं वा । ते देवा महीं महतीं
> पूज्यामुरुषां बहुदात्रीं रयिमुरु प्रभूतं ज्रयो वेगं बृहन्महत्सुवीरं
> शोभनवीर्यमपत्यमनपच्युतमनुपक्षीणं सहो बलं चाभिभावुकमस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छंत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this Ṛk is addressed to the All-gods. In whatever form the deity is seen, in that very form he is spoken of: he is praised as he is seen, and not on the strength of another's word. Since the gods, together with their radiance (which he glosses as brightness) and with that which accomplishes, firmly hold their own form or their praise in the waters, that is, in the praises that pervade, or else in the waters themselves, let those gods give us great and venerable wealth that gives abundantly, plentiful speed, great and excellent valour and offspring, and strength that is unexhausted and overcomes (enemies). Such, he says, is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यादृगेव (*yādṛgeva*)—(the deity) in whatever form
- ददृशे (*dadṛśe*)—is seen (becomes perceptible)
- तादृक् (*tādṛk*)—precisely according to that form
- उच्यते (*ucyate*)—is designated
- सिध्रया (*sidhrayā*)—consisting of a combination
- छायया (*chāyayā*)—with radiance (all those deities)
- अप्पु (*appu*)—in the waters
- आ सं दधिरे (*ā saṃ dadhire*)—(all their own forms) they have taken up as if gathered together; (those same deities)
- महीं (*mahīṃ*)—great
- उरुषां (*uruṣāṃ*)—and abundant wealth
- उरु (*uru*)—abundant
- ज्रयः (*jrayaḥ*)—power (speed)
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—abundantly
- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*)—excellent sons
- अनपच्युतं (*anapacyutaṃ*)—freedom from decay
- सहः (*sahaḥ*)—strength
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us, may they graciously give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In whatever way a deity becomes perceptible, in that same way he is designated. All those deities too have taken up their forms in the waters, as if gathered together, with their radiance that consists of a combination. May the deities graciously give us great and abundant wealth, abundant speed, excellent sons, freedom from decay, and strength.

##### English translation
Such as (the deity) is beheld, such is he said (to be): they abide with concentrated splendour in the waters: (may they bestow) upon us honourable and ample (riches), great energy, numerous male offspring, and undecaying vigour.

### Printed p. 467

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this mantra beginning यादृगेव ददृशे तादृगुच्यते (*yādṛgeva dadṛśe tādṛgucyate*) the nature of the vision of the supreme reality is explained. It is not possible for everyone to know the true nature of the supreme reality. Each person describes the supreme reality in his own personal language only to the extent to which he has realised its nature according to his own capacity. Sāyaṇa has given the purport of this as यथा दृष्टमेव श्रूयते न तु परवचनप्रत्ययेन (*yathā dṛṣṭameva śrūyate na tu paravacanapratyayena*).

In the commentary on the Brahma Sūtras the difference between what depends on the thing itself and what depends on the person has been shown thus:
इह तु भूतं ब्रह्म जिज्ञास्यं नित्यत्वान्न पुरुषव्यापारतंत्रं । (*iha tu bhūtaṃ brahma jijñāsyaṃ nityatvānna puruṣavyāpārataṃtraṃ |*) (Bra. Sū. Bhā. 1-1-1).
What depends on the thing itself lies beyond the vision of a person; what is within a person's vision is not what depends wholly on the person, as it is explained there. In the same way Sāyaṇa too has shown the difference between the two kinds of conviction, the conviction from seeing and the conviction from another's word. The purport of this very mantra is explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa in this way:

तमेतमग्निरित्यध्वरव उपासते । यजुरित्येष हीदग्ं सर्वं युनक्ति सामेति छंदोगा एतस्मिन् हीदग्ं सर्वग्ं समानमुक्थमिति बह्वृचा एष हीदग्ं सर्वमुत्थापयति यातुरिति यातुविद एतेन हीदग्ं सर्वं यतं विषमिति सर्पाः सर्प इति सर्पविद ऊर्गिति देवा रयिरिति मनुष्या मायेत्यसुराः स्वधेति पितरो देवजन इति देवजनविदो रूपमिति गंधर्वा गंध इत्यप्सरसस्तं यथा यथोपासते तदेव भवति तद्धैनान्भूत्वावति तस्मादेतमेवंवित्सर्वैरेवैतैरुपासीत सर्वग्ं हैतद्भवति सर्वग्ं हैनमेतद्भूत्वावति ॥ (*tametamagnirityadhvarava upāsate | yajurityeṣa hīdagṃ sarvaṃ yunakti sāmeti chaṃdogā etasmin hīdagṃ sarvagṃ samānamukthamiti bahvṛcā eṣa hīdagṃ sarvamutthāpayati yāturiti yātuvida etena hīdagṃ sarvaṃ yataṃ viṣamiti sarpāḥ sarpa iti sarpavida ūrgiti devā rayiriti manuṣyā māyetyasurāḥ svadheti pitaro devajana iti devajanavido rūpamiti gaṃdharvā gaṃdha ityapsarasastaṃ yathā yathopāsate tadeva bhavati taddhainānbhūtvāvati tasmādetamevaṃvitsarvairevaitairupāsīta sarvagṃ haitadbhavati sarvagṃ hainametadbhūtvāvati ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-5-2-20).

The divine principle that exists, the Adhvaryus worship as Agni (the fire-altar). The Adhvaryus are those who follow the Yajur Veda. Because it joins the whole universe together under one rule, this principle is called Yajus. Sāyaṇa has explained in his commentary: एष पुरुष इदं सर्वं जगद्युनक्ति सर्वत्र स्वयं संगत इति (*eṣa puruṣa idaṃ sarvaṃ jagadyunakti sarvatra svayaṃ saṃgata iti*), that is, this great Person, pervading everywhere by himself, brings unity into the whole world. Because in this principle all the individuals of the universe receive a common support, the Chandogas called this principle

### Printed p. 468

by the name सामन् (*sāman*). Sāyaṇa's explanation is एतस्मिन् परमात्मनि कारणे सर्वं कार्यजातं समानमिति (*etasmin paramātmani kāraṇe sarvaṃ kāryajātaṃ samānamiti*): in this Supreme Self, which is the cause of the world, all the effects that are produced from it find an equal place, and hence the name. This is the manner in which the followers of the Sāma Veda describe the supreme reality.

Because this great cause raises up everything, and everything arises from it, the Bahvṛcas (the followers of the Ṛg Veda) have called it Uktha.

Because everything is drawn by it, those who practise spells call it a thing of illusion (यातु (*yātu*)). Those who know the serpents worship the same as the serpent. The gods call this same thing Ūrk (Ūrj), that is, food full of strength. The Asuras describe and worship it as a thing of illusion. The Fathers who have gone to heaven worship it as Svadhā. The divine folk worship it as the divine folk, the Gandharvas as form, and the Apsarases as fragrance.

In this way, because it appears in a different manner to each point of view, the supreme reality too has the capacity of nature to assume that very form. To those who, assuming each form, worship that form, it gives the fruit that corresponds to that form. But the one who, having realised all these forms together in a single reality, worships it, sees that whole reality and obtains the full fruit: thus the manifoldness of vision is the subject here. This passage of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa conveys both the unity of the supreme reality described in the present mantra, and the manifoldness of the vision of this reality that has many forms. This very thing is stated in the Bhagavad Gītā:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यंते तांस्तथैन भजाम्यहं । (*ye yathā māṃ prapadyaṃte tāṃstathaina bhajāmyahaṃ |*) (Bha. 96. 3-11) **NOTE**
in the form of the assurance of the Supreme Self: in whatever way any persons worship and adore me, in that very way I approach each of them.

In the divisions stated above the manifold forms of the supreme reality have been shown. The three kinds of division, the pure, the passionate and the dark, also appear. That is to say, the Self of the universe is all-pervading, containing all things, real and unreal, and is the inner controller of all. Whatever principle is of the nature of light, and whatever principle is of the nature of darkness, all of it is a particular manifestation of the Supreme Self. Both these kinds of nature are in the divisions stated above. They are as follows:

### Printed p. 469

1) the fire-altar; 2) साम (*sāma*); 3) Uktha; 4) illusion; 5) Ūrk (Ūrj); 6) Svadhā; 7) form; 8) fragrance, and so on.

Although such a unity that has diversity has been described before in one or two places (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164), the description of the nature of the principle here is in a special form. What the seers who have faith in the true principle worship as the spiritual principle, the sorcerers of dark nature worship as the instrument of their magic and as having the form of illusion. Therefore the division into real and unreal is only what depends on the person. What depends on the thing itself consists of both kinds. That which is full of divinity and that which is of demonic nature, both these, the divine and the demonic, are branches of what depends on the thing itself. This very thing is stated in the Ṛk Saṃhitā:
एक एवाग्निर्बहुधा समिद्ध एकः सूरो विश्वमनु प्रभूतः । एकैवोषाः सर्वमिदं वि भात्येकं ना इदं नि बभूव सर्वं ॥ (*eka evāgnirbahudhā samiddha ekaḥ sūro viśvamanu prabhūtaḥ | ekaivoṣāḥ sarvamidaṃ vi bhātyekaṃ nā idaṃ ni babhūva sarvaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-58_2).
In mantras such as this the oneness of Brahman is set forth. Moreover, in the present mantra two matters must be noted chiefly: what the conviction from another's word that Sāyaṇa mentions means, and what छायया संदधिरे (*chāyayā saṃdadhire*) means. Therefore, first, what is indicated by the word छाययू (*chāyayū*) **NOTE** deserves examination.

**Shade**
In the present mantra Sāyaṇa has taken the word for shade to mean दीप्त्या (*dīptyā*), that is, "by brightness". This is a meaning contrary to common usage. The word for shade ordinarily means shadow, that is, something devoid of brightness. What is intended in saying here that it is bright must be considered.

यान्त्राये मर्तान्नुषूदो अग्ने ते स्याम मघवानो वयं च । छायेव विश्वं भुवनं सिसक्ष्यापप्रिवान्नोदसी अंतरिक्षु ॥ (*yāntrāye martānnuṣūdo agne te syāma maghavāno vayaṃ ca | chāyeva viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sisakṣyāpaprivānnodasī aṃtarikṣu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-77-8).
Here the all-pervading nature of Agni, who has spread round heaven and earth and everything, is compared to a shade. But if there is to be a comparison with the shade, what is the quality that Agni and the shade have in common? It is that of being a place of refuge for protection. Because the quality of being a refuge for protection is present, the simile of the shade

### Printed p. 470

is present, and therefore the word for shade is used in a special sense. In this same sense this word is used also in mantras such as उपच्छाया मिन घृणेः (*upacchāyā mina ghṛṇeḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-38).

In the present mantra the word conveys not only the meaning of a refuge for protection, but also the clear meaning that the deities who pervade all the waters are reflections, and that these reflections are by nature such as to spread a very radiant brightness. All these deities are particular manifestations of the supreme reality and nothing different from it. Therefore, when it is said that the deities pervaded the whole universe with their shade, the purport is that the supreme reality itself pervades the whole universe with its shade, in the form of the deities, that is, with its reflection. The shade of this supreme reality is the means by which the individual forms of that whole world, which in the state of sleep lay contained within the Lord himself and (from the world's point of view) in a condition of darkness, may become manifest in the waking state. Before this manifestation there was neither light, nor sign, nor shade, nor shelter. Only the principle in the form of heat, hidden behind the world, lay asleep. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-1-2) तम आसीत्तमसा गूह्ममग्रे . . . (*tama āsīttamasā gūhmamagre . . .*)

ऋतं पिबंतौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहां प्रविष्टा परमे पराधे । छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदंति प्रंचाग्नयो ये च प्रिणाचिकेताः ॥ (*ṛtaṃ pibaṃtau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭā parame parādhe | chāyātapau brahmavido vadaṃti praṃcāgnayo ye ca priṇāciketāḥ ‖*) (Ka. Ka. U. 3-1) **NOTE**
Two principles have joined together in the most hidden space of the heart, having attained the union that is the fruit of their good deeds. The knowers of Brahman call them shade and heat. Here the meaning is that the nature of the undivided Supreme Brahman has these two natures. This is the same idea:
असच्च सच्च परमे व्योमन्दक्षस्य जन्मन्नदितेरुपस्थे । अग्निर्ह नः प्रथमजा ऋतस्य पूर्व आयुनि वृषभश्च धेनुः ॥ (*asacca sacca parame vyomandakṣasya janmannaditerupasthe | agnirha naḥ prathamajā ṛtasya pūrva āyuni vṛṣabhaśca dhenuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-25-7).
In this Ṛk the description that Agni, in the most excellent region of the sky, at the time when he is united with Varuṇa, is the union of the real and the unreal, also conveys this same idea.

For the original reality, which is of the nature of the real and the unreal and of the nature of shade and heat **NOTE**, the desire to develop itself is just the desire to be transformed from death into the state that takes the form of the living being. मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतात् (*mṛtyormukṣīya māmṛtāt*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7 59-12)

### Printed p. 471

The support of the principle of development, which is lit up by the principle that is hidden (not reachable by the perception of the world) and enveloped in darkness, is the extremely extensive earth (Bhūmi); this earth is the support. But it does not follow, because freedom from death has been obtained, that there is again no death at all.

In the passage य आत्मदा बलदा यस्य विश्व उपासते प्रशिषं यस्य देवाः । यस्य छायामृतं यस्य मृत्युः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधॆम ॥ (*ya ātmadā baladā yasya viśva upāsate praśiṣaṃ yasya devāḥ | yasya chāyāmṛtaṃ yasya mṛtyuḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhèma ‖*) (Mṛ. Saṃ. 10-121-2) **NOTE** it is stated that even for Prajāpati, the creator, the bondage of death has not been removed. Hiraṇyagarbha, Agni, Prajāpati and the rest include both the principles, of life and of death. This point is praised in sentences such as स संनयः स विनयः (*sa saṃnayaḥ sa vinayaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-24.9). Therefore in this mantra that has been quoted (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-121-2), what is indicated by the word for shade is the whole world of practical life. The purport is that in this practical world the individuals, each according to the form of the principle, shine as reflections of their original principle. In this way the usages छायामृत (*chāyāmṛta*), सदसत् (*sadasat*) and अदिति—दिति (*aditi—diti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5.62.8) all indicate one and the same idea.

Thus, in giving the word for shade the meaning of light, and in stating the purport that this light means the manifold forms of manifestation of the supreme principle that are seen in the practical world, and the reflections of the original principle, the sentences of the Saṃhitā themselves are the basis. Contrary to this, there are also some contexts in which the word for shade is used in the sense of darkness. For example:

यज्ञवल्क्य वेद ना अहं तं पुरुषं सर्वस्यात्मनः परायणं यमात्थ य एवायं छायामयः पुरुषः स एष वदैव शाकल्य तस्य का देवतेति मृत्युरिति होवाच ॥ (*yajñavalkya veda nā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yamāttha ya evāyaṃ chāyāmayaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣa vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti mṛtyuriti hovāca ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-14)

Here Śaṅkarācārya has stated the purport of छायामयः (*chāyāmayaḥ*) as अज्ञानमयः (*ajñānamayaḥ*). For such a person (puruṣa) अप एवायतनम् (*apa evāyatanam*): the waters alone are his dwelling. What is described in the Ṛk Saṃhitā as तमसा गॊळ्हं (*tamasā gòḷhaṃ*) is described as छायामयः (*chāyāmayaḥ*). The same is described also by the epithets अपामुपस्थे (*apāmupasthe*), अदितेरुपस्थे (*aditerupasthe*) and निर्ऋतेरुपस्थे (*nirṛterupasthe*). The Upaniṣads describe it by अमूर्त (*amūrta*), अशब्द (*aśabda*), शांत (*śāṃta*) and the like.

Therefore the word for shade is used also in the context of describing the two states of the supreme principle. When the Brahman that is the cause has been transformed into the state of effect **NOTE**, his particular radiances are designated by the word

### Printed p. 472

for shade. One meaning is that the whole moving and unmoving world, in the forms of gods, men and animals, also reflects this very thing by the shade-form of this Supreme Brahman.

Secondly, that which before the time of creation was praised by the epithets अमूर्त (*amūrta*), अशब्द (*aśabda*), शांत (*śāṃta*) and the like (Maitrī. 6-3-22 ; 36) **NOTE**, and by descriptions such as नैवेह किंचनास आसीन्मृत्युनैवेदमावृतमासीत् (*naiveha kiṃcanāsa āsīnmṛtyunaivedamāvṛtamāsīt*) (Bṛ. U. 1-2-1), "everything was enveloped by death alone", that unmodified state of the Supreme Brahman, which is the cause, is also described by the very word for shade.

In the present mantra the first meaning is the natural one. In Sāyaṇa's explaining the word छायया (*chāyayā*) as दीप्त्या (*dīptyā*), the purport is that they are the multiple, luminous reflections of that very principle which, being the cause, is praised in manifold forms through the variety of views.

**The original principle**
This same original principle has been described by names such as अग्नि (*agni*), सामन् (*sāman*), उक्त (*ukta*), ऊर्ज (*ūrja*) and गंधर्व (*gaṃdharva*), on the basis of the qualities that came within the vision of each, and has been worshipped by worshippers such as the Adhvaryus and the Bahvṛcas. That Indra and the other deities are all manifold particular manifestations of one principle, and that by the greatness of that principle रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव (*rūpaṃrūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-18), one thing assumes different forms, has been set out at length, as the Vedic view on the unity of the deities, by citing sentences such as those of the Nirukta. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164, the 46th mantra, for example: इंद्रं मित्रं वरुण मग्निमाहुः (*iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇa magnimāhuḥ*).) Although the same subject is present here too, this mantra, which sets forth the unity of the universe, is explained here without raising merely the unity of the deities; and the opposed elements that shine forth in the world, being and non-being, shade and heat, birth and death, light and darkness, also have one and the same support. The views stated in the Vedic sentences on the point that there is no thing other than Brahman are examined closely.

The word for shade has been said above to denote both the manifest and the unmanifest nature of the supreme principle: manifoldness in the manifest world, and unity in the unmanifest state. Sentences such as अपादशीर्षा गुहमानो अंता (*apādaśīrṣā guhamāno aṃtā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-1-11) explain these two points. (The purport of the quoted mantra 4-1-11 was given above in explaining the subject of अहिर्बुध्न्य (*ahirbudhnya*).) In the same way the epithets सहस्रशीर्षा (*sahasraśīrṣā*) and सहस्राक्षः (*sahasrākṣaḥ*) and the like also indicate it. Here the word for thousand

### Printed p. 473

does not, as a numeral, designate merely the number one thousand. The word for thousand means infinite; it means ब्रह्मयोनि (*brahmayoni*) (Mu. U. 3-1-3) **NOTE**, which holds in itself infinite forms. Mantras such as तदेकं (*tadekaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-2), विश्वमेकं (*viśvamekaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3.54-8) and वचोभिरेकं संतं बहुधा कल्पयंति (*vacobhirekaṃ saṃtaṃ bahudhā kalpayaṃti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114-5) convey this same purport. That is, whatever manifestation takes place in the form of shade, the designation of names follows accordingly. The present aim is thus to understand in what way the sentences of the Saṃhitā have examined the point that both the manifest and the unmanifest natures belong to one and the same original thing, and that its transformation and recurrence are the form of the activity of the world.

ये अर्वांचस्ता उ पराच आहुर्ये परांचस्ता उ अर्वाच आहुः । (*ye arvāṃcastā u parāca āhurye parāṃcastā u arvāca āhuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-19)

Those rays of the sun's disc that have a downward movement are said by those who know time to be of upward position, and those rays that have an upward spreading they call downward-going. The same is indicated also in the sentence या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी (*yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī*) (Bha. Gī. 2-69) **NOTE**. In this way a single word sometimes indicates both elements, light and darkness. For example, the purports of one or two words such as विश्वरूप (*viśvarūpa*) and वृत्र (*vṛtra*) can be examined by looking at certain contexts.

Viśvarūpa: this word is an epithet of an Asura. It is likewise an epithet of Tvaṣṭṛ, the creator of all the gods, men and others.

अस्मभ्यं तत्वाष्ट्रं विश्वरूपमरंधयः साख्यस्य त्रिताय (*asmabhyaṃ tatvāṣṭraṃ viśvarūpamaraṃdhayaḥ sākhyasya tritāya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-19)

त्वाष्ट्रस्य चिद्विश्वरूपस्य गोनामाचक्राणस्त्रीणि शीर्षा परा वर्क् । (*tvāṣṭrasya cidviśvarūpasya gonāmācakrāṇastrīṇi śīrṣā parā vark |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 18-8-9) **NOTE**

In all such contexts the slaying of the Asura Viśvarūpa is narrated. These descriptions of Viśvarūpa, such as that he had three heads, six eyes and seven rays, show both his demonic nature and his divinity. As soon as this Viśvarūpa, who is an Asura, is slain, Vṛtra comes into being. At once Agni and Soma both come under the demonic power called Vṛtra. Indra and Tvaṣṭṛ are alarmed at this. Then Tvaṣṭṛ makes the thunderbolt for Indra. As soon as Indra raises the thunderbolt, Agni and Soma, both of whom were contained in

### Printed p. 474

Vṛtra, show their fear, and Indra makes the Asura Vṛtra open his mouth wide. Then Agni and Soma both come out. When this is so, one must note what the purport of this account is. (मुखादिंद्रश्चाग्निश्च (*mukhādiṃdraścāgniśca*) Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90.13: it is stated that from the mouth of the Puruṣa both Indra and Agni came into being.) Describing the nature of this Vṛtra, who was produced by the resolve of Tvaṣṭṛ in order to obstruct Indra, the Taittirīya Saṃhitā says thus:

स इमांल्लोकानवृणोद्यदिमांल्लोकानवृणोत्तद्वत्रस्य वृत्रत्वं (*sa imāṃllokānavṛṇodyadimāṃllokānavṛṇottadvatrasya vṛtratvaṃ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12 2)

Because, as soon as he was produced, he pervaded all the worlds, his name is Vṛtra; thus the very characteristics that are stated elsewhere of Viṣṇu and of Viśvarūpa are stated also of this Vṛtra. Just as it is stated that Agni and Soma were contained in Vṛtra, it is stated also that Heaven and Earth were contained in this very Vṛtra. When, as soon as Agni and Soma had come out of Vṛtra, Indra raised the thunderbolt again, Heaven and Earth also stopped Indra, saying: "We two are in him; do not strike him." When it is stated that Heaven and Earth, having then come out from him, obtained their own individual light, the all-pervading nature of Vṛtra is understood. In this context the word that Indra says to Viṣṇu is noteworthy.

सोऽब्रवीद्विष्णवेहीदमा हरिष्यावो येनायमिद मिति स विष्णुस्त्रेधात्मानं नि न्यथत्त पृथिव्यां तृतीयमंतरिक्षे तृतीयं दिवि तृतीयं ॥ (*so 'bravīdviṣṇavehīdamā hariṣyāvo yenāyamida miti sa viṣṇustredhātmānaṃ ni nyathatta pṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamaṃtarikṣe tṛtīyaṃ divi tṛtīyaṃ ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2.4-1-3)

"O Viṣṇu, help me to slay this Vṛtra, who has made the three worlds contained in himself." Then Viṣṇu too pervaded the three worlds, in order to check Vṛtra, who had pervaded the three worlds. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-9, the description यस्मिन्नाजुहवुर्भुवनानि विश्वा (*yasminnājuhavurbhuvanāni viśvā*), that they offered the entire universe in Agni as an oblation, indicates the same point in the pervasiveness of Vṛtra. The gods, the scriptures, fame, food and form, all of these went out from the mouth of Vṛtra. The same kind of descriptions that occur in the Puruṣa Sūkta occur at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra. Therefore, at the time of the destruction of both Viśvarūpa and Vṛtra, who are famed as Asuras, a preparation preceding the time of creation appears. The division of the Puruṣa described in the Puruṣa Sūkta and the division of Vṛtra at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra are of one

### Printed p. 475

and the same kind. At the time of the division of the Puruṣa, the effort at creation and the origin of the gods, men and others, as indicated by sentences such as व्यदधुः (*vyadadhuḥ*), कतिधा (*katidhā*) and व्यकल्पयन् (*vyakalpayan*), are described also at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra. The word Vṛtra is formed from the root vṛ, which gives such meanings as "be enveloped" and "revolve". Therefore this epithet can praise also the qualities of Agni, the sun and the others who have these qualities. Just as the word अहि (*ahi*) explains the quality of Vṛtra, so it also makes known the quality of Agni and Soma. The epithet अहि (*ahi*), which indicates the individual quality of Vṛtra, in the same way makes known the quality of Agni and the others. (This subject has been stated in the section on अहिर्बुध्न्य (*ahirbudhnya*).) In this section it is also necessary to consider the similarity between Vṛtra and Varuṇa. As described in mantras such as आनीदवातं (*ānīdavātaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-2), the lower power by which the whole universe is covered may be denoted by the word Vṛtra or by the word Varuṇa. Both words are formed from the root vṛ, which gives the meaning "be enveloped". From this root not only the meaning "pervade" or "be enveloped" but also the meaning "be enveloped again and again" is possible. Because this meaning is possible, the word for shade can have two meanings, one a manifest state and the other an unmanifest state. Creation and dissolution being in the form of recurrence, the meaning of the word for shade also follows this order. For this very reason the movement of Agni too is in alternation. He who reflects the original principle in the form of अहिर्बुध्न्य (*ahirbudhnya*) is in the sacrificial hall in the form of the Gārhapatya and the rest, and having absorbed the whole world in himself, makes it shine forth now and again. Describing this very thing, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says स ना एषोऽग्निरेव यदग्निष्टोमः (*sa nā eṣo 'gnireva yadagniṣṭomaḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 3-43). It means that Agni, hidden in the cave, is not ordinarily within the sight of the world, but is the one who appears on the altar in the form of the Agniṣṭoma. That is, in the enveloped form he is the one who reveals the spiritual and the divine natures. That is, there is neither eternal concealment nor eternal manifestation.

For this very reason this Agniṣṭoma has been compared to a chariot wheel. (यथैव प्रायणं यथोदयनं (*yathaiva prāyaṇaṃ yathodayanaṃ*)) यदस्य पूर्वं अपरं तदस्य (*yadasya pūrvaṃ aparaṃ tadasya*): what is the beginning of this is its end also. For this very reason the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa describes the Agniṣṭoma as अहेरेव सर्पणं (*ahereva sarpaṇaṃ*). Just as the supreme principle is described as न ह ना अस्मा उदेति न निम्लोचति (*na ha nā asmā udeti na nimlocati*) (Chā. U. 3-11-3), neither rising nor setting, so the Agniṣṭoma, which has a revolution of every form, is described.

### Printed p. 476

In this way the principle of shade, which is in the form of recurrence, now hidden within and now with an outer light, is praised in the Ṛk Saṃhitā in many contexts. But in all those places the word for shade need not be expressed; the same idea is indicated precisely.

समानमेतदुदकमुच्चैत्यव चाहभिः (*samānametadudakamuccaityava cāhabhiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-51)

सदृशीरद्य सदृशीरिदु श्वो दीर्घं सचंते वरुणस्य धाम (*sadṛśīradya sadṛśīridu śvo dīrghaṃ sacaṃte varuṇasya dhāma*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-8)

अनंतास उरवो विश्वत्वः सीं परि द्यावापृथिवी यंति पंथाः (*anaṃtāsa uravo viśvatvaḥ sīṃ pari dyāvāpṛthivī yaṃti paṃthāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-47-2)

The views contained in sentences such as these convey the very purport that is in the present mantra. The Taittirīya Saṃhitā describes very eminently this principle, which is of the nature of recurrence and shows unity even in variety. The shade principle that has two forms, though they are two transformations of one and the same thing, as light and darkness are two transformations: this is the description of it.

द्वौ समुद्रौ विततावजूर्यौ पर्यावर्तेते जठरेव पादाः । तयोः पश्यंतो अति यंत्यन्यमपश्यंतः । सेतुनाति यंत्यन्यं । द्वे द्रधसी सतती वस्त एकः केशी विश्वा भुवनानि विद्वान् । तिरोधायैत्यसितं वसानश्चक्रमा दत्ते अनुहाय जार्यै ॥ (*dvau samudrau vitatāvajūryau paryāvartete jaṭhareva pādāḥ | tayoḥ paśyaṃto ati yaṃtyanyamapaśyaṃtaḥ | setunāti yaṃtyanyaṃ | dve dradhasī satatī vasta ekaḥ keśī viśvā bhuvanāni vidvān | tirodhāyaityasitaṃ vasānaścakramā datte anuhāya jāryai ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-2-19, 2)

There are two oceans that do not waste away. They are imperishable. As waves in the midst of the sea arise one after another in alternation, so these oceans revolve in alternation. Men pass these days and nights knowing the nature of one of them and not knowing the nature of the other. Of these, Āditya covers one with his rays (this is the shade in the form of radiance), and he hides the other. Then he leaves the night, which is in the form of darkness, and takes possession of the shining day. Then he leaves the night, which is in the form of darkness, and takes possession of the shining day. In this way the two shades are described.

Therefore, although in the present mantra the beyond-perception of the supreme principle is described by the description यादृगेव ददृशे (*yādṛgeva dadṛśe*), certain aspects come within the sight of certain views through the manifestation of that same thing in the form of shade. This very thing again in the Ṛk Saṃhitā,

### Printed p. 477

सुपर्णं विप्राः कवयो वचोभिरेकं संतं बहुधा कल्पयंति । छंदांसि च दधतो अध्वरेषु ग्रहान्सोमस्य मिमते द्वादश ॥ (*suparṇaṃ viprāḥ kavayo vacobhirekaṃ saṃtaṃ bahudhā kalpayaṃti | chaṃdāṃsi ca dadhato adhvareṣu grahānsomasya mimate dvādaśa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114-5)

It is said that wise mortals, of transcendent insight, conceive by manifold imaginings the Supreme Self, who is of fair flight and non-dual, and praise him. This single principle is the beginning and the support of the universe. Describing this very thing in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad:

तद्धेवं तर्हव्याकृतमासीत् तन्नामरूपाभ्यामेव व्याक्रियतासौ नामायमिदं रूपं इति तदिदमस्येतर्हि नामरूपाभ्यामेव व्याक्रियतेऽसौ नामायमिदं रूप इति स एष इह प्रविस्थः ॥ (*taddhevaṃ tarhavyākṛtamāsīt tannāmarūpābhyāmeva vyākriyatāsau nāmāyamidaṃ rūpaṃ iti tadidamasyetarhi nāmarūpābhyāmeva vyākriyate 'sau nāmāyamidaṃ rūpa iti sa eṣa iha pravisthaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-7)

Before this Brahman was transformed into a manifested form it was undifferentiated and non-dual. Then it had neither name nor form. When, in the state of manifested form, it acquired individual differentiation, individual name and form became established; only in the state of worldly dealing are there such designations as "this is the name of this person" and "this is the form of this person". Before that there was only the non-dual principle, devoid of name and form. The whole empirical world is only a part of this supreme principle. Thus the Upaniṣads describe this supreme principle.

This One is the soul of the universe, the consciousness-power pervading the universe, and the support of universal energy. It is not merely the earth that is described in many other mantras, nor the atmosphere, nor the light of the sun, nor the physical force of nature. The Brahman-principle whose existence is established in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka by the very negating statements नेति नेति (*neti neti*) is the cosmic consciousness. The universal principle that is described elsewhere as Ṛta and Aditi is here the subject of praise. This power, which fills the principle of life into the many living beings of the universe, is all-pervading.

In this way, if the description of the principle that teaches the oneness of the universe, रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव (*rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva*), teaches non-duality, then is the very principle that is propounded in the sentences of the Ṛk Saṃhitā also described in the Upaniṣads and other texts? What relation between the world, which is an effect, and the causal entity is indicated in the Ṛk Saṃhitā? Is the same relation indicated in the Upaniṣads and other texts, or is there a difference of opinion there? Can the meaning that has been given to the word "shade" in the present mantra also be possible in the Upaniṣads? Since these points are essential for the examination of spiritual truth, it must be examined critically whether or not there is a difference between the purport of the sentences that propound this same principle in the Upaniṣads and the purport indicated in the present mantra. This matter will be explained in a suitable context later.

### Printed p. 478

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वेत्यगु॒र्जनि॑वा॒न्वा अति॒ स्पृधः॑ समर्य॒ता मन॑सा॒ सूर्यः॑  ॒
> कविः ।  
> घ्रं॒सं रक्षं॑तं॒ परि॑ वि॒श्वतो॒ गय॑म॒स्माकं॒ शर्म॑ वनव॒त्  ॑
> स्वावसुः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वेति । आग्रुः । जनिवान् । वै । अति । स्पृधः । समर्यता । मनसा । सूर्यः । कविः।  
> घ्रंसं । रक्षंतं । परि । विश्वतः । गयं । अस्माकु । शर्म । वनवत् । स्ववसुः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयं सौरी । सूर्यो देवोऽगुरग्रगामिा जनिवान्वै जन्मवान् जायानान्वा ।
> उषा ह्यस्य जाया । वा इति प्रसिद्धौ । कविः क्रांतदर्शी समर्यता समरमिच्छता
> मनसा स्पृधः संग्रामानति वेति । अति गच्छति मंदेहानसुरान्नोद्दुं । फ्रंसं
> दीप्तं गयं गृहमंतरिक्षं ना विश्वतः सर्वतो रक्षंतं । परिचरेमेति शेषः । स
> देवोऽस्माकं शर्म सुखं परि सम्यग्वनवत् । दद्यात् । स्वावसुः स्वायत्तधनः सन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is addressed to Sūrya. The god Sūrya goes in front, and is जनिवान्वै (*janivānvai*), that is, one who has a birth or one who has a wife; Uṣas is his wife. **NOTE**. He is कविः (*kaviḥ*), the one of far-reaching vision. With a mind that desires battle he goes forth against the combats, that is, he goes to throw down the demons called Mandehas. गयं (*gayaṃ*) means a house, here the middle region; it is shining and protective on every side, and the words "we attend it" are to be supplied. May that god grant us happiness in full measure. He is स्वावसुः (*svāvasuḥ*), one whose wealth is under his own control.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

The far-seeing god Sūrya goes in front, and, united with his wife Uṣas, rushes forward to the battle with a mind that fights the demons called Mandehas.

> धायि धत्ते ॥ कर्तरि चिण् ॥ सामर्थ्यान्मनो गम्यते । तं । यथानिर्देशं प्रतिनिर्दिष्टव्यत्वात्तादृशमित्यर्थो ज्ञातव्यः । तादृशं काममपस्यया कर्मणा हविःस्तुत्यादिलक्षणेन विदत् । विंदते । य उ य एव स्वयमनन्यप्रेरितः सन् स्वमनीषय्येव
> वहते धारयति फलं सोरमलमत्यर्थं करत् । करोति । अथवा य उ य एव
> स्वयं वहते स्वयमेवानुतिष्ठति सोत्यर्थं कुर्यात् । न ह्यन्येन कारितं
> फलवद्भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is addressed to Agni or to Sūrya. O god, the one who is greatly grown, of this goer Sūrya (यतुनस्य (*yatunasya*); the root yat means movement), distinguished by a banner, that is, by a sign such as the rising that makes known his action, and praised by the Ṛṣis, is approached, that is, served, by the sacrificer. By what means? By the praises in which your name or your form is present. Or else: the sacrificer approaches you, who are distinguished by your banner, namely the action of removing darkness and the like, and who are ever moving. On whatever desire the mind is fixed, that very desire, as Sāyaṇa explains from the context, he obtains by his action consisting of oblation, praise and the like. He who, of his own accord, uninstigated by another and by his own judgment, bears the fruit, brings it fully to completion. Or else: he who himself carries out the rite does it fully, for what is done through another does not bear fruit.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Sūrya) यासु (*yāsu*)—in whichever praises (of the Ṛṣis)
- ते (*te*)—your
- नाम (*nāma*)—well-known recitation of your name exists
- ऋषिस्वरं (*ṛṣisvaraṃ*)—one who is praised by the hymns of the Ṛṣis
- ज्यायांसं (*jyāyāṃsaṃ*)—the eldest (among the gods)
- केतुना (*ketunā*)—one who is designated by marks such as rising
- अस्य यतुनस्य (*asya yatunasya*)—and who is ever moving, you
- चरति (*carati*)—(the sacrificer) approaches (worships)
- यादृश्मिन् (*yādṛśmin*)—in what kind of wish
- धायि (*dhāyi*)—he fixes his mind
- तं (*taṃ*)—that same desired object
- अपस्यया (*apasyayā*)—by his devout action
- विदत् (*vidat*)—he obtains
- य उ (*ya u*)—whoever
- स्वयं (*svayaṃ*)—of his own accord (without compulsion)
- करत् (*karat*)—offers worship and the like
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- अरं (*araṃ*)—abundant fruit
- वहते (*vahate*)—bears (obtains)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Sūrya, the sacrificer approaches you, who are praised by the hymns of those Ṛṣis in whose praises your well-known name is sung, who are the eldest among the gods, who are designated by marks such as rising, and who are ever moving. Whatever desired object the sacrificer resolves to obtain, that very object he obtains by his devout action. He who offers worship and the like of his own accord, without compulsion, obtains abundant fruit.

##### English translation
The (pious man) proceeds to you, most excellent (of the gods, who are indicated) by the sign of this moving (revolution); who are hymned by the Rishis in whose praises your name (is glorified): he obtains that blessing by his devotion, on whatsoever (his desire) has been fixed; and he also, who of his own accord offers (worship), acquires abundant (reward).

### Printed p. 481

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यादृश्मिन् (*yādṛśmin*)—When Yāska gives the explanation of this word, he takes the present Ṛk itself as the example, यादृश्मिन् धायि तमपस्ययाविदत् (*yādṛśmin dhāyi tamapasyayāvidat*) (Ni. 6-16), and explains the meaning as यादृशेऽधायि तमपस्ययाविदत् । (*yādṛśe 'dhāyi tamapasyayāvidat |*). Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, says:

यादृश्मिन् यादृशे कामे धायि मनो धत्ते तं तादृशं कामं तया अपस्त्यया क्रियया हविःस्तुत्यादिलक्षणया तन प्रसादात् अविदत् अलभतेत्यर्थः ॥ (*yādṛśmin yādṛśe kāme dhāyi mano dhatte taṃ tādṛśaṃ kāmaṃ tayā apastyayā kriyayā haviḥstutyādilakṣaṇayā tana prasādāt avidat alabhatetyarthaḥ ‖*)

The sacrificer who performs a sacrifice obtains, in whatever kind of desire he fixes his mind, that is, whatever object he wishes for, that very object by offering oblations and the like to Indra, that is, by action such as the giving of oblations; this is the main purport. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 482

> स्तोत्राणि तत्सवनमिति । अत्रास्मिन्यजमानगृहे क्रवणस्य स्तुतिकर्तुर्हार्दि हृदयसंबंधि हृदयगतं काम्यं फलं न रेजते । न विचलति । न मृषा भवति । यत्र यस्मिन्
> स्तोतृगृहे मतिः स्तुतिः पूतबंधनी पूतं सूर्यमनुबध्नती विद्यते अत्र न रेजत
> इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk too is addressed to Sūrya. Sūrya is the ocean of these praises, the final resting place like an ocean; our most excellent praise goes to him. Or else, the praise is of these subjects, the priests. सवनं (*savanaṃ*) is the house of sacrifice, where Soma is pressed. It is not harmed, but rather prospers. It is the sacrifice in which extended hymns of praise are recited. Here, in the house of the sacrificer, the desired fruit of the praiser (क्रवणस्य (*kravaṇasya*)), the fruit that lies in his heart (हार्दि (*hārdi*)), does not waver, does not become false. In whichever house of the praiser the praise is found that binds to the pure one, that is, to the pure Sūrya, there it does not waver.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—of all these praises of ours
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—Sūrya, who like the ocean is the one receptacle
- अग्रिमा (*agrimā*)—this most excellent praise of ours
- अव तस्थे (*ava tasthe*)—goes, joins and abides (in him)
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which sacrificial rite
- आयता (*āyatā*)—the praises are recited at length
- सवनं (*savanaṃ*)—that sacrifice
- न रिष्यति (*na riṣyati*)—is not impeded
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which house of sacrifice
- मतिः (*matiḥ*)—the praise (meditation) (of the sacrificer)
- पूतबंधनी विद्यते (*pūtabaṃdhanī vidyate*)—is directed to the pure Sūrya alone
- अत्र (*atra*)—in such a house of sacrifice
- क्रवणस्य (*kravaṇasya*)—of the praiser
- हार्दि (*hārdi*)—the dear desired object
- न रेजते (*na rejate*)—does not move (is not wasted)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Our most excellent praise goes to Sūrya, who like the ocean is the one receptacle for all these praises of ours, and abides there. The sacrifice in which praises are recited at length is not impeded. In whatever house of sacrifice the praise of the sacrificer, which is meditation, is directed to the pure Sūrya, in such a house of sacrifice the dear desired object of the praiser is not wasted.

##### English translation
The chiefest of these (our praises) proceed to the ocean-like sun : that chamber of sacrifice fails not in which (his praises) are prolonged : there the heart's desire of the worshipper is not disappointed where the mind is known to be attached to the pure (sun).

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अवत्सारस्य । स्पृणवाम । रण्वभिः । शविष्ठं । वाजं । विदुषा । चित् । अर्थ्यं ॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयमपि सौरी । स हि स खलु सविता देवः सर्वैः स्तुत्यः । सर्वकामपूरक
> इत्यर्थः । हिशब्दो लोकवेदयोः प्रसिद्धिद्योतकः । तस्मात्सकाशात् । अत्रान्ये च
> ऋषयोऽत्र दृष्टलिंगा इत्युक्तत्वात् क्षत्रादय ऋषयः । क्षत्रस्य मनसस्यॆवावदस्य
> यजतस्य सध्रेरवत्सारस्य चैषामृषीणामस्माकं रण्वभी रमणीयाभिश्चित्तिभिः स्पृणवामु । पूरयाम । किं शविष्ठं वाजमतिशयेन बलवदन्नं । अन्नं वै वाज इति
> श्रुतेः । विदुषा चिद्विपश्चितार्ध्यं समर्धनीयं स्पृणवामु । क्षत्रादयो वयमिति
> संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk too is addressed to Sūrya. He, the god Savitṛ, is to be praised by all; that is, he is the fulfiller of all desires. The particle हि (*hi*) shows that this is well known in the world and in the Veda. From him, and here also the other seers, since it is said that the seers saw the marks here, namely Kṣatra and the rest, are named: Kṣatra, Manasa, Evāvada **NOTE**, Yajata, Sadhri and Avatsāra. "We would fill", that is, we would satisfy, with the pleasing thoughts of these seers; what do we fill? शविष्ठं वाजं (*śaviṣṭhaṃ vājaṃ*), food that is exceedingly strong, since the Śruti says that food is वाज (*vāja*). Food that is to be honoured even by the wise, that is, food that is to be duly increased, we would fill; the construction is "we, Kṣatra and the rest".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहि (*sahi*)—this very Āditya (is to be praised by all)
- क्षत्रस्य (*kṣatrasya*)—of Kṣatra
- मनसस्य (*manasasya*)—of Manasa
- एवावदस्य (*evāvadasya*)—of Evāvada
- यजतस्य (*yajatasya*)—of Yajata
- सध्रेः (*sadhreḥ*)—of Sadhri
- अवत्सारस्य (*avatsārasya*)—of Avatsāra (of all these seers)
- रण्वभिः (*raṇvabhiḥ*)—pleasing
- चित्तिभिः (*cittibhiḥ*)—together with the meditative minds
- विदुषा चित् (*viduṣā cit*)—even by the wise
- अर्ध्यं (*ardhyaṃ*)—that which is to be honoured
- शविष्ठं (*śaviṣṭhaṃ*)—exceedingly strong
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- स्पृणवाम (*spṛṇavāma*)—let us fill fully

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Āditya is to be praised by all. With the very meditative mind with which all the seers, Kṣatra, Manasa, Evāvada, Sadhri, Yajata, Avatsāra and the rest, expressed their devotion, with that mind and with all those feelings of devotion, let us fully obtain food that is to be honoured even by the wise and that is exceedingly strong.

### Printed p. 484

##### English translation
He verily (is to be glorified): let us, with the pleasant thoughts of Kshtra, Manasa, Avada, Yajata, Sadhri and Avatsara, fill up the invigorating food, (the portion) to be shared by the wise.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मददेवत्येयं । विश्ववारादीनां त्रयाणामृषीणां स्वभूत आसामपां
> सोमरसलक्षणानां मदः श्येनः शंसनीयगमनः शीघ्रं पातृसकाशं गंतादितिरदीनोऽतिसमृद्धः कक्ष्यः कक्ष्यपूरकश्च भवतीति शेषः । ते विश्ववारादयः सत्ते प्रवृत्ता
> एतवे सोमं प्राप्तुं तत्पानायान्यमन्यं परस्परं समर्थयंति।याचंतेऽनुज्ञां।
> ते विषाणं विशेषेण मदस्य दातारं परिपानमंत्यंतिके विदुः । जानंति लभंते वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is addressed to Mada, intoxication. Of the waters, that is, the Soma juices, that belong to the three seers Viśvavāra and the rest, the exhilaration is श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*), of praiseworthy going, quickly going to the drinker; अदितिः (*aditiḥ*), not poor, exceedingly rich; and कक्ष्यः (*kakṣyaḥ*), one that fills the girth; "becomes" is to be supplied. Those seers, Viśvavāra and the rest, engaged in the sacrifice, to obtain Soma and to drink it, mutually entreat each other, that is, ask for permission. They know or obtain close at hand the draught that is a special giver of intoxication.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववारस्य (*viśvavārasya*)—of Viśvavāra
- यजतस्य (*yajatasya*)—of Yajata
- मायिनः (*māyinaḥ*)—of the one called Māyi (belonging to all these seers)
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—of the Soma juice
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—the exhilaration
- श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*)—is of praiseworthy going
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—exceedingly rich
- कक्ष्यः (*kakṣyaḥ*)—and has satisfaction that fills to the throat
- अन्यमन्यं (*anyamanyaṃ*)—these seers, one to another
- सं अर्थयंति (*saṃ arthayaṃti*)—ask for permission
- ते (*te*)—they
- विषाणां (*viṣāṇāṃ*)—exceedingly productive of intoxication
- परिपानं (*paripānaṃ*)—this drinking of Soma
- अंती (*aṃtī*)—close at hand
- विदुः (*viduḥ*)—obtain

### Printed p. 485

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The exhilaration of the Soma juice that belongs to the seers Viśvavāra, Yajata and Māyi is praiseworthy, exceedingly rich, and gives satisfaction to the very throat. For this same Soma-drinking these seers mutually ask each other for permission. Then they immediately obtain, and drink, this Soma, which is exceedingly productive of intoxication.

##### English translation
Swift is the excessive and girth-distending inebriation of Vishwavara, Yajata and Mayin : (by dr nking) of these (juices) they urge one another to drink : they find the copious draught the promt giver of intoxication.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सदापृणः (*sadāpṛṇaḥ*) is one who is always generous, a seer of this name; यजतः (*yajataḥ*) is the sacrificer; बाहुवृक्तः (*bāhuvṛktaḥ*) is one whose sacred grass is cut by his arms **NOTE**; श्रुतवित् (*śrutavit*) is the knower of what is heard (the Veda), **NOTE**; and तर्यः (*taryaḥ*) is a seer of that name. The singular is used for each of these five in mutual relation. Each such seer would destroy the enemies; वः (*vaḥ*) means "of you", and सचा (*sacā*) means "together", that is, together with you. That seer reaches the two most excellent desires, those relating to this world and to the next, and shines, because he serves this host of the gods with praises that are well and abundantly mingled with offerings.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सदापृणः (*sadāpṛṇaḥ*)—Sadāpṛṇa
- यजतः (*yajataḥ*)—Yajata
- बाहुवृक्तं (*bāhuvṛktaṃ*)—Bāhuvṛkta
- श्रुतवित् (*śrutavit*)—Śrutavit
- तर्यः (*taryaḥ*)—Tarya (all these seers, individually)
- वः (*vaḥ*)—with you
- सचा (*sacā*)—united
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—the enemies
- वि वधीत् (*vi vadhīt*)—may they destroy utterly
- यत् (*yat*)—which seer
- ईं गणं (*īṃ gaṇaṃ*)—this host of gods
- सुप्रयावभिः (*suprayāvabhiḥ*)—with oblations joined with praises
- भजते (*bhajate*)—worships
- सः (*saḥ*)—that seer
- वरा (*varā*)—the most excellent
- उभा (*ubhā*)—and belonging to both worlds, this and the next, the desired objects
- प्रत्येति (*pratyeti*)—obtains
- भाति च (*bhāti ca*)—and shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Sadāpṛṇa, Yajata, Bāhuvṛkta, Śrutavit and Tarya, all these seers, individually united with you, utterly destroy the enemies. The seer who worships this host of gods with oblations mingled with praises obtains the most excellent desired objects, belonging to both worlds, this and the next, and shines.

##### English translation
May Sadaprina, Yajata, Bahuvrikta, Shrutavit, Tarya, associated, with you, destroy your foes: the Rishi obtains his desires in both (worlds), and shines brightly, whenever he adores with well-mingled (offerings and praises) the host (of heaven).

> धियां सर्वेषां कर्मणामूध उद्धततरं फलमुदंचन ऊर्ध्वमुद्गमयिता ।

> स्वापमकुर्वन् अनवरतमध्येति । स्मरत्यवत्सारः । सुतंभरस्तादृश इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सुतंभरः (*sutaṃbharaḥ*) is the conductor of the sacrifice for me, Avatsāra, the sacrificer; he is a seer of that name. He is सत्पतिः (*satpatiḥ*), the protector of the fruits that exist; that is, he becomes the Hotṛ. He is the one who brings up on high the udder, that is, the lofty fruit, of all the acts (धियां (*dhiyāṃ*)); that is, he is the one who obtains the fruit. The cow (धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*)) brought juicy, essential milk; there the milk was resorted to, and by implication it resorts to him. Reciting all that in order, not sleeping, that is, without making sleep, he studies without interruption; Avatsāra remembers; Sutaṃbhara is such.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यजमानस्य (*yajamānasya*)—for the sacrificer (named Avatsāra)
- सुतंभरः (*sutaṃbharaḥ*)—the seer called Sutaṃbhara
- सत्पतिः (*satpatiḥ*)—is in the form of the Hotṛ
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- विश्वासां (*viśvāsāṃ*)—all
- धियां (*dhiyāṃ*)—the acts
- ऊधः (*ūdhaḥ*)—the fruits
- उदञ्ञानः (*udaññānaḥ*)—is the one who makes them arise
- धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*)—the cow
- रसवत् (*rasavat*)—juicy
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—milk
- भरत् (*bharat*)—provides
- शिश्रिये (*śiśriye*)—(it) is distributed
- अनुब्रुवाणः (*anubruvāṇaḥ*)—reciting these very things in order
- न स्वपन् (*na svapan*)—without being at all idle
- अध्येति (*adhyeti*)—(Sutaṃbhara) studies (meditates)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the sacrificer called Avatsāra, the seer called Sutaṃbhara is in the form of the Hotṛ. He causes the fruit of all acts to arise. The cow provides juicy milk. Reciting these very things in order, without being at all idle, Sutaṃbhara studies.

##### English translation
Sutambhara is the ministrant priest of the institutor of the sacrifice, the causer of the upward ascent of all holy rites : the milch-cow offers juicy

### Printed p. 488

(milk), the milk is distributed : announcing this in order, (Avatsara) studies the holy texts) without repose.

> यो देवो जागार सर्वदा विनिद्रो जागरूको गृहे वर्तते तम्मृचः
> सर्वशास्त्रात्मिकाः कामयंते । यश्च जागार तमु तमेव सामानि स्तोत्ररूपाणि
> यंति । प्राप्नुवंति । यो जागार तमयमभिषुतः सोम आह वक्ति मां स्वीकुर्विति ।

> भवामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The god who is always awake, sleepless and vigilant in the house, him the Ṛks, which embody all the śāstras, desire. And him who is awake, him alone, the Sāmans, which are in the form of hymns, go to and reach. Him who is awake this pressed Soma addresses: "Accept me." O Agni, in the friendship of you, such as you are, in doing what is good in the same renown, I am firmly established. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The matters stated in the preceding Ṛk are stated here. There, with यः (*yaḥ*) जागार (*jāgāra*), the question was asked, "Who remains vigilant in the house at all times without sleeping?", and in this Ṛk the seer gives the answer: with अग्निः (*agniḥ*) जागार (*jāgāra*), Agni himself is at all times vigilant in the house of the sacrificers.

## Sūkta 45 (Maṇḍala 5)

The forty-fifth hymn.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ चतुर्थेनुवाके द्वादश सूक्तानि । तत्र विदा दिव इत्येकादशर्चं प्रथमं
> सूक्तं । सदापृणो नामात्रेय ऋषिः । त्रिष्टुप् छंदः । वै तदित्युक्तत्वादिदमपि
> वैश्वदेवं । विदा एकादश सदापृण इत्यनुक्रमणिका । विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now, in the fourth anuvāka there are twelve sūktas. Of these, the first sūkta, beginning विदा दिव (*vidā diva*), has eleven Ṛks. Its seer is Sadāpṛṇa, of the Ātreya line, and its metre is Triṣṭubh. Because of the statement that it is "that indeed", this one too is addressed to the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇikā says: विदा एकादश सदापृण (*vidā ekādaśa sadāpṛṇa*). The application is the one derived from indicative marks.

Anuvāda: In the fourth anuvāka of the fifth maṇḍala there are twelve sūktas. Of these, this sūkta beginning विदा दिवः (*vidā divaḥ*) is the first. It has eleven Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the one called Sadāpṛṇa Ātreya; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: विदा एकादश सदापृण (*vidā ekādaśa sadāpṛṇa*). The application is by indicative marks.

### Printed p. 492

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here Indra and the others are the deities indicated by the marks. Here the release by Indra of the cows of the Aṅgirases, which the Paṇis had carried off and placed under the mountain, is set forth. विदाः (*vidāḥ*): Indra caused to be found. What? The hidden cows; that is the connection. Doing what? Casting the thunderbolt (अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)) by means of the praises of the Aṅgirases as the cause, casting it upon the guards and in order to split the mountain. The rays of the approaching Uṣas went, that is, they spread everywhere. Sūrya, the one who moves, the Āditya, uncovered the nights, which were full of masses of darkness, and rose. Having done so, the god Sūrya opened the doors that belong to men, that is, by removing the darkness he made them available for the dealings of men and others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra)
- उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*)—as the reward of the praise of the Aṅgirases
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the atmosphere
- अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)—the thunderbolt
- विस्यन् (*visyan*)—hurling
- विदाः (*vidāḥ*)—found out (the cows that were hidden)
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—of the goddess Uṣas
- आयत्याः (*āyatyāḥ*)—very extensive
- अर्चिनः (*arcinaḥ*)—the rays
- गुः (*guḥ*)—spread everywhere
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—Āditya
- उदगात् (*udagāt*)—rose
- व्रजिनीः (*vrajinīḥ*)—the pitch darkness
- अपावृत (*apāvṛta*)—dispersed
- मानुषीः (*mānuṣīḥ*)—useful for the dealings of men
- दुरः (*duraḥ*)—the doors (the openings)
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the god Sūrya, who is divine in nature
- वि आवः (*vi āvaḥ*)—opened

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the reward of the praise of the Aṅgirases, Indra, hurling the thunderbolt from the atmosphere, found the cows that were hidden. The very extensive rays of the goddess Uṣas spread everywhere. Āditya rose and dispersed the pitch darkness; the god Sūrya, who is divine in nature, provided the openings that are useful for the dealings of men.

##### English translation
(Indra) recovered (the hidden cattle), hurling his thunderbolt from heaven at the prayers of the Angirasas : the rays of the approaching dawn are spread around : the divine sun, scattering the clustered gloom, has risen and set open the doors of (the habitations of) men.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this sūkta it is described that the cows of the Aṅgirasa seers were carried off by the asuras called Paṇis and hidden in a cave of the mountain, and that Indra, with the help of the divine bitch called Saramā, found the cave regions where those cows were and released them.
