> न । रूपनामैतत् । रूपमिव द्रव्यं । यथा द्रव्याणि घटपटादीनि नीलपीतादिरूपं
> लभंते तद्वत् । तथा गवां रश्मीनां मातोषा जानती सूर्य उदेष्यति मया च
> व्युच्छनं कर्तव्यमिति जानत्यूर्वान्महतोऽंतरिक्षादा गात् । आगच्छति । तथा नद्यश्च
> धन्वर्णसः । धन्वतिर्गतिकर्मा । धन्वंति गच्छंत्यर्णांसि यासु तास्त्रथोक्ताः । दीर्घाभावश्यांदसः ॥ खादोअर्णा भक्षितकूलोदकाः । कूलंकषा इत्यर्थः । नद्यश्चैवंरूपा भवंति । किंच द्यौश्च सुमिता सुष्टु गृहे स्थापिता स्फूणेव गृहाधारस्तंभ इव
> दृंहत । दृढाभवत् । एतत्सर्वं सूर्यस्याज्ञयेति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The god Sūrya distributes his splendour, that is, he makes it shine. रूपनामैतत् (*rūpanāmaitat*) **NOTE**: the word means "form". As substances such as jars and cloths take on forms such as blue and yellow, so it is here. Uṣas, the mother of the rays, knowing that Sūrya will rise and that she herself must dawn, comes from the great atmosphere. So too the rivers are धन्वर्णसः (*dhanvarṇasaḥ*): the root धन्व (*dhanva*) means going, and they are those in which the waters go. खादोअर्णा (*khādoarṇā*) means those whose waters eat away the banks, that is, they cut into the banks; the rivers become of this kind. Moreover, heaven was made firm, well placed like a pillar that supports a house. The sense is that all this is by the command of Sūrya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Sūrya
- अमतिं न (*amatiṃ na*)—as forms such as blue and yellow are distributed to substances such as jars
- श्रियं (*śriyaṃ*)—his radiance
- वि सात् (*vi sāt*)—causes to spread and extend everywhere
- गवां (*gavāṃ*)—to the rays
- माता (*mātā*)—the mother, the goddess Uṣas
- जानती (*jānatī*)—knowing her duty at the time of sunrise
- ऊर्वात् (*ūrvāt*)—from the great atmosphere
- आ गात् (*ā gāt*)—she comes into being and arrives
- धन्वर्णसः (*dhanvarṇasaḥ*)—swiftly flowing
- नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)—the rivers
- खादोआर्णाः (*khādoārṇāḥ*)—have currents that cut into their banks
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the atmosphere
- सुमिता (*sumitā*)—firmly set
- स्थूणा इव (*sthūṇā iva*)—like a pillar of a house
- दृंहत (*dṛṃhata*)—is firmly established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As forms such as blue and yellow are distributed to substances such as jars and cloths, so Sūrya makes his radiance spread and extend everywhere. Uṣas, the mother of the rays, knowing her duty at the time of sunrise, comes into being and arrives from the great atmosphere.

### Printed p. 494

Swiftly flowing rivers have currents that cut into their banks. The atmosphere is firmly established like a pillar of a house that has been set firmly.

##### English translation
The sun distributes his radiance as if it was a substance: the parent of the rays of light, (the dawn), knowing his approach, comes from the spacious (firmament): the rivers with running waters flow, breaking down their banks: the heaven is stable like a well-constructed pillar.

> वि । पर्वतः । जिहीत । साधत । द्यौः । आऽविवासंतः । दसयंत । भूम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मै मुख्यमुक्ताय स्तोत्रे पर्वतस्य पर्ववतो मेघस्य गर्भो गर्भस्थानीयमुदकं जिहीत । चलति । चालयति वेंद्रः । कीदृशायास्मै । महीनां महतीनां स्तुतीनां जनुष उत्पादयित्रे पूर्वाय्य प्रत्नाय । तदेव पुनरुच्यते ।
> पर्वतो मेघो वि जिहीत । द्यौश्च साधत । साधयति वृष्टिं । आविवासंतः सर्वतपरिचरंतोंगिरसो भूमात्यधिकं दसयंत । उपक्षपयंत्यात्मानं कर्मभिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For this one, who is the chief and is praised with the stotra, the womb of the cloud, that is, the water that stands as its womb, moves; or Indra sets it moving. What kind is this one? The producer of great praises, the ancient one. The same is repeated: the cloud opens, and heaven brings about rain. The Aṅgirases, serving all around, दसयंत (*dasayaṃta*), bring themselves low exceedingly, that is, they wear themselves down by their rites.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महीनां (*mahīnāṃ*)—for the praises possessed of great qualities
- जनुषे (*januṣe*)—for the producer
- पूर्वार्याय (*pūrvāryāya*)—in the same manner as it came about for the seer of today
- उक्ताय (*uktāya*)—for the praiser
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for my **NOTE**

### Printed p. 495

- हितक्कागि (*hitakkāgi*)—benefit
- पर्वतस्य (*parvatasya*)—of the cloud
- गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—the water that lies in the womb
- जिहीत (*jihīta*)—is released and flows
- पर्वत् (*parvat*)—the cloud
- वि (*vi*)—(the cloud) splits open, for the release of rain
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the atmosphere
- साधत (*sādhata*)—brings about the sprinkling of rain
- आविवासंतः (*āvivāsaṃtaḥ*)—the Aṅgirases, who worship everywhere
- भूम (*bhūma*)—exceedingly
- दसयंत (*dasayaṃta*)—are worn out by the labour of the rite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As it came about for the former seer, the producer of praises possessed of great qualities, so for the benefit of me, the praiser, the water that lies in the womb of the cloud is released and flows. The cloud splits open to release rain. The atmosphere brings about the sprinkling of rain. The Aṅgirases, who worship everywhere, are worn out by the exceedingly great labour of the rite.

##### English translation
To me, when offering praise, as to an ancient author of sacred songs, the burden of the cloud (descends); the cloud parts (with its burden); the sky performs (its office): the assiduously worshipping Angirasas are exhausted by much (adoration).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रा हे अग्नी ॥ परस्परापेक्षया प्रत्येकं द्विवचनं । यद्यस्येकमेव
> पदं मध्ये व्यवधानं छांदसं ॥ हे इंद्राग्नी वो युवां ॥ व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं ॥

> स्रोत्रैः कवयोऽनूचानाः पूर्व ऋषयः सुयज्ञाः शोभनयागा आविवासंतः
> स्तुत्यादिना परिचरंतो मरुतो मरुत्सदृशाः कर्मसु शीघ्रायजंति । पूजयंति ॥
> हि स्मेति पूरणौ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, O Agni": each of the two is addressed separately, with the dual used in view of their mutual connection; where a single word stands between them, that is Vedic usage. The plural "you" stands in place of the dual "you two". With words that are well spoken, that are sought by the gods and that make plain excellent qualities, I invoke you (हुवध्यै (*huvadhyai*)) for our protection, and quickly. The ancient seers, the Anūcānas, who perform good sacrifices and serve you with praise and the like, worship you with hymns, swift in their rites like the Maruts. The two particles हि स्मेति (*hi smeti*) are mere fillers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) इंद्रा (*(he) iṃdrā*)—O Indra; (हे) अग्नी (*(he) agnī*)—O Agni, that is, O Indra and Agni
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- देवजुष्टैः (*devajuṣṭaiḥ*)—worthy of being served by the gods
- सूक्तेभिः (*sūktebhiḥ*)—that have the form of a sūkta (well made)
- वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*)—with words of praise
- अवसॆ (*avasè*)—for our protection
- हुवध्यै (*huvadhyai*)—I call you, praying
- नु (*nu*)—certainly
- सुयज्ञाः (*suyajñāḥ*)—excellent conductors of sacrifice
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the seers, the Anūcānas
- आविवासंतः (*āvivāsaṃtaḥ*)—serving you
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—swift in their dealings like the Maruts
- उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*)—with instruments in the form of praise **NOTE**
- यजंतिहि स्म (*yajaṃtihi sma*)—they worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, with words of praise that are worthy of being served by the gods, that have the form of praise and are well made, I call you for our protection. The seers, excellent conductors of sacrifice and Anūcānas, serving you, worship you with instruments in the form of praise, swift in their dealings like the Maruts.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, I invoke you for my salvation with well-uttered words, agreeable to the gods; for verily, sages excelling in sacrifice, and deligently adoring, worship you with sacred songs, prompt as the Maruts (in devotion).

> वरीयः । अत्यंतमित्यर्थः । तदेवोच्यते । सनुतः संभक्त्वान् द्वेषांसि यजमानस्य
> द्वेष्टानारे दूरे दधाम । स्थापयाम । यद्वा । सनुतरित्यंतर्हितनाम । पूर्वं
> प्रकाशवैरिणां वध उक्त इदानीं प्रच्छन्नानामिति विवेकः । तदर्थं यजमानं
> प्रांचः सदापृणमवत्सारं चाच्छाभिमुखमयाम । गच्छाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is a speech of the Aṅgirases. Today, at this sacrifice, come quickly (एतो (*eto*) means: go). Let us be doers of good deeds. Let us strike down the haters of the sacrificer with violence, exceedingly. The same is then said again: the word सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*) is explained by a word that is damaged in the print, and we shall set the enemies of the sacrificer far away. Or else, the same word means hidden: earlier the slaying of open enemies was spoken of, now that of the concealed ones, this being the distinction. For that purpose, facing forward, we shall go toward the sacrificer; the words that follow, about Sadāpṛṇa and Avatsāra, are damaged in the print. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्य (*adya*)—to this sacrifice
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- एतो (*eto*)—come
- सुध्यः (*sudhyaḥ*)—endowed with good deeds
- भवानु (*bhavānu*)—let us be **NOTE**
- दुच्छनाः (*ducchanāḥ*)—the haters
- वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)—exceedingly
- प्र विनवामु (*pra vinavāmu*)—let us strike down **NOTE**
- सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*)—entering into the rite of sacrifice
- द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*)—the enemies (of the sacrificer)
- आरे (*āre*)—far away
- दधाम (*dadhāma*)—let us put
- यजमानं (*yajamānaṃ*)—to the sacrificer
- प्रांचः (*prāṃcaḥ*)—facing
- अच्छ अयानु (*accha ayānu*)—let us go and join **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Come quickly, all of you, to this sacrifice. Let all of us be endowed with good deeds. Let us strike down our haters completely and destroy them. Let us drive far away all the enemies of the sacrificer who enters into the rite of sacrifice. For this work let us go facing the sacrificer.

### Printed p. 498

##### English translation
Come to-day quickly: let us be engaged in pious acts: let us entirely annihilate the hostile: let us keep off all secret enemies: let us hasten to the presence of the institutor of the rite.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> एता॒ धियं॑ कृ॒णवा॑मा सखा॒योs प॒ या मा॒ता ऋ॑णु॒त  
> व्र॒जं गोः ।  
> यया॒ मनु॑र्वितिशि॒प्रं जि॒गाय॒ यया॑ व॒णिग्वं॒कुरापा॒  ॑
> पुरीषं ॥ ६ ॥

> यया । मनुः । विशिशिप्रं । जिगाय । यया । वणिक् । वंकुः । आप । पुरीषं ॥६॥

> नाम । हे सखायः परस्परं सखिभूता अंगिरस इत्यंगिरसां वचनं । या धीर्माता
> गवां निर्मात्रि गोर्गवां व्रजं पणिभिरपहृतमप ऋणुत अपावृणोत् । यया
> च मनुर्विशिशिप्रं निगतहनुं शत्रुं जिगाय जितवान् । यद्वा। मनुः सर्वस्य मंतें.
> द्रो विशिशिप्रो वृत्रः । स तमस्माभिः कृतया स्तोमलक्षणया धिया जिगाय ।
> यया च वणिक् वणिगिवाल्पेन कर्मणा बहुफलाकांक्षी कक्षीवान् वंकुर्जलेच्छया
> वनगामि पुरीषं पूरकमुदकमाप । याभिः सुदानू औशिजाय वणिजे दीर्घश्रवसे मधु कोशः । ऋग्वे १. ११२. ११. । इति हि श्रुतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This too is a speech of the Aṅgirases. Come: having come, let us make a hymn of praise. O friends, that is, Aṅgirases who are friends to one another, this is their word. The hymn which, as a mother, a maker of cows, opened the cow-pen of the cows that had been carried off by the Paṇis; and by which Manu conquered Viśiśipra, an enemy whose jaw had fallen. Or else, Manu is Indra, the thinker of all, and Viśiśipra is Vṛtra; he conquered him by the hymn in the form of a stoma made by us. And by which the merchant, like a trader who desires much fruit from little work, Vaṅku, that is, Kakṣīvān, going to the forest from a wish for water, obtained the filling water. So it is heard in a verse that Sāyaṇa cites with its reference (Ṛgve 1. 112. 11), the passage in which Kakṣīvān is spoken of together with the Aśvins. **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The hymn that, as a mother, as soon as it was recited, caused the cow-pen of the cows carried off by the Paṇis to be opened; by which hymn Manu conquered the asuras called Viśiśipra; with the help of which Kakṣīvān, who dealt as a merchant, wandering in the forest from a wish for water, obtained water: let us compose and recite such a hymn. O friends, Aṅgirases, come, all of you.

##### English translation
Come, friends, let us celebrate that solemn rite which was effectual in setting open the (secret) stalls of the (stolen) cattle; by which Manu overcame Visisipra ; by which the merchant, going to the wood (for it), obtained the water.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विशिशिप्रं (*viśiśipraṃ*)—Here the commentator has explained the word Viśiśipra as Vṛtra. Vṛtra also means an enemy. Therefore the sense is suggested that in the present Ṛk Manu conquered his enemy by the power of the hymn he had made. Or it may be said that Viśiśipra is a person or an asura. In this context, since this word is recited only in this Ṛk and nowhere else, nothing can be said about him.

यया वणिक् वंकुः पुरीषं आप (*yayā vaṇik vaṃkuḥ purīṣaṃ āpa*)—It is said here that the seer called Kakṣīvān, wandering in the forest for the sake of water, obtained water by the power of this hymn. But the commentator has cited the verse

याभिः सुदानू औशिजाय वणिजे दीर्घश्रवसे मधु कोशो अक्षरत् । कक्षीवंतं स्तोतारं याभिरावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥ (*yābhiḥ sudānū auśijāya vaṇije dīrghaśravase madhu kośo akṣarat | kakṣīvaṃtaṃ stotāraṃ yābhirāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gataṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-11)

### Printed p. 500

and in that Ṛk it is said that the seer Kakṣīvān praised the Aśvin deities and obtained protection from them. Whatever deity the hymn was recited to, Kakṣīvān obtained the fulfilment of his wish by the power of that hymn; therefore that matter is explained here in order to show that the greatness of that hymn is exceedingly high.

> ऋ॒तं य॒ती स॒रमा॒ गा अ॑विंद॒द्विश्वा॑नि स॒त्यांगि॑राश्चकार ॥ ७ ॥

> ऋतं । यती । सरमा । गाः । अविंदत् । विश्वानि । सत्या । अंगिराः । चकार ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नौतिरत्र शब्दमात्रे वर्तते । अशब्दयत् । येन ग्राव्णा तदभिषवेण दश मासो
> मासान् दशमासपर्यंतं नवग्वाः । नवमासपर्यंतं गवार्थमनुतिष्ठंतोऽंगिरसो नवग्वाः । नवगोयुक्ता वार्चन् अपूजयन्निंद्रं । यद्वा! दशसंख्याकमासोपेता दशमासानुष्ठाना अंगिरसोऽपरे नवग्वाल्मैते सर्वॆऽपि येनार्चंति ।
> नवग्दासः सुतसोमास इंद्रं । ऋग्वे ५. २९ १२ । इति हि निगमः । ऋतं सत्यं यज्ञं
> ना यती प्राप्नुवती सरमा सरणीला स्तुतिरूपा वागंगिरसां गवार्थमिंद्रॆण
> प्रहिता देवशुनी वा गा अविंदत् पणिभिरपहृताः । विश्वानि सर्वाणि स्तुत्यादिलक्षणानि
> सत्या सत्यानि चकारांगिराः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, at this sacrifice, the pressing stone (adri), held in the hand, sounded; the root "nu" here has only the sense of making a sound. By this stone, through the pressing, the Navagvas, the Aṅgirases who performed the rite for the sake of cows for nine months, worshipped Indra for ten months. Or else, the other Aṅgirases, endowed with ten months and performing the rite for ten months, and these Navagvas, all worship by it. So the Vedic text has it: the verse with the Navagvas, the soma pressed, and Indra (Ṛgve 5. 29 12) **NOTE**. Reaching the truth, that is the sacrifice, Saramā, the swift speech in the form of praise of the Aṅgirases, or the divine bitch sent by Indra for the sake of the cows, found the cows carried off by the Paṇis. All the things, praise and the rest, the Aṅgirā made true.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The pressing stone, by the help of which the seers called Navagva worshipped Indra for ten months entire, is held in the hand at this sacrifice and makes a sound; the divine bitch called Saramā, entering the sacrifice, found the cows. The Aṅgirā seers made all the rites of sacrifice true in nature.

##### English translation
At this sacrifice the stone (set in motion) by the hands (of the priests) makes a noice, whereby the nine-months ministrants celebrated the ten- months worship: when Sarama, going to the ceremony, discovered the cattle and Angiras rendered all the rites effective.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नवग्वाः (*navagvāḥ*)—It is the custom in the Ṛgveda to call the foremost among the Aṅgirā seers by the names Navagva and Daśagva. To explain the reason for these names the commentator has explained thus:

नवग्वै, दशग्वै—नवभिर्मासैर्गच्छंतीति नवग्वाः । दशभिर्मासैर्गच्छंतीति दशग्वाः । अंगिरसां सत्रमासीनानां मध्ये ये नवभिर्मासैरवाप्तफला उत्ति तास्तेषां नवग्वा इति संज्ञा । दशभिर्मासैर्दशग्वा इति च ॥ (*navagvai, daśagvai—navabhirmāsairgacchaṃtīti navagvāḥ | daśabhirmāsairgacchaṃtīti daśagvāḥ | aṃgirasāṃ satramāsīnānāṃ madhye ye navabhirmāsairavāptaphalā utti tāsteṣāṃ navagvā iti saṃjñā | daśabhirmāsairdaśagvā iti ca ‖*)

Some in the lineage of the seer Aṅgirā obtained their success by performing the sacrifice in only nine months, in the sattra sacrifice that lasts a year. Of them the custom is to say that the Navagvas are the foremost of those in the Aṅgirā lineage who obtained their desired end in nine months, and the Daśagvas those in the Aṅgirā lineage who obtained their desired end in ten months. On this matter Western scholars, when explaining the meaning of this word, say: The term Navagva is applied to a man generally an Angiras, in the highest degree ( Angirastama-अंगिरस्तम (*aṃgirastama*) ) who appears as a mystic race of olden times coupled with, and conceived probably as related to the Angirasas they are often associated with the Dasagvas (दशग्व (*daśagva*)). This word is used in many Ṛks of the Ṛgveda. We shall give some examples.

### Printed p. 502

येना नवग्वो दध्यज्ज पोर्णुते येन विप्रास आपिरे । (*yenā navagvo dadhyajja porṇute yena viprāsa āpire |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9.108.4)

नवग्वो नु दशग्वो अंगिरस्तमः सचा देवेषु महंते । (*navagvo nu daśagvo aṃgirastamaḥ sacā deveṣu mahaṃte |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.62-6)

सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवग्वैरभिज्ञा सत्वभिर्गा अनुग्मन् । (*sakhā ha yatra sakhibhirnavagvairabhijñā satvabhirgā anugman |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3.39.5)

अंगिरसो नः पितरो नवग्वा अथर्वाणो भृगवः सोम्यासः । (*aṃgiraso naḥ pitaro navagvā atharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somyāsaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.14-6)

येना नवग्वे अंगिरे दशग्वे सप्तास्यॆ रेवती रेवदूष ॥ (*yenā navagve aṃgire daśagve saptāsyè revatī revadūṣa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-51-4)

These words are used in these and many other Ṛks of the Ṛgveda, and in mantras such as Atharvaveda Saṃ. 19-1-56; 18-3-20. Of these, it is noteworthy that in the second example the foremost of the Aṅgirā lineage, who has obtained the famous names Navagva and Daśagva, is honoured even by the gods.

In this Ṛk and in the following Ṛks it is said that the divine bitch called Saramā found the cows. In this matter, the commentator has told a story here. Saramā is a female dog that belongs to the gods. When the demons called Paṇis had carried off the cows of the gods and hidden them in a cave, Indra sent this divine bitch Saramā to search for those cows. As, in worldly practice, a hunter sends the hunting dog that he keeps to search for beasts, so Indra also told this divine bitch to go in search of the cows. Then she said to Indra: O Indra, if you will give food such as milk for my pup, I shall go and bring the cows after searching for them. (As the followers of the Śāṭyāyana branch tell it: अन्नादिनीं ते सरमे प्रजां करोमि या नो गा अन्वविंद (*annādinīṃ te sarame prajāṃ karomi yā no gā anvaviṃda*), that is, when he said: O Saramā, I shall provide food for your pup; go and search for the cows and come back.) When Indra said: Be it so, that bitch set out, searched, found the region where the Paṇis had hidden the cows, and informed Indra of it. Having learned of it, Indra destroyed those demons, set free the cows of the gods and brought them back. This very sense is set forth in this Ṛk, so he says.

### Printed p. 503

It is known that Saramā, the bitch of the gods, that is, of Indra, had two pups, that they were with Yama, the deity of death, and that after the name of their mother they were called Sārameya:

अति द्रव सारमेयौ श्वानौ चतुरक्षौ शबलौ साधुना पथा । (*ati drava sārameyau śvānau caturakṣau śabalau sādhunā pathā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-10)

यौ ते श्वान् यम रक्षितार् चतुरक्षौ पथिरक्षी नृचक्षसौ ॥ (*yau te śvān yama rakṣitār caturakṣau pathirakṣī nṛcakṣasau ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-11)

In these Ṛks the matter of the two dogs called Sārameya, the two pups of the divine bitch Saramā, and the matter of their having four eyes become known. The matter of the above-mentioned divine bitch Saramā going to the Paṇis and negotiating with them is described in the 108th sūkta of the 10th maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda thus:

किमिच्छंती सरमा प्रेवमानडूरे ह्यध्वा जगुरिः पराचैः । कास्मेहितिः का परितक्क्यासीत्कथं रसाया आतरः पयांसि ॥ (*kimicchaṃtī saramā prevamānaḍūre hyadhvā jaguriḥ parācaiḥ | kāsmehitiḥ kā paritakkyāsītkathaṃ rasāyā ātaraḥ payāṃsi ‖*)

इंद्रस्य दूतीरिषिता चरामि मह इच्छंती पणयो निधीन् वः । अतिष्कदो भियसा तन्न आनत्तथा रसाया अतरं पयांसि ॥ (*iṃdrasya dūtīriṣitā carāmi maha icchaṃtī paṇayo nidhīn vaḥ | atiṣkado bhiyasā tanna ānattathā rasāyā ataraṃ payāṃsi ‖*)

कीदृज्जूंद्रः सरमे का दृशीका यस्येदं दूतीरसरः पराकात् । आ च गच्छान्मित्रमेना दधामाथा गवां गोपतिर्नो भवाति ॥ (*kīdṛjjūṃdraḥ sarame kā dṛśīkā yasyedaṃ dūtīrasaraḥ parākāt | ā ca gacchānmitramenā dadhāmāthā gavāṃ gopatirno bhavāti ‖*)

नाहं तं वेद दभ्यं दभत्स यस्येदं दूतीरसरं पराकात् । न तं गूहंति स्रवतो गभीरा हता इंद्रेण पणयः शयद्वे ॥ (*nāhaṃ taṃ veda dabhyaṃ dabhatsa yasyedaṃ dūtīrasaraṃ parākāt | na taṃ gūhaṃti sravato gabhīrā hatā iṃdreṇa paṇayaḥ śayadve ‖*)

इमा गावः सरमे या ऐच्छः परि दिवो अन्तान् सुभगे पतंती । कस्त एना अव सृजादयुध्युतास्माकमायुधा संति तिग्मा ॥ (*imā gāvaḥ sarame yā aicchaḥ pari divo antān subhage pataṃtī | kasta enā ava sṛjādayudhyutāsmākamāyudhā saṃti tigmā ‖*)

असेन्यावः पणयो वचांस्यनिषव्यास्तन्वः संतु पापीः । अदृष्टो न एतना अस्तु पन्था बृहस्पतिर्व उभया न मृळात् ॥ (*asenyāvaḥ paṇayo vacāṃsyaniṣavyāstanvaḥ saṃtu pāpīḥ | adṛṣṭo na etanā astu panthā bṛhaspatirva ubhayā na mṛḷāt ‖*)

अयं निधिः सरमे अद्रिबुध्नो गोभिरश्वेभिर्वसुभिर्नृष्टः । रक्षंति तं पणयो ये सुगोपा रेकु पदमलकमा जगंथ ॥ एह गमनृषयः सोमशिता अयास्को अंगिरसो ववग्वाः । त एतमूर्व० विभजंत गोनामथैतद्वचः पणयो वमन्नित् ॥ एवा च त्वं सरनु आजगंथ (*ayaṃ nidhiḥ sarame adribudhno gobhiraśvebhirvasubhirnṛṣṭaḥ | rakṣaṃti taṃ paṇayo ye sugopā reku padamalakamā jagaṃtha ‖ eha gamanṛṣayaḥ somaśitā ayāsko aṃgiraso vavagvāḥ | ta etamūrva0 vibhajaṃta gonāmathaitadvacaḥ paṇayo vamannit ‖ evā ca tvaṃ saranu ājagaṃtha*)

एह गमनृषयः सोमशिता अयास्को अंगिरसो ववग्वाः । त एतमूर्व० विभजंत गोनामथैतद्वचः पणयो वमन्नित् ॥ (*eha gamanṛṣayaḥ somaśitā ayāsko aṃgiraso vavagvāḥ | ta etamūrva0 vibhajaṃta gonāmathaitadvacaḥ paṇayo vamannit ‖*)

एवा च त्वं सरनु आजगंथ प्रबाधिता सहसा देव्येन । स्वसारं त्वा कृणवै मा पुनर्गा अप ते गवां सभगे भजाम ॥ (*evā ca tvaṃ saranu ājagaṃtha prabādhitā sahasā devyena | svasāraṃ tvā kṛṇavai mā punargā apa te gavāṃ sabhage bhajāma ‖*)

### Printed p. 504

नाहं वेद भ्रातृत्वं नो स्वसृत्वमिंद्रो विदुरंगिरसश्च घोराः । गोकामा मे अच्छदयन् यदायमपात इत पणयो वरीयः ॥ (*nāhaṃ veda bhrātṛtvaṃ no svasṛtvamiṃdro viduraṃgirasaśca ghorāḥ | gokāmā me acchadayan yadāyamapāta ita paṇayo varīyaḥ ‖*)

दूरमित पणयो वरीय उद्गावो यंतु मिनतीर्युतेन । बृहस्पतिर्या अविंदन्निगूळ्हाः सोमो ग्रावाण ऋषयश्च विप्राः ॥ (*dūramita paṇayo varīya udgāvo yaṃtu minatīryutena | bṛhaspatiryā aviṃdannigūḷhāḥ somo grāvāṇa ṛṣayaśca viprāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-18-1 to 11) **NOTE**

Its translation is given below. It is in the form of a conversation between the Paṇis and Saramā. Formerly the cows of Bṛhaspati were carried off by the Paṇis, the followers of Vala, and hidden in a secret place. Then, at Bṛhaspati's request, Indra sent the divine bitch Saramā to search for those cows. Searching for the cows, Saramā travelled a very long way, crossed a great river called Rasā that lay across the path, and came near the Paṇis. Then the Paṇis, knowing the purpose for which Saramā had come, held this conversation with her, with the thought of making friends with her:

The Paṇis: O Saramā, you appear to have come here from a long way off, with great trouble. What is the purpose for which you have come here? How did you come here? How did you cross the river called Rasā?

Saramā: Listen, O Paṇis. Directed by Indra, I have come here as his messenger. Indra desires the treasures that you have hidden. The river Rasā, in fear, helped me to cross. Therefore I crossed that river and came.

The Paṇis: O Saramā, very well. You said that Indra has sent you as his messenger. What is that Indra like to look at? (The Paṇis speak thus among themselves:) Let Saramā come, if she comes. Let us make friends with her, and let her be the mistress of our cows.

Saramā: That Indra cannot be conquered as you imagine. That Indra who sent me conquers his enemies, but others cannot conquer him. Even deep rivers cannot hold him back. Slain by him, you will have to lie on the bed of death.

The Paṇis: O Saramā, is it not for these very cows that you have come a long way by the path of the sky and desire them? But who will hand those cows over to you for nothing, without a fight? Our weapons are very sharp.

### Printed p. 505

Saramā: What is the use of your words? Is there in those words the strength of an army, or the power that bows and arrows have, in your bodies filled with sin? The path that you follow is very hard. Bṛhaspati (the owner of the cows) will show you no mercy, and will set no value on your words.

The Paṇis: O Saramā, this wealth of cattle, that is, cows, horses, goods and the like, we have gathered and brought to the mountains, and we, the Paṇis, are guarding it with great care. Your coming alone to so inaccessible a place is in vain.

Saramā: Listen, O Paṇis. The seers and the Aṅgirases, having gained strength and capacity by drinking soma, will come here under the leadership of Ayāsya, take these cows by force and divide them among themselves. Then you will know that the words you speak are in vain.

The Paṇis: O Saramā, it appears that you have the support of the gods. Therefore we shall regard you as our sister. Do not go back to Indra. Stay here. We shall give you a share in these cows too.

Saramā: I do not want the friendship and sisterhood that you offer. Indra and the terrible Aṅgirases know my nature. When I came here searching for the cows, they learned your dwelling-place by a hidden path. Therefore, O Paṇis, run far away and save yourselves. Do not delay; go to the safe region that is far off. Let the cows that are kept in the cave come out in order. Bṛhaspati, Soma and the wise seers, having found this secret place, will break open the door of the cave where the cows are and burst in.

In this conversation, one Ṛk is spoken by the Paṇis and another, in reply, by Saramā. These matters of the Paṇis' carrying off the cows are indicated in many places in the Ṛgveda.

Although in the Ṛgveda the word Paṇi has the meaning of a wealthy man who carries on trade and the like, it also means a man who does not perform sacrifices and the like and does not give gifts such as sacrificial fees; so it appears that the seers not only looked on him with contempt but regarded him as one unworthy of honour and a base man. In some places Paṇi appears as a single separate person, but since the plural use of this word is especially frequent, it should be understood that the word पणयः (*paṇayaḥ*) denotes a class of people. According to some, these Paṇis were earlier inhabitants of this country who were engaged in trade and the like, but since they had no honesty, people said that they belonged to the company of the asuras. Since they did not perform sacrifices, had no interest in the practice of any good rite, and, by just or unjust means, considered the mere acquisition of wealth the chief thing and lived accordingly, the Āryas **NOTE** regarded them as dasyus and men of base livelihood, and gave out that opinion in the mantras and elsewhere. There are many Ṛks in the Ṛgveda concerning the Paṇis.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वे॑ अ॒स्या व्युषि॒ माहि॑नायाः॒ सं यद्गोभि॒रंगि॑रसो॒ नवं॑त।  
> उत्स॑ आसां पर॒मे स॒धस्थ॑ ऋ॒तस्य॑ प॒था स॒रमा॑ विद॒द्गाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वे । अस्याः । विउषि । माहिनायाः । सं । यत् । गोभिः । अंगिरसः । नवंत ॥  
> उत्सः । आसां । परमे । सधस्थे । ऋतस्य । पथा । सरमा । विदत् । गाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वे सर्वॆंगिरसो माहिनाया मंहनीयाया अस्या उषसो व्युषि
> व्युच्छने सति गवामावरकेंधकारेपवृते सति यद्यदा गोभिः सं नवंत संजग्निरे
> तदासां गवामुत्सः क्षीराद्युत्सा वः परम उत्कृष्टे सधस्थे सहस्थाने यज्ञ उपयुक्तोऽभवदित्यर्थः । ऋतस्य सत्यस्य पथा मार्गेण सरमा वाक् देवशुनी ना गा
> निगूढा विदत् । अलभत । यद्वा । आसां गवां परमे सधस्थे सहस्थाने व्रजस्य निगूहनप्रदेश उत्स उदकस्य प्रस्रवणो वर्तते । बिलमित्यर्थः । तेन ऋतस्कोदकस्य पथा
> मार्गेण सरमा गा विदत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

All the Aṅgirases, when at the dawn of this Uṣas, the worshipful one, the darkness that covered the cows having been uncovered, they came together with the cows, then the spring of these cows, that is, milk and the like, became useful at the sacrifice, in the highest common abode; this is the sense. By the path of truth, Saramā, that is, speech, the divine bitch, found the hidden cows. Or else: in the highest common abode of these cows, the place where the cow-pen was hidden, there is a spring, a flow of water, that is, a cave; by the path of that water Saramā found the cows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—the Aṅgirases
- माहिनायाः (*māhināyāḥ*)—the venerable
- अस्माःउषस्सिन (*asmāḥuṣassina*)—of this Uṣas
- व्युषि (*vyuṣi*)—at the time of her appearing
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with the cows
- सं नवंत (*saṃ navaṃta*)—they joined (then)
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—of these cows
- उत्सः (*utsaḥ*)—the stream of milk
- परमे (*parame*)—in the excellent
- सदस्ये (*sadasye*)—place of sacrifice (it was offered) **NOTE**
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of truth
- पथा (*pathā*)—on the path
- सरमा (*saramā*)—the divine bitch
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows (that were hidden)
- विदत् (*vidat*)—found

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When all the Aṅgirases, at the time of the appearing of the venerable Uṣas, joined with the cows, then the stream of milk of these cows was offered in the excellent place of sacrifice. On the path of truth the divine bitch found the cows that had been hidden.

##### English translation
When all the Angirasas, on the opening of this adorable dawn, came in contact with the (discovered) cattle, then milk and the rest were offered in the august assembly, for Sarama had found cows by the path of truth.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यः सर्वस्य प्रेरको देवः सप्ताश्वः सर्पणस्वभावाश्वोपेतः सप्तसंख्याकाश्वो ना आ यातु। अस्मदभिमुखमागच्छतु । यद्यस्मादस्य सूर्यस्य दीर्घयाथे
> दीर्घगमने क्षेत्रं गंतव्यप्रदेश उर्वियोरु अतिप्रभूतायामः । स एव देवो
> रघुर्लघुगमनः सन् श्येनः शंसनीयगमनोऽंधो दीयमानं हविरच्छाभिलक्ष्य
> पतयत् । आगच्छति । युवा सर्वत्र मिश्रयिता कविः क्रांतदर्शि सन् गोषु रश्मिषु
> गच्छन्मध्यॆ वर्तयन् दीदयत् । दीप्यते । यद्वा । श्येनः सुपर्णोऽंधोऽच्छ
> पतयत् । द्युलोकस्थं सोमलक्षणं देवानामन्नमस्मद्यागार्थमानेतुं तदभिमुखमगात् । युवेत्यादि शिष्टं समानं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sūrya, the god who impels all, with seven horses of a creeping nature, that is, with seven horses, let him come toward us. Because the field of this Sūrya to be traversed, in his long journey, is very wide, that same god, swift in going, praiseworthy in going like a hawk, directing himself to the oblation that is being given, comes. Ever young, mixing with all, and far-seeing, moving among the cows, that is, the rays, he shines. Or else: the hawk is the bird Suparṇa, who flew toward the soma in heaven, the food of the gods, in order to bring it for our sacrifice. The rest, beginning with the youth, is the same.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- अस्य (*asya*)—of the sun
- दीर्घयाथे (*dīrghayāthe*)—to be travelled over a great distance
- क्षेत्रं (*kṣetraṃ*)—the region to be traversed
- उर्विया (*urviyā*)—because it has a path that has grown very wide
- सूर‍्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- सप्ताश्वः (*saptāśvaḥ*)—together with the seven horses
- आ यातु (*ā yātu*)—let him come
- श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*)—like a hawk
- रघुः (*raghuḥ*)—the sun, swift in going
- अंधः अच्छ (*aṃdhaḥ accha*)—facing the oblation
- पतयत् (*patayat*)—descends and comes
- युवा (*yuvā*)—ever young
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—far-seeing, the sun
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—among the rays
- गच्छन् (*gacchan*)—moving
- दीदयत् (*dīdayat*)—shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For which reason the region to be traversed by the sun, over a great distance, has a path that has grown very wide, therefore let the sun come together with his seven horses. The sun, swift in going like a hawk, descends facing the oblation. The sun, ever young and far-seeing, moving among the rays, shines.

##### English translation
May Surya, lord of seven steeds, arrive, for he has a distant goal (to reach) by a tedious route : fleet as a hawk he pounces upon the offered (sacrificial) food : ever young and far-seeing, he shines, moving amidst rays of light.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सप्ताश्व (*saptāśva*)—The horses of the sun are seven. They are called हरितः (*haritaḥ*) (Ni. 2.2.8). We have already explained the matter of the sun's horses earlier.

> अभवन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The god Sūrya mounted the bright, shining water, that is, he appears on all sides. When he yoked to his chariot the bay horses with their lovely backs, then the wise, the intelligent sacrificers and the rest, led that Sūrya by the water, as if one were leading a boat. Then the waters, giving their assent on every side, stood facing downward, that is, they became so.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वीतपृष्ठाः (*vītapṛṣṭhāḥ*)—having backs full of radiance
- हरितः (*haritaḥ*)—his horses
- अयुक्त (*ayukta*)—he yoked to the chariot (then)
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—shining
- अर्णः (*arṇaḥ*)—in the place of water
- आ रुहत् (*ā ruhat*)—appears
- धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—the wise sacrificers
- उद्ना (*udnā*)—by water
- नावं न (*nāvaṃ na*)—as one draws a boat
- अनयंत (*anayaṃta*)—they have drawn him toward them
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- आशृण्वतीः (*āśṛṇvatīḥ*)—obeying his command
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—with their current flowing downward

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as he yoked to his chariot his horses with their backs full of radiance, the sun appears in the shining place of water. The wise sacrificers have drawn him toward them, as one draws a boat by water. The waters, obeying his command, became waters with their currents flowing downward.

##### English translation
Surya has ascended above the glistening water, as soon as he has put to his bright-backed steeds: sage (worshippers) have drawn him, like a ship, across the sea : the waters, hearing his commands, have come down.

the offering;

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, I offer to you, for the sake of water, the giver of all, that hymn by which the Aṅgirases called Navagva performed the sacrifice for ten months. By the offering of this same hymn, may we become people brought under the protection of the gods. With its help may we cross over all sin.

##### English translation
I offer to you, (gods), for the sake of water, an all-bestowing sacrifice, whereby the nine-months ministrants have completed the ten- months rite: may we, by this sacrifice, be the protected of the gods: may we, by this sacrifice, cross over the boundaries of sin.

## Sūkta 46 (Maṇḍala 5)

The forty-sixth hymn.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हयो नेत्यष्टर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं प्रतिक्षत्रस्यार्षं । अष्टमी द्वितीया च
> त्रिष्टुभौ शिष्टाः षट् जगत्यः । आदितः षड्वैश्वदेव्यः सप्तम्यष्टमोर्देवपत्न्यो
> देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । हयोऽष्टौ प्रतिक्षत्रोऽंत्यो द्वचो देवपत्नीस्तवोऽंत्या त्रिष्टुप् द्वितीया चेति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning हयो नेत्यष्टर्चं (*hayo netyaṣṭarcaṃ*) is the second sūkta, of eight Ṛks, and its seer is Pratikṣatra. The eighth and the second are Triṣṭubh; the remaining six are Jagatī. From the beginning, six are addressed to the Viśvedevas; the seventh and eighth have the wives of the gods as deity. So the Anukramaṇī has it: हयोऽष्टौ प्रतिक्षत्रोऽंत्यो द्वचो देवपत्नीस्तवोऽंत्या त्रिष्टुप् द्वितीया चेति ॥ (*hayo 'ṣṭau pratikṣatro 'ṃtyo dvaco devapatnīstavo 'ṃtyā triṣṭup dvitīyā ceti ‖*). The use of the sūkta is लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*).

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning हयो न (*hayo na*) is the second sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the one called Pratikṣatra Ātreya; the first six Ṛks of this sūkta are addressed to the Viśvedevas; the deity of the seventh and eighth Ṛks is the wives of the gods; the second and eighth Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining six Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre; in the Anukramaṇī it is said: हयोऽष्टौ प्रतिक्षत्रोऽन्नो द्वृचो देवपत्निस्तवोऽ न्ता त्रिष्टुप् द्वितीया च (*hayo 'ṣṭau pratikṣatro 'nno dvṛco devapatnistavo ' ntā triṣṭup dvitīyā ca*). The use of the sūkta is Laiṅgika.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हयो॒ न वि॒द्वा अ॑युजि स्व॒यं धु॒रि तां व॑हामि प्र॒तर॑णीमव॒स्युवं॑ ।  
> नास्या॑ वश्मि वि॒मुचं॒ नावृतं॒ पुन॑र्वि॒द्वान्प॒थः पु॑रए॒त ऋ॒जु  ॑
> नेषति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हयः । न।विद्वान् । अयुजि । स्वयं । धुरि । तां । वहामि । प्रतरणीं । अवस्युवं।  
> न । अस्याः । वश्मि । विमुचं । न । असृतं । पुनः । विद्वान् । पथः । पुरः एता' ऋजु।  
> नेषति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हयो न अश्व इव विद्वान् सर्वज्ञः प्रतिक्षत्रः स्वयमनन्यप्रेरितः सन् धुरि
> यज्ञात्मिकायामयुजि । युक्तोऽभवत् । तां धुरं प्रतरणीं प्रकर्णेण तारयित्रिमवस्युवं रक्षयित्रीं वहामि : धारयाम्यहमध्वर्युर्होता ना । अस्या
> धुरो विमुचं विमोचनं परित्यागं न वश्मि । न कामाये । नावृतं पुनः पुनरावरणं धारणमपि न च वश्मि । मम को भार इति तदेवोच्यते । पिद्वान्मार्गाभिज्योऽंतर्यामी देवः पुरएता पुरतो गंता सन् पथो यज्ञमार्गानृज्जकुटिलं नेषति । प्रापयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Like a horse, the all-knowing Pratikṣatra, himself impelled by no other, was yoked to the yoke-pole that is the sacrifice. That yoke-pole, which carries across and protects, I bear, I, the Adhvaryu or the Hotā. I do not desire the release of this yoke-pole, its abandonment, nor do I desire taking it up and bearing it again and again. What burden is it to me? The same is then said: the knowing god, the inner controller, who knows the way, going before as leader, leads the paths of the sacrifice straight, not crooked.

- न वश्मि (*na vaśmi*)—I do not desire

- न (*na*)—I do not desire

- पुरएता (*puraetā*)—being the leader
- ऋजु (*ṛju*)—straight
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—to the paths of the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wise Pratikṣatra, like a horse yoked to a chariot, has of his own accord been appointed to the work of conducting the sacrifice. That burden, which can be carried out excellently and which protects, I bear. Evading this work, I do not desire to abandon this burden. The wise seer, being a guide, shows the straight paths of the sacrifice and leads others along that path.

##### English translation
The sage, (Pratikshatra), has, of his own accord, attached himself, to the burden (of sacrifice), like a horse (to a chariot): I support that transcendent and preservative load: I do not desire release from it, nor yet its reiterated imposition: the sage, going first, conducts (men) by the right path.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, gods, you bring us strength (शर्धो (*śardho*), which is might); the verb means "bestow". Further, O host of the Maruts, that is, the powers of the Maruts, and O Viṣṇu, you also bring strength. And both the Nāsatyas, who are true beings, Rudra, then the wives of these gods, Pūṣan, Bhaga and Sarasvatī: may they enjoy our sacrifice or our praise, that is, accept it.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who are gods in your nature, provide us with strength. And, O host of the Maruts, O Viṣṇu, you also provide it. May the Aśvin gods, Rudra, the wives of the gods, the god Pūṣan, Bhaga and Sarasvatī enjoy our sacrifice.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च नोऽस्माकं विष्णुर्व्यापको देवो मयस्करत् । मय इति
> सुखनाम ! सुखं करोतु । उतापि च वातो वायुरस्त्रिधोऽहिंसकः सन् मयस्करत् । किंच द्रविणोदा धनस्य दाता सोमोऽपि मयस्करत् । उतापि च ऋभवो
> नोऽस्मभ्यं राये धनायानु मंसते । अनुमन्यंतां । उताश्विनाश्विन् च उत
> त्वष्टा देव उत विभ्वा ऋभूणामन्यतमो देवः । एते सर्वेऽप्यनु मंसते । यद्वा!
> अनुमंस्त इति प्रत्येकं संबंधनीयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And may Viṣṇu, the pervading god, make happiness for us. The word मय (*maya*) is a name for happiness: let him create happiness. And may Vāta, the wind, being non-injuring, create happiness. Further, Draviṇodā, the giver of wealth, Soma also creates happiness. And the Ṛbhus approve for us, for wealth: let them consent. Likewise the two Aśvins, the god Tvaṣṭṛ, and Vibhvan, who is one of the Ṛbhus: all these approve. Or else, "approves" is to be connected with each of them separately. **NOTE**

- द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*)—Agni, in the form of the giver of wealth
- उत (*uta*)—and
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- मयः (*mayaḥ*)—happiness

- राये (*rāye*)—for the sake of wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Viṣṇu, the non-injuring wind, Agni in the form of the giver of wealth, and Soma produce happiness for us. May the Ṛbhus and the Aśvin gods, Tvaṣṭṛ and Vibhvan favour us (approve) for the sake of wealth.

##### English translation
Or may Vishnu grant us felicity, or the innocuous wind, or Soma the bestower of riches; or may the Ribhus, the Aswins, Twashtri, or Vibhwan bɔ favaurably disposed to our enrichment.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विभ्वा (*vibhvā*)—Vibhvan is the second of the three Ṛbhus, Ṛbhu, Vibhva and Vāja. **NOTE** In this Ṛk the three are referred to by the word ऋभवः (*ṛbhavaḥ*), yet the name Vibhvan is read once again.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And may that well-known host of the Maruts, the strength and company of the Maruts, come to us. What is it like? Dwelling in the heavenly world, and worthy of worship. Why does it come? That is said: to sit upon the sacred grass; that is, to sit down and accept the oblation. Further, may the god Bṛhaspati give happiness; and to us Pūṣan also is to give. What kind of happiness? Fit for a house: that which wards off cold wind and the like is a वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*), a house; what is worthy of it is वरूथ्यं (*varūthyaṃ*). Further, the three beginning with Varuṇa, each separately, are to give happiness.

- यमत् (*yamat*)—may they give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the well-known host of the Maruts, dwelling in the heavenly world and worthy of worship, come to us to sit upon the sacred grass seat. May Bṛhaspati, the god Pūṣan, Varuṇa and Aryaman give us happiness pertaining to a house.

##### English translation
Or may the adorable, heaven-abiding company of the Maruts, come to us to take their seats on the sacred grass; or may Brihaspati, Pushan, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, bestow upon us domestic happiness.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the well-known clouds, and the highly praiseworthy, generous-minded rivers, be engaged in our protection. May Bhaga, who has the power of distributing wealth, come with food and with other protection. May Aditi, of wide pervasion, hear my call.

> नोऽस्मभ्यं शर्म यच्छत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings made to the wives of the gods, the two verses beginning with देवानां पत्नीः (*devānāṃ patnīḥ*) are the yājyā and the anuvākyā. It is laid down by a sūtra that the two verses beginning "Devānāṃ patnīr uśatīr avantu naḥ" are used (Ā. 1. 10.). These two are also used in the Agnimāruta śastra, where the sūtra names the two "Devānāṃ patnīr uśatīr avantu naḥ" and the two "Rākām aham" (Ā. 5. 20.). Sāyaṇa explains: the wives of the gods, Indra and the others, desiring our praise and rite, protect us. Likewise, may they protect us for the sake of our strong son, for the winning of food, or for battle; protect thoroughly, or else may they go. Those who belong to the earth, and those who abide in the rite of the waters in the atmosphere, those goddesses, well invoked, give us happiness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods, Indra and the rest
- पत्निः (*patniḥ*)—the wives
- उशतीः (*uśatīḥ*)—desiring our praises
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*)—may they protect
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- तुजये (*tujaye*)—for the gaining of a strong son also
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the gaining of food also
- प्रावंतु (*prāvaṃtu*)—may they protect us completely
- याः (*yāḥ*)—those who
- पार्थिवासः (*pārthivāsaḥ*)—those of you who dwell on the earth, and
- याः (*yāḥ*)—those who
- अपांव्रते (*apāṃvrate*)—those of you who dwell in the atmosphere, protector of the waters
- ताः अपि (*tāḥ api*)—such as these too
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—O wives of the gods
- सुहवाः (*suhavāḥ*)—being exceedingly entreated by us
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यच्छत (*yacchata*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the wives of Indra and the other gods, desiring our praises, protect us. May they protect us completely for the gaining of a strong son and for the gaining of food. O wives of the gods, both those who dwell on the earth and those who dwell in the atmosphere, protector of the waters, being exceedingly entreated by us, give us happiness.

##### English translation
May the wives of the gods, desiring (our homage), defend us: may they so protect us that (we may obtain) vigorous (offspring) and abundant food : whether terrestrial, or those in charge of the waters (in the firmament), do you, goddesses, earnestly invoked, bestow upon us felicity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Patnīsaṃyāja homas, the homas made with the wives of the gods in view, this Ṛk देवानांपत्नीः (*devānāṃpatnīḥ*) and the following Ṛk उत ग्ना व्यंतु (*uta gnā vyaṃtu*) are to be recited respectively as the yājyā and the anuvākyā mantras; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, देवानां पत्नीरुशतीरवंतु न इति द्वे (*devānāṃ patnīruśatīravaṃtu na iti dve*) (Ā. 1-10). And these two Ṛks are also applied in the Agnimāruta śastra mantras, as set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, देवानां पत्नीरुशती रवंतुन इति द्वे राकामहमिति द्वे (*devānāṃ patnīruśatī ravaṃtuna iti dve rākāmahamiti dve*) (Ā. 5-20).

### Printed p. 522

देवानां पत्नीः (*devānāṃ patnīḥ*)—here पत्न्यः (*patnyaḥ*) ought to have stood, but through the interchange of case-endings पत्नीः (*patnīḥ*) stands. Such interchange of case-endings and numbers is called Chāndasa; that is, the commentators say that in the Chandas (the Ṛks) they are used optionally. Yāska gave, for the word देवपत्न्यः (*devapatnyaḥ*), the explanation देवपत्नो देवानां पत्न्यः (*devapatno devānāṃ patnyaḥ*), "the wives of the gods" (Ni. 12-44); and to explain the meaning of this word he took this very Ṛk as an example and gave an explanation of this Ṛk —
देवानां पत्न्य उशत्योऽवंतु नः प्रावंतु नस्तुजयेऽपत्यजननाय चान्नसंसननाय च याः पार्थिवासो या अपामपि कर्मणि व्रते ता नो देव्यः सुहवाः शर्म यच्छंतु शरणं ॥ (*devānāṃ patnya uśatyo 'vaṃtu naḥ prāvaṃtu nastujaye 'patyajananāya cānnasaṃsananāya ca yāḥ pārthivāso yā apāmapi karmaṇi vrate tā no devyaḥ suhavāḥ śarma yacchaṃtu śaraṇaṃ ‖*)
(Ni. 22-45) **NOTE**
May the wives of the gods protect us of their own wish, and show love and friendship towards us. May they grant that we obtain progeny of sons and food and the like. May the wives of the gods who are on the earth, and those who are in the atmosphere, the realm of the waters, where work (creation) is prominent, accept our auspicious invocation and provide us with a home and protection. **NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च ग्नाः स्त्रियो देवपत्नीर्देवपत्न्यो देवाः पतयो यासां ताः ।
> शादृश्यो व्यंतु । हविर्भक्षयंतु । ता विविच्योच्यंते । इंद्राणींद्रस्य पत्नग्नाय्यग्नेः पत्नश्विन्यश्विनोः पत्नि राट् राजमाना । किंच रोदसी । रुद्रस्य पत्नीति

### Printed p. 523

> यास्केनोक्तं । एवं सति विषितस्तुका रोदसी । ऋग्वे. १. १६७. ५. । इत्यत्र यथाद्युदात्तप्रगृह्यते न स्तस्तद्वदत्रापि भाव्यं । तथापि शाकल्येन महर्षिणैवमुक्तत्वात्तथैव द्रष्टव्यं । वरुणानी वरुणस्य पत्न्या सर्वतः प्रत्येकं शृणोतु । किंच देवीः
> पत्नीसंयाजदेव्यो व्यंतु । खादंतु हविः । यो जनीनां देवजायानामृतुः
> कालस्तदभिमानी देवोऽपि शृणोतु वेतु च । अत्रापि च ग्ना व्यंतु देवपत्न्यः । नि.
> १२. ४६. । इत्यादि निरुक्तं द्रष्टव्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And the ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*), the women, the wives of the gods, those whose husbands are gods: such women may enjoy, may eat the oblation. They are now distinguished: Indrāṇī the wife of Indra, Agnāyī the wife of Agni, Aśvinī the wife of the Aśvins, Rāṭ the shining one. Further, Rodasī: that she is the wife of Rudra was said by Yāska. And Varuṇānī, the wife of Varuṇa, may hear from all sides, each separately. Further, the goddesses of the Patnīsaṃyāja may enjoy, may eat the oblation. The god who presides over the Ṛtu, the season, of the wives of the gods, may also hear and enjoy. Here too the Nirukta is to be seen, beginning "gnā vyantu devapatnyaḥ" (Ni. 12. 46.). Sāyaṇa cites Ṛgve. 1. 167. 5. in connection with the accent of Rodasī, and says that, since Śākalya the great seer has said it so, it is to be understood so. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- देवपत्निः (*devapatniḥ*)—those who have the gods as their husbands
- ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*)—the goddesses
- व्यंतु (*vyaṃtu*)—may they eat the oblation
- इंद्राणी (*iṃdrāṇī*)—the wife of Indra
- अग्नायी (*agnāyī*)—the wife of Agni
- अश्विनी (*aśvinī*)—the wife of the Aśvin gods
- राट् (*rāṭ*)—the radiant one
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—the wife of Rudra
- वरुणानि (*varuṇāni*)—the wife of Varuṇa
- आ (*ā*)—gathering around
- शृणोतु (*śṛṇotu*)—may she hear our prayer
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—those goddesses
- व्यंतु (*vyaṃtu*)—may they accept the oblation (drink)
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- जनीनां (*janīnāṃ*)—of the wives of the gods
- ऋतुः (*ṛtuḥ*)—the god who regulates time (may he also hear our praise and accept the oblation)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the goddesses, the wives of the gods, eat our oblation. May the wife of Indra, the wife of Agni, the wife of the Aśvin gods, the radiant wife of Rudra, and the wife of Varuṇa gather together and hear our prayer. May those goddesses accept our oblation. May the god who regulates time for the wives of the gods also hear our praise and accept the oblation. **NOTE**

##### English translation
Or may the goddessse, the wives of the gods, accept (the offering) : Indrani, Agnayi, the radiant Aswini, Rodasi, Varunani, may each hear (our prayer) : may the goddesses partake (of the oblation) : may'the (personified) season of the wives of the gods, accept it.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given an explanation for this Ṛk as well, and has also named some of the wives of the gods here. As to the names: the wives of the gods have no separate names; that is, in the Ṛgveda the wives of Indra and the others do not have names such as शची (*śacī*) and the like, as stated in the Purāṇas and elsewhere. Only the words that mark them as the wife of the respective god are applied to the wives of the respective gods. For instance, the wife of Indra is called इंद्राणी (*iṃdrāṇī*)

### Printed p. 524

and the wife of Agni अग्नायी (*agnāyī*), the wife of Varuṇa वरुणानी (*varuṇānī*), and so on. Yāska has explained this in his Nirukta —
अपि च ग्ना व्यंतु देवपत्न्यः । इंद्राणींद्रस्य पत्न्यग्नाय्यग्नेः पत्न्यश्विन्य श्विनोः पत्नि राट् राजते । रोदसीः रुद्रस्य पत्नि । वरुणानी च वरुणस्य पत्नि । व्यंतु देव्यः कामयंतां य ऋतुः कालो जायानां (*api ca gnā vyaṃtu devapatnyaḥ | iṃdrāṇīṃdrasya patnyagnāyyagneḥ patnyaśvinya śvinoḥ patni rāṭ rājate | rodasīḥ rudrasya patni | varuṇānī ca varuṇasya patni | vyaṃtu devyaḥ kāmayaṃtāṃ ya ṛtuḥ kālo jāyānāṃ*)
(Ni. 12.46)
And may the goddesses, the wives of the gods, receive and drink the oblation in the form of ghee. Who they are: the wife of Indra is named इंद्राणी (*iṃdrāṇī*), the wife of Agni is named अग्नाया (*agnāyā*). The wife of the Aśvin gods is named अश्विनी (*aśvinī*). राट् (*rāṭ*) means the shining goddess. The wife of Rudra is named रोदसी (*rodasī*) (nominative singular). The wife of Varuṇa is named वरुणानी (*varuṇānī*). ऋतुः (*ṛtuḥ*) means time; ऋतुर्जनीनां (*ṛturjanīnāṃ*) means the time at which these wives of the gods receive the oblation. Therefore the chief purport of the explanation is that all the wives of the gods mentioned above, at the particular time at which they are to receive the oblation, desiring their oblation, may receive it and be satisfied.

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)
इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तकश्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणामात्येन विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये चतुर्थाष्टके द्वितीयोऽध्यायः समाप्तः (*iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartakaśrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇāmātyena viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye caturthāṣṭake dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ*)

Here ends the Second Chapter in the Fourth Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and with a Karnāṭaka translation.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्धनेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोस्तु ते॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yaddhanet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namostu te‖*)
शुभं भूयात् (*śubhaṃ bhūyāt*)
मंगळं (*maṃgaḷaṃ*)

श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः (*śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ*)
वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)
यस्य निश्यसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विदातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśyasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*)
वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*)

Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with the bhāṣya of Sāyaṇa.

चतुर्थाष्टके तृतीयोऽध्यायः (*caturthāṣṭake tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ*)
The Third Chapter in the Fourth Aṣṭaka.
The forty-seventh sūkta in the fifth maṇḍala.

In this chapter the first five sūktas (that is, sūktas 47-51 of this maṇḍala) have the Viśvedevas as their deity. We have explained the subject of the Viśvedevas in detail in the previous chapter, that is, on pages 336-352 of this part. For sūktas 52 to 61 (ten sūktas in all) the Maruts are the deity. For the last sūkta of this chapter, sūkta 62, Mitra and Varuṇa are the deity. Since not much is known about the seers who appear in this chapter, Pratiratha, Pratibhānu, Pratiprabha, Svasti, Śyāvāśva and Śrutavit, there is no room for an account of them. But about the seer Śyāvāśva we have already explained some matters before.

## Sūkta 47 (Maṇḍala 5)

The forty-seventh sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ तृतीयोऽध्याय आरभ्यते । तत्र प्रयुंजतीति सप्तर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं
> प्रतिरथस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं । पूर्वत्र वैश्वदेवं वै तदित्युक्तत्वादिदमपि वैश्वदेवं ।
> प्रयुंजती सप्त प्रतिरथ इत्यनुक्रमणिका विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now the third chapter begins. In it the third sūkta, beginning प्रयुंजती (*prayuṃjatī*), of seven Ṛks, has Pratiratha as its seer and Triṣṭubh as its metre. Since it was said in the preceding sūkta वैश्वदेवं वै तदित्युक्तत्वादिदमपि (*vaiśvadevaṃ vai tadityuktatvādidamapi*), this one too is addressed to the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇī says प्रयुंजती सप्त प्रतिरथ (*prayuṃjatī sapta pratiratha*). The use in ritual is लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*).

Anuvāda: Since the Second Chapter in the Fourth Aṣṭaka has now ended, the explanation of the meaning and translation of the Third Chapter will begin henceforth. The first sūkta of this chapter, the sūkta called प्रयुंजती (*prayuṃjatī*), is the third sūkta in the fourth anuvāka of the fifth maṇḍala. It has seven Ṛks. Its seer is Pratiratha Ātreya; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said प्रयुंजती सप्त प्रतिरथः (*prayuṃjatī sapta pratirathaḥ*); the use in ritual is Laiṅgika.

- Deity: the Viśvedevas

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र॒युं॒ज॒ती दि॒न ए॑ति ब्रुवा॒णा म॒ही मा॒ता दु॑हि॒तुर्बो॒धयं॑ती ।  
> अ॒विवा॑संती युव॒तिर्म॑नी॒षा पि॒तृभ्य॒ आ सद॑ने॒ जोहु॑वाना ॥

> आविवासंती । युवतिः । मनीषा । पितृभ्यः । आ । सदने । जोहुवाना ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषोषस्या । प्रयुंजती प्राणिनः प्रस्तुतेषु कर्मसु दिवो द्युलोकादेति ।
> आगच्छति ब्रुवाणा स्तूयमाना ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ मही महती माता
> प्रकाशस्य देवानां वा निर्माश्री दुहितुर्भूम्या बोधयंती बोधं कुर्वाणा ।
> तदुपजीव्यत्वात् दुहितृत्वमुपचर्यते । यद्वा दुहितुर्दिव इति संबंधः ॥ उषसो
> दिवो दुहितृत्वं व्युच्चा दुहितर्दिवः । ऋग्वे. १-४८-१ । इत्यादिषु प्रसिद्धं । अन्यत
> च दिवो दुहिता भुवनस्य पत्नि ! ऋग्वे. ७-३५-४ । इत्युषसो द्युदुहितृत्वमान्नातं
> अत इदमधिगम्यते । कदाचिद्भौरुषसो जायत उषाश्च दिन इति । प्रजापतिर्वै

> सर्वत्र नित्यतरुणी ना मनीषा स्तुतिमती पितृभ्यः ॥ तृतीयार्थे पंचमी ॥ पितृभिः
> पालकैर्देनैः सह सदने यागगृह आ सर्वतो जोहुवानाहूयमाना । यद्वा
> पितृभ्यः कर्मणां पालकेभ्यो जनमानेभ्य इष्टप्रापणेन पालकेभ्यो ना तेषामर्थाय जोहुवाना ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

प्रयुंजती (*prayuṃjatī*): she who impels living beings to the rites in hand comes from heaven, from the heavenly world; ब्रुवाणा (*bruvāṇā*) means "being praised", the active ending being used in the sense of the passive. मही (*mahī*) is the great one, the mother, the maker, of light or of the gods; she awakens her daughter, the earth, making her know. Because the earth lives on her, daughterhood is figuratively ascribed to the earth. Or else connect दुहितुर्दिव (*duhiturdiva*) together, "of the daughter, of heaven". That Uṣas is the daughter of heaven is well known from passages such as "Dawn, O daughter of heaven, shine forth" (Ṛgve. 1-48-1), and elsewhere "the daughter of heaven, the consort of the world" (Ṛgve. 7-35-4), where Uṣas is declared to be heaven's daughter. From this it is understood that sometimes heaven is born of Uṣas and Uṣas of heaven. For it is heard: "Prajāpati desired his own daughter, some say heaven, others say Uṣas" (Ai. Brā. 3-33). A reversal of cause and effect is also seen: "From Aditi Dakṣa was born, from Dakṣa Aditi" (Ṛgve. 10-22-4). Further, आविवासंती (*āvivāsaṃtī*) means serving; युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*) is she who is ever young everywhere; मनीषा (*manīṣā*) is she who is praised. पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*) stands, in the sense of the instrumental, for "with the protecting gods": in the sacrificial house, invoked from all sides together with them. Or else पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*) means: for the sake of the protectors of the rites, who protect by granting what is desired, she is invoked. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मही (*mahī*)—she who is of great nature
- माता (*mātā*)—Uṣas, who is the mother of the world
- दुहितुः (*duhituḥ*)—to her daughter, the earth
- बोधयंती (*bodhayaṃtī*)—giving wakefulness
- प्रयुंजती (*prayuṃjatī*)—and appointing all living beings to their several works
- ब्रुवाणा (*bruvāṇā*)—being praised
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the heavenly world
- एति (*eti*)—she comes
- युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*)—ever young
- मनीषा (*manīṣā*)—and full of praise, Uṣas
- आविवासंती (*āvivāsaṃtī*)—serving (the world)
- पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*)—together with all the protecting gods
- सदने (*sadane*)—in the sacrificial house
- आ (*ā*)—everywhere
- जोहुवाना (*johuvānā*)—being entreated (she comes)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Uṣas, who is of great nature and the mother of the world, giving wakefulness to her daughter the earth, and appointing all living beings to their several works, being praised by the world, appears from the

### Printed p. 528

heavenly world. Ever young and full of praise, Uṣas serving the world comes together with all the protecting gods to the sacrificial house, entreated everywhere.

##### English translation
Arousing (men to their labours), the adorable (Dawn) comes from the heaven, a mighty mother, the awakener of her daughter (earth): pious, ever young, and glorified (she comes), when invoked, to the chamber of sacrifice with the protecting (gods).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

माता दुहितुः (*mātā duhituḥ*)—this Ṛk gives the account that the goddess Uṣas, the mother, is the mother of her daughter, the earth. But in the Ṛgveda it is said in many places that heaven and earth are, by nature, the mother and father of the other gods; accordingly —
सह वामेन न उषो व्युच्छा दुहितर्दिवः । (*saha vāmena na uṣo vyucchā duhitardivaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-48-1)
अभिपश्यंती वयुना जनानां दिवो दुहिता भवनस्य पत्नी । (*abhipaśyaṃtī vayunā janānāṃ divo duhitā bhavanasya patnī |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-25.4)
In such places the goddess Uṣas is clearly called the daughter of heaven and earth. Is it not then a mutual contradiction that in the present Ṛk the earth is called the daughter of the goddess Uṣas? To this the commentator gives the following answer: in some places, that is, in
कदा चिद्भौरुषसो जायत उषाश्च दिन इति । (*kadā cidbhauruṣaso jāyata uṣāśca dina iti |*)
and
प्रजापतिर्वै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायद्दिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्थन्ये । (*prajāpatirvai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyaddivamityanya āhuruṣasamitthanye |*)
(Ai. Brā. 3-3-3)
अदितेर्दक्षो अजायत दक्षाद्वदितिः परि । (*aditerdakṣo ajāyata dakṣādvaditiḥ pari |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.72.4)
such a contradictory view is found; that is, in some places it is said that द्यौः (*dyauḥ*), the heavenly world, was born of the goddess Uṣas, and in other places that the goddess Uṣas arose from the goddess of heaven. And in the passage of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa cited above, after speaking of the daughter of Prajāpati, it is shown that there is a difference of view: some say that the daughter is the deity of heaven, some that she is the goddess Uṣas. Besides, in the third example given above, that from Aditi Dakṣa was born and from Dakṣa the birth of Aditi, a mutually contradictory view is indicated in a single sentence. How is this reasonable? Here, that is, in these places, these views or meanings should not be taken to be contradictory. In them a definite meaning alone is stated, and to confirm that meaning there is लिंगव्यत्यय (*liṃgavyatyaya*), a reversal of the indication, but no mutually contradictory meaning is suggested here; so the answer has been given.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒जि॒रास॒स्तद॑प॒ ईय॑माना आतस्थि॒वांसो॑ अ॒मृत॑स्य॒ नाभिं॑ ।  
> आ॒नं॒तास॑ उ॒रवो॑ वि॒श्वतः॑ सीं॒ परि॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी यं॑ति॒  ॑

> अनंतासः । उरवः । विश्वतः । सीं । परि । द्यावापृथिवी इति । यंति । पंथाः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अजिरासो गमनशीलाः ॥ अजिरिरच् प्रत्ययांतोऽजिरशिशिरेत्यादिना निपातितः ॥
> तदपस्तदेव प्रकाशनरूपं कर्म यस्य तत्तादृशमहरीयमाना गच्छंतोऽमृतस्य
> सूर्यस्य नाभिं संनाहकं मंडलं अमृतस्योदकस्य वा नाभिमंतरिक्षमातस्थिवांस
> आतिष्ठंतोऽनंतासोऽपरिमिता उरवो व्याप्ताः पंथाः पतनशीला रश्मयो द्यावापृथिवी परि दिवं च पृथिवीं चांतरिक्षं च विश्वतः परितो यंति । गच्छंति । सीमिति
> पूरणः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अजिरासः (*ajirāsaḥ*) are those given to going. तदपः (*tadapaḥ*) are those whose work is just that, the work of making light, going about such a day; so they go, abiding at the centre (nābhi) of the immortal one, the Sun, that is, his orb which binds all together; or at the centre of the immortal water, the atmosphere. They are endless, that is, unmeasured; उरवः (*uravaḥ*) means wide, pervading; the पंथाः (*paṃthāḥ*) are the rays, given to falling. They go all around heaven and earth, that is, heaven, earth and the atmosphere, on every side. सीं (*sīṃ*) is a filler.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अजिरासः (*ajirāsaḥ*)—those given to going
- तदपः (*tadapaḥ*)—having as their one work the lighting up of the day
- ईयमानाः (*īyamānāḥ*)—moving about
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—of the Sun, who is free of the nature of death
- नाभिं (*nābhiṃ*)—the orb
- आतस्थिवांसः (*ātasthivāṃsaḥ*)—resting on
- अनंतासः (*anaṃtāsaḥ*)—unmeasured
- उरवः (*uravaḥ*)—widely pervading
- पंथाः (*paṃthāḥ*)—the rays, given to falling
- द्यावापृथिवी परि (*dyāvāpṛthivī pari*)—around heaven and earth
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—everywhere
- यंति (*yaṃti*)—they move about

### Printed p. 530

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The rays, ever given to moving, having as their one work the lighting up of the day, resting on the orb of the Sun, who is free of the nature of death, unmeasured, widely pervading and given to falling, move about everywhere around heaven and earth.

##### English translation
The rays (of light) extending round, fulfilling their duty (of bringing on the day), abiding in contact with the orb of the immortal (sun), unlimited and diffusive, spread everywhere through heaven and earth.

> मध्ये । दिवः । निहितः । पृश्निः । अश्मा । वि । चक्रमे । रजसः । पाति । अंतौ ॥ ३ ॥

> यद्वा । संमोदंते तस्मिन्देवा इति समुद्रः । अरुष आरोचमानः सुपर्णः
> सुगमनः पूर्वस्य । अवयवलक्षणेयं । पूर्वदिगवयवस्य पितुः पालकस्यांतरिक्षस्य
> योनिमुत्पादकमवयवमा विवेश । आविष्टवान् । पश्चाद्दिवो मध्यॆ निहितः पृश्नि ।
> प्राश्नुत एनं वर्ण इति पृश्निरादित्यः । अश्मा सर्वत्र व्याप्तः । लुप्तोपमा ना । अत्मसदृशो रजसोऽन्तरिक्षस्यांतौ पूर्वापरभागौ वि चक्रमे । विक्रमते । पाति च जगत् ।
> जगद्रक्षार्थं क्रमत इत्यर्थः ॥

### Printed p. 531

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This triplet is addressed to Sūrya. उक्षा (*ukṣā*) is the sprinkler of water or of desires; समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*) is the moistener, or else that in which the gods rejoice together. अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*) is the shining one; सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*) the good goer. पूर्वस्य (*pūrvasya*) is here a mark of a part: of the part belonging to the eastern quarter, of the father, the protecting atmosphere, he entered the womb, the producing part. Afterwards he is placed in the middle of heaven as पृश्निः (*pṛśniḥ*), the Āditya, since colour partakes of him. अश्मा (*aśmā*) is the all-pervading one, a simile that has been dropped, so that he is like himself. He strides to the two ends of the atmosphere, its eastern and its western parts, and protects the world; that is, he strides in order to protect the world.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उक्षा (*ukṣā*)—that which is the sprinkler of water
- समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*)—that which wets everything
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—that which is golden-coloured
- सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*)—that which has an excellent flight (the chariot of the Sun)
- पितुः (*pituḥ*)—of the protecting atmosphere
- पूर्वस्य (*pūrvasya*)—of the eastern part
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—the place
- आ विवेश (*ā viveśa*)—has entered
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- मध्यॆ (*madhyè*)—in the middle
- निहितः (*nihitaḥ*)—placed
- पृश्निः (*pṛśniḥ*)—the Āditya
- अश्मा (*aśmā*)—being all-pervading
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- अंतौ (*aṃtau*)—both the eastern and the western parts
- विचक्रमे (*vicakrame*)—he strides over and moves about
- पाति (*pāti*)—he protects (the world)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The chariot of the Sun, which sprinkles water, which wets everything with drops of water, which is golden-coloured and has an excellent flight, has entered the place in the eastern part of the protecting atmosphere. The Āditya, placed in the middle of the atmosphere, being all-pervading, strides over and moves about both the eastern and the western parts of the atmosphere, and protects the world.

##### English translation
The showerer (of rain), the shedder of dew, the radiant and quick-going (car) has entered the region of the paternal east: the many-tinted and pervading (luminary) proceeds to both extermities of the firmament, (and so) preserves (the world).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चत्वार ऋत्विज ईमेनमादित्यं क्षेमयंतः क्षेममात्मन इच्छंतो बिभ्रति ।
> धारयंति हविर्भिः स्तुतिभिश्च । किंच दश दिशो गर्भं गर्भवन्मध्य उत्पन्नमेनं चरसे
> चरणायोदयास्तमयव्यवहाराय धापयंते । गमयंति । त्रिधातवस्त्रिप्रकाराः
> शीतोष्णवर्षभेदेन त्रिविधा अस्यादित्यस्य परमा उत्कृष्टा गावो रश्मयो दिवोऽंत
> रिक्षस्यांतान् परि परितः सद्य उदयानंतरमेव चरंति । गच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The four priests bear this Āditya, desiring welfare for themselves, sustaining him with oblations and with praises. Further, the ten quarters, like a womb, send forth him who is produced in the midst of them, to move, that is, for the daily course of rising and setting. Threefold, according to the division into cold, heat and rain, are the excellent rays of this Āditya, and immediately after his rising they move round the ends of the atmosphere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चत्वारः (*catvāraḥ*)—the four priests also
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Āditya
- क्षेमयंतः (*kṣemayaṃtaḥ*)—desiring it for their own welfare
- बिभ्रति (*bibhrati*)—they bear (with oblations and the like)
- दश (*daśa*)—the ten quarters
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—Āditya, produced in the midst of them like an embryo
- चरसे (*carase*)—for his movement
- धापयंते (*dhāpayaṃte*)—send forth
- त्रिधातवः (*tridhātavaḥ*)—of three kinds
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Āditya
- परमाः (*paramāḥ*)—excellent
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—the rays
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- अंतान् (*aṃtān*)—from the border region
- परि (*pari*)—all around
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—immediately upon rising
- चरंति (*caraṃti*)—they move about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The four priests also bear this Āditya, desiring him for their own welfare, with oblations and the like. The ten quarters send forth Āditya, who is produced in the midst of them like an embryo, for his movement. The excellent rays of this Āditya, which are of three kinds, namely cold, heat and rain, move about all around from the border region of the atmosphere immediately upon his rising.

##### English translation
The four (chief priests) sustain him (with oblations and praises), seeking their own welfare : the ten (regions of space) invigorate him, their embryo, to travel (his daily course): his three elementary rays swiftly traverse the boundaries of the sky.

> यन्मंडलमधितस्थुः । मंडलाधीनत्वात्तासां । ईमेतदुक्तलक्षणं यन्मंडलं द्वे
> अहोरात्रे मातुर्निर्मातुर्मातृस्थानीयादंतरिक्षादन्ये इहेह जाते इह चेह च
> सूर्ये जाते निष्पन्ने यम्या यम्ये नियमनीये युग्मभूते ना सबंधू
> समानबले समानबंधने उभयोरप्येक एव सूर्यो बंधकोऽक्षो ययोस्तादृश्यौ बिभृतः धारयतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O people, O priests, this body seen before us, the orb, is to be praised; relying on which orb the rivers flow and the waters stand, since they depend on the orb. This orb, of the characteristics stated: the two, day and night, which are different from the mother, the maker, the atmosphere, and are born here and there, that is, are produced from the Sun, यम्या (*yamyā*), controllable, a pair, सबंधू (*sabaṃdhū*), of equal strength and equal bond, having one and the same Sun as the binding axle of both, he bears; that is, he upholds them. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जनासः (*janāsaḥ*)—O people
- यत् (*yat*)—by relying on which orb of Āditya
- नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)—the rivers
- चरंति (*caraṃti*)—flow
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- तस्तुः (*tastuḥ*)—such as rest relying on which
- निवचनं (*nivacanaṃ*)—worthy of praise
- इदं वपुः (*idaṃ vapuḥ*)—this is the orb of Āditya
- मातुः (*mātuḥ*)—from the atmosphere
- जाते (*jāte*)—those born
- यम्या (*yamyā*)—which bring about the control of the world
- सबंधू (*sabaṃdhū*)—having (Āditya himself) as the common kinsman
- द्वे (*dve*)—day and night
- अन्ये (*anye*)—and the other priests and the like
- यत् ईं (*yat īṃ*)—which bear the sun
- इहेह (*iheha*)—in all their several fixed regions
- बिभ्रतः (*bibhrataḥ*)—bear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O people, behold this praiseworthy orb of Āditya, by the support of which the rivers flow, relying on which the waters stand. From the atmosphere

### Printed p. 534

born, which regulate the world, and day and night, which have Āditya himself as their common kinsman, and the other priests and the like, bear this same sun in all their several fixed regions.

##### English translation
(Behold), men, this indescribable form from which the rivers (spring), and where the waters dwell; which (form, the firmament), the two, (day and night), associated and equally allied, as well as other (seasons), born (of it, as of a parent), here and there sustain.

> उपप्रक्षे । वृषणं । मोदमानाः । दिवः । पथा । वध्वः । यंति । अच्छ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मै सूर्याय धियः स्तुतीरपांसि कर्माणि च पि तन्वते । विस्तारयंति
> यजमानाः । पुत्राय पुत्रस्थानीयाय मातरो निर्मात्र्य उषसो दिशो वा
> वस्त्रा वस्त्राणि वयंति । निष्पादयंति । वस्त्रसदृशानि तेजांसि निविडानि संपादयंतीत्यर्थः । वृषणः सेक्तुः सूर्यस्योपप्रक्ष उपपर्चने संपर्के सति मोदमाना
> हृष्यंतो वध्वो वधूस्थानीया रश्मयो दिवस्पथा सूर्यसंबंधिना मार्गेणाच्छास्मदभिमुखं यंति । गच्छंति । प्रसरंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The worshippers extend praises and rites for this Sūrya. For the son-like Sūrya the mothers, that is the Uṣases who bring forth, or the directions, weave garments; that is, they produce dense lights like garments. When the showering Sūrya is in contact with them, the wives, that is the rays that stand in the place of brides, rejoicing, come and spread toward us by the path of the sky, the path belonging to Sūrya.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The worshippers extend sacrificial rites and praises with reference to this Sūrya. The directions, which are like mothers, weave garments of the form of light for their son Sūrya. When there is contact with Sūrya, the giver of rain, the rays, which rejoice and have the form of wives, spread and come toward us by the path belonging to Sūrya.

##### English translation
To him (worshippers) multiply praises and acts of adoration: for (him as for) a son, the (divine) mothers weave garments (of light): rejoicing in the contact of their impregnation, the wives of the sun, (the solar rays), come to our presence by the path of the sky.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In this Ṛk the deities are determined by indication. O Mitra and Varuṇa, may this sūkta, this praise, be praised, that is, be so. O Agni, may that same praise be so. For our happiness and for the non-mixture of sorrows may this praise be. And may we obtain a firm footing,

and also the unbroken continuance of that footing. I bow to the shining Sūrya, the great one, the support of the universe.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, may this praise recited by us be worthy of your praise. O Agni, may that same praise, praised also by you, be the means for us of happiness free from sorrow. May we obtain a state that is excellent and lasting. To Sūrya, the radiant, of great nature, the support of the whole universe, we offer our homage.

##### English translation
May this (hymn), Mitra and Varuna, be valued (by you): may it, Agni, be valued (by you) as the means to us of happiness unmixed : may we (thence) obtain stability and permanence : reverence be to you, radiant and mighty asylum (of the universe).

## Sūkta 48 (Maṇḍala 5)

The forty-eighth sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कदु प्रियायेति पंचर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं । प्रतिभानुर्नामात्रेय यषिः ।
> जगती छंदः । विश्वे देवा देवता । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । कदु पंच प्रतिभानुर्जागतमिति ॥ अभिप्लविके पंचमेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्र इदं सूक्तं निविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च ।
> कदु प्रियायेति वैश्वदेवं । आ. ७. ७. । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning कदु प्रियायेति पंचर्चं (*kadu priyāyeti paṃcarcaṃ*), of five Ṛks, is the fourth sūkta. Its seer is Pratibhānu of the Ātreya line, its metre is Jagatī, and its deity is the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇī says: कदु पंच प्रतिभानुर्जागतमिति (*kadu paṃca pratibhānurjāgatamiti*). In the Abhiplava rite, on the fifth day, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, this sūkta is the nivid-sūkta. It is also laid down in the sūtra: कदु प्रियायेति वैश्वदेवं (*kadu priyāyeti vaiśvadevaṃ*) (Ā. 7. 7).

### Printed p. 537

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning कदु प्रियाय (*kadu priyāya*) is the fourth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is the one called Pratibhānu Ātreya; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the metre is Jagatī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: कदु पंच प्रतिभानुर्जागतं (*kadu paṃca pratibhānurjāgataṃ*). It is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, कदु प्रियायेति वैश्वदेवं (*kadu priyāyeti vaiśvadevaṃ*) (Ā. 7-7), that in the sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, on the fifth day, in the middle of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, this sūkta is to be inserted and recited as the nivid sūkta.

- Sūkta 48
- Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 48
- Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 3, Varga 2
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Seer: Pratibhānu Ātreya
- Deity: the Viśvedevas
- Metre: Jagatī

### Printed p. 538

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र वैद्युताग्निसंस्तवः । कदु कदा । उ इति पूरणः । प्रियाय सर्वॆषां
> प्रियभूताय । वृष्टिद्वारा हविरादिप्रयोजकत्वात्सर्वप्रियत्वमस्य प्रसिद्धं । तादृशाय धान्ने तेजसे वैद्युताय । उत्तरवाक्येऽभ्रेऽपो वितनोतीति वक्ष्यमाणत्वादिदं लभ्यते । कीदृशाय । स्वक्षत्राय स्वभूतबलाय किंच स्वयशसे स्वभूतान्नाय।
> सर्वमप्यन्नं ह्यस्य स्वं । महे महते पूज्याय वयं कदा मनामहे । स्तवाम ।
> यत् ॥ उत्तरत्र स्त्रीलिंगनिर्देशाद्वेति विपरिणामयितव्यं॥ याग्नॆयी शक्तिरामेन्यस्य
> समंतान्मातव्यस्य रजसोऽंतरिक्षस्य । अपरिमितमपि नभ इयुदिति सर्वैर्मियते ।
> संबंधिन्यभ्रे मेघ आ अधि मेघस्योपर्यप उदकानि वृष्टिलक्षणानि वितनोति
> विस्तारयति वृणानाज्जादयंती सेव्यमाना ना मायिनी । मायेति प्रज्ञानाम ।
> प्रज्ञावती सती । यद्यस्य संबंधिनी माध्यमिकी वागिति वा योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here the praises are of the lightning-fire. कदु (*kadu*) means "when"; the particle that follows is a filler. प्रियाय (*priyāya*) means dear to all: its being dear to all is well known, because through rain it provides the oblations and so on. To such a splendour, the splendour of lightning. Since it will be said in the next sentence that it spreads waters in the cloud, this meaning is obtained. Of what kind? One having strength of its own, and one having food of its own, for all food is its own. महे (*mahe*) means great, worthy of worship. When shall we praise it? In the later part the word is feminine, so it must be changed accordingly. The fiery power spreads waters, that is, rain, above the cloud that belongs to the atmosphere, which is measured on every side; for although the sky is unbounded, it is measured by all. Covering, that is, being served; it is possessed of wisdom, the word for illusive power being a name for wisdom. Or else it may be construed as the speech of the middle region, whose it is.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रियाय (*priyāya*)—to that which is beneficial to all
- स्वक्षत्राय (*svakṣatrāya*)—having a strength that is its own
- स्वयशसे (*svayaśase*)—having food obtained by itself
- महे (*mahe*)—and worthy of worship
- धाम्ने (*dhāmne*)—with reference to the splendour of the form of lightning
- कदु (*kadu*)—when
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- मनामहे (*manāmahe*)—shall we offer praise
- मायिनी (*māyinī*)—endowed with wisdom
- यत् (*yat*)—which this light
- आमेन्यस्य (*āmenyasya*)—determined by measure
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—belonging to the atmosphere
- अभ्रे आ (*abhre ā*)—in the region above the cloud
- वृणाना (*vṛṇānā*)—covering the atmosphere
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- वितनोति (*vitanoti*)—spreads widely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When shall we offer praise to the splendour of the form of lightning, which is beneficial to all, which has a strength of its own, which has food obtained by itself, and which is worthy of worship? This light, endowed with the power of wisdom, pervading the atmosphere, which is unbounded and yet determined by measure, in the region above the cloud, spreads the waters widely.

##### English translation
When may we offer adoration to the benevolent splendour, strong in its own (strength), self-sustaining with food, deserving of worship : when the delusive (energy of Agni), investing (the heavens), spreads the waters above the clouds over the unbounded firmament.

> ता अ॑त्यत व॒युनं॑ वी॒रव॑क्षणं समा॒न्या वृ॒तया॒ विश्व॒मा रजः॑ ।  
> अपो॒ अपा॑ची॒रप॑रा॒ अपे॑जते॒ प्र पूर्वा॑भिस्तिरते देव॒युर्जनः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)
