> अपो इति । अपाचीः । अपराः । अप । ईजते।प्र।पूर्वाभिः । तिरते । देव्ययुः । जनः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयमुषस्या । ता उषसोऽत्नत । वितन्वंति । किं । वयुनं प्रज्ञानं । कीदृशं ।
> वीरवक्षणं वीरैर्ऋत्विग्निर्वहनीयं । यद्वा । वक्षणाः कार्यवोढारो येन
> प्रेर्यंते तत्तादृशं । किंच समानैकरूपया वृतयावरकया दीप्त्या विश्वमा
> सर्वमपि रजो जगदत्नत । एवं सति देवयुर्देवकामो जनोऽपाचीरपांचनाः
> प्रतिनिवृत्तमुखीरपरा अन्या आगामिनीरुषसोऽपेजते । अपचालयति । अपरोऽपशब्दः पूरणः । पूर्वाभिस्ताभिः प्रतिरते । प्रपूर्वस्तियतिर्वर्धनार्थः । वर्धयति
> स्वमनीषां वर्धते ना स्वयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is addressed to Uṣas. Those Uṣases spread out. What? Knowledge. Of what kind? That which is to be borne by heroes, that is, by priests; or else, that by which the bearers of the work are impelled. Moreover, with a radiance of one uniform kind, an enveloping one, they spread over the whole world. This being so, the man who longs for the gods turns away the other Uṣases, those yet to come, whose faces have turned back; and with the former ones he increases. Here the prefix together with the root is meant to express growth: he increases his own wisdom, he grows himself.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ताः (*tāḥ*)—those Uṣases
- वीरवक्षणं (*vīravakṣaṇaṃ*)—to be borne by wise priests and the like
- वयुनं (*vayunaṃ*)—knowledge
- अत्यत (*atyata*)—they spread **NOTE**
- समान्या (*samānyā*)—of one form
- वृतया (*vṛtayā*)—and pervading, by the radiance
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—the whole
- आ रजः (*ā rajaḥ*)—the whole world (it covers)
- देवयुः (*devayuḥ*)—longing for the gods
- जनः (*janaḥ*)—the man
- अपाचीः (*apācīḥ*)—those whose faces have turned back
- अपराः (*aparāḥ*)—and which will appear later, the Uṣases
- अपेजते (*apejate*)—he sends away
- पूर्वाभिः (*pūrvābhiḥ*)—together with the Uṣases that appeared before
- प्रतिरते (*pratirate*)—he attains growth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Uṣases spread knowledge that is to be borne by wise priests and the like. With a radiance that is of one form and pervading, it covers the whole world. The man who longs for the gods

### Printed p. 540

of the gods sends away the Uṣases that have turned their faces back and will appear later. With the Uṣases that appeared before he attains growth.

##### English translation
These dawns diffuse the consciousness that is apprchended by pious men and (overspread) the whole world with uniform, investing (light): the devout man disregards the dawns which have turned back and (those which) are to come, and improves (his understanding) by those which have proceded. **NOTE**

> स्वकीये गृह आकाशे प्रचरन् प्रचरंति । किं कुर्वंतः । संवर्तयंतः प्राणिनो

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the first half of this Ṛk Indra is spoken of; in the second half, Sūrya, who is the self of Indra. The verb "is invoked" is to be supplied. By what? By the pressing-stones, by the Soma pressings prepared by day and by night, that is, accomplished in them. Here the word for the instrument stands for what is accomplished by it: the pressings, brought about by the stones, being the occasion. Having come here, Indra, now possessed of Soma, kindles on every side his very great thunderbolt, when the occasion of Vṛtra the beguiler is present. Moreover, of him, that is of Āditya, whose self is Indra, a hundred rays move in their own house, the sky. What do they do? Making an end of living beings,

### Printed p. 541

> नाशयंतः । यद्वा । अहाहानि दिवसान् संवर्तयंतः सम्यक् प्रवर्तयंतो वि च
> वर्तयन् अहाहानि निवर्तयंति गतानैव पुनः प्रापयंति च । तपनपरिस्यंदाधीनत्वात्पाणिनामायुःक्षयस्याहोरात्रादिव्यवहारस्य ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

or else, bringing the days into order and also turning them back, they bring back the days that have gone. This is so because the decay of the life of living beings and the course of day and night and the like depend on the movement of the sun.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Indra, who is Āditya himself
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—the hundred rays
- संवर्तयंतः (*saṃvartayaṃtaḥ*)—making the days that have appeared go away
- वि च वर्तयन् (*vi ca vartayan*)—and again making those same days appear
- स्वे दमे (*sve dame*)—in the sky, their own place
- प्रचरन् (*pracaran*)—move about; such an Indra
- अहन्येभिः (*ahanyebhiḥ*)—produced in the days
- अक्तुभिः (*aktubhiḥ*)—and produced at night
- आ ग्रावभिः (*ā grāvabhiḥ*)—by the Soma juices (stimulated)
- मायिनि (*māyini*)—upon the beguiler Vṛtra, to be used
- वरिष्ठं (*variṣṭhaṃ*)—and extensive
- वज्रं (*vajraṃ*)—the thunderbolt
- आ जिघर्ति (*ā jigharti*)—makes sharp

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Such an Indra, who is Āditya himself, whose hundred rays move about in their own place, making the days that have appeared go to their setting and again making those same days appear, stimulated by the Soma juices produced at both times, day and night, makes sharp the extensive thunderbolt that is to be used against Vṛtra the beguiler.

##### English translation
(Animated) by the libations offered by day and by night, (Indra) sharpens his vast thunderbolt against the beguiler (Vritra); he whose hundred (rays) attend him in his own abode, sending away, and bringing back (revolving) days.

> सचा । यदि । पितुमंतंइव । क्षयं । रत्नं । दधाति । भरहूतये । विशे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयमाग्नेया । तां प्रसिद्धामस्याग्ने रीतिं स्वभावं गतिं वा परशोरिव प्रति
> परशोः प्रतिनिधिमिव पश्यामि । परशुर्यथा स्वस्वामिन्यभिमतं साधयति तद्वदित्यर्थ;।
> अस्य वर्पसो रूपवतोऽस्यादित्यस्यानीकः रश्मीसमूहं भुजे भोगायाख्यं । कथयाम्यहं । यदि यस्मात्स च देवः सचास्मत्सहायः सन् पितुमंतमन्नवंतं क्षॆयमिव निवासमिव भरहूतये संग्रामे यज्ञे वाह्वानयुक्ताय विशे यजमानाय
> रत्नं रमणीयं धनं दधाति धारयति । उभयमपि ददातीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is addressed to Agni. I see that well-known nature, or movement, of this Agni as a counterpart of the axe: as an axe accomplishes what its owner desires, so does he. Of this radiant Āditya, who has form, I declare the host of rays for enjoyment. Since that god, being our helper, bestows beautiful wealth, like a dwelling abounding in food, on the sacrificer who is called to battle or to sacrifice, the meaning is that he gives both.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- तां (*tāṃ*)—the well-known
- रीतिं (*rītiṃ*)—nature (course of conduct)
- परशोः प्रति (*paraśoḥ prati*)—like a counterpart of the axe (I behold)
- अस्य वर्पसः (*asya varpasaḥ*)—of this Āditya, who has the form of splendour
- अनेकं (*anekaṃ*)—the host of rays
- भुजे (*bhuje*)—as a means of enjoyment for living beings
- अख्यं (*akhyaṃ*)—I worship **NOTE**
- यदि (*yadi*)—if
- सचा (*sacā*)—(this Āditya) is a helper together with the sacrificer, (then)
- भरहूतये (*bharahūtaye*)—who invokes him at the place of sacrifice
- विशे (*viśe*)—to the sacrificer
- पितुमंतं (*pitumaṃtaṃ*)—filled with food
- क्षयं इव (*kṣayaṃ iva*)—like a house
- रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*)—beautiful wealth
- दधाति (*dadhāti*)—he gives

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I behold the well-known course of conduct of Agni as a counterpart of the axe. I worship the host of rays of this Āditya, who has the form of splendour, as a means of enjoyment for living beings. When this Āditya is with the sacrificer, he gives to the sacrificer who invokes him at the place of sacrifice beautiful wealth, like a house filled with food.

##### English translation
(I behold) the practice of that (Agni) as of a deputy: I celebrate the host (of rays) of that (resplendent) form, (designed for the enjoyment (of mankind): if he be with (the worshipper), he bestows upon the man who invokes him at a sacrifice such opulence as a mansion abounding with food.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Agni, four-flamed, that is, with flames spread in the four directions, goes with his tongue, that is, goes to the ghee and the like; or else, being four-flamed by his tongue, he adorns himself. Doing what? Covering himself with beautiful, delightful splendour, being Varuṇa, the remover of darkness, he roots out the enemy. Of him, that is, him, we do not know, as endowed with manhood or as the fulfiller of desires. Since this Bhaga, the great and adorable one, Savitā, the god who impels, gives desirable wealth.

- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with the flames that take the form of tongues
- ऋंजते (*ṛṃjate*)—adorns the place of sacrifice
- यतः (*yataḥ*)—by whose greatness
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—the adorable
- सविता (*savitā*)—god Savitṛ
- वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)—desired wealth
- दाति (*dāti*)—gives
- तस्य (*tasya*)—that god
- पुरुषत्वता (*puruṣatvatā*)—in the form of a man

- न विद्म (*na vidma*)—cannot know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni spreads beautiful splendour, uproots the enemy as the remover of darkness, spreads his flame in all four directions, and with the flames that take the form of tongues adorns the sacrificial

ground. That god, by whose greatness the adorable Savitṛ gives the desired wealth, we cannot know in the form of a man.

##### English translation
Blazing with his (fiery) tongue in the four quarters (of the horizon) he proceeds (to the sacrifice), wearing beautiful (lustre), the disperser of darkness, extirpating foes: we know him not (as endowed) with manhood. whereby this adorable Savitri bestows desirable (wealth).

## Sūkta 49 (Maṇḍala 5)

The forty-ninth sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवं व इति पंचर्चं पंचमं सूक्तमात्रेयस्य प्रतिप्रभस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं
> वैश्वदेवं । देवं वः प्रतिप्रभोऽंत्या तृणपाणिरित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ विनियोगो
> लैंगिकः ॥ .

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning देवं व इति पंचर्चं (*devaṃ va iti paṃcarcaṃ*), of five Ṛks, is the fifth sūkta; its seer is Pratiprabha of the Ātreya line, its metre is Triṣṭubh, and it is addressed to the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇī says: देवं वः प्रतिप्रभोऽंत्या तृणपाणिरित्यनुक्रमणिका (*devaṃ vaḥ pratiprabho 'ṃtyā tṛṇapāṇirityanukramaṇikā*). The use in ritual is by indication.

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning देवं वः (*devaṃ vaḥ*) is the fifth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is the one called Pratiprabha; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: देवं वः प्रतिप्रभोऽन्ता तृणपाणिः (*devaṃ vaḥ pratiprabho 'ntā tṛṇapāṇiḥ*). The use in ritual is Laiṅgika.

- Sūkta 49
- Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 49
- Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 3, Varga 2
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Seer: Pratiprabha Ātreya
- Deity: the Viśvedevas
- Metre: Triṣṭubh

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The god, the shining Savitā, the sanctioner of all, I approach for you; that is, you. Or else this is the speech of the Hotṛ: now, for you the sacrificers, I come near. And I come near to Bhaga, the adorable god, who divides the delightful oblation, the wealth, for the man, the sacrificer. That Bhaga divides is well known; and the Śruti says: रायो विभक्ता संभरश्च वस्वः (*rāyo vibhaktā saṃbharaśca vasvaḥ*) (Ṛgve. 4. 17. 11) **NOTE**, and: भगो विभक्ता शवसा (*bhago vibhaktā śavasā*) (Ṛgve. 5. 46. 6) **NOTE**. Or else the genitive stands for the dative: dividing for the sacrificer the delightful wealth. O leaders, O Aśvins who enjoy much: day by day I turn you toward us, wishing for your friendship. The particle that follows is a filler. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 546

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificers, on your behalf, at this time of sacrifice, I approach to pray to the god Savitṛ in nature, and to Bhaga, who divides delightful wealth for man. Leaders, who have the capacity to enjoy many excellent things, O Aśvin gods, wishing for your friendship, I pray to you again and again every day.

##### English translation
For you, (worshippers), I approach to-day the divine Savitri and Bhaga, the distributors of precious (wealth) amongst men : Aswins, (leaders of rites), enjoyers of many (good things), desiring your friendship, I solicit your daily presence.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first half of this Ṛk two deities, Savitṛ and Bhaga, are praised, and in the second half the Aśvin gods.

वः (*vaḥ*)—Here, instead of the singular त्वां (*tvāṃ*), the plural वः (*vaḥ*) is used. त्वां (*tvāṃ*) "you" means you who are the god Savitṛ. Or else, the commentator says, it may be thought that this sentence is recited by the priest called Hotṛ, addressing the sacrificers. In that case वः (*vaḥ*) means युष्मभ्यं (*yuṣmabhyaṃ*), and the meaning of the sentence देवं वः अद्य सवितारं एषे (*devaṃ vaḥ adya savitāraṃ eṣe*) is: "I approach to praise the god Savitṛ so that you, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, may gain wealth." The following sentences too can be explained in the same way.

भगं च रत्नं आयोः विभजंतं (*bhagaṃ ca ratnaṃ āyoḥ vibhajaṃtaṃ*)—for this sentence also he says that two kinds of meaning are possible. The word रत्न (*ratna*) in this sentence means रमणीयं हविः (*ramaṇīyaṃ haviḥ*): a delightful oblation or food; or delightful wealth and other things. One who distributes such food or wealth to the man who is the sacrificer, that is, one who gives wealth and the like as the fruit, in accordance with the sacrifices and other rites performed by each sacrificer: this is the intention. Yāska gave as the etymology of the word Bhaga भगो भजतेः (*bhago bhajateḥ*) (Ni. 1.7): since this god divides and gives wealth and the like, his name is Bhaga. In the Purāṇas and the like, and in modern Sanskrit, the word Bhaga is generally current in the sense of the sun (one of the twelve Ādityas), but in the Ṛgveda Bhaga is clearly indicated as a separate deity. The chief function of this deity is to divide or share out (for the sacrificers or the worshippers) wealth and the like, which are the fruit of the rites. This matter

### Printed p. 547

is stated clearly in the present Ṛk by the word विभजंतं (*vibhajaṃtaṃ*). And as examples in this matter the commentator quotes the Śruti sentences:

विभिन्नभिर्नृतमो अस्य शाकै रायो विभक्ता संभरश्च वस्वः । (*vibhinnabhirnṛtamo asya śākai rāyo vibhaktā saṃbharaśca vasvaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-17-11)

भगो विभक्ता शवसावसा गमदुरुव्यचा अदितिः श्रोतु मे हवं । (*bhago vibhaktā śavasāvasā gamaduruvyacā aditiḥ śrotu me havaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46.6)

The description of the qualities of this god Bhaga is very well explained in the 41st sūkta of the 7th maṇḍala. In that sūkta Bhaga and other deities are invoked in the morning; that is, Bhaga is included in the group of deities invoked in the morning, such as Agni and the Aśvin gods. Yāska says तस्य (भगस्य) काल प्रागुत्सर्पणात् (*tasya (bhagasya) kāla prāgutsarpaṇāt*) (Ni. 12-13), stating that this deity is one to be invoked in the morning, and gives as an example the Ṛk of this same sūkta प्रातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम (*prātarjitaṃ bhagamugraṃ huvema*). As a rule it is the custom to invoke this Bhaga together with Savitṛ and the Aśvin gods, the deities of the morning. So it is also in the present Ṛk.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Knowing the return, that is the approach, of Savitā, the asura, that is, the one who casts out enemies, serve the god Savitā with good hymns, O inner self; and further, for the man,

> ज्येष्ठं रत्नं धनं च विभजंतं गमयंतमित्यर्थः । नमसा नमस्कारेण हविषा वा
> विजानन् । विशेषेण भावयन्नित्यर्थः ॥ यद्वांतर्णीतण्यर्थोऽयं ॥ ज्ञापयन्
> उप ब्रुवीत । स्तौतु भवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

distributing the best wealth, that is, causing it to go to him. With homage, or with oblation, knowing, that is, perceiving in a special way; or else this has the sense of a causative, making known: let you declare, that is, may you praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- असुरस्य (*asurasya*)—of Savitṛ, the destroyer of enemies
- प्रतिप्रयाणं (*pratiprayāṇaṃ*)—the coming again
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—knowing
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—the god in nature
- सवितारं (*savitāraṃ*)—the god Savitṛ
- सूक्तैः (*sūktaiḥ*)—with excellent praises
- दुवस्य (*duvasya*)—worship
- आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—to man
- ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—praiseworthy
- रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*)—wealth
- विभजंतं (*vibhajaṃtaṃ*)—as one who divides
- विजानन् (*vijānan*)—knowing in a special way
- नमसा (*namasā*)—together with the oblation
- उप ब्रुवीत (*upa bruvīta*)—recite the praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Knowing the coming again of Savitṛ, the destroyer of enemies, worship the god Savitṛ, divine in nature, with excellent praises; knowing in a special way that he divides praiseworthy wealth for man, recite the praise together with the oblation.

##### English translation
Knowing the approach of the expeller (of the foes of the gods from heaven), worship the divine Savitri with holy hymns: praise him with reverence, distinguishing him as distributing precious (treasures) amongst men.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the deity Savitṛ is praised. In the sentence जेष्ठं च रत्नं विभजंतमायोः (*jeṣṭhaṃ ca ratnaṃ vibhajaṃtamāyoḥ*) of this Ṛk the distinction of the deity Bhaga is attributed to Savitṛ and described. That is, although it is the deity Bhaga who distributes wealth and the like, the prayer is expressed here that the god Savitṛ may share out to the sacrificer the best jewels and the like.

> इंद्रः । विष्णुः । वरुणः । मित्रः । अग्निः । अहानि । भद्रा । जनयंत । दस्माः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमग्निरदत्रयादनीयानि ॥ अदेरौणादिकोऽत्रप्रत्ययः । सुपां सुलुगिति
> याजादेशः॥ अथवात्तीत्यदत्रा जिह्वा । तया वार्याणि वरणीयानि काष्ठानि दयते .
> दयतिरनेककर्मात्र दहने वर्तते । दहतीत्यर्थः । सामर्थ्यादग्निरिति गम्यते ।
> यद्वा अदनीयानि वरणीयान्यन्नानि दयते। ददाति यजमानाय ॥ दय दानगतिहिंसाबलाख्यानेषु ॥ कीदृशोऽग्निः पूषा पोषको भगो भजनीयोदितिरखंड।
> नीयः । यद्वा । पूषादयस्त्रयोऽपि प्रत्येकमदनीयानि वार्याणि चान्नानि
> दयते । उस्रः सूर्यो वस्ते । आच्छादयति । सामथ्यात्तेजांसि । इंद्रादयः
> पंचापि देवा दस्मा दर्शनीया अहानि सर्वाण्यागंत्यणि भद्रा शोभनीयानि
> जनयंत । जनयंति ! दिवसानां यागदानादिविशिष्टत्वमेव भद्रत्वं ॥'

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni gives, for the sacrificer, edible things, or, otherwise, the word means the tongue, the organ that eats; with it he burns choice pieces of fuel. The root has many senses and here it is used for burning; that it is Agni is understood from the context. Or else he gives to the sacrificer desirable foods. Of what kind is Agni? Pūṣan, the nourisher; Bhaga, the adorable; Aditi, the indivisible. Or else the three, Pūṣan and the others, each give edible and desirable foods. The ruddy one, Sūrya, covers; by implication, he covers with his radiance. Indra and the other five gods, the handsome ones, bring forth all the coming days as auspicious; the auspiciousness of days is just their being distinguished by sacrifices, gifts and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—Pūṣan
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—Bhaga
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—and Aditi
- अदत्रया (*adatrayā*)—fit for enjoyment
- वार्याणि (*vāryāṇi*)—and desired foods
- दयते (*dayate*)—they give
- उस्रः (*usraḥ*)—the sun
- वस्ते (*vaste*)—puts on radiance
- दस्माः (*dasmāḥ*)—having a form worth seeing
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Viṣṇu
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—and Agni
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—auspicious
- अहानि (*ahāni*)—days
- जनयंत (*janayaṃta*)—bring forth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Pūṣan, Bhaga and Aditi give foods that are fit for enjoyment and desired. The sun puts on radiance. Indra, Viṣṇu, Varuṇa, Mitra and Agni, who have a form worth seeing, bring forth auspicious days.

### Printed p. 550

##### English translation
Pushan, Bhaga, Aditi. bestow (severally) excellent viands : the fierce (sun) robes (himself with radiance): the good-looking (deities), Indra, Vishnu, Varuna, Mitra, Agni, give birth to happy days.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अदत्रया (*adatrayā*)—अदनीयानि (*adanīyāni*): oblations and the like fit to be eaten; or अत्तीतित्यदत्ता जिह्वा तया अदत्रया (*attītityadattā jihvā tayā adatrayā*): the organ that is the means of eating, that is, the tongue. In the first sense the word अदत्रया (*adatrayā*) is a word ending in the accusative plural and is an adjective of the word वार्याणि (*vāryāṇi*). In the second sense, that is, in the sense of the tongue, the word अदत्रया (*adatrayā*) is a word ending in the dative singular. **NOTE**

पूषा (*pūṣā*), भगः (*bhagaḥ*), अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—पूषा पोषकः (*pūṣā poṣakaḥ*): one who nourishes by giving food and the like. भगः भजनीयः (*bhagaḥ bhajanīyaḥ*): the deity worthy to be worshipped. आदितिः अखंडनीयः (*āditiḥ akhaṃḍanīyaḥ*): one who pervades everywhere. These three words are explained as epithets of Agni. Or else the commentator says that they may be explained as three separate deities, Pūṣan, Bhaga and Aditi. When it is explained as referring to Agni, the verb दयते (*dayate*): दयते । दयतिरनेककर्मात्र दहने वर्तते (*dayate | dayatiranekakarmātra dahane vartate*); the root has many meanings, and here it is used in the sense of burning. That is, the intention is that Agni burns the oblations and other substances. Or else दयते ददाति यजमानाय (*dayate dadāti yajamānāya*): he gives food and other substances to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice; thus the sense of giving may also be stated for the root. The act of burning applies to Agni alone. The act of giving applies to Agni and also to the other deities, Pūṣan and the rest.

वस्ते (*vaste*), उस्रः (*usraḥ*)—The word उस्र (*usra*) is formed from the root meaning "to spread"; since he spreads everywhere with his rays, उस्रः (*usraḥ*) means the sun. Here the commentator explains that this sun covers, that is, envelops, everything with his radiance.

अहानि (*ahāni*)—सर्वाण्यागंत्यणि (*sarvāṇyāgaṃtyaṇi*): he has explained it as all the works that may come in future, that is, that will be attained.

In this Ṛk the deities Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aditi, the sun, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra and Agni are prayed to, that in what follows, that is, in succession, they may bring about all welfare for us.

> ग्मन् ।

> तत् । नः । अनर्वा । सविता । वरूथं । तत् । सिंधवः । इषयंतः । अनु । ग्मन् ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्प्रसिद्धं वरूथं वरणीयमस्मदभिमतं धनं नोऽस्मभ्यमनर्वाप्रत्यृतः
> केनाप्यतिरस्कृतः सविता देवः प्रयच्छत्विति शेषः ॥ तद्दनं सिंधवः स्कंदनशीला
> इषयंतो गच्छंत्यो नद्योऽनु अनुसृत्य ग्मन् । गच्छंतु । धनं दातुं गच्छंतित्यर्थः। यद्यस्मादध्वरस्य यागस्य होता होमनिष्पादकोऽहमुप वोचे उपेत्य
> ब्रवीमि तस्मात्तत्पयच्छंत्विति शेषः । वयं चात्रयो रायो धनस्य बहुविधस्य
> पतयः स्वामिनः स्याम । भवेम । वाजरत्ना अन्नेन बलेन वा रमणीयाः । अथवा
> यद्यस्माद्वोचे सौमि तस्मात्सविता नो वरूथमागच्छतु । तस्मान्नद्यश्च नो वरूथं
> यज्ञमनु ग्मन् अनुगच्छंत्विति ना योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That well-known wealth which we desire and which is worth choosing, may the unopposed god Savitā, whom nobody has repelled, bestow on us: this is to be supplied. The rivers, which flow, going along, follow after that wealth; the sense is that they go to give wealth. Since I, the Hotṛ, the one who brings about the oblation of the sacrifice, approach and speak, therefore may they bestow it. And may we, the Ātreyas, be lords of wealth of many kinds, delightful through food or strength. Or else: since I speak, therefore may Savitā come to our desired wealth, and therefore may the rivers too follow the sacrifice, our desired wealth: so it is to be construed. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अनर्वा (*anarvā*)—the unopposed
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- तत् (*tat*)—that well-known
- वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)—and desired wealth (may he give)
- इषयंतः (*iṣayaṃtaḥ*)—flowing
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—the rivers
- तत् (*tat*)—that same wealth (to give to us)
- अनु ग्मन् (*anu gman*)—may they come toward us
- यत् (*yat*)—by which same cause
- अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—of the sacrifice
- होता (*hotā*)—I, the Hotṛ
- उप वोचे (*upa voce*)—approach them and praise
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth
- पतयॆः (*patayèḥ*)—lords
- वाजरत्नाः (*vājaratnāḥ*)—and possessed of delightful wealth of food
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we become (may the gods grant it)

### Printed p. 552

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the unopposed god Savitṛ give us that well-known and desired wealth. May the flowing rivers come toward us, so as to bring us that same wealth. I, the Hotṛ in the sacrifice, approach them for that very reason and praise them. May the gods grant that we become lords of wealth and possessed of delightful wealth of food.

##### English translation
May the irreproachable Savitri (grant) us that desirable (wealth); may the flowing rivers hasten to (convey) it to us; for which purpose I, the ministering priest of the sacrifice, repeat (pious praises): affluent in food, may we be the lords of (manifold) riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the god Savitṛ and the rivers are praised. The word वरूथ (*varūtha*) used here can be given two kinds of meaning. वरूथं । वरणीयमस्मदभिमतं धनं (*varūthaṃ | varaṇīyamasmadabhimataṃ dhanaṃ*): wealth that we desire, this is one meaning. The meaning is that the god Savitṛ and the rivers should give us the wealth that we desire. As regards the rivers, wealth may mean money and material goods. Since the rivers supply water for agricultural work and food and the like is obtained from agriculture, wealth may also be understood as wealth in the form of food and other nourishment. The prayer that they give us these is stated here. In the second meaning, if the word वरूथ (*varūtha*) is taken to mean sacrifice, then, as the Hotṛ prays in the second half of this Ṛk with the sentence उप यद्योचे अध्वरस्य होता (*upa yadyoce adhvarasya hotā*), a petition is stated that the god Savitṛ and the rivers come to this sacrifice that we are performing and give us wealth and the like. This is another kind of meaning. **NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र ये वसु॑भ्य॒ ईव॒दा नमो॒ दुर्ये मि॒त्रे वरु॑णे सू॒क्तवा॑चः ।  
> अवै॒त्वभ्वं॑ कृणु॒ता वरी॑यो दि॒वस्सृ॑थि॒व्योरव॑सा मदेम ॥५॥

> प्र । ये । वसुभ्यः । ईवत् । आ । नमः । दुः । ये । मित्रे । वरुणे । सूक्तवाचः॥  
> अव । एतु । अभ्वं । कृणुत । वरीयः । दिवः पृथिव्योः । अवसा । मदेम ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये यजमाना वसुभ्यो यज्ञनिवासेभ्यो देवेभ्य ईवद्गमनवन्नमोऽन्नं
> पश्वात्मकं प्र दुः प्रादुः । ये च मित्रे देवे वरुणे च सूक्तवाचः सूक्तवचसो
> भवंति तानस्मानभ्वं महद्धनं तेजो नावैतु । अवगच्छतु । हे देवाः कृणुत
> कुरुत चैतेभ्यो वरीय उरुतरं सुखं । दिवस्पृथिव्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योरवसा
> रक्षणेन मदेम । हृष्येम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificers who gave to the Vasus, that is to the gods who have their dwelling at the sacrifice, food in the form of animals, food that is able to move about, and who are good speakers of praise toward the god Mitra and toward Varuṇa: to us, such sacrificers, may great wealth and splendour come near; he explains the verb as "may it approach". O gods, make for them wider, that is more spacious, happiness. By the protection of heaven and earth may we rejoice, that is, be glad. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which sacrificers
- वसुभ्यः (*vasubhyaḥ*)—to the Vasus
- ईवत् (*īvat*)—fit to move about
- नमः (*namaḥ*)—food (food in the form of animals)
- प्र दुः (*pra duḥ*)—offered
- ये (*ye*)—who
- मित्रे (*mitre*)—to Mitra
- वरुणे (च) (*varuṇe (ca)*)—and to Varuṇa
- सूक्तवाचः (*sūktavācaḥ*)—offered excellent praises (to such sacrificers)
- अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*)—great wealth
- अवैतु (*avaitu*)—may it come near
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods (to such sacrificers)
- वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)—the greatest happiness
- कृणुत (*kṛṇuta*)—bring about
- दिवस्पृथिव्योः (*divaspṛthivyoḥ*)—of heaven and earth
- अवसा (*avasā*)—by the protection
- मदेम (*madema*)—may we be happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May great wealth come to us, the sacrificers, who offered food in the form of animals to the Vasus and who offered excellent praises to Mitra and Varuṇa. O gods, bring about the greatest happiness for us, who are devoted in this way. May we be happy through the protection of heaven and earth.

##### English translation
May ample wealth devolve upon those who have presented victims to the Vasus, and upon those who have repeated praises to Mitra and Varuna : confer upon them, (gods), felicity, and may we rejoice in the protection of heaven and earth.

### Printed p. 554

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वसुभ्यः (*vasubhyaḥ*): यज्ञनिवासेभ्यो देवेभ्यः (*yajñanivāsebhyo devebhyaḥ*). Explaining the word vasu as "dwelling", the commentators have taken the word वसुभ्यः (*vasubhyaḥ*) to mean: to the gods who come to the sacrificial ground to receive the oblations and the like and who dwell there until the sacrifice is completed. सूक्तवाचः (*sūktavācaḥ*) means those who praise the gods such as Mitra and Varuṇa with excellent words. This word is an adjective of the word ये (*ye*) (the sacrificers).

## Sūkta 50 (Maṇḍala 5)

The fiftieth sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वो देवस्येति पंचर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं स्वस्तात्रेयमुनेरार्षं वैश्वदेवं
> पंचमी पंक्तिराद्याश्चतस्रोऽनुष्टुभः । तदुक्तमनुक्रमण्यां । विश्वः स्वस्तात्रेयः
> पंक्त्यंतमिति ॥ पृष्टाभिप्लवषडहयोः प्रथमेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे विश्वो देवस्येति
> प्रतिपत्तृचस्याद्यः । सूत्रितं च । विश्वो देवस्य नेतुरित्येका । आ. ७.६. । इति ॥
> आभिप्लविकेषु द्वितीयचतुर्थषष्ठॆष्वहस्वेष्टैव वैश्वदेवस्य शस्त्रस्य प्रतिपत् । युग्मेस्वेवमभिप्लवे । आ. ७. ६. । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning विश्वो देवस्येति (*viśvo devasyeti*), of five Ṛks, is the sixth sūkta. Its seer is the sage Svastyātreya, and it is addressed to the Viśvedevas. The fifth Ṛk is in the Paṅkti metre, the first four in Anuṣṭubh. This is stated in the Anukramaṇī: विश्वः स्वस्तात्रेयः पंक्त्यंतमिति (*viśvaḥ svastātreyaḥ paṃktyaṃtamiti*). Use in ritual: on the first day of the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍaha rites, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, the first Ṛk of this sūkta, विश्वो देवस्य (*viśvo devasya*), is the first of the Pratipat triplet. It is laid down in the sūtra: विश्वो देवस्य नेतुरित्येका (*viśvo devasya neturityekā*) (Ā. 7.6). In the Ābhiplavika rites, on the second, fourth and sixth days, the same Ṛk is likewise the Pratipat of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, since it is so laid down in the sūtra युग्मेस्वेवमभिप्लवे (*yugmesvevamabhiplave*) (Ā. 7. 6). **NOTE**

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning विश्वो देवस्य (*viśvo devasya*) is the sixth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is called Svastātreya; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the first four Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Anuṣṭubh metre, the fifth Ṛk in the Paṅkti metre. It is said in the Anukramaṇī: Viśvaḥ Svastātreyaḥ Paṅktyantam. On the first day of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭha and Abhiplava ṣaḍaha, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, the first Ṛk of this sūkta beginning विश्वो देवस्य (*viśvo devasya*) is to be recited as the first mantra of the Pratipat triplet; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, विश्वो देवस्य नेतुरित्येका (*viśvo devasya neturityekā*) (Ā. 7-6). And on the second, fourth and sixth days of the sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, the first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be recited as the opening mantra of the Pratipat triplet among the mantras of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, युग्मेष्टेवमभिप्सवे (*yugmeṣṭevamabhipsave*) (Ā. 7-6).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वो॑ दे॒वस्य॑ ने॒तुर्मर्तो॑ पुरीत स॒ख्यं ।  
> विश्वो॑ रा॒य इ॑षुध्यति द्यु॒म्नं वृ॑णीत पु॒ष्यसे॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वः । देवस्य । नेतुः । मर्तः । वुरीत । सख्यं ।  
> विश्वः । राये । इषुध्यति । द्युन्नुं । वृणीत । पुष्यसे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वः सर्वो मर्तो नेतुर्देवस्य । सवितुरित्यर्थः । तस्य सख्यं पुरीत ।
> वृणीत विश्वो जनो राये धनस्येषुध्यति ॥ पंचमलकारः ॥ ईशीत । तस्यानुग्रहात्
> सर्वो जनो द्युम्नं धनं वृणीत पुष्यसे पुष्टैश्च पर्याप्तं धनं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Every mortal should choose the friendship of the leading god, that is, of Savitṛ; "choose" is Sāyaṇa's gloss of the verb. Every man, for the sake of wealth, should be lord of wealth, so Sāyaṇa glosses इषुध्यति (*iṣudhyati*) with ईशीत (*īśīta*). By his favour every person should choose wealth, wealth that is sufficient for nourishment. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वः (*viśvaḥ*)—all
- वर्तुः (*vartuḥ*)—the man **NOTE**
- नेतुः (*netuḥ*)—of the leading
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of the god Savitṛ
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—the friendship
- पुरीत (*purīta*)—may he obtain by praying
- विश्वः (*viśvaḥ*)—every man
- राये (*rāye*)—for the gain of wealth
- इषुध्यति (*iṣudhyati*)—may he look for favour (from Savitṛ)
- पुष्यसे (*puṣyase*)—for a well-nourished life
- द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*)—wealth
- वृणीत (*vṛṇīta*)—may he desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May every man pray for and obtain the friendship of the leading god Savitṛ. May every man gain wealth through Savitṛ's favour alone. For a well-nourished life let him desire wealth from him alone.

### Printed p. 556

##### English translation
Let every man solicit the friendship of the divine leader (of heaven, the sun); let every man desire (of him) riches: let him request affluence (wherewith) to nourish (his descendants).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Although the Viśvedevas are said to be the deity of this sūkta, in all the Ṛks of the sūkta it is the god Savitṛ in particular who is praised. Since Savitṛ is ordinarily invoked in the morning, the time when the sacrifice begins, the seer prays that Savitṛ himself, as guide of this sacrifice which we perform, may see that the sacrificial rite is carried out completely, and that as the fruit of that sacrifice he may bestow on us things that bring happiness, such as a house together with sons and grandsons, wealth, food and the like.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते ते॑ देव नेत॒र्ये चे॒मा अ॑नु॒शसे॑ ।  
> ते रा॒या ते ह्या॒३॒॑पिपृचे॒ सचे॑महि सच॒थ्यैः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । ते । देव । नेतः । ये । च । इमान् । अनुशसे ।  
> ते । राया । ते । हि । आपृचे । सचेमहि । सचथ्यैः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नेतर्देव ते तव स्वभूतास्ते वयं यजमाना ये चान्य इमान् ॥
> विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ॥ इमे होत्रादयोऽनुशसे शंसितुं प्रभवंति तेऽपि त्वदीयाः ।
> यद्वा । इमानन्यानिंद्रादीननुशसे क्रमेण शंसितुं प्रभवंति । एकैव ना महानात्मा देवता स सूर्यः स हि सर्वभूतात्मेकृत्याद्विदितरासां देवतानां तदंतर्भावादिति भावः । न केवलं त्वच्छंसका एवेत्यर्थः । त उभये वयं राया धनेन
> सचेमहीति संबंधः । ते हि ते खल्वापृच आपर्चनीयाः ॥ कृत्यार्थे केन्प्रत्ययः ।
> कृन्मेजंत इत्यव्ययत्वादिभक्तेरदर्शनं ॥ सचथ्यैः सर्वैः कामैः सचेमहि । संगच्छेमहि ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O leader, O god: we the sacrificers are yours, belong to you, and so are those others who are able to praise these (the Hotṛ priests and the rest); they too are yours. Or else, those who are able to praise in turn these others, Indra and the rest, are yours as well. Only one great Self is the deity, namely Sūrya; he is the Self of all beings, and the other deities are included in him; this is the sense. The meaning is that they are not only your praisers. Both of these groups, we, are to be united with wealth: this is the connection. Those indeed are the ones to be connected (with wealth). With all desires may we be united, may we come together. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 557

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सेतः (*setaḥ*)—O leader **NOTE**
- देव (*deva*)—O Savitṛ **NOTE**
- ते (*te*)—we, these sacrificers
- ते (*te*)—who belong to your protection
- ये च (*ye ca*)—and who
- इमान् (*imān*)—the other gods, Indra and the rest
- अनुशसे (*anuśase*)—praise and worship (they too are yours)
- ते (*te*)—these both our groups
- राया (*rāyā*)—may they be joined with wealth
- ते हि (*te hi*)—we ourselves
- आपृचे (*āpṛce*)—for our satisfaction
- सचथ्यैः (*sacathyaiḥ*)—with all our desires
- सचेमहि (*sacemahi*)—we shall unite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O leader, O Savitṛ, we, these sacrificers, belong to your protection. Not only we, but those here who praise and worship Indra and the other gods are also yours. May both these groups of ours be possessed of wealth; may we be united with all our desires, for the fulfilment of our wishes and for our satisfaction.

##### English translation
Divine leader of heaven), these (worshippers) are yours, and (so are they) who praise these (other gods): these (both) we associate with opulence, we (seek) to unite with (our) des res. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

इंद्रादीन् शंसितुं प्रभवंति तेऽपि त्वदीयाः (*iṃdrādīn śaṃsituṃ prabhavaṃti te 'pi tvadīyāḥ*). In this Ṛk the god Savitṛ is praised. Therefore the seer says that the people, such as the priests and sacrificers, who praise Savitṛ are dear to Savitṛ. But it may be asked whether it is right, addressing the god Savitṛ, to say that likewise the people who praise Indra and the other gods are also yours. To this the commentator says that Savitṛ dwells in the other gods as their inner self, and that therefore, if the other gods are worshipped, it is as though Savitṛ or Sūrya himself were worshipped, and in support of this he has quoted the sentence एकैन वा महानात्मा देवता स सूर‍्यः स हि सर्वभूतात्मा । (*ekaina vā mahānātmā devatā sa sūryaḥ sa hi sarvabhūtātmā |*). In this way he has made clear that Savitṛ has the feeling that even those who praise Indra and the other gods are his own.

> आतोऽस्मिन्यज्ञे ॥ सार्वविभक्तिकस्तसिः ॥ नोऽस्माकमृत्तिजां नन्नेत्थानतिथीन्

> पत्नीरपि दशस्यत हनिष्प्रदानादिना । यद्वा । नोऽस्मभ्यं नन् पुत्रभृत्यादीनतिथीन्

> मार्गे वर्तमानं वैरिणं द्विषोऽन्यानपि द्विषो द्वेष्ट्यन्युयोतु पृथक्करोतु
> देवसंघः सविता वा यूयुविः सर्वस्यामिश्रयिता पृथक्कर्ता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Therefore", that is, in this sacrifice: for us, the priests, the leaders (न्नेत्थानतिथीन् (*nnetthānatithīn*)), the gods who are honoured like guests, worship all around, serve them. Therefore, in this sacrifice, serve also the wives of the gods, with offerings of oblations and the like. Or else: for us, serve here these three, namely sons, servants and the like as guests, and the wife; O gods, grant them. Far away, at a distance, let him drive every enemy who stands in the path, and the other haters as well; let him separate them, either the company of the gods or Savitṛ, the discriminator who separates all that is mingled. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अतः (*ataḥ*)—therefore
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- न्यन् (*nyan*)—those who are leaders
- अतिथीन् (*atithīn*)—the gods who are to be honoured like guests
- आ दशस्यत (*ā daśasyata*)—worship exceedingly
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—for that same reason
- पत्नीः (*patnīḥ*)—the wives of the gods also (worship)
- यूयुविः (*yūyuviḥ*)—Savitṛ, who separates the good from the bad
- पथेष्ठाः (*patheṣṭhāḥ*)—who stand as thorns in our path
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—the enemies
- आरे युयोतु (*āre yuyotu*)—may he separate and push far away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Worship exceedingly the gods who are our leaders and who are to be honoured like guests. For that same reason worship also the wives of the gods. May Savitṛ, who separates the good from the bad, separate all the enemies who stand as thorns in our path and push them far away.

##### English translation
Worship, therefore, the leaders (of our rites), our guests, (the gods) and the wives (of the deities): may the (divine) discriminator drive to a distance every adversary, (and all our) enemies.

### Printed p. 559

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the gods are praised together. The commentator has said that the sentence in the first half, अतः नः न्यून् अतिथीन् पत्निः आ दशस्यत (*ataḥ naḥ nyūn atithīn patniḥ ā daśasyata*), can be explained in two ways. For the words न्यून् (*nyūn*) and अथितीन् (*athitīn*) he gives नेत्यन् अतिथिवत्पूज्यान् देवान् (*netyan atithivatpūjyān devān*): the gods who carry out the sacrificial rites or are guides in performing them and who are honoured like guests; so one meaning is: attend, in this our sacrifice, on such gods and on their wives, the wives of the gods. For the words न्यून् (*nyūn*) अतिथीन् (*atithīn*) the ordinary meaning is taken, that is: entertain with worship and the like the human guests who come, or have come, to our sacrifice; this is another kind of meaning. Both these meanings are possible here. **NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्र यस्मिन्यज्ञे वह्निर्यज्ञस्य वोढाभिहितो यूपं प्रापितो द्रोण्यो

> अर्णारणकुशला धीरेव योषिदिव । यद्वा । अर्णानि हवींष्यभिलक्ष्य सनिता भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In which sacrifice Agni, the carrier of the sacrifice, has been brought to the post, and the animal fit for the post runs toward the post, there Savitṛ, whose mind is on the sacrificer, is "of the house of heroes"; heroes are the priests, the sacrificers, sons, servants and the like, and the house is such as has them; or else, he who has impelled a house; that is, the giver of a house furnished with sons and the like. He is the distributor. He is like a woman skilled in अर्णारणकुशला (*arṇāraṇakuśalā*). Or else: with regard to the oblations (अर्णानि हवींष्यभिलक्ष्य (*arṇāni havīṃṣyabhilakṣya*)) he is the distributor. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which sacrifice
- वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—Agni, the manager of the sacrifice
- अभिहितः (*abhihitaḥ*)—has been established, and
- द्रोण्यः (*droṇyaḥ*)—fit for the post
- पशुः (*paśuḥ*)—the sacrificial animal
- दुद्रवत् (*dudravat*)—is carried to the neighbourhood of the post (there)

### Printed p. 560

- नृमणाः (*nṛmaṇāḥ*)—Savitṛ, favourably minded toward the sacrificer
- अर्णा (*arṇā*)—skilled in giving
- धीरेव (*dhīreva*)—like a wife
- वीरपत्न्यः (*vīrapatnyaḥ*)—houses furnished with sons and the rest **NOTE**
- सनिता (*sanitā*)—is the distributor

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In which sacrifice Agni, the manager of the sacrifice, has been established and the sacrificial animal fit for the post is carried to the neighbourhood of the post, there Savitṛ, favourably minded toward the sacrificers, like a wife skilled in giving, is the distributor of houses furnished with sons and the rest.

##### English translation
When the victim fit to be bound, the subject (of the sacrifice), has been stationed (at the saerificial post) : he, (Savitri), with mind well disposed towards the worshipper, the donor of dwellings and descendants is like a clever wife, the bestower (of wealth). **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this sacrifice that we are performing, Agni stands kindled, established in the Āhavanīya fire-pit on the upper altar. The animal prepared for the sacrifice has also been brought to the post to which it is bound and consecrated with mantras. In such a sacrifice the god Savitṛ, satisfied with the oblations and the like that we offer and with our praises, to show favour to the sacrificer, as a clever woman serves the people of the house, dividing food and other nourishment properly (serving it out), may provide a house made prosperous by sons and the rest and by other kinds of comfort; this is the main intention stated here.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒ष ते॑ देव नेता॒ रथ॒स्पतिः॒ शं र॒यिः ।  
> शं रा॒ये शं स्व॒स्तय॑ इषः॒स्तुतो॑ मनामहे देव॒स्तुतो॑  
> मनामहे ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 561

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । ते । देव । नेतरिति । रथः पतिः । शं । रयिः ।  
> शं । राये । शं । स्वस्तये । इषःस्तुतः । मनामहे । देवस्तुतः । मनामहे ॥५॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नेतर्देव सवितस्ते तवैष रथःपतिः सर्वस्य पालको रयिर्दातव्यधनवान् ॥
> मत्त्वर्थो लुप्यते । शं करोश्विति शेषः । वयं च राये धनस्य शं सुखाय
> यद्वा । राये धनाय शं सुखाय च स्वस्तयेऽविनाशायेषःस्तुत एषणीयस्य
> सवितुः स्तोतारो वयं मनामहे । स्तुमः । देवस्तुतो देवानां देवस्य वा
> सवितुः स्तोतारो मनामहे । स्तुमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O leader, O god Savitṛ, this lord of the chariot of yours, the protector of all, and the one rich in wealth to be given (the possessive suffix is dropped), "may he make happiness" is to be supplied. And we, for wealth, for happiness, for well-being, that is, for freedom from destruction, praisers of the desirable Savitṛ, we glorify him, we praise. Praisers of the gods, or of the god Savitṛ, we glorify, we praise. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नेतः (*netaḥ*)—O leader **NOTE**
- देव (*deva*)—O Savitṛ
- ते (*te*)—your
- रयिः (*rayiḥ*)—filled with wealth
- एषःरथस्पतिः (*eṣaḥrathaspatiḥ*)—this chariot, which is also the protector
- शं (*śaṃ*)—may it be a bringer of happiness (to us)
- रायी (*rāyī*)—for wealth **NOTE**
- शं (*śaṃ*)—for happiness
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for well-being
- इषः स्तुतः (*iṣaḥ stutaḥ*)—we who are praisers of the honoured Savitṛ
- मनामहे (*manāmahe*)—we praise
- देवस्तुतः (*devastutaḥ*)—we who are praisers of Savitṛ, the god in essence
- मनामहे (*manāmahe*)—we praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O leader, O Savitṛ, may this chariot of yours, filled with wealth and a protector, bring us happiness. We, the praisers of the god Savitṛ, praise him for wealth, for happiness and for well-being.

##### English translation
Leader (of heaven), may this your protecting chariot, laden with riches, (come for our) happiness : praisers of the honoured (Savitri), we glorify him for felicity through well-being : praisers of the gods, we glorify (them).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, which forms the conclusion of the sūkta, the seer who saw the sūkta prays that the chariot of the god Savitṛ, the guide, and Savitṛ himself also, may provide us with happiness, wealth and well-being, and says that for this we praise this god.

## Sūkta 51 (Maṇḍala 5)

The fifty-first sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्ने सुतस्येति पंचदशर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । अग्ने
> पंचोना चतस्रो गायत्र्यः षळुष्ठि हस्तिस्रो जगत्यस्त्रिष्टुभो वांत्ये अनुष्टुभाविति।
> ऋषिश्चान्यस्मादिति परिभाषया स्वस्त्यात्रेय ऋषिः । आदितश्चतस्रो गायत्र्यः पंचम्याद्याः षडुष्टिह एकादश्याद्यास्त्रिस्रो जगत्यस्त्रिष्टुभो वा चतुर्दशीपंचदश्यावनुष्टुभौ । विश्वे देवा देवता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning अग्ने सुतस्येति (*agne sutasyeti*), of fifteen Ṛks, is the seventh sūkta. Here is this Anukramaṇī: अग्ने पंचोना चतस्रो गायत्र्यः षळुष्ठि हस्तिस्रो जगत्यस्त्रिष्टुभो वांत्ये अनुष्टुभाविति। (*agne paṃconā catasro gāyatryaḥ ṣaḷuṣṭhi hastisro jagatyastriṣṭubho vāṃtye anuṣṭubhāviti|*). By the rule "and the seer from another", the seer is Svastyātreya. The first four Ṛks are Gāyatrī, from the fifth the six Uṣṇih, from the eleventh three Jagatī or Triṣṭubh, and the fourteenth and fifteenth are two Anuṣṭubh. The deity is the Viśvedevas. **NOTE**

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning अग्ने सुतस्य (*agne sutasya*) is the seventh sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has fifteen Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अग्ने पंचोना चतस्रो गायत्र्यः षळुष्टिहस्तिस्रो जगत्यस्त्रिष्टुभो वांत्ये अनुष्टुभौ (*agne paṃconā catasro gāyatryaḥ ṣaḷuṣṭihastisro jagatyastriṣṭubho vāṃtye anuṣṭubhau*). The seer of this sūkta is called Svastātreya; the Viśvedevas are the deity; the first four Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Gāyatrī metre; the following six Ṛks (Ṛks 5-10) are in the Uṣṇik metre; the three Ṛks following the eleventh (Ṛks 11-13) are in the Jagatī or Triṣṭubh metre. The fourteenth and fifteenth Ṛks are in the Anuṣṭubh metre.

- Sūkta 51
- Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 51
- Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 3, Varga 5, 6, 7
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 15
- Seer: Svastyātreya
- Deity: the Viśvedevas
- Metre: Ṛks 1-4 Gāyatrī; 5-10 Uṣṇik; 11-13 Triṣṭubh or Jagatī; 14, 15 Anuṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ सु॒तस्य॑ पी॒तये॒ विश्वै॒रूमे॑भि॒रा ग॑हि ।  
> दे॒वेभि॑र्ह॒व्यदा॑तये ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 563

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । सुतस्य । पीतये । विश्वैः । ऊमेभिः । आ । गहि ।  
> देवेभिः । हव्यसदातये ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं सुतस्य पीतये सोमपानाय विश्वैरूमेभिरूमैः सर्वैरपि
> रक्षकैर्देवेभिर्देवैरिंद्रादिभिः सह हव्यादातयेऽस्माकं हनिर्दानाय तद्दात्रे यजमानाय वा आ गहि ! आगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, for the drinking of the pressed Soma, that is, for the Soma-drinking, come together with all the protecting gods, Indra and the others, to the one who gives oblations, that is, to the sacrificer, the giver of them; आ गहि (*ā gahi*), come. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed Soma
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for the drinking
- ऊमेभिः (*ūmebhiḥ*)—(with) the protecting
- विश्वैति देवेभिः (*viśvaiti devebhiḥ*)—with all the gods **NOTE**
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblations
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—come graciously

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, for the drinking of the pressed Soma juice, come graciously, together with all the protecting gods, to the sacrificer who gives oblations.

##### English translation
Come, Agni, with all the protecting deities, to drink the libation : come with the gods.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋत॑धीतय॒ आ ग॑त॒ सत्य॑धर्माणो अध्व॒रं ।  
> अ॒ग्नेः पि॑बत जि॒ह्वया॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋत्यधीतयः । आ । गत । सत्यधर्माणः । अध्वरं ।  
> अग्नेः । पिबत । जिह्वया ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 564

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋतधीतयः सत्यस्तु तयोऽबाध्यकर्माणो वा देवा अध्वरमस्मद्यज्ञमा
> गत । आगच्छत । आगत्य च हे सत्यधर्माणः सत्यस्य धारयितारो यूयमग्नेर्जह्वया
> पिबताज्यसोमादिकं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Ṛtadhītayaḥ, gods whose praises are true or whose deeds cannot be obstructed, come to our sacrifice. And having come, O Satyadharmāṇaḥ, upholders of truth, drink with the tongue of Agni the ghee, the Soma and the rest. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतधीतयः (*ṛtadhītayaḥ*)—O gods who have truthful works
- सत्यधर्माणः (*satyadharmāṇaḥ*)—and upholders of truth
- अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—to our sacrifice
- आ गत (*ā gata*)—come graciously
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of Agni
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with the mouth of the flame, which is like a tongue
- पिबत (*pibata*)—drink the Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods who have truthful works and are upholders of truth, come graciously to our sacrifice and drink the Soma with the mouth of the flame, which is like the tongue of Agni.

##### English translation
(Gods who are) devoutly praised and worshipped in truth, come to the sacrifice, and drink the libation with the tongue of Agni.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋतधीतयः (*ṛtadhītayaḥ*)—सत्यस्तु तयोs बाध्यकर्मणो वा (*satyastu tayos bādhyakarmaṇo vā*). Those who are praised with true sentences: the qualities that the praising people have described and extolled in the gods are all true. In the hymns they sing or the descriptions they make there is no exaggeration; this is the intention. Or else अबाध्यकर्माणः (*abādhyakarmāṇaḥ*): no one can obstruct the deeds or the heroic acts that these gods perform; that is, no one is able to hinder or put an obstacle in the way of the gods or of the works they do; this other kind of meaning is also stated here. More or less the same meaning applies to the word सत्यधर्माणः (*satyadharmāṇaḥ*) in this same Ṛk. Or else, the main intention is that they uphold truth alone, that they impel and regulate good people so that they do good works, or that their rules and works always rest on truth alone, and therefore they are called सत्यधर्माणः (*satyadharmāṇaḥ*).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विप्रे॑भिर्विप्र संत्य प्रात॒र्यान॑भि॒रा ग॑हि ।  
> दे॒वेभिः॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विप्रेभिः । विप्र । संत्य । प्रातर्याव्यभिः । आ । गहि ।  
> देवेभिः । सोमपीतये ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विप्र मेधाविन् विविधकानानां वा पूरक हे संत्य संभजनीयाग्ने
> विप्रेभिरुक्तलक्षणैः प्रातर्यावभिः प्रातःकाल आगंतृभिर्देवेभिर्देवैः सार्धमा गहि ।
> आगच्छ । किमर्थं । सोमपीतये सोमपानाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O wise one, O विप्र (*vipra*), who fulfils the various (desires), O Agni who is to be shared, come, together with the gods who come in the morning, with the wise ones of the kind described: आ गहि (*ā gahi*), come. For what purpose? For the drinking of Soma. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्र (*vipra*)—O wise one
- संत्य (*saṃtya*)—and adorable Agni
- विप्रेभिः (*viprebhiḥ*)—with the wise
- प्रातर्यावभिः (*prātaryāvabhiḥ*)—who come in the morning
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—with the gods
- सोमपितये (*somapitaye*)—for drinking Soma **NOTE**
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—come graciously

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise and adorable Agni, come graciously, together with the wise gods who come in the morning, to drink the Soma.

##### English translation
Sage and adorable Agni, come with the wise and early-stirring divinities to drink the Soma libation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to come to the sacrificial ground together with the gods who come in the morning and to drink Soma with them. Who are the gods who come to the sacrificial ground in the morning? Namely—

### Printed p. 566

प्रातरग्निं प्रातरिंद्रं हवामहे प्रातर्मित्रावरुणा प्रातरश्विना । प्रातर्भगं पूषणं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं प्रातस्सोममुत रुद्रं हुवेम ॥ (*prātaragniṃ prātariṃdraṃ havāmahe prātarmitrāvaruṇā prātaraśvinā | prātarbhagaṃ pūṣaṇaṃ brahmaṇaspatiṃ prātassomamuta rudraṃ huvema ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-41-1). In this Ṛk the seer Vasiṣṭha says that Agni, Indra, Mitra and Varuṇa, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Soma and Rudra are invoked in the morning. Besides, among these gods it is the custom to invoke chiefly Agni, the Aśvins, Uṣas and Savitṛ in the morning. प्रातर्हि यज्ञमश्विना दधाते प्र शंसंति कवयः पूर्वभाजः । प्रातर्यजध्वमश्विना हिनोत न सायमस्ति देवया अजुष्टं ॥ (*prātarhi yajñamaśvinā dadhāte pra śaṃsaṃti kavayaḥ pūrvabhājaḥ | prātaryajadhvamaśvinā hinota na sāyamasti devayā ajuṣṭaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-77-1,2). In this Ṛk the matter of invoking the Aśvins in the morning is stated. Because Agni is absolutely necessary for sacrificial rites, and because the sacrificial rite begins in the morning, it is well known that Agni too is churned and invoked in the morning, the time when the sacrifice begins. In the same way, since the dawn appears before sunrise, the goddess Uṣas also is a deity of the morning; and since Savitṛ is the rising sun himself, Savitṛ too is a deity of the morning. Therefore Agni is prayed to come to the sacrificial ground in the morning with these gods and to drink Soma. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं सोम॑श्च॒मू सु॒तोऽम॑त्रे॒ परि॑ षिच्यते ।  
> प्रि॒य इंद्रा॑य वा॒यवे॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । सोमः । चमू इति । सुतः । अमत्रे । परि । सिच्यते ।  
> प्रियः । इंद्राय । वायवे ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 567

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं पुरतो वर्तमानः सोमश्चमू चन्नोरत्र्योरधिषवणफलकयोः
> सुतोऽभिषुतः सन् अमत्रे पात्रे परि षिच्यते । पूर्यते । स चेंद्राय वायवे
> च प्रियः । तं पातुं हे इंद्रवायू आगच्छतमिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, present before us, pressed between the two चमू (*camū*), that is, the two pressing-boards, is poured around into the vessel; that is, it is filled. And it is dear to Indra and to Vāyu. To drink it, O Indra and Vāyu, come: this is to be supplied. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—to Indra
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—and to Vāyu
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—dear
- अयं सोमः (*ayaṃ somaḥ*)—this Soma
- चमू (*camū*)—in the camū vessels
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed
- अनत्रे (*anatre*)—in the Soma vessel **NOTE**
- परि षिच्यते (*pari ṣicyate*)—is filled

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Soma, dear to Indra and Vāyu, is pressed between the two wooden boards (चमू (*camū*)) that are used for pressing out the Soma juice, and is filled into the Soma vessel.

##### English translation
The Soma juice, effused into the ladles, is poured out into the vase, acceptable to Indra and Vayu.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

चन्नोः (*cannoḥ*): अत्रोः अधिषवणफलकयोः (*atroḥ adhiṣavaṇaphalakayoḥ*), "of the two pressing-boards". The Soma plants are crushed with stones and the juice is pressed out. Those stones are called ग्रावा (*grāvā*). In some places they are called अद्रि (*adri*). Some say that अद्रि (*adri*) is a stone broad at the bottom and hollow in the middle like a mortar, and that ग्रावा (*grāvā*) is another stone with which the Soma plants, placed on the stone called अद्रि (*adri*), are crushed. This stone called ग्रावा (*grāvā*) is thick at the base and shaped like a round stone so that it is convenient to hold in the hand. These stones may be compared, more or less, with the pestle and mortar (Pestle & Mortar) that physicians use for grinding medicines and the like. Ordinarily the use of such stones is the more common for crushing the Soma plants and pressing out the Soma juice, and it is their description that is found especially. But in place of these stones wooden boards or pieces are also used. The lower board is somewhat broad and hollow in the middle. Another piece of wood, thick and long, with which the Soma plants placed on it are crushed. These two kinds of wooden pieces are what is indicated here by the word चन्नोः (*cannoḥ*). In this Ṛk and in the next three Ṛks, Indra and Vāyu are prayed to come to the sacrificial ground to drink Soma. In the next Ṛk Vāyu alone is prayed to.

### Printed p. 568

For it is well known that in the sacrifice Vāyu is the first to be entitled to drink Soma, and that for another reason Indra joins Vāyu and the two drink Soma together. In this matter, that is, on how the god Vāyu is entitled to the first drinking of Soma, there is an ancient story in the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa. देवा वै सोमस्य राज्योऽग्रपेये न समपादयन्नहं प्रथमः पिबीयमहं प्रथमः पिबीयमित्येवाकामयंत ते संपादयंतोऽब्रुवन् हंताजिमयाम स यो न उज्जॆष्यति स प्रथमः सोमस्य पास्यतीति तथेति त आजिमयुस्तेषामाजिं यतामभिसृष्टानां वायुर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यताथेंद्रोऽथ मित्रावरुणावथाश्विन् । (*devā vai somasya rājyo 'grapeye na samapādayannahaṃ prathamaḥ pibīyamahaṃ prathamaḥ pibīyamityevākāmayaṃta te saṃpādayaṃto 'bruvan haṃtājimayāma sa yo na ujjèṣyati sa prathamaḥ somasya pāsyatīti tatheti ta ājimayusteṣāmājiṃ yatāmabhisṛṣṭānāṃ vāyurmukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyatātheṃdro 'tha mitrāvaruṇāvathāśvin |*) (Ai. Brā. 9-25). In ancient times all the gods wished to drink Soma together, and when a dispute arose as to who among them should drink Soma first, a discussion began, each saying that he himself should drink first. Since the matter could not be settled in any way, they all met, deliberated and came to an agreement: "Let us all arrange a contest; whoever wins in it will be entitled to drink Soma first." Everyone agreed to this, and the contest was fixed thus: running from one place to another place far away, whoever first reaches a rock or a tree there is to be considered the winner. When all agreed to the pact that the winner among them should first drink Soma as the victor, all the gods began to run at the same moment. Of all the gods who were running, Vāyu reached the appointed place ahead of all. Indra came right behind Vāyu and was second. Afterwards Mitra and Varuṇa ran behind Indra, and behind them the Aśvins, and they reached the appointed place. Therefore among these gods Vāyu ran ahead of all and became the victor.

सोऽवेदिंद्रो वायुमुद्वै जयतीति तमनु परापतत्सह नावथोज्जयावेति स नेत्त्वब्रवीदहमेवोज्जॆष्यामाति तृतीयं मेऽथोज्जयावेति नेति हैवाब्रवीदहमेवोज्जॆष्यामाति तुरीयं मेऽथोज्जयावेति तथेति तं तुरीयेऽत्यार्जत तत्तुरीयभागिंद्रोऽभवत्रिभाग्वायुः ॥ (*so 'vediṃdro vāyumudvai jayatīti tamanu parāpatatsaha nāvathojjayāveti sa nettvabravīdahamevojjèṣyāmāti tṛtīyaṃ me 'thojjayāveti neti haivābravīdahamevojjèṣyāmāti turīyaṃ me 'thojjayāveti tatheti taṃ turīye 'tyārjata tatturīyabhāgiṃdro 'bhavatribhāgvāyuḥ ‖*). While Vāyu was running, and Indra behind him, the following conversation took place between them. Seeing Vāyu running swiftly, Indra, who was behind him, thought: "This Vāyu will run ahead of all and be the victor. I must somehow run along with him and win", and, using all his strength, ran close to Vāyu.

### Printed p. 569

Yet there was no sign that he would leave Vāyu behind and go forward. Then Indra said to Vāyu: "O Vāyu, we two are ahead of everyone. Therefore let us consider that we have both won, and let us share the first drinking of Soma, half for me and half for you. Let us win the victory together, helping each other." Hearing this, Vāyu said: "O Indra, I am ahead of you, if only by a little. Therefore I alone shall be the victor. In the first drinking of Soma everything must belong to me. I cannot give you half." Then Indra said: "Very well, then I do not want half. Take two of three parts and give me only one part." Vāyu did not agree even to that: "Whatever happens, I shall win. All of it will belong to me, and I do not wish to give you even one part in three." Then Indra again entreated Vāyu: "I do not want even one in three. Still less; it is enough if you give me one in four. Agree at least to that." Vāyu said, "So be it", and agreed. Therefore it was arranged that in the Aindravāyava cup (that is, the vessel in which Indra and Vāyu drink Soma together) Indra should have one part and Vāyu three parts.

तौ सहैवेंद्रवायू उदजयतां सह मित्रावरुणौ सहाश्विन् श एषामेते यथोज्जि तं भक्षा इंद्रवाय्वोः प्रथमोऽथ मित्रावरुणयोरथाश्विनो 8 स एष इंद्रतुरीयो ग्रहो गृह्यते यद्यैंद्रवायवः । (*tau sahaiveṃdravāyū udajayatāṃ saha mitrāvaruṇau sahāśvin śa eṣāmete yathojji taṃ bhakṣā iṃdravāyvoḥ prathamo 'tha mitrāvaruṇayorathāśvino 8 sa eṣa iṃdraturīyo graho gṛhyate yadyaiṃdravāyavaḥ |*). In this way Indra and Vāyu, helping each other, won the contest and first reached the appointed place. Behind them Mitra and Varuṇa came and arrived. Behind them the Aśvins came. Therefore, among these gods, in the order of the places they obtained in the contest, they became entitled to drink Soma. That is, an arrangement was made that first Indra and Vāyu, then Mitra and Varuṇa, and after them the Aśvins should drink Soma. In this way the order of the cup of two deities (the order in which two deities together drink Soma) came into use. Therefore in the Aindravāyava cup only a fourth part of the Soma-drinking is assigned to Indra. **NOTE**

तदेतदृषिः षश्यन्नभ्यनूवाच नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिरिति (*tadetadṛṣiḥ ṣaśyannabhyanūvāca niyutvā iṃdrasārathiriti*). The seer, knowing by divine sight that in the Aindravāyava cup Indra has one part in four, expressed this matter in the following Ṛk, that is, in the Ṛk शतेना नो अभिष्टिभिर्नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिः (*śatenā no abhiṣṭibhirniyutvā iṃdrasārathiḥ*) (Ṛ. Sa 4-46-2) by the sentence नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिः (*niyutvā iṃdrasārathiḥ*). **NOTE** Here, according to the Nirukta statement नियुतो वायोः (*niyuto vāyoḥ*) (Ni. 2-28), the horses called नियुत (*niyuta*) are well known as the vehicle of the god Vāyu.

### Printed p. 570

Therefore the word नियुत्वच्छब्द (*niyutvacchabda*) indicates a connection with Vāyu. In the Ṛk above the word नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*) indicates Indra together with Vāyu. Mantras such as अधा वायुं नियुतः सश्चतस्वाः (*adhā vāyuṃ niyutaḥ saścatasvāḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 2-8-1-1) support this. The meaning of the word इंद्रसारथिः (*iṃdrasārathiḥ*) is: Indra, who is the charioteer of Vāyu. Since Indra stands in the place of charioteer to Vāyu, this indicates that Indra has only a fourth part in the first drinking of Soma.

तस्माद्वाप्येतर्हि भरताः सत्वनां नित्तिं प्रयंति तुरीये हैव संग्रहितारो वदंतेऽमुनैवानूकाशेन यदद इंद्रः सारथिरिव भूत्वो दजयत् । (*tasmādvāpyetarhi bharatāḥ satvanāṃ nittiṃ prayaṃti turīye haiva saṃgrahitāro vadaṃte 'munaivānūkāśena yadada iṃdraḥ sārathiriva bhūtvo dajayat |*) (I. Cā. 9-25). **NOTE** The matter stated above is made clear by an example from worldly practice. Warriors in battle sit in chariots and, with the help of their charioteer, win in the battle and seize the wealth and other possessions of the enemies. When they seize them in this way, they give one part of that wealth and so on, that is, one part in four, to the charioteers who helped them. This custom is current in the world. In the same way, in this contest arranged by the gods Indra acted as charioteer to Vāyu and, since Vāyu was the victor, a fourth part of the first Soma-drinking won in the contest became Indra's share. The main meaning is that Indra gained his fourth part as charioteer to Vāyu.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वाय॒वा या॑हि वी॒तये॑ जुषा॒णो ह॒व्यदा॑तये ।  
> पिबा॑ सु॒तस्यांध॑सो अ॒भि प्रयः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नायो इति । आ । याहि । नीतये । जुषाणः । हव्यदातये ।  
> पिब । सुतस्य । अंधसः । अभि । प्रयः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 571

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वायवा याहीत्येषा पृष्ठस्य तृतीयेऽहनि प्रलुगशस्त्रे वायव्यतृचस्याद्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । वायवा याहि नीतय इत्येका वायो याहि शिवा दिन इति द्वे । आ
> ७-१० । इति ॥
> हे वायो प्रयोऽन्नं सोमाख्यमभि अभिलक्ष्या याहि वीतये भक्षणाय
> जुषाणः प्रीयमाणो हव्यदातये हविर्दात्रे यजमानाय तदर्थं । अगत्य च
> सुतस्यांधसोऽभिशुतमंधोऽन्नं सोमलक्षणं पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk, beginning वायवा याहीत्येषा (*vāyavā yāhītyeṣā*), is the first Ṛk of the tṛca addressed to Vāyu in the Praüga-śastra of the third day of the Pṛṣṭha rite. **NOTE** The sūtra is cited: the Āśvalāyana text (Ā. Sū. 7-10) prescribes वायवा याहि नीतय इत्येका वायो याहि शिवा दिन इति द्वे । (*vāyavā yāhi nītaya ityekā vāyo yāhi śivā dina iti dve |*). Sāyaṇa explains: O Vāyu, come with regard to the food called Soma, for partaking of it, delighting in it, for the sacrificer who offers the oblation, and on his behalf; and drink the pressed Soma, the food.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)—one who bears a mind of favour towards the sacrificer
- वायो (*vāyo*)—O Vāyu
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- प्रयः अभि (*prayaḥ abhi*)—looking to the oblation
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—for its partaking
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—deign to come
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—of the food in the form of Soma
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, who bear a mind of favour towards the sacrificer, deign to come to the sacrificer who offers the oblation, looking to the oblation, for its partaking. Drink the pressed Soma.

##### English translation
Come, Vayu, propitious to the offerer of the libation, to partake of the sacrificial food, and drink of the effused juice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk, वायवा याहि (*vāyavā yāhi*), is to be recited as the first Ṛk of the tṛca (a group of three Ṛks) addressed to Vāyu, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Praüga-śastra on the third day of the sacrifice called Pṛṣṭha. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, वायवा याहि वीतय इत्येका वायो याहि शिवा दिव इति द्वे (*vāyavā yāhi vītaya ityekā vāyo yāhi śivā diva iti dve*) (Ā. Sū. 7-10). For the detailed account we have written on the invitation, in this Ṛk, to Vāyu to be the first of all the gods to drink Soma, see the Special Topics of the preceding Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑श्च वायवेषां सु॒तानां॑ प्री॒तिम॑र्हथः ।  
> ताञ्चु॑षेधामरे॒पसा॑व॒भि प्रयः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । च । वायो इति । एषां । सुतानां । पीतिं । अर्हथः ।  
> तान् । जुषेथां । अरेपसौ । अभि । प्रयः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पृष्ठस्य तृतीयेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्र ऐंद्रवायवतृच इंद्रश्च इत्यादिके द्वे ऋचौ
> शंसेत् । तयोः प्रथमां द्वितीयां नावर्त्य तृच संपादयेत् । तथा च सूत्रितं।
> इंद्रश्च वायवेषां सुतानामिति द्वयोरन्यतरां द्विः । आ. ७-१८ । इति ॥
> हे वायो त्वं चेंद्रश्चैषां पुरतो गृहीतानां सुतानामभिषुतानां
> सोमानां पीतिं पानमर्हथः । यस्मादेवं तस्मात्तान् सोमरसान् जुषेथां
> सेवेथामरेपसावहिंसकौ । तदर्थं प्रयः सोमाख्यमन्नमभिलक्ष्यागच्छतमिति
> शेषः । यद्वा । प्रयोऽन्नरूपान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Praüga-śastra of the third day of the Pṛṣṭha rite, in the Aindra-Vāyava tṛca, the two Ṛks beginning इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*) are to be recited. The tṛca is to be completed by repeating one of the two, the first or the second. **NOTE** The sūtra is cited accordingly (Ā. Sū. 7-18). **NOTE** Sāyaṇa explains: O Vāyu, you and Indra are worthy of drinking these pressed Soma juices, those taken in the first place. Since this is so, enjoy and partake of those Soma juices, being free from harm to others. For that purpose come, looking to the food called Soma; the words "come" are to be supplied. Or else the food-like Soma juices are the object of "enjoy".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वायो (*vāyo*)—O Vāyu, you
- इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*)—and Indra as well
- सुतानां (*sutānāṃ*)—of the pressed
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these Soma juices
- पीतिं (*pītiṃ*)—for the drinking
- अर्हथः (*arhathaḥ*)—you are worthy
- अरेपसौ (*arepasau*)—being free from harm
- तान् (*tān*)—these juices
- जुषेथां (*juṣethāṃ*)—partake of
- प्रयः अभि (*prayaḥ abhi*)—come looking to the food in the form of juice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, you and Indra as well are worthy of drinking these Soma juices that have been pressed and prepared. Being free from harm, partake of these juices. For that very reason, come looking to this food in the form of juice.

##### English translation
Indra and Vayu, you ought to drink of these libations: be gratified by them, benevolent (divinities), and partake of the sacrificial food.

### Printed p. 573

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the third day of the sacrifice called Pṛṣṭha, for the Aindra-Vāyava tṛca among the mantras of the Praüga-śastra, this Ṛk इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*) and the Ṛk that follows it, सुता इंद्राय (*sutā iṃdrāya*), are to be recited. That is, of these two Ṛks, either the first or the second is to be taken again as the third and the tṛca (a tṛca is three Ṛks) is recited. This matter is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra on repeating one of the two Ṛks (Ā. Sū. 7-10).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अभिषुताः । संपादिताः । ते च निम्मं गर्तं सिंधवो न नद्य इव हे इंद्रवायू
> युवामभि यंति प्रयोऽन्नरूपाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For Indra and for Vāyu the Soma juices mixed with curds have been pressed and prepared. O Indra and Vāyu, like rivers to a hollow place, these food-like juices flow towards you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- वायवे च (*vāyave ca*)—and for Vāyu as well
- दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*)—mixed with curds
- सोमासः (*somāsaḥ*)—the Soma juices
- सुताः (*sutāḥ*)—have been prepared (O Indra and Vāyu)
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—rivers
- निम्मं न (*nimmaṃ na*)—as they flow swiftly in low-lying places
- प्रयः (*prayaḥ*)—this food in the form of juice
- अभि यंति (*abhi yaṃti*)—come hastily towards you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For Indra and Vāyu, Soma juices mixed with curds have been prepared. O Indra and Vāyu, as rivers flow swiftly in low-lying places, these Soma juices flow swiftly and come towards you.

### Printed p. 574

##### English translation
The Soma juices mixed with curds are poured out to Indra and to Vayu : the sacrificial viands proceed to you as rivers flow downwards.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*)—Soma juice mixed with curds. The Soma juice pressed from the Soma plant is well strained and drunk. This kind of Soma is called pure and sharp. To enhance the taste of the Soma juice it is also drunk after mixing milk, curds or barley flour into the juice. The things mixed into the juice, such as milk, are called आशिर (*āśira*) substances. Therefore it is the custom to speak of Soma juice mixed with milk by one name, Soma juice mixed with curds by another (the one used here), and Soma juice mixed with barley flour by yet another. In the present Ṛk Indra and Vāyu are prayed to drink the Soma juice mixed with curds.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒जूर्विश्वे॑भिर्दे॒वेभि॑र॒श्वभ्या॑मु॒षसा॑ स॒जूः ।  
> आ या॑ह्यग्ने अत्रि॒वत्सु॒ते र॑ण ॥८॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सजूः । विश्वेभिः । देवेभिः । अश्विभ्यां । उषसा । सजूः ।  
> आ । याहि । अग्ने । अत्रिवत् । सुते । रण ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तृतीयेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्रे सजूर्विश्वेभिरिति वैश्वदेवस्त्रृचः । सूत्रितं च ।
> सजूर्विश्वेभिर्देवेभिरुत नः प्रिया प्रियासु । आ ७-१० । इति ॥
> हे अग्ने विश्वेभिः सर्वैर्देवेभिर्देवैः सजूः संगतः सन् अश्विभ्यामुषसा च
> सजूः समानप्रीतिः सन् आ याहि । आगहि । अत्रिवदत्रिरिव । अत्रेय्यज्ञे यथा
> तथेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । अत्रियथा यज्ञे रमते तद्वत्सुतेऽभिषुते सोमे रण ।
> रमस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Praüga-śastra of the third day, the tṛca beginning सजूर्विश्वेभिरिति (*sajūrviśvebhiriti*) is the one addressed to the Viśvedevas; the sūtra is cited (Ā. Sū. 7-10). Sāyaṇa explains: O Agni, come, united with all the gods, and in equal love with the Aśvins and Uṣas. Like Atri: just as Atri delights in the sacrifice, so delight in the pressed Soma. Or else, as Atri rejoices in the sacrifice, so likewise rejoice in the pressed Soma.

### Printed p. 575

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*)—with all
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—the gods
- सजूः (*sajūḥ*)—united
- अश्विभ्यां (*aśvibhyāṃ*)—with the Aśvin gods
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with the goddess Uṣas
- सजूः (*sajūḥ*)—joined in equal love
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—deign to come
- अत्रिवत् (*atrivat*)—like Atri
- सुते (*sute*)—with this prepared juice
- रण (*raṇa*)—take delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, united with all the gods, with the Aśvin gods and with the goddess Uṣas, joined in equal love, deign to come. With this prepared juice take delight, like Atri.

##### English translation
Accompanied by all the gods, accompanied by the Aswins, and by Ushas, come, Agni, and, like Atri, delight in the libation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the third day of the sacrifice, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Praüga-śastra, the tṛca beginning सजूर्विश्वेभिः (*sajūrviśvebhiḥ*) (the 8th, 9th and 10th Ṛks of this sūkta) is a tṛca to be recited addressed to the Viśvedevas. This matter is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra on this tṛca (Ā. Sū. 7-10).

सजूः (*sajūḥ*)—For this word Yāska has given the etymology सजूः सहजोषण (*sajūḥ sahajoṣaṇa*) (Ni. 9-15), समानप्रीतिः (*samānaprītiḥ*), "one having equal love"; that is, the sense is: accompanied by the deity who is with him, with mutual love (friendship) and co-operation. In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to come to the place of sacrifice together with the Viśvedevas, the Aśvin gods and the goddess Uṣas.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒जूर्मि॒त्रावरु॑णाभ्यां स॒जूः सोमे॑न॒ विष्णु॑ना ।  
> आ या॑ह्यग्ने अत्रि॒वत्सु॒ते र॑ण ॥९॥

### Printed p. 576

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सजूः । मित्रावरुणाभ्यां । सजूः । सोमेन । विष्णुना ।  
> आ । याहि । अग्ने । अत्रिवत् । सुते । रण ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वे नवमीदशम्या स्पष्टे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ninth and the tenth, two Ṛks, are clear.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- मित्रावरुणाभ्यां (*mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ*)—with Mitra and Varuṇa
- सजूः (*sajūḥ*)—united
- सोमेन (*somena*)—with Soma
- विष्णुना (*viṣṇunā*)—with Viṣṇu
- सजूः (*sajūḥ*)—united
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—deign to come to this sacrifice
- सुते (*sute*)—with this prepared juice
- अत्रिवत् (*atrivat*)—like Atri
- रण (*raṇa*)—take delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, united with Mitra and Varuṇa, with Soma and with Viṣṇu, deign to come to this sacrifice. With this prepared juice take delight, like Atri.

##### English translation
Accompanied by Mitra and Varuna, accompanied by Soma and Vishnu, come, Agni, and like Atri, delight in the libation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to come to the place of sacrifice together with the deities Mitra and Varuṇa, the Soma deity, and Viṣṇu. The latter half of the preceding Ṛk is recited again in this Ṛk and in the next Ṛk. Saying that the meaning is clear, the bhāṣya-writer has not written a bhāṣya for this Ṛk and for the next Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒जूरा॑दि॒त्यैर्वसु॑भिः स॒जूरिंद्रे॑ण वा॒युना॑ ।  
> आ या॑ह्यग्ने अत्रि॒वत्सु॒ते र॑ण ॥१०॥
