> निरालंबे मार्गे राक्षसादिभिरनुपद्रुतौ संचरतस्तद्वत् । किंच वयं प्रवसंतः
> पुनर्ददताभिमतमघ्नता चरकालविलंबकोपेनाहिंसता जानताविस्मरता मदीयश्शिरकालं गतः कोऽयमिति संदेहमकुर्वता। मदीयोऽयमिति बुध्यमानेनेत्यर्थः।
> उक्तलक्षणेन बंधुजनेन सं गमेमहि । यद्वा । पूर्वार्ध० प्रवसतां वाक्यमुत्तरार्ध० बंधूनां । वयं बंधवो ददताभिमतमुपार्जितं यच्छताघ्नता
> प्रयामकोपेनाहिंसता जानता सस्नेहमधिगच्छता प्रवसता सं गमेमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May we travel along the path in welfare, that is, in safety, like the sun and the moon: just as those two travel on a supportless course, unharmed by rākṣasas and the like, so may we. Further, we who are living abroad: पुनर्ददता (*punardadatā*) means one who gives back what is desired; अघ्नता (*aghnatā*) means one who does not harm through anger at our long delay; जानता (*jānatā*) means one who does not forget, who does not doubt "who is this who has been gone for a long time?" but understands "this one is mine". May we meet such kinsfolk, as described. Or else: the first half is the speech of those who live abroad, the second half that of the kinsfolk. We, the kinsfolk, may meet the one who lives abroad, who gives what he has earned and desired, who does not harm through anger at his departure, who knows us and approaches us with affection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर‍्याचंद्रमसौ इव (*sūryācaṃdramasau iva*)—as the moon and the sun follow their own paths eternally
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we too
- पंथां (*paṃthāṃ*)—our path of conducting the sacrifice
- स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—without obstacle
- अनु चरेम (*anu carema*)—may we follow
- पुनर्ददता (*punardadatā*)—who return a benefit for our benefit
- अघ्नता (*aghnatā*)—who do not harm
- जानता (*jānatā*)—who know well our kinship; with such kinsfolk
- सं गमेमहि (*saṃ gamemahi*)—may we be united

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the moon and the sun follow their own paths eternally, so may we too follow our path of conducting the sacrifice without obstacle. May we be united with kinsfolk who return a benefit for our benefit and who know well our kinship.

### Printed p. 591

##### English translation
May we ever follow prosperously our path, like the sun and the moon: may we be associated with a requiting, grateful, and recognisant (kinsman).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In addition to the meaning stated above, the commentator says that the phrase पथां स्वस्ति अनुचरेम (*pathāṃ svasti anucarema*) may also be given the meaning: may we travel without obstacle and in safety together with the travellers whom we may meet in the middle of the road at the time of the journey.

## Sūkta 52 (Maṇḍala 5)

The fifty-second sūkta.

For the ten sūktas of this maṇḍala from 52 to 61, one called Śyāvāśva is the seer. The deity of all these ten sūktas is the Maruts. First the introduction of the seer Śyāvāśva will be given, and afterwards the matter of the Marut deities will be explained. Sāyaṇa has given some particulars concerning the seer Śyāvāśva in his bhāṣya on the sixty-first sūkta. They will be stated later when that sūkta is explained. Now we shall explain what is said about the seer Śyāvāśva in the work called the Bṛhaddevatā.

राजर्षिरभवद्धार्भ्यो रथवीतिरिति श्रुतः । स यक्षमाणो राजात्रिमभिगम्य प्रसाद्य च ॥ आत्मानं कारमर्थं च ख्यापयन्प्रांजलिः स्थितः । अवृणीतर्षिमात्रेयमार्त्विज्यायार्चनानसु ॥ स सपुत्रोऽभ्यगच्छत्तं राजानं यज्ञसिद्धये । श्यावाश्वस्यात्रिपुत्रस्य पुत्रः खल्वर्चनानसः !! सांगोपांगान्सर्ववेदान् यः पित्राध्यापितो मुदा । अर्चनानाः सपुत्रोऽथ गत्वा नृपमयाजयत् ॥ यज्ञे च विततेऽपश्यद्राजपुत्रीं यशस्विनीं । स्नुषा मे राजपुत्री स्वादिति तस्य मनोऽभवत् ॥ (*rājarṣirabhavaddhārbhyo rathavītiriti śrutaḥ | sa yakṣamāṇo rājātrimabhigamya prasādya ca ‖ ātmānaṃ kāramarthaṃ ca khyāpayanprāṃjaliḥ sthitaḥ | avṛṇītarṣimātreyamārtvijyāyārcanānasu ‖ sa saputro 'bhyagacchattaṃ rājānaṃ yajñasiddhaye | śyāvāśvasyātriputrasya putraḥ khalvarcanānasaḥ !! sāṃgopāṃgānsarvavedān yaḥ pitrādhyāpito mudā | arcanānāḥ saputro 'tha gatvā nṛpamayājayat ‖ yajñe ca vitate 'paśyadrājaputrīṃ yaśasvinīṃ | snuṣā me rājaputrī svāditi tasya mano 'bhavat ‖*)

### Printed p. 592

श्यावाश्वस्य च तस्यां वै सक्तमासीत्तदा मनः । संयुज्यस्व मया राजन्निति याज्यं च सोऽब्रवीत् ॥ श्यावाश्वाय सुतां दित्सुर्महिषीं स्वां नृपोऽब्रवीत् । किं ते मतमहं कन्यां श्यावाश्वाय ददामि हि ॥ अत्रिपुत्रोऽदुर्बलो हि जामाता त्ावयोरिति । राजानमब्रवीत्सापि नृपर्षिकुलजा ह्यहं ॥ नानृषिर्नौ तु जामाता नैष मंत्रान् हि दृष्टवान् । ऋषये दीयतां कन्या वेदस्यांबा भवेत्तथा ॥ ऋषिर्मंत्रदृशं वेदपितरं मन्यते यतः । प्रत्याचष्टे स तं राजा सह संमंत्र भार्यया ॥ अनृषिनैव जामाता कच्चिद्भवितुमर्हति । प्रत्याख्यात ऋषिस्तेन वृत्ते यज्ञे न्यवर्तत ॥ (*śyāvāśvasya ca tasyāṃ vai saktamāsīttadā manaḥ | saṃyujyasva mayā rājanniti yājyaṃ ca so 'bravīt ‖ śyāvāśvāya sutāṃ ditsurmahiṣīṃ svāṃ nṛpo 'bravīt | kiṃ te matamahaṃ kanyāṃ śyāvāśvāya dadāmi hi ‖ atriputro 'durbalo hi jāmātā tāvayoriti | rājānamabravītsāpi nṛparṣikulajā hyahaṃ ‖ nānṛṣirnau tu jāmātā naiṣa maṃtrān hi dṛṣṭavān | ṛṣaye dīyatāṃ kanyā vedasyāṃbā bhavettathā ‖ ṛṣirmaṃtradṛśaṃ vedapitaraṃ manyate yataḥ | pratyācaṣṭe sa taṃ rājā saha saṃmaṃtra bhāryayā ‖ anṛṣinaiva jāmātā kaccidbhavitumarhati | pratyākhyāta ṛṣistena vṛtte yajñe nyavartata ‖*)

श्वावाश्वस्य तु कन्याया मनो नैव न्यवर्तत । ततस्तौ तु निवर्तेतामुभावेवाभिजग्मतुः ॥ शशीयसीं तरंतं च पुरुमीळं च पार्थिवं । तरंतपुरुमीळौ तु राजानौ वैददश्वृषी ॥ ताभ्यां तौ चक्रतुः पूजां ऋषिभ्यां नृपती स्वयं । ऋषिपुत्रं महिष्याश्च दर्शयामास तं नृपः ॥ अजाविकं गवाश्वं च श्यावाश्वाय शशीयसी । अश्रिं याज्यार्चितौ गत्वा पितापूत्रौ स्वमाश्रमं ॥ अभ्यवादयतामत्रिं महर्षिं दीप्ततेजसं । (*śvāvāśvasya tu kanyāyā mano naiva nyavartata | tatastau tu nivartetāmubhāvevābhijagmatuḥ ‖ śaśīyasīṃ taraṃtaṃ ca purumīḷaṃ ca pārthivaṃ | taraṃtapurumīḷau tu rājānau vaidadaśvṛṣī ‖ tābhyāṃ tau cakratuḥ pūjāṃ ṛṣibhyāṃ nṛpatī svayaṃ | ṛṣiputraṃ mahiṣyāśca darśayāmāsa taṃ nṛpaḥ ‖ ajāvikaṃ gavāśvaṃ ca śyāvāśvāya śaśīyasī | aśriṃ yājyārcitau gatvā pitāpūtrau svamāśramaṃ ‖ abhyavādayatāmatriṃ maharṣiṃ dīptatejasaṃ |*)

श्वावाश्वस्य वनस्यासीन्मंत्रस्यादर्शनादहं ॥ न लब्धवानहं कन्यां हंत सर्वांगशोभनां । अप्यहं मंत्रदर्शि स्यां भवेद्धर्षो महान्मनु । इत्यरण्य चिंतयतः प्रादुरासीन्मरुद्दणः । ददर्श संस्थिन्नार्श्वे तुल्यरूपानिवात्मनः ॥ समानवयसश्चैन मरुतो रुक्मवक्षसः । तांस्तुल्यवयसो दृष्ट्वा देवान्पुरुषनिग्रहान् ॥ (*śvāvāśvasya vanasyāsīnmaṃtrasyādarśanādahaṃ ‖ na labdhavānahaṃ kanyāṃ haṃta sarvāṃgaśobhanāṃ | apyahaṃ maṃtradarśi syāṃ bhaveddharṣo mahānmanu | ityaraṇya ciṃtayataḥ prādurāsīnmaruddaṇaḥ | dadarśa saṃsthinnārśve tulyarūpānivātmanaḥ ‖ samānavayasaścaina maruto rukmavakṣasaḥ | tāṃstulyavayaso dṛṣṭvā devānpuruṣanigrahān ‖*)

### Printed p. 593

श्यावाश्वो विस्मितोऽपृच्छत्के स्थेति मरुतस्तदा । ततस्तु मरुतो देवान् रुद्रसूनूनबुध्यत ॥ य ईं वहंत इत्याभिर्बुद्ध्वा तुष्टाव तांस्तथा । अतिक्रमं हि तं मेने ऋषिर्विपुलमात्मनः ॥ रथनीतेर्दुहितरमगच्छन्मनसा तदा । स सद्म ऋषिरात्मानं प्रवक्ष्यन् रथवीतये ॥ आदाय कन्यां तां दार्भ्य उपेयायार्चनानसं । पादौ तस्योपसंगृह्य स्थित्वा प्रह्वः कृतांजलिः ॥ (*śyāvāśvo vismito 'pṛcchatke stheti marutastadā | tatastu maruto devān rudrasūnūnabudhyata ‖ ya īṃ vahaṃta ityābhirbuddhvā tuṣṭāva tāṃstathā | atikramaṃ hi taṃ mene ṛṣirvipulamātmanaḥ ‖ rathanīterduhitaramagacchanmanasā tadā | sa sadma ṛṣirātmānaṃ pravakṣyan rathavītaye ‖ ādāya kanyāṃ tāṃ dārbhya upeyāyārcanānasaṃ | pādau tasyopasaṃgṛhya sthitvā prahvaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ ‖*)

रथनीतिरहं दार्भ्य इति नाम शशंस च । मया संगतिमिच्छंतं त्वां प्रत्याचक्षि यत्पुरा ॥ तत् क्षमस्व नमस्तेऽस्तु मा च मे भगवन्नृधः । ऋषेः पुत्रः स्वयमृषिः पितासि भगवन्नृषेः ॥ हंत प्रतिगृहाणेमां स्नुषामित्येवमब्रवीत् । पाद्यार्यम्यमधुपर्कैश्च पूजयित्वा स्वयं नृपः ॥ शुक्लमश्वशतं दत्वा अनुजज्ञॆ गृहान्नृति । शशीयसीं तरंतं च पुरुमीळं च पार्थिवं ॥ षड्भिः सनदिति स्तुत्वा जगामर्षिरपि क्षयं । (*rathanītirahaṃ dārbhya iti nāma śaśaṃsa ca | mayā saṃgatimicchaṃtaṃ tvāṃ pratyācakṣi yatpurā ‖ tat kṣamasva namaste 'stu mā ca me bhagavannṛdhaḥ | ṛṣeḥ putraḥ svayamṛṣiḥ pitāsi bhagavannṛṣeḥ ‖ haṃta pratigṛhāṇemāṃ snuṣāmityevamabravīt | pādyāryamyamadhuparkaiśca pūjayitvā svayaṃ nṛpaḥ ‖ śuklamaśvaśataṃ datvā anujajñè gṛhānnṛti | śaśīyasīṃ taraṃtaṃ ca purumīḷaṃ ca pārthivaṃ ‖ ṣaḍbhiḥ sanaditi stutvā jagāmarṣirapi kṣayaṃ |*)

(Bṛ. De. 5-50 to 80)

The royal seer called Rathavīti Dārbhya, intending to perform a sacrifice, went to the seer Atri, worshipped him, and requested that Atri's son Arcanānas accept the office of priest at his sacrifice and help him to perform the sacrifice. Arcanānas agreed to this and went with his son Śyāvāśva to the king's house for the sacrificial work, and carried out the sacrifice. At the time of the sacrifice Arcanānas saw the king's daughter and, attracted, wished that she be married to Śyāvāśva. Śyāvāśva too became infatuated with her. Then the father and the son made their wish known to the king; he too consented to that connection and said that he would give his answer after asking his wife, but his wife did not consent. She made it known that Śyāvāśva was not a seer, and that they did not agree to give their daughter, born in a line of seers, to one who was not a seer. In the same way the king too gave the answer to both father and son, and after that they returned to their own town. But Śyāvāśva alone remained with his mind fixed on the king's daughter. On the way back they met Śaśīyasa

### Printed p. 594

and Taranta, and the king Purumīḷha. Taranta and Purumīḷha were both sons of the king Vidadaśva and were themselves seers. Both of them saluted the visiting father and son, honoured them and worshipped them. Then the women of the inner apartments also honoured them with gifts such as cows and horses. Śyāvāśva alone, grieving that he had not obtained a beautiful wife, was wandering in the forest when he met the host of the Maruts. Then, understanding that they were the Maruts, sons of Rudra and of divine portion, he praised them. He became the seer of the sūkta के ष्ठा नरः (*ke ṣṭhā naraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-6-1) **NOTE**. Learning of this, Rathavīti, the son of Darbha, brought his daughter and prayed that he be forgiven for having earlier refused to give his daughter, and that, since Śyāvāśva was now a seer and so fit to accept his daughter, he should accept her. When Śyāvāśva and his father agreed to this, he then gave the maiden in marriage, preceded by the offering of arghya, pādya and the like. Then Śyāvāśva, in gratitude to Purumīḷha and the others for the help they had given him, saluted them and composed six Ṛks praising them. Among them,

उत मेऽरपद्युवतिर्ममंदुषी प्रति श्यावाय वर्तनिं । वि रोहिता पुरुमीळ्याय येमतुर्विप्राय दीर्घयशसे ॥ (*uta me 'rapadyuvatirmamaṃduṣī prati śyāvāya vartaniṃ | vi rohitā purumīḷyāya yematurviprāya dīrghayaśase ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-61-9)

this Ṛk is one that praises Purumīḷha.

युवां गोतमः पुरुमीळ्हो अत्रिर्दस्रा हवतेवसे हविष्मान् । दिशं न दिष्टामृजूयेव यंता मे हवं नासत्योप यातं ॥ (*yuvāṃ gotamaḥ purumīḷho atrirdasrā havatevase haviṣmān | diśaṃ na diṣṭāmṛjūyeva yaṃtā me havaṃ nāsatyopa yātaṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-183-5)

in this Ṛk it is stated that Purumīḷha praised the Aśvin deities and obtained their protection.

Introduction to the Marut deities

In the Ṛgveda it is customary to call the Marut deities sons of Rudra. On how they came to be sons of Rudra, Sāyaṇa has explained as follows—

रुद्रो यद्वो मरुतो रुक्मवक्षसो वृषाजनि पृश्न्याः शुक्र ऊधनि । (*rudro yadvo maruto rukmavakṣaso vṛṣājani pṛśnyāḥ śukra ūdhani |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-33-2)

As said in this Ṛk, there is a well-known story that the Maruts were born as sons of Rudra in Pṛśni; therefore this epithet is used most often whenever they are addressed. In explaining this Ṛk, Sāyaṇācārya tells yet another story.

### Printed p. 595

पृश्निर्नानावर्णा इयं भूमिः पुरा गोरूपधरासीत् । तस्यां महेशो वृषो भूत्वा मरुत उत्पादयामासेत्याचक्षते । (*pṛśnirnānāvarṇā iyaṃ bhūmiḥ purā gorūpadharāsīt | tasyāṃ maheśo vṛṣo bhūtvā maruta utpādayāmāsetyācakṣate |*)

(Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Mu. Saṃ. 2-34-2) **NOTE**

By saying that there is a story that when the earth, which has various colours, formerly assumed the form of a cow, Maheśa became a bull and produced the Maruts, Sāyaṇa has indicated the father-and-son relation of Rudra and the Maruts. And since the story told in the Ṛk 2-34-2 above is told also in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, he has cited the sentence from there as well.

पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः । (*pṛśniyai vai payaso maruto jātāḥ |*)

(Śai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-4) **NOTE**

For this very reason the Maruts are addressed as sons of Rudra in many places. For example—

प्र ये शुंभंते जनयो न सप्तयो यामनुद्रस्य सूनवः सुदंससः । (*pra ye śuṃbhaṃte janayo na saptayo yāmanudrasya sūnavaḥ sudaṃsasaḥ |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.85-1)

इदं पित्रे मरुतामुच्यते वचः स्वादोः स्वादीयो रुद्राय वर्धनं । रास्वा च नो अमृत मर्तभोजनं त्मने शोकाय तनयाय मृळ । (*idaṃ pitre marutāmucyate vacaḥ svādoḥ svādīyo rudrāya vardhanaṃ | rāsvā ca no amṛta martabhojanaṃ tmane śokāya tanayāya mṛḷa |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-6)

In these Ṛks, and likewise in 1-168-9, 2-33-1 and many other places, the epithet "sons of Rudra" is applied to the Maruts. In explaining the Ṛk 1-114-6 cited above, Sāyaṇa has told another story.

रुद्रस्य च मरुतां पितृत्वमेवमाख्यायते । पुरा कदाचिदिंद्रोऽसुरान् जिगाय । तदानीं दितिरसुरमाता इंद्रहननसमर्थं पुत्रं कामयमाना तपसा भर्तुः सकाशाद्गर्भं लेभे। इमं वृत्तांतमवगच्छन्निंद्रो वज्रहस्तः सन् सूक्ष्मरूपो भूत्वा तस्या उदरं प्रविश्य तं गर्भं सप्तधा बिभेद । पुनरप्येकैकं सप्तखंडमकरोत् । ते सर्वे गर्भैकदेशायोनेनिर्गत्य अरुदन् । एतस्मिनवसरे लीलार्थं गच्छंतौ पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ इमान् ददृशतुः । महेशं प्रति पार्वती एवमवोचत् । इमे मांसखंडा यथा प्रत्येकं पुत्राः संपद्यतामेवं त्वया कार्यं मयिचेत्प्रीतिरस्तीति। स च महेश्वरस्तान् समानरूपान् समानवयसः समानालंकारान् पुत्रान् कृत्वा गौरै प्रददौ तवेमे पुत्राः संत्विति । अतः सर्वेषु मारु- (*rudrasya ca marutāṃ pitṛtvamevamākhyāyate | purā kadācidiṃdro 'surān jigāya | tadānīṃ ditirasuramātā iṃdrahananasamarthaṃ putraṃ kāmayamānā tapasā bhartuḥ sakāśādgarbhaṃ lebhe| imaṃ vṛttāṃtamavagacchanniṃdro vajrahastaḥ san sūkṣmarūpo bhūtvā tasyā udaraṃ praviśya taṃ garbhaṃ saptadhā bibheda | punarapyekaikaṃ saptakhaṃḍamakarot | te sarve garbhaikadeśāyonenirgatya arudan | etasminavasare līlārthaṃ gacchaṃtau pārvatīparameśvarau imān dadṛśatuḥ | maheśaṃ prati pārvatī evamavocat | ime māṃsakhaṃḍā yathā pratyekaṃ putrāḥ saṃpadyatāmevaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ mayicetprītirastīti| sa ca maheśvarastān samānarūpān samānavayasaḥ samānālaṃkārān putrān kṛtvā gaurai pradadau taveme putrāḥ saṃtviti | ataḥ sarveṣu māru-*)

### Printed p. 596

तेषु सूक्तेषु मरुतो रुद्रपुत्रा इति स्तूयंते । रौद्रेषु च मरुतां पिता रुद्र इति । (*teṣu sūkteṣu maruto rudraputrā iti stūyaṃte | raudreṣu ca marutāṃ pitā rudra iti |*)

(Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Mu. Saṃ. 1-114-6)

Formerly, on one occasion, Indra conquered the Asuras. Then Diti, the mother of the Asuras, desiring a son capable of killing Indra, performed austerities and by the grace of her husband conceived a womb. Indra learnt of this, took his thunderbolt in hand, came in a subtle form, entered her belly and split that embryo into seven parts. Again he made each of them into seven pieces. Then all of them came out and were weeping. Then, as Pārvatī and Parameśvara were wandering for pleasure, they saw them, and Pārvatī, moved to pity, begged Maheśvara to change all of them into children. Then Īśvara made all of them of one form, of one age and with the same ornaments, and gave them to Gaurī as sons, saying, "Let these be your sons." Sāyaṇa has told this story to explain that, therefore, in all the Marut sūktas the Maruts are called sons of Rudra, and in the Rudra sūktas Rudra is called the father of the Maruts.

The companionship of Indra and the Maruts

The eternal companionship of Indra and the Maruts is well known from the Śruti. The relation of king and subjects between Indra and the Maruts, the offering of oblations in the chief sacrificial rites to Indra accompanied by the Maruts, and the help that the Maruts give to Indra when he fights with the demon Vṛtra are praised in many places in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa tells an ancient story of how Indra joined the Maruts and stood apart from the other gods.

आतिथ्येन वै देवा इष्ट्वा । तान्त्समदविंदत्ते चतुर्धा व्यद्रवन्नन्योन्यस्य श्रियातिष्ठमाना अग्निर्वसुभिः, सोमो रुद्रैर्वरुण आदित्यैरिंद्रो मरुद्धिर्भृहस्पतिर्विश्वेदेवैः । (*ātithyena vai devā iṣṭvā | tāntsamadaviṃdatte caturdhā vyadravannanyonyasya śriyātiṣṭhamānā agnirvasubhiḥ, somo rudrairvaruṇa ādityairiṃdro maruddhirbhṛhaspatirviśvedevaiḥ |*)

(Ka. Brā. 3-4-2-1) **NOTE**

Formerly, when the gods performed the hospitality rite, ill feeling arose among them and, not wishing to be defeated by one another, they formed four groups and separated. Agni joined with the Vasus, Soma with the Rudras, Varuṇa with the Ādityas, Indra with the Maruts, and Bṛhaspati with the Viśvedevas, and each formed a separate group. In this story it is told that Indra

### Printed p. 597

developed companionship with the Maruts and kept a close relation with them. Besides this, it is said in many places that Indra is the king and the Maruts the subjects. For example—

क्षत्रं ना इंद्रो विशो मरुतो विशा वै क्षत्रियो बलवान् भवति । (*kṣatraṃ nā iṃdro viśo maruto viśā vai kṣatriyo balavān bhavati |*)

(Śa. Brā. 4-3-3-6)

Indra is the king, possessed of the splendour of the warrior class, and the Maruts are the subjects. It is indicated that by the co-operation of the subjects the king becomes powerful, and that by the help of the Maruts Indra's valour increased. Because of this close relation and companionship, the Śrutis also show the practice of offering oblations addressed to Indra and the Maruts together.

अनवद्यैरभिद्युभिर्मखः सहस्वदर्चति । गणैरिंद्रस्य काम्यैः ॥ (*anavadyairabhidyubhirmakhaḥ sahasvadarcati | gaṇairiṃdrasya kāmyaiḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-6-8)

मंद्राः सुजिह्वाः स्वरितार आसभिः संमिश्ला इंद्रे मरुतः परिष्टुभः । (*maṃdrāḥ sujihvāḥ svaritāra āsabhiḥ saṃmiślā iṃdre marutaḥ pariṣṭubhaḥ |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-166-11)

स नो मरुद्विर्वृषभ श्रवो धा उग्र उग्रेभिः स्थविरः सहोदाः । (*sa no marudvirvṛṣabha śravo dhā ugra ugrebhiḥ sthaviraḥ sahodāḥ |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-5)

By these and similar Ṛks Indra and the Maruts are invited together and oblations are offered to them together. Because of this companionship, here too the epithet Marutvān is found. In all contexts where Indra accompanied by the Maruts is meant he is called Marutvān; this is how the Bṛhaddevatā explains this epithet that indicates the relation of these deities.

मरुद्भिः सह यत्रेंद्रो मरुत्वांस्तत्र सोऽभवत् । (*marudbhiḥ saha yatreṃdro marutvāṃstatra so 'bhavat |*)

(Bṛ Ve. 4.56) **NOTE**

Further account of the Marut deities

In the Purāṇas and other works, and in modern literature, no special difference is found in the meaning of the words मरुत् (*marut*) and वायु (*vāyu*). The practice is to take these words as meaning wind or the wind-god. But in the Ṛgveda there is much difference between the two words, in meaning and in use. Vāyu or Vāta means the wind pervading the atmosphere or the sky, or the wind-god. The use as wind-god is more common than the sense of wind. And whenever this god is praised, the singular is used. But the Marut deities are always spoken of in the plural. Besides, between Vāyu

### Printed p. 598

and the Maruts there is also much difference in their characteristics. There is no special description of the qualities of Vāyu. Because Vāyu dwells in the atmosphere, he is known as a deity of the middle region. Since the Maruts are many, it is the custom to call them a troop of gods. In general it is the custom to speak of them by the words मारुतं शर्धः (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ*) and मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*) or by other words of the same meaning. Like Vāyu, they too are deities of the middle region.

The Maruts are the form of the storm wind that blows with great violence. Before the rain comes at the time of the monsoon showers, or while the rain is pouring, the wind blowing with great violence is a matter of everyone's experience. This violently blowing storm itself is described in the Ṛgveda as the host of the Marut deities. The force of the wind is especially great before the rain falls or while it falls. Therefore there is a special relation between the rain and the Maruts. For that very reason the Maruts are praised with epithets such as उक्षण (*ukṣaṇa*), जलस्य सेक्तारः (*jalasya sektāraḥ*), that is, those who drench everything with water. Moreover, since the rain accompanied by thunder, lightning and thunderbolts and by the violently blowing wind has a relation to Indra, who is of the form of the slayer of Vṛtra and the like, it is said in many places that the Marut deities and Indra have friendship and companionship. Indra strikes with his thunderbolt the clouds that withhold the rain, or Vṛtra, and makes the rain fall. In that rain-making act the Maruts scatter the clouds and make the rain fall, so that they help Indra in the rain-making act. For this reason there is a special kind of friendship between Indra and the Maruts. The epithet Marutvān too came to Indra for this reason.

The derivation of the word मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)

अथातो मध्यस्थाना देवगणाः । तेषां मरुतः प्रथमागाविनो भवंति। मरुतः । मरुतो मितराविणो ना मितरोचिनो ना महद्द्रवंतीति वा ॥ (*athāto madhyasthānā devagaṇāḥ | teṣāṃ marutaḥ prathamāgāvino bhavaṃti| marutaḥ | maruto mitarāviṇo nā mitarocino nā mahaddravaṃtīti vā ‖*)

(Ni. 1-13)

Thus Yāska has given the derivation of the word Marut. Now we shall speak of the troops of gods of the middle region, that is, of those dwelling in the atmosphere. Among these troops the first place belongs to the Maruts. The word Marut is formed from the two roots मि+रु (*mi+ru*). These gods are called Maruts because they make a measured sound, that is, a sound of one kind or of one evenness. Or if the word Marut is formed from the roots मि+रुच् (*mi+ruc*), then it means those who have an even radiance, and if it is formed from the root महत्+द्रु (*mahat+dru*), then it means those who move (blow) greatly (with violence); such is the meaning of the derivation **NOTE**.

### Printed p. 599

These Marut deities have a very important place among the other deities. Thirty-three sūktas entirely, seven together with Indra, and one each with Agni and Pūṣan, thus a total of forty-two sūktas, praise them. Together they are one गण (*gaṇa*) or शर्धरु (*śardharu*) (1-37-1 and so on), and they are used in the plural only. In number they are said to be "thirty of sixty" (8-85.8) **NOTE** or "three of seven" (1-133-6; A. Ve. 13-1-13) **NOTE**. It is said many times that they were born (5-57-5 and so on). They are the sons of Rudra, and their very name is Rudras (1-39-4 and 7 and so on); sometimes they are called Rudriyas (1-38-7; 2.34-10 and so on); they are the children of Pṛśni (2.34-2, 5-52-16, 5-60-5, 6.66-3), and they are called many times पृश्निमातरः (*pṛśnimātaraḥ*) (those who have Pṛśni as mother) (1-23-10 and so on; A. Ve. 5-21-11). The cow called Pṛśni (5-52-16), or a cow in general (8-83-1), is their mother, and they are also called गोमातरः (*gomātaraḥ*) (1-85-3; compare 8-20.8). This cow is probably the cloud of various colours of the storm. Where it is said that cows with great udders come burning (2-34-5), that can be nothing other than the cloud with lightning and thunderbolts at the time of a storm. When they are born of Pṛśni, the Maruts are compared with Agni (6-66-1 to 3). The Maruts were born from the laughter of the lightning (1-23-12; compare 1-38-8). Agni gave them form or obtained them (6.3-8; 1-71-8). Vāyu placed them in the womb of the atmosphere (1-134-4), and they are children of the sky (11-77-2) **NOTE**, and heroes of the sky (वीराः (*vīrāḥ*) 1-64-4; 1.122-1; 5-54-10) or males of the sky (3.54-13; 5-59-6). In one place it is said that the sea is their mother (समुद्र मातरः (*samudra mātaraḥ*)) (10-78-6). In some other places it is said that they are self-born (1-1782: 5-87-2) **NOTE**.

They are brothers, but there is no distinction of elder or younger (5-59-6; 5-60-5), because all of them are of the same age (1-165-1). All of them grew up together (5-56-5, 7-58-1) and are of one mind (8-20-1 and 21). All have one birthplace (5-53-3) and one dwelling place (1-165-1; 7-56-1). They grew up in the sky, on the earth, in heaven (5.55-6) or in the three heavens (5-60-6). In one place (8-83-1 and 2) they are also called dwellers of the mountains. Indrāṇī is a friend to them. They mingle with Indrāṇī (10-86-9) and with Sarasvatī (7-96-2). Their relation is closest with the goddess रोदसी (*rodasī*). She, providing them the means of comfort, stands with them in their chariot (5-56-8) or stands at their side (6-66-6). In all five places where her name occurs she is in the company of the Maruts (compare 1-167-4 and 5). Therefore, like Sūryā for the Aśvins, she is regarded as their bride. For this reason they have the epithet भद्रजानयः (*bhadrajānayaḥ*) (those who have a beautiful

### Printed p. 600

wife) (5-61-4), and the epithet of being compared to bridegrooms (5-60-4). And their being compared to bridegrooms (5-60-4) or to young lovers (10-78-6). The splendour of the Marut deities is mentioned again and again. They are of golden colour, of a brilliance bright like the sun, slightly red like a blazing fire (6 66-2; 7 59-11; 8-7-7); they shine like the flames of a fire (10 78-3). They are of the form of Agni or of the splendour of Agni (10-84-1, 3-26-5); they are compared to Agni in splendour (11 78-2) **NOTE**. They are like Agni (2-34-1) or like a kindled Agni (6-66-2); their very name is Agni (3-26-4); they are of the brilliance of serpents (हिभानवः (*hibhānavaḥ*) 1-172-1). They shine on the mountains (8-7-1). They are स्वभानु (*svabhānu*) (self-luminous, 1-37-2 and so on); this epithet is not said of any other gods. That they are radiant and blazing is said again and again (1-165-12 and so on). They have a special relation to lightning (5-54-2, 3 and 11; 1-64-5). When the Maruts pour out ghee, the lightnings look at the earth and smile (compare 1-168-8, 5.52-6). When the Maruts call the rain, the thunderbolt roars like a cow following her calf (7-56-13). So closely is lightning related to them that of the five places where the word lightning is used in a compound, all except one are together with the word Marut. They hold the thunderbolt in their hands (8-7-25; 5-54 11); the thunderbolt gives them great delight (5-54-3). They have spears in their hands. Here the spear (ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*)) too must be the thunderbolt, because they have the epithet ऋष्टिविद्युत् (*ṛṣṭividyut*) (those who use the thunderbolt as a spear) (1-168-5, 5 52-13). In some other places it is said that their weapon is also an axe made of gold (8-7-22) (1-37-2, 1-88-3; 5.33-4; 5-57-2; 8-20-4). In one place it is said that they bear the thunderbolt weapon. In some places they are called bearers of bow and arrow (5.53-4, 5 57-2; 8-20-4 and 12) and once archers who shoot arrows, but this characteristic is rare in them. They are adorned with ornaments such as garlands (5-53-4). They wear golden girdles (5-55-6); like a wealthy man seeking marriage, they adorn their bodies with golden ornaments (5-60-4). Armlets or anklets are their personal ornament. Adorned with these ornaments they glitter like the star-studded sky or like the drops of rain falling from a cloud. They have spears on their shoulders, anklets on their feet, golden ornaments on their breasts, thunderbolts spitting embers in their hands, and golden helmets on their heads (5 54-11).

The chariots that the Marut deities use shine with lightning (1-88-1; -54-13) **NOTE**; they are made of gold (55-7-1) **NOTE**; the wheels or rims are of gold (1-64-11; 1-58-5). In them

### Printed p. 601

there are weapons (5-57-6). There are water-jars (1-87-2). The horses that draw the chariot are brown (1-88 2; 5 57-4); they have golden hooves (8-7-27) and are swift as thought (1-85-4). These horses are spotted; their personal name is पृषदश्वरॆंदु (*pṛṣadaśvarèṃdu*) (those who have spotted horses). It is also said that mares are yoked to their chariot (1-39-6). It is said that they yoked the wind as a horse to their chariot (5-58-7).

The Maruts are huge like the sky (5-57-4); they have measured heaven and earth (10-77-3). Their greatness is immeasurable (5-58-2); no one can know the limit of their power (1 167-9). They are young (1-64-2; 1-165-2; 5-42-15) and for them there is no old age (1-64-3). They are Asuras, full of energy, mighty, without impurity (1-64-2 and 12) and without dust (6-66-2). They are of terrible form (1 19-4) and of irritable nature (7-56-8); they are terrible (5-56-2 and 3, 7-58-2); they are fearsome like wild beasts (2-34-1 and so on); they are playful like children or calves (1-166-2; 7-56-16; 20-78-6) **NOTE**. They are like swans with dark backs (7-59.7). They are wild boars with tusks of iron (1-88-5); they are like lions (1-64-8).

They make a loud sound (1-169. 7 and so on). That sound is the thunder (1 23-11); it is also the sound of the blowing wind (7.56.3). When they come, it is as if the sky cries out in fear (8-7-26). They make the mountains tremble, and make the earth or the two worlds shake. They break into pieces the mountains or rocks that are the rims of the chariot (1-64 11; 5-52-9). It is when they come accompanied by the wind that they make the mountains tremble (8-7-4). They overturn trees and devour the forests like wild elephants (1-39-5, 1 64-7). The forests, afraid of them, bend down to the ground (5.60.2). Unobstructed like mountains, they throw down the creatures of heaven and earth (1-64-3). All creatures fear them (1-85.8). They move swiftly like a storm (10-78-3). They raise the dust upward in whirls (1-64-12]. They produce wind or the sound of the wind (7-56-3). They come together with the wind (8-7-3, 4 and 17); they make it their horse (5-58-7).

The pouring of rain is the chief of their deeds. Rain is their garment (5-57-4). They rise up from the sea and pour rain (1-38 9). Pouring rain in both the worlds, they blow (1-64-6; 8-7-6). Rain follows them (5-53-10). They bring water and produce rain (5-58-3). With the rain they hide their radiance

### Printed p. 602

(5-59-1). They cover the eye of the Sun with rain (5.59-5). When they pour rain, they produce darkness from the clouds (1-38-9). Moving swiftly with the wind, they scatter hail (8-7-4). They make the jar of the atmosphere (the cloud, 5-53-6; 5-59-8) and the mountain streams pour water (5-59-7). When they rush, water flows (5-58-6). Because of this, a river of the earth has received the name मरुद्वधा (*marudvadhā*) (that which is made to grow by the Maruts, 10-75.5). The sweat of the sons of Rudra became rain (5.58-7). The rain produced by the Maruts is figuratively called milk (1-166 3), ghee (1-85-3; 10-88-4), milk and ghee (1-64-6). They pour the spring (honey) (1-85-11) or drench the earth with honey (5-54-8). Raising water from the sea to the sky, they pour it from there on the earth in the form of rain (A. Ve. 4.27-4) **NOTE**. Lightning and thunder are always present along with the rain they pour. Desiring to pour water, the Maruts rush with violence, roaring (5-54-3). By their power they produce wind, lightning and thunderbolts; milking the heavenly things with the udder, they fill the earth with milk (1-64-5); the spring that is milked by them roars (1-64-6). When water is rained by them, the sky, the red bull, bellows (5.58-6). They cause the horse to pour out water (1-64-6). Favouring the rain of the sky, they make the streams born of the horse flow well (5.83-6). When they join with the horse and produce water, the Maruts become golden in colour (2-34-13). When the clouds sound, the streams echo the sound of the chariot rims of the Maruts (1.168-8). The waters that Indra pours are named मरुत्वती (*marutvatī*) (accompanied by the Maruts) (1-80-4). In the sense of being the causers of rain they have the names पुरुद्रप्पाः (*purudrappāḥ*) (5-57-5) or द्रप्पिनः (*drappinaḥ*) (1-64-2) (those who have many drops of water) and सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*) (those who are well drenched in water). They reduce heat (5.54-1). But they themselves also drive away darkness (7-56-20), produce light (1-86-10) and make a path for the Sun (8-7-8); they have fixed the limit of the wind (5-55-2); they have extended the regions of the earth and the radiant regions of the sky and separated the two worlds (8-83-9 and 11). Perhaps because of the sound heard in the wind, they are called singers (5.52-1: 5-60-8; 5.35.9). They are the singers of the heavenly world (5.57-5). They sing a song (1-19-4; 1-166-7). By singing they made the Sun shine (8-29-10); playing the flute they split the mountain (1-85-10). When Indra slew the serpent, the Maruts sang for him and prepared the Soma juice (5-29-2; 5-30-6). By singing they produced strength in Indra (1-85-2). Their song is chiefly the sound that is heard in the wind (compare 4-22-4); even so

### Printed p. 603

it is regarded as praise (3-14-4). When they are with Indra, they are invoked as priests (5-29-3) and are compared with priests (10-78-1). They were the first to perform the sacrifice (2-36-2); it is they also who purified the fire in the houses of their disciples; those who kindled the fire were the Bhṛgus (10-122-5). Like many other gods they too are said to drink Soma (2-36-2; 8-83-9 to 12 and so on).

Because of the idea that thunder, rain and these are one, by nature they are friends of Indra; as colleagues they have a close relation with him; by their praises and songs (1-165-11 and so on) they increase Indra's strength and power (3-25-9; 6-17-11). In the battle with Vṛtra it is generally the Maruts who are his helpers (8-65.2 and 3; 10-113-3). They help Trita and Indra in the slaying of Vṛtra (8-7-24). They are entreated to sing the sūkta that effects the slaying of Vṛtra (8-78-1 to 3). In the battles that Indra fought with the serpent and with Śambara they helped him (3-47-3 and 4). Only along with the Maruts did Indra obtain light (8-65.4) and the cows (1-6-5) and become the support of the sky (7-47-5). In truth it is with their help that Indra performed all his heroic deeds (the sūktas 1-100, 101 and 165; 10-65). In some cases the Marut deities are more independent than Indra in these heroic deeds. Accompanied by Indra, the Maruts strike Vṛtra (1.23-9). They severed the joints of the demon Vṛtra (8-7-23). They found the cows (2-34-1). Like the other gods, they too have Indra as leader (1-23-8; and so on). They are joined with Indra (10-128-2). They are like sons to Indra (1 100-5). They are called his brothers (1-170-2). Only once or twice is it said that the Maruts abandoned Indra: creating a situation in which he fought alone with the serpent (1.165-6), they left him alone (8-7-31). In a single Ṛk even enmity between Indra and them is mentioned. The Maruts have said to Indra, "O Indra, why do you wish to slay us? Do not slay us in battle" (compare 1-170-2; 1-171.6). In one Brāhmaṇa too (Tai. Brā. 2.7.11-1) it is said that there was a clash between Indra and the Maruts.

When they are not in the company of Indra, violent qualities are seen in the Maruts. In this respect they show the qualities of their father Rudra. They are prayed that the thunderbolt may not trouble their worshippers and that their ill temper may not touch them (7-56-9). Of the arrows and stones that they throw (1-172-2), the thunderbolt (7-57-4), and the thunderbolt weapon that slays cows and men (7-56-13), they are begged to

### Printed p. 604

avert them. Harm may come from them (1-39-8); there is a request that they should not be angry (1-71-1; 7-58-5): they become angry like serpents (1-64-8 and 9). Like Rudra, from them also the Sindhu, the Asikni, the seas and the herbs on the mountains are begged for (8-20-23 to 26); pure, favourable and comfortable healing remedies are with Rudra accompanied by the Maruts (2-33-13). The Maruts give that in the form of rain (5-53-14); therefore "herb" must mean water. Like Agni, they too have the name पावक (*pāvaka*) (purifiers) (7-56-12; and so on).

From the qualities stated above it becomes clear that the Maruts are deities of the storm. Although it is largely correct to take the word मरुत् (*marut*) as meaning wind, all the qualities seen above are not included in it.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र श्यावाश्वेति सप्तदशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । श्यावाश्व
> त्र्यूना श्यावाश्वो मारुतं ह तत्पंक्तिः षष्ठ्यंता चेति । आत्रेयः श्यावाश्व ऋषिः ।
> ह तदिति प्रयोगादिदमादीनि दश सूक्तानि मरुद्देवत्यानि । षष्ठि सप्तदशी च पंक्तौ
> शिष्टाः पंक्त्यंतपरिभाषयानुष्टुभः । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning प्र श्यावाश्वेति (*pra śyāvāśveti*), of seventeen Ṛks, is the eighth sūkta. Here is this Anukramaṇī: त्र्यूना श्यावाश्वो मारुतं ह तत्पंक्तिः षष्ठ्यंता चेति । (*tryūnā śyāvāśvo mārutaṃ ha tatpaṃktiḥ ṣaṣṭhyaṃtā ceti |*). The seer is Śyāvāśva Ātreya. By the expression ह तदिति (*ha taditi*) the ten sūktas beginning with this one have the Maruts as deity. The sixth and the seventeenth Ṛks are Paṅkti; the remaining Ṛks are Anuṣṭubh, by the rule that what follows the Paṅkti is Anuṣṭubh. The application (viniyoga) has been stated.

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning प्र श्यावाश्व (*pra śyāvāśva*) is the eighth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has seventeen Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: प्र श्यावाश्व त्रूना श्वावाश्वो मारुतं ह तत्पंक्तिः षष्ठ्यंता च (*pra śyāvāśva trūnā śvāvāśvo mārutaṃ ha tatpaṃktiḥ ṣaṣṭhyaṃtā ca*). The seer of this sūkta is called Śyāvāśva; the ten sūktas following this one (sūktas 52-61) have the Maruts as deity. The sixth and the seventeenth Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Paṅkti metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Anuṣṭubh metre. The application has been stated before.

- Sūkta 52
- Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 52
- Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 3, Varga 8, 9, 10
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 17
- Seer: Śyāvāśva Ātreya
- Deity: the Maruts
- Metre: Ṛks 1-5, 7-16 Anuṣṭubh; 6, 17 Paṅkti

### Printed p. 605

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र श्या॑वाश्व धृष्णु॒यार्चा॑ म॒रुद्भि॒र्युक्व॑भिः ।  
> ये अ॑द्रो॒घम॑नुष्व॒धं श्रवो॒ मदं॑ति य॒ज्ञियाः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । श्याव्‌अश्व । धृष्ट्णुया । अर्च ! मरुत्भिः । ऋक्वभिः ।  
> ये । अद्रोघं । अनुस्वधं । श्रवः । मदंति । यज्ञियाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे श्यावाश्व एतन्नामक ऋषे धृष्णुया धृष्णुस्त्वमृक्वभिः स्तुत्यान्मरुद्भिर्मरुतः प्रार्च ॥ द्वितीयार्थे तृतीया ॥ एवं स्वयमेव संप्रेष्यति । यद्वा । यजमानो होतारं श्यावाश्वं ब्रूते । यद्वा । मरुद्भिर्मरुत्सदृशैर्युक्वभिः स्तोतृभिः
> सह स्तोत्रैर्वार्च । स्तुहीत्यर्थः । ये मरुतो यज्ञिया यज्ञार्हा अनुष्पधं
> प्रत्यहं । हनिर्लक्षणान्नप्रदानं स्वधा । अनु पश्चाद्वा । अद्रोघमहिंसकं श्रवोऽन्नं
> लब्ध्वा मदंति हृष्यंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śyāvāśva, seer of this name, being bold, worship the Maruts, who are to be praised by ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*); the instrumental stands in the sense of the accusative. Thus he sends himself forth. Or else: the sacrificer says it to the Hotṛ Śyāvāśva. Or else: worship, that is, praise, along with the Maruts, along with praisers like the Maruts, who are ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*), or with hymns. The Maruts who are worthy of sacrifice, अनुष्पधं (*anuṣpadhaṃ*) daily (स्वधा (*svadhā*) is the giving of food in the form of an oblation; or अनु (*anu*) means afterwards), having obtained harmless food, rejoice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्वावाश्व (*śvāvāśva*)—O Śyāvāśva
- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts
- यज्ञियाः (*yajñiyāḥ*)—being worthy of sacrifice
- अनुष्वधं (*anuṣvadhaṃ*)—every day
- अद्रोघं (*adroghaṃ*)—harmless
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food (having obtained)
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—rejoice; such
- ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*)—worthy of praise
- मरुद्भिः (*marudbhiḥ*)—the Maruts
- धृष्णुया (*dhṛṣṇuyā*)—you who are tolerant of hair **NOTE**
- प्र अर्च (*pra arca*)—worship exceedingly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Śyāvāśva, you who are tolerant of hair **NOTE**, worship exceedingly those praiseworthy Maruts who, being worthy of sacrifice, rejoice every day in harmless food.

##### English translation
Offer worship with perseverance, Shyavaswa, to the praise-deserving Maruts: they who are adorable and delight in the daily offered and inoffensive sacrificial food.

### Printed p. 606

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the seer of the sūkta, Śyāvāśva, addresses himself, saying "worship the Marut deities". Or else it may be said that the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice addresses in this Ṛk the seer Śyāvāśva, who is carrying out the sacrifice taking the part of the priest called Hotṛ.

ऋक्वभिः मरुद्भिः प्र अर्च (*ṛkvabhiḥ marudbhiḥ pra arca*)—स्तुत्यान् मरुतः पूजय (*stutyān marutaḥ pūjaya*): worship the praiseworthy Maruts. In this sentence, although the words ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*) and मरुद्भिः (*marudbhiḥ*) are words ending in the instrumental plural, the commentator has said that for these words, द्वितीयार्थे तृतिया (*dvitīyārthe tṛtiyā*), the instrumental case is used to indicate the sense of the accusative. That is, instead of the natural sense "by the Marut deities worthy of worship", it must be understood as "the Marut deities who are worthy of praise or of worship". Or for this sentence, मरुद्धिर्मरुत्सदृशैर्युक्वभिः स्तोत्रैर्वा अर्च स्तुहीत्यर्थः । (*maruddhirmarutsadṛśairyukvabhiḥ stotrairvā arca stuhītyarthaḥ |*), the meaning "praise with priests who chant hymns and are equal to the Marut deities, or with hymns" can also be given; thus Sāyaṇa has made two kinds of explanation of the meaning.

अनुष्टदं (*anuṣṭadaṃ*)—प्रत्यहं (*pratyahaṃ*): the meaning is "every day". For the indeclinable word अनु (*anu*) Yāska has given the derivation अन्विति शादृश्यापरभावं (*anviti śādṛśyāparabhāvaṃ*) (Ni. 1-3). अनु (*anu*) means likeness: when pointing to one thing that is like another, the word अनु (*anu*) is used in stating likeness or comparison, "like that". Or the word अनु (*anu*) is used also when the meaning "one after another" is stated. In the present Ṛk, for the word अनुस्वधं (*anusvadhaṃ*) the meaning given is "the next day after one day", that is, every day.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते हि स्थि॒रस्य॒ शव॑सः॒ सखा॑यः॒ संति॑ धृष्ण॒या ।  
> ते याम॒न्ना धृ॑ष॒द्विन॒स्त्मनां॑ पांति॒ शश्व॑तः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । हि । स्थिरस्य । शवसः । सखायः । संति । धृष्णुया ।  
> ते । यामन् । आ । धृषत्‌निनः । त्मना । पांति । शश्वतः ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 607

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते हि ते खलु स्थिरस्याविचलितस्य शवसो बलस्य सखायः संति । भवंति मह्यं ।
> धृष्णया धृष्णवः । ते च यामन्ना । आ इति चार्थे । गमनेऽपि धृषद्विनो धर्षणवंतस्त्मनात्मनानुग्रहेणैवास्मदुपकारमनपेक्ष्यैव शश्वतो बहूनस्मान्पुत्रभृत्यादी
> न्पांति । रक्षॆंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They indeed are the friends of steady, unwavering strength (शवसः (*śavasaḥ*)); they are to me bold ones (धृष्णया (*dhṛṣṇayā*) means bold). And they, even on the march (आ (*ā*) is in the sense of "and"), being daring, by themselves, out of favour alone, without regard to any service from us, always protect us, who are many, with our sons, servants and the rest.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—those very gods
- यामन् (*yāman*)—even at the time of going about
- धृषद्विनः (*dhṛṣadvinaḥ*)—having the power to confront (enemies)
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—by their own impulse
- शश्वतः (*śaśvataḥ*)—our numerous sons, servants and the rest
- पांति (*pāṃti*)—protect; such
- धृष्णुया (*dhṛṣṇuyā*)—having the power of boldness
- ते (*te*)—the same gods
- स्थिरस्य (*sthirasya*)—eternal
- तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)—to strength **NOTE**
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—as dear men
- संति (*saṃti*)—they are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those very gods who, even at the time of going about, having the power to confront enemies, protect by their own impulse our numerous sons, servants and the rest, those same gods, possessed of the power of boldness, are dear men to eternal strength.

##### English translation
They are the firm friends of steady vigour, who, proceeding resolute on their way, willingly protect (our) numerous (descendants).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ते स्थिरस्य शवसः सखायः संति (*te sthirasya śavasaḥ sakhāyaḥ saṃti*)—those Marut deities are friends of steady strength; that is, there is always a mutual relation between them and strength; they are always powerful. The meaning is that their strength and power are great and never fail.

The form of the word त्मना (*tmanā*)-आत्मना (*ātmanā*) has lost its initial letter according to the Vedic usage, and only त्मना (*tmanā*) remains. Even so, the word त्मना (*tmanā*) has the very meaning of the word आत्मना (*ātmanā*). This kind of usage is particularly common in the Ṛgveda.

Yāska has said that the indeclinable आ (*ā*) has many meanings and has made them clear by examples.

आ इत्यर्नागर्थेः (*ā ityarnāgartheḥ*)

(Ni. 1-3)

### Printed p. 608

From here onward, or all around, is the meaning. In आ पर्वतात् (*ā parvatāt*) the meaning is the regions beyond the mountain, or the regions around the mountain.

एतस्मिन्नेवार्थे (समुच्चयार्थे) देवेभ्यश्च पितृभ्य एत्याकारः ॥ (*etasminnevārthe (samuccayārthe) devebhyaśca pitṛbhya etyākāraḥ ‖*) (Ni. 1.4)

The meaning "and" (samuccaya: showing the connection between two words) also belongs to the word आ (*ā*). In the sentence देवेभ्यश्च पितृभ्य आ (*devebhyaśca pitṛbhya ā*) the word आ (*ā*) has just the meaning "and" that the word च (*ca*) has. That is, the sentence means "to the gods and to the fathers".

नवोत्तराणि पदानि सर्वपदसमान्नाये । (*navottarāṇi padāni sarvapadasamānnāye |*) (Ni. 3-14)

Nine words beginning with हिकं (*hikaṃ*) are included in the list called सर्वपदसमाम्नाय (*sarvapadasamāmnāya*). Among these words the word अ (*a*) also occurs. That is, the word आ (*ā*) is used merely to fill out a sentence, without any particular meaning.

अथाप्युपमार्थे दृश्यते । जार आ भगं । (ऋ. सं. १०-११-६) जार इव भगं । आदित्योऽत्र जार उच्यते । रात्रेजरयिता । स एव भासां ॥ (*athāpyupamārthe dṛśyate | jāra ā bhagaṃ | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-11-6) jāra iva bhagaṃ | ādityo 'tra jāra ucyate | rātrejarayitā | sa eva bhāsāṃ ‖*) (Si, Pi.-13) **NOTE**

The word आ (*ā*) is also used in the sense of comparison (likeness); that is, the word आ (*ā*) has the meaning of the word इव (*iva*). The sentence जार आ भगं (*jāra ā bhagaṃ*) means जार इव भगं (*jāra iva bhagaṃ*): the deity Bhaga, who is like the Sun (Āditya).

आ । आ इत्याकार उपसर्गः पुरस्तादेव व्याख्यातः । अथाप्यध्यर्थे दृश्यते । अभ्र आ अपः । अभ्रे आ अपो sपोऽभ्रेऽधीति ॥ (*ā | ā ityākāra upasargaḥ purastādeva vyākhyātaḥ | athāpyadhyarthe dṛśyate | abhra ā apaḥ | abhre ā apo spo 'bhre 'dhīti ‖*) (Ni. 5-2)

The word आ (*ā*) is a preposition (upasarga). Some of its meanings have been stated above. Besides these meanings, this word also has the meaning "above, over" (अधि (*adhi*)). For example, in अभ्र आ आपः (*abhra ā āpaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-48.1) the meaning is the water that is above the cloud; and in तोदस्येव आ महस्य (*todasyeva ā mahasya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-150-1) also, the word आ (*ā*) has the meaning "above" (अधि (*adhi*)).

### Printed p. 609

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते स्यं॒द्रासो॒ नोक्षणोऽति॑ स्कंदंति॒ शर्व॑रीः ।  
> म॒रुता॒मधा॒ महो॑ दि॒वि क्ष॒मा च॑ मन्महे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । स्यंद्रासः । न । उक्षणः । अति । स्कंदंति । शर्वरीः ।  
> मरुतां । अध । महः । दिवि । क्षमा । च । मन्महे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते मरुतः स्यंद्रासः स्यंदनशीला उक्षणो जलस्य सेक्तारत्थ । नेति चार्थे ।
> यस्मात्स्यंद्रा अन्येषां तस्मात् शर्वरीः i शर्वयो रात्रयः । कालावयवानित्यर्थः।
> तानति स्कंदंति । अतिक्रम्य गच्छंति । नित्या इत्यर्थः ! यस्मादेत एवंविधान्तस्मान्रुतामधाधुना महस्तेजो दिवि द्युलोके क्षमा क्षमायां भूमौ च वर्तमानं
> मन्महे । स्तुमः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Maruts are flowing, that is, of a flowing nature, and sprinklers of water. The word न (*na*) is used in the sense of "and". **NOTE** The शर्वरीः (*śarvarīḥ*) are the nights, that is, the divisions of time. They go beyond these, pass over them: the meaning is that they are everlasting. Since they are of such a kind, we now praise the might (tejas) of the Maruts, which abides in the heaven-world above and on the earth below.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—the Maruts
- स्यंद्रासः (*syaṃdrāsaḥ*)—who make (the world) wet with drizzles
- उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*)—who are sprinklers of water
- शर्वरीः (*śarvarīḥ*)—the nights
- अति स्कंदंति (*ati skaṃdaṃti*)—move on, transgressing (being free of the regulations of time) (therefore)
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the heaven-world
- क्षमा (*kṣamā*)—and on the earth
- मरुतां (*marutāṃ*)—of the Maruts
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—the might, which is spread out
- आध (*ādha*)—now
- मन्महे (*manmahe*)—we praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts move about with their powers, making the world wet with drizzles and sprinkling water, and transgressing the regulations of time such as the nights. Therefore we now praise the might of the Maruts, which is spread out in the heaven-world and on the earth.

##### English translation
Gliding along, and shedding moisture, they pass through the nights: therefore we now celebrate the might of the Maruts, manifested in both heaven nad earth. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 610

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Because the movement of the Maruts is especially marked while rain is falling, that is, because the wind blows with great force, the Maruts are described here as sprinklers of water.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒रुत्सु॑ वो दधीमहि॒ स्तोमं॑ य॒ज्ञं च॑ धृष्णु॒या ।  
> विश्वे॒ ये मानु॑षा यु॒गा पांति॒ मर्त्यं॑ रि॒षः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मरुत्सु । वः । दधीमहि । स्तोमं । यज्ञं । च । धृष्णुया ।  
> विश्वे । ये । मानुषा । युगा । पांति । मर्त्यं । रिषः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्युहोत्रादयो वो यूयं मरुत्सु धृष्णुया धर्षकेषु
> दधीमहि ॥ व्यत्ययेनोत्तमः ॥ धत्त । किं । स्तोमं स्तोत्रं यज्ञंच । इज्यतेऽनेनेति यज्ञं हविः । तदुभयं किमर्थं दीयत इति । ये मरुतो विश्वे सर्वेऽपि
> मानुषा मानुषाणि युगा युगानि । सर्वेषु कालेष्टित्यर्थः । मर्त्यं मरणधर्माणं यजमानं रिषो हिंसकात्सकाशात्पांति रक्षंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing the Adhvaryus, Hotṛs and others: "you" offer to the Maruts, who are assailants, that is, to the Maruts among the assailants. The first person दधीमहि (*dadhīmahi*) stands, by an interchange of person, for the imperative second person धत्त (*dhatta*), "offer". What is offered? Praise (stoma, hymn) and the sacrifice (यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)): that by which one sacrifices, namely the oblation. Why are both given? Because the Maruts, all the human ages, that is, at all times, protect the mortal sacrificer, one subject to death, from the harmful one who injures.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts (O Adhvaryus)
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—entire
- मानुषा युगा (*mānuṣā yugā*)—throughout the life-spans of man
- मर्त्यं (*martyaṃ*)—the human sacrificer
- रिषः (*riṣaḥ*)—from the injuring enemy
- पांति (*pāṃti*)—protect; to such
- धृष्णया (*dhṛṣṇayā*)—who assail enemies **NOTE**
- मरुत्तु (*maruttu*)—to the Maruts **NOTE**
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—praise
- यज्ञं च (*yajñaṃ ca*)—and the oblation
- दधीमहि (*dadhīmahi*)—offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adhvaryus, offer praise and oblation to those Maruts who assail enemies, and who through all the life-spans of man protect the human sacrificer from the injuring enemy.

### Printed p. 611

##### English translation
We enjoin you, (priests), to offer earnestly praise and sacrifice to the Maruts, who through all human ages, protect the mortal worshipper from harm.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मानुषा युगा (*mānuṣā yugā*)—मानुषाणि युगानि । सर्वेषु कालेष्टित्यर्थः । (*mānuṣāṇi yugāni | sarveṣu kāleṣṭityarthaḥ |*) In the time that a man lives; the intention is, in the time that the sacrificer lives.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अर्हं॑तो॒ ये सु॒दान॑वो॒ नरो॒ असा॑मिशवसः ।  
> प्र य॒ज्ञं य॒ज्ञिये॑भ्यो दि॒वो अ॑र्चा म॒रुद्भ्यः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अर्हंतः । ये । सुदानवः । नरः । असामिशवसः ।  
> प्र । यज्ञं । यज्ञियेभ्यः । दिवः । अर्च । मरुत्स्भ्यः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे होतः हे आत्मन्वा येऽर्हंतः पूज्याः सुदानवः शोभनदाना नरो
> नेतारः कर्मणामसामिशवसोऽनल्पबलाः संति तेभ्यो यज्जियेभ्यो यज्ञाहर्हेभ्यो दिवो द्योतमानेभ्यो मरुद्भ्यः ॥ विभक्तिवचनयोर्व्यत्ययः ॥ यद्वा कर्मणि
> षष्ठी ॥ दीप्तं यज्ञं यज्ञसाधनं हविः प्रार्च । पूजय । प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः । अथवा
> दिवोऽंतरिक्षादागतेभ्य इति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressed to the Hotṛ, or to oneself (आत्मन् (*ātman*)): the Maruts who are worthy of worship, bountiful in giving, leaders of rites, and of no small strength: to those Maruts, worthy of the sacrifice and shining, offer the sacrifice. Case-endings and number are interchanged here; or else the genitive stands in the sense of the object. "The shining sacrifice" is the oblation, the means of the sacrifice: प्रार्च (*prārca*) means present, offer. Or else the connection is "to those come from the heaven, that is, from the atmosphere".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts (O Hotṛ)
- अर्हंतः (*arhaṃtaḥ*)—who are worthy of worship
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—who have an excellent disposition to give
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—who are leaders of rites
- असामिशवसः (*asāmiśavasaḥ*)—who have exceedingly great strength; to such
- यज्ञियेभ्यः (*yajñiyebhyaḥ*)—to those worthy of the sacrifice
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—and shining
- मरुद्भ्यः (*marudbhyaḥ*)—the Maruts, addressing them
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the oblation
- प्र अर्च (*pra arca*)—offer in abundance

### Printed p. 612

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Hotṛ, offer the oblation with devotion to those Maruts who are worthy of the sacrifice and shining, who are worthy of worship, have an excellent disposition to give, are leaders of rites, and have exceedingly great strength.

##### English translation
Offer sacrifice to the adorable Maruts, who (have come) from heaven who are worthy of worship, munificent leaders (of rites), and possessors of unequalled strength.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

असामिशवसः (*asāmiśavasaḥ*)—अनल्पबलाः (*analpabalāḥ*). Not small, that is, having abundant strength, is the meaning. Yāska has given the etymology of the word असामि (*asāmi*) in this way:

असामि । बृहस्पतिं वर्धय नव्यमर्कैरर्चनीयैः स्तोमैरसामि सामि प्रतिषिद्धं । सामि स्यतेः । असाम्योजो बिभृथा सुदानवः । अनुसमाप्तं बलं बिभृत कल्याणदानाः ॥ (*asāmi | bṛhaspatiṃ vardhaya navyamarkairarcanīyaiḥ stomairasāmi sāmi pratiṣiddhaṃ | sāmi syateḥ | asāmyojo bibhṛthā sudānavaḥ | anusamāptaṃ balaṃ bibhṛta kalyāṇadānāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 6-23)

The word सामि (*sāmi*), formed from the root स्यति (*syati*) ("kill"), means that which brings to an end, that which is small. When the negative prefix अ (*a*) joins this word, असामि (*asāmi*) results. Therefore the word असामि (*asāmi*) has the meaning opposed to that of the word सामि (*sāmi*), which has the meaning "small". So for the word असामि (*asāmi*) one may give the meaning "not small", that is, "very great". In the illustrative sentences given here by the author of the Nirukta, बृहस्पतिं वर्धय नव्यमर्कैरसामि (*bṛhaspatiṃ vardhaya navyamarkairasāmi*) and असाम्योजो बिभृथा सुदानवः (*asāmyojo bibhṛthā sudānavaḥ*), the meaning of the word असामि (*asāmi*) is "great, abundant".

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ रु॒क्मैरा यु॒धा नर॑ ऋ॒ष्वा ऋ॒ष्टीर॑सृक्षत ॥  
> अन्वे॑ना॒ अह॑ वि॒द्युतो॑ म॒रुतो॒ जज्ञ॑तीरव भा॒नुर॑र्त॒ त्मना॑  ॒
> दिवः ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 613

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । रुक्मैः । आ । युधा । नरः । ऋष्वाः । ऋष्टीः । अस्पृश्यत ।  
> अनु । एनान् । अह । विद्युतः । मरुतः । जज्ञतीः इव । भानुः । अर्त । त्मना ।  
> दिवः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नरो वृष्टेर्नेतार ऋष्टा महांतो मरुतो रुक्मै रोचमानैराभरणविशेषैरा रोचंत इति शेषः ॥ उपसर्गश्रुतेः संगतक्रियाध्याहारः ॥ तथा युधा
> प्रहरणसाधनेनायुधेना रोचंते । एते मरुत ऋष्टिरायुधविशेषानसृक्षत ।
> प्रक्षिपंति मेघभेदार्थं । एनान्मरुतो विद्युतोऽपि जझुतीरिन शब्दकारिण्य आप
> इव । जझुतीरापो भवंति शब्दकारिण्यः । नि-६-१६ । इति निरुक्तं । अन्वह अनुगच्छंत्ये व । दिवो द्योतमानस्य मरुद्धणस्य भानुर्दीप्तिस्त्मना स्वयमेवार्त ।
> निरगात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts, leaders of the rain, mighty, shine with brilliant ornaments of various kinds; "they shine" is the word to be supplied, because the preposition आ (*ā*) is heard (the verb is understood from the preposition). Likewise they shine with a weapon, an instrument of striking. These Maruts hurl the spears, a special kind of weapon, to split the cloud. Their lightnings also follow them, like noisy waters. The Nirukta says: जझुतीरापो भवंति शब्दकारिण्यः (*jajhutīrāpo bhavaṃti śabdakāriṇyaḥ*) (Ni-6-16) **NOTE**. The lightnings follow the shining host of Maruts; the radiance of the host came forth of itself.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the leaders
- ऋष्टाः (*ṛṣṭāḥ*)—the great-souled Maruts
- रुक्मैः (*rukmaiḥ*)—with their golden ornaments
- आ (रोचंते) (*ā (rocaṃte)*)—shine
- युधा (*yudhā*)—with a weapon, an instrument of striking
- आ (*ā*)—shine
- ऋष्टीः (*ṛṣṭīḥ*)—their spears
- असृक्षत (*asṛkṣata*)—hurl (at their enemies)
- एनान् मरुतः (*enān marutaḥ*)—these Maruts
- विद्युतः (*vidyutaḥ*)—the lightnings
- जज्ञतीरिव (*jajñatīriva*)—like streams of water flowing with a noise
- अनु अह (*anu aha*)—certainly follow
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the shining host of Maruts
- भानुः (*bhānuḥ*)—the radiance
- त्मना अर्त (*tmanā arta*)—becomes self-luminous

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, leaders and great-souled, shine with their golden ornaments and with their weapons of striking. They hurl their spears at their enemies. These lightnings follow the Maruts constantly, like waters flowing with a noise. The radiance of the shining host of Maruts is self-luminous.

##### English translation
Leaders (of the rains), the mighty Maruts shine with brilliant ornaments and weapons, and hurl javelin (at their foes, the clouds): the

### Printed p. 614

lightnings, like roaring (torrents), daily follow the Maruts: the radiance of the resplendent (cohort) spontaneously breaks forth,

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये वा॑वृ॒धंत॒ पार्थि॑वा॒ य उ॒रावं॒तरि॑क्ष॒ आ ।  
> वृ॒जने॑ ना न॒दीनां॑ स॒दस्ये॑ वा म॒हो दि॒वः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । नवृधंत । पार्थिवाः । ये । उरौ । अंतरिक्षे । आ ।  
> वृजने । वा । नदीनां । सधस्थे । वा । महः । दिवः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये मरुतः पार्थिवाः पृथिवीसंबद्धाः संतो ववृधंत वर्धंते । ये चोर्
> महत्यंतरिक्षे च ववृधंत । आ इति चार्थे । नदीनां नदनवतीनां वृजने ना बले
> ववृधंत । महो महतो दिवो द्युलोकस्य सधस्थे सहस्थाने च ववृधंत । उभयत्र
> वाशब्दश्चार्थे । एवं सर्वत्र वर्धमाना मरुतो वृष्ट्यर्थमृष्टीरसृक्षतेति पूर्वत्र
> संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Maruts who, being connected with the earth, increase; and those who increase also in the vast atmosphere. The word आ (*ā*) is used in the sense of "and" (आ इति चार्थे (*ā iti cārthe*)). They increase also in the strength (बले (*bale*)) of the rivers, that is, of the resounding ones; and in the common abode (सहस्थाने (*sahasthāne*)) of the great heaven-world. In both places the word वा (*vā*) is used in the sense of "and". Thus the Maruts, growing everywhere, hurl their spears for the sake of rain: this is the connection with the preceding verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पार्थिवाः (*pārthivāḥ*)—those who dwell on the earth
- ये (*ye*)—whichever Maruts there are, they
- ववृधंत (*vavṛdhaṃta*)—attain increase
- उरौ (*urau*)—vast
- अंतरिक्षे (*aṃtarikṣe*)—in the atmosphere
- ये (*ye*)—whoever there are
- आ (*ā*)—they too attain increase
- नदीनां (*nadīnāṃ*)—of the rivers, which are of the nature of floods
- वृजने वा (*vṛjane vā*)—in the speed, whoever are there, they too
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heaven-world
- सधस्थे (*sadhasthe*)—in the abode, whichever Maruts there are, all of them too gain increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts who dwell on the earth, those who dwell in the atmosphere, those who produce the speed of the rivers that are of the nature of floods, and whichever Maruts dwell in the great heaven-world: all of them gain increase.

### Printed p. 615

##### English translation
The Maruts, who are of the earth are augmented, so are those in the vast firmament; they increase in the force of the rivers, and in the aggregate of the spacious heaven.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शर्धो॒ मारु॑त॒मुच्छं॑स स॒त्यश॑वस॒मृभ्व॑सं ।  
> उ॒त स्म॒ ते शु॒भे नरः॒ प्र स्क्॒यंद्रा यु॑जत॒ त्मना॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शर्धः । मारुतं । उत् । शंस । सत्यशवसं । यभ्वसं ।  
> उत । स्त । ते । शुभे । नरः । प्र । स्कंद्राः । युजत । त्मना ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतर्मारुतं शधर्ण बलमुत् उत्कृष्टं शंस । स्तुहि । कीदृशं शर्धः।
> सत्यशवसं सत्यवेगमृभ्वसं महदतिप्रवृद्धं । उत स्मापि च नरो वृष्टेर्नेतारस्ते
> मरुतः शुभ उदकार्थं प्र युजत प्रायुंजत समयोजयन् त्मनात्मनैव जगद्रक्षाबुद्धैव स्यंद्राश्चलनस्वभावाः पृषतीरित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, praise the might (शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*), strength) of the host of Maruts, excellently (उत् (*ut*)). Of what kind is that might? Of true speed, and great, exceedingly grown. Moreover those Maruts, the leaders of the rain, for the sake of water, yoke, that is, harness forth by their own will, with the thought of protecting the world, the moving ones, that is, the dappled mares: this is the meaning. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सत्यशवसं (*satyaśavasaṃ*)—(O praiser) possessing strength of the nature of truth
- यभ्वसं (*yabhvasaṃ*)—and great **NOTE**
- मारुतं शर्धः (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ*)—the might of the host of Maruts
- उत् (*ut*)—excellently
- शंस (*śaṃsa*)—praise
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the leaders
- ते (*te*)—the Maruts
- स्यंद्राः (*syaṃdrāḥ*)—being of a moving nature
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—by their own impulse
- शुभे (*śubhe*)—for our welfare
- प्र युजत (*pra yujata*)—strive

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, the Maruts, the leaders, being of a moving nature, strive of their own impulse for our welfare. Therefore praise excellently the might of the host of Maruts, which possesses strength of the nature of truth and is great.

### Printed p. 616

##### English translation
Glorify the truth-invigorated and infinite strength of the Maruts, for they, the leaders (of the rains), gliding along, are labouring voluntarily for (our) good.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त स्म॒ ते परु॑ष्या॒मूर्णा॑ वसत शुं॒ध्यवः॑ ।  
> उ॒त प॒व्या रथा॑ना॒मद्रिं॑ भिंदं॒त्योज॑सा ॥ ९ ॥

> उत । पव्या । रथानां । अद्रिं । भिंदंति । ओजसा ॥ ९ ॥

> उत स्मापि च ते मरुतः परुष्यामेतन्नामिकायां नद्यां वर्तंते । य
> ऊर्णा दीप्तिः शुंध्यवः शोधिका वसत अच्छादयंति ते । उतापि च पव्या नेम्या
> रथानां स्वकीयानां रथचक्रेणौजसा बलेन चाद्रिं भिंदंति । मेघं गिरिं वा
> विदारयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Moreover those Maruts abide in the river of that name, the Parushni. The radiance (दीप्तिः (*dīptiḥ*)) of those purifiers they put on, that is, they cover themselves with it. And with the felloe (नेम्या (*nemyā*)) of their own chariot wheels and with their strength they split the mountain (अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)), that is, they tear apart the cloud or the mountain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—moreover
- ते (*te*)—those same Maruts
- परुष्णां (*paruṣṇāṃ*)—(they abide) in the river Parushni **NOTE**
- ऊर्णाः (*ūrṇāḥ*)—a radiant
- शुंध्यवः (*śuṃdhyavaḥ*)—and purified splendour
- वसत् (*vasat*)—they wear
- उत (*uta*)—and
- रथानां (*rathānāṃ*)—of their chariots
- पव्या (*pavyā*)—of the form of a felloe
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—with strength
- अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)—the cloud
- भिंदंति (*bhiṃdaṃti*)—split

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts abide in the river Parushni. They are clothed with a splendour that is radiant and purified. And with the strength of the felloes of their chariots they split the cloud.

> आपथयः । अस्मदभिमुखा मार्गा येषां ते तादृशाः । विपथयो विस्वज्मार्गा अंतस्पथा दरीसुषिरादिमार्गा अनुपथा अनुकूलमार्गाश्च ये मरुतः संति त
> एतेभिरेतैश्चतुर्विधैर्नामकैः स्वरूपैर्मह्यं मदर्थं यज्ञं विस्तारो विस्तृताः
> संत ओहते । वहंति । यद्वा । एतैनामभिरुदकैः सार्धं यज्ञमोहते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आपथयः (*āpathayaḥ*): those Maruts whose paths lead towards us. विपथयः (*vipathayaḥ*): those whose paths are of various kinds **NOTE**. अंतस्पथा (*aṃtaspathā*): those whose paths are caves, hollows and the like. अनुपथा (*anupathā*): those whose paths are favourable. With these four kinds of names, that is, forms, those Maruts, being spread out, bear the sacrifice for me, for my sake. Or else: with these names, that is, with waters, they bear the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आपथयः (*āpathayaḥ*)—let them follow the path that faces us (or)
- विपथयः (*vipathayaḥ*)—let them follow various different paths (or)
- अंतस्पथाः (*aṃtaspathāḥ*)—let them resort to paths such as mountain caves (or)
- अनुपथाः (*anupathāḥ*)—let them have a favourable path
- एतेभिः (*etebhiḥ*)—even though they are of these four kinds
- नामभिः (*nāmabhiḥ*)—by their respective forms
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—for me
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- विस्तारः (*vistāraḥ*)—extending and increasing it
- ओहते (*ohate*)—they bear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Whether the Maruts follow the path that faces us, or follow various different paths, or resort to paths such as mountain caves, or have a favourable path, even though they are of these four

### Printed p. 618

kinds, they bear the sacrifice for me, extending and increasing it, each in their respective forms.

##### English translation
(Whether), following the paths that lead (to us), or that spread diversely, or those that sink into the hollows (of the mountain), or those that extend smoothly, they, (however) scattered, accept the sacrifice for my benefit, (when invoked by these appellations).

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधा॒ नरो॒ नृपो॑ह॒तेधा॑ नि॒युत॑ ओहते ।  
> अधा॒ पारा॑वता॒ इति॑ चि॒त्रा रू॒पाणि॒ दर्श्या॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । नरः । नि । ओहते । अध । नियुतः । ओहते ।  
> अध । पारावताः । इति । चित्रा । रूपाणि : दर्श्या । ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अधाथ नरोऽभिमतवृष्टा दिनेतारो न्यूहते । नितरां वहंति जगत् । अध
> नियुतः स्वयमेव मिश्रयितारः संत ओहते । अधाथ पारावताः । परावद्दूरदेशः।
> तत्संबंधिनश्चांतरिक्षादिदूरदेशे ग्रहतारामेघादिधारकाः संत ओहत इत्यर्थः ।
> इत्युक्त प्रकारेण तेषां रूपाणि चित्रा नानाविधानि चायनीयानि वा दर्श्या स्वव्यापारैर्दर्शनीयानि भवन्त्विति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now the leaders, the bringers of the desired rain and the like, carry the world down, that is, bear it constantly. Now the नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*), themselves mixing (all things together), bear. Now the पारावताः (*pārāvatāḥ*): परावद्दूरदेशः (*parāvaddūradeśaḥ*); those belonging to it, that is, those who in the distant regions such as the atmosphere are the upholders of planets, stars, clouds and the like, bear: this is the meaning. In the manner thus stated their forms are manifold, of many kinds, or worthy of being gathered, and दर्श्या (*darśyā*), that is, to be seen through their own activities: may they be so; this is what is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध (*adha*)—once
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the Maruts who are leaders
- न्यूहते (*nyūhate*)—bear the burden of the world
- अध (*adha*)—in another way
- नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)—all gathered together
- ओहते (*ohate*)—bear the burden of conducting the sacrifice
- अध (*adha*)—in another manner
- पारावताः (*pārāvatāḥ*)—being situated in very distant regions, they bear the burden of planets, stars and the like
- इति (*iti*)—in this way
- रूपाणि (*rūpāṇi*)—the forms of the Maruts
- चित्रा (*citrā*)—are manifold
- दर्श्या (*darśyā*)—and attractive

### Printed p. 619

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts in one way, as leaders of the rain and the like, bear the burden of protecting the world. In another way, all gathering together, they bear the burden of conducting the sacrifice. In another way, being situated in very distant regions, they bear the burden of planets, stars and the like. In this way they are of manifold forms and of an attractive nature.

##### English translation
Now, leaders (of the rains), they support (the world): now, blending together, they bear (the oblation): now, situated remote, (they uphold distant objects): so may their manifold forms be manifest.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> छं॒दः॒स्तुभः॑ कुभ॒न्यव॒ उत्स॒मा की॒रिणो॑ नृतुः ।  
> ते मे॒ के चि॒न्न ता॒यव॒ ऊमा॑ आसन्दृ॒ति त्वि॒षे ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> छंदःस्तुभः । कुभन्यवः । उत्सं । आ। कीरिणः । नृतुः ।  
> ते । मे । के । चित् । न । तायवः । ऊमाः । आसन् । दृशि । त्विषे ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> छंदःस्तुभश्चंद्रोभिः स्तोतारः कुभन्यव उदकेच्छवः कीरिणः स्तोतार उत्सं
> कूपमपेक्ष्य तृषिताय गोतमाय यान्मरुत आ नृतुः सर्वतोऽकुर्वन् अनयन्वा
> स्तोत्रं । यद्वा । ये छंदःस्तुभश्चंद्रोभिः स्तुत्याः ॥ स्तोभतिः स्तुतिकर्मा ॥
> कुभन्यवः सेक्तारो वृष्टुदकस्य । कुभिरुंदनकर्मा ॥ कीरिणः स्तोतुर्गोतमस्य
> पानार्थमुत्सं कूपमा नृतुः आनीतवंतः । असिंचन्नुत्सं गोतमाय तृष्णजे ।
> ऋग्वे-१-८५.११ । इति ह्युक्तं ॥ नृ नय इत्यस्य वा नर्ततीर्वा विक्षेपमात्रार्थस्येदं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

छंदःस्तुभः (*chaṃdaḥstubhaḥ*): praisers with metres (चंद्रोभिः (*caṃdrobhiḥ*) **NOTE**). कुभन्यवः (*kubhanyavaḥ*): those desiring water. कीरिणः (*kīriṇaḥ*): praisers. Having regard to the well, for the thirsty Gotama, the Maruts whom (the praisers) set going all around, or led, with praise. Or else: those who are to be praised with metres; the root स्तोभतिः (*stobhatiḥ*) means the act of praising. कुभन्यवः (*kubhanyavaḥ*) are the sprinklers of the rain-water; कुभि (*kubhi*) means the act of wetting. कीरिणः (*kīriṇaḥ*): of the praiser Gotama, for the sake of drinking, the Maruts brought the well. For it is said: असिंचन्नुत्सं गोतमाय तृष्णजे । (*asiṃcannutsaṃ gotamāya tṛṣṇaje |*) (Ṛgve-1-85.11) **NOTE**. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 620

> रूपं ॥ ते मरुतः के चिन्मे मह्यं तायवो न कदाचिदप्यदृश्यास्तस्करा इव स्थिता
> ऊमा रक्षका दृशि दर्शन आसन् । विषयभूता अभवन् । केचित्विषे शरीरदीप्तैश्चि
> बलाय वासन् । प्राणरूपेणेति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Maruts, "some of them", for me, are the "thieves" (तायवो (*tāyavo*)): they stood like thieves, never visible, as ऊमा (*ūmā*), protectors. Others came into view, into sight. Some, with the radiance of their bodies, for strength **NOTE**, were in the form of the life-breath: this is the idea.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- छंदस्तुभः (*chaṃdastubhaḥ*)—those who are praised with metres
- कुभन्यवः (*kubhanyavaḥ*)—and who pour down the water of the rain: the Maruts
- कीरिणः (*kīriṇaḥ*)—for the praiser Gotama
- उत्सं (*utsaṃ*)—a well
- आ नृतुः (*ā nṛtuḥ*)—made to come into being
- ते (*te*)—among those Maruts
- के चित् (*ke cit*)—some
- मे (*me*)—for me
- तायवो न (*tāyavo na*)—staying hidden like thieves
- ऊमाः (*ūmāḥ*)—are protectors; (the others)
- त्विषे (*tviṣe*)—through the power of their splendour
- दृशि आसन् (*dṛśi āsan*)—have come into view

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, who are praised with metres and who pour down the water of the rain, caused a well to come into being for the thirsty Gotama, the praiser. Some of those Maruts, staying hidden like thieves, are my protectors. The others, through the power of their splendour, are visible right before me, and are protectors.

##### English translation
The reciters of sacred metres, desirous of water, and celebrating (the Maruts), have drawn them to (provide) a well (for Gotama): some of them, (invisible) as thieves, have been my defenders: some have been (obvious) to view through the light (of life).

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य ऋ॒ष्वा ऋ॒ष्टिवि॑द्युतः क॒वयः॒ संति॑ वे॒धसः॑ ।  
> तम्मृ॑षे॒ मारु॑तं ग॒णं न॑म॒स्या र॒मया॑ गि॒रा ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । ऋष्टाः । ऋष्टिऽविद्युतः । कवयः । संति । वेधसः ।  
> तं । ऋषे । मारुतं । गणं । नमस्य । रमय । गिरा ॥ १३ ॥

### Printed p. 621

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये मरुत ऋष्वा दर्शनीया ऋष्टिविद्युत आयुधैर्विद्योतमानाः कवयो
> मेधाविनो वेधस: सर्वस्य विधातारः सति तं तेषां मारुतं गणं रमया रमणीयया गिरा स्तुत्या हे ऋषे श्यावाश्व नमस्य । परिचर । स्तुहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts who are ऋष्वा (*ṛṣvā*), worthy to be seen, shining with their weapons (ऋष्टिविद्युत (*ṛṣṭividyuta*)), wise (कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)), intelligent, वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*), the creators of everything: the host of those Maruts, with a pleasing (रमणीयया (*ramaṇīyayā*)) praise, O sage Śyāvāśva, venerate, serve, praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋषे (*ṛṣe*)—O sage Śyāvāśva
- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts
- ऋष्वाः (*ṛṣvāḥ*)—who are worthy to be seen
- ऋष्टिविद्युतः (*ṛṣṭividyutaḥ*)—who shine with their weapons
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—who are wise
- वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)—and creators
- संति (*saṃti*)—there are
- तं (*taṃ*)—the host of such Maruts
- रमया (*ramayā*)—pleasing
- गिरा (*girā*)—with praise
- नमस्य (*namasya*)—worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sage Śyāvāśva, worship with a pleasing praise the host of those Maruts who are worthy to be seen, who shine with their weapons, and who are wise and creators.

##### English translation
Glorify, Rishi, with grateful praise, the company of the Maruts, who are manifest, bright with lightning lances, who are wise, and the creators (of all things).

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अच्छ॑ ऋषे॒ मारु॑तं ग॒णं दा॒ना मि॒त्रं न यो॒षणा॑ ।  
> दि॒वो वा॑ धृष्णव॒ ऒज॑सा स्तु॒ता धी॒भिरि॑षण्यत ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अच्छ । ऋषे । मारुतं ' गणं । दाना । मित्रं । न । योषणा ।  
> दिवः । ना । धृष्णवः । ओजसा । स्तुताः । धीभिः । इषण्यत ॥ १४ ॥

### Printed p. 622

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋषे मारुतं गणं मरत्संघं मित्रं न आदित्यमिव दाना हविर्दानेन
> योषणा ॥ यौतेरिदं रूपं । यौतीति योषा स्तुतिः ॥ तया चाच्छ अभिगच्छेति
> शेषः । ऋषेरुत्तरार्धः प्रत्यक्षवादः । ओजसा बलेन हे धृष्णवो धर्षका मरुतो
> दिवो ना द्युलोकाद्वा । नाशब्दश्रुतेरितरलोकद्वयाद्वा । धीभिरस्मदीयाभिः स्तुतिभिः
> स्तुता इषण्यत । गच्छत यज्ञं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O sage, approach the host of Maruts, like Mitra, that is, like Āditya, with the gift of the oblation and with praise (योषणा (*yoṣaṇā*), which is explained as praise); the verb "approach" is to be supplied. The latter half of the verse is the sage's direct address: with strength, O bold Maruts, assailers, from the heaven-world, or, because the word ना (*nā*) is heard, from the other two worlds, praised by our hymns, come to the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋषे (*ṛṣe*)—O sage
- मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*)—the host of Maruts
- मित्रं न (*mitraṃ na*)—as one approaches a friend
- दाना (*dānā*)—with gifts of the oblation
- योषणा (*yoṣaṇā*)—and with praise
- अच्छ (*accha*)—approach
- धृष्णवः (*dhṛṣṇavaḥ*)—O Maruts, of enduring strength
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—by our hymns
- स्तुताः (*stutāḥ*)—being praised
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—with your strength
- दिवो वा (*divo vā*)—whether from the heaven-world or from any other region
- इषण्यत (*iṣaṇyata*)—graciously come to our sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sage, approach the host of Maruts, as one approaches a friend, with the gift of the oblation and with praise. O Maruts of enduring strength, praised by our hymns, graciously come to our sacrifice with your strength, whether from the heaven-world or from any other region.

##### English translation
Approach, Rishi, with offerings and with praise, the company of the Maruts like a friend: come, sustaining (Maruts), with your strength, from heaven or (any other region), glorified by our hymns.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नू म॑न्वा॒न ए॑षां दे॒वा अच्छा॒ न व॒क्षणा॑ ।  
> दा॒ना स॑चेत सू॒रिभि॒र्याम॑श्रुतेभिरं॒जिभिः॑ ॥ १५ ॥

### Printed p. 623

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नु । मन्वानः । एषां । देवान् । अच्छ । न । वक्षणा ।  
> दाना । सचेत । सूरिभिः । याम्यश्रुतेभिः । अंजिभिः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नु क्षिप्रमेषां मरुतां । एतान्मरुत इत्यर्थः । मन्वानः स्तुवन् देवान्मरुद्व्यतिरिक्तान्वक्षणा वहनेन निमित्तेनाच्छ अभिप्राप्तुं न मनुते । सस्तोता सूरिभिर्मेधाविभिर्यामश्रुतेभिः शीघ्रगमनेन विश्रुतैरंजिभिः फलस्य व्यंजकैर्मरुद्भिः ॥ सर्वाः
> पंचम्यर्थे तृतीयाः ॥ उक्तलक्षणेभ्यो मरुद्भो दानाभिमतदानानि सचेत '
> संगच्छते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Quickly, praising these Maruts, he does not intend, as a means of conveying (them), to approach deities other than the Maruts. The praiser, with the wise ones, famed for their swift going (यामश्रुतेभिः (*yāmaśrutebhiḥ*)), the Maruts, who are the revealers of the fruit (अंजिभिः (*aṃjibhiḥ*)): all the instrumentals here are in the sense of the ablative. From the Maruts of the said characteristics he joins (सचेत (*saceta*)) the desired gifts, that is, he receives them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—these Maruts
- मन्वानः (*manvānaḥ*)—praising
- देवान् (*devān*)—(other than the Maruts) deities
- वक्षणा (*vakṣaṇā*)—for the purpose of invoking
- अच्छ (*accha*)—to approach
- न (*na*)—(the sacrificer) does not wish
- सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)—by the wise ones
- यामश्रुतेभिः (*yāmaśrutebhiḥ*)—renowned for their swift going
- अंजिभिः (*aṃjibhiḥ*)—by the Maruts, the revealers of the fruit (by their favour)
- दाना (*dānā*)—the desired gifts
- सचेत (*saceta*)—obtains (the sacrificer receives)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer, praising these Maruts duly, does not approach deities other than them, to invoke them. By the favour of the Maruts, who are wise, renowned for their swift going and revealers of the fruit, he receives the desired gifts.

##### English translation
Glorifying them promptly, desiring not to bring (other) deities to (his) presence, let (the worshipper) associate his gifts with those wise (divinites) renowned for their velocity, and distributors (of rewards).

> ये मरुतो मे मह्यं बंध्वेषे स्वेषां बंधूनामन्वेषणी सति सूरयः
> प्रेरका गां माध्यमिकां वाचं गोदेवतां वा प्र वोचंत प्रावोचन् ॥ अविशिष्टमृषेर्वाक्यं । ऋषिर्मरुद्वाक्यमनुवदति । तस्मादुत्तरयोराख्यातयोर्यच्छब्दानन्वयान्निघातः ॥ ते पृश्निं द्युदेवतां पृश्निवर्णां गां वा मातरं वोचंत ।

> पुत्रत्वपरिग्रहो बहुकृत्व उपपादितः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts who, for me, in the seeking of their own kinsmen, being impellers (सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)), uttered गां (*gāṃ*), that is, the speech of the middle region, or the cow deity. The sage repeats the speech of the Maruts. They called Pṛśni, the deity of the sky, or the cow of dappled colour, their mother: for it is said, पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाता इति श्रुतेः (*pṛśniyai vai payaso maruto jātā iti śruteḥ*). Then they, being capable, called their own father the moving, food-possessing Rudra. The adoption of Rudra as father of the Maruts has been established many times.

- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—impellers of the world

- मे (*me*)—to me
- गां (*gāṃ*)—in the form of the speech of the middle region
- प्र वोचंत (*pra vocaṃta*)—gave a reply
