> योजनं ।  
> एताः । न । यामे । अगृभीतशोचिषः । अनश्वदां । यत् । नि । अयातन । गिरिं ॥

### Printed p. 662

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो वो युष्माकं तद्वीर्यं प्रसिद्धं सामर्थ्यं महित्वनं महत्त्वं
> दीर्घमत्यंतमायतं ततान । तनोति । लोके सूर्यो न योजनं सूर्यस्तेज
> इव । एता न एतवर्णा देवानामश्वा इव । ते यथा यामे गमने योजनं
> दीर्घं तन्नंति तद्वदित्यपरो दृष्टांतः । ते जागृभीतशोचिषोऽगृहीततेजस्काः ।
> यद्वैतन्मरुतां विशेषणं । हे मरुतो यूयमगृभीतशोचिषः संतो यद्यदानश्वदां व्यापकोदकादातारं पणिभिरपहृतानामश्वानामप्रदातारं वा गिरिं मेघं
> पर्वतं ना न्ययातन निहतवंतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, that well-known prowess of yours has spread your greatness far and wide. As in the world the sun spreads his radiance, so do you; and there is a second comparison: as the dappled horses of the gods, in their going, stretch their course a long way, so is your greatness extended. Your lustre is not seized, that is, not held in check; or else this is simply an epithet of the Maruts. O Maruts, being of unseized lustre, you struck down the cloud that holds back the water: the word अनश्वदां (*anaśvadāṃ*) is explained as one who holds the all-pervading water, or else as one who does not give the horses carried off by the Paṇis; the mountain, the cloud, is what you struck down. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts (you)
- सूर‍्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- योजनं न (*yojanaṃ na*)—as he spreads his radiance throughout the universe
- एताः यामे न (*etāḥ yāme na*)—as the horses of the gods pervade everywhere
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- तद्वीर्यं (*tadvīryaṃ*)—well-known prowess
- महित्वनं (*mahitvanaṃ*)—your glory
- दीर्घं (*dīrghaṃ*)—exceedingly wide
- ततान (*tatāna*)—has extended and made famous
- अगृभीतशोचिषः (*agṛbhītaśociṣaḥ*)—you who are of unrestrained radiance
- यत् (*yat*)—by which same greatness
- अनश्वदां (*anaśvadāṃ*)—that does not pour out water
- गिरिं (*giriṃ*)—the cloud
- न्ययातन (*nyayātana*)—you have cleft (and poured down rain)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, as the sun spreads all his radiance throughout the universe, and as the horses of the gods pervade everywhere in their course, so your well-known prowess has extended and made famous your glory exceedingly wide. You, of unrestrained radiance, by that same greatness have cleft the cloud that does not pour out water, and have poured down rain

##### English translation
Your prowess, Maruts, has spread wide your glory as the sun (sends afar his) radiance, or the white (horses of the gods travel far) in their course : of unbounded lustre, you clove the cloud withholding the waters

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मरुतः महित्वनं सूर्यो न योजनं दीर्घं ततान (*marutaḥ mahitvanaṃ sūryo na yojanaṃ dīrghaṃ tatāna*)—As the sun spreads his splendour or light everywhere, so the Marut deities spread their exceedingly great strength and power and their glory most widely, that is, everywhere; thus the seer has compared the sun's splendour, as an illustration, with the range of the strength and power of the Marut deities.
### Printed p. 663
अनश्वदां (*anaśvadāṃ*)—व्यापकोदकादातारं (*vyāpakodakādātāraṃ*). The word aśva, formed from the root अशू व्याप्तौ (*aśū vyāptau*), is used here in the sense of water. आश्वद (*āśvada*) means the cloud that gives water; अनश्वद (*anaśvada*), on the contrary, means the cloud that holds back the water and does not pour it down as rain: this is the meaning specified here.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अभ्रा॑जि॒ शर्धो॑ मरुतो॒ यद॑र्ण॒सं मोष॑था वृ॒क्षं क॑प॒नेव॑  
> वेधसः ।  
> अध॑ स्मा नो अ॒रम॑तिं सजोषस॒श्चक्षु॑रिव॒ यंत॒मनु॑ नेषथा  ॒
> सुगं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभ्राजि । शर्धः । मरुतः । यत् । अर्णसं । मोषथ । वृक्षं । कपनाऽइव । वेधसः ।  
> अध । स्म । नः । अरमतिं । सजोषसः । चक्षुऽइव । यंतं । अनु । नेषथ । सुgं॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वेधसो वृष्टेर्विधातारो हे मरुतः शर्धो भवतां गणमभ्राजि ।
> भ्राजते । यद्यस्मादर्णसमुदकवंतं वृक्षं । वृश्चते विदार्यत इति वृक्षो मेघः।
> तं मोषथ । ताडयथेत्यर्थः । कपनेव । इवेत्यनर्थकः । कंपनाः संतः । यद्वा ।
> कपनाः क्रिमयो वृक्षं घुणादयः । ते यथा मुष्णंति तद्वत् । अधापि च । स्मेति
> पूरणः । नोऽस्मान् । मामित्यर्थः । हे सजोषसो युष्मासु परस्परं समानप्रीतयो यूयमरमतिमारमणं धनादिकं प्रति यंतं गच्छंतमनु नेषथ
> अनुक्रमेण नयथ सुगं सुगमनं मार्गं । तत्र दृष्टांतः । चक्षुरिव । तद्यथा
> मार्गप्रदर्शनेन नायकं भवति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vedhasaḥ, makers of rain, O Maruts, your host shines forth, because you strike the water-laden tree. The tree is the cloud, so called because it is torn open, split. To strike it means to beat it. The word for "like" is without meaning here, so: shaking it. Or else, as worms such as wood-borers gnaw a tree, so you do. The particle स्मेति (*smeti*) is a mere filler; "us" means "me". O you of one accord, of equal affection among yourselves, lead us in due order, as we go toward wealth and the like, along an easy road. The illustration is the eye: as the eye becomes a guide by showing the way, so you do.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)—O makers of rain
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अर्णसं (*arṇasaṃ*)—water-laden
- वृक्षं (*vṛkṣaṃ*)—the cloud
- कपनेव (*kapaneva*)—as if shaking it
- मोषथ (*moṣatha*)—you strike (then)
- शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)—your host, full of strength
- अभ्राजि (*abhrāji*)—shines forth
### Printed p. 664
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—you who rejoice among yourselves with equal affection
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- चक्षुरिव (*cakṣuriva*)—as the eye carries its master to the desired place
- अरमतिं (*aramatiṃ*)—to the place of wealth
- यंतं (*yaṃtaṃ*)—going and reaching
- सुगं (*sugaṃ*)—to the excellent road
- अनु नेषथ (*anu neṣatha*)—you have led

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, makers of rain, when you strike the water-laden cloud as if shaking it, then the strength of your host shines forth, manifest. You who rejoice among yourselves with equal affection, lead us on the excellent road that goes to the place of wealth, as the eye (the organ of sight) carries its master to the desired place.

##### English translation
Maruts, dispensers of rain, your strength is manifested when, haking the water-laden cloud, you let loose the shower: conjointly propitiated, conduct us by an easy path leading to prosperity, as the eye (shows the way). **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वृक्षं (*vṛkṣaṃ*)—Here the word vṛkṣa is given the meaning of cloud: वृश्चते विदार्यत इति वृक्षो मेघः (*vṛścate vidāryata iti vṛkṣo meghaḥ*). For the sake of rain, that is, to pour down rain, Indra splits the clouds with his thunderbolt; and the Marut deities (the violently blowing winds) split, that is, scatter, the clouds gathered together in the atmosphere and make the rain fall. Therefore, because they are split for the sake of rain, the clouds are called trees, and the etymological sense of the word vṛkṣa is thus explained with reference to the cloud.
इव (*iva*)—(कसनाइव (*kasanāiva*), चक्षुःइव (*cakṣuḥiva*)) **NOTE** The word has two or three meanings:
अथ निपाताः । उच्चावचेष्वर्थेषु निपतंति । अप्युपमार्थेऽपि कर्मोपसंग्रहार्थेऽपि पदपूरणाः । तेषामेते चत्वार उपमार्थे भवंति । इवेति भाषायां च । अन्वध्यायञ्चाग्निरिवेंद्र इवेति ॥ (*atha nipātāḥ | uccāvaceṣvartheṣu nipataṃti | apyupamārthe 'pi karmopasaṃgrahārthe 'pi padapūraṇāḥ | teṣāmete catvāra upamārthe bhavaṃti | iveti bhāṣāyāṃ ca | anvadhyāyañcāgniriveṃdra iveti ‖*) (3 1-4) **NOTE**
Thus Yāska has given the explanation. Beginning with "now we shall explain the nature of the words called nipāta", and answering the question what nipātas are: certain words or letters, upasargas or indeclinables, that join with nouns and verbs, that is, with the subanta and tiṅanta words denoting agent and action, and produce many meanings, are called nipātas. Because they are used in many kinds of meanings (अनेकप्रकारेष्टर्थेषु निपतंतीति निपाताः (*anekaprakāreṣṭartheṣu nipataṃtīti nipātāḥ*)), they are called nipātas.
### Printed p. 665
Of these nipātas, their use in meanings such as "and" and "comparison" is the more frequent. The four given below have the sense of comparison. Among them the word इव (*iva*) is used in the language, that is, in prose sentences not bound by metre or in modern Sanskrit, and also in chandas (the Ṛks). Thus, in अग्निरिव (*agniriva*) and इंद्र इव (*iṃdra iva*) the word is used in the sense of comparison. And it is also seen (इवोऽपि दृश्यते (*ivo 'pi dṛśyate*); sometimes it is without meaning, is the remainder of the sentence), as in सुविदुरिव (*suviduriva*), सुविज्ञायेतॆ इव (*suvijñāyetè iva*). In some contexts the word is used merely to fill out the sentence, without any specific meaning. In such contexts it has no meaning of any kind. In सुविदुरिव (*suviduriva*) the sense is only "is well known"; the word इव (*iva*) has no meaning.

> वा । सुसूदथ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयं यमृषिं मंत्रद्रष्टारं ब्राह्मणं राजानं वा
> सूषूदथ क्षारयथ प्रेरयथ सत्कर्मसु स ऋषी राजा ना न जीयते । अन्न्यैर्न
> पराभाव्यते ॥ जि जये ज्या वयोहानावित्यस्य वा रूपं ॥ हे मरुतो न हन्यते ।
> न हिंस्यते । अत्यर्थं प्राणैर्न वियुज्यते । न स्त्रेधति । न क्षीयते । न व्यथते । न
> पीड्यते । न रिष्यति । न हिंस्यते । अत्र हिंसा बाधमात्रं । अस्य रायो धनानि नोप
> दस्यंति । नोपक्षीयंते । तथा नोतयो रक्षा अप्युप दस्यंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, whatever seer, a Brāhmaṇa who sees the mantra, or whatever king you rouse and impel to good works, that seer or king is not overcome, not defeated by others; जि जये ज्या वयोहानावित्यस्य (*ji jaye jyā vayohānāvityasya*): he refers to the root for conquering, or this is a form of the root for decay of life. O Maruts, he is not slain, not harmed; he is not violently separated from his life-breaths. He does not decay, does not waste away. He is not pained, not afflicted. He is not injured; here injury means mere hindrance. His riches do not fall away, and likewise his protections do not fall away.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts (you)
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whichever

- सुषूदथ (*suṣūdatha*)—you impel to good works
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- न जीयते (*na jīyate*)—is not overcome by anyone
- न हन्यते (*na hanyate*)—is not slain
- न प्रेधति (*na predhati*)—does not suffer decay **NOTE**
- न व्यथते (*na vyathate*)—is not afflicted
- न रिष्यति (*na riṣyati*)—is not injured
- अस्य (*asya*)—his
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—riches
- न उप दस्यंति (*na upa dasyaṃti*)—do not decay
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- न (*na*)—do not decay

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, whatever seer or king you impel to good works, he is not overcome by anyone. He is not slain. He does not suffer decay. He is not afflicted. He is not injured. His riches do not decay. His protections also do not fail.

##### English translation
The sage, or the sovereign, whom you, Maruts, direct, is never overcome nor slain: he perishes not, nor suffers pain, nor undergoes injury, nor are his riches or his safety imperilled.

> नियुत्वंतो नियुत्संज्ञकैरश्वैस्तंद्वतो मरुतो ग्रामजितः संघात्मकस्य
> पदार्थस्य विश्लेषयितारो नरो नराकारा नेतारो ना । मरुतो नियुत्वंतः ।
> अयं शब्दोऽत्राश्वसामान्ये वर्तते । नितरां यवनवंतोऽश्ववंतो ग्रामजितो
> ग्रामस्य जेतारो नर इव मनुष्या इव तथा भवंति । आर्यमणो न आर्यमप्रभृतय आदित्या इव । दीप्ता इति शेषः । तादृशा मरुतः कवंधिन उदकवंतो
> भवंति । यद्यदेनास ईश्वरा उत्सं कूपादिनिम्न प्रदेशं मेघं वा पिन्नंति व्याययंत्युदकेन। यदास्वरन् शब्दयंति यदा व्युंदंति पृथिवीं मध्यो मधुरस्कोदकस्यांधसा सारेण तदैवं भवंति । यद्वा । यदास्वरन् तदा पिन्नंत्युत्समिनासः
> तदांधस्य पृथिवीं व्युंदंतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Kārīrī alone, the verse नियुत्वंत इत्येषा (*niyutvaṃta ityeṣā*) is the yājyā of the third piṇḍī. **NOTE** It is also stated in the sūtra: नियुत्वंतो ग्रामजितो यथा नरोऽर्यमणो न मरुतः कवंधिनः । पिन्वंत्युत्सं यदिनासो अस्वरन्‌व्यंदंति पृथिवीं मध्यो अंधसा ॥ ८ ॥ नियुत्वंतः । ग्रामजितः । यथा । नरः । अर्यमणः । न । मरुतः । कवंधिनः । पिन्वंति । उत्सं । यत् । इनासः । अस्वरन् । वि । उंदंति । पृथिवीं । मध्यः । अंधसा ॥ ८ ॥ कारीर्यामेव तृतीयस्याः पिंड्या याज्या नियुत्वंत इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । नियुत्वंतो ग्रामजितो यथा नरोऽग्ने बाधस्व वि मृधो वि दुर्गहा । (*niyutvaṃto grāmajito yathā naro 'ryamaṇo na marutaḥ kavaṃdhinaḥ | pinvaṃtyutsaṃ yadināso asvaranvyaṃdaṃti pṛthivīṃ madhyo aṃdhasā ‖ 8 ‖ niyutvaṃtaḥ | grāmajitaḥ | yathā | naraḥ | aryamaṇaḥ | na | marutaḥ | kavaṃdhinaḥ | pinvaṃti | utsaṃ | yat | ināsaḥ | asvaran | vi | uṃdaṃti | pṛthivīṃ | madhyaḥ | aṃdhasā ‖ 8 ‖ kārīryāmeva tṛtīyasyāḥ piṃḍyā yājyā niyutvaṃta ityeṣā | sūtritaṃ ca | niyutvaṃto grāmajito yathā naro 'gne bādhasva vi mṛdho vi durgahā |*) (Ā. 2-13). The Maruts are possessed of the horses called Niyut, and this word here refers to horses in general; they are those who are strongly yoked, owners of horses. They are conquerors of a multitude, that is, dissolvers of a thing that is a compound whole; they are men in form, leaders, like men who conquer a village. They are like the Ādityas beginning with Aryaman, shining. Such Maruts are water-bearing. When, as lords, they fill the well or any low place, or the cloud, with water, when they sound, and when they moisten the earth with the essence of the sweet water, then they are so. Or else: when they sound, then the lords fill the spring, and then they moisten the earth with the sustenance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नियुत्वंतः (*niyutvaṃtaḥ*)—possessors of the horses called Niyut
- ग्रामजितः (*grāmajitaḥ*)—dissolvers of what is in compound form
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—leaders
- आर्यमणो न (*āryamaṇo na*)—radiant like the Ādityas beginning with Aryaman
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—Maruts
- कवंधिनः (*kavaṃdhinaḥ*)—are water-bearing
- यत् (*yat*)—at the very time when
- ईनासः (*īnāsaḥ*)—the Maruts, who are lords
- उत्सं (*utsaṃ*)—places such as wells
- पिन्नंति (*pinnaṃti*)—they fill with water
- अस्वरन् (*asvaran*)—sounding
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of the water **NOTE**
- अंधसा (*aṃdhasā*)—with the essence
- व्युंदंति (*vyuṃdaṃti*)—they make it drenched

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, who are possessed of the horses called Niyut, dissolvers of what is in compound form, leaders, radiant like the Ādityas beginning with Aryaman, are water-bearing. Those same Maruts, lords of all water, fill places such as wells with water. Sounding, they make the earth drenched with the essence of the water.

##### English translation
Lords of the Niyut steeds, overcomers of multitudes, leaders (of rites), radiant as the Adityas, are the dispensers of water : when sovereign lords, they fill the clouds, and, loud sounding, moisten the earth with sweet (watery) sustenance.

### Printed p. 668

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the third piṇḍa offering of the Kārīrī sacrifice this Ṛk beginning नियुत्वंत (*niyutvaṃta*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra नियुत्वंतो ग्रामजितो यथा नरोऽग्ने बाधस्व वि मृधो वि दुर्गहा (*niyutvaṃto grāmajito yathā naro 'gne bādhasva vi mṛdho vi durgahā*) (Ā. 2-13).
नियुत्वंतः (*niyutvaṃtaḥ*)—The word नियुत् (*niyut*) denotes the horse that is the vehicle of the deity Vāyu; in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-28) it is read नियुतो वायोः (*niyuto vāyoḥ*). But in the present Ṛk, since it is an epithet of the word नरः (*naraḥ*), which means a man, the bhāṣyakāra has said अयं शब्दोऽत्राश्वसामान्ये वर्तते । नितरां यवनवंतोऽश्ववंतो जेतारो नर इव मनुष्या इव । (*ayaṃ śabdo 'trāśvasāmānye vartate | nitarāṃ yavanavaṃto 'śvavaṃto jetāro nara iva manuṣyā iva |*). Here this word नियुत् (*niyut*) has the general meaning of horse. नितरां यवनवंतः नियुतः (*nitarāṃ yavanavaṃtaḥ niyutaḥ*): because they have especially, that is swiftly, the nature of going (the nature of running), नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*) means horses; this is the etymological sense of the word. The meaning stated here is: like men who are provided with such horses and are victorious.
आर्यमणः (*āryamaṇaḥ*)—The deity Aryamā is one of the deities called Ādityas, the sons of Aditi. To indicate these Ādityas, or the other deities who are sons of Aditi, the plural of the word अर्यमन् (*aryaman*) is used here.
आदित्यान् विष्णुं सूर्यं ब्रह्माणं च बृहस्पतिं । इंद्रवायू बृहस्पतिं सुहवेह हवामहे । अर्यमणं बृहस्पतमिंद्रं दानाय जोदय । वातं विष्णुं सरस्वतीं सवितारं च वाजिनं ॥ (*ādityān viṣṇuṃ sūryaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca bṛhaspatiṃ | iṃdravāyū bṛhaspatiṃ suhaveha havāmahe | aryamaṇaṃ bṛhaspatamiṃdraṃ dānāya jodaya | vātaṃ viṣṇuṃ sarasvatīṃ savitāraṃ ca vājinaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-141-3, 4, 5)
In these Ṛks the deities called Ādityas are indicated as the deities Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Brahmā, Bṛhaspati, Indra, Vāyu, Aryamā, Sarasvatī and so on. And on the question who the deities that are sons of Aditi are:
सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः । उपप्रैत्पूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्यवे तत् । परामार्तांडमाभरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंशश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्श्चेत्येते । (*saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ | upapraitpūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyave tat | parāmārtāṃḍamābharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃśaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāgścetyete |*) (Trai. Ā. 1-13-2) **NOTE**
In this sentence of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka it is said that Aditi has eight sons: Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Aryamā, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān. Either these eight deities or other deities are indicated in the present Ṛk by the word आर्यमणः (*āryamaṇaḥ*).

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र॒वत्व॑ती॒यं पृ॑थि॒वी म॒रुद्भ्यः॑ प्र॒वत्व॑ती॒ द्यौर्भ॑वति  ॒॑
> प्र॒यद्भ्यः॑ ।  
> प्र॒वत्व॑तीः प॒थ्या॑ अं॒तरि॑क्ष्याः प्र॒वत्वं॑तः॒ पर्व॑ता जी॒रदा॑नवः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रवत्वती । इयं । पृथिवी । मरुत्ऽभ्यः । प्रवत्वती । द्यौः । भवति । प्रयुत्ऽभ्यः ।  
> प्रवत्वतीः । पथ्याः । अंतरिक्ष्याः । प्रवत्वंतः । पर्वताः । जीरदानवः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयं पृथिवी मरुद्भ्यो मरुतामर्थाय प्रवत्वती । प्रवंतः प्रकर्षवंतो
> विस्तीर्णाः प्रदेशा यस्यां सा प्रवत्वती । तादृशी भवति । कृत्सापि भूमिर्मरुत्परा
> भवतीत्यर्थः । तां सर्वामपि व्याप्नुवंतीति यावत् । तथा द्यौरपि प्रयद्भ्यः प्रकर्षेण गच्छद्भ्यस्तेभ्यः प्रवत्वती भवति । सापि मरुतां संचाराय ।
> तथांतरिक्ष्या अंतरिक्षे भवाः पथ्याः स्नुगतयोऽपि प्रवत्वतीः प्रवत्वत्यो मरुद्भ्यो
> भवंति । पर्वता अद्रयो मेघा वा प्रवत्वंतो भवंति जीरदानवः क्षिप्रदाना
> मरुद्भ्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This earth is for the Maruts, for the sake of the Maruts, prakṛṣṭa, full of wide expanses: the places in it are extensive and wide-spreading. That is, the whole earth is devoted to the Maruts; the meaning is that they pervade all of it. So too heaven becomes full of wide expanses for them as they go forth; it too is for the Maruts' movement. Likewise the paths that belong to the atmosphere, **NOTE** are also wide-spreading for the Maruts. The mountains, whether rocks or clouds, are wide-spreading, and the जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*) are those that give quickly to the Maruts.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इयं पृथिवी (*iyaṃ pṛthivī*)—this earth
- मरुद्भ्यः (*marudbhyaḥ*)—for the Maruts
- प्रवत्वती (*pravatvatī*)—having wide expanses
- भवति (*bhavati*)—is
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the heavenly world also
- प्रयद्भ्यः (*prayadbhyaḥ*)—for the Maruts, who have excellent movement
- प्रवत्वती (*pravatvatī*)—has widely spread expanses
- अंतरिक्ष्याः (*aṃtarikṣyāḥ*)—belonging to the atmosphere
- पथ्याः (*pathyāḥ*)—the paths also
- प्रवत्वतीः (*pravatvatīḥ*)—are spread out (for their very movement)
- जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*)—that give rain abundantly
- पर्वताः (*parvatāḥ*)—the clouds also
- प्रवत्वंतः (*pravatvaṃtaḥ*)—have the same quality

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the easy movement of the Maruts, this earth, the atmosphere, the heavenly world, the mountains, and all the places where the Maruts move, are greatly extending their regions and helping the Maruts.
### Printed p. 670

##### English translation
This wide-extended earth is for the Maruts: the spacious heaven is for the spreading winds; the paths of the firmament are provided (for their course); for them the expanding clouds quickly bestow (their gifts).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यन्म॑रुतः सभरसः स्वर्णरः॒ सूर्य॒ उदि॑ते॒ मद॑था दिवो  
> नरः ।  
> न वोऽश्वाः॑ श्रथयं॒ताह॒ सिस्र॑तः स॒द्यो अ॒स्माध्व॑नः पा॒रम॑श्नुथ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । मरुतः । सभरसः । स्वःनरः । सूर्ये । उत् इते । मदथ । दिवः । नरः ।  
> न । वः । अश्वाः । श्रथयंत । अह । सिस्रतः । सद्यः । अस्य । अध्वनः । पारं । अश्नुथ ॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतः सभरसः सहबलाः स्वर्णरः सर्वस्य नेतारो यूयं यद्यदा
> सूर्य उदित उद्दते मध्याह्ने मदथ सोमेन हे दिवो द्युलोकस्य नरो
> नेतारः । यदा सोमं पातुमिच्छथेत्यर्थः । तदा वोऽश्वाः सिस्रतः सरंतो नाह
> श्रथयंत । नैव श्लथयंति । सद्यस्तदानीमेवास्याध्वनो देवयजनमार्गस्य पारमश्नुथ । व्याप्नुथ । यद्वा । यदा सोमेन मदथ तदा त्वदीया अश्वा न शिथिला
> भवंति । यूयं च कृत्स्नस्य लोकत्रयमार्गस्य पारमश्नुथ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, of equal strength, leaders of all, when the sun has risen, at midday, you rejoice with Soma, O leaders of the heavenly world; that is, when you wish to drink Soma, then your horses, running, do not slacken at all. **NOTE** Immediately then you reach the far end of this road, the path to the place of the gods' sacrifice; you pervade it. Or else: when you rejoice with Soma, then your horses are not slack, and you reach the end of the whole path of the three worlds.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सभरसः (*sabharasaḥ*)—those of combined strength
- स्वर्णरः (*svarṇaraḥ*)—leaders of the whole universe
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—leaders
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सूर्य्य उदिते (*sūryya udite*)—when the sun has risen
- मदथ (*madatha*)—when you rejoice with the drinking of Soma, then
### Printed p. 671
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- सिस्रतः (*sisrataḥ*)—swift-going
- अश्वाः (*aśvāḥ*)—horses
- न अह श्रथयंत (*na aha śrathayaṃta*)—do not take rest at all
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—immediately
- अस्य अध्वनः (*asya adhvanaḥ*)—of the road that comes to this sacrificial ground
- पारं (*pāraṃ*)—the end
- अश्नुथ (*aśnutha*)—you reach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, of combined strength, leaders of the whole universe, as soon as the sun has risen you rejoice with the drinking of Soma. At that time your swift-going horses have no rest whatever. Immediately you traverse fully the road that leads to the sacrificial ground and come here.

##### English translation
Maruts of combined strength, leaders of the universe, guides of heaven, when the sun has risen you rejoice (in the Soma beverage), then your rapid steeds know no relaxation, but quickly you reach the limits of this road (to the sacrifice).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, on your shoulders the ऋष्टयः (*ṛṣṭayaḥ*), the weapons, shine (this is to be supplied). On your feet are the खादयः (*khādayaḥ*), anklets. On your breasts are the रुक्मा (*rukmā*), necklaces. In the chariot are the शुभः (*śubhaḥ*), the waters **NOTE**. The lightnings, blazing with fire, shine in your arms, that is, in your hands. On the heads the हिरण्ययीः (*hiraṇyayīḥ*), golden, शिप्राः (*śiprāḥ*), turbans, are spread out. The word वितता (*vitatā*) is not to be connected with each sentence.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- अंगेषु (*aṃgeṣu*)—on the arms **NOTE**
- ऋष्टयः (*ṛṣṭayaḥ*)—weapons
- पत्सु (*patsu*)—on the feet
- खादयः (*khādayaḥ*)—anklets
- वक्षसु (*vakṣasu*)—on the breasts
- रुक्माः (*rukmāḥ*)—necklaces
- रथे (*rathe*)—in the chariot
- शुभः (*śubhaḥ*)—sweet waters
- गभस्त्योः (*gabhastyoḥ*)—in the hands
- अग्निभ्राजसः (*agnibhrājasaḥ*)—having the radiance of fire
- विद्युतः (*vidyutaḥ*)—lightnings
- शीर्षसु (*śīrṣasu*)—on the heads
- हिरण्ययीः (*hiraṇyayīḥ*)—made of gold
- शिप्राः (*śiprāḥ*)—tiaras
- वितताः (*vitatāḥ*)—shine widely spread

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, on your arms weapons, on your feet anklets, on your breasts necklaces, in your chariot sweet waters, in your hands lightnings with the radiance of fire, and on your heads tiaras made of gold shine, widely spread.

##### English translation
Lances (gleam), Maruts, upon your shoulders, anklets on your feet, golden cuirasses on your breasts, and pure (waters shine) in your chariots: lightnings blazing with fire glow in your hands, and golden tiaras are towering on your heads

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is explained in detail on which limbs the Marut deities wear which ornaments. Thus: on the arms they wear weapons called ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*) (spears); on the legs they wear anklets or foot-rings; on the chest they wear necklaces; in the hands they wear lightning (the flash) that shines like fire, or special weapons that gleam like lightning; on the head they wear शिप्राः (*śiprāḥ*), that is, a golden head-covering or the ornament called a tiara; thus the adornments and so on of the Marut deities are described very well.

> धूनुथेति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, goers, you set in motion that well-known नाकं (*nākaṃ*), the sun: it is so called because there is no pain in it. Its lustre is not seized, that is, not carried off by the Asuras; it is bright-coloured, white, and you shake the water, the pippala, variously; the verb takes two objects. When the strengths are united, that is, when you become strong, through the oblations given by us, and afterwards become radiant, the person of the verb is changed in both cases. Or else: when the Asuras, with their strengths united, blaze, then you, desiring water, make a far-spread, fear-causing sound, घोषं (*ghoṣaṃ*). Or else the second half is to be explained as about the priest and the sacrificer: when those desiring sacrifice, the sacrificers and the rest, are gathered, their strengths blaze and they sound the stotra spread far, then the connection is that you shake the water.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—you who move about
- तं नाकं (*taṃ nākaṃ*)—the well-known atmosphere **NOTE**
- अगृभीतशोचिषं (*agṛbhītaśociṣaṃ*)—having a lustre not carried off by enemies
- रुशत् (*ruśat*)—having a brightly shining part
- पिप्पलं (*pippalaṃ*)—and the water
- वि धूनुथ (*vi dhūnutha*)—you set in motion
- ऋतायवः (*ṛtāyavaḥ*)—you who wish to pour water in the form of rain
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वृजना (*vṛjanā*)—your powers
- समच्यंत (*samacyaṃta*)—you gather together, then
- अति त्विष्टंत (*ati tviṣṭaṃta*)—you shine exceedingly **NOTE**
- विततं (*vitataṃ*)—widely spread
- घोषं (*ghoṣaṃ*)—the sound
- स्वरंति (*svaraṃti*)—you make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, you who move about, set in motion the well-known atmosphere and the water, whose lustre is not carried off by enemies and which is bright and shining. You who wish to pour down water in the form of rain, when you gather your powers together, then, shining exceedingly, you make a far-spread sound.

##### English translation
Maruts, when moving, you agitate the heaven of unchecked radiancc, and (stir) the bright water : when you combine your energies and are shining brilliantly, and when purposing to send down rain, you utter a loud shout. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Nirukta-writers include the word नाक (*nāka*) among six common names and explain their meaning as common: साधारणान्युत्तराणि षट् दिवश्चादित्यस्य च (*sādhāraṇānyuttarāṇi ṣaṭ divaścādityasya ca*), that is, they declare them to be synonyms common to the heavenly world and to the sun (Ni. 2-13). Afterwards, showing the explanation of this word: नाक आदित्यो भवति—नेता रसानां। नेता भासां ज्योतिषां प्रणयः । (*nāka ādityo bhavati—netā rasānāṃ| netā bhāsāṃ jyotiṣāṃ praṇayaḥ |*) (Ni. 2-14): having shown that the name नाक (*nāka*) belongs to the sun, who is the carrier of the sap and the carrier of splendour, as a synonym of the sun, they go on: अथ द्यौः। कमिति सुखनाम तत्पतिषिद्धं प्रतिषिध्येत । (*atha dyauḥ| kamiti sukhanāma tatpatiṣiddhaṃ pratiṣidhyeta |*). The word कं (*kaṃ*) is a synonym for happiness; the absence of happiness is अकं (*akaṃ*), and the absence of that, that is, the absence of the lack of happiness, means that which is free from sorrow. Explaining thus, they cite the sentence न ना अमुं लोकं जग्मु षे किं च नाकं (*na nā amuṃ lokaṃ jagmu ṣe kiṃ ca nākaṃ*) (Kāraka. Saṃ. 21.-2) **NOTE** and then न ना अमुं लोकं गतवते किंच नासुखं ; पुण्यकृतो ह्येव तत्र गच्छंति । (*na nā amuṃ lokaṃ gatavate kiṃca nāsukhaṃ ; puṇyakṛto hyeva tatra gacchaṃti |*). Those who have gone to this world (heaven) have no sorrow at all; only the virtuous have entry into this world: thus they have given the meaning of the word नाक (*nāka*). In the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā this word is used in some places as a synonym of the sun and in some places as a synonym of heaven.
त्रिरश्विना सिंधुभिः सप्तमातृभिस्त्रिय आहानास्त्रेधा हविष्कृतं । तिस्रः पृथिवीरुपरि प्रवा दिवो नाकं रक्षेथे द्युभिरक्तुभिर्हितं ॥ (*triraśvinā siṃdhubhiḥ saptamātṛbhistriya āhānāstredhā haviṣkṛtaṃ | tisraḥ pṛthivīrupari pravā divo nākaṃ rakṣethe dyubhiraktubhirhitaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-8)
### Printed p. 675
ये नाकस्याधि रोचने दिवि देवास आसते । मरुद्भिरग्न आ गहि ॥ (*ye nākasyādhi rocane divi devāsa āsate | marudbhiragna ā gahi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-19-6)
In these and other Ṛks the word is a synonym of the sun; and in
तेवर्धंत स्वतवसो महित्वना नाकं तस्थुरुरु चक्रिरे सदः । विष्णुरद्धावद्वृषणं मदच्युतं वयो न सीदन्नधि बर्हिषि प्रिये ॥ ( (*tevardhaṃta svatavaso mahitvanā nākaṃ tasthururu cakrire sadaḥ | viṣṇuraddhāvadvṛṣaṇaṃ madacyutaṃ vayo na sīdannadhi barhiṣi priye ‖ (*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.85.7)
यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवास्तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् । ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचंत यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः संति देवाः ॥ (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāstāni dharmāṇi prathamānyāsan | te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacaṃta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ saṃti devāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-50)
and other Ṛks it is also a synonym of heaven.
व्यस्यॆव कपिलो भूत्वा यन्नाकमधिरोहति (*vyasyèva kapilo bhūtvā yannākamadhirohati*) (Bṛ. De. 2-66)
In this sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā it is clear that the atmosphere is meant.
इतोऽसावादित्यो द्वाविंशेन परमादित्याज्जयति तन्नाकं तद्विशोकं (*ito 'sāvādityo dvāviṃśena paramādityājjayati tannākaṃ tadviśokaṃ*)
इतोऽसावादित्यो द्वाविंशेन परमादित्याज्जयति तन्नाकं तद्विशोकं (*ito 'sāvādityo dvāviṃśena paramādityājjayati tannākaṃ tadviśokaṃ*) (Chā. U. 2-10-5)
In this sentence of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad it is said that the sorrowless heavenly world is better than the world of the sun.
[In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad the name नाक (*nāka*) is well known for the son of Mudgala, who knew Brahman; there it means one free from sorrow.]
In the present Ṛk, न विद्यते अकं दुःखं तत्साधनं पापं वेति नाको द्युलोकः । (*na vidyate akaṃ duḥkhaṃ tatsādhanaṃ pāpaṃ veti nāko dyulokaḥ |*): the commentator has explained it as the atmosphere, in which there is neither sorrow nor the sin that is its cause.
अच्यंत (*acyaṃta*), अतित्विषंत (*atitviṣaṃta*)—in these two verbs there is a change of person; that is, instead of the plural of the middle person, the plural of the first person is used.
यत् वृजना समच्यंत अतित्विषंत—यदा अस्मद्दत्तैर्हनिर्भिः बलिनो भवथ तदा दीप्ता भवथ । (*yat vṛjanā samacyaṃta atitviṣaṃta—yadā asmaddattairhanirbhiḥ balino bhavatha tadā dīptā bhavatha |*). O Marut deities, when you accept (eat) the oblations and the like that we offer, then, grown strong by accepting the oblations, that is, by their power, shine well: this is one kind of meaning that the commentator has stated, and he has shown that another kind of meaning is possible. यदासुरा वृजना अतित्विषंत तदा घोषं विततु स्वरंति (*yadāsurā vṛjanā atitviṣaṃta tadā ghoṣaṃ vitatu svaraṃti*): when the Asuras, grown strong with the pride of their strength, swagger about, then you (the Marut deities), to subdue them, make a terrible sound: this is another kind of meaning.
### Printed p. 676
Or else, for the second half of this Ṛk, besides these two meanings, another meaning with reference to the priests and sacrificers is possible, and he has explained it also: यत् ऋतायवः समच्यंत वृजन अति त्वषंत च स्वरंति घोषं पिप्पलं विधूनुथ (*yat ṛtāyavaḥ samacyaṃta vṛjana ati tvaṣaṃta ca svaraṃti ghoṣaṃ pippalaṃ vidhūnutha*) and यदा यज्ञकामा यजमानादयो संगताः बलान्यतित्वषंत स्तोत्रं विततं स्वरंति च तदानीं पिप्पलं विधूनुथ । (*yadā yajñakāmā yajamānādayo saṃgatāḥ balānyatitvaṣaṃta stotraṃ vitataṃ svaraṃti ca tadānīṃ pippalaṃ vidhūnutha |*). When people such as the priests and sacrificers, with the wish to perform a sacrifice addressed to you, all assemble together in one place and, reciting stotras and mantras in a loud voice, extend, that is, carry forward, the sacrificial rite, then you, Marut deities, make the excellent water pour down for the satisfaction of the sacrificers: this is the chief intention.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts of manifold wisdom, may we become lords of the wealth given by you, wealth that gives food, we who are owners of chariots. **NOTE** The wealth given by you does not fail, does not decay: as the sun, Tiṣya, does not fail from the sky, so grant us among us this wealth, a thousandfold, without measure. Make us delight, O Maruts.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts of manifold wisdom, may we, who are lords of chariots, become lords of the wealth given by you and endowed with food. As the sun in the atmosphere is imperishable, in the same way that wealth given by you does not perish. O Maruts, give us immeasurable wealth and make us rejoice.

##### English translation
May we, who are possessed of chariots, intelligent Maruts, become (proprietors) of wealth, comprising food bestowed by you : of wealth that vanishes not, as Tishya (declines not) from the sky: therefore, Maruts, gratify us with infinite (riches).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अस्मे (*asme*)—The Nirukta-writers explain that the word अस्मे (*asme*), although it has one and the same form in all the case-endings, conveys the sense of each case-ending according to the context, and show the difference in the respective examples:
(1) अस्मे ते बंधुः । वयमित्यर्थः (*asme te baṃdhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ*)
अस्मे इत्येतत्पदं सर्वविभक्त्यंतं । तस्मादनेकार्थं । एकमेव ह्येतच्छब्दरूपं सप्तस्वपि विभक्त्यर्थेषु वर्तते । प्रकरणादिवशात् तस्य नियमो भवति । (*asme ityetatpadaṃ sarvavibhaktyaṃtaṃ | tasmādanekārthaṃ | ekameva hyetacchabdarūpaṃ saptasvapi vibhaktyartheṣu vartate | prakaraṇādivaśāt tasya niyamo bhavati |*). Thus, for the first case-ending: अस्मे ते बंधुः । वयमित्यर्थः (*asme te baṃdhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ*). That is, the word अस्मे (*asme*) is used in the sense of all seven case-endings according to the context; that is, according to the context, this word can be said to have the meaning of any one of the seven case-endings. Thus, in the sentence अस्मे ते बंधुः (*asme te baṃdhuḥ*) the word अस्मे (*asme*) has the meaning वयं (*vayaṃ*), "we". This is an example of the sense of the first case-ending.
### Printed p. 678
(2) अस्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । अस्मानित्यर्थः (*asme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | asmānityarthaḥ*)
Thus, for the second case-ending: the word अस्मे (*asme*) has the meaning of the second case-ending, अस्मान् (*asmān*), "us". As an example of this meaning they have given the Ṛk
आ श्येनस्य जवसा नूतनेनास्मे यातं नासत्या शजोषाः । हवे हि वामश्विना रातहव्यः शश्वत्तमाया उषसो व्युष्टौ ॥ (*ā śyenasya javasā nūtanenāsme yātaṃ nāsatyā śajoṣāḥ | have hi vāmaśvinā rātahavyaḥ śaśvattamāyā uṣaso vyuṣṭau ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-11) **NOTE**
In this Ṛk the word अस्मे (*asme*) means अस्मान् (*asmān*), "us".
(3) अस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । अस्माभिरित्यर्थः (*asme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | asmābhirityarthaḥ*)
Thus, for the third case-ending: here अस्मे (*asme*) means अस्माभिः (*asmābhiḥ*), "by us", the sense of the third case-ending. On this point
भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । भूरीणि हि कृणवामा शविष्ठेंद्र क्रत्वा मरुतो यद्वशाम ॥ (*bhūri cakartha yujyebhirasme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭheṃdra kratvā maruto yadvaśāma ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-7)
this Ṛk has been given as the example. Here अस्मे (*asme*) means अस्माभिः (*asmābhiḥ*), "by us".
(4) अस्मे प्रयंधि मघवन्नृजीषिन् । अस्मभ्यमित्यर्थः (*asme prayaṃdhi maghavannṛjīṣin | asmabhyamityarthaḥ*)
Thus, for the fourth case-ending: here अस्मे (*asme*) means अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*), "for us", the sense of the fourth case-ending, is the example.
अस्मे प्र यंधि मघवन्नृजीषिन्निंद्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः । अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीराञ्श्वत इंद्र शिप्रिन् ॥ (*asme pra yaṃdhi maghavannṛjīṣinniṃdra rāyo viśvavārasya bhūreḥ | asme śataṃ śarado jīvase dhā asme vīrāñśvata iṃdra śiprin ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-36-10)
In the words अस्मे (*asme*) of this Ṛk the sense is अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*), "for us", the fourth case-ending.
(5) अस्मे आराच्चिद्देषः सनुतर्युयोतु । अस्मदित्यर्थः (*asme ārācciddeṣaḥ sanutaryuyotu | asmadityarthaḥ*)
Thus, for the fifth case-ending: here अस्मे (*asme*) means अस्मत् (*asmat*), "from our side". The example:

तस्य वयं सुमता यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम । स सुत्रामा स्वना इंद्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ॥ (*tasya vayaṃ sumatā yajñiyasyāpi bhadre saumanase syāma | sa sutrāmā svanā iṃdro asme ārācciddveṣaḥ sanutaryuyotu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-13)
In this Ṛk the word अस्मे (*asme*) has the sense of the fifth case-ending, अस्मत् (*asmat*), "from our side".
(6) ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे ! अस्माकमित्यर्थः (*ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme ! asmākamityarthaḥ*)
Thus, for the sixth case-ending: here अस्मे (*asme*) means अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*), "to us". To explain this meaning:
आ नो भर भगमिंद्र द्युमंतं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि प्ररेके । ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनां ॥ (*ā no bhara bhagamiṃdra dyumaṃtaṃ ni te deṣṇasya dhīmahi prareke | ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme tamā pṛṇa vasupate vasūnāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3 31--19) **NOTE**
In this Ṛk the word अस्मे (*asme*) has the sense of the sixth case-ending, अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*), "our, to us".
(7) अस्मे धत्त वसवो वसूनि । अस्मास्वित्यर्थः (*asme dhatta vasavo vasūni | asmāsvityarthaḥ*)
Thus, for the seventh case-ending: here अस्मे (*asme*) means "in us". The example:
अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो ! अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥ (*agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho ! asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-69-4) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-79-4)
In this Ṛk the word अस्मे (*asme*) has the sense of the seventh case-ending, अस्मासु (*asmāsu*), "in us".

> श्रुष्टि॒मंतं॑ ॥ ८४ ॥

### Printed p. 680

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यूयं । रयिं । मरुतः । स्पार्हवीरं । यूयं । ऋषिं । अवथ । सामविप्रं।  
> यूयं । अर्वंतं । भरताय । वाजं । यूयं । धत्थ । राजानं। श्रुष्टिमंतं॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयं रयिं धनं स्पार्हवीरं स्पृहणीयैर्वीरैः पुत्रभृत्यादिभिरुपेतं धत्थ । दत्थ । हे मरुतो यूयं सामविप्रं साम्मां विविधं प्रेरयितारां यद्वा सामसहिता विप्रा यस्य तादृशमृषिमवथ । रक्षथॆ । हे यूयमर्वंतमश्वं वाजमन्नं च भरताय देवान् बिभ्रते श्यावाश्वाय धत्थ । हे
> मरुतो यूयं राजानं दीप्तं स्वामिनं वा श्रुष्टिमंतं सुखवंतं । पुत्रमित्यर्थः । धत्थ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, you bestow wealth, that is, wealth accompanied by enviable heroes, namely sons, servants and the like; the verb धत्थ (*dhattha*) here means "you give". O Maruts, you protect the sage who is a सामविप्रं (*sāmavipraṃ*): either one who variously impels the Sāman, or one whose learned men (vipras) are accompanied by the Sāman. **NOTE** You give a horse and food to Bharata, that is, to Śyāvāśva, who bears the gods. O Maruts, you also grant a king, that is, a resplendent one or a master, who is endowed with happiness (श्रुष्टिमंतं (*śruṣṭimaṃtaṃ*)); the meaning is a son.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- स्पार्हवीरं (*spārhavīraṃ*)—enviable heroic sons and the like
- धत्त (*dhatta*)—you give
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- सामविप्रं (*sāmavipraṃ*)—who praises, knowing the nature of the Sāma mantras
- ऋषिं (*ṛṣiṃ*)—the sage
- अवथ (*avatha*)—you protect
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- भरताय (*bharatāya*)—to me, who bear the gods
- अर्वंतं (*arvaṃtaṃ*)—a horse
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food (you give)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- राजानं (*rājānaṃ*)—the king
- श्रुष्टिमंतं (*śruṣṭimaṃtaṃ*)—you make him endowed with prosperity and happiness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, you give wealth and enviable heroic sons and the like. You protect the sage who praises, knowing the nature of the Sāma mantras. To me, who bear the gods, you give a horse and food. You make the king endowed with prosperity and happiness.

##### English translation
You bestow, Maruts, wealth and enviable posterity: you protect the sage learned in the Sama: you grant horses and food to (me) the ministrant priest; you render a prince prosperous.

### Printed p. 681

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, which is the conclusion of the sūkta, and in the next Ṛk, the seer Śyāvāśva prays to the Marut deities to grant wealth, horses, food and other nourishment, sons, grandsons and the like, and long life, so that he may live up to a hundred years.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तद्यो॑ यामि॒ द्रवि॑णं सद्यऊतयो॒ येना॒ स्व१॒॑र्ण त॒तना॑म॒  ॒
> स्वरभि ।  
> इ॒दं सु मे॑ मरुतो हर्यता॒ वचो॒ यस्य॒ तरे॑म॒ तर॑सा ॒ ॑
> शतं हिमाः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । वः । यामि । द्रविणं । सद्यःऊतयः । येन । स्वः । न । ततनाम । न्यान् ।  
> अभि ।  
> इदं । सु । मे । मरुतः । हर्यत । वचः । यस्य । तरेनु । तरसा । शतं । हिमाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सद्यऊतयः । तदानीमेव रक्षा येषां ते तादृशाः । सद्योगमना वा
> वो युष्मान् तद्द विणं धनं यामि । याचामहे । येन धनेन नृनस्मत्पुत्रभृत्यादीनभि । ततनाम स्वर्ण आदित्य इव रश्मीन् । हे मरुतो मे मनु स्वभूतमिद.
> मिदानीं क्रियमाणं वचः स्तोत्रं सु सुष्टु हर्यत । कामयध्वं । यस्य स्तोत्रवचसस्तरसा बलेन शतं शतसंख्याकान् हिमा हेमंतान् तरेम । शतसंवत्सरं
> जीवेमेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O you who are सद्यऊतयः (*sadyaūtayaḥ*), that is, whose protection comes at that very moment, or whose coming is immediate: from you we ask that wealth, by which we may extend our sons, servants and the rest, as the sun extends his rays. O Maruts, desire well this praise now being made by me **NOTE**; by the strength of this praise we may pass a hundred winters, that is, live a hundred years.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सद्यऊतयः (*sadyaūtayaḥ*)—O Maruts, who give protection at once
- येन (*yena*)—by which wealth
- स्वर्ण (*svarṇa*)—as the sun spreads out his rays
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—our sons and the rest of our progeny

### Printed p. 682
- अभि (*abhi*) ततनाम (*tatanāma*)—we may extend and increase
- तत् (*tat*) द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—such wealth
- वः (*vaḥ*)—from you
- यामि (*yāmi*)—I ask
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which praise
- तरसा (*tarasā*)—by the strength
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—a hundred
- हिमाः (*himāḥ*)—winters (years)
- तरेम (*tarema*)—we may live
- मे (*me*)—by me
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—now made
- वचः (*vacaḥ*)—praise
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- हर्यत (*haryata*)—desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, who give protection as soon as you are prayed to, I ask of you that wealth by whose help we may extend and increase our sons and the rest of our progeny, as the sun spreads out his rays. O Maruts, desire exceedingly this praise made by me, by the strength of which we may live a hundred years.

##### English translation
Therefore do I solicit wealth of you, who are prompt to grant protection, whereby we may multiply our descendants, as the sun (spreads wide his rays): be propitiated, Maruts, by this my praise, by the efficacy whereof may we pass over a hundred winters.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तदानीमेव रक्षा येषां ते तादृशाः । सद्योगमना ना (*tadānīmeva rakṣā yeṣāṃ te tādṛśāḥ | sadyogamanā nā*) (on सद्यऊतयः (*sadyaūtayaḥ*)). The word सद्यऊतयः (*sadyaūtayaḥ*) suggests two meanings: that you should give us your protection at once, immediately; or that you should come to this place of sacrifice at once.

येन धनेन अस्मत्पुत्रभृत्यादीन् आदित्यरशीनिव ततनाम (*yena dhanena asmatputrabhṛtyādīn ādityaraśīniva tatanāma*). What is expressed here is the hope: just as the sun spreads his rays widely, so by the wealth and other gifts that the Marut deities give us, may we increase and extend our line of sons, grandsons and so on.

स्तोत्रवचसः बलेन वयं शतसंख्याकान् हेमंतान् शतसंवत्सरं जीवेमेत्यर्थः । (*stotravacasaḥ balena vayaṃ śatasaṃkhyākān hemaṃtān śatasaṃvatsaraṃ jīvemetyarthaḥ |*). The seer prays that, by the power of the hymns we recite addressed to the Marut deities, we may live up to a hundred years. The word हिमाः (*himāḥ*) means Hemanta, the Hemanta seasons. The Hemanta season comes only once in a

### Printed p. 683
year, and therefore शतं हिमाः (*śataṃ himāḥ*) means a hundred years. In the same way the use of the words शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*) also indicates the sense of a hundred years. Such usages are especially frequent in the Ṛgveda.

## Sūkta 55 (Maṇḍala 5)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रयज्यव इति दर्चशमेकादशं सूक्तं श्यावाश्वस्यार्षं मारुतं । दशमी
> त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा जगत्यः । प्रयज्यवो दशांत्या त्रिष्टुबित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ अभिप्लविके
> षष्ठेऽहन्याग्निमारुत इदं सूक्तं मारुतनिविद्धानीयं । सूत्रितं च । प्रयज्यव इमं
> स्तोममित्याग्निमारुतं । आ-७-७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning प्रयज्यव (*prayajyava*) is the eleventh, of ten Ṛks, and is the vision of Śyāvāśva, addressed to the Maruts. The tenth Ṛk is Triṣṭubh and the rest are Jagatī, as the Anukramaṇikā says: प्रयज्यवो दशांत्या त्रिष्टुप् (*prayajyavo daśāṃtyā triṣṭup*). In the Abhiplava rite, on the sixth day, in the Agni-Marut recitation, this sūkta serves as the Māruta nivid-inserted hymn. It is also taught in the sūtra: प्रयज्यव इमं स्तोममित्याग्निमारुतं (*prayajyava imaṃ stomamityāgnimārutaṃ*) (Ā. 7-7).
Anuvāda: The sūkta beginning प्रयज्यव (*prayajyava*) is the eleventh sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. Śyāvāśva is the seer of this sūkta; the Maruts are the deity. The tenth Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. The Anukramaṇikā states: प्रयज्यवो दशांत्या त्रिष्टुप् (*prayajyavo daśāṃtyā triṣṭup*). In the Abhiplava sacrifice, on the sixth day, when the Agni-Marut Śastra mantras are recited, this sūkta is to be inserted and recited as the मारुतनिविद्धानीयसूक्तवन्नागि (*mārutanividdhānīyasūktavannāgi*); this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra प्रयज्यव इमं स्तोममित्याग्निमारुतं (*prayajyava imaṃ stomamityāgnimārutaṃ*) (Ā. 7-7).
- Sūkta: 55.
- Maṇḍala 5; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 55.
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 3; Varga 17, 18.
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10.
- Ṛṣi: Śyāvāśva Ātreya.
- Deity: Maruts.
- Metre: 1–9 Jagatī; 10 Triṣṭubh.

> श्रीघ्रगैरश्वैरीयंते । प्राप्यंते । शुभं शोभनं यथा भवति तथा । यद्वा। उदकमभिलक्ष्य यातां गच्छतां मरुतां रथा अप्यन्ववृत्सत । अनुवर्तंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts are प्रयज्यवः (*prayajyavaḥ*), eminent sacrificers, and भ्राजदृष्टयः (*bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*), having shining weapons. They bear abundant वयः (*vayaḥ*), which is either the youthful age that is their mark or abundant food. They are रुक्ष्मवक्षसः (*rukṣmavakṣasaḥ*), having necklaces spread over their chests. Those Maruts are brought by swift horses that can be easily controlled, and they come splendidly. Or else: aiming at the water, the chariots of the Maruts as they go also follow them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रयज्यवः (*prayajyavaḥ*)—eminent sacrificers
- भ्राजदृष्टयः (*bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*)—having shining weapons
- रुक्ष्मवक्षसः (*rukṣmavakṣasaḥ*)—having necklaces on their chests
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—abundant
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—possess (and)
- सुयमेभिः (*suyamebhiḥ*)—capable of bearing them with ease
- आशुभिः (*āśubhiḥ*)—swift-moving
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—by horses
- ईयंते (*īyaṃte*)—are brought
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of well-being
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of them as they go
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots
- अनु (*anu*) अवृत्सत (*avṛtsata*)—follow them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, eminent sacrificers, having shining weapons and necklaces on their chests, possess abundant food. They are brought by swift-moving horses that are capable of bearing them with ease. As bringers of well-being, they go, and their chariots also follow them.

### Printed p. 685

##### English translation
The adorable Maruts, armed with bright lances and cuirassed with golden breast-plates, enjoy vigorous existence: may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

भ्राजदृष्टयः (*bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*)—भ्राजत् ऋष्टर्य (*bhrājat ṛṣṭarya*) **NOTE**. ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*) is a particular weapon of the Marut deities. It is said to be sharp, shining and spear-shaped. The meaning of the word भ्राजदृष्टयः (*bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*) is those who bear such shining weapons. The use of this word in describing the qualities of the Marut deities is special to them, and it indicates their distinction. This word is not much used of the other deities.

बृहत् (*bṛhat*) वयः (*vayaḥ*)—The commentator gives two kinds of meaning for these words. बृहत् (*bṛhat*) means large, much, abundant. If वयः (*vayaḥ*) is taken to mean food (Ni. 3-9), the sense is that they have abundant wealth of food, or that they give abundant food and other sustenance to the sacrificers who praise them. If वयः (*vayaḥ*) is taken to mean age, then बृहत् (*bṛhat*) means greater, and वयः (*vayaḥ*) means having age; that is, not young children but those who are like young men, endowed with the marks of youth; this is the intended sense.

रुक्मवक्षसः (*rukmavakṣasaḥ*)—Like the word भ्राजदृष्टयः (*bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*), the word रुक्मवक्षसः (*rukmavakṣasaḥ*) also is used only of the Marut deities. It too describes their distinction. The meaning is those who wear golden necklaces and other ornaments on their chests.

सुयमेभिः आशुभिः अश्वैः ईयंते (*suyamebhiḥ āśubhiḥ aśvaiḥ īyaṃte*)—The word सुयमेभिः (*suyamebhiḥ*) means horses that have the strength to carry the Marut deities easily, that is, without difficulty or effort. Or the meaning may be given as having easy control, that is, "Well-Controlled", subject to the charioteer's hold. The word आशुभिः (*āśubhiḥ*) means able to run swiftly. Therefore the chief meaning of this sentence is that these Marut deities are carried by their chariot horses, which bear the load easily and go quickly.

शुभं यातां रथाः अनु आवृत्सत (*śubhaṃ yātāṃ rathāḥ anu āvṛtsata*)—The chariots of the Marut deities, which travel happily, follow them. That is, the chariots carry them, according to their wish, to wherever the Marut deities desire to go. Or for the word शुभं (*śubhaṃ*) the sense water

### Printed p. 686
is taken (Ni. 2.24), then the sense can also be given that the chariots of the Maruts, going toward the clouds for the sake of water, carry them there. It is well known that the chariot of the Maruts is made of water. The last pāda of this Ṛk, शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत (*śubhaṃ yātāmanu rathā avṛtsata*), is repeated again and again, like a refrain, as the last pāda in all the Ṛks of this sūkta.

> इत्यर्थः । हे महांतो यूयमुर्वियोरवः संतो वि । राजथ । उतापि चांतरिक्षमोजसा बलेन वि ममिरे । व्याप्नुथ । शुभमित्यादिगतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, you yourselves, without any helper, दधिद्वे (*dadhidve*), that is, you hold or exercise. What? तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*), strength, capacity. As you know, that is, your capacity is unobstructed. O great ones, you shine widely **NOTE**. And you also pervade the firmament with your power. The rest, beginning शुभं (*śubhaṃ*), has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Maruts) यथा (*yathā*) विद (*vida*)—as seems fitting to you
- तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*)—strength
- स्वयं (*svayaṃ*)—you yourselves, without the help of others
- दधिध्वै (*dadhidhvai*)—you have held
- महांतः (*mahāṃtaḥ*)—you who are great
- उर्विया (*urviyā*)—exceedingly
- वि (*vi*) राजथ (*rājatha*)—you shine
- उत (*uta*)—and
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the firmament
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—with your power
- वि (*vi*) ममिरे (*mamire*)—you have pervaded
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of well-being
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of the Maruts as they go
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots also
- अनु (*anu*) अवृत्सत (*avṛtsata*)—follow them

### Printed p. 687

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, as seems fitting to you, you have held your strength without the help of others. You who are great shine exceedingly. You have pervaded the firmament with your power. The chariots of the Maruts, who go as bringers of well-being, also follow them.

##### English translation
Maruts, you have of yourselves maintained your vigour according as you judge (fit): you shine most mighty and vast, and you pervade the firmament with your power: may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यथा विद तविषीं स्वयं दधिध्वे (*yathā vida taviṣīṃ svayaṃ dadhidhve*)—O Maruts, if you wish, you display your strength, capacity and the rest, without the help of others, so that all may know it. Your strength, capacity and the rest are unfathomable. You are not ones who look for another's help. The surpassing greatness of your capacity becomes visible to all when you move in the firmament (when you blow with force). The chief sense of the sentence is that you make this display of your strength only when it pleases you. The sentences that follow, बृहन्महांत उर्विया वि राजथ (*bṛhanmahāṃta urviyā vi rājatha*) and उतांतरिक्षं ममिरे वोजसा (*utāṃtarikṣaṃ mamire vojasā*), make clear in another form the very sense just stated.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> साकं सहैव जाता उत्पन्ना सुभ्वः सुष्टु भवंतः । महांत इत्यर्थः । तथैव
> साकं सहैवोक्षिताः सेक्तारो वर्षकाः श्रिये चित् शोभाया एव प्रतरं प्रकृष्टतरमा सर्वतो नवृधुः । अवर्धयन् । नरः कर्मणां नेतारो विरोकिणः विरोचमानाः सूर्यस्येव रश्मयः सूर्यरश्मय इव । शुभमित्यादि गतं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Born साकं (*sākaṃ*), that is, together; सुभ्वः (*subhvaḥ*), those who are well, meaning great. In the same way they are sprinklers together, givers of rain; they have increased exceedingly, more and more, on all sides, for splendour alone. They are the leaders of rites, shining like the rays of the sun. The rest, beginning शुभं (*śubhaṃ*), has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—together
- जाताः (*jātāḥ*)—born
- सुभ्वः (*subhvaḥ*)—great ones
- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—together
- उक्षिताः (*ukṣitāḥ*)—the Maruts, who pour down rain
- श्रिये (*śriye*) चित् (*cit*)—as bringers of the utmost beauty
- प्रतरु (*prataru*)—exceedingly
- आ (*ā*)—everywhere
- ववृधुः (*vavṛdhuḥ*)—have grown
- सूर्यस्येव (*sūryasyeva*)—of the sun
- रश्मयः (*raśmayaḥ*)—like the rays
- विरोकिणः (*virokiṇaḥ*)—they are radiant
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of auspiciousness
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of the Maruts as they go
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots also
- अनु (*anu*) अवृत्सत (*avṛtsata*)—follow them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, born together, great, and pouring down rain together, have grown exceedingly everywhere, as bringers of the utmost beauty. They are radiant like the rays of the sun. The chariots of the Maruts, who go as bringers of auspiciousness, also follow them.

##### English translation
Born simultaneously, mighty, co-dispensers of moisture, they have grown exceedingly in glory: leaders (of rites), and radiant (are they) as the rays of the sun : may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

साकं जाताः (*sākaṃ jātāḥ*)—सहैव उत्पन्नाः (*sahaiva utpannāḥ*). Those born together. We have already explained the origin of the Marut deities, on page 596 of this part. It was said earlier that Indra cut with his thunderbolt the embryo in the womb of the goddess Diti into seven parts, and each of those seven parts again into seven, and that the Supreme Lord, out of a mind of grace, turned all those forty-nine fragments of the embryo into separate sons; these are the Marut hosts. Therefore the seer describes these forty-nine Marut deities as साकं जाताः (*sākaṃ jātāḥ*), born at one time.

### Printed p. 689
सुष्टु भवंतः । महांत इत्यर्थः (*suṣṭu bhavaṃtaḥ | mahāṃta ityarthaḥ*)—those who shine well; that is, as described earlier in the Ṛk
अंसेषु व ऋष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षःसु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः । अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्तोः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययाः ॥ (*aṃseṣu va ṛṣṭayaḥ patsu khādayo vakṣaḥsu rukmā maruto rathe śubhaḥ | agnibhrājaso vidyuto gabhastoḥ śiprāḥ śīrṣasu vitatā hiraṇyayāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-11),
these Marut deities bear on their arms the weapon called ṛṣṭi; they wear anklets on their feet, necklaces on their chests and a golden crown on their heads; holding in their hands divine weapons gleaming like lightning, seated on an excellent chariot, they shine with a divine brilliance blazing like Agni. This is the intended sense. Besides, they may also be called those of great glory and of immense strength and capacity.

विरोकिणः सूर्यस्येव रश्मयः आ ववृधुः (*virokiṇaḥ sūryasyeva raśmayaḥ ā vavṛdhuḥ*)—As the rays of the shining sun spread everywhere in the firmament, so the Marut deities, whose nature is to move in the firmament, also increased everywhere, that is, spread. (The chief sense is that, because the wind blows everywhere in the firmament, it spread as the light of the sun spreads everywhere.)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो वो युष्माकं महित्वनं महत्त्वमाभूषेण्यं स्तुत्यं । किंच

> मोक्षे । स्वर्ग इत्यर्थः । तत्र दधातन । धारयत । शिष्टं गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, your greatness is to be praised (आभूषेण्यं (*ābhūṣeṇyaṃ*)). Moreover, it is to be seen, like the form of the sun (दिदृक्षेण्यं (*didṛkṣeṇyaṃ*)). And set us in immortality, that is, in liberation, which means heaven. The rest has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- महित्वनं (*mahitvanaṃ*)—greatness
- आभूषेण्यं (*ābhūṣeṇyaṃ*)—is to be praised
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- चक्षणं (*cakṣaṇaṃ*) इव (*iva*)—like the form
- दिदृक्षेण्यं (*didṛkṣeṇyaṃ*)—is worthy of being seen
- उतो (*uto*)—and
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- अमृतत्वे (*amṛtatve*)—so that we attain freedom from death
- दधातन (*dadhātana*)—set
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of auspiciousness
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of the Maruts as they go
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots
- अनु (*anu*) अवृत्सत (*avṛtsata*)—follow them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, your greatness is to be praised. Your form, like the orb of the sun, is worthy of being seen and of being meditated upon. Grant that we become immortal. The chariots of the Maruts, who go as bringers of auspiciousness, follow them.

##### English translation
Your might, Maruts, is to be glorified : it is to be contemplated like the orb of the sun : sustain us ever in immortality: may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कारीर्यां प्रथमस्याः पिंड्या उदीरयथेत्यनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । उदीरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतः प्र वो मरुतस्तविषा उदन्यवः । आ-२-१३ । इति ॥
> हे मरुतो यूयं समुद्रतः समुद्रवणसाधनादंतरिक्षादुदीरयथ ।
> प्रेरयथ वृष्टिं । अयमेर्वाथः पुनरुच्यते । हे पुरीषिणः । पृणतेः प्रीणातीर्वा
> पुरीषमुदकं । हे तद्वंतो यूयं वृष्टिं वर्षयथ । हे दस्रा दर्शनीयाः
> शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितारो ना वो युष्माकं धेनवः प्रीणयितारो मेघा
> नोप दस्यंति । न शुष्यंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the कारीर्यां (*kārīryāṃ*) rite, for the first पिंड्या (*piṃḍyā*) offering, उदीरयथ (*udīrayatha*) is the अनुवाक्या (*anuvākyā*) verse. The sūtra also states it: उदीरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतः प्र वो मरुतस्तविषा उदन्यवः (*udīrayathā marutaḥ samudrataḥ pra vo marutastaviṣā udanyavaḥ*) (Ā. 2-13). O Maruts, you send forth rain from the ocean, that is, from the firmament **NOTE**. This is the same sense repeated. O you who are पुरीषिणः (*purīṣiṇaḥ*), पुरीष (*purīṣa*) being water, derived from पृणतेः (*pṛṇateḥ*): you who possess it shower down rain. O दस्रा (*dasrā*), beautiful ones, destroyers of your enemies, your धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*), the clouds that gratify, do not dry up.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- समुद्रतः (*samudrataḥ*)—from the firmament
- वृष्टिं (*vṛṣṭiṃ*)—rain
- उदीरयथ (*udīrayatha*)—you send forth
- पुरीषिणः (*purīṣiṇaḥ*)—you who are filled with water
- वर्षयथ (*varṣayatha*)—you shower down rain
- दस्राः (*dasrāḥ*)—O Maruts, of beautiful form
- वः (*vaḥ*)—belonging to you
- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—the gratifying clouds
- न (*na*) उप (*upa*) दस्यंति (*dasyaṃti*)—never dry up
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of auspiciousness
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of the Maruts as they go
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots also
- अनु (*anu*) अवृत्सत (*avṛtsata*)—follow them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, you send forth rain from the firmament. You who are filled with water shower down rain. O Maruts, of beautiful form, the gratifying clouds that belong to you never dry up. The chariots of the Maruts, who go as bringers of auspiciousness, also follow them.

##### English translation
You send (the rain), Maruts, from the firmament : charged with the waters you shower down the rain : destroyers of foes, your milch cows are never dry : may the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the कारीर्यॆष्टियल्लि (*kārīryèṣṭiyalli*), in the first पिंडिहोमदल्लि (*piṃḍihomadalli*), this Ṛk beginning उदीरयथा (*udīrayathā*) is to be recited as the अनुवाक्या (*anuvākyā*) mantra; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra उदीरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतः प्र वो मरुतस्तविषा उदन्यवः (*udīrayathā marutaḥ samudrataḥ pra vo marutastaviṣā udanyavaḥ*) (Ā. 2-13).

समुद्रतः (*samudrataḥ*)—The word समुद्र (*samudra*) is read among the names of the firmament (Ni. 2.10), and in this Ṛk it is used in this same sense.

### Printed p. 692
Since the word समुद्र (*samudra*) is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā in various senses, the authors of the Nirukta have included the word समुद्र (*samudra*) among the names of the firmament (Ni. 2.10). Afterwards they have shown the difference between the terrestrial ocean and the ocean that is a synonym of the firmament. Addressing those who do not know the difference between the two and give an interpretation that leaves room for doubt, they say: तत्र समुद्र इत्येतत्पार्थिवेन समुद्रेण संदिह्यते। (*tatra samudra ityetatpārthivena samudreṇa saṃdihyate|*) Many mistake the ocean that is a synonym of the firmament for the terrestrial ocean and interpret accordingly. That is not right, and so they have given an etymology of the word समुद्र (*samudra*):

समुद्रः कस्मात्समुद्भवंत्यस्मादापः समभिद्रवंत्येनमापः संमोदंतेऽस्मिन् भूतानि समुदको भवति समुनत्तीति वा । (*samudraḥ kasmātsamudbhavaṃtyasmādāpaḥ samabhidravaṃtyenamāpaḥ saṃmodaṃte 'smin bhūtāni samudako bhavati samunattīti vā |*) (Ni. 2-11).

First, the root dru, meaning to move, joined with the two prefixes sam and ud, gives the sense "it flows overflowing upward"; or, secondly, the same root dru with the prefixes sam and abhi gives the sense that the waters (of the rivers) flow toward it; or the root mud, meaning to rejoice, with the prefix sam, gives the sense that the aquatic creatures find joy in it; or because it is the store of water; or the root ud, meaning to wet, with the prefix sam, gives the sense "that which drenches". In these ways they have shown that the word समुद्र (*samudra*) is formed (Ni. 2-10). In this connection, to show the difference between the word समुद्र (*samudra*) as a synonym of the firmament and the terrestrial ocean, they have also cited an ancient story:

तयोर्विभागस्तत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । देवापिश्चाष्टिषेणः शंतनुश्च कौरव्या भ्रातरा बभूवतुः । स शंतनुः कनीयानभिषेजचयांचक्रे । देवापिस्तपः प्रतिपेदे । ततः शंतनो राज्ये द्वादश वर्षाणि देवो न ववर्ष । तमूचुब्राह्मणा अधर्मस्त्वया चरितो ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरमंतरित्याभिषेचितं तस्मात्ते देवो न वर्षतीति । स शंतनुर्देवापिं शिशिक्ष राज्येन । तमुवाच देवापिः पुरोहितस्तेऽसानि याजयानि च त्वेति । तस्यैतद्वर्षकामसूक्तं तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*tayorvibhāgastatretihāsamācakṣate | devāpiścāṣṭiṣeṇaḥ śaṃtanuśca kauravyā bhrātarā babhūvatuḥ | sa śaṃtanuḥ kanīyānabhiṣejacayāṃcakre | devāpistapaḥ pratipede | tataḥ śaṃtano rājye dvādaśa varṣāṇi devo na vavarṣa | tamūcubrāhmaṇā adharmastvayā carito jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaramaṃtarityābhiṣecitaṃ tasmātte devo na varṣatīti | sa śaṃtanurdevāpiṃ śiśikṣa rājyena | tamuvāca devāpiḥ purohitaste 'sāni yājayāni ca tveti | tasyaitadvarṣakāmasūktaṃ tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*).

Of the two, Devāpi and Śaṃtanu, of the Kuru line and sons of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, the younger, Śaṃtanu, had himself consecrated and became king of that kingdom. Devāpi went away to the forest to practise austerity. Thereafter, for twelve years, no rain fell in Śaṃtanu's kingdom. Then the Brāhmaṇas said to Śaṃtanu

### Printed p. 693
that, since he had sent his elder brother to the forest and become king himself, he had committed a sinful deed; therefore the god of rain had not poured rain in his kingdom. Then, when Śaṃtanu tried to have Devāpi consecrated king, Devāpi said, "I shall be your priest and perform sacrifice for you", and had the sacrifice performed for the sake of rain. Thereafter rain poured from the ocean in the upper region to the ocean in the lower region. To show the difference between the two oceans, they cite the Ṛk

आर्ष्टिषेणो होत्रमृषिर्निषीदन् देवापिर्देवसुमतिं चिकित्वान् । स उत्तरस्मादधरं समुद्रमपो दिव्या असृजद्वर्ष्या अभि ॥ (*ārṣṭiṣeṇo hotramṛṣirniṣīdan devāpirdevasumatiṃ cikitvān | sa uttarasmādadharaṃ samudramapo divyā asṛjadvarṣyā abhi ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-98-5)

and show by it the difference between the upper ocean and the lower ocean. Here the upper ocean means the firmament, and the lower ocean means the terrestrial ocean.

In some places in the Ṛksaṃhitā the word समुद्र (*samudra*) can be said decidedly to mean the terrestrial ocean. But in Ṛks such as

यथा वातो यथा वनं याथा समुद्र विजति (*yathā vāto yathā vanaṃ yāthā samudra vijati*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-78-8)

it is difficult to say whether it is the synonym of the firmament or the terrestrial ocean. In

अग्निं विश्वा अभि पृक्षः सचंते समुद्रं न स्रवतः सप्त यह्वीः (*agniṃ viśvā abhi pṛkṣaḥ sacaṃte samudraṃ na sravataḥ sapta yahvīḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-71-7),

सं यं स्तुभोऽवनयो न यंति समुद्रं न स्रवतो रोधचक्राः (*saṃ yaṃ stubho 'vanayo na yaṃti samudraṃ na sravato rodhacakrāḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-190-7)

and

या आपो दिव्या उत वा स्रवंति खनित्रिमा उत वा याः स्वयंजाः । समुद्रार्था याः शुचयः पावकास्ता आपो देवीरिह मामवंतु ॥ (*yā āpo divyā uta vā sravaṃti khanitrimā uta vā yāḥ svayaṃjāḥ | samudrārthā yāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāstā āpo devīriha māmavaṃtu ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-49-2)

and in many other Ṛks, it can be said decidedly to be the terrestrial ocean. In some places this word is used as an adjective and gives the sense "flowing". In the Ṛk

अद्भिर्याति वरुणः समुद्रॆयुर्युष्मा इच्छंतः शवसो नपातः (*adbhiryāti varuṇaḥ samudrèyuryuṣmā icchaṃtaḥ śavaso napātaḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-161-14)

the meaning of समुद्रॆः समुंदनस्वभावैः अद्भिः (*samudrèḥ samuṃdanasvabhāvaiḥ adbhiḥ*) is "with waters whose nature is to flow". Thus the meaning must be determined according to the context.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदश्वा॑न्थू॒र्षु पृष॑ती॒रयु॑ग्ध्वं हिर॒ण्यया॒न्प्रत्यत्का॒  ॑
> अमुग्ध्वं ।  
> विश्वा॒ इत्‌स्पृधो॑ मरुतो॒ व्य॑स्यथ॒ शुभं॑ या॒तामनु॒ रथा॑  
> आवृत्सत ॥ ६ ॥

> अमुग्ध्वं ।  
> विश्वाः । इत् । स्पृधः । मरुतः । वि । अस्यथ । शुभं । यातां । अनु । रथाः ।  
> अवृत्सत ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयं यद्यदाश्वान् धूर्षु रथसंबंधनीष्टयुग्ध्वं योजितवंतः स्थ । कीदृशानश्वान् । पृषतीः । पृषत्यो मरुतामितुक्तत्वात् । पृषद्वर्णा
> वडवाः । सारंगी वात्राश्वशब्द वाच्या । हिरण्ययान्हिरण्यवर्णानत्कान्कवचान् प्रत्यमुग्ध्वं प्रत्यमुंचत । एवं कृत्वा विश्वा इत् स्वृधः सर्वानपि संग्रामान् हे मरुतो
> व्यस्यथ । विक्षिपथ । शुभमित्यादि गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, when you have yoked to the poles of the chariot the horses, which are पृषतीः (*pṛṣatīḥ*), spotted (since the Maruts' horses are stated to be spotted): these are spotted mares; or else the female antelope is what is meant by the word "horse" here. You put on in turn the golden-coloured अत्कान् (*atkān*), that is, coats of mail. Having done so, O Maruts, you hurl away all battles. The rest, beginning शुभं (*śubhaṃ*), has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Maruts) यत् (*yat*)—when
- पृषतीः (*pṛṣatīḥ*)—spotted
- अश्वान् (*aśvān*)—horses
- धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*)—to the yoke-poles of your chariot
- आयुग्ध्वं (*āyugdhvaṃ*)—you join and fasten (then)
- हिरण्ययान् (*hiraṇyayān*)—made of gold
- आत्कान् (*ātkān*)—your coats of mail
- प्रति (*prati*) आमुग्ध्वं (*āmugdhvaṃ*)—you put on (afterwards)
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- विश्वा (*viśvā*) इत् (*it*)—all
- स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)—enemies
- व्यस्यथ (*vyasyatha*)—you strike down and overthrow
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of auspiciousness
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of the Maruts as they go
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots also
- अनु (*anu*) अवृत्सत (*avṛtsata*)—follow them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, when you join and fasten to the yoke-poles of your chariots your horses (antelopes) of spotted colour (marked with dots), you put on your golden

### Printed p. 695
coats of mail. Thereafter, O Maruts, you strike down and overthrow all enemies. The chariots of the Maruts, who go as bringers of auspiciousness, also follow them.

##### English translation
When you yoke your spotted mares to the poles (of your chariots), you lay aside your golden breast-plates, for you dissipate all hostility; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk describes the Marut deities making their preparations for battle and going to war. First the Maruts harness to their chariot spotted deer, that is, deer with white spots, and make the chariot ready. Next, so that their bodies may be impenetrable to the weapons of their enemies, they put on golden coats of mail (Armours). Then, seated in their chariot, which has the power to go wherever they wish, they strike and drive away their enemies (the clouds). Such is the description of the battle given here.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो वो युष्मान् पर्वताः शिलोच्चया न वरंत । न वारयंतु ।
> तथा नद्यश्च न वारयंतु । किंतु यत्र यस्मिन्यज्ञादिस्थानेऽचिध्वं जानीथ संकल्पयथ तत्स्थानं गच्छथेदु । गच्छथैव। उतापि च द्यावापृथिवी च परि परितो याथन।
> याथ वृष्ट्यर्थमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, let mountains, the heaps of rock, not ward you off; likewise let rivers not ward you off. Rather, to whatever place, such as a place of sacrifice, you know and resolve to go, to that place you go indeed. And you go all around heaven and earth for the sake of rain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- पर्वताः (*parvatāḥ*)—mountains
- न (*na*) वरंत (*varaṃta*)—let them not stop
- नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)—rivers also
- न (*na*)—let them not stop
- यत्र (*yatra*)—to whatever region
- अचिध्वं (*acidhvaṃ*)—you resolve that you must go
- तत् (*tat*)—to that place
- गच्छथेदु (*gacchathedu*)—you go and arrive without fail
- उत (*uta*)—and
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- परि (*pari*)—all around
- याथन (*yāthana*)—you travel
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of auspiciousness
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of the Maruts who travel
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots also
- अनुअवृत्सत (*anuavṛtsata*)—follow them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, let neither mountains nor rivers stop you. To whatever region you resolve to go, to that region you go and arrive without fail. And for the sake of rain you travel all around heaven and earth. The chariots of the Maruts, who travel as bringers of auspiciousness, also follow them.

##### English translation
Let not the mountains, let not the rivers, arrest you : whither you purpose, (Maruts), thither repair, and compass heaven and earth; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The use of the word पर्वत (*parvata*) is most frequent in the sūktas of Indra and the Maruts. Its ordinary meaning is mountain (hill), but it is customary for it to be a synonym of cloud. The authors of the Nirukta say: पर्ववान् पर्वतः । पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातीर्वा । मेघोऽपि गिरिरेतस्मादेव । (*parvavān parvataḥ | parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇātīrvā | megho 'pi giriretasmādeva |*) (Ni. 1-20). They show that the word पर्वत (*parvata*) comes from the word पर्व (*parva*), which is formed either from the root pṛ, meaning to fill, or from the root prī, meaning to worship or to satisfy, and so explain that it means mountain (hill) or cloud. This derivation gives the idea either of filling a region that is empty, or of satisfying beings (with rain and the like). In this, one must note which mountain is obstructive and which is helpful.

### Printed p. 697
In general, Indra's fight with the Asuras and with the mountains may be called the fight of darkness and light. In the Ṛk

वि चिद्वृत्रस्य दोधतो वज्रेण शतपर्वणा । शिरो बिभेद वृष्टिना ॥ (*vi cidvṛtrasya dodhato vajreṇa śataparvaṇā | śiro bibheda vṛṣṭinā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-6)

he destroyed the Asura, who is of the nature of darkness and is an obstructor, with the thunderbolt that has a hundred joints (parvans) of the nature of rays. From such examples it may be said that, just as words such as Vṛtra show the embodied form of the darkness that covers the world, so too the word पर्वत (*parvata*) points to darkness in the shape of a mountain. Besides, if only the ordinary meaning, mere mountain or cloud, is given, it does not give the full sense suited to the circumstances. For instance, there is described a fourfold accomplishment: the release of the cows and waters hidden away by the slaying of the mountain, and the bringing forth of Uṣas and of the sun. Therefore, if the word पर्वत (*parvata*) is explained merely as a cloud, it will not suit the circumstances.

In the Ṛk

अदर्दरुत्समसृजो वि खानि त्वमर्णवान्बद्बधाना अरम्माणः । महांतमिंद्र पर्वतं वि यद्वः सृजो वि धारा अव दाननं हन् ॥ (*adardarutsamasṛjo vi khāni tvamarṇavānbadbadhānā arammāṇaḥ | mahāṃtamiṃdra parvataṃ vi yadvaḥ sṛjo vi dhārā ava dānanaṃ han ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-32-1)

and in the Brāhmaṇa sentence

शिशुं नदीनां हरिमद्रिबुध्नमिति गिरिर्वा अद्रिर्गिरिबुध्ना (*śiśuṃ nadīnāṃ harimadribudhnamiti girirvā adrirgiribudhnā*)
(Śa.
(Śa. Brā. 7-5-2-18)

it is understood that the words पर्वत (*parvata*) and cloud have a surpassing and supernatural meaning. It is described as a mass of darkness in the shape of a mountain, situated in the world of heaven, concealing the waters and the cow. Having pierced this darkness, Indra causes the Maruts to spread out the waters and the light.

In Ṛks such as

अहन्नहिं पर्वते शिश्रियाणं त्वष्टास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष (*ahannahiṃ parvate śiśriyāṇaṃ tvaṣṭāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-2)

it is said that Indra, who destroys the Asuras Ahi, Śambara, Vṛtra and others, who hide in this mass of darkness in the shape of a mountain and obstruct the flowing waters, is worthy of praise. In the same way

### Printed p. 698

In many places the word पर्वत (*parvata*) is described as a synonym of "enemy", or as a support of enemies. Therefore in Ṛks such as आरंस्त पर्वतश्चित्सरिष्यन् (*āraṃsta parvataścitsariṣyan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-7) and शुष्माच्चिदस्य पर्वता भयंते (*śuṣmāccidasya parvatā bhayaṃte*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-13) it is said that as soon as Indra, who is of the nature of light, became manifest, the mountain-shaped masses of darkness trembled with fear, and that Indra hid them in the nether world.

Contrary to these descriptions, it is said in many places that the mountain is the thunderbolt weapon, which is of the nature of light, and also that it is Parjanya, the presiding deity of rain, water and the like.

प्राक्तादपाक्तादधरादुदक्तादभि जहि रक्षसः पर्वतेन । (*prāktādapāktādadharādudaktādabhi jahi rakṣasaḥ parvatena |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-19)

अस्मे रुद्रा मेहना पर्वतासो वृत्रहत्ये भरहूत् सजोषाः । (*asme rudrā mehanā parvatāso vṛtrahatye bharahūt sajoṣāḥ |*) **NOTE**
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-63-12)

In Ṛks such as these the mountains are instruments that help Indra in the work of destroying enemies.

प्र पूषणं विष्णुमग्निं पुरंधिं सवितारमोषधीः पर्वतांश्च । (*pra pūṣaṇaṃ viṣṇumagniṃ puraṃdhiṃ savitāramoṣadhīḥ parvatāṃśca |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-21-9)

शं नः पर्वता ध्रुवयो भवंतु शं नः सिंधवः शमु सन्त्वापः । (*śaṃ naḥ parvatā dhruvayo bhavaṃtu śaṃ naḥ siṃdhavaḥ śamu santvāpaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-35-8)

In Ṛks such as these there is an invocation of the mountain together with deities such as Mitra, Varuṇa and Pūṣan.

युवं तमिंद्रापर्वता पुरोयुधा यो नः पृतन्यादप तंतमिद्धतं वज्रेण तंतमिद्धतं । (*yuvaṃ tamiṃdrāparvatā puroyudhā yo naḥ pṛtanyādapa taṃtamiddhataṃ vajreṇa taṃtamiddhataṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-133-6)

इंद्रापर्वता बृहता रथेन वामीरिष आ वहतं सुवीराः । (*iṃdrāparvatā bṛhatā rathena vāmīriṣa ā vahataṃ suvīrāḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53-1)

In these places and in other Ṛks there is a joint invocation and praise of Indra and of the mountain. Sāyaṇa has said that the mountain here means Parjanya. Here the mountain is a deity to be worshipped.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्पू॒र्व्यं म॑रुतो॒ यच्च॒ नूत॑नं॒ यदु॒द्यते॑ वसवो॒ ॑ ॒॑
> यच्च॑ श॒स्यते॑ ।  
> विश्व॑स्य॒ तस्य॑ भवथा॒ नवे॑दसः॒ शुभं॑ या॒तामनु॒ रथा॑ अवृत्सत ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । पूर्व्यं । मरुतः । यत् । च । नूतनं । यत् । उद्यते । वसवः । यत् ।  
> च । शस्यते !  
> विश्वस्य । तस्य । भवथ । नवेदसः । शुभं । यातां । अनु । रथाः । अवृत्सत ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयं यत्पूर्व्यं पूर्वतनं पूर्वमनुष्ठितं यत्कर्मास्ति
> तदित्यर्थः । यच्च नूतनं कर्मास्ति । यच्चोद्यत ऊर्ध्वं प्राप्यते । स्तूयत
> इत्यर्थः । हे वसवो वासका यच्च शस्यते शंसनं क्रियते तस्य विश्वस्योत्कृष्टस्य
> नवेदसो जानंतो भवथ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, whatever work is पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*), that is, ancient, performed before; and whatever work is new; and whatever is उद्यते (*udyate*), that is, raised up, praised; and, O Vasus, that is, givers of dwelling, whatever praise is made: of all that excellent work you are knowers."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यत् (*yat*)—what rite
- पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*)—was performed anciently
- यच्च (*yacca*)—and what
- नूतनं (*nūtanaṃ*)—is performed now
- यत् (*yat*)—what hymn
- उद्यते (*udyate*)—is recited aloud
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—O Maruts, givers of dwelling
- यच्च (*yacca*)—and what hymn
- शस्यते (*śasyate*)—is recited in your praise
- तस्य विश्वस्य (*tasya viśvasya*)—of all those rites and hymns
- नवेदसः (*navedasaḥ*)—you, as those who know
- भवथ (*bhavatha*)—become
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of good
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of the Maruts who are going
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots also
- अनु अवृत्सत (*anu avṛtsata*)—follow them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, givers of dwelling, whatever rite was performed in the past in your honour, whatever is performed now, whatever hymn is recited aloud, whatever is

### Printed p. 700

laudatory to you: all those rites and hymns you know fully. The chariots also of the Maruts, who go as bringers of good, follow them.

##### English translation
Whatever (rite has been addressed to you), Maruts of old; whatever is recent; whatever (hymn) is recited, Vasus, whatever prayer is repeated, do you be cognizant of all: may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यंतन ।  
> अधि॑ स्तो॒त्रस्य॑ स॒ख्यस्य॑ गातन॒ शुभं॑ या॒तामनु॒ रथा॑ अवृत्सत ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अधि । स्तोत्रस्य । सख्यस्य । गातन । शुभं । यातां । अनु । रथाः । अवृत्सत ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो नोऽस्मान् मृळत । सुखयत । मा वधिष्टन । असम्यक्करणादिजनितेन कोपेन मा वधिद्वं । किंत्वस्मभ्यं शर्म सुखं बहुलमत्यधिकं वि यंतन ।
> कुरुत । किंच स्तोत्रस्य स्तोत्रं सख्यस्य सख्यमधि गातन । अधिगच्छथ । स्तुतिमनुभूयास्मासु सख्यं कुरुतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, make us happy, give us joy. Do not slay us: do not strike us down in anger caused by improper performance and the like; but bestow upon us abundant, exceeding happiness. Further, attain our praise and our friendship: having experienced our praise, make friendship with us."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
