- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळत (*mṛḷata*)—make happy
- मा वधिष्टन (*mā vadhiṣṭana*)—do not harm
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- बहुलं (*bahulaṃ*)—exceedingly
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- वि यंतन (*vi yaṃtana*)—bring about
- स्तोत्रस्य (*stotrasya*)—our praise
- सख्यस्य (*sakhyasya*)—and our friendship
- अधि गातन (*adhi gātana*)—know
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—as bringers of good
- यातां (*yātāṃ*)—of the Maruts who are going
- रथाः (*rathāḥ*)—the chariots also
- अनु अवृत्सत (*anu avṛtsata*)—follow them

### Printed p. 701

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, make us happy, do not harm us. Bring about exceeding happiness for us. Knowing our praise and our friendship, give a reward for it. The chariots also of the Maruts, who go as bringers of good, follow them.

##### English translation
Send us felicity, Maruts; harm us not ; bestow upon us exceeding happiness: reward our adoration by your friendship: may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गृणानाः ।

> रयीणां ॥ १० ॥

> जुषध्वं । नः । हव्यदातिं । यजत्राः । वयं । स्याम । पतयः । रयीणां ॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयमस्मान्वस्यो वसीयो धनं स्वर्गादिलक्षणं स्थानं
> वाच्छाभिलक्ष्य नयत । प्रापयत । किंचांहतिभ्यः पापेभ्यो निर्णयत । निर्गमयत
> गृणानाः स्तूयमानाः ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ जुषध्वं सेवध्वं नोऽस्माकं
> हव्यदातिं हविर्दानवंतं यज्ञं हे यजत्रा यष्टव्या यूयं । वयं च रयीणां
> बहुविधानां धनानां पतयः स्याम । भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, lead us towards वस्यो (*vasyo*), that is, better wealth, or a place such as heaven, desiring it: cause us to reach it. Further, lead us out of अंहतिभ्यः (*aṃhatibhyaḥ*), that is, sins; take us out of them, you who are praised. Accept our sacrifice, which is rich in gifts of oblation, O you who are worthy of worship; and may we be the lords of manifold riches."

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, lead us to a region rich in prosperity. Being praised by us, release us from sin. You who are worthy of sacrifice, accept the oblation we have offered. May we be lords of riches of many kinds.

##### English translation
Maruts, conduct us to opulence: propitiated by our praises, extricate us from sin: accept, adorable (Maruts), our offered oblation, and may we be the possessors of riches.

The fifty-sixth hymn.

## Sūkta 56 (Maṇḍala 5)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्ने शर्धंतमिति नवर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं श्यावाश्वस्यार्षं मारुतं । तृतीयासप्तम्या सतोबृहत्या शिष्टा बृहत्यः । अग्ने नव बार्हतं तृतीयासप्तम्या सतोबृहत्यावित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the twelfth hymn, of nine Ṛks. Its seer is Śyāvāśva and its deity the Maruts. The third and seventh Ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre; the rest are in the Bṛhatī metre. The Anukramaṇikā says: Agni, nine, Bārhata; the third and seventh in Satobṛhatī.

Translation: This hymn beginning अग्ने शर्धं (*agne śardhaṃ*) is the twelfth hymn in the fourth Anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. The seer of this hymn is Śyāvāśva; the deity is the Maruts. The third and seventh Ṛks of this hymn are in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अग्ने नव बार्हतं तृतीयसप्तम्या सतोबृहत्या (*agne nava bārhataṃ tṛtīyasaptamyā satobṛhatyā*).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ शर्धं॑त॒मा ग॒णं पि॒ष्टं रु॒क्मेभि॑रं॒जिभिः॑ ।  
> विशो॑ अ॒द्य म॒रुता॒मन॑ ह्वये दि॒वश्चि॑द्रोच॒नादधि॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आग्ने । शर्धंतं । आ । गणं । पिष्टं । रुक्मेभिः । अंजिभिः ।  
> विशः । अद्य । मरुतां । अव । ह्वये । दिवः । चित् । रोचनात् । अधि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने शर्धंतं शत्रूनभिभवंतं यज्ञायोत्सहमानं ना गणं मरुतां
> गणमा ह्वयेति शेषः । कीदृशं गणं । रुक्मेभी रुक्मै रोचमानैरंजिभिराभरणैश्च
> पिष्टमवयवितं । युक्तमित्यर्थः । अद्यास्मिन्यागदिने मरुतां विशः प्रजाः । गणानित्यर्थः । तान्रोचनाद्रोचमानात् दिवो द्युलोकात् । अधीति पंचम्यर्थानुवादी।
> चित्तूरणः अवावस्तादस्मदभिमुखं ह्वये । आह्वयामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, call the host of the Maruts, which is शर्धंतं (*śardhaṃtaṃ*), that is, overcoming enemies and eager for the sacrifice; the words 'I call' are to be supplied." **NOTE** What kind of host? One endowed with shining golden ornaments and with अंजिभि (*aṃjibhi*) ornaments, that is, furnished with them. "Today, that is, on this day of the sacrifice, I call the Maruts' विशः (*viśaḥ*), that is, subjects, meaning hosts, from the shining heaven, the world of the sky; the word अधीति (*adhīti*) merely restates the sense of the ablative. I call them towards us." **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- रुक्मेभिः (*rukmebhiḥ*)—with shining
- अंजिभिः (*aṃjibhiḥ*)—ornaments
- पिषम् (*piṣam*)—those who are adorned **NOTE**
- शर्धंतं (*śardhaṃtaṃ*)—those who are able to destroy enemies
- गणं (*gaṇaṃ*)—the host of the Maruts
- आ (ह्वये) (*ā (hvaye)*)—I call
- अद्य (*adya*)—on this day of the sacrifice
- मरुतां विशः (*marutāṃ viśaḥ*)—the host of the Maruts
- रोचनात् (*rocanāt*)—from the shining
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—heaven
- अधि अव (*adhi ava*)—so that they may come down towards us
- ह्वये (*hvaye*)—I call with prayer

### Printed p. 704

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, I invoke the host of the Maruts, who are adorned with shining ornaments and are able to destroy enemies. On this day of the sacrifice I call and pray to the host of the Maruts to come down towards us from the shining world of heaven.

##### English translation
I invoke, Agni, the victorious company (of the Maruts) decorated with brilliant ornaments; (I invoke them), the people of the Maruts, to descend to-day from above the shining heaven.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अव (*ava*)—The word अव (*ava*) is a preposition. Concerning prepositions Yāska has given the following explanation—

न निर्बद्धा उपसर्गार्थान्निराहुरिति शाकटायनः । नामाख्यातयोस्तु कर्मोपसंयोगद्योतका भवंति। उच्चावचाः पदार्था भवंतीति गार्ग्यः। तद्य एषु पदार्थेः प्राहुरिमे नामाख्यातयोरर्थविकरणं ॥ (*na nirbaddhā upasargārthānnirāhuriti śākaṭāyanaḥ | nāmākhyātayostu karmopasaṃyogadyotakā bhavaṃti| uccāvacāḥ padārthā bhavaṃtīti gārgyaḥ| tadya eṣu padārtheḥ prāhurime nāmākhyātayorarthavikaraṇaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 1-3)

It is the view of Śākaṭāyana that when the words called prepositions are not used together with other nouns and verbs they do not indicate any meaning. But when they join nouns and verbs they explain the meaning of those words in a special or altered way. The teacher called Gārgya has expressed his opinion that prepositions have many kinds of meanings. Whatever meaning these prepositions may have, only this much is certain: when they are used together with nouns and verbs they make the meaning of those nouns and verbs somewhat more or less altered. In the same way—

न्यवेति विनिग्रहार्थीयौ ॥ (*nyaveti vinigrahārthīyau ‖*)

The prepositions नि (*ni*) and अव (*ava*) indicate the sense "below, downwards". For example, the word तरति (*tarati*), a form of the root तृ (*tṛ*) with the senses प्लवनतरणयोः (*plavanataraṇayoḥ*), means "crosses, goes from one place to another". If the preposition अव (*ava*) is added to this root, it becomes अवतरति (*avatarati*) and indicates the sense "comes down from above to below". In the present Ṛk this very sense is stated.

चित् (*cit*)—Although the word चित् (*cit*) has many meanings, here it is used in the sense of completion, that is, to fill out the sentence. Therefore the word has no specific meaning here.

> ये । ते । नेदिष्टं । हवनानि । आऽगमन् । तान् । वर्ध । भीमसंदृशः ॥ २ ॥

> येन प्रकारेणातिपूजितं जानासि । तेष्वादरं करोषीत्यर्थः । तदित्तथैव मे
> मदर्थं जग्मुर्गच्छंत्वाशस आशंसितार इच्छंतः शत्रून् हिंसंतो वा । अनंतरं ये
> मरुतो नेदिष्टमत्यंतांतिकं संनिधावेव ते तव हवनान्याह्वानानि श्रुत्वागमन्

> हविष्प्रापणेन ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, in whatever manner you think of the Maruts in your heart": the word चित् (*cit*) is used in the sense of worship, that is, in the manner in which you know them to be highly honoured, you show regard for them. "Just so may they come for my sake", wishing for my good, or else destroying enemies. Next, those Maruts who come very near, in close attendance, having heard your invocations: "increase" those terrible-looking ones, who cannot bear delay, by bringing them oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) हृदा (*hṛdā*)—in your heart
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner (the Maruts)
- चिन्मन्यसे (*cinmanyase*)—you meditate with devotion
- तदित् (*tadit*)—in the same way
- मे (*me*)—for me
- आशसः (*āśasaḥ*)—desiring welfare
- जग्मुः (*jagmuḥ*)—let them come
- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts
- नेदिष्टं (*nediṣṭaṃ*)—very near
- ते (*te*)—your
- हवनानि (*havanāni*)—invocations, having accepted
- आगमन् (*āgaman*)—graciously come
- तान् (*tān*)—those
- भीमसंदृशः (*bhīmasaṃdṛśaḥ*)—Maruts of terrible form
- वर्ध (*vardha*)—satisfy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in the manner in which you meditate with devotion on the Maruts in your heart, in the same way may they come to me, desiring my welfare. Satisfy those Maruts of terrible form who graciously come, accepting your invocations, very near.

### Printed p. 706

##### English translation
In whatever manner you honour the (Maruts, Agni), in your heart, may they come to me as benefactors: gratify, ( by oblations ), those fierce-looking Maruts, who most promptly come to your invocations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The seer Śyāvāśva has prayed to Agni, the Hotṛ, that Agni should bring the Marut deities to the sacrificial ground in the sacrifice, and that, although those Marut deities are of terrible form, he should satisfy them, meditating on them with devotion, with the view that they may grant us welfare.

चित् (*cit*)—चिदित्येषोऽनेककर्मा (*cidityeṣo 'nekakarmā*). Yāska has explained with examples that the word चित् (*cit*) has many meanings such as worship and censure. We have said this before. In the present Ṛk the word चित् (*cit*) is used in the sense of worship, that is, in a sense that indicates devotion and respect.

इत् (*it*)—The particles कं (*kaṃ*), ईं (*īṃ*), इत् (*it*) and उ (*u*) are used to fill out the verse-line. On this subject Yāska—

अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रंथेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छंति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्विति । (*atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu graṃtheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchaṃti padapūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidviti |*) (2. 1-9). **NOTE**

has explained that the words कं (*kaṃ*), ईं (*īṃ*), इत् (*it*) and उ (*u*) (or particles) are used to fill out the sentence in sentences that are not in metre, and to fill out the pāda in metrical Ṛks or mantras (of measured syllables); therefore these words need not have any specific meaning.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मी॒ळ्हुष्म॑तीव पृथि॒वी परा॑हता॒ मदं॑त्येत्य॒स्मदा ।  
> ऋक्षो॒ न वो॑ मरुतः॒ शिमी॑वा॒ अमो॑ दु॒ध्रो गौरि॑व  ॒
> भीमयुः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> माळ्हुष्मतीऽइव । पृथिवी । पराहता । मदंती । एति । अस्मत् । आ ।  
> ऋक्षः । न । वः । मरुतः । शिमीऽवान् । आमः । दुध्रः । गौऽइव । भीमयुः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मीळ्हुष्मती प्रबलस्वामिका पराहतान्यैरभिभूता पृथिवीव । आत्र पृथिवीशब्दस्तदधिष्ठितां प्रजां लक्षयति । सा यथा स्वस्वामिनमुपद्रुताभिगच्छति तद्वदिति ।
> मरुतां साकल्येन सर्वथा प्राप्तेर्दृष्टांतः । एवं मदंती हृष्यंती मरुत्सेनास्मत् ।
> अस्मानित्यर्थः । ऐति । आगच्छति हे मरुतो वो युष्माकममो बलं गण ऋक्षो न
> अग्निरिव शिमीवान् कर्मवान् दुध्रो दुर्धरो गौरिव भीमयुर्भीमैर्वृषभैर्युक्तो गौरिव । स यथा शिमीवान् कर्मवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मीळ्हुष्मती (*mīḷhuṣmatī*) means having a powerful lord, like the earth overcome by others; here the word "earth" denotes the people who dwell on it. As that people, when attacked, run to their own lord, so in the same way, the example being for the complete arrival of the Maruts, the army of the Maruts, rejoicing, comes to us. O Maruts, your strength, your host, is like fire, active; irresistible; like a bull accompanied by formidable bulls. As he is active **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मीळ्हुष्मती (*mīḷhuṣmatī*)—having a strong and able lord
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the people of the earth
- पराहता इव (*parāhatā iva*)—as, when confronted by enemies, they become glad at the coming of that lord
- मदंती (*madaṃtī*)—both causing us joy and expressing their own joy
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—towards us
- आ एति (*ā eti*)—(the army of the Maruts) comes
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- अमः (*amaḥ*)—the strength of the host
- ऋक्षो न (*ṛkṣo na*)—like Agni
- शिमावान् (*śimāvān*)—is endowed with action **NOTE**
- दुध्रः (*dudhraḥ*)—having unobstructed power
- गौरिव (*gauriva*)—like a bull
- भीमयुः (*bhīmayuḥ*)—is terrible

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the people of the earth, who have the help of a strong and able lord, rejoice at the coming of that lord when they are confronted by enemies, so the coming of the army of the Maruts gives us joy. O Maruts, the strength of your host is active like Agni and terrible like a bull of unobstructed power.

##### English translation
As the (people of the) earth having a powerful lord have recourse to him when oppressed (by others), so comes (the host of the Maruts) exulting to us: your company, Maruts, active as fire, is as difficult to be resisted as a formidable ux.

### Printed p. 708

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—The commentator has given the word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) here the sense "the people who live on the earth", just as the word "cow" is used to indicate milk, a product of the cow. In this Ṛk three illustrations are given concerning the Marut deities—

(1) मीळ्हुष्मतीव पृथिवी पराहता मदंती । (*mīḷhuṣmatīva pṛthivī parāhatā madaṃtī |*) When a multitude of people with a powerful leader or chief is confronted by enemies, and that leader comes forward to help them, they rejoice; in the same way we rejoice at the coming of the Marut deities. The seer has described the relation of a leader to his people as an illustration for the Marut deities.

(2) वः अमः ऋक्षो न शिमीवान् (*vaḥ amaḥ ṛkṣo na śimīvān*) O Maruts, your strength is like Agni endowed with action. As the influence of Agni in sacrifices and the like is full of greatness, or endowed with action, so the power and capacity of the Marut deities are excessive; thus the seer has described. This is the second illustration.

(3) दुध्रः गौरिव भीमयुः (*dudhraḥ gauriva bhīmayuḥ*) Another comparison is also given regarding the power of the Marut deities. The strength of the Marut deities is terrible like a bull of unobstructed power. As a well-fattened bull in rut rushes forward fearlessly, heeding nothing, and behaves in a terrible way, injuring those it meets, so also the Marut deities, in the time of their violent coming, behave without any hindrance, throwing down trees and the like with their roots, so as to be terrible to those who see them. Thus the strength of the Marut deities and the strength of a bull in rut are compared with each other, as both are capable of producing terrible results.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि ये रि॒णंत्योज॑सा॒ वृथा॒ गावो॒ न दु॒र्धुरः॑ ।  
> अश्मा॑नं चित्स्व॒र्यं१॒॑१ पर्व॑तं गि॒रिं प्र च्या॑वयंति॒ याम॑भिः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । ये । रिणंति । ओजसा । वृथा । गावः । न । दुःधुरः ।  
> अश्मानं । चित् । स्वर्यं । पर्वतं । गिरिं । प्र । च्यवयंति । यामभिः ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 709

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये मरुत ओजसा स्वीयेन बलेन नि रिणंति हिंसंति शत्रून् वृथानायासेन
> स्वसंचारमात्रेण गावो न दुर्धुरो दुःखेन हिंस्का अश्वा इव ते मरुतः स्वयं
> शब्दयंतमश्मानं व्याप्तं पर्वतं जगत्पूरकोदकवंतं । पर्ववान्पर्वतः पर्व पुनः
> पृणातेः प्रीणातीर्वा । नि-१-२० । इति निरुक्तं । तादृशं गिरिं मेघं । यद्वा ।
> पर्वतमिति विशेष्यं गिरिमिति विशेषणं । निगिरत्युदकमिति गिरिः । तं यामभिर्गमनैः पु
> च्यावयंत्यु दकनिर्गमनार्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Those Maruts who by their own strength ओजसा (*ojasā*) destroy enemies" वृथा (*vṛthā*), that is, without effort, merely by their own passage, "like horses hard to harm", दुर्धुरः (*durdhuraḥ*) meaning those that can be injured only with difficulty: those Maruts cause to descend the अश्मानं (*aśmānaṃ*), the self-sounding, the vast पर्वतं (*parvataṃ*), the cloud full of water that fills the world. The Nirukta says: पर्ववान्पर्वतः पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातीर्वा । (*parvavānparvataḥ parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇātīrvā |*) (Ni. 1-20). Such is the गिरिं (*giriṃ*), the cloud. Or else: पर्वतं (*parvataṃ*) is the noun to be qualified and गिरिं (*giriṃ*) the qualifier; it is गिरिः (*giriḥ*) because it swallows water. The Maruts cause it to move by their goings, so that the water may come out. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by their strength
- दुर्धुरः (*durdhuraḥ*)—having unobstructed power
- गावो न (*gāvo na*)—like horses
- वृथा (*vṛthā*)—without the least effort
- नि रिणंति (*ni riṇaṃti*)—they destroy enemies; (those Maruts)
- स्वरं-शब्द (*svaraṃ-śabda*)—that which makes sound **NOTE**
- अश्वानु (*aśvānu*)—that which pervades and spreads **NOTE**
- पर्वतंउदकपूर्णवादुदू (*parvataṃudakapūrṇavādudū*)—and mountain-like, filled with water **NOTE**
- गिरिं (*giriṃ*)—the cloud
- यामभिः (*yāmabhiḥ*)—by their goings
- प्र च्यावयंति (*pra cyāvayaṃti*)—they make it descend

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those Maruts who, like horses of unobstructed power, destroy enemies by their strength without the least effort, make the sounding, spread out, water-filled cloud descend by their goings.

##### English translation
They who with ease destroy (their foes) by their prowess, like horses difficult to be restrained, they send down by their movements the vast and sounding water-laden cloud.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ये ओजसा नि रिणंति (*ye ojasā ni riṇaṃti*)—In this sentence it is said that the Marut deities destroy enemies by their own capacity. Here the enemies are the clouds that hold water within themselves without raining. The Marut deities spread their very great power everywhere in the atmosphere, blow with extreme force, scatter the mass of clouds gathered together in one place, and make them spread to all places and pour down rain.

### Printed p. 710

गावो न दुर्धुरः (*gāvo na durdhuraḥ*)—Here an illustration is given concerning the Marut deities' destroying of enemies (the clouds). When spirited horses (Spirited horses), which nobody can restrain, charge upon enemies on the battlefield, nobody is able to face and stop them; in the same way nobody can stop the Maruts when they blow with the utmost force to urge the clouds to rain. Therefore the unobstructed power of the Marut deities is compared with horses that charge forward boldly. Here the commentator has taken the word गावः (*gāvaḥ*) to mean horses and has explained the sense as stated above. Although it is reasonable to take the word for cow to mean cattle in general and therefore horses, the word गावः (*gāvaḥ*) used in the present Ṛk may also be taken to mean bulls or oxen belonging to the cow species. Another kind of meaning is possible for this sentence: as these bulls, free of anyone's hindrance or fear, that is, heeding nobody, in the pride of their strength charge wherever they please and injure those they meet.

अश्मानं चित् स्वर्य० पर्वतं गिरिं यामभिः प्र च्यावयंति (*aśmānaṃ cit svarya0 parvataṃ giriṃ yāmabhiḥ pra cyāvayaṃti*)—The word पर्वत (*parvata*) or गिरि (*giri*) in this sentence means only a cloud. Although the words पर्वत (*parvata*) and गिरि (*giri*) have the general sense of a hill, here they must be taken to mean a cloud only. For, because of the attribute स्वर्य० (*svarya0*), "sounding", only clouds can make sounds such as lightning and thunder; mountains have no power to make any kind of sounds. And the word अश्मानं (*aśmānaṃ*), formed from the root अशू व्याप्तौ (*aśū vyāptau*), is also an attribute of the word पर्वत (*parvata*); it means "pervading and spread out in the atmosphere". The Marut deities make the cloud, which pervades the atmosphere everywhere making the sounds called lightning and thunder, descend by their goings, that is, by blowing swiftly or violently; that is, they make it fall from the atmosphere to the earth in the form of rain: this is the purport. For the word पर्वत (*parvata*) Yāska has given the etymology पर्ववान् पर्वतः पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातीर्वा (*parvavān parvataḥ parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇātīrvā*) (Ni. 1-20). The cloud is called पर्वत (*parvata*) because it is gathered together in masses in one place; or because it pervades and fills the region of the atmosphere; or because it gladdens people by providing them with rain-water: thus he has given three kinds of meaning. In the sense of a hill, too, these three kinds of meaning apply. How? A hill has three kinds of qualities: it consists of masses of rocks; it occupies or pervades a very large region on earth, as if filling it; and it gladdens people by its plants, trees and other vegetation and by being the source of rivers. Therefore the name applies. For the word गिरि (*giri*) there is the sense निगिरत्युदकं (*nigiratyudakaṃ*), that is, "it emits water"; therefore the word गिरि (*giri*), like the word पर्वत (*parvata*), has the sense of a cloud. Therefore

### Printed p. 711

since the two words पर्वत (*parvata*) and गिरि (*giri*) in this Ṛk indicate the same meaning, the commentator has explained that one of them may be taken as the qualifying word and the other as the word qualified.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्ति॑ष्ठ नू॒नमे॑षां॒ स्तोमैः॒ समु॑क्षितानां ।  
> म॒रुतां॑ पुरु॒तम॒नुपू॑र्व्यं॒ गवां॒ सर्ग॑मिव ह्वये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । तिष्ठ । नूनं । एषां । स्तोमैः । संऽउक्षितानां ।  
> मरुतां । पुरुतनुं । अपूर्व्यं । गवां । सर्ग०इव । ह्वये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयमुत्तिष्ठ । उत्तिष्ठत ॥ व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं ॥ नूनं निश्चयमेषां स्तोमैः स्तोत्रैः समुक्षितानां वर्धितानां मरुतां । यद्वा ।
> स्तोमैरुपह्वय इति संबंधः । तादृशां मरुतां पुरुतमं प्रभूततममपूर्व्यं।
> न विद्यते पूर्वो येभ्यस्तमपूर्व्यं सर्गं संघं गवामुदकानां प्रसिद्धानां
> गवां वा सर्गं संघमिन ह्वये । आह्वये ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, rise up": the singular is used by variation for the plural. नूनं (*nūnaṃ*) means certainly. Of these Maruts, who are increased by praises, that is, by hymns; or else the connection is "I call with praises". Of such Maruts I call the most abundant and unprecedented, that is, one before which none exists, host सर्गं (*sargaṃ*), that is, company, like a company of waters or of well-known cows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Maruts) उत्तिष्ठ (*uttiṣṭha*)—rise up
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—certainly
- स्तोमैः (*stomaiḥ*)—by hymns
- समुक्षितानां (*samukṣitānāṃ*)—who have grown together
- एषां मरुतां (*eṣāṃ marutāṃ*)—of these Maruts
- पुरुतमं (*purutamaṃ*)—most abundant
- अपूर्व्यं (*apūrvyaṃ*)—and incomparable
- सर्गं (*sargaṃ*)—the company
- गवां (*gavāṃ*)—of cows or of waters
- सर्गं इव (*sargaṃ iva*)—as one calls a host
- ह्वये (*hvaye*)—I call with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, rise up. By the hymns we make I call with prayer the most abundant and incomparable company of these Maruts, who have grown together, as one calls a herd of cows.

### Printed p. 712

##### English translation
Rise up (Maruts) : verily by my praises I invoke the mighty and unpreceded (troop) of these exalted (Maruts) like a heap of waters.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गवां सर्गमिव ह्वये (*gavāṃ sargamiva hvaye*)—Here the seer, while desiring the coming of the Marut deities, has stated the illustration "like a herd of cows". As, when the cows have gone to the forest to graze and return home in the evening, the masters receive and welcome the herd with affection, so I call with prayer, with devotion and respect, the host of the Marut deities, who are pleased with the hymns and the like that I have made, to come to our sacrificial ground; thus, comparing the host of the Marut deities to a herd of cows, he has expressed the excess of regard he has for the Marut deities. Here the commentator has given another meaning for the word गवां (*gavāṃ*), namely उदकानां (*udakānāṃ*). गवां संघं (*gavāṃ saṃghaṃ*) then means a collection of waters, or, as people desire for the sake of rain the clouds that pour down rain, another kind of meaning also becomes possible.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> युं॒ग्ध्वं ह्यरु॑षी॒ रथे॑ युं॒ग्ध्वं रथे॑षु रो॒हितः॑ ।  
> युं॒ग्ध्वं हरी॑ अजि॒रा धु॒रि वोळ्ह॑वे॒ वहि॑ष्टा धु॒रि वोळ्ह॑वे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युंग्ध्वं । हि । अरुषीः । रथे । युंग्ध्वं । रथेषु । रोहितः ।  
> युंग्ध्वं । हरी इति । अजिरा । धुरि । वोळ्हने । नहिष्ठा । धुरि । वोळ्हने ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयं रथे युष्मदीये सर्वेषां साधारणभूतेऽरुषीरारोचमाना वडवा युंग्ध्वं । योजयध्वं । तथा रथेषु युष्मदीयेषु रोहितो रोहितवर्णा युंग्ध्वं । हरी अश्वावजिराजिरानाशुगमनौ धुरि वोळ्हवे वहनाय युंग्ध्वं । आदरार्थं पुनर्वचनं । वहिष्ठा वोढृतमावश्वा धुरि वोळ्हवे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, in your chariot, which is common to all, yoke the अरुषीः (*aruṣīḥ*), the shining mares. Likewise in your chariots yoke the रोहितः (*rohitaḥ*), those of red colour. Yoke the हरी (*harī*), the two horses, the अजिरा (*ajirā*), the swift-going, to the yoke, वोळ्हवे (*voḷhave*), to bear the load." The repetition is out of respect. वहिष्ठा (*vahiṣṭhā*) are the best bearers of loads, horses, to bear the load in the yoke.

### Printed p. 713

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Maruts) रथे (*rathe*)—in your chariot
- अरुषीः (*aruṣīḥ*)—golden horses
- युज्ग्ध्वं (*yujgdhvaṃ*)—join and harness
- रथेषु (*ratheṣu*)—in the chariots
- रोहितः (*rohitaḥ*)—horses of red colour
- युज्ग्ध्वं (*yujgdhvaṃ*)—yoke
- अजिरा (*ajirā*)—the swift-going
- हरी (*harī*)—horses
- धुरि (*dhuri*)—in the yokes
- वोळ्हवे (*voḷhave*)—to bear the load
- युज्ग्ध्वं (*yujgdhvaṃ*)—yoke and harness
- वहिष्ठा (*vahiṣṭhā*)—horses capable of bearing the load
- वोळ्हवे (*voḷhave*)—(yoke) for bearing the load

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, harness to your chariots golden horses and horses of an attractive colour. Join to the yokes your swift horses, for bearing the load.

##### English translation
Yoke the bright steeds to the car ; yoke the red steeds to the cars; yoke the swift pair of horses to bear the burden ; the strong bearing to bear the burden.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has said in his etymology (Ni. 2-28) that the horses of the Marut deities are पृषत्यः (*pṛṣatyaḥ*), deer with white spots. But in this Ṛk the seer, addressing the Marut deities, has prayed that three kinds of horses be joined to the yoke of their chariot.

अरुषीः—आरोचमानाः वडबाः (*aruṣīḥ—ārocamānāḥ vaḍabāḥ*). The meaning is: shining, that is, horses that are plump and attractive to look at. It is a matter of experience that healthy, strong horses are pleasing to the eye. The word अरुष (*aruṣa*) may also be explained as dull red, slightly reddish horses. That the golden-coloured horses of this kind are mentioned here applies also to the natural horses of the Marut deities, the पृषत्यः (*pṛṣatyaḥ*), that is, deer marked with white spots. As the colour of such horses and the colour of deer are generally of one kind, such deer are described here as horses, the vehicles of the Marut deities.

रोहितः—रोहितवर्णाः (*rohitaḥ—rohitavarṇāḥ*). Horses of blood-red colour, that is, of red colour. Yāska has said, in the etymology रोहितोऽग्नेः (*rohito 'gneḥ*) (Ni. 2-28), that the vehicle of Agni is रोहित (*rohita*). But here the vehicles of the Marut deities are designated by the very word रोहित (*rohita*). Probably, because the colour of the deer, the vehicle of the Maruts, is also red, the seer may have used the word रोहित (*rohita*) to convey this detail.

### Printed p. 714

हरी (*harī*)—Yāska has indicated by the sentence हरी इंद्रस्य (*harī iṃdrasya*) (Ni. 2-28) that the two horses of Indra are named हरी (*harī*). Since the word अरुष (*aruṣa*) and the word रोहित (*rohita*) mentioned above both state the colour of the deer called पृषत्यः (*pṛṣatyaḥ*), the vehicle of the Marut deities, there was a common quality in them. But हरी (*harī*) is a word used only for Indra's horses. The word हरी (*harī*) is also a word with a dual ending, indicating the number: Indra's two horses. It is the custom to refer to the horses of the Marut deities by plural words. This being so, why has the seer used the word हरी (*harī*)? Is it not a mistake to have used it? To that the following answer may be given. Indra's horses are of very great strength and capacity. Understanding by themselves the intention of Indra's mind, they have the capacity to be yoked to the chariot of their own accord in a moment and to carry Indra wherever he wishes. Such strength and capacity do not exist in the vehicles of other deities. Therefore it may be thought that, in describing the vehicles of the Marut deities in a special way, the seer has transferred to the vehicles of the Marut deities also the qualities and the excess of capacity found in Indra's horses, and that for this very reason the use of the word हरी (*harī*) is justified.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒तास्य वा॒ज्य॑रु॒षस्तु॑ वि॒ष्वणि॑रि॒ह स्म॑ धायि दर्श॒तः ।  
> मा वो॒ यामे॑षु मरुतश्चि॒रं क॑र॒त्प्र तं रथे॑षु चोदत ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । स्यः । वाजी । अरुषः । तुविस्वनिः । इह । स्म । धायि । दर्शतः ।  
> मा । वः । यामेषु । मरुतः । चिरं । करत् । प्र । तं । रथेषु । चोदत ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च स्य स वाजी वेजनवानरुष आरोचमानस्तु विष्वणिः प्रभूतध्वनिरश्वः।
> अरुष इत्यनेन रोहित इत्युक्तं भवति । प्रष्टिर्वहति रोहितः । ऋग्वे-१-३९-६ । इति
> ह्युक्तं । इहेदानीं दर्शतो दर्शनीयः सन् धायि । रथे नियोजितः । स्मेति

### Printed p. 715

> पूरणः । हे मरुतो वो यामेषु गमनेषु सोऽश्वश्चिरं विलंबं मा करत् ।
> मा करोतु । तं रथेषु । रथे युक्तमिति शेषः । प्र चोदत । प्रेरयत । यथा
> विलंबं न कुर्यात्तथा प्रेरयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"And that horse, वाजी (*vājī*), possessed of speed, अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*), shining, तुविष्वणिः (*tuviṣvaṇiḥ*), of abundant sound": by the word अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*) the red horse is meant, as has been said: प्रष्टिर्वहति रोहितः (*praṣṭirvahati rohitaḥ*) (Ṛgve. 1-39-6). **NOTE** Here now, being fair to look at, it has been placed, yoked in the chariot; the word स्म (*sma*) is a filler. "O Maruts, in your goings may that horse cause no delay. Urge it, yoked in the chariots, so that it may not delay." **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and (O Maruts)
- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—that famous
- वाजी (*vājī*)—swift
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—and shining
- तुविष्टणिः (*tuviṣṭaṇiḥ*)—and loud-sounding horse **NOTE**
- इह (*iha*)—now
- दर्शतः (*darśataḥ*)—having a form fair to look at
- धायि (*dhāyi*)—has been yoked to the chariot
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts (that same horse)
- यामेषु (*yāmeṣu*)—at the time of your going
- चिरं (*ciraṃ*)—for a long time, delay
- मा करत् (*mā karat*)—let it not make
- तं (*taṃ*)—that horse
- रथेषु (*ratheṣu*)—having joined it in the chariots
- प्र चोदत (*pra codata*)—urge on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, the swift, shining, loudly neighing horse, of a form fair to look at, has been yoked to the chariot. O Maruts, let that same horse make no delay at the time of your going. Join those horses to your chariots and urge them on.

##### English translation
And let not that horse, bright-shining, loud-neighing, of graceful form, who has been placed (in harness), delay you, Maruts, on your journey: urge him on in the car.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk also the horse of the Marut deities is described, and the prayer is stated: yoke the horse to the chariot and urge it on so that, without stopping anywhere on the way, it may come straight to the sacrificial ground.

The words स्यः (*syaḥ*) and त्यं (*tyaṃ*) have the sense of the word "that": स्यः (*syaḥ*) means सः (*saḥ*), त्यं (*tyaṃ*) means तं (*taṃ*) and त्यत् (*tyat*) means तत् (*tat*). The use of words such as स्यः (*syaḥ*), त्यं (*tyaṃ*) and तत् (*tat*) is characteristic of the Ṛgveda.

अरुषः—आरोचमानः । अरुष इत्यनेन रोहित इत्युक्तं भवति । (*aruṣaḥ—ārocamānaḥ | aruṣa ityanena rohita ityuktaṃ bhavati |*) The meaning of the word अरुष (*aruṣa*) has been explained in the Special Topics of the previous Ṛk. It can be understood from the commentator's explanation that the two words अरुष (*aruṣa*) and रोहित (*rohita*) generally have one meaning. The previous

### Printed p. 716

Ṛk has the use of the plural. In this Ṛk, beginning with अरुषः दर्शतः (*aruṣaḥ darśataḥ*), the singular is used. Since interchange of case and number is the general rule in the metre, it is not wrong to give the sense of the plural to the singular and the sense of the singular to the plural. The use of the word रोहित (*rohita*) when the vehicle of the Marut deities is described is found in Ṛks such as उपो रथेषु पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं प्रष्टिर्वहति रोहितः । (*upo ratheṣu pṛṣatīrayugdhvaṃ praṣṭirvahati rohitaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-29-6), and the commentator has cited the above Ṛk as an example.

The commentator has explained that the word स्म (*sma*) is used here as a filler of the pāda; that is, this word has no particular meaning of its own. It is used to complete the fixed number of syllables that the metre must have. In modern Sanskrit, when this word is used together with roots denoting the present tense, it conveys the sense of the past tense. For example, when the word स्म (*sma*) is joined to the word वहति (*vahati*) ("he carries"), it becomes वहति स्म (*vahati sma*), and it is the established usage to give such words the past sense "he carried".

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रथं॒ नु मारु॑तं व॒यं श्र॑व॒स्युमा हु॑वामहे ।  
> आ यस्मि॑न्त॒स्थौ सु॒रणा॑नि॒ बिभ्र॑ती॒ सचा॑ म॒रुत्सु॑ रोद॒सी ॥८॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रथं । नु । मारुतं । वयं । श्रवस्युं । आ । हुवामहे ।  
> आ । यस्मिन् । तस्थौ । सुरणानि । बिभ्रती । सचा । मरुत्सु । रोदसी ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयमात्रेया रथं रंहणस्वभावं मारुतं मरुतां संबंधिनं रथं श्रवस्युमन्नेच्छुं नु अद्या हुवामहे । आह्वयामः । यस्मिन्रथे सुरणानि सुरमणानि
> जलानि बिभ्रती धारयंती रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नि मरुतां माता । यद्वा । रुद्रो
> वायुः । तत्पत्नि माध्यमिका देवी मरुत्सु सचा सहिता आ तस्थौ आस्थितवती तं
> रथॆमाहुवे ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, the Ātreyas, today invoke the chariot of the Maruts, of rushing nature, desirous of food. In that chariot Rodasī, the wife of Rudra and the mother of the Maruts, stands together with the Maruts, bearing the pleasant-flowing waters. Or else, Rudra is the wind; his wife is the Mādhyamikā goddess, who stands together with the Maruts in that chariot. That chariot is invoked.

### Printed p. 717

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which chariot
- सुरणानि (*suraṇāni*)—waters
- बिभ्रती (*bibhratī*)—bearing
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—the wife of Rudra (the mother of the Maruts)
- मरुत्सु सचा (*marutsu sacā*)—together with the Maruts
- आ तस्थौ (*ā tasthau*)—stands, such
- मारुतुं (*mārutuṃ*)—belonging to the Maruts **NOTE**
- श्रवस्युं (*śravasyuṃ*)—desirous of food

- आ हुवामहे (*ā huvāmahe*)—we invoke with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We invoke with prayer the chariot of the Maruts, desirous of food, in which the wife of Rudra, the mother of the Maruts, or the goddess called Mādhyamikā Vāk, bearing waters, stands.

##### English translation
We invoke the food laden chariot of the Maruts, in which Rodasi stood with the Maruts, bearing the delicious (waters).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the chariot of the Marut deities is praised, and Yāska has given a nirvacana of this Ṛk:

रथं क्षिप्रं मारुतं मेघं वयं श्रवणीयमाह्वयामह आ यस्मिन्तस्था सुरमणीयान्न्युदकानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुद्भिः सह रोदसीरोदसी ॥ (*rathaṃ kṣipraṃ mārutaṃ meghaṃ vayaṃ śravaṇīyamāhvayāmaha ā yasmintasthā suramaṇīyānnyudakāni bibhratī sacā marudbhiḥ saha rodasīrodasī ‖*) (Ni. 11-50)

The chariot of the Marut deities is swift-moving and renowned for glory. In that chariot the goddess named Rodasī, the wife of Rudra and the mother of the Marut deities, stands with the Marut deities, bearing excellent waters. We invoke with prayer that chariot of the Marut deities: this is the main import of the nirvacana.

रथं (*rathaṃ*)—On the word रथं (*rathaṃ*) Yāska in his Nirukta has said: रथो रहंतेर्गतिकर्मणः। स्थिरतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य । रममाणोऽस्मिंस्तिष्ठतीति वा रपतेवा रसतेर्वा (*ratho rahaṃtergatikarmaṇaḥ| sthiratervā syādviparītasya | ramamāṇo 'smiṃstiṣṭhatīti vā rapatevā rasatervā*) (Ni. 9-11). That is, it may be derived either from the root रंह् (*raṃh*), which denotes the action of going, or from the root स्थिरति (*sthirati*), meaning "be firm". Because this chariot is always going (moving about), it is called रथ (*ratha*). Or, the warrior who sits in it remains steady: when one sits on vehicles such as horses the body shakes, but when one sits in a chariot one can sit firm without shaking, and so it is called रथ (*ratha*). Or, because one sports sitting in this chariot, it is called रथ (*ratha*). Thus he has explained the meanings of its component parts.

### Printed p. 718

रोदसी (*rodasī*)—रोदसी (*rodasī*) means heaven and earth. The proper name रोदसी (*rodasī*) also denotes, in many contexts, a person (the wife of Rudra). Therefore this word is used both in the singular and in the dual. Its meaning must be taken according to the context. The Nirukta author, quoting the Ṛk

उताभये पुरुहूत श्रवोभिरेको दृळ्हमवदो वृत्रहा सन् । इमे चिदिंद्र रोदसी अपारे यत्संगृभ्णा मघवन् काशिरित्ते ॥ (*utābhaye puruhūta śravobhireko dṛḷhamavado vṛtrahā san | ime cidiṃdra rodasī apāre yatsaṃgṛbhṇā maghavan kāśiritte ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-5)

and stating there the nirvacana of the word रोदसी (*rodasī*), (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-5)

रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य विरोधनात् । (*rodasī dyāvāpṛthivya virodhanāt |*) (Ni. 6-1)

has said that the name रोदसी (*rodasī*) is well known for heaven and earth because they are bound and regulated by a limited boundary (limit); this should be understood. This is the nirvacana of the word रोदसी (*rodasī*) ending in the dual. Again, giving the meaning of the word ending in the singular, he says:

रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नीः (*rodasī rudrasya patnīḥ*) (Ni. 11-49)

Explaining that Rodasī is the wife of Rudra, he quotes the present Ṛk

रथं नु मारुतं वयं श्रवस्युमा हुवामहे । आ यस्मिन्तस्थौ सुरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ॥ (*rathaṃ nu mārutaṃ vayaṃ śravasyumā huvāmahe | ā yasmintasthau suraṇāni bibhratī sacā marutsu rodasī ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-56-8)

and has shown that here, in the word Rodasī, there is the use of the proper name meaning the wife of Rudra. **NOTE** But here another problem arises. Does "the wife of Rudra" mean the wife of the deity Rudra, or, the word Rudra meaning Marut, the wife of the Marut deities? Sāyaṇa has commented in both places in a way that leaves room for this doubt. While explaining the present Ṛk he says:

रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नि मरुतां माता । यद्वा रुद्रो वायुः । तत्पत्नी माध्यमिका देवी ॥ (*rodasī rudrasya patni marutāṃ mātā | yadvā rudro vāyuḥ | tatpatnī mādhyamikā devī ‖*) (Sa. Bha.) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 719

One meaning may be that Rodasī is the wife of Rudra and the mother of the Maruts. Or, since the word Rudra means the wind, Rodasī is the wife of the wind, the Mādhyamikā Vāk: this is the second meaning. Thus he has explained it in two ways. And in explaining the Ṛk

परा शुभ्रा अयासो यव्या साधारण्येव मरुतो मिमिक्षुः । न रोदसी अप नुदंत घोरा जुषंत वृधं सख्याय देवाः ॥ (*parā śubhrā ayāso yavyā sādhāraṇyeva maruto mimikṣuḥ | na rodasī apa nudaṃta ghorā juṣaṃta vṛdhaṃ sakhyāya devāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-167-4)

**NOTE** he says, as stated earlier:

रोदसा शब्देन रोदनस्वभावो रुद्रः । तस्य स्त्री रोदसीति केचिदाहुः । अपरे तु मरुतां स्त्रीयो रोदसीति नामधेयमित्याहुः । अयमेव पक्षो युक्त उत्तरत्रैवं व्यवहारात् ॥ (*rodasā śabdena rodanasvabhāvo rudraḥ | tasya strī rodasīti kecidāhuḥ | apare tu marutāṃ strīyo rodasīti nāmadheyamityāhuḥ | ayameva pakṣo yukta uttaratraivaṃ vyavahārāt ‖*)

That Rodasī is the wife of Rudra is one view; that she is the wife of the Maruts is another. Of these, the second alone seems to be correct: thus he has stated his opinion. Besides, in explaining the Ṛk

जोषद्यदीमसुर्य्या सचध्यै विषितस्तुका रोदसी नृमणाः ॥ (*joṣadyadīmasuryyā sacadhyai viṣitastukā rodasī nṛmaṇāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-167.5)

he has stated: रोदसी मरुत्पत्नी विद्युद्वा । (*rodasī marutpatnī vidyudvā |*) Rodasī is the wife of the Maruts, or lightning is known by this name. And he has also cited the matter, described there, that this Rodasī is to be found only in pursuit of the Maruts. And if some more contexts in which the word रोदसी (*rodasī*) is used are examined, in the single Ṛk

त इदुग्राः शवसा धृष्णुषेणा उभे युजंत रोदसी सुमेके । अध स्मैषु रोदसी स्वशोचिरामवत्सु तस्थौ न रोकः ॥ (*ta idugrāḥ śavasā dhṛṣṇuṣeṇā ubhe yujaṃta rodasī sumeke | adha smaiṣu rodasī svaśocirāmavatsu tasthau na rokaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-66-6)

the word रोदसी (*rodasī*) is used in both senses. Here Sāyaṇa has explained the first word as द्यावापृथिव्य (*dyāvāpṛthivya*) and the second as रुद्रस्य पत्नि माध्यमिका वाक् (*rudrasya patni mādhyamikā vāk*). And in

मिन्यक्ष येषु रोदसी नु देवी सिषक्ति पूषा अभ्यर्धयज्वा । श्रुत्वा हवं मरुतो यद्ध याथ भूमा रेजंते अध्वनि प्रविक्ते ॥ (*minyakṣa yeṣu rodasī nu devī siṣakti pūṣā abhyardhayajvā | śrutvā havaṃ maruto yaddha yātha bhūmā rejaṃte adhvani pravikte ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-50-5)

### Printed p. 720

too it is explained only as देवी द्योतमाना माध्यमिका वाक् (*devī dyotamānā mādhyamikā vāk*). While giving the explanation of the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-167-3, the scholar Max Muller states as follows the matter of the word रोदसी (*rodasī*), used in the senses of lightning, Mādhyamikā Vāk and heaven and earth.

In our verse, we take वाक् (*vāk*) in the sense of thunder, but as a feminine, of the lightning and thunder as the two companions of the Maruts, represents the first, रोदसी (*rodasī*) or lightning, as the recognised wife, hiding herself in the house, while the other, the loud thunder, is represented as a more public companion of the Maruts. This contrast, if it is really what the poet intended, throws a curious light on the social character of the Vedic times, as it presupposes two classes of wives, not necessarily simultanious, however—, a house wife, who stays at home and is not much seen, and a wife who appears in public and takes part in the society......... The loud voice of the thunder as well as the usual hiding of the lightning might well suggest this comparison. [ S. B. E. XXXII p. 276 ]

Showing in this way the difference between the use of the singular and the use of the dual, the Bṛhaddevatā says:

रोदसी देवपत्नीनां अथर्वांगिरसे यथा । (*rodasī devapatnīnāṃ atharvāṃgirase yathā |*) (Bṛ. De. 2-143)

Here is an example of the use of the singular: according to the view of the Atharvāṅgirasa (the Atharvaveda), Rodasī is one of the wives of the gods. And:

द्वे द्वे पदे संस्तुते रोदसी च देवाश्चार्चेन विभक्तमन्यत् । (*dve dve pade saṃstute rodasī ca devāścārcena vibhaktamanyat |*) (Bṛ. De. 4-6)

In all such places where the dual is used, heaven and earth are meant.

### Printed p. 721

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं वः॒ शर्धं॑ रथे॒शुभं॑ त्वे॒षं प॑न॒स्कुमा हु॑वे ।  
> यस्मि॒न्तु जा॑ता सु॒भगा॑ मही॒यते॒ सचा॑ म॒रुत्सु॑ मीळु॒षी ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । वः । शर्धं । रथेऽशुभं ' त्वेषं । पनस्युं । आ । हुवे ।  
> यस्मिन् । सुजाता । सुभगा । महीयते । सचा । मरुत्सु । विळ्ळुषी ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो वः शर्धं युष्मदीयं बलं गणं रथेशुभं रथे शोभनं
> त्वेषं दीप्तं पनस्युं स्तुत्यमा हुवे । आह्वये । यस्मिन् शर्धे सुजाता सुष्टु
> प्रवृद्धा सुभगा शोभनभाग्यातिमहती मीळ्हुषी मीळ्हुष्टम शिवतमेत्यादौ दर्श
> नान्मीढ्वानुद्रः । तत्पत्नी मीळ्हुषी । मरुत्तु सजा सह महीयते पूज्यते तं शर्धमा हुवे । आपस्तंबोऽपि रुद्रपत्नीं मीळ्हुषीसंज्ञया व्यवजहार । उत्तरया
> दक्षिणस्यामीशानमावाहयति लौकिक्या वाचोत्तरस्यां मीळ्हुषीं मध्यॆ जयंतं । अप. गृ. २०. १.३. । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, I invoke your शर्धं (*śardhaṃ*), that is, your strength, your host, which graces the chariot, brilliant and adorable. In that host Sujātā, well grown, and Subhagā, of auspicious fortune and very great, is worshipped, together with the Maruts. She is Mīḷhuṣī: because Rudra is seen to be called मीढ्वान् (*mīḍhvān*) in such places as मीळ्हुष्टम शिवतमेत्यादौ (*mīḷhuṣṭama śivatametyādau*), Mīḷhuṣī is his wife. That host I invoke. Āpastamba too, he adds, used the name Mīḷhuṣī for the wife of Rudra, and he quotes a passage (Apa. Gṛ. 20. 1.3) **NOTE** in which Īśāna is invoked in the south, and Mīḷhuṣī in the north, with the next verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which host
- सुजाता (*sujātā*)—of divine birth
- सुभगा (*subhagā*)—of auspicious form
- मीळ्हुषी (*mīḷhuṣī*)—the wife of Rudra
- मरुत्तु सचा (*maruttu sacā*)—together with the Maruts **NOTE**
- महीयते (*mahīyate*)—shines, worshipped
- तं (*taṃ*)—that
- रथेशुभं (*ratheśubhaṃ*)—that which is an ornament to the chariot
- त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)—brilliant
- पनस्युं (*panasyuṃ*)—adorable
- वः शर्धं (*vaḥ śardhaṃ*)—your host
- आ हुवे (*ā huve*)—I invoke with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, I invoke with prayer that host of yours, an ornament to the chariot, brilliant and adorable, in which the wife of Rudra, of divine birth and of auspicious form, stands together with the Maruts, worshipped and shining.

### Printed p. 722

##### English translation
I invoke that, your cohort, gracing the chariot, brilliant and adorable, amidst which the rain-bestowing (goddess), of goodly origin, and auspicious, is worshipped together with the Maruts.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk also the chariot of the Marut deities, Rodasī, the wife of Rudra, and the Marut host, all of them, are praised.

मीळ्हुषी—मीळ्हुष्टम शिवतनु इत्यादौ दर्शनात् मीढ्वान् रुद्रः । तत्पत्नि मीळ्हुषी । (*mīḷhuṣī—mīḷhuṣṭama śivatanu ityādau darśanāt mīḍhvān rudraḥ | tatpatni mīḷhuṣī |*) In the Rudra chapter of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 4-5-10-4) it is said मीळ्हुष्टम शिवतनु (*mīḷhuṣṭama śivatanu*), so the word मीढ्वान् (*mīḍhvān*) denotes Rudra. The commentator has explained that मीळ्हुषी (*mīḷhuṣī*) means the wife of that Rudra, and in support of this he has cited the passage of the Āpastamba Gṛhya Sūtra

उत्तरया दक्षिणस्यामीशानमावाहयति लौकिक्या वाचोत्तरस्यां मीळ्हुषीं मध्ये जयंतं ॥ (*uttarayā dakṣiṇasyāmīśānamāvāhayati laukikyā vācottarasyāṃ mīḷhuṣīṃ madhye jayaṃtaṃ ‖*) (Āsa. Gṛ. Sū. 20-1-3) **NOTE**

and has shown that the word माळ्हुषीं (*māḷhuṣīṃ*) there denotes the wife of Rudra. **NOTE** Besides, in the 18th anuvāka of the second Prapāṭhaka of the part of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda called एकाग्नि कांड (*ekāgni kāṃḍa*):

वाताजिरैरायाहि मम हन्याय शर्वोपस्पृशतु मीढ्वान् मीढुषे स्वाहोपस्पृशतु मीढुषी मीढुष्यै स्वाहा जयंतोपस्पृश जयंताय स्वाहा भवाय देवाय स्वाहा । (*vātājirairāyāhi mama hanyāya śarvopaspṛśatu mīḍhvān mīḍhuṣe svāhopaspṛśatu mīḍhuṣī mīḍhuṣyai svāhā jayaṃtopaspṛśa jayaṃtāya svāhā bhavāya devāya svāhā |*) (Tai. एकाग्नि कांड (*ekāgni kāṃḍa*). Pra. 2.18) **NOTE**

in this Śruti sentence it is clear that the word माध्वान् (*mādhvān*) **NOTE** indicates Rudra and the word माधुषी (*mādhuṣī*) indicates the wife of Rudra.

The fifty-seventh hymn. **NOTE**

## Sūkta 57 (Maṇḍala 5)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पंचमेऽनुवाके षोडश सूक्तानि । तत्रा रुद्रास इत्यष्टर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं
> श्यावाश्वस्यार्षं मारुतं । सप्तम्यष्टम्या त्रिष्टुभौ शिष्टाः षट् जगत्यः। आ रुद्रासोऽष्टौ
> द्वित्रिष्टुबंतमित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the fifth Anuvāka there are sixteen hymns. Of these, the first, the hymn with the word रुद्रास (*rudrāsa*), is of eight Ṛks; its seer is Śyāvāśva and its deity the Maruts. The seventh and the eighth Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining six are in the Jagatī metre. The Anukramaṇikā says: आ रुद्रासोऽष्टौ द्वित्रिष्टुबंतमित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ (*ā rudrāso 'ṣṭau dvitriṣṭubaṃtamityanukramaṇikā ‖*). The application of the hymn is by indication (liṅga).

### Printed p. 723

Translation: In the fifth Anuvāka of the fifth Maṇḍala there are sixteen hymns. Of these, this hymn beginning आ रुद्रासः (*ā rudrāsaḥ*) is the first. It has eight Ṛks. The seer of this hymn is Śyāvāśva; the deity is the Maruts. The seventh and eighth Ṛks of this hymn are in the Triṣṭubh metre. The remaining six Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: द्वित्रिष्टुबंतं (*dvitriṣṭubaṃtaṃ*) **NOTE**. The application is by indication (liṅga).

- Sūkta: 57
- Maṇḍala 5; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 57
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 3; Varga 21, 22
- Number of Ṛks in the Sūkta: 8
- Ṛṣi: Śyāvāśva Ātreya
- Devatā: Maruts
- Chandas: 1-6 Jagatī; 7-8 Triṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ रु॑द्रास॒ इंद्र॑वंतः स॒जोष॑सो॒ हिर॑ण्यरथाः सुवि॒ताय॑  
> गंतन ।  
> इ॒यं वो॑ अ॒स्मत्पति॑ हर्यते म॒तिस्त्रृ॒ष्णजे॒ न दि॒व उत्सा॑  ॒॑
> उदन्यवे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । रुद्रासः । इंद्रवंतः । सजोषसः । हिरण्यरथाः । सुविताय । गंतन ।  
> इयं । वः । अस्मत् । प्रति । हर्यते । मतिः । तृष्णजे । न । दिवः । उत्साः ।  
> उदन्यवे ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 724

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे रुद्रासो रुद्रपुत्रा इंद्रवंत इंद्रेण युष्मत्स्वामिना तद्वंतः सजोषसः परस्परं समानप्रीतयो हिरण्यरथा हिरण्यमयरथाः संतः सुविताय सुगमनाय तत्साधनाय सुष्टु सर्वैर्गंतव्याय यज्ञाय तदर्थमा गंतन । आगच्छत ।
> किमत्र विद्यत इति तदुच्यते । इयमस्मदस्मदीया मतिः स्तुतिवोर्युष्मान् प्रति
> हर्यते । कामयते । तस्मादागच्छत । उदन्यव उदकेच्छवे तृष्णजे गोतमाय
> दिवो द्युलोकसकाशादुत्सा उदकनिष्यंदा यथा युष्माभिः प्रेरितास्तद्वदस्मदर्थमप्यागत्याभिमतं ददतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Rudras, sons of Rudra, accompanied by Indra, your lord, of one mind and mutual delight, having golden chariots, come for सुविताय (*suvitāya*), that is, for the sacrifice, the means of good going, to which all should go well; come to it. He then says what there is here: this our praise (मतिः (*matiḥ*)) desires you; therefore come. As the streams of water (उत्साः (*utsāḥ*)), sent by you from the heavenly world, came for Gotama, thirsty and desiring water, so also come for us, and grant what we wish.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रवंतः (*iṃdravaṃtaḥ*)—companions of Indra
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—having mutual affection
- हिरण्यरथाः (*hiraṇyarathāḥ*)—having chariots made of gold
- रुद्रासः (*rudrāsaḥ*)—O sons of Rudra (Maruts)
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—to the sacrifice, an excellent place
- आ गंतन (*ā gaṃtana*)—come
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—made by us
- वः (*vaḥ*)—addressed to you
- इयं मतिः (*iyaṃ matiḥ*)—this praise
- प्रति हठते (*prati haṭhate*)—being offered, desires to reach you **NOTE**
- तृष्णजे (*tṛṣṇaje*)—tormented by thirst
- उदन्यवे (*udanyave*)—desiring water, for Gotama
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the atmosphere
- उत्साः न (*utsāḥ na*)—taking flowing waters, as you descended (so be gracious to our sacrifice also)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, companions of Indra, mutually affectionate, having chariots made of gold, sons of Rudra, come to the sacrifice, an excellent place. This praise, made by us and addressed to you, being offered, desires to reach you. As you came from the atmosphere, taking flowing waters for Gotama, who was tormented by thirst and desired water, so come to our sacrifice also.

##### English translation
Rudras, servants of Indra, mutually kind, riding in golden cars come to the accessible (sacrifice): this our praise is addressed to you: (come to us as you came) from heaven, (bringing) oozing water to the thirsty (Gotama) longing for moisture.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

रुद्रासः— रुद्रपुत्राः मरुतः । (*rudrāsaḥ— rudraputrāḥ marutaḥ |*) The Marut deities, the sons of Rudra, are here designated रुद्रासः (*rudrāsaḥ*) by their father's name alone.

### Printed p. 725

The eternal companionship between Indra and the Maruts, the relation of king and subjects between them, the offering of the oblation in the principal sacrificial acts to Indra together with the Maruts, and the help given by the Maruts to Indra when he fought with the demon Vṛtra are praised in many places in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. A story of former times telling how Indra, joined with the Maruts, stood apart from the other deities is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:

आतिथ्येन वै देवा इष्ट्वा । तान्त्समदविंदत्ते चतुर्धाव्यद्रवन्नन्योन्यस्य श्रिया तिष्ठमाना अग्निर्वसुभिः सोमो रुद्रैर्वरुण आदित्यैरिंद्रो मरुद्भिर्भृहस्पतिर्विश्वेदेवैः । (*ātithyena vai devā iṣṭvā | tāntsamadaviṃdatte caturdhāvyadravannanyonyasya śriyā tiṣṭhamānā agnirvasubhiḥ somo rudrairvaruṇa ādityairiṃdro marudbhirbhṛhaspatirviśvedevaiḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 3-4-2-1)

In former times, when the deities performed the Ātithya rite, discord arose among them; unwilling to join one another, they formed four groups and became separate. Agni joined the Vasus, Soma the Rudras, Varuṇa the Ādityas, Indra the Maruts, and Bṛhaspati the Viśvedevas, and each formed a separate group. **NOTE** In this story the close relation that Indra has kept with the Maruts, having developed companionship with them, is told.

Besides, it is said in many places that Indra is the king and the Maruts are the subjects. For example, in the same Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:

क्षत्रं ना इंद्रो विशो मरुतो विशा नै क्षत्रियो बलवान् भवति । (*kṣatraṃ nā iṃdro viśo maruto viśā nai kṣatriyo balavān bhavati |*) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-3-6)

Indra is a king possessed of the splendour of the warrior class. The Maruts are his subjects. It is indicated that only through the cooperation of the subjects does the king become powerful, and that Indra's valour increased through the help of the Maruts. Because there is such a close relation and companionship, the practice of offering oblations addressed jointly to Indra and the Maruts is found in the Śrutis. And in Ṛks such as

स नो मरुद्भिवृषभ श्रवो धा उग्र उग्रेभिः स्थविरः सहोदाः । (*sa no marudbhivṛṣabha śravo dhā ugra ugrebhiḥ sthaviraḥ sahodāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-5)

there are the invitation and the offering of the oblation jointly to Indra and the Maruts. Describing this companionship, the Bṛhaddevatā says:

मरुद्भिः सह यत्रेंद्रो मरुत्वांस्तत्र सोऽभवत् । (*marudbhiḥ saha yatreṃdro marutvāṃstatra so 'bhavat |*) (Bṛ. De. 4-56)

### Printed p. 726

By sentences such as this the qualifying word indicating the relationship of these deities is explained. But in one hymn, as a result of a dispute between Indra and the Maruts, their discord and Indra's anger are indicated. The dispute between them that is the source of this anger is told thus:

क्वंस्यावो मरुतः स्वधासीद्यन्मामेकं समधत्ताहिहॆत्ये । आहं ह्युंग्रस्तविषस्तुविष्मान्विश्वस्व शत्रोरनमं वधस्नैः ॥ (*kvaṃsyāvo marutaḥ svadhāsīdyanmāmekaṃ samadhattāhihètye | āhaṃ hyuṃgrastaviṣastuviṣmānviśvasva śatroranamaṃ vadhasnaiḥ ‖*) (Mu. Saṃ. 1..165-6) **NOTE**

"O Maruts, it is false to say that with your help I killed Ahi. Where was that strength of yours? Because my own strength is extraordinary, it helped me at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra without seeking the help of any other strength. I alone am fierce, of wonderful power, and endowed with greatness." Thus he looks at the Maruts with contempt and shows his anger. Here that anger is indicated. It is well known that Indra received the help of the Maruts at the time of the slaying of the demon Vṛtra. Even so, when the Maruts mentioned that matter and asked that, in memory of that help, they too be given a share in the oblation due to Indra, Indra says that no help whatever came from the Maruts and that he killed all his enemies by his own strength. The author of the Nirukta, telling this same matter, has said:

अगस्त्य इंद्राय हविर्निरुप्य मरुद्भः संप्रदित्सांचकार । स इंद्र एत्य परिदेवयांचक्रे । (*agastya iṃdrāya havirnirupya marudbhaḥ saṃpraditsāṃcakāra | sa iṃdra etya paridevayāṃcakre |*) (Ni. 1-5)

When the sage Āgastya prepared an oblation for Indra and wished to offer a share in it to the Maruts also, Indra objected in that matter. Having stated this context, the Nirukta author quoted the Ṛk that conveys this point:

न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतं । अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं विनश्यति ॥ (*na nūnamasti no śvaḥ kastadveda yadadbhutaṃ | anyasya cittamabhi saṃcareṇyamutādhītaṃ vinaśyati ‖*) (Ma. Sa. 1-170-1). **NOTE**

So that the force of that anger might abate and not harm him, and with the intention that the share of the oblation justly due to the Maruts must reach them, the Maruts are addressed in prayer here. After this kind of conciliatory speech, Indra's friendship grew as before, and he himself gives a share of his oblation to the Maruts also. This same matter the seer has stated and praised in the eighth Maṇḍala thus:

### Printed p. 727

वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अजहुर्ये सखायः । मरुद्धरिंद्र सख्यं ते अस्त्वथेमा विश्वाः पृतना जयासि ॥ (*vṛtrasya tvā śvasathādīṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahurye sakhāyaḥ | maruddhariṃdra sakhyaṃ te astvathemā viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-7)

O Indra, your friendship with the Maruts is well known; giving them also a share in your oblation, conquer all the enemies with their help: thus the prayer is made.

उदन्यवे तृष्णजे दिवः उत्साः—उदकेच्छवे गोतमाय द्युलोकसकाशात् उदकनिष्यंदा युष्माभिः प्रेरिताः । (*udanyave tṛṣṇaje divaḥ utsāḥ—udakecchave gotamāya dyulokasakāśāt udakaniṣyaṃdā yuṣmābhiḥ preritāḥ |*) It is stated here that, to satisfy the seer named Gotama, who was wandering in the forest with thirst, they brought from the atmosphere a well full of water.

परावतं नासत्यानुदेथामुच्चा बुद्धं चक्रथुर्जिह्मबारं ॥ क्षरन्नापो न पायनाय राये सहस्राय तृष्यते गोतमस्य ॥ (*parāvataṃ nāsatyānudethāmuccā buddhaṃ cakrathurjihmabāraṃ ‖ kṣarannāpo na pāyanāya rāye sahasrāya tṛṣyate gotamasya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-9)

In this Ṛk there is a description of this matter. A seer named Gotama, suffering from great thirst while wandering in a desert (a sandy forest), searched for water to drink, and since he found none, he prayed to the Aśvin deities for water. They brought him a well full of water, and made it so that its bottom was upward and the upper part with the water faced downward, so that the seer drank water, as it were, from a vessel. By this his thirst was quenched: this history is described here. And:

जिह्मं नुनुद्रेऽवतं तया दिशासिंचन्नुत्सं गोतमाय तृष्णजे । आ गच्छंतीमवसा चित्रभानवः कामं विप्रस्य तर्पयंत धामभिः ॥ (*jihmaṃ nunudre 'vataṃ tayā diśāsiṃcannutsaṃ gotamāya tṛṣṇaje | ā gacchaṃtīmavasā citrabhānavaḥ kāmaṃ viprasya tarpayaṃta dhāmabhiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-85-11)

In this Ṛk the Marut deities set the well they had dug in the direction in which the seer Gotama dwelt and made water available. Then, placing that well in the seer's hermitage itself, they made a stream of water flow for the thirsty seer Gotama. The Maruts, of manifold radiance, approaching the devoted seer Gotama with such protection, satisfied the desire of that wise one with the waters that sustain life: so it is said. Although the word गोतम (*gotama*) is not used in the present Ṛk, the commentator has said that the matter applies to the seer Gotama, and that by this the greatness of the Marut deities is described.

### Printed p. 728

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वाशी॑मंत ऋष्टि॒मंतो॑ मनी॒षिणः॑ सु॒धन्वा॑न॒ इषु॑मंतो  ॒॑
> निषंगिणः ।  
> स्वश्वाः॑ स्थ सु॒रथाः॑ पृत्विमातरः स्वायु॒धा म॑रुतो याथना॒  ॑
> शुभं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वाशीमंतः । ऋष्टिमंतः । मनीषिणः । सुधन्वानः । इषुमंतः । निषंगिणः ।  
> सुअश्वाः । स्थ । सुरथाः । पृश्निमातरः । सुआयुधाः । मरुतः । याथन । शुभं॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयं नाशीमंतः । नाशीति तक्षणसाधनमायुधं । तद्वंतः
> स्थ । ऋष्टिमंतः । ऋष्टिर्नामभुरिका । तद्वंतः स्थ । एवं सर्वत्र योज्यं । मनीषिणो मनस ईश्वरा मनस्सिनः सुधन्वानः शोभनधनुष्का इषुमंतो वाणवंतो
> निषंगिणो निषंगवंतः स्वश्वाः स्थ । शोभनाश्वा भवथ । सुरथाः शोभनरथाः पृश्निमातरः पृश्नेः पुत्राः स्वायुधाः खड्ग परश्वादिसकलायुधोपेताः । एवं
> महात्मानः संतः शुभं शोभनं यथा भवति तथा शुभमुदकाय वा रथेन याथन।
> गच्छथ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, you possess the weapon नाशीमंतः (*nāśīmaṃtaḥ*), नाशी (*nāśī*) being a weapon that serves for cutting. **NOTE** You have ऋष्टिमंतः (*ṛṣṭimaṃtaḥ*), ऋष्टि (*ṛṣṭi*) being called भुरिका (*bhurikā*); and so it is to be construed with every word. You are मनीषिणः (*manīṣiṇaḥ*), lords of the mind, thoughtful; having fine bows, with arrows, with quivers; you have fine horses and fine chariots; you are the sons of Pṛśni, equipped with every weapon such as sword and axe. Being such great ones, come in the chariot शुभं (*śubhaṃ*), that is, in an auspicious way; or else come शुभमुदकाय (*śubhamudakāya*), for water.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनीषिणः (*manīṣiṇaḥ*)—wise
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- वाशीमंतः (*vāśīmaṃtaḥ*)—having a sharp-edged sword
- ऋष्टिमंतः (*ṛṣṭimaṃtaḥ*)—having spears
- सुधन्वानः (*sudhanvānaḥ*)—having excellent bows
- इषुमंतः (*iṣumaṃtaḥ*)—bearing arrows
- निषंगिणः (*niṣaṃgiṇaḥ*)—having quivers
- स्वश्वाः (*svaśvāḥ*)—having excellent horses
- सुरथाः (*surathāḥ*)—possessing excellent chariots
- स्थ (*stha*)—you are
- पृश्निमातरः (*pṛśnimātaraḥ*)—sons of Pṛśni
- स्वायुधाः (*svāyudhāḥ*)—having excellent weapons
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- शुभं (*śubhaṃ*)—to bring us auspiciousness
- याथन (*yāthana*)—come

### Printed p. 729

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise Maruts, you are possessed of sharp-edged swords and of shields; you are possessed of excellent bows, arrows and quivers, and you are furnished with excellent chariots and horses. O Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, come with your excellent weapons to bring us auspiciousness.

##### English translation
Intelligent Maruts, you are armed with swords, with lances, with bows, with arrows, with quivers; you are well mounted and have handsome chariots; sons of Prishni, you are well armed; come for our good.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वाशीमंतः (*vāśīmaṃtaḥ*)—Explaining the word वाशी (*vāśī*), Yāska cites the Ṛk आ तू षिंच हरिमीं द्रोरुपस्थे वाशीभिस्तक्षताश्मन्मयाभिः । परि ष्वजध्वं दश कक्ष्याभिरुभे धुरौ प्रति वह्निं युनक्त ॥ (*ā tū ṣiṃca harimīṃ drorupasthe vāśībhistakṣatāśmanmayābhiḥ | pari ṣvajadhvaṃ daśa kakṣyābhirubhe dhurau prati vahniṃ yunakta ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-101-10), and for the word वाशीभिः (*vāśībhiḥ*) occurring in that Ṛk he gives the etymology वाशीभिरश्मयाभिरिति ना । वाग्निरितिवा । (*vāśībhiraśmayābhiriti nā | vāgniritivā |*) (Ni. 4-19). The word वाशी (*vāśī*) is read among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23). Here वाशीभिः (*vāśībhiḥ*) means a special pointed weapon made of stone, fashioned from stone itself with chisels. In this Ṛk the weapons of the Maruts are stated: वाशी ऋष्टि (*vāśī ṛṣṭi*), the bow, the arrow and other weapons. That is, a special weapon made of stone or as hard as stone, a spear with a sharp edge, a bow, an arrow and other weapons: wearing these and seated in a fine chariot, they are prayed to set out in order to pour down water in the form of rain.

पृश्निमातरः (*pṛśnimātaraḥ*)—Those who have Pṛśni as their mother. The name of the mother of the Maruts is Pṛśni, a cow, or the wife of Rudra. The explanation of the word पृश्निमातरः (*pṛśnimātaraḥ*) we have already given earlier.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धू॒नु॒थ द्यां पर्व॑तान्ना॒शुषे॒ वसु॒ नि वो॒ वना॑ जिहते॒ ॑ ॒
> याम॑नो भि॒या ।

### Printed p. 730

> कोपयथ पृथिवीं पृश्निमातरः शुभे यदुग्राः पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ॥ सदपाठ ॥  
> धूनुथ । द्यां । पर्वतान् । दाशुषे । वसु । नि । वः । वना । जहते । यामनः ।  
> भिया ।  
> कोपयथ । पृथिवीं । पृश्निमातरः । शुभे । यत् । उग्राः । पृषतीं । आयुग्ध्वं॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो द्यां । दिवीत्यर्थः । पर्वतान्नेघान्दाशुषे हविर्दात्रे यजमानाय वसु धनानि च धूनुथ । प्रापयथ । वो युष्माकु यामनो गमनस्य
> भिया भीत्या वना वनानि वृक्षादिसमूहा नि जिहते । नितरां कंपंते । अवनता भृशं
> शंसंतीत्यर्थः । हे पृश्निमातरः पृश्ने पुत्राः । पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाता
> इति हि श्रुतिः । हे मरुतः पृथिवीं कोपयथ । अभिवृष्टा क्षोभयथ । हे उग्रा
> उद्धूर्णबला यूयं यद्यदा शुभ उदकार्थं पृषतीर्युष्मदीया अश्वा
> अयुग्वं योजयथ तदा कोपयथ पृथिवीं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing the Maruts, Sāyaṇa says: O Maruts, you shake the sky, that is, in the heaven, the clouds, and you bring wealth, riches, to the sacrificer who offers oblations. Through fear of your going, the forests, that is, the masses of trees and the like, tremble violently; he adds that they bow down, and some further words of the gloss are unclear.**NOTE** He then explains "sons of Pṛśni" as the sons of Pṛśni, for there is a Śruti that the Maruts were born from the milk of Pṛśni. O Maruts, you agitate the earth, making it quake with the rain that falls on it. O fierce ones, whose strength is stirred up: when, for the sake of water, you yoke your spotted horses, then you agitate the earth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—(O Maruts) to the sacrificer who gives oblations
- वसु (*vasu*)—for providing wealth
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—in the heaven (the atmosphere)
- पर्वतान् (*parvatān*)—the clouds
- धूनथ (*dhūnatha*)—you cause to shake
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- यामनः (*yāmanaḥ*)—of the going
- भिया (*bhiyā*)—through fear
- वना (*vanā*)—the masses of trees
- नि जिहते (*ni jihate*)—tremble completely
- उग्रा: (*ugrā:*)—fierce
- पृश्निमातरः (*pṛśnimātaraḥ*)—sons of Pṛśni, O Maruts
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- शुभे (*śubhe*)—for the sake of water
- पृषतीः (*pṛṣatīḥ*)—your horses (spotted deer)
- आयुग्ध्वं (*āyugdhvaṃ*)—you yoke to the chariot (then)
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- कोपयथ (*kopayatha*)—you cause to be agitated

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, in order to provide wealth to the sacrificer who gives oblations, you cause the clouds to shake in the atmosphere. Through fear of your going, the masses of trees tremble completely. O fierce Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, when for the sake of water you yoke your spotted deer to the chariot, then you cause the earth to be agitated.

### Printed p. 731

##### English translation
You agitate the clouds in the sky; (you give) wealth to the donor (of oblations); through fear of your approach the forests bow down; sons of Prishni, you incense the earth when, for the purpose of (sending) water, you fierce (Maruts), yoke your spotted steeds.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वात॑त्विषो म॒रुतो॑ व॒र्षनि॑र्णिजो य॒माइ॑व॒ सुस॑दृशःसु॒पेश॑सः ।  
> पि॒शंगा॑श्वा अरु॒णाश्वा॑ अरे॒पसः॒ प्रत्व॑क्षसो महि॒ना द्यौरि॑वो॒रवः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वातृषिषः । मरुतः । वर्षनिर्निजः । यमाः इव । सुसदृशः । सुपेशसः ।  
> पिशंगाश्वाः । अरुणाश्वाः । अरेपसः । प्रत्वक्षसः । महिना । द्यौ इव । उरवः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वातत्विषः सर्वदा संप्राप्तदीप्तयो वर्षनिर्णिजो वृष्टेः शोधयितारः ।
> अथवा निर्णिगिति रूपनाम ! वर्षमेव रूपं येषां ते तादृशाः । वृष्टि प्रदा
> इत्यर्थः । यमा इव युगलोत्पन्ना इव सुसदृशाः परस्परं बलरूपादिभिरत्यंतं
> सरूपाः सुपेशसः शोभनरूपाः पिशंगाश्वाः पिशंगवर्णाश्वेतास्तथारुणाश्वा
> अरेपसोऽपापाः प्रत्वक्षसः प्रकृष्टं तनूकर्तारो द्वेष्ट्याणां महिना महत्त्वेन
> दौरिवांतरिक्षमिवोरवो विस्तीर्णाः । उक्तलक्षणा नाम भेजिर इत्युत्तरेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts are always endowed with attained radiance, and they are purifiers of the rain. Or else, taking the word for "form" as a name of form, they are those whose form is rain itself, that is, givers of rain. They are like twins, born as a pair: very much alike one another in strength, form and so on, of beautiful form, having tawny horses and likewise ruddy horses, sinless, greatly thinning out the bodies of those who hate them, and by their greatness vast like the sky, the atmosphere. These characteristics are to be connected with the verb of the following Ṛk, which says that they obtained the said names.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- वातत्विषः (*vātatviṣaḥ*)—possessed of ever-attained radiance
- वर्षनिर्णिजः (*varṣanirṇijaḥ*)—purifiers of the rain
- यमा इव (*yamā iva*)—like twins
- सुसदृशः (*susadṛśaḥ*)—of one and the same form

### Printed p. 732

- सुपेशसः (*supeśasaḥ*)—of beautiful shape
- पिशंगाश्वाः (*piśaṃgāśvāḥ*)—having horses of tawny colour
- अरुणाश्वाः (*aruṇāśvāḥ*)—having horses of golden-red colour
- अरेपसः (*arepasaḥ*)—free from sin
- प्रत्वक्षसः (*pratvakṣasaḥ*)—destroyers of enemies, being such
- महिना (*mahinā*)—by their greatness
- द्यौरिन (*dyaurina*)—like the atmosphere
- उरवः (*uravaḥ*)—shine forth as having a vast form

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, who always possess radiance, who purify the rain, who like twins have one and the same form, who are of beautiful shape, who have horses of tawny colour and of golden-red colour, who are sinless and destroyers of enemies, shine forth by their greatness as having a form vast like the atmosphere.

##### English translation
The Maruts, radiant with light, purifiers of the rain, like twins of goodly aspect and graceful form, masters of tawny and of ruddy steeds, devoid of guile, thinners (of foes), and vast in magnitude as the sky.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वर्षनिर्णिजः (*varṣanirṇijaḥ*)—Purifiers of the rain; or, if the word निर्णिक् (*nirṇik*) is taken to mean form, those whose form or nature is rain itself, that is, those who produce rain: thus the commentator has given two kinds of explanation of this word.

यमा इव (*yamā iva*)—Born as a pair. Yama means twins, those born at one time from the womb of one and the same mother; it means twin children. Since the forty-nine Maruts who are in the seven groups were produced at one and the same time, they are referred to by the qualification "like twins". The next two words, सुसदृशः सुपेशसः (*susadṛśaḥ supeśasaḥ*), also are to be construed together with this expression. सुसदृशः सुपेशसः (*susadṛśaḥ supeśasaḥ*) means those who are each like the other, that is, all having the same kind of body, shape and age. Therefore they are compared to twins, to twin children. That twin children are alike in form, shape and so on is a matter of common experience; therefore the seer, when describing the Maruts, has given the illustration of twins.

पिशंगाश्वाः अरुणाश्वाः (*piśaṃgāśvāḥ aruṇāśvāḥ*)—The colour of the horses of the Maruts is described by these words. Earlier, that is in the 6th Ṛk of 5-56, in the context of praying to the Maruts to yoke their horses to the chariot, the colour of their horses was described by the words अरुष (*aruṣa*) and रोहित (*rohita*). That very matter

### Printed p. 733

the seer here describes again by the words पिशंगाश्वाः अरुणाश्वाः (*piśaṃgāśvāḥ aruṇāśvāḥ*).

महिना द्यौरिव उरवः (*mahinā dyauriva uravaḥ*)—महत्वेन अंतरिक्षमिव विस्तीर्णाः । (*mahatvena aṃtarikṣamiva vistīrṇāḥ |*) That the atmosphere is exceedingly vast is well known. It is explained, with an illustration, that the greatness of the Maruts also is as exceedingly vast as the atmosphere.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒रु॒द्र॒प्सा अं॑जि॒मंतः॑ सु॒दान॑वस्त्वे॒षसं॑दृशो अनव॒भ्ररा॑धसः।  
> सु॒जा॒तासो॑ ज॒नुषा॑ रु॒क्मव॑क्षसो दि॒वो अ॒र्का अ॒मृतं॒ नाम॑  
> भेजिरे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुरुद्रप्साः । अंजिमंतः । सुदानवः । त्वेषसंदृशः । अनवभ्रराधसः ।  
> सुजातासः । जनुषा । रुक्ष्मवक्षसः । दिवः । आर्काः । अमृतं । नाम । भेजिरे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुरुद्रप्साः प्रभूतोदका अंजिमंत आभरणवंतः सुदानवः शोभनदानास्त्वेषसंदृशो दीप्तरूपा अनवभ्रराधसोऽनवभ्रष्टधनाः सुजातासः शोभनजनना
> जनुषा जन्मनैवोक्तरूपा रुक्ष्मवक्षसो हारवक्षस्का अर्काः पूज्या मरुतो दिवो
> द्युलोकादागत्यामृतममरणसाधनं नामोदकं नमनहेतुकमुक्तलक्षणं हविर्वा
> भेजिरे । लब्धवंतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts have abundant water, are adorned with ornaments, are good givers, of brilliant form, and have undiminished wealth, that is, wealth that has not fallen away. They are well born, of the said form by birth itself, with necklaces on their breasts, and worshipful. Having come from the world of heaven, they have obtained the immortal, that is, the means of not dying, which is water, a name for what is the cause of bowing, as described above; or else they have obtained the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुद्रप्साः (*purudrapsāḥ*)—having abundant water
- अंजिमंतः (*aṃjimaṃtaḥ*)—having ornaments
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—excellent givers
- त्वेषसंदृशः (*tveṣasaṃdṛśaḥ*)—having a radiant form
- अनवभ्रराधसः (*anavabhrarādhasaḥ*)—having imperishable wealth
- सुजातासः (*sujātāsaḥ*)—having an excellent birth
- जनुषा (*januṣā*)—from the very time of origin
- रुक्ष्मवक्षसः (*rukṣmavakṣasaḥ*)—having necklaces on their breasts
- अर्काः (*arkāḥ*)—worshipful Maruts
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—having manifested from the world of heaven
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—deathless
- नाम (*nāma*)—fame (or water)
- भेजिरे (*bhejire*)—have taken

### Printed p. 734

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, who have abundant water, ornaments, who are excellent givers, of radiant form, of imperishable wealth, of excellent birth, who from the very time of their origin have necklaces on their breasts, and who are worshipful, having manifested from the world of heaven have obtained deathless fame.

##### English translation
Shedders of abundant showers, wearers of ornaments, munificent, of brilliant aspect, of inexhaustible wealth, well- descended by birth, wearing golden breast-plates, entitled to adoration, (coming) from heaven, accept the ambrosial oblation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अनवभ्रराधसः (*anavabhrarādhasaḥ*)—अनवभ्रष्टधनाः अथवा अभ्रष्टहविरादिधनाः । (*anavabhraṣṭadhanāḥ athavā abhraṣṭahavirādidhanāḥ |*) Since the word राधः (*rādhaḥ*) is read among the twenty-eight names of wealth beginning with मघं (*maghaṃ*) and रेक्णः (*rekṇaḥ*) (Ni. 3-9), राधः (*rādhaḥ*) means wealth. Here the word wealth means wealth such as oblations. अनवभ्र (*anavabhra*) means not fallen, not wasted. The wealth such as oblations offered to the Maruts is not wasted. Because they accept it and bestow on the sacrificers the reward that corresponds to it, the chief meaning of this word is that the wealth in the form of oblation offered to the Maruts is not wasted.

अर्का (*arkā*)—पूज्या मरुतः । (*pūjyā marutaḥ |*) It means the worshipful Maruts, the gods. The word अर्क (*arka*) has various meanings, which are to be used according to the context. The word अर्क (*arka*) has various meanings: food (Ni. 3-9), the thunderbolt weapon (Ni. 3-11), god and mantra (Ni. 5-4). On the word अर्क (*arka*) Yāska has stated four kinds of meaning in these words:

अर्कः । अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चति । अर्को मंत्रो भवति यदनेनार्चंति । अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि । अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ॥ (*arkaḥ | arko devo bhavati yadenamarcati | arko maṃtro bhavati yadanenārcaṃti | arkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtāni | arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimnā ‖*) (Ni. 5-4).

Its explanation can be given in this way.—

तावत्सर्व एवार्क इत्युच्यते यद्यस्मादेनं देवं अर्चंति (*tāvatsarva evārka ityucyate yadyasmādenaṃ devaṃ arcaṃti*) The god: अर्क (*arka*) means a deity, because it is the person or god whom the devotees use it for worshipping; that is, the object (deity) that the devotees worship is called अर्क (*arka*).

### Printed p. 735

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अर्को मंत्रो भवति । यद्यस्मादनेन मंत्रेणार्चंति (*arko maṃtro bhavati | yadyasmādanena maṃtreṇārcaṃti*) **NOTE** Arka is understood to mean a mantra also. Because those who praise worship the deity with this (with arka, that is, with the mantra), the word अर्क (*arka*) has also the name mantra.

अर्कमन्नं भवति—तद्धि अर्चति भूतानि यो हि पूज्यः तस्यान्नमपि संस्कारविशेषेण संस्कृतं पूजायां क्रियते, (*arkamannaṃ bhavati—taddhi arcati bhūtāni yo hi pūjyaḥ tasyānnamapi saṃskāraviśeṣeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pūjāyāṃ kriyate,*) **NOTE** Arka is understood to mean food also. Since food is necessary for all living beings, everyone honours and desires food. That is, because everyone honours it with love and regard and wishes for it, the word अर्क (*arka*) is understood to mean food also.

अर्क वृक्षो भवति य एष प्रसिद्धः । संवृत्तः हि संगतः संव्याप्तः कटुकिम्ना कटुकभावेन (*arka vṛkṣo bhavati ya eṣa prasiddhaḥ | saṃvṛttaḥ hi saṃgataḥ saṃvyāptaḥ kaṭukimnā kaṭukabhāvena*) **NOTE** Further, the name of a special tree is well known for the word अर्क (*arka*). The arka tree is called in the Karṇāṭaka language ekkadagiḍa. Because its samits (twigs) are used in homas and because it is customary to use it in medicines and the like, the arka tree is a thing known to everyone. Because it is bitter it is called कटुकिम्ना (*kaṭukimnā*). In the present Ṛk the commentator has explained the word अर्क (*arka*) as meaning अर्चनीयाः (*arcanīyāḥ*), that is, those who are worthy of worship.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, on your shoulders special weapons, the spears, are placed, that is, rest; the word "placed", which is to be mentioned later, must be changed in form to fit, and the word "upon" only repeats the sense of the locative. Likewise in your arms there is a force that overpowers enemies; the word for vigour is the name of the eighth bodily element, and strength in that form is placed there. On your heads golden things, turbans of silk and the like, are placed. In your chariots weapons, instruments of battle, are placed. Your splendour, your lustre, is spread over your bodies, that is, rests upon them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- अंगयोरधि (*aṃgayoradhi*)—upon the shoulders
- ऋष्टयः (*ṛṣṭayaḥ*)—spears (shine)
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- बाह्वोः (*bāhvoḥ*)—in the arms
- सहः (*sahaḥ*)—able to face the enemy
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—vigour
- बलं (*balaṃ*)—and strength
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—are placed
- शीर्षस्सु (*śīrṣassu*)—on your heads
- नृम्मा (*nṛmmā*)—attractive turbans and the like shine
- वः रथेषु (*vaḥ ratheṣu*)—in your chariots
- आयुधा (*āyudhā*)—weapons
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- तनूषु अधि (*tanūṣu adhi*)—also on the limbs of the body
- श्रीः (*śrīḥ*)—splendour
- पिपिशे (*pipiśe*)—pervades and shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, spears shine upon your shoulders. In your arms the vigour and strength that can face the enemy are placed. Attractive turbans and the like shine on your heads. In your chariots there are weapons, and on all your limbs splendour pervades and shines.

##### English translation
Lances rest, Maruts, upon your shoulders; strength (of) foe-destroy ing powor is seated in your arms; golden (tiaras) are on your heads weapons are placed in your chariots, all glory is assembled in your limbs.**NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

the description is, with a little more or less, the same as that of the present Ṛk.
