##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो नोऽस्मभ्यं गोमद्बहुभिर्गोभिरुपेतमश्वानद्बहुभिरश्चैरुपेतं रथवद्रथोपेतं सुवीरं सुष्टु पुत्रोपेतं चंद्रवद्धिरण्योपेतं राधोऽन्नं
> दद । ददत । व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं । अथवा लोडर्थस्य लिटो मध्यमबहुवचनं ॥ हे
> रुद्रियासो रुद्रपुत्रा मरुतो नोऽस्मदीयां प्रशस्तिं । समृद्धिमित्यर्थः । तां
> कृणुत । कुरुत। वो युष्माकं स्वभूतमवसोऽवो रक्षणं दैव्यस्य दैव्यं देवार्हं
> भक्षीय । भजेय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, give us wealth, food, accompanied by cattle, that is, furnished with many cows, with horses, that is, furnished with many horses, with chariots, with good sons, that is, furnished with excellent sons, and with gold. The verb is given in the singular by a change of number; or else it is the perfect in the sense of the imperative, second person plural. O sons of Rudra, Maruts, make for us praise, that is, prosperity. May I partake of your own protection, which is divine, that is, fit for gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- गोमत् (*gomat*)—accompanied by cows
- अश्वावत् (*aśvāvat*)—distinguished by horses
- रथवत् (*rathavat*)—furnished with chariots
- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*)—filled with excellent sons and the like
- चंद्रवत् (*caṃdravat*)—possessed of gold
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—wealth
- दद (*dada*)—give
- रुद्रियासः (*rudriyāsaḥ*)—O Maruts, sons of Rudra
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- प्रशस्तिं (*praśastiṃ*)—prosperity of a special kind
- कृणुत (*kṛṇuta*)—produce
- नः (*naḥ*)—your**NOTE**
- दैव्यस्य (*daivyasya*)—worshipful
- अवसः (*avasaḥ*)—protection
- भक्षीय (*bhakṣīya*)—grant that we may enjoy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, give us wealth that is accompanied by cows, distinguished by horses, furnished with chariots, filled with excellent sons and the like, and rich in gold. O Maruts, sons of Rudra, create for us prosperity of a special kind. Grant that we may always enjoy your worshipful protection.

### Printed p. 738

##### English translation
Maruts, bestow upon us affluence, comprehending cattle,horses, cars, treasure, and male descendants ; sons of Rudra, grant us distinction : may I ever enjoy your divine protection.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, which is the conclusion of the sūkta, and in the next Ṛk also, the seer Śyāvāśva has prayed to the Maruts to give wealth in the form of cows and the like.

गोमत् अश्वावत्, रथवत्, सुवीरं चंद्रवत् राधः (*gomat aśvāvat, rathavat, suvīraṃ caṃdravat rādhaḥ*)—When the seer Śyāvāśva prays to the Maruts to give him the things he needs, he has prayed that they give राधः (*rādhaḥ*), wealth or riches. In what form that wealth should be, he has explained in the same place. He has asked that they give cows, horses, chariots, good sons and wealth in the form of gold, all of these. Wealth does not mean only property. That animal wealth such as cows and horses has been counted as wealth from ancient times is the established custom. The custom of calling wealth any thing that people need most urgently has come down from earlier times. In the Ṛgveda also it is just so.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O leaders, Maruts, make us happy; or else be happy for our good. O you of abundant wealth, immortal, that is, of a nature not subject to death, knowers of water or of sacrifice, that is, doers of it.**NOTE** Renowned for truth, that is, famed for the truth of the fruit of what you do; wise; ever young; of abundant praises; and, being served with oblations in great measure, or sprinkling water: such as you are, be gracious to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तुवीमघासः (*tuvīmaghāsaḥ*)—possessing abundant wealth
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—free from death
- ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*)—knowing the truth
- सत्यश्रुतः (*satyaśrutaḥ*)—having true fame
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the wise
- युवानः (*yuvānaḥ*)—ever young
- बृहद्दिरयः (*bṛhaddirayaḥ*)—worthy of abundant praises
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—exceedingly
- उक्षमाणाः (*ukṣamāṇāḥ*)—those to whom oblations are offered
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—leaders, being such
- हये मरुतः (*haye marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळत (*mṛḷata*)—make happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, who possess abundant wealth, who are free from death, who know the truth, who have true fame, who are wise, ever young, worthy of abundant praises, to whom oblations are offered in great measure, and who are leaders: make us happy.

##### English translation
Ho, Maruts, leaders (of rites), be propitious to us, you who are infinitely opulent, immortal, shedders of rain, renowned for truth, wise, young, greatly glorified and worshipped with copious oblations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हये (*haye*)—The word हये (*haye*) is used in the vocative sense like the word हे (*he*). Therefore here हये मरुतः (*haye marutaḥ*) means हे मरुतः (*he marutaḥ*), that is, O Maruts. The word हये (*haye*) occurs in

हये देवा यूयमिदापयः स्थ ते मृळत नाधमानाय मह्यं । (*haye devā yūyamidāpayaḥ stha te mṛḷata nādhamānāya mahyaṃ |*) (Mṛ. Saṃ. 2-29-4)**NOTE**

### Printed p. 740

हये नरो मरुतो मृळता नस्तु वीमघासो अमृता ऋतज्ञाः । (*haye naro maruto mṛḷatā nastu vīmaghāso amṛtā ṛtajñāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5 57-8)**NOTE**

हये जाये मनसा तिष्ठ घोरे वचांसि मिश्रा कृणवावहै नु । (*haye jāye manasā tiṣṭha ghore vacāṃsi miśrā kṛṇavāvahai nu |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-1)

and in these three Ṛks only. This word is not used anywhere else in the Ṛgveda. In all three places it is used in the vocative sense of हे (*he*).

## Sūkta 58 (Maṇḍala 5)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तमु नूनमित्यष्टर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं श्यावाश्वस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं मारुतं।
> तम्मित्यनुक्रमणिका । विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning तमु नूनं (*tamu nūnaṃ*) is the second hymn, of eight Ṛks; its seer is Śyāvāśva, its deity the Maruts, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā begins तम्मित्यनुक्रमणिका (*tammityanukramaṇikā*). The application is by indication (liṅga).

Translation: This hymn beginning तमु नूनं (*tamu nūnaṃ*) is the second hymn in the fifth Anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. The seer of this hymn is Śyāvāśva; the deity is the Maruts; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said to begin तमु (*tamu*). The application is by indication (liṅga).

- Sūkta: 58
- Maṇḍala 5; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 58
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 3; Varga 23
- Number of Ṛks in the Sūkta: 8
- Ṛṣi: Śyāvāśva Ātreya
- Devatā: Maruts
- Chandas: Triṣṭubh

> नव्यसीनां ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सायणभाष्यं ॥ ४
> तमु तमेव पूर्वं स्तुतमेव मारुतं मरुतां संबंधिनं तं गणं तविषीमंतं दीप्तिमंतं नूनमद्य स्तुषे । कीदृशां मरुतां । नव्यसीनां ॥ लिंगव्यत्ययः ॥
> नवतराणां स्तुत्यानां वा । एषां मारुतं गणं । गणावयवभूता मरुतः । कीदृशा
> इत्युच्यते । ये मरुत आश्वश्वाः शीघ्रगाम्यश्चोपेता अमवत् बलवंतो यथा
> भवंति तथा वहंते गच्छंति । उतापि चेशिरे ईश्वरा भवंत्यमृतस्योदकस्य स्वराजः
> स्वायत्तदीप्तयः स्वयमेव राजमानाः तेषां गणं स्तुषे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Him": that very Mārut host which was praised before, belonging to the Maruts, radiant, I praise today. Of what Maruts? Of the more praiseworthy ones; he notes a change of gender, and says the word means newer or worthy of praise. Of these Maruts, the host: the Maruts are the members that make up the host. What kind are they? Those Maruts who, furnished with swift horses, move along in such a way that they are strong. And they are also lords of the immortal, that is, of water, self-radiant, shining of themselves. I praise the host of those.

- तविषीमंतं (*taviṣīmaṃtaṃ*)—luminous
- तमु (*tamu*)—and well known
- गणं (*gaṇaṃ*)—the host
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—now
- स्तुषे (*stuṣe*)—I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those Maruts who move about with swift horses and with exceeding strength, and who, self-dependent and radiant, are lords of water: of such worshipful Maruts I now praise the luminous and well-known host.

##### English translation
I praise to-day that brilliant company of the adorable Maruts, lords of swift horses, who pass along in strength, who, self-radiant, preside over the ambrosial rain.

### Printed p. 742

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

उ (*u*)—Concerning the particle उ (*u*) Yāska has spoken thus:

अथाप्युकार एतस्मिन्नेवार्थ उत्तरेण मृषेमे वदंति सत्यमु ते (मे) वदंतीति । अथापि पदपूरण इदमु तदु ॥ (*athāpyukāra etasminnevārtha uttareṇa mṛṣeme vadaṃti satyamu te (me) vadaṃtīti | athāpi padapūraṇa idamu tadu ‖*) (Ni. 1-5)

The particle उ (*u*) is used in the sense of restraint, that is, in a context that indicates mutual opposition. For example, in the sentence मृषेमे वदंति सत्यमु ते (*mṛṣeme vadaṃti satyamu te*), "These speak falsehood; those speak only truth", there are two matters indicating mutual opposition, speaking falsehood and speaking truth. The use of the word उ (*u*) is in a context in which these two are said in comparison with each other. Besides this, the word उ (*u*) is used also for completing a sentence, or a foot of a metre, by adding a syllable that is lacking. In such a context this word has only the sense of "this" or "that", and no other definite meaning. In the sentence तदु प्रयक्षतममस्य कर्म (*tadu prayakṣatamamasya karma*), "that very act of Indra, worthy of worship or praise", when the words that are joined indicate "that very act" or "that itself", the word उ (*u*) merges into the sense of the word for "that"; it has no separate meaning. Therefore the chief intention of the Nirukta statement is that in such a context the word is used for filling out the word. On the use of the word उ (*u*) for filling out the word, the author of the Nirukta has stated another Nirukta passage:

ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रंथेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छंति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्विति । (*ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu graṃtheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchaṃti padapūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidviti |*) (Ni. 1-9)**NOTE**

That is, the particles कं (*kaṃ*), ईं (*īṃ*), इत् (*it*) and उ (*u*) are used in prose works not bound by metre for completing a sentence, and in metres of a fixed number of syllables for completing a foot. It is explained that these need not have a separate definite meaning; thus the use of these words is described.

नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—Yāska:

विचिकित्सार्थीयो भाषायामुभयमन्वध्यायं विचिकित्सार्थीयश्च पदपूरणश्च । (*vicikitsārthīyo bhāṣāyāmubhayamanvadhyāyaṃ vicikitsārthīyaśca padapūraṇaśca |*) (Ni. 1-5)**NOTE**

The word नूनं (*nūnaṃ*) is used in the sense of deliberation in places other than the Vedic verses also. In the Vedic metre he has described it as used both in the sense of deliberation and in the sense of filling out the word.

### Printed p. 743

Durgācārya has explained: विवेकपूर्वको अवधारणाभिप्रायः (*vivekapūrvako avadhāraṇābhiprāyaḥ*). The determining of a matter by discernment, in situations where doubt has arisen, is called deliberation. Sāyaṇa has supported that in the Ṛk न नूनमस्ति (*na nūnamasti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-170-1), which is given as an example for this word, it is used in the sense of deliberation and also in the sense of determination.

> कंपयितृकर्माणं मायिनं प्रज्ञावंतं दातिवारं दत्तधनं हे विप्र होतर्वंदस्व ।
> स्तुहीति संबंधः । हे मरुतो मयोभुवः सुखस्य भावयितारो महित्वा महत्वेनामिता अपरिच्छिन्नाः । तान् तुविराधसः प्रभूतधनान् नृन् नेत्यन् वंदस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The radiant host of the Maruts, the strong one, that has bracelets on its hands, whose work is shaking, that is intelligent, whose given wealth is bestowed: O wise priest, the hotṛ, praise it; this is the connection. O Maruts, causers of happiness, unbounded, that is, unlimited, in greatness: praise them, the leaders of abundant wealth.

- ये (*ye*)—those Maruts who
- मयोभुवः (*mayobhuvaḥ*)—makers of happiness

O wise hotṛ, praise the host of the Maruts, which is radiant, powerful, has hands adorned with bracelets, has as its chief activity the making of trees and the like tremble, is endowed with wisdom, and is of a nature to give wealth in gift. Praise that host of the Maruts, who are makers of happiness and of unmeasured nature by their greatness, who are leaders and possess abundant wealth.

##### English translation
Adore, priest, the resplendent and powerful company, whose arms (are decorated) with bracelets, whose function is the agitation (of the trees), who are wise and by whom wealth is eonferred: they who are bestowers of felicity, whose greatness is unbounded: glorify the opulent leaders (of rites)**NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गणं (*gaṇaṃ*)—मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*). In contexts in which the Maruts are indicated, it is the custom to denote the Maruts, who are accompanied by seven groups, by मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*) and मारुतं शर्धः (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ*). सप्तगणा वै मरुतः (*saptagaṇā vai marutaḥ*): the groups of the Maruts are seven. In each group there are seven Maruts. In all there are forty-nine deities in the seven groups. All of them together are called by the words मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*), मारुतं शर्धः (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ*) or मरुतः (*marutaḥ*). Although in the present Ṛk there is only the word गणं (*gaṇaṃ*), yet because in the previous Ṛk it is मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*), it should be understood that here too it is indicated as मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*). In the first half of this Ṛk the Maruts are praised collectively by the word गणं (*gaṇaṃ*). In the second half they are praised, as मरुतः (*marutaḥ*), by words ending in the accusative plural, such as नैन् (*nain*). Although there is a change of number, both sentences have the same meaning.

अमिताः (*amitāḥ*)—अपरिच्छिन्नाः । (*aparicchinnāḥ |*) Those who are free from limitation. The intention is that these Maruts never leave one another but always remain together; or, when the words महित्वा अमिताः (*mahitvā amitāḥ*) are construed together, those who excel in greatness, that is, without the difference that one is greater and another smaller in greatness, all are of one and the same, equal kind of greatness.

विप्र (*vipra*)—होतः । (*hotaḥ |*) Here the word विप्र (*vipra*) denotes the hotṛ in the sense of wise. The sacrificer who performs the yajña addresses the hotṛ, who is the chief among the priests, by the word विप्र (*vipra*) and directs him to praise the Maruts, who are endowed with glory.

### Printed p. 745

मायिनं (*māyinaṃ*)—Although the word from which this is formed has several meanings, such as wisdom and stratagem, here it is used in the sense of wisdom. It means possessing wisdom, of much intellect.

धुनिव्रतं (*dhunivrataṃ*)—कंपयितृकर्माणं । (*kaṃpayitṛkarmāṇaṃ |*) The second member of the compound is read among the names of action. From the root धूज् कंपने (*dhūj kaṃpane*) the first member is formed, meaning to shake, to cause to tremble. Because the Maruts, blowing with very great violence as storms, are of a nature to make trees and the like tremble (sway), they are described by this word.

For the word नैन् (*nain*) Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning, नेत्यन् मनुष्यान्यस्मान् मरुतो (*netyan manuṣyānyasmān maruto*)**NOTE**: us, who are leaders, or the Maruts. The qualification मयोभुवः (*mayobhuvaḥ*), "causers of happiness", fits both meanings. If the seer has said it with reference to himself and his family, the meaning is that by the grace of the Maruts powerful happiness was obtained by them. Or, if it is a qualification of मरुतः (*marutaḥ*), it amounts to a description of the natural power of the Maruts. The natural and collective power of the Maruts, and the heroic deeds accomplished by that power, are indicated by the many qualifications such as अमिता महित्वा (*amitā mahitvā*).

सप्त सप्त हि मरुतो गणस्तस्मान्मारुतः सप्तकपालः। (*sapta sapta hi maruto gaṇastasmānmārutaḥ saptakapālaḥ|*) (Śa. Brā. 2-5-1-13)

सप्त सप्त हि मारुतो गणः सर्वमेवैतेन रथं प्रीणाति । (*sapta sapta hi māruto gaṇaḥ sarvamevaitena rathaṃ prīṇāti |*) (Śa. Brā. 5-4-3-17) (Śa. Brā. 5-4-3-17)

From such sentences it is understood that the Maruts always remain in groups, and that in such a group a kind of vitality and strength is natural to them. Therefore the qualification अमिता (*amitā*) is appropriate in the present Ṛk.

नैन् (*nain*) has been explained also as the Maruts, who are leaders and of the nature of subjects. The Maruts are well known as the subjects of the gods.

स एतामैंद्रीं मरुत्वतीमज्ञ पत् । क्षत्रं ना इंद्रो विशो मरुतः क्षत्रं वै विशो निषेद्धा ॥ (*sa etāmaiṃdrīṃ marutvatīmajña pat | kṣatraṃ nā iṃdro viśo marutaḥ kṣatraṃ vai viśo niṣeddhā ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 2-5-2-27)

This meaning is stated in such sentences. Therefore there is propriety in giving to the word नृन् (*nṛn*) also the other meaning, मरुतः (*marutaḥ*). It can be noticed that the word नरः (*naraḥ*) is used as a qualification of the Maruts in many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself. For example,

### Printed p. 746

चित्रैरंजिभिर्वपुषे व्यंजते वक्षःसु रुक्मा अधि येतिरे शुभे । अंसेष्वेषां नि मिमृक्षुर्ऋष्टयः साकं जज्जिरे स्वधया दिवो नरः । (*citrairaṃjibhirvapuṣe vyaṃjate vakṣaḥsu rukmā adhi yetire śubhe | aṃseṣveṣāṃ ni mimṛkṣurṛṣṭayaḥ sākaṃ jajjire svadhayā divo naraḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-4)

विश्ववेदसो रयिभिः समोकसः संमिश्ला सस्तविषीभिर्विरप्यनः । आस्तार इषुं दधिरे गभस्त्योरनंतशुष्मा वृषखादयो नरः ॥ (*viśvavedaso rayibhiḥ samokasaḥ saṃmiślā sastaviṣībhirvirapyanaḥ | āstāra iṣuṃ dadhire gabhastyoranaṃtaśuṣmā vṛṣakhādayo naraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-10)

In many such Ṛks the word नरः (*naraḥ*) shows the nature of the Maruts; in the same way in the present Ṛk also the word नन् (*nan*) may have the meaning "the Maruts".

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ वो॑ यंतूदवा॒हासो॑ अ॒द्य वृ॒ष्टिं ये विश्वे॑ म॒रुतो॑  ॒॑
> जुनंति ।  
> अ॒यं यो अ॒ग्निर्म॑रुतः॒ समि॑द्ध ए॒तं जु॑षध्वं कवयो  
> युवानः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । वः । यंतु । उदऽवाहासः । अव्य । वृष्टिं । ये । विश्वे । मरुतः । जुनंति ।  
> अयं । यः । अग्निः । मरुतः । संइद्धः । एतं । जुषध्वं । कवयः । युवानः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये विश्वे व्याप्ता मरुतो वृष्टिं जुनंति प्रेरयंति त उदवाहास उदकस्य
> वोढारो मरुतोऽद्येदानीं वो युष्माना यंतु आगच्छंतु हे ऋत्विग्यजमानाः । अथ प्रत्यक्षवादः । हे मरुतो यः प्रसिद्धोऽयमग्निः समिद्धः सम्यक्
> दीपित एतमग्निं जुषध्वं सेवध्वं हे कवयो मेधाविनो हे युवानो नित्यतरुणाः सर्वत्र व्याप्ता ना ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those all-pervading Maruts who impel rain, who are the carriers of water, may they come to you today, O priests and sacrificers. Now he turns to direct address: O Maruts, this well-known Agni is kindled, that is, well lit; enjoy this Agni, serve it, O wise ones, O ever-young ones, who are pervading everywhere.

### Printed p. 747

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—who
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all-pervading
- वृष्टिं (*vṛṣṭiṃ*)—rain
- जुनंति (*junaṃti*)—who urge on and pour down (the rain), such
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- उदवाहासः (*udavāhāsaḥ*)—bearing waters
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to your sacrifice
- आ यंतु (*ā yaṃtu*)—may they graciously come
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—wise
- युवानः (*yuvānaḥ*)—ever-young
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- आयं. अग्निः (*āyaṃ. agniḥ*)—this Agni
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—is kindled
- एतं (*etaṃ*)—this (Agni), such
- जुषध्वं (*juṣadhvaṃ*)—enjoy, serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests and sacrificers, may those Maruts who, being all-pervading, urge on and pour down the rain, come to your sacrifice now, bearing waters. O Maruts, wise and ever young, enjoy this Agni which is blazing here.

##### English translation
May the universal Maruts, who urge on the rain, come to you to-day laden with water: Maruts who are wise and young, be pleased by this fire which is kindled for you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अद्य—इदानीं । अस्मिन् यज्ञे । (*adya—idānīṃ | asmin yajñe |*) "Now", or at the time of this sacrifice that we are performing: that is, an invitation is stated here, "come to this sacrifice that we are performing and enjoy Agni." In this sacrifice of ours Agni is kindled and shining. A prayer is stated that you, the Marut deities, should come through such an Agni to the sacrificial ground to receive the oblations and the rest.

In the first half of this Ṛk the Marut deities are praised with a sentence of the indirect kind, and in the second half with a sentence of the direct kind. Yāska has explained what परोक्षकृत, प्रत्यक्षकृत (*parokṣakṛta, pratyakṣakṛta*) mean, in the following way. Yāska, the great sage and author of the Nirukta, has spoken thus on the interpretation of the Vedic mantras.

तद्यानि नामानि प्राधान्यस्तु तीनां देवतानां तद्दैवतमित्याचक्षते ॥ यत्काम ऋषियस्क्यां देवतायावार्थपत्यमिच्छन्सुतिं प्रयुं (*tadyāni nāmāni prādhānyastu tīnāṃ devatānāṃ taddaivatamityācakṣate ‖ yatkāma ṛṣiyaskyāṃ devatāyāvārthapatyamicchansutiṃ prayuṃ*)

### Printed p. 748

क्ते तद्दैवतः स मंत्रो भवति ॥ (*kte taddaivataḥ sa maṃtro bhavati ‖*) तास्त्रिविधा ऋचः परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृता आध्यात्मिकाश्च । तत्र परोक्षकृताः सर्वाभिर्नामविभक्तिभिर्युज्यंतॆ, प्रथमपुरुषैश्चाख्यातस्य ॥ अथ प्रत्यक्षकृता मध्यमपुरुषोपयोगास्त्वमिति चैतेन सर्वनाम्ना ॥ अथाध्यात्मिक्य उत्त मपुरुषयोगा अहमिति चैतेन सर्वनाम्ना॥ परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृताश्च मंत्रा भूयिष्ठा अल्पश आध्यात्मिकाः ॥ (*tāstrividhā ṛcaḥ parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtā ādhyātmikāśca | tatra parokṣakṛtāḥ sarvābhirnāmavibhaktibhiryujyaṃtè, prathamapuruṣaiścākhyātasya ‖ atha pratyakṣakṛtā madhyamapuruṣopayogāstvamiti caitena sarvanāmnā ‖ athādhyātmikya utta mapuruṣayogā ahamiti caitena sarvanāmnā‖ parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtāśca maṃtrā bhūyiṣṭhā alpaśa ādhyātmikāḥ ‖*) (Nirukta, the section on deities, chapter 7, sections 1-3)

That is, among mantras there are many kinds: the mantra of a deity, the mantra of praise, the mantra of blessing, oath, curse, exposition of some matter, lament, censure, eulogy, दानस्तुति (*dānastuti*) and so on. A deity-mantra is one that describes the greatness of the deities; praise means a hymn, a mantra containing prayers; blessing is a mantra that wishes good; an oath is a vow; a curse is an evil wish; the exposition of some matter is the explanation of a subject or principle; lament is grief; censure is blame; eulogy is praise.

Among the many kinds mentioned above, the Ṛks that are deity-mantras are of three kinds: indirect, direct and personal. The indirect kind: since the deity who is praised is not present before the speaker, the mantras that in praising that deity use third-person nouns and verbs (Third person both in subject and predicate). The direct kind: mantras in which the deity who is praised is imagined as actually present in front, and is addressed and praised with second-person words (Second person) such as "thou" and "thy". The personal kind: mantras that praise by using the first person (First person). Of these three kinds, the two kinds, indirect and direct, are the more numerous, and the personal mantras are only few.

कवयः:—क्रांतदर्शिनः मेधाविनो ना (*kavayaḥ:—krāṃtadarśinaḥ medhāvino nā*) Thus Sāyaṇa has given the meaning of this word. In some other places Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning of this word in two ways: first, following the Veda sentence ये वा अनूचानास्ते कवयः (*ye vā anūcānāste kavayaḥ*), as scholars who have studied the Veda together with its limbs; second, following the Nirukta sentence कविः, मनीषी (*kaviḥ, manīṣī*) (Ni. 3-15), as a wise man. The author of the Nirukta says:

मेधावी कविः क्रांतदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्ना (*medhāvī kaviḥ krāṃtadarśano bhavati kavaternā*) (2 12-13)**NOTE**

### Printed p. 749

Thus the author of the Nirukta has stated the derivation of the word kavi. Derived from the root क्रम् (*kram*) it can mean one possessed of far-reaching vision; or derived from the root कम् (*kam*) it can mean the praiser who is to praise: so the derivation of the Nirukta author explains. What is the nature of a kavi? What is his power? In what nature and power is the word kavi used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā? It is necessary to understand this.

It may be said that the word kavi is useful for conveying the same distinctive nature that the words ऋषि, सुमेध, धीर, रेभ (*ṛṣi, sumedha, dhīra, rebha*) show. One who has the extraordinary and supernatural power of knowing all the doings of past, future and present times is the wise one; he is the seer, and he is the kavi. One who has this power is also fit for the creation of poetry in the form of hymns. Therefore the praiser also has names such as kavi and रेभ (*rebha*). In worldly literature and in treatises on poetics the words kavi and poem likewise stand for a name indicating an extraordinary power of this kind, but it is to be understood, according to the context, that the explanation there differs somewhat from this one. To make known the true nature of the kavi, the author of the Nirukta quotes the Ṛk

विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । नि नाकमख्यत्सविता वरेण्योऽनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति ॥ (*viśvā rūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviḥ prāsāvīdbhadraṃ dvipade catuṣpade | ni nākamakhyatsavitā vareṇyo 'nu prayāṇamuṣaso vi rājati ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-8,2)**NOTE**

and explains what nature of Savitṛ the word kavi, which is here an epithet of Savitṛ, shows. It is understood that this epithet belongs to Savitṛ because he brings to light all the forms of the world; that is, he has the power by his own might to light up those aspects that lie hidden and are not visible to the eye of the world, and to make them fall within the sight of the world. In this same sense the name kavi is well known also for the praiser, the one who praises. This idea is indicated in the Ṛk of the Ṛk-saṃhitā,

ब्रह्मा कृणोति वरुणो गातुविदं तमीमहे । व्यूर्णोति हृदा मतिं नव्यो जायतामृतं वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥ (*brahmā kṛṇoti varuṇo gātuvidaṃ tamīmahe | vyūrṇoti hṛdā matiṃ navyo jāyatāmṛtaṃ vittaṃ me asya rodasī ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-15)

and likewise in other Ṛks. In this quoted Ṛk Sāyaṇa has explained the word व्यूर्णोति (*vyūrṇoti*) as उच्चारयति, प्रकाशयति (*uccārayati, prakāśayati*). The root ऊर्णु (*ūrṇu*), meaning to cover or to veil, becomes ऊर्णोति (*ūrṇoti*). Here, joined with the prefix vi, it gives the meaning of removal of covering, that is, of taking away the veil,

### Printed p. 750

and the purport is: to make manifest. It is understood from this that the power to create, in the form of making manifest a thought hidden in the mind, and the power to reveal what is hidden by bringing it to light, are the special quality of the kavi or praiser. Therefore the word kavi is an epithet that conveys to both Savitṛ and the praiser the quality they have in common. Explaining this same characteristic and the work of a kavi, the Ṛk-saṃhitā says:

समानं नीळं वृषणो वसानाः सं जग्मिरे महिषा अर्वतीभिः । ऋतस्य पदं कवयो नि पांति गुहा नामानि दधिरे पराणि । (*samānaṃ nīḷaṃ vṛṣaṇo vasānāḥ saṃ jagmire mahiṣā arvatībhiḥ | ṛtasya padaṃ kavayo ni pāṃti guhā nāmāni dadhire parāṇi |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-5-2)

बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं यत्प्रैरत नामधेयं दधानाः । यदेषां श्रेष्ठं यदरिप्रमासीत्प्रेणा तदेषां निहितं गुहाविः ॥ (*bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ yatprairata nāmadheyaṃ dadhānāḥ | yadeṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yadaripramāsītpreṇā tadeṣāṃ nihitaṃ guhāviḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-1)

This idea is expressed in all such Ṛks. It is described that the kavis, entering the path of the cosmic order, have borne in the most hidden heart the most excellent secret names, and make them manifest so that the world may know. The vision of this kavi too is possible only through the means that has the form of making manifest.

यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन् तामन्वनिंदन्नृषिसु प्रविष्टां । तामाभृत्या व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा तां सप्त रेभा अभि सं नवंते ॥ (*yajñena vācaḥ padavīyamāyan tāmanvaniṃdannṛṣisu praviṣṭāṃ | tāmābhṛtyā vyadadhuḥ purutrā tāṃ sapta rebhā abhi saṃ navaṃte ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-3)

The kavis obtained, by the means that has the form of sacrifice, speech that lay dormant in the seers who see beyond the senses. Afterwards, for the benefit of the people of the world, they taught it to them also. The metres such as the Gāyatrī serve this speech, which is of the nature of the principle of the universe. Thus, in some places the identity, and in others the relation of cause and effect, is shown between creation, which has the form of the manifestation of speech, and the rite, which has the form of sacrifice. The same idea is stated in this way in the Brāhmaṇas, the Śatapatha and others:

आयुरेतज्योतिः प्रविशति य एतमनु ना ब्रूते भक्षयति वा तस्य व्रतचर्या या सृष्टौ ॥ (*āyuretajyotiḥ praviśati ya etamanu nā brūte bhakṣayati vā tasya vratacaryā yā sṛṣṭau ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 14-1-2-26)

Here the identity of the rite accompanied by the utterance of mantras with new creation is stated. In the present Ṛk the word is an epithet that shows the extraordinary quality of the Marut deities, who are endowed with knowledge of matters beyond the senses and are all-knowing. Since this epithet is used in many places, it should be interpreted according to each context.

### Printed p. 751

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यू॒यं राजा॑न॒मिर्यं॒ जना॑य विभ्वत॒ष्टं ज॑नयथा  
> यजत्राः ।  
> यु॒ष्मदे॑ति मुष्टि॒हा बा॒हुजू॑तो यु॒ष्मत्सद॑श्चो मरुतःसु॒वीरः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यूयं । राजानं । इर्यं । जनाय । विभ्वतष्टं । जनयथ । यजत्राः ।  
> युष्मत् । एति । मुष्टिहा । बाहुजूतः । युष्मत् । सत्अश्वः । मरुतः ।  
> सुवीरः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यूयं जनाय यजमानाय राजानं स्वामिनं राजमानं
> वेर्यं शत्रूणां प्रेरकं च्यावयितारं विभ्वतष्टं। विभ्वा नाम ऋभूणां मध्यमः।
> स कुशली । तेन निर्मितं । अत्यंतरूपवंतमित्यर्थः । तादृशं पुत्रं जनयथ ।
> उत्पादयथ हे यजत्रा यष्टव्याः । हे मरुतो युष्मद्युष्मत्त एति गच्छति पुत्रः ।
> कीदृशः । मुष्टिहा । मुष्टिशब्दो बाहूपलक्षकः । स्वभुजबलेनैव हंता शत्रूणां ।
> तदेवोच्यते । बाहुजूतः । बाहुः प्रेरकः शत्रूणां यस्य तादृशः पुत्र एति । तथा
> युष्मद्युष्मत्तः सदश्वो विद्यमानाश्वः । बह्वश्व इत्यर्थः । सुवीरः शोभनवीय्यः
> पुत्र एति । जायत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, you beget for the sacrificer a son who is a ruler, that is, a lord, shining; an urger of enemies, one who makes them fall away; and विभ्वतष्टं (*vibhvataṣṭaṃ*). Vibhvan is the middle one of the Ṛbhus; he is skilled, and the son made by him is exceedingly handsome. O worshipful ones, you bring forth, that is, produce, such a son. O Maruts, from you there comes a son. What kind of son? मुष्टिहा (*muṣṭihā*): the word "fist" stands for the arm; he is the slayer of enemies by the strength of his own arms. The same is said again: बाहुजूतः (*bāhujūtaḥ*), one whose arm is the impeller of enemies; such a son comes. Likewise, from you comes a son who has good horses, that is, an existing horse or many horses, and who is of excellent valour. That is, such a son is born.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)—O Maruts, worthy of worship
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- जनाय (*janāya*)—to the sacrificer
- राजानं (*rājānaṃ*)—shining
- इर्यं (*iryaṃ*)—destroyer of enemies
- विभ्वतष्टं (*vibhvataṣṭaṃ*)—made by Vibhvan, such a son
- जनयथ (*janayatha*)—you cause to be born
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- युष्मत् (*yuṣmat*)—from you
- मुष्टिहा (*muṣṭihā*)—one who destroys enemies with blows of the fist
- बाहुजूतः (*bāhujūtaḥ*)—one who conquers enemies with the strength of his arms, such a son
- एति (*eti*)—is born
- युष्मत् (*yuṣmat*)—by your favour alone
- सदश्वः (*sadaśvaḥ*)—one who has an excellent horse
- सुवीरः (*suvīraḥ*)—one who has excellent valour, such a son is born

### Printed p. 752

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O worshipful Maruts, you cause to be born to the sacrificer a son who is shining, a destroyer of enemies, and made by Vibhvan. O Maruts, by your favour a son is born who destroys enemies by the strength of his fist, wins victory by the strength of his arms, and has an excellent horse and excellent valour.

##### English translation
Adorable Maruts, you cause (a son) to be born to the man (who worships you), a ruler, an over-comer of foes, and modelled by Vibhwan: from you, Maruts comes a valiant descendant, strong-fisted, mighty-armed; from you (he acquires) an excellent steed.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विभ्वतष्टं—विश्वानाम ऋभूणां मध्यमः । स कुशली । तेन निर्मितं । अत्यंतरूपवंतमित्यर्थः। (*vibhvataṣṭaṃ—viśvānāma ṛbhūṇāṃ madhyamaḥ | sa kuśalī | tena nirmitaṃ | atyaṃtarūpavaṃtamityarthaḥ|*) In former times the sage Aṅgiras had a son named Nītimañjarī. In his line the sage Sudhanvan had three sons, Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja. By good works such as the performance of righteous rites and the helping of the gods, they obtained the birth of gods, or became gods, so it is traditionally held. It is the custom to call all three sons of Sudhanvan, Ṛbhu and the others, together by the name of the eldest son, the Ṛbhus. The Vibhu named in the present Ṛk is neither the eldest nor the youngest of these Ṛbhus, but the middle one. Since he is very skilled in the making of things, the son made, or given, by him is renowned as exceedingly handsome. By the use of the word विभ्वतष्टं (*vibhvataṣṭaṃ*) here, the Maruts are prayed to bring forth such a son.

मुष्टिहा, बाहुजूतः—मुष्टिशब्दो बाहूपलक्षकः ॥ स्वभुजबलेनैव हंता शत्रूणां । तदेवोच्यते । बाहुजूतः बाहुः प्रेरकः शत्रूणां यस्य तादृशः पुत्र इति । (*muṣṭihā, bāhujūtaḥ—muṣṭiśabdo bāhūpalakṣakaḥ ‖ svabhujabalenaiva haṃtā śatrūṇāṃ | tadevocyate | bāhujūtaḥ bāhuḥ prerakaḥ śatrūṇāṃ yasya tādṛśaḥ putra iti |*) The word "fist" also means the arm; or else, "fist" is the name for folding the five fingers of the hand inwards and using that hand itself as a weapon. The meaning is a son who has the power to slay enemies by using the fist itself as a weapon, by the strength of his arm alone, without using any kind of weapon. To fight a wrestling bout by blows of the fist alone, without the help of weapons, much sturdiness and strength are needed in the body. In order to pray to the Marut deities to grant such an exceedingly strong and firm-limbed son, the words मुष्टिहा, बाहुजूतः (*muṣṭihā, bāhujūtaḥ*) are used in the present Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒राइ॒वेदच॑रमा॒ अहे॑व॒ प्रप्र॑ जायंते॒ अक॑वा॒ महो॑भिः ।  
> पृश्नेः॑ पु॒त्रा उ॑प॒मासो॒ रभि॑ष्टाः॒ स्वया॑ म॒त्या म॒रुतः॒ सं  ॑
> मिमिक्षुः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अराःइव । इत् । अचरमाः । अहाइव । प्रप्र । जायंते । अकवाः । महःभिः ।  
> पृश्नेः । पुत्राः । उपमासः । रभिष्ठाः । स्वय्या । मत्या । मरुतः । सं । मिमिक्षुः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वरुणप्रघासे मारुत्या आमिक्षाया अरा इवेति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । अरा
> इवेदचरमा अहेवेमं मे वरुण श्रुधि । आ-२-१७ । इति ॥ एकादशिने मारुते पशावेषैन पशुपुरोडाशस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं च । अरा इवेदचरमा अहेव या व
> शर्म शशमानाय संति । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> अरा इवेत् रथशंकव इवाचरमा अनिकृष्टाः । सर्वसमाः सहैवोत्पन्नाश्चेत्यर्थः । अहेवाहानीव । दिवसा यथा सर्वेऽपि षष्टिघटिकात्मकास्तद्वत्सप्तसंख्योपेतसप्तगणरूपेण समा इत्यर्थः । अनेन दृष्टांतद्वयेन वैसदृश्याभावः प्रतिपादितः । एवमुक्तलक्षणा महोभिस्तेजोभिः प्रप्र जायंते । प्रकर्षेण प्रादुर्भवंति ॥
> एकः प्रसमुपोदः पादपूरण इत्युपसर्गाभ्यासः स च पूरणः ॥ ते चाकवा अनल्पाः।
> यद्वा महोभिरित्यस्य विशेषणं । पृश्नेर्माध्यमिकाया वाचो गोरूपाया
> अंतरिक्षस्य ना पुत्रस्थानीया उपमासः प्रत्येकं समाना रभिष्ठाः प्रकृष्टवेगाः ।
> एवं महानुभावा मरुतः स्वया मत्या स्वकीययैवानुग्रहबुद्ध्या संमिमिक्षुः ।
> वृष्टा सम्यक् सिंचंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the Varuṇa-praghāsa rite, for the Marut offering of curds (āmikṣā), अरा इव (*arā iva*) is the yājyā verse; and the sūtra says: अरा इवेदचरमा अहेवेमं मे वरुण श्रुधि (*arā ivedacaramā ahevemaṃ me varuṇa śrudhi*) (Ā. 2-17). It is also the yājyā verse of the animal-cake offering in the Marut animal sacrifice of the eleven-stake kind**NOTE**; and the sūtra says: अरा इवेदचरमा अहेव या व शर्म शशमानाय संति । (*arā ivedacaramā aheva yā va śarma śaśamānāya saṃti |*) (Ā. 3-7).

अरा इवेत् (*arā ivet*): like the spokes of a chariot wheel; अचरमाः (*acaramāḥ*): not inferior, that is, all alike, born together. अहेवाहानीव (*ahevāhānīva*): like the days; as all days consist of sixty ghaṭikās, so they are equal in the form of seven groups of seven each. By these two examples the absence of any dissimilarity is shown. Being of this nature, they are born forth with their splendours (mahas), that is, they appear in glory. The prefix is repeated to fill out the foot of the verse, and the repeated prefix is a filler. They are अकवा (*akavā*), not small. Or else it is an epithet of महोभिः (*mahobhiḥ*). Pṛśni is the middle speech in the form of a cow, that is, the atmosphere; those who stand as her sons are उपमासः (*upamāsaḥ*), each one like the other, and रभिष्ठाः (*rabhiṣṭhāḥ*), of surpassing speed. Such mighty Maruts, by their own mind, that is, by their own intention of showing favour, संमिमिक्षुः (*saṃmimikṣuḥ*): they pour down rain well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरा इवेत् (*arā ivet*)—like the spokes of a chariot wheel
- अचरमाः (*acaramāḥ*)—none inferior to another
- अहेव (*aheva*)—the Maruts, all equal like the days
- अकवाः (*akavāḥ*)—not small, having greatness

### Printed p. 754

- महोभिः (*mahobhiḥ*)—with great splendours
- प्रप्र जायंते (*prapra jāyaṃte*)—appear together in the same manner
- उपमासः (*upamāsaḥ*)—those who resemble one another
- रभिष्ठाः (*rabhiṣṭhāḥ*)—those of excellent speed
- पृश्नेः पुत्राः (*pṛśneḥ putrāḥ*)—sons of Pṛśni
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- स्वया मत्या (*svayā matyā*)—by their own self-prompted intention of favour
- सं मिमिक्षुः (*saṃ mimikṣuḥ*)—pour down rain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, who like the spokes of a chariot wheel are none inferior to another, and who like the days are all equal, being great appear together in the same manner with their great splendours. The Maruts, who resemble one another, are of excellent speed and are the sons of Pṛśni, pour down rain by their own self-prompted intention of favour.

##### English translation
Like the spokes of a wheel, none (of you) are inferior (to the rest), but equal as days (of like duration): the sons of Prishni are born all alike, none inferior in splendour: rapid in speed, the Maruts, of their own free favour, send down (the rains).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the rite called वरुणप्रघास (*varuṇapraghāsa*), in the offering made to the deities Āmikṣā and the Maruts, this Ṛk अरा इवेदचरमा (*arā ivedacaramā*) is to be used as the yājyā mantra, as is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अरा इवेदचरमा अहेवेनुं मे वरुण श्रुधि (*arā ivedacaramā ahevenuṃ me varuṇa śrudhi*) (Ā. 2-17). In the animal sacrifice connected with the eleven-stake Marut rite also, this very Ṛk is to be used as the yājyā mantra in the offering of the animal-cake, as is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अरा इवेदचरमा अहेव या वः शर्म शशमानाय संति (*arā ivedacaramā aheva yā vaḥ śarma śaśamānāya saṃti*) (Ā. 3-7).

In this Ṛk two comparisons are given for the point that all the Marut deities are alike. अराइवेत् अचरमाः (*arāivet acaramāḥ*): as the spokes (spokes) of a chariot wheel are all equal, neither more nor less, and all of one kind, so each one of the Marut deities is of one kind. There is no difference whatever among them in form, in quality, in shape, in greatness or in origin. It is fitting that this has been explained by the example of the spokes of a chariot wheel. In the same way the other example, अहेव (*aheva*), is also most fitting. The days are all of one kind. As yesterday, so today; as today, so tomorrow; as tomorrow, so the day after, and so on: every day is of one kind without any difference, whether in brightness,

### Printed p. 755

or in measure. Therefore these two kinds of example suit the Marut deities very well.

स्वया मत्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः—स्वकीयैवानुग्रहबुद्ध्या वृष्टा सम्यक् सिंचंति । (*svayā matyā marutaḥ saṃ mimikṣuḥ—svakīyaivānugrahabuddhyā vṛṣṭā samyak siṃcaṃti |*) These Marut deities pour down rain by their own mind, that is, without the compulsion or prompting of others, by the good intention that they should show favour to the people: this is the meaning.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्प्राया॑सिष्ट॒ पृष॑तीभि॒रश्वै॑र्वीळुप॒विभि॑र्मरुतो॒ रथे॑भिः।  
> क्षोदं॑त॒ आपो॑ रिण॒ते वना॒न्यवो॒स्स्रियो॑ वृष॒भः क्रं॑दतु॒  
> द्यौः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । प्र । अयासिष्ट । पृषतीभिः । अश्वैः । वीळुपविभिः । मरुतः । रथेभिः ।  
> क्षोदंते । आपः । रिणते । वनानि । अव । उस्रियः । वृषभः । क्रंदतु । द्यौः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो यद्यदा प्रायासिष्ट प्रगच्छथ पृषतीभिः पृषत्संज्ञकैरश्वैर्वाहनसाधनैरश्वैः । अश्वशब्दोऽत्र वाहनसामान्यवचनः । अतः पुल्लिंगता । तथान्यत्र !
> यदश्वान्सूष्टु पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं । ऋग्वे-५-५५-६ । रोहिदश्वोऽजाश्व इति समानाधिकरण्यप्रयोगः । एवंभूताश्वयुक्तैर्वीळुपविभिर्दृढरथनेमिभी रथेभिः प्रायासिष्ट। यद्वा। अश्वै रथैश्च सह मरुतो यदा प्रायासिष्ट तदापः क्षोदंते। क्षरंति!
> वनानि वृक्षसमूहा रिणते । हिंस्यंते । वेगेन भज्यंते । उस्रियः! उस्राः सूर्यरश्मयः । तत्संबंधी पर्जन्यो वृषभोऽपां वर्षिता द्यौर्द्योतमानोऽव क्रंदतु।
> अवाङ्मुखं शब्दयतु वृष्ट्यर्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, when you set out with spotted horses, horses called pṛṣat, which are the means of conveyance (the word horse here is a general word for a conveyance, hence the masculine form). So elsewhere also: यदश्वान्सूष्टु पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं (*yadaśvānsūṣṭu pṛṣatīrayugdhvaṃ*) (Ṛgve. 5-55-6)**NOTE**; रोहिदश्वोऽजाश्व (*rohidaśvo 'jāśva*) are similar usages in the same case. You set out with chariots yoked with such horses and having firm wheel-rims. Or else: when the Maruts set out together with horses and chariots, then the waters flow forth, the clusters of trees are damaged, that is, broken by the speed. उस्रियः (*usriyaḥ*) are the rays of the sun; Parjanya connected with them, the showerer of the waters, the shining heaven, let him roar downward, let him sound with his face turned down, for the sake of rain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- पृषतीभिः (*pṛṣatībhiḥ*)—with those named pṛṣat
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—yoked with horses
- वीळुपविभिः (*vīḷupavibhiḥ*)—having firm wheel-rims**NOTE**
- रथेभिः (*rathebhiḥ*)—with chariots

- प्रायासिष्ट (*prāyāsiṣṭa*)—you set out (then)
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- क्षोदंतॆ (*kṣodaṃtè*)—flow forth and run
- वनानि (*vanāni*)—clusters of trees
- रिणते (*riṇate*)—are damaged
- उस्रियः (*usriyaḥ*)—one impelled by the sun's rays
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—Parjanya, the maker of rain
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—shining
- अवक्रंदतु (*avakraṃdatu*)—let him sound with his face turned down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, when you set out with chariots yoked with the horses called pṛṣat and having firm wheel-rims, then the waters flow forth and run, the clusters of trees are damaged. Let Parjanya, impelled by the sun's rays and the maker of rain, shining, make a sound with his face turned down, for the sake of rain.

##### English translation
When, Maruts, you come with stout-axled cars drawn by spotted steeds, then the waters descend, the forests are damaged, and the bright showerer (of the rain), influenced by the solar rays, may emit a downward sound.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the pouring down of rain is described. When the Marut deities set out seated in their chariots, that is, when the atmosphere is covered with black clouds and the storm wind is blowing with the utmost force, the rain falls from the atmosphere upon the earth and runs in the form of floods. As the wind blows with the utmost speed, the trees shake, and sometimes are overthrown with their roots, and so suffer damage. In such a situation Parjanya, the maker of creation, produces fearful sounds such as thunder and lightning as signs of rain: this description of rain is stated here.

पृषतीभिः अश्वैः— पृषत्संज्ञकैरश्वैर्वाहनसाधनैरश्वैः। अश्वशब्दोऽत्र वाहनसामान्यवचनः । (*pṛṣatībhiḥ aśvaiḥ— pṛṣatsaṃjñakairaśvairvāhanasādhanairaśvaiḥ| aśvaśabdo 'tra vāhanasāmānyavacanaḥ |*) In describing the various vehicles of the deities, Yāska has said पृषत्यो (*pṛṣatyo*): the deer with white spots are themselves the vehicles of the Marut deities (Ni. 2.28).

यदश्यान्नूर्षु पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं हिरण्ययान्यत्या अमुग्धं (*yadaśyānnūrṣu pṛṣatīrayugdhvaṃ hiraṇyayānyatyā amugdhaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-55-6)

In this Ṛk it is said, "yoke to the chariot your horses called पृषतीः (*pṛṣatīḥ*)." In the present Ṛk there are the two words पृषतीभिः (*pṛṣatībhiḥ*) and अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*). If पृषतीभिः (*pṛṣatībhiḥ*) means the vehicles of the Marut deities,

### Printed p. 757

is not the use of the word अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*) useless? To this: the commentator has explained the word horse here as a general word for a vehicle. That is, the meaning of these two words is to be understood as the horses (deer) called pṛṣatī that carry the Marut deities.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रथि॑ष्ट॒ याम॑न्‌पृथि॒वी चि॑देषां॒ भर्ते॑व॒ गर्भं॒ स्वमिच्छवो॑  
> धुः ।  
> वाता॒न्‌ह्यश्वा॑न्थु॒र्या॑युयु॒ज्रे व॒र्षं स्वेदं॑ चक्रिरेरु॒द्रिया॑सः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रथिष्ट । यामन् । पृथिवी । चित् । एषां । भर्ताऽइव । गर्भं । स्वं । इत् । शवः ।  
> धुः ।  
> वातान् । हि । अश्वान् । धुरि । आयुयुज्रे । वर्षं । स्वेदं । चक्रिरे । रुद्रियासः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषां मरुतां यामन्यामनि गमने पृथिवी चित् भूमिः । चिदिति पूरणः ।
> प्रथिष्ट । प्रख्याताभवत् । गर्भयोग्याभवदित्यर्थः । ते च मरुतो भर्ता लौकिकः
> पतिर्गर्भमिव भार्यायास्तथा भूम्याः स्वमित्स्वभूतं गर्भं गर्भस्थानीयं शव
> उदकं धुः । स्थापितवंतः । हि यस्माद्वातात् गंत्र्यनश्वान् धुरि रथसंबंधिन्यायुयुज्रे आयोजितवंतः तस्माद्वर्षं स्वेदं स्वेदस्थानीयं वृष्टिसंस्कृत्यायं
> चक्रिरे कुर्वंति रुद्रियासो रुद्रपुत्राः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the going of these Maruts, the earth became renowned, that is, became fit for conception; चित् (*cit*) is a filler. And those Maruts, as a worldly husband places an embryo in his wife, so placed in the earth their own embryo-like water (शव (*śava*) means water). Because they have yoked to the yoke of the chariot horses swift as the wind**NOTE**, therefore they make rain, which stands in the place of sweat**NOTE**. रुद्रियासो (*rudriyāso*) means the sons of Rudra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these Maruts
- यामन् (*yāman*)—at the time of going
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth
- प्रथिष्ट (*prathiṣṭa*)—became fertile
- भर्ता (*bhartā*)—a worldly husband
- गर्भं इव (*garbhaṃ iva*)—as he places the embryo in his wife (so the Maruts also)
- स्वमित् (*svamit*)—their own, in the form of an embryo
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—the water
- धुः (*dhuḥ*)—have placed (in the earth)

### Printed p. 758

- हि (*hi*)—therefore
- वातान् (*vātān*)—swift like the wind
- अश्वान् (*aśvān*)—their horses
- धुरि (*dhuri*)—to the yoke of the chariot
- आ युयुज्रे (*ā yuyujre*)—have joined and tied
- रुद्रियासः (*rudriyāsaḥ*)—the Maruts, sons of Rudra
- स्वेदं (*svedaṃ*)—their own, in the form of sweat
- वर्षं (*varṣaṃ*)—the rain
- चिक्रिरे (*cikrire*)—pour down**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time of the going of these Maruts the earth becomes fertile. As a worldly husband places an embryo in his wife, the Maruts also have placed in the earth their own water, which is like an embryo. Therefore they have joined and tied their horses, swift as the wind, to the yoke of the chariot. The Maruts, sons of Rudra, pour down their rain, which is like sweat.

##### English translation
On their approach the earth becomes capable of fertility, and they deposit in her water as their germ, as the husband generates the embryo of the child : they have harnessed their horses fleet as the wind: the sons of Rudra have emitted their perspiration, (the rain).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

एषां यामन् पृथिवी प्रथिष्टा चित्—मरुतां गमने भूमिः प्रख्याताभवत् । (*eṣāṃ yāman pṛthivī prathiṣṭā cit—marutāṃ gamane bhūmiḥ prakhyātābhavat |*) It is said here that by the coming of the Marut deities the earth became fertile. With the coming of the Marut deities the rain pours down abundantly, the earth becomes wet, and this helps plants and the like to sprout. Therefore the assertion that the coming of the Marut deities is the cause of the earth's fertility is only natural. In this matter the Ṛṣi has here given an example:

भर्तेव गर्भं स्वमिच्छवो धुः—ते च मरुतो लौकिकः पतिः गर्भमिव भार्यायास्तथा भूम्याः स्वमित् स्वभूतं गर्भं गर्भस्थानीयं शव उदकं धुः स्थापितवंतः । (*bharteva garbhaṃ svamicchavo dhuḥ—te ca maruto laukikaḥ patiḥ garbhamiva bhāryāyāstathā bhūmyāḥ svamit svabhūtaṃ garbhaṃ garbhasthānīyaṃ śava udakaṃ dhuḥ sthāpitavaṃtaḥ |*)

The idea stated here is that, as in the ways of the world a husband places an embryo in his wife and from it a son is born, so the Marut deities, by pouring water (rain) on the earth, which stands in the place of the wife, are the cause of the birth of plants and the like.

स्वेदं वर्षं-स्वेदस्थानीयं वृष्टिसंत्यायं (*svedaṃ varṣaṃ-svedasthānīyaṃ vṛṣṭisaṃtyāyaṃ*)**NOTE** Here the water in the form of rain

### Printed p. 759

is compared to the sweat of the Marut deities. As sweat comes out of a man's body and oozes when he moves about in the sun, so, the Ṛṣi describes, when the Marut deities come, the water in the form of rain pours down upon the earth.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ह॒ये नरो॒ मरु॑तो मृ॒ळता॑ न॒स्तुवी॑मघासो॒ अमृ॑ता॒  ॑
> ऋतज्ञाः ।  
> सत्य॑श्रुतः॒ कव॑यो॒ युवा॑नो॒ बृह॑द्गिरयो बृ॒हदु॒क्षमा॑णाः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हये । नरः । मरुतः । मृळत । नः । तुविमघासः । अमृताः । ऋतज्ञाः ।  
> सत्यश्रुतः । कवयः । युवानः । बृहत्गिरयः । बृहत् । उक्षमाणाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हये हे नरो नेतारो मरुतो नोऽस्मान्मृळत । सुखयत । अस्मभ्यं
> हिताय ना सुखिनो भवत । हे तुवीमघासः प्रभूतधना अमृता अमरणस्वभावा
> ऋतज्ञा उदकस्य यज्ञस्य वा ज्ञातारः । कर्तार इत्यर्थः । सत्यश्रुतः सत्येन सत्यफलत्वेन प्रसिद्धाः कवयो मेधाविनो युवानो नित्यतरुणा बृहद्गिरयः प्रभूतस्तुतयो बृहदत्यधिकमुक्षमाणा हविर्भिः सेविता उदकं वा सिंचंतो यूयं
> मृळत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O leaders, O Maruts, make us happy; become happy for our good. O you of abundant wealth (तुवीमघासः (*tuvīmaghāsaḥ*)), you immortal ones, of deathless nature, you who know the water or the sacrifice, that is, who accomplish them; renowned for truth, that is, famed for the truth of the fruit you give; wise; ever young; of abundant praises; and, in great measure, served with oblations or sprinkling water: such as you are, make us happy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तुवीमघासः (*tuvīmaghāsaḥ*)—those of abundant wealth
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—those without death
- ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*)—those who know the truth
- सत्यश्रुतं (*satyaśrutaṃ*)**NOTE**—those of true fame
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the wise
- युवानः (*yuvānaḥ*)—the ever-young
- बृहद्गिरयः (*bṛhadgirayaḥ*)—worthy of abundant praises
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—in great measure
- उक्षमाणाः (*ukṣamāṇāḥ*)—those to whom oblations are offered
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—leaders
- हये मरुतः (*haye marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळत (*mṛḷata*)—make happy

### Printed p. 760

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, you of abundant wealth, deathless, knowers of the truth, of true fame, wise, ever young, worthy of abundant praises, to whom oblations are offered in great measure, and leaders: make us happy.

##### English translation
Ho, Maruts, leaders (of rites), be propitious to us, you who are infinitely opulent, immortal, shedders of rain, renowned for truth, wise, young, greatly glorified, and worshipped with copious oblations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हये (*haye*): the word is used in the vocative sense, like the word हे (*he*). Therefore हये मरुतः (*haye marutaḥ*) here means O Maruts, O Marut deities. This word is found only in these three Ṛks:

हये देवा यूयमिदापयः स्थ ते मृळत नाधमानाय मह्यं (*haye devā yūyamidāpayaḥ stha te mṛḷata nādhamānāya mahyaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-29-4)

हये नरो मरुतो मृळता नस्तुवीमघासो अमृता ऋतज्ञाः (*haye naro maruto mṛḷatā nastuvīmaghāso amṛtā ṛtajñāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 557-8)**NOTE**

हये जाये मनसा शिष्ठ घोरे वचांसि मिश्रा कृणवावहै नु (*haye jāye manasā śiṣṭha ghore vacāṃsi miśrā kṛṇavāvahai nu*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-1)

This word is not used anywhere else in the Ṛgveda. In all three places it is used in the vocative sense of हे (*he*).

The fifty-ninth hymn.**NOTE**

## Sūkta 59 (Maṇḍala 5)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र वः स्पळित्यष्टर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं श्यावात्वस्यार्षं मारुतं । अष्टमी
> त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टाः सप्त जगत्यः । प्र वः स्पट् त्रिष्टुबंतमित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ विनियोगो
> लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn of eight Ṛks that begins with प्र वः (*pra vaḥ*) is the third hymn; its seer is Śyāvāśva**NOTE**, its deity the Maruts; the eighth Ṛk is in Triṣṭubh metre, and the remaining seven are in Jagatī metre. The Anukramaṇikā says प्र वः स्पट् त्रिष्टुबंतमित्यनुक्रमणिका (*pra vaḥ spaṭ triṣṭubaṃtamityanukramaṇikā*). The application is by indication.

### Printed p. 761

Translation: This hymn beginning प्र वः स्पळक्रन् (*pra vaḥ spaḷakran*) is the third hymn in the fifth Anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. The seer of this hymn is Śyāvāśva; the deity is the Maruts; the eighth Ṛk of this hymn is in Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining seven Ṛks are in Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said प्र वः स्पट् त्रिष्टुबंतं (*pra vaḥ spaṭ triṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). The application is by indication (लैंगिकवु (*laiṃgikavu*)).

- Ṛṣi: Śyāvāśva Ātreya
- Devatā: Maruts
- Chandas: 1-7 Jagatī; 8 Triṣṭubh

> सुष्टु प्राप्तन्याय दानायाक्रन् ॥ क्रंदतेः शब्दकर्मणो लडर्थे लुणु तिपि

> संचरंति । स्वं भानुं स्वकीयं तेजोर्णवर्मेघैः सहानु श्रथयंते ।
> अनुश्लेषयंति । अनुकूलं प्रापयंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, for you, for the giver of oblations, who is well reached, the clear-voiced Hotṛ priest cries out aloud, that is, praises you; or he cries out for the well-reached gift to you. O Hotṛ, to the shining heaven, the deity of heaven, offer praise aloud, O my self. And to the earth I bring the hymn of praise, that is, I accomplish it; since heaven and earth are the support of the Maruts, they too come in as sharers here**NOTE**. Moreover those Maruts sprinkle the pervading hosts of water; they cross the atmosphere on all sides, that is, they roam; they cause their own light to cling together with the clouds, that is, they bring it favourably.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वः (*vaḥ*)—you (O Maruts)
- स्पट् (*spaṭ*)—the Hotṛ priest
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—easily reached
- दावने (*dāvane*)—for the sake of giving
- प्र अक्रन् (*pra akran*)—praises exceedingly (O Hotṛ)
- दिवे (*dive*)—to the shining atmosphere
- प्र अर्च (*pra arca*)—offer exceeding praise
- पृथिव्यै (*pṛthivyai*)—addressed to the earth
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the hymn of praise
- भरे (*bhare*)—I compose
- अश्वान् (*aśvān*)—the all-pervading waters
- उक्षंते (*ukṣaṃte*)—(the Maruts) cause to pour down
- रजः (*rajaḥ*)—the atmosphere
- आ तरुषंते (*ā taruṣaṃte*)—go round and roam
- स्वं भानुं (*svaṃ bhānuṃ*)—their own radiance
- अर्णवैः (*arṇavaiḥ*)—with the clouds
- अनु श्रथयंते (*anu śrathayaṃte*)—join and unite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, the Hotṛ priest praises you exceedingly for the sake of a gift that he may happily obtain. O Hotṛ, offer exceeding praise to the shining atmosphere. I offer praise addressed to the earth. The Maruts cause the all-pervading waters to pour down. And they go round and roam through the whole atmosphere, uniting their own radiance with the clouds.

##### English translation
The priest glorfies you, Maruts, for the good of the donor of the oblation : offer worsip to the shining (heaven): I bring offerings to the earth : they, the Maruts, scatter the rapid (rain); they traverse the firmment ; they combine their own radiance with (that of) the clouds.

### Printed p. 763

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

स्पट्—स्पष्ट होता । (*spaṭ—spaṣṭa hotā |*) Since he touches the oblations and the like at the time of the homa, the priest called Hotṛ is here called स्पट् (*spaṭ*).

अश्वान् (*aśvān*): the word aśva, formed from the root अशू व्याप्तौ (*aśū vyāptau*), is explained here as the all-pervading waters. Since when rain falls water spreads everywhere, the all-pervading water is indicated by the word अश्वान् (*aśvān*).

रजः (*rajaḥ*): it is explained here as the atmosphere. The word has many meanings. Yāska, on this word, says:

रजो रज्यतेर्ज्योती रज उच्यते उदकं रज उच्यते । लोका रजांस्युच्यंते । (*rajo rajyaterjyotī raja ucyate udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā rajāṃsyucyaṃte |*) (Ni. 4-19)

The word रजस् (*rajas*), formed from the root रंज् (*raṃj*) which gives the sense of shining, means light, and water, and also the worlds.

रजांसि चित्रा वि चरंति तन्यवो दिवः सम्राजा पयसा न उक्षतं । (*rajāṃsi citrā vi caraṃti tanyavo divaḥ samrājā payasā na ukṣataṃ |*) (Kha. Saṃ. 5-63-5)**NOTE**

Quoting this Ṛk, the author of the Nirukta has said that रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) means the worlds; in the 44th section of the 10th chapter of the Nirukta,

अज्जामुक्थैरहिं गृणीषे बुद्धे नदीनां रजस्सु षीदन् (*ajjāmukthairahiṃ gṛṇīṣe buddhe nadīnāṃ rajassu ṣīdan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-16)

in explaining this Ṛk, he says that रजस्सु (*rajassu*) means उदकेषु (*udakeṣu*), that is, in the waters; and in the 7th section of the 12th chapter,

एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमंजते । (*etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumaṃjate |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1)

in explaining this Ṛk, he explains रजसः (*rajasaḥ*) as the atmosphere.

श्रीणि भांति रजांस्यस्य यत्पदानि तु तेजसा (*śrīṇi bhāṃti rajāṃsyasya yatpadāni tu tejasā*) so the author of the Bṛhaddevatā, describing Viṣṇu's striding over the three worlds, used the word रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) as a synonym for the three worlds.

### Printed p. 764

Generally रजः, रजांसि (*rajaḥ, rajāṃsi*) is a word that is a synonym of the worlds. But in Ṛks such as

यन्ना सोमासो ममदन्यदुक्कोभे भयेते रजसी अपारे (*yannā somāso mamadanyadukkobhe bhayete rajasī apāre*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-42-6)

this word is in the dual and only the technical meaning, heaven and earth, is stated. Only in some places, that is, in a couple of Ṛks such as

अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः (*ahaśca kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1)

the original meaning of the root is primary, as in रजसी जगद्रंजयंतौ (*rajasī jagadraṃjayaṃtau*). In the present Ṛk it means the shining atmosphere.

भानुं (*bhānuṃ*): the word भानु (*bhānu*) is read among the names of the day (2-20). भानु (*bhānu*) has several meanings: the sun, a ray of the sun, light, the day. Here the word is used in the sense of light.

#### Ṛk 2

> अमा॑देषां भि॒यसा॒ भूमि॑रेजति॒ नौर्न पू॒र्णा क्ष॑रति॒व्यथि॑र्य॒ती ।  
> दू॒रे॒दृशो॒ ये चि॒तयं॑त॒ एम॑भिरं॒तर्म॒हे वि॒दथे॑ येतिरे॒  
> नरः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अमात् । एषां । भियसा । भूमिः । एजति । नौः । न । पूर्णा । क्षरति । व्यथिः । यती।  
> दूरेदृशः । ये । चितयंते । एमभिः । अंतः । महे । विदथे । येतिरे । नरः॥

### Printed p. 765

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषां ॥ अन्वादेशविषयत्वादनुदात्तः ॥ एषां मरुतां भियसा भयेन
> भूमिरेजति । कंपते नार्न पूर्णा प्राणिभिः । सा यथोदकमध्यॆ क्षरति चलति
> व्यथिर्व्यथिता यती गच्छंती । एतदुभयं नौविशेषणं । दूरेदृशो दूरे दृश्यमाना अपि ये मरुत एमभिर्गमनैश्चितयंते ज्ञायंते ते महांतो मरुतो
> विदथे यज्ञे महे महते हविषे हविर्भक्षणायांतर्द्वानापृथिव्योर्मध्यॆ
> येतिरे । यतंते । नरो नेतारो मरुतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of these Maruts, through fear, the earth trembles, like a boat full of living beings, which, going through the midst of the water, sways and moves, being shaken; both these are epithets of the boat. Those Maruts who, though seen far away, are known by their goings: those great Maruts strive between heaven and earth in the sacrifice, for the great oblation, to eat the oblation. They are leaders: the Maruts.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूर्णा (*pūrṇā*)—filled with people
- नार्न (*nārna*)—the boat
- क्षरति (*kṣarati*)—as it trembles
- व्यथिः (*vyathiḥ*)—being alarmed
- यती (*yatī*)—and moving forward, so
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these Maruts
- भियसा (*bhiyasā*)—through fear
- भूमिः (*bhūmiḥ*)—the earth
- एजति (*ejati*)—trembles
- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts
- दूरेदृशाः (*dūredṛśāḥ*)—even though seen very far away
- एमभिः (*emabhiḥ*)—by their goings
- चितयंते (*citayaṃte*)—are exactly known
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—such Maruts, the leaders
- विदथे (*vidathe*)—in the sacrifice
- महे (*mahe*)—to eat the great oblation
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the midst of heaven and earth
- येतिरे (*yetire*)—go about and come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a boat full of people trembles and, as it moves forward, is alarmed, so the earth trembles through the fear of these Maruts. The Maruts who, though seen very far away, are exactly known by their individual goings, those Maruts, the leaders, go about and come between heaven and earth to eat the great oblation in the sacrifice.

##### English translation
From their approach the earth trembles with fear, as a crowded boat goes quivering (through the water) : visible from afar, they are recog- nized by their movements : the Maruts, leaders (of rites), pass between (heaven and earth) to the solemn sacrifice.
